title: M12 — Pair-only endpoint and independent-work retention limit
note: Development addendum 0.1 · 5 October 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Three-qubit constant pair generator has the exact joint endpoint. Uniform full-state window error is 1/2, above 11/100; the independent-clock single-work-qubit family cannot improve it. Toy resource caps and structured costs checked. 11 exact and 56 numerical checks; full controller open; independent review pending; physical promotion 0. UD M12: pair-only endpoint and retention limit5 October 2026 · Development addendum 0.1 · Independent review pending · Physical promotion 0Fresh checks: 11 exact and 56 numerical. Pair-only endpoint comparator; selected retention window fails.Development — no registry entry. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. This follows WBS 5.2 with an explicit changed-generator candidate, WBS 5.3/4.3 with its full-state window test, and WBS 3.1–3.2 with small-instance structure/cost calculations. It does not implement the full 380-qubit bank, native preparation or a general autonomous pair controller. M11’s direct encoded-generator obstruction remains valid and unchanged. 1. Candidate scope and its predeclared small resource envelope Keep M11’s clock encoding: addresses 0,1,2 correspond to binary 00,01,11, with 10 padding. There are two clock qubits and one work qubit B. Clock dimension 3 is prime; encoded clock capacity is 4=2^2. Full encoded dimension is 8=2^3, valid dimension is 6=2·3, and padding dimension is 2. Initial clock |00> and the work state are supplied. The work may be entangled with arbitrary external spectators. No external switch or pulse timestamp acts after launch. Choose positive engineered frequency scale kappa_C, distinct from the full-controller scale kappa_0=4096. For this toy, set N_max=3 binary factors, grouped onsite/pair norm cap h_max=3·kappa_C/2, and total term-norm cap J_max=4·kappa_C. These are finite design limits for this small test, not measured capability, native constants or full-controller limits. The three-address free clock encoded on its two qubits has generator HCenc=κC2(IX+ZX+XI−XZ). H_C^{\mathrm{enc}}=\frac{\kappa_C}{\sqrt2}(IX+ZX+XI-XZ). Replace the dressed gate-history generator with an independent clock and an onsite work rotation: Hpair=HCenc⊗IB−κCIC⊗YB=κC2(IXI+ZXI+XII−XZI)−κCIIY. H_{\mathrm{pair}}=H_C^{\mathrm{enc}}\otimes I_B-\kappa_C I_C\otimes Y_B =\frac{\kappa_C}{\sqrt2}(IXI+ZXI+XII-XZI)-\kappa_C IIY. Every term acts on at most two binary factors. The full generator, including the clock, is pair-supported; there are no extra ancillary qubits. The encoded valid clock subspace is invariant. Unlike M11’s global zero extension, the padding block here contains work precession -kappa_C·Y. That explicitly declared changed extension is allowed; the candidate is not claimed equal to M11’s generator on the full space. The clock and work do not interact. This is an endpoint-compressed comparator, not a timer that causes chronological X-then-Z execution. The known product ZX=iY has been supplied directly in the work generator. That operation is unusually simple; no general many-qubit source word is thereby synthesized. 2. WBS 5.2: exact joint endpoint with a constant pair generator Theorem M12.1 (ready-clock endpoint). For any work input, including its entanglement with any spectator, at T_C=pi/(2·kappa_C), e−iTCHpair|00⟩|ψ⟩=−|11⟩ZX|ψ⟩. e^{-iT_C H_{\mathrm{pair}}}|00\rangle|\psi\rangle =-|11\rangle ZX|\psi\rangle. The encoded clock stays valid at every time. At 2T_C=pi/kappa_C, the complete encoded unitary is -I, hence its channel returns to identity. Proof. The clock and onsite work terms commute and have disjoint support. Their propagator factors. The free three-address spin clock transfers |00> to -|11> at T_C; the work factor is eiκCTCY=iY=ZXe^{i\kappa_C T_CY}=iY=ZX. Their tensor product gives the same joint ready-clock endpoint as M11. The clock free spectrum is -2·kappa_C,0,0,2·kappa_C on its encoded space, so it returns at 2T_C. The work propagator then equals -I. Clock invariance follows from its support-wise encoded free-clock construction; the work term cannot leave the clock code. Spectator tensoring preserves these identities. ▫\square Thus an autonomous pair-only endpoint exists for this tiny supplied task. M11’s positive direct-generator distance never implied endpoint impossibility. The intermediate joint trajectories differ: M11 correlates its clock prefixes with X and ZX, while this candidate keeps the clock independent and continuously rotates B about Y. A numerical midpoint comparison records that difference. No source-production, capture, donor-renewal or failure-history claim is inherited from endpoint equivalence alone. 3. WBS 4.3 and 5.3: compute the actual full-state window error Fix the auxiliary target before execution as the same freely propagated encoded clock state chi_C(t). The work target is the completed ZX operation. Therefore, for an arbitrary work/spectator state rho_BR, ρactual(t)=χC(t)⊗[(eiκCtY⊗IR)ρBR(e−iκCtY⊗IR)], \rho_{\mathrm{actual}}(t)=\chi_C(t)\otimes [(e^{i\kappa_CtY}\otimes I_R)\rho_{BR}(e^{-i\kappa_CtY}\otimes I_R)], ρtarget(t)=χC(t)⊗[(ZX⊗IR)ρBR(ZX⊗IR)†]. \rho_{\mathrm{target}}(t)=\chi_C(t)\otimes [(ZX\otimes I_R)\rho_{BR}(ZX\otimes I_R)^{\dagger}]. Because the clock is identical and independent in these two explicitly proved states, tensoring it preserves trace distance. This is a legitimate full-state reduction for this candidate, not permission to ignore timer correlations in another design. Theorem M12.2 (worst joint error). With trace distance using the one-half convention, the supremum over work inputs and arbitrary spectators at a fixed time is E(t)=|sin(κCt−π/2)|. E(t)=|\sin(\kappa_Ct-\pi/2)|. For the interval [pi/(3·kappa_C),2·pi/(3·kappa_C)], its uniform supremum is exactly 1/2, attained at either endpoint by work |0>. Consequently the candidate fails M11’s 11/100 window threshold even with perfect preparation and exact couplings. Proof. Relative to ZX the work evolution is a Y rotation through delta=kappa_C·t-pi/2, up to an irrelevant global phase. For any purified work/spectator input, its overlap with the rotated state is cos(delta)+i·sin(delta)·expectation(Y). Its squared magnitude is at least cos(delta)^2, so pure-state distance is at most |sin(delta)|. Partial trace gives the same upper bound for mixed inputs. Work |0> has expectation(Y)=0 and attains it. Delta ranges from -pi/6 to pi/6 on the selected interval, giving the exact maximum 1/2. ▫\square On the common left-endpoint work input |0>, M11’s joint error is sqrt(247)/16, while this candidate’s is 1/2. The improvement is real but insufficient. Reducing the requested interval to a narrower neighborhood would change the contract: E(t)<=epsilon near T_C requires |t−TC|≤arcsin(ϵ)/κC|t-T_C|\le\arcsin(\epsilon)/\kappa_C for 0<=epsilon<=1. We do not change the interval or the threshold to admit this candidate. 4. A scoped family limit: higher winding does not rescue the window Consider the broader independent-clock, single-work-qubit family. The clock follows the chosen common reference independently, while B evolves under any time-independent Hermitian H_B. Require the complete work channel at T_C to equal ZX for every work/spectator input. Identity energy shifts are irrelevant to this channel. Theorem M12.3 (best independent-work uniform retention). Every such H_B has form alpha·I+omega·Y with omega=(2m+1)·kappa_C for an integer m. Over the same interval, its worst joint error is at least 1/2. The least winding magnitude, |omega|=kappa_C, attains 1/2; all larger allowed magnitudes attain error one somewhere in the interval. Proof. Endpoint channel equality means e−iTCHB=eiϕZXe^{-iT_CH_B}=e^{i\phi}ZX. A Hermitian generator commutes with its exponential; because ZX has distinct eigenvalues, H_B must commute with Y and hence has the displayed qubit form. Its two eigenphase difference must be an odd multiple of pi, so 2ωTC=(2m+1)π2\omega T_C=(2m+1)\pi, giving the stated frequencies. At time T_C+s its worst error is |sin(omega·s)|. The interval includes all s between -T_C/3 and T_C/3. For minimal frequency, the sine argument reaches pi/6 and the maximum is 1/2. For larger odd magnitudes, this range contains pi/2 and the maximum is one. ▫\square This is a lower bound on actual worst channel error in the stated family, not a Duhamel sufficient-bound failure. It does not rule out clock/work coupling, additional work/timer/mediator factors, different allowed encodings, dissipative models with fully owned environments, or other architectures. Those changes require new full-domain proofs and resource accounting. The result identifies which family cannot meet the present contract. 5. WBS 1.3, 3.1–3.2: bounded small-instance structure and costs Group the clock pair terms on support C_0,C_1 and keep the three onsite terms separate. Their norms are kappa_C/sqrt(2), kappa_C/sqrt(2), sqrt(2)·kappa_C and kappa_C. Their sum is (2·sqrt(2)+1)·kappa_C, less than 4·kappa_C; the maximum is sqrt(2)·kappa_C, less than 3·kappa_C/2. Thus the declared small-instance h and J caps hold. The full candidate spectrum is {-3·kappa_C, -kappa_C repeated three times, kappa_C repeated three times, 3·kappa_C}; its norm is 3·kappa_C. For supplied clock |00> and work |0>, the mean energy is zero and variance is 3·kappa_C^2. Compared with M11, the generator norm and that variance rise by a factor 3/2. Norm and variance do not measure preparation work or prove native coupling availability. The exact Pauli structure is small enough to evaluate, advancing the WBS method without constructing a dense 380-qubit operator: Quantity Exact toy value Scope Nonidentity strings L 5 Four clock strings and one work string Coefficient norm Lambda (22+1)κC(2\sqrt2+1)\kappa_C Sum of absolute Pauli coefficients Anticommute coefficient C κC2\kappa_C^2 Two anticommuting clock pairs, each contributing kappa_C^2/2 Literal parity basis action B 15π/215\pi/2 M10 compiler action summed over the five strings Extra ancillary qubits 0 Three qubits include the encoded clock and work The anticommuting pairs are IXI with XZI and ZXI with XII. IIY commutes with all clock terms. If one chose an external digital approximation, M9/M10 would give digital norm error at most t2·kappa_C2/r and literal pulse action r·(15·pi/2)+t·(2·sqrt(2)+1)·kappa_C. That approximation is not needed by the specified autonomous analog generator, and an external pulse implementation would change its autonomy claim. The B calculation is a structural cost comparison, not a hidden driving schedule. For an actual autonomous implementation with full generator defect bounded by delta, Duhamel adds at most t·delta to the ideal full-state error, plus separately admitted preparation defects. These sufficient debits cannot repair an ideal actual error already above 11/100. No gain, calibration, background or preparation capability has been measured. 6. WBS dispositions and next admitted attempt Package Executed work Remaining work 5.2 Changed pair-only generator has the exact joint endpoint Candidate rejected for the selected window; full architecture remains open 5.3 / 4.3 Full-state error and independent-work family limit proved Coupled/resource-extended autonomous retention design 3.1 Exact structured toy operator and valid-code action Complete retained controller operator 3.2 Toy L, Lambda, C and B evaluated Useful full-controller bounds and synthesis costs 1.3 Small finite N/h/J envelope specified and met Full-controller numerical resource envelope remains open The next WBS 5.2 attempt must leave the failed independent single-qubit family: specify genuine clock/work or mediator coupling with all extra factors owned, audit pair support, then prove its interval error under finite resource limits before scaling. WBS 3.1–3.2 should separately continue on the structured retained source word. No complete-controller gate is marked closed by this small comparator. Replay separates exact Gaussian-integer support/commutation and rational cost/cap inequalities from floating-point spectra, propagated entangled inputs, padding, return and winding witnesses. The written family theorem supplies the general conclusion; six sampled winding choices do not replace its proof. M11 source/receipt and attached governance/ledger are preserved. Constructor checking does not constitute independent review. Missing Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was unavailable and not used.

title: M11 — Full-state contract and finite autonomous clock audit
note: Development addendum 0.1 · 5 October 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: WBS acceptance/domain specification and supplied noncommuting clock toy. Exact endpoint, explicit retention failure, and attained best direct Gray-encoded pair-generator defect kappa. Resource sizing and full autonomous pair architecture remain open. Independent review pending; physical promotion 0. UD M11: autonomous clock contract and audit5 October 2026 · Development addendum 0.1 · Independent review pending · Physical promotion 0Fresh checks: 46 exact and 22 numerical. Finite autonomous comparator; direct binary pair-only encoding fails.Development — no registry entry. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. This executes the first WBS batch at specification and small-instance level. The acceptance contract is a constructor’s development design rule, not a custodian promotion or measured specification. It preserves M8–M10 and the unmodified ledger/governance attachments. There is no complete autonomous pair-qubit controller or native preparation result. 1. WBS 1.1: define the target and retain the whole domain The selected endpoint is WBS D2: a supplied finite autonomous controller implementing the retained production/capture/donor-renewal semantics, with an admitted pair-qubit architecture. D1, the externally scheduled full supplied controller, remains an intermediate target. Native origin and physical qualification remain additional gates. Retain M8’s entire source/output/donor bank, every individual fuel factor, reference, flag, attempt record, END and original global address clock Q. The retained instance uses 380 binary encoding factors under M9’s support-wise extension policy. Any new scheduling timer C, program, mediator, ancillary or quantum control-reservoir factor is additional; do not rename or discard Q to hide it. Padding and arbitrary admitted spectators Y also remain in the comparison domain. The semantic bank target is the retained M7/M8 completed-bank target at the same declared parameter t, including old reference correlations and the unused final module. Define the auxiliary target state chi_A(t) before executing a candidate: it must come from an explicit reference evolution/program-resource specification, not from tracing the candidate’s actual output. The enlarged target has form $$ \rho_{\rm target}(t)=J\rho^{M8}_{\rm semantic}(t)J^{\dagger} \otimes\chi_A(t), $$ with spectator correlations carried by the specified semantic map. Product separation here deliberately requires a certified debit for undesired work/auxiliary correlations. If resources are consumed, their named final states belong in chi_A; a clean or reusable timer is not assumed. The semantic guarantee remains scoped to the admitted ready-bank input class and full-joint preparation defects used by the retained source theorem. It is not promoted to all arbitrary source states. Exact unitary implementation comparisons may be uniform on the full encoded space and arbitrary spectator extensions; the toy below has that stronger work-input statement. Postselection, output-only trace distance and discarded padding cannot replace the complete comparison. 2. WBS 1.2: define the permitted architecture For the intended binary realization, the complete post-launch Hermitian generator must be constant and decompose as onsite and two-qubit terms on the named tensor factors. All backgrounds and timer-conditioning interactions count. Auxiliary binary factors and changed encodings are allowed only when explicitly named and included in the state/resource certificate. Arbitrary abstract pair connectivity is allowed at this development stage; geometric locality is not claimed. Initial preparation is supplied. After launch there is no external pulse timestamp, classical switching schedule, hidden reset, measurement-conditioned renewal, or discarded control reservoir. A native ready-bank law is not inferred. Approximate mediator/encoded realizations are permitted only with full finite-time error, leakage, preparation and correlation costs. No infinite coupling, unbounded ancillary reservoir or uncharged effective projection is admitted. For each candidate, predeclare finite resource limits N_max (all binary factors), h_max (each grouped onsite/pair control term), J_max (sum of term norms), energy spread and initial preparation cost, as well as the observation interval. Group terms on each support before stating the cap; splitting a large term into many small ones cannot evade it. These numerical limits for the full controller are not yet sized. That unresolved envelope is part of WBS 1.3, so this release does not mark the entire first phase complete. The comparator toy below deliberately uses one three-address register and one binary work factor. It is pair-supported as a register construction. Its binary encoding is then audited against the stricter intended qubit definition. Neither result changes M8’s fixed-factor theorem. 3. WBS 1.3: specify the complete acceptance predicate Keep the retained comparison scale kappa_0=4096; it is an engineered development parameter, not calibrated proper time. The requested full-controller completion is T_0=pi/8192, with the M8 retention interval [pi/12288,pi/6144]. The candidate must compare at actual elapsed time tau=t across that interval, or charge the complete semantic-time difference. A separate circuit selected for each t is not an autonomous retention certificate. Use complete trace distance with the one-half convention. The selected sufficient threshold is 11/100, matching the retained example. Its inherited outward certificate B8 already owns the original source semantic, native-bare comparison, clock tail and phase debits under the original ideal preparation/implementation assumptions. A revised source assumption requires revising B8; its confidence does not improve by another citation. Reserve an additional total 1/1000, provisionally partitioned as follows. These are acceptance allocations, not certified errors and not new UD coefficients. Additional debit Allocation Must cover Digital approximation 1/5000 Any finite product-formula or corresponding encoded-channel approximation Realization/control 1/5000 Full implementation defect, background or finite mediator approximation Timer and correlations 1/5000 Autonomous timing mismatch and work/auxiliary correlation comparison New encoding/preparation 1/5000 Additional encoding, auxiliary readiness and preparation defects Semantic elapsed time 1/5000 Full target difference when actual elapsed and logical time differ Exact Fraction arithmetic verifies B8+1/1000<11/100. Every comparison must be defined in a telescoping chain so that the same defect is charged once. Timer timing can reside in the timer debit or a channel-realization debit, not both; the final semantic-time debit compares different target times. The original epsilon_F is already in B8. Moving budget between categories requires a versioned contract amendment and a new outward total, not convenient relabeling after a failed check. Acceptance requires the complete budget and each resource limit to hold over the declared interval, with finite reserves and correct failure/exhaustion semantics. A sufficient bound exceeding the threshold is a failed certificate; it is not automatically a lower bound on actual error. A direct full-state counterexample is stronger and must be recorded. Since the full numerical resource envelope and new debit proofs remain open, full-controller feasibility is not established here. 4. WBS 4.1–4.2: a supplied finite autonomous comparator Let C have addresses 0,1,2 and B be a binary work factor with degenerate bare energy. Supply initial C=|0>. The gate word is X followed chronologically by Z, so its completed product is ZX; these gates do not commute. Define prefixes P_0=I, P_1=X, P_2=ZX and W=∑j=02|j⟩⟨j|⊗Pj,HC=2κC(|1⟩⟨0|+|2⟩⟨1|+adjoints), W=\sum_{j=0}^{2}|j\rangle\langle j|\otimes P_j, \quad H_C=\sqrt2\kappa_C(|1\rangle\langle0|+|2\rangle\langle1|+\mathrm{adjoints}), HCB=W(HC⊗I)W†=2κC(|1⟩⟨0|⊗X+|2⟩⟨1|⊗Z+adjoints). H_{CB}=W(H_C\otimes I)W^{\dagger} =\sqrt2\kappa_C(|1\rangle\langle0|\otimes X +|2\rangle\langle1|\otimes Z+\mathrm{adjoints}). The scale kappa_C of this toy is distinct from kappa_0 of the full retained controller. This uses the previously retained spin-clock/prefix-dressing method as a small comparator; no new universal clock method or priority claim is made. All couplings are constant after launch. No external pulse schedule drives the ordering. Theorem M11.1 (finite autonomous noncommuting word). For every work input, including entanglement with a spectator, at TC=π/(2κC)T_C=\pi/(2\kappa_C), e−iTCHCB|0⟩|ψ⟩=−|2⟩ZX|ψ⟩. e^{-iT_C H_{CB}}|0\rangle|\psi\rangle =-|2\rangle ZX|\psi\rangle. At 2TC=π/κC2T_C=\pi/\kappa_C, the full unitary returns to identity. The full generator norm is 2κC2\kappa_C. The supplied initial clock has energy mean zero and variance 2κC22\kappa_C^2. Proof. Conjugation by the unitary W gives exact dressed propagation. H_C is the n=2 spin clock: its eigenvalues are −2κC,0,2κC-2\kappa_C,0,2\kappa_C, and its transfer at T_C maps |0> to -|2>. Since P_0=I and P_2=ZX, dressing gives the stated full-input map. All three eigenphases return to one at 2T_C. Norm and initial variance follow from the spectrum and the first edge amplitude 2κC\sqrt2\kappa_C. Tensoring a spectator preserves the identity. ▫\square This establishes ordered computation from a supplied finite state. It does not establish native timer formation or a permanent record. Reversible return undoes the completed word; no reservoir is silently renewed. 5. WBS 4.3: endpoint correctness does not give a retention plateau At t=T_C/2 and work input |0>, the dressed state has work probabilities 1/4 and 3/4. Its reduced-work purity is 5/8, demonstrating clock/work entanglement. Compare with the completed work state ZX|0> and the freely propagated clock reference. The work marginal trace distance is 1/4, whereas the full pure-state trace distance is sqrt(15)/4. Thus a favorable marginal does not certify the requested joint target. On the comparator interval [π/(3κC),2π/(3κC)][\pi/(3\kappa_C),2\pi/(3\kappa_C)], the unfinished-prefix tail is R=1-(3/4)^2=7/16 at the endpoints. The retained full-target tail bound is 2R(1−R)=37/82\sqrt{R(1-R)}=3\sqrt7/8. For this work input, the actual joint error at the left endpoint is D=24716>11100. D=\frac{\sqrt{247}}{16}>\frac{11}{100}. Indeed the target/actual overlap is 3/16 there, giving D squared=247/256. This is an actual counterexample to that toy meeting the selected uniform window threshold, not merely a conservative-bound failure. Identity padding and a larger clock may improve a window but change dimension, energy and support costs; that work remains open. 6. WBS 5.1: direct binary encoding has an exact locality gap Encode clock addresses 0,1,2 as binary labels 00,01,11, with 10 padding. Let J embed C tensor B into the resulting three-qubit space and use zero extension on this clock/work support. In qubit order C_0,C_1,B, K=JHCBJ†=κC2(IXX+ZXX+XIZ−XZZ). K=JH_{CB}J^{\dagger} =\frac{\kappa_C}{\sqrt2}(IXX+ZXX+XIZ-XZZ). The first edge changes the low clock bit and B conditional on the high bit being zero. The second changes the high clock bit, applies Z to B, and requires the low bit to be one. These conditions create the weight-three strings ZXX and XZZ. Gray labeling reduces changed bits; it does not remove conditional support. Theorem M11.2 (best direct two-qubit generator defect). On this fixed full eight-dimensional encoded space, infK2sumofonsite/pairterms∥K−K2∥=κC. \inf_{K_2\ \mathrm{sum\ of\ onsite/pair\ terms}} \|K-K_2\|=\kappa_C. Proof. Every such Hermitian K_2 has only Pauli strings of weight at most two. Orthogonality of the Pauli basis leaves weight-three coefficients +κC/2+\kappa_C/\sqrt2 on ZXX and −κC/2-\kappa_C/\sqrt2 on XZZ in K-K_2. Its normalized squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm is therefore at least κC2\kappa_C^2; operator norm is at least this root. The two weight-three strings anticommute and each squares to identity. Choosing K2=(κC/2)(IXX+XIZ)K_2=(\kappa_C/\sqrt2)(IXX+XIZ) leaves a residual whose square is κC2I\kappa_C^2 I. Its operator norm is exactly kappa_C, attaining the lower bound. ▫\square This concerns direct equality or uniform generator comparison for this explicit full-space Gray encoding and extension. It is not an impossibility theorem for other encodings, auxiliary factors, approximate effective designs or final unitaries. An onsite Y rotation alone can implement the work product ZX at one endpoint, while reproducing neither this clock trajectory nor its full joint dynamics. The replay includes that negative control. The direct norm-defect Duhamel debit at the comparator interval’s upper time is at least 2π/32\pi/3, so the same-generator sufficient bound is vacuous after capping trace distance at one. This does not prove every finite-time two-qubit approximation is inaccurate. It shows that the selected direct-small-generator-defect route cannot meet the contract. 7. title: M10 — Pulse strength, elapsed time and balanced error certificate
note: Development addendum 0.1 · 5 October 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Explicit centered pulse schedule and finite strength/time budget; timing, gain, background and switching-work contracts. More product-formula steps can worsen the combined certificate. External timer remains supplied. Independent review pending; physical promotion 0. UD M10: pulse strength and elapsed time5 October 2026 · Development addendum 0.1 · Independent review pending · Physical promotion 0Fresh checks: 64 exact and 65 numerical. Externally scheduled circuits; autonomous pair-only apparatus remains open.Development — no registry entry. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. This is a resource contract for an externally scheduled, supplied pair-interaction construction. There is no autonomous timer, native pulse preparation, geometric routing, complete large-controller execution, or physical measurement. M8’s fixed-factor static-generator obstruction and all earlier source assumptions remain intact. Ledger v0.39 is unmodified: 235 typed objects, Q06=0. Constants below are engineering examples, not new UD coefficients. 1. Declare the allowed controls Retain M9’s binary edge He=βXQ⊗SWAPBCH_e=\beta X_Q\otimes\mathrm{SWAP}_{BC} and its four commuting rotations with θ=βt/2\theta=\beta t/2. Work on three supplied binary factors, optionally entangled with any spectator. The external classical schedule applies exactly one pulse at a time. Every intended control generator has operator norm at most h>0 and is supported on at most two binary factors. The background is either disabled, or separately admitted with full norm at most b. A non-pair-supported native background would prevent labeling the entire physical generator pair-only even if its controls are pair-supported. The literal M9 circuit has 16 Hadamards, 12 CNOTs, two S gates, two S-dagger gates and four RZ rotations. We choose centered generators rather than importing the uncentered exact-gate logarithms used as an existence example in M9. The circuit itself is unchanged. Gate Pulse exponent Norm action H e−iπH/2=−iHe^{-i\pi H/2}=-iH π/2\pi/2 CNOT e−iπCNOT/2=−iCNOTe^{-i\pi\mathrm{CNOT}/2}=-i\mathrm{CNOT} π/2\pi/2 S e−iπZ/4=e−iπ/4Se^{-i\pi Z/4}=e^{-i\pi/4}S π/4\pi/4 S-dagger e+iπZ/4=e+iπ/4S†e^{+i\pi Z/4}=e^{+i\pi/4}S^{\dagger} π/4\pi/4 RZ(2 theta) e−iθZe^{-i\theta Z} |θ||\theta| Each displayed axis is a Hermitian involution. A pulse of action a uses generator h times its signed axis and duration a/h. Hadamards/CNOTs contribute (−i)28=1(-i)^{28}=1 to the complete circuit, and the S/S-dagger phases cancel. Thus this particular whole circuit is an exact operator identity, including its global phase. No extra correction pulse is required. When theta=0, its zero-action RZ slots may be omitted; all other literal basis/parity pulses are still counted. The identity circuit could of course be simplified, but that is outside this fixed schedule. 2. Pulse action fixes the sequential time budget Theorem M10.1 (declared binary schedule). The ideal pulse action and shortest elapsed time within this prescribed sequential, fixed-axis, unwrapped-angle schedule are A(θ)=15π+4|θ|,τmin=A(θ)h. A(\theta)=15\pi+4|\theta|, \qquad \tau_{\min}=\frac{A(\theta)}h. All active pulses at strength h attain this duration. This is not a globally optimal circuit or a universal speed-limit theorem. Proof. There are 28 H/CNOT pulses of action pi/2, four S/S-dagger pulses of action pi/4, and four rotations of action |theta|. Their sum is the displayed A. In the declared pulse family, realizing action a with norm at most h requires duration at least a/h; sequential intervals add. Choosing maximal allowed strength attains every interval minimum. No angle wrapping, gate merging, parallelization, or changed axes is included. ▫\square For beta nonzero and positive target time t, matching the simulated time with the physical nominal elapsed time requires ht≥15π+2|β|t. ht\ge15\pi+2|\beta|t. If this inequality holds, stretching all pulse durations proportionally and reducing their strengths realizes tau=t without changing the ideal unitary. At transfer time t=π/(2|β|)t=\pi/(2|\beta|), theta has magnitude pi/4, so A=16*pi and the condition is h≥32|β|h\ge32|\beta|. If h is smaller, the literal circuit still works ideally but takes longer than that target time. It cannot silently inherit M9’s semantic target at elapsed t. This exposes a real supplied-control cost hidden by a gate-only description. The unsynthesized three-factor edge has norm |beta|; the prescribed circuit needs a much larger control cap to keep its transfer duration. The comparison is scoped to this circuit and does not rule out a better pairwise synthesis. 3. Timing, gain and background debits Suppose pulse l has intended action a_l and nominal duration a_l/h. Its actual amplitude gain is gamma_l and relative duration gain is zeta_l, with |γl|≤g,|ζl|≤z<1. |\gamma_l|\le g,\quad |\zeta_l|\le z<1. These are supplied deterministic full-domain bounds, not measured calibration. For the same pulse axis, the action defect is |al[(1+γl)(1+ζl)−1]|≤al(g+z+gz). |a_l[(1+\gamma_l)(1+\zeta_l)-1]| \le a_l(g+z+gz). The norm difference between two exponentials of that axis is at most this angle difference. Telescoping the complete pulse sequence gives A(g+z+gz). Adding an actual background with norm at most b over the entire actual elapsed interval gives, by Duhamel, at most btau_actual. Since tau_actual<= (1+z)*A/h, $$ \epsilon_{\rm control}\le \min\{2,A[g+z+gz+(b/h)(1+z)]\} $$ in operator norm; complete trace distance is at most the uncapped expression, capped at one. No initial supply debit is included here; it must be separately owned if present. The clock/work bank and arbitrary spectators are included. The external timer and control reservoir have no quantum state in this model; certifying their correlations remains open. If comparing to the same logical target at t, this is the entire pulse-control debit. If comparing instead to a semantic target at actual elapsed tau, add that target’s full time-change debit. For the binary edge itself it is at most |β||τ−t||\beta||\tau-t|. For a larger semantic bank use its full declared generator, not an output marginal. These terms compare different targets and are not redundant charges. An independently certified gate error can replace the gain/timing account; do not add both for the same defect. Conditional example. Choose beta>0, h=32beta, t=pi/(2beta), b=beta/65536 and g=z=1/16777216. These values merely illustrate a specified design contract. All 36 nonzero pulses have ideal duration at maximal strength, and nominal tau equals t. Using the outward enclosure pi<22/7, exact Fraction arithmetic gives $$ \epsilon_{\rm control} <\frac{1845493859}{61572651155456}, \quad \epsilon_{\rm actual\ elapsed\ target} <\frac{264465861}{8796093022208} <\frac1{32768}. $$ The second inequality includes the binary target-time debit πz/2\pi z/2. The executed small-matrix cases corroborate the bound, but none of h, b, g or z has been measured. This single-edge bound cannot be reused as a complete M8-controller control budget. 4. Switching work remains a separate observable For a closed model with a constant bare background and externally switched pulse controls absent initially/finally, retain M9’s signed mean work formula $$ W_{\rm switch}=\sum_l (\langle G_l\rangle_{{\rm in},l}-\langle G_l\rangle_{{\rm out},l}), \quad |W_{\rm switch}|\le2\sum_l\|G_l\|. $$ In the 36-pulse maximal-strength example, this coarse bound is 72h; with gain uncertainty it is 72h*(1+g). A closed finite system additionally gives signed switching work equal to its bare-energy gain because each interval conserves its total fixed Hamiltonian expectation. The replay checks this equality on a specified random pure input with onsite background b(ZB+ZC)/2b(Z_B+Z_C)/2. This bound concerns signed mean work only. It is not total apparatus energy throughput, switching losses, fluctuations, fabrication, or timer preparation cost. Zero signed mean work in the disabled-background idealization does not discharge those obligations. Norm action is a duration/strength measure; it is not itself thermodynamic work. 5. More digital steps also mean more pulses Now apply the same declared pulse convention to M9’s supplied finite encoded Hamiltonian Pauli expansion. For a weight-w nonidentity string with x X symbols and y Y symbols, its parity compiler has fixed basis/parity action b(P)=π(x+32y+w−1)≤π(52w−1). b(P)=\pi(x+\tfrac32y+w-1) \le\pi(\tfrac52w-1). Proof. There are 2(x+y) Hadamards and 2(w-1) CNOTs, each of action pi/2. There are 2y S/S-dagger basis gates, each of action pi/4. Summing gives the formula and maximizing over x+y<=w gives the bound. Global phases of a general string compiler are tracked or removed for density-operator comparisons; unlike the special binary-edge count, they need not multiply to one. ▫\square Let B=sum_l b(P_l), Lambda=sum_l abs(lambda_l), and C be M9’s anticommute coefficient. Use the literal r-step first-order product formula at positive target parameter t. Its pulse action and minimal nominal sequential duration are Ar=rB+tΛ,τr=Ar/h. A_r=rB+t\Lambda,\qquad \tau_r=A_r/h. The repeated basis/parity overhead grows with r, while the summed rotation action t*Lambda is unchanged. Under the same uniform gain/timing/background inputs, put e=g+z+gz+(b/h)(1+z). e=g+z+gz+(b/h)(1+z). The combined sufficient logical-channel certificate is Er≤t2Cr+e(rB+tΛ), E_r\le\frac{t^2 C}{r}+e(rB+t\Lambda), capped at one for complete trace distance, with any preparation, encoding and semantic-time debits added separately. This is a conservative upper certificate, not a lower bound on observed error. For B>0 and e>0, the real-valued minimum of its r-dependent terms occurs at r*=tCeB. r_*=t\sqrt{\frac{C}{eB}}. An allowed positive integer minimizer lies among the neighboring integers, or an endpoint when restricted by time. For a nominal wall-time cap tau_max, feasibility requires rB+tΛ≤hτmax. rB+t\Lambda\le h\tau_{\max}. If the cap must hold despite duration uncertainty, instead require (1+z)(rB+tΛ)≤hτmax(1+z)(rB+t\Lambda)\le h\tau_{\max}. To keep nominal elapsed time equal to t, the same inequality uses tau_max=t, with proportionally stretched pulses if slack is positive. Merely increasing r can eventually worsen this certificate or violate the elapsed-time cap. That is a constraint on this unoptimized synthesis, not a no-go for error cancellation, better compilation, or other architectures. For the retained numerical toy H=(3/5)XII+(2/7)ZZI+(1/3)IXXH=(3/5)XII+(2/7)ZZI+(1/3)IXX, t=1, C=4/15, Lambda=128/105, B=5*pi. Taking e=1/10000 and replacing pi by 22/7 yields an outward rational upper certificate whose optimal positive integer is r=13: exact differences show improvement from 12 to 13 and worsening from 13 to 14. The receipt compares r=1,4,13,14,32,128,267. This is resource/error arithmetic, not a noisy full-controller execution. The complete 380-qubit M8 expansion still lacks evaluated B, Lambda, C and an admitted pulse schedule. 6. Scope, provenance and the next gate The constructor replay independently enumerates the centered pulse types and action sums, certifies the fractional illustration and integer tradeoff, and tests full eight-dimensional matrices at positive, negative and zero angles. Entangled spectator comparisons and signed switching-work checks are numerical. Literal-angle support/action bounds and general tradeoff statements depend on the written proofs. The attached governance and coefficient ledger are preserved byte for byte. Repeated self-checking does not supply non-constructor review. This step closes the ideal prescribed-circuit strength/time accounting, with an explicit conditional control-defect bound. It does not close autonomy or native supply. Next, an autonomous timer must be introduced as an actual finite quantum factor and compared against the external schedule with all timer correlations, return behavior and resource costs retained. Alternatively, a more efficient compiled schedule must be specified before improving these budgets. Missing Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was not read or used.

It does not construct an autonomous pair-only replacement for M8, native preparation, geometric locality, a permanent END record, or a physical apparatus. What changes, and what does not M8 forbids direct equality between its clock-conditioned swap generator and a sum of two-register terms on the same fixed factors. That statement is retained. No clock, timer, work source, or control apparatus is supplied natively by this circuit identity. There are two distinct results. First, one binary clock/swap edge has an exact circuit, requiring 12 CNOTs and 24 literal one-qubit gates, without ancillary qubits. Second, any specified finite encoded Hamiltonian admits a conditional product-formula circuit with a full-operator-norm error contract. Only small instances are executed here. The 380-qubit retained controller is neither expanded nor simulated. The scheduler is external and classical in this model: full-joint channel bounds cover the encoded work/clock bank and arbitrary spectators, not an unmodeled quantum timer or control reservoir. Such apparatus would need its own state and correlation certificate. These are elementary Pauli/parity and product-formula constructions, derived below; no novelty or priority claim is made. Another constructor replay does not constitute non-constructor review. 2. An exact binary edge Let Q, B, C each be a two-dimensional factor, and let beta be real. Define He=βXQ⊗SWAPBC. H_e=\beta X_Q\otimes\operatorname{SWAP}_{BC}. This is the isolated two-address version of one Hermitian clock edge. It is not the whole 257-address M8 clock. The full-domain identity SWAP=II+XX+YY+ZZ2 \operatorname{SWAP}=\frac{II+XX+YY+ZZ}{2} gives He=β2(XII+XXX+XYY+XZZ). H_e=\frac{\beta}{2}(XII+XXX+XYY+XZZ). The four Pauli strings commute: their work parts are II and the three matched Pauli pairs; distinct matched pairs acquire two minus signs upon exchange. Consequently, with theta=beta*t/2, e−itHe=e−iθXIIe−iθXXXe−iθXYYe−iθXZZ. e^{-itH_e}=e^{-i\theta XII}e^{-i\theta XXX} e^{-i\theta XYY}e^{-i\theta XZZ}. This is exact for every real t and beta, not a Trotter approximation. Theorem M9.1 (exact binary-edge pair circuit). Each factor on the right has a finite circuit of one-qubit gates and CNOTs on pairs. Their chronological composition implements the left side on every input, including inputs entangled with arbitrary spectators. The literal compiler below uses 12 CNOTs and 24 one-qubit gates in total, with no additional qubit. Proof. For a nonidentity Pauli string P, choose local basis changes B_P taking each active Pauli to Z by conjugation. Use H for X; use HS†HS^{\dagger} for Y, chronologically S-dagger then H; use identity for Z. Thus B_P P B_P-dagger is the product of active Z operators. Choose the last active qubit as root. Let C_P be the product of CNOTs from all other active qubits into the root. Then $$ C_P^{\dagger}Z_{\rm root}C_P=\prod_{q\in\operatorname{supp}P}Z_q, \quad e^{-i\theta P}=B_P^{\dagger}C_P^{\dagger} RZ_{\rm root}(2\theta)C_P B_P. $$ Here RZ(phi)=exp(-iphiZ/2). The chronological circuit applies B_P, C_P, RZ, reverse CNOTs, then reversed adjoint basis gates. It implements an operator identity, hence its tensor extension with identity on any spectator is also exact. Counts follow directly. ▫\square Rotation CNOTs Literal one-qubit gates XII 0 3 XXX 4 7 XYY 4 11 XZZ 4 3 Total 12 24 Identity angles still use the literal schedule in this accounting. These counts are not optimized, minimality claims, or physical elementary-pulse counts for an unspecified hardware gate set. A supplied CNOT itself can be generated by a two-qubit Hermitian pulse: over duration τ>0\tau>0 use G=π(I−CNOT)/(2τ)G=\pi(I-\mathrm{CNOT})/(2\tau), for which exp(−iτG)=CNOT\exp(-i\tau G)=\mathrm{CNOT}. One-qubit unitaries likewise have Hermitian logarithms. Thus the ideal circuit has a finite time-dependent pair-supported generator. Pulse durations, strengths and switching are external inputs. Making the elapsed duration shorter requires stronger controls; no bound on available strength or work is inferred. 3. Energy and schedule are not free For matched bare energies h_B=h_C, the complete SWAP commutes with h_B+h_C. This does not make its compiled pulses individually energy preserving. For the binary witness h_B+h_C=Z_B+Z_C, H_e commutes with the bare energy, while XXX does not. Basis changes and CNOTs may also exchange energy with the control apparatus. Native energy-preserving admission cannot be inherited pulse by pulse from the completed unitary. Specify a physical schedule of s pulse intervals with durations tau_l>0 and elapsed time tau=sum(tau_l). In the ideal model, interval l implements a supplied constant G_l. The target channel parameter t and the wall-clock elapsed time tau are separately owned. An assumption that the background is disabled is part of this model. If it cannot be disabled, or calibration/timing differs, compare the actual interval generator to the intended one as a full joint defect nu(u). Unitary Duhamel gives $$ \|U_{\rm actual}-U_{\rm scheduled}\| \le\int_0^{\tau}\|\nu(u)\|\,du. $$ Alternatively, if full gate deviations e_l are certified, telescoping gives a total norm error at most sum(e_l). Do not charge the same discrepancy through both accounts. Neither marginal output accuracy nor postselection can replace this full-domain bound. If the native background is not itself pair-supported, adding it also prevents calling the complete physical generator pair-only; a pairwise control circuit is not evidence to the contrary. For a closed switched model H_bare+G_l, with the controls absent initially and finally and instantaneous switches, the signed mean switching work is $$ W_{\rm switch}=\sum_l\bigl( \langle G_l\rangle_{{\rm in},l}-\langle G_l\rangle_{{\rm out},l}\bigr), \qquad |W_{\rm switch}|\le2\sum_l\|G_l\|. $$ This follows by summing expectations of Hamiltonian jumps at the boundaries; the terms telescope into the displayed interval differences. It is a conservative finite-input bound on signed mean work, not a bound on apparatus dissipation, energy fluctuations, or the cost of building the timer. In the background-free ideal pulse model each constant G_l conserves its own expectation within the interval; that special cancellation is not a physical zero-cost conclusion. Specifying physical durations fixes the pulse norms; arbitrary compression does not preserve the displayed resource bound. 4. A finite encoded-controller contract Let a target Hamiltonian H be explicitly supplied on the finite M8 factors. To use its locality information, supply a decomposition H=sum_A h_A with each h_A on its declared support. Encode a factor of dimension d into b=ceil(log2(d)) binary qubits by an explicit isometry J_d. Fix the code basis, which unused states are padding, the initial encoded bank, and the implementation of decoding. Extension policy matters. Extend each local h_A to its support’s encoded space by zero on that support’s padding, and tensor identity on all other encoded qubits. Sum these extensions to obtain K. The entire valid code subspace is invariant, and KJ=JHKJ=JH for the tensor encoding J. This proves exact encoded dynamics on valid inputs. K need not vanish on states with padding in an untouched factor. A global zero extension JHJ†JHJ^{\dagger} would instead multiply untouched factors by code projectors and can destroy the local support bound. M9 uses the support-wise policy, not both policies at once. Expand the resulting Hermitian K in the binary Pauli basis: K=λ0I+∑l=1LλlPl,λl=2−NTr(PlK)∈ℝ. K=\lambda_0 I+\sum_{l=1}^{L}\lambda_l P_l, \quad \lambda_l=2^{-N}\operatorname{Tr}(P_l K)\in\mathbb R. Aggregate duplicate strings before estimating cost. Identity contributes a global phase, which must be retained for literal operator comparisons but has no effect on density operators. Define Λ=∑l|λl|,C=∑i<j:PiPj=−PjPi|λiλj|. \Lambda=\sum_l|\lambda_l|, \quad C=\sum_{i<j:\,P_iP_j=-P_jP_i}|\lambda_i\lambda_j|. For positive integer r, apply r identical first-order steps, each containing every exp(-itlambda_l*P_l/r) in one fixed chronological order. Call the phase-adjusted resulting unitary S_r(t). Theorem M9.2 (full encoded product-formula error). ∥Sr(t)−e−itK∥≤t2Cr≤t2Λ22r. \|S_r(t)-e^{-itK}\|\le\frac{t^2 C}{r} \le\frac{t^2\Lambda^2}{2r}. Every nonidentity weight-w rotation has the exact pair circuit in M9.1, using 2(w-1) CNOTs and at most 4w+1 one-qubit gates. The bound applies on the whole encoded Hilbert space and arbitrary spectator extensions, not just the valid code or one selected input. Proof. For Hermitian A,B, the two-term unitary splitting defect over an interval h has norm at most h2∥[A,B]∥/2h^2\|[A,B]\|/2. To see this, differentiate the interpolating exact/split propagator; its integrand contains e−isABeisA−Be^{-isA}Be^{isA}-B, whose norm is at most |s|∥[A,B]∥|s|\|[A,B]\| by a second Duhamel integral. Integrating from 0 to |h| gives h2/2h^2/2. Iterating this argument over the ordered terms bounds one step by h2/2h^2/2 times the sum of pair commutator norms. For Pauli strings, this norm is zero for commuting pairs and 2|λiλj|2|\lambda_i\lambda_j| for anticommuting pairs. Telescoping r unitary steps with h=t/r gives t2C/rt^2 C/r. Finally C is bounded by the sum of all pair coefficient products, at most Λ2/2\Lambda^2/2. The parity compiler already proved the per-term circuit; its basis changes require at most 4w local gates and one RZ. Spectator tensoring preserves operator norm. ▫\square For digital allocation epsilon>0, r=max(1,ceil(t^2*C/epsilon)) suffices. If C=0, the whole Pauli product is exact in one step. No efficient expansion, optimal circuit, bounded-strength realization, or practical runtime is promised. Complete trace distance, with convention D=rho-sigma trace norm /2, is at most the unitary norm defect for a common input, by purification and contractivity. If the initial encoding/supply is imperfect, add its own full-joint debit. Intermediate primitive gates can leave the valid code. The exact target preserves it, so final padding leakage probability on any valid pure input is at most the square of the full norm error. This is a final bound, not a claim of invariant code during pulses. Discarding leaked states or renormalizing successful decodes changes the channel and is not licensed by this certificate. 5. Retained example: costs and conditional budget For the ideal M8 example, register dimensions imply the following explicit encoding sizes. These are engineering representation choices, not native UD physical qubit identifications. Supplied carrier family Binary encoding count 15 source cells, dimension 59049 each 15*16=240 3 reference ladders, dimension 1102072 each 3*21=63 60 fuel qubits 60 3 module flags 3 4 attempt records and END 5 Clock, dimension 257 9 Total 380 Under the retained declared support decomposition, the largest encoded edge support is a 9-qubit clock and two 21-qubit references: 51 qubits. A deliberately loose finite Pauli-term upper bound for the ideal native-bare-plus-dressed-clock operator is L≤Lmax=256451+15416+3421+60. L\le L_{\max}=256\,4^{51}+15\,4^{16}+3\,4^{21}+60. This counts all possible strings per supported term, overcounts identities/duplicates, and uses no sparsity. It is not the actual expansion size. It excludes unspecified nonlocal implementation defects. Parseval and Cauchy-Schwarz imply Lambda<=sqrt(L)norm(K); support-wise extension further bounds norm(K) by M=sum_A norm(h_A). Hence a finite but extremely loose sufficient step count uses C<=L_maxM^2/2, once M and the target time are supplied. Neither M nor a practical r for the massive controller is evaluated in this release. Let B8 be the exact outward sufficient M8 semantic-window bound retained in the provenance receipt. Conditional on its original ideal supply, source intervals and implementation assumptions, an encoded circuit compared at the same target parameter t satisfies $$ \epsilon_{\rm joint}\le\min\{1, B8+\epsilon_{\rm digital}+\epsilon_{\rm controls} +\epsilon_{\rm encode/supply}+\epsilon_{\rm target\ time}\}. $$ The original epsilon_F is already included in B8; do not add it a second time unless a genuinely new preparation defect is introduced. The clock, all donors, reference correlations, records, unused final module, output bank and padding remain in the domain. This is a channel transfer statement, not a new source-preparation result. Exact Fraction arithmetic verifies B8+1/1000<11/100. This is a conditional allocation, taking new control/encoding/target-time debits as zero, not measured performance. The product-formula theorem shows how to request that digital allocation, but no 380-qubit expansion or circuit was executed. If elapsed pulse time tau differs from t, reproducing the logical channel at t does not automatically reproduce the semantic target at tau. Either choose and resource a schedule with tau=t, or include the full-joint distance between the two semantic targets as epsilon_target_time. If a declared full semantic generator H_sem governs that difference, a sufficient bound is $|\tau-t|\inf_c\|H_{\rm sem}-cI\|$. An output-only phase correction is not adequate for freely evolving donors, references and clock. A separately scheduled circuit for each t in a retention interval is a family of target channels, not one autonomous retention plateau. 6. Replay boundaries, rejected shortcuts and next gate The fresh replay checks Gaussian-integer SWAP/Pauli identities and commutation, literal gate counts, the primitive-energy counterexample, and rational encoding/budget arithmetic. Numerical checks compare all eight-dimensional edge matrices at six angles, including negative time, and an entangled spectator. Further small numerical examples test noncommuting product-formula convergence and a padded qutrit. Exact and floating-point checks are reported separately. These toys corroborate the general proofs but do not replace them or test the large source cutoff algorithm. Rejected shortcuts: calling a two-address toy the whole clock; importing native energy conservation into each pulse; hiding the timer; claiming a same static generator; silently changing padding policies; simulating t while claiming elapsed tau; replacing complete error by an output marginal; promoting repeated constructor work to independent review; or claiming the huge finite bound is efficient. The achieved result is an explicit externally scheduled pair circuit and a complete encoded-channel error contract. The remaining decisive gate is to specify a bounded-strength apparatus, its pulse background, elapsed time, schedule source and switching resources, then either certify their full-joint debits or construct an autonomous clock with its own finite state/resource proof. Spatial routing and native supply remain separate open gates. Missing attachment Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was not read and provides no evidence here.

title: M8 — Register-local compiler and direct pair-generator obstruction
note: Development addendum 0.1 · 4 October 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Exact endpoint compiler, three-register clock edges and scoped pair-only generator no-go. New 109-edge word/256-edge clock certificate; geometric locality open. Independent review pending; physical promotion 0. M8 development addendum 0.1. Fixed tensor-register compilation and direct-generator obstruction. Geometric locality remains open. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0.Register-local compilation and pair-interaction obstruction144 exact checks and 8 numerical checks passed. The completed source word is preserved; the compiled clock has at most three-register edge support. A same-factor pair-only generator cannot equal that full clock/SWAP operator. This does not forbid a different pair-interaction design.Readable report · Complete source, replay and hash release · M7 source-bank certificate · M6 controllerDevelopment — no registry entry. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. This is a finite tensor-register result. It establishes neither geometric locality, a two-qubit interaction realization, native coherent supply, permanent exhaustion nor physical apparatus. Manuscript editions and M6/M7 releases are preserved. There is no new coefficient or confidence-rung promotion. 1. Define the locality constraint before claiming closure Keep the M7 tensor factors separately named: each source cell, reference ladder, individual fuel qubit, module flag, output cell, donor counterpart, record and the global address clock Q. A two-register gate is a unitary supported on at most two of these factors. A two-register Hamiltonian is a sum of Hermitian terms each supported on at most two such factors, with identity on all others. Onsite terms are allowed. The clock Q counts as one factor even though it has many addresses. This factorization is fixed. Grouping a whole module into one factor would change the question. No auxiliary register, encoded subspace, discarded degree of freedom, effective low-energy projection or changed clock is allowed in the direct-generator comparison below. Neither definition supplies a metric, bounded spatial range, bounded vertex degree, two-qubit gates or scalable fabrication. A source cell and the reference ladder remain large carriers. The question has two parts: can the completed M7 word be compiled into gates of bounded register support, and can its resulting same full generator be a sum of pair-interaction terms on these factors? 2. Exact compiler for the complete word Production already consists of q fuel/reference gates, each on F_j and R, followed by m finite lifts, each on S_l and R. Their full finite complements and energy-block definitions remain the retained M7 inputs. Replace each aggregate capture by m separate SWAP(S_l,O_il), followed by X on L_flag, X on M_i, and X on E_i. Replace each full-module SWAP(A,D_i) by separate matching SWAPs on the m source cells, R, each of the q fuel qubits, and L_flag. Append X_Z once after the last renewal. Each pair in a given capture or renewal partition is disjoint, so these factors commute within that aggregate. Their product is exactly the original aggregate unitary on every state, including arbitrary spectators and correlated failures. Part of one attempt M7 aggregate edges Compiled edges Gate register support Binary producer and ladder lifts q+m q+m 2 Output capture and records 1 m+3 2 for swaps, 1 for flips Full-module donor renewal 1 m+q+2 2 Theorem M8.1 (full-domain endpoint equivalence). For a attempts, the compiled word has k′=a(2q+3m+5)+1, k'=a(2q+3m+5)+1, and exactly the same completed product P as M7’s k=a(q+m+2)+1 word. Every compiled gate commutes with the additive comparison bare generator. Its full-bank semantic target and M7 overlap eta_a are unchanged. Proof. SWAP of identified tensor products equals the tensor product of the SWAPs of their respective factors. Disjoint output SWAPs multiply to the m-cell output SWAP; the three disjoint X factors multiply to the original flag/record factor. Thus replacing each aggregate preserves the product on the full tensor space. Each matched factor swap commutes with the sum of its two equal bare energy operators; record flips have zero bare energy. The retained producer/lift commutation is unchanged. Adding the displayed counts and the final X_Z gives k’. Equal products on a common input and common free endpoint have identical semantic overlap. ▫\square Intermediate prefixes differ. A partly executed capture or renewal has no right to the completed-record or fresh-module claim. All incomplete prefixes are retained in the new clock-tail debit. The compiler does not condition on a successful production or erase failures. 3. The compiled constant generator is three-register supported For n’>=k’, append n’-k’ identities and supply the M6 spin clock with scale kappa. An edge from j to j+1 contributes βj(|j+1⟩⟨j|Q⊗Gj+1+|j⟩⟨j+1|Q⊗Gj+1†),βj=κ(j+1)(n′−j). \beta_j\left(|j+1\rangle\langle j|_Q\otimes G_{j+1} +|j\rangle\langle j+1|_Q\otimes G_{j+1}^{\dagger}\right), \quad \beta_j=\kappa\sqrt{(j+1)(n'-j)}. If G acts on two work registers, this Hermitian edge term acts on at most three declared registers, including Q. Flips give two-register terms and padding gives a clock-only term. The additive comparison bare operator is onsite. Thus the compiled H_0 has an exact decomposition into terms of register support at most three; its clock norm is kappa*n’. This is an abstract constant-Hamiltonian construction after supplied launch. The completion time remains T=pi/(2kappa). Increasing the gate count at fixed kappa does not lengthen this engineered clock’s T; it raises its dimension/couplings and changes its prefix distribution. At fixed permitted clock norm h, one instead needs kappa<=h/n’, hence T>=pin’/(2*h). The speed improvement is not free. 4. Direct two-register generator obstruction Lemma M8.2 (three changed factors). If product-basis vectors |x> and |y> differ orthogonally in three distinct named factors, then any two-register Hamiltonian K has <y|K|x>=0. Proof. Each term acts on at most two factors, so at least one changed orthogonal factor is outside its support and contributes a zero inner product. Every term vanishes separately; their sum also vanishes. ▫\square Theorem M8.3 (direct equality and norm obstruction). Suppose an edge j carries a full SWAP on two matched factors B,C of dimension at least two. Choose distinct labels u,v on them, and keep all other work factors fixed. Between |x⟩=|j⟩Q|u⟩B|v⟩C|z⟩,|y⟩=|j+1⟩Q|v⟩B|u⟩C|z⟩, |x\rangle=|j\rangle_Q|u\rangle_B|v\rangle_C|z\rangle, \quad |y\rangle=|j+1\rangle_Q|v\rangle_B|u\rangle_C|z\rangle, the compiled H_0 has matrix element beta_j. Therefore no two-register K on the same full factors equals H_0, and ∥H0−K∥≥βj. \|H_0-K\|\ge\beta_j. The same witness applies to the matched fuel/reference transfer, when both populated labels change. It also applies to a swapped pair of degenerate binary module flags. Proof. The stated vectors differ in Q,B,C, so Lemma M8.2 gives zero for K. The forward clock edge gives beta_j because SWAP maps its work input exactly to the chosen output. The reverse edge and all other edges have different clock matrix elements, and the onsite bare operator cannot change Q. Thus <y|(H_0-K)|x>=beta_j. Operator norm bounds every unit-vector matrix element from above, giving the lower bound. ▫\square This is an obstruction to direct full-generator equality or small uniform generator defect in the specified factorization. It is not a ban on producing the same final unitary using time-dependent pair interactions, a different static design, extra ancillary factors, approximate encoded dynamics or new geometry. Even a sum of three onsite Pauli X operators has zero generator matrix element from |000> to |111>, yet its finite-time unitary at pi/2 maps one to the other up to phase. The replay includes this counterexample to an overbroad dynamical no-go. For the example below, the final flag-renewal swap is edge j=107 with n’=256, so β107=κ108⋅149=κ16092. \beta_{107}=\kappa\sqrt{108\cdot149}=\kappa\sqrt{16092}. No direct two-register replacement can make that same-generator defect smaller than this. Feeding this lower bound into the M7 full-domain Duhamel sufficient certificate makes its uniform term at least 2pisqrt(16092)/3, greater than one. Consequently that particular small-defect certificate cannot validate a direct pair-only replacement. This does not prove its observed state error is large; the sufficient norm certificate can be conservative. Lowering kappa alone does not rescue this term because the window time scales inversely with kappa. 5. Recompute the clock and retain the complete-bank certificate Take the retained M7 a=2, q=20, m=3. The coarse k=51 becomes k’=109 (prime). Choose n’=256=2^8, clock dimension 257 (prime) and 147=3*7^2 identity-padding edges. With kappa=4096=2^12, clock norm is 2^20, twice the old 2^19; completion and return times remain pi/2^13 and pi/2^12. The retention interval remains [pi/12288,pi/6144]. Source, output, donor, fuel and reference counts are unchanged. The new tail is R256,109=4−256∑j=0108(256j)3j,f(R)=1−[max{0,1−2R}]2. R_{256,109}=4^{-256}\sum_{j=0}^{108}\binom{256}{j}3^j, \quad f(R)=\sqrt{1-[\max\{0,1-2R\}]^2}. Exact rational arithmetic certifies R<2^-93. Retaining n=128 with the longer word would instead give R_{128,109}>9/10, making the uniform complete-target tail debit one. Merely changing k without recomputing the clock would therefore lose the old retention certificate. Corollary M8.4 (compiled semantic window). With the M7 supplied independent ready bank and the same admitted source certificates, the full-joint uniform sufficient debit is min{1,ϵF+ηa+2πδB3κ+f(Rn′,k′)+πdO6κ}, \min\left\{1,\epsilon_F+\eta_a+ \frac{2\pi\delta_B}{3\kappa}+f(R_{n',k'})+ \frac{\pi d_O}{6\kappa}\right\}, where delta_B owns every module/output source operator and the actual implementation defect, and d_O owns the complete output bank. The example retains delta_B=3/4 and d_O=3/10 when no extra implementation error is admitted. Using inherited M7 outward source inputs, the new rational certificate remains below 11/100 for epsilon_F=0 and zero added implementation defect. Proof. Apply M6’s prefix-tail theorem to the compiled word. M8.1 preserves its completed product, comparison-energy commutation and M7 full-bank target overlap. Thus M7’s actual-to-comparator and native-output target-phase comparisons remain applicable, with the new prefix count and tail. ▫\square No old pulse duration, switched work debit or static-capture norm is imported. Sequential factor compilation changes coherent intermediate states; the new whole-word clock comparison owns those states. The supplied three-register edge synthesis has not been realized by pair-only apparatus. If a later construction approximates it, its complete error and resource cost must enter delta_B or a separately proved matching channel bound. 6. Replay, provenance and next frontier Fresh replay compares aggregate and compiled capture/renewal permutations on every stored basis state of small complete modules, checks equal matched energies, counts gates, and includes arbitrary entangled vectors. It constructs explicit three-factor clock/SWAP matrices, tests the prohibited matrix element against two-factor basis terms, and checks the finite-time onsite-X negative control. New padding tails, norm ratios and sufficient-bound arithmetic use exact integers/Fractions and outward integer square roots. Numerical equality checks are separate. General results depend on the written proofs; the large source/controller Hilbert space is not simulated. Large source interval inputs are inherited from M7, which itself retained the source interval receipt. Those assumptions do not gain confidence by another citation. Existing source cutoff, isolation, independence, full complements and phase conventions remain dependencies. Constructor and reviewer are the same Codex lineage; no non-constructor review is claimed. Ledger remains 235 typed objects with Q06=0; physical promotion stays 0. This closes bounded register-support compilation and identifies a precise obstruction for direct pair-only equality. Geometric locality and native apparatus remain open. The next meaningful choice is to define a genuinely allowed pair-interaction architecture with explicit ancillas/encoding and derive its complete finite-time error, or to adopt supplied three-register couplings as the declared construction and investigate spatial routing/clock degree. Neither route can be inferred from this compiler alone.
