content: Retained binary producer and ladder lifts in M6; complete independent-bank overlap and full native-domain debit. 795 exact/51 numerical checks; inherited large interval inputs. Independent review pending; physical promotion 0. M7 development addendum 0.1. Source-word/complete-bank certificate. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. The large source interval inputs are inherited; the full large Hilbert space is not simulated.Source production in the finite controller795 exact and 51 numerical checks passed. For the retained two-attempt example, the complete sufficient bound is below 11/100 with ideal supply and no added implementation defect. Three prepared modules and all fifteen native source operators are included.Readable report · Complete source, replay and hash release · M6 controller · Paper IVDevelopment — no registry entry. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. This inserts the retained binary-fuel and finite-ladder source word into the M6 scheduled controller. No native coherent supply, local apparatus, permanent exhaustion, laboratory scale or new coefficient is established. Papers I–III 1.1.1, Paper IV 0.1 and M6 0.1 remain unchanged. 1. Source and complete resource domain The retained controller source, audit 0.26, supplies q binary energy-preserving fuel exchanges and m finite block lifts. The retained ladder source supplies the cutoff tail q_b, integer energy labels a_l, finite margins and signed-word overlap. Their exact source hashes and historical certificates accompany this release. We derive the new full-bank contract; the large original source suites and interval algorithm are not rerun here. Use distinct symbols: a is the number of attempts, m is the number of source cells per attempt, q is the number of fuel qubits, L=2^q is the packet length, C_* is the maximum admitted integer shift, and M_R=L+2(m+1)C_* is the reference dimension. The seed is n_0=(m+1)C_. Native source energies remain E_l=2J sin(2pil/K); comparison energies are Deltaa_l on the admitted cutoff and equal native energies outside it. Delta>0 is a supplied resource spacing. Every admitted mismatch has norm at most Delta/2. The source ground label g=0 has E_g=bar E_g=0. The active module A=(S_1,…,S_m,R,F_0,…,F_{q-1},L_flag) contains m selected cells, one reference, q fuel qubits and a degenerate flag. Supply a+1 mutually independent ready modules: the initial A and a matched donors D_1,…,D_a. Each starts in source |g>^m, seed |n_0>, coherent fuel |+>^q and flag 0. Supply a distinct m-cell output bank O_i in |g>^m for each attempt, two degenerate blank records M_i,E_i per attempt, and blank END witness Z. One global M6 clock Q is supplied in address 0. Prior retained history Y is independent of this ideal complete ready bank. Deviations, including correlations and bad blanks, enter one complete supply distance epsilon_F. There are m(a+1) module source carriers and ma output carriers, hence m(2a+1) native source cells on the owned domain. The last donor leaves a fresh unconsumed active module after the a-th renewal. Calling only the a consumed modules the whole supply would omit that final resource. 2. Full finite production word and common endpoint phase For each attempt, first use the q disjoint finite fuel/reference exchanges proved in Paper IV IV.2. They map the seed and coherent fuel to the uniform L-level ladder and ground-state fuel. All complementary basis states are specified by identity, and no reference wrap is used. Then apply one complete finite lift to each of the m source cells. On each complete energy block r+a_l=u, insert a supplied cutoff unitary V with V|g⟩=∑lcleiE‾lT|l⟩, V|g\rangle=\sum_l c_l e^{i\bar E_l T}|l\rangle, where c_l are the normalized cutoff packet coefficients and T=pi/(2*kappa) is the common final clock endpoint. Incomplete blocks and source-complement states carry identity. The lift commutes with the complete comparison bare generator. Reference margins protect the populated signed histories for all m lifts. Use one common endpoint T in every attempt’s programmed V. Gates in a history Hamiltonian are not applied at classical per-edge times: the comparator factors into one common free evolution and a prefix. All future donors evolve freely from launch, and energy commutation carries those phases consistently. No classical phase reset at each renewal is assumed. The unused final active module is its supplied ready state freely evolved from launch, not a newly rephased |+> bank at T. For reuse beyond this controller, its phase would require a new complete contract. Append matched m-cell output SWAP with flag/record flips, then matched full-module renewal SWAP, as specified in M6. Append X_Z after the last renewal. Each production block has b=q+m gates. The completed word length is k=a(q+m+2)+1. k=a(q+m+2)+1. Choose n>=k clock edges; the remaining n-k gates are identity padding. Source lifts, capture/record gates and renewal gates all commute with the additive comparison bare generator bar H_B. The constant dressed clock has norm kappa*n and dimension n+1. Gate synthesis, launch and every complete complement action remain supplied. 3. Exact full-bank overlap In an interaction representation at T, each consumed production module emits the correlated cell/reference state |Ψm⟩=∑𝐥(∏j=1mclj)|𝐥⟩⊗T−s(𝐥)|ηL⟩,s(𝐥)=∑j=1malj. |\Psi_m\rangle=\sum_{\boldsymbol l}\left(\prod_{j=1}^m c_{l_j}\right) |\boldsymbol l\rangle\otimes T_{-s(\boldsymbol l)}|\eta_L\rangle, \qquad s(\boldsymbol l)=\sum_{j=1}^m a_{l_j}. The consumed fuel is in its ground state. The corresponding ideal semantic target consists of m independent uncut source packets, the undisplaced reference packet, and the same ground fuel. Its overlap is h=(1−qb)m/2Am,Am=𝔼(1−|s|L)+,Am≥(1−mμL)+,μ=∑l|cl|2|al|. h=(1-q_b)^{m/2}A_m, \quad A_m=\mathbb E\left(1-\frac{|s|}{L}\right)_+, \quad A_m\ge\left(1-\frac{m\mu}{L}\right)_+, \quad \mu=\sum_l|c_l|^2|a_l|. The expectation describes coefficients, not independence of actual emitted cells and reference. Free reference phases and common source phases cancel in this overlap. Theorem M7.1 (complete independent-attempt target). At the completed comparator prefix, including all output slots, consumed donor waste, records, END, the final fresh active module and arbitrary retained independent Y, the trace distance from the specified semantic target is ηa=1−h2a=1−(1−qb)amAm2a. \eta_a=\sqrt{1-h^{2a}} =\sqrt{1-(1-q_b)^{am}A_m^{2a}}. In particular, ηa≤1−(1−qb)am(1−mμL)+2a≤min{1,aη1}. \eta_a\le\sqrt{1-(1-q_b)^{am}\left(1-\frac{m\mu}{L}\right)_+^{2a}} \le\min\{1,\sqrt a\,\eta_1\}. Proof. Before routing, the independent ready modules yield a tensor product of a separate production states and one unused ready state. The M6 finite gate word relocates their factors: each output receives its produced cells; consumed references and ground fuel move into D_i, along with the output blanks and flipped module flag; records and END have their prescribed values. Later preparation never acts on these consumed references. This common unitary relabeling preserves overlap with the target relabeled in the same way. Each consumed module contributes h, the unused module and prescribed records contribute one, so the total overlap is h^a. Pure-state trace distance gives sqrt(1-h^(2a)). Tensoring a common arbitrary mixed Y changes no distance. Monotonicity and the source overlap lower bound give the first inequality. Applying 1-(1-x)^a<=a*x to x=eta_1^2 gives the second. ▫\square This is a complete-state target comparison, not a diamond-norm claim. Correlated donors, an initially correlated active source, interleaved contacts on a consumed reference or an incomplete complement specification invalidate the product-overlap premise unless their discrepancy is included in an admitted full-bank/channel comparison. Marginal slot fidelities cannot justify h^a. The source’s cutoff and reference debit are combined once in eta_a. We do not add a*eta_1 or separate cutoff penalties on top of it. Nor does renewal erase correlations from the complete domain: the actual deviations remain in the retained output/reference/donor state. 4. Actual native generator and padded target window Let H_0=bar H_B+H_d be the comparator and H_act=H_B+H_d+V_err the actual generator on the same complete domain. H_B retains every native module/output source operator; ladder, fuel and records are matched. If the additional implementation operator has norm at most d_imp, a sufficient uniform full-domain bound is $$ \delta_B=\|H_{\rm act}-H_0\|\le\frac{m(2a+1)\Delta}{2}+d_{\rm imp}. $$ This includes unused donor and output carrier complements. The parent m*Delta/2 bound for one production bank cannot be copied onto this larger domain. A smaller reachable-state estimate would need a separately proved invariant-domain theorem; source-ground occupancy at one endpoint is insufficient. The M6 incomplete-prefix tail is r_{n,k}(t)=Pr[Bin(n,sin^2(kappa*t))<k]. Let f(r)=sqrt(1-max(0,1-2r)^2). Define the semantic target at time t to retain the clock |chi(t)>, all prescribed records, blank source partitions in consumed donors, ground waste fuel, undisturbed freely evolving reference packets, and the final ready module freely evolved from launch. Output packets are native freely evolved from their desired state at T. This time-indexed target does not reset resource phases. The completed comparison output target instead uses bar H_O after T. With d_O<=amDelta/2 on the complete output bank, their target difference is at most |t-T|d_O. The retained resource target has only source |g> partitions outside O; there native/comparator source phases agree. All other free resource phases are common. Theorem M7.2 (whole-bank native window bound). Under the complete initial supply distance epsilon_F, $$ D_{\rm tr}(\rho_{\rm act}(t),\tau_{\rm semantic}(t)) \le\min\{1,\epsilon_F+t\delta_B+f(r_{n,k}(t))+\eta_a+|t-T|d_O\}. $$ On t in [pi/(3kappa),2pi/(3*kappa)], the uniform sufficient debit is ϵF+2πδB3κ+f(Rn,k)+ηa+πdO6κ,Rn,k=4−n∑j=0k−1(nj)3j, \epsilon_F+\frac{2\pi\delta_B}{3\kappa}+f(R_{n,k})+\eta_a+ \frac{\pi d_O}{6\kappa}, \quad R_{n,k}=4^{-n}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\binom nj3^j, capped at one. Proof. Transport epsilon_F by contractivity. Compare actual native evolution to H_0 with Duhamel on the whole domain, costing t*delta_B. M6.2 compares its padded coherent prefixes to the complete scheduled word, costing f(r). M7.1 compares that completed word to the specified uncut packet/resource target, costing eta_a; common free evolution preserves this distance. Finally replace only the target output comparator phases after T by native phases, costing |t-T|d_O. Triangle inequality and the time/tail bounds prove the assertion. ▫\square The two native terms bound different steps of this conservative comparison: full evolution against H_0, and target-phase replacement. They are not old per-pulse mismatch/reset debits. No mtauDelta/2, timed capture pulse debit or static renewal-clock norm is added to this architecture. Extra storage/detector/contact terms require their matching full channel and cannot be hidden by scheduled-transfer records. The bound is not an observed error or an optimally minimized one. 5. Explicit retained example and resource receipt Retain K=59049=3^10, w=32=2^5, b=768=32^8, J=4096=2^12, Delta=1/10, q=20, L=2^20, m=3, C_=6687 and M_R=1102072. The source’s outward rational endpoints for q_b and mu are inherited, not freshly regenerated. New bound arithmetic uses those endpoints as exact rational inputs and outward integer square roots. Take a=2 and n=128=2^7, with k=51=317 and 77=711 identity-padding edges. Clock dimension is 129=3*43, norm 2^19 and T=pi/2^13. The certified window is [pi/12288,pi/6144], and return is pi/4096. The replay receipt gives R_{128,51} exactly as a reduced fraction and encloses the complete sufficient bound. Choosing a different n changes tail, dimension and norm; it does not change the source’s packet/reference term. The fresh resource bank has three 20-qubit fuel banks: 60 coherent qubits, of which 40 are consumed and 20 remain in the final active ready module. It supplies three loaded reference seeds, nine module source cells, six output source cells, two donor exchanges, two output banks, four operational/witness records, three module flags and one END record. The complete mismatch upper bound is delta_B=3/4 when d_imp=0; d_O=3/10. Even though the unused seed cells start at g, a uniform complete-domain bound still owns all fifteen source operators. For a+1 independent ideal fuel banks, $$ \langle H_{F,\rm total}\rangle=(a+1)\frac{\Delta(L-1)}2, \qquad\operatorname{Var}H_{F,\rm total}=(a+1)\frac{\Delta^2(L^2-1)}{12}. $$ With the example this is fuel mean 629145/4 and variance 219902325555/80. Three reference seeds require total energy 40122/5. These are initial supplied-resource receipts in model units. Fuel QFI for the pure independent bank is four times that variance; arbitrary correlations or mixed fuel require a different complete calculation. No seed, blank output or leftover coherent module is counted as free merely because it is not consumed. Small replays construct the actual complete finite fuel maps and cutoff lifts, check their full-domain unitarity and energy commutation, verify safe translations and common-endpoint phase cancellation, and compare the complete overlap to a tensor-product target. The multi-attempt factorization is checked on direct small vectors and complete SWAP correlation export. The large 60-qubit/source example is certified arithmetic on inherited interval inputs; its full Hilbert space is not numerically simulated. 6. Scientific disposition and next gate M7 discharges the missing source-word/semantic-target premise for M6 under an independent ready-bank supply and the retained source certificates. It also rejects an accounting shortcut during construction: the uniform native mismatch must own unused donor and output source carriers. This new construction records the rejected shortcut explicitly; no old manuscript is silently rewritten. Native coherent supply, physical geometry/admission, gate synthesis locality, calibrated action/time scale, permanently irreversible END, external export beyond the window, detector acquisition and empirical validation remain open. Same-constructor checking does not supply a non-constructor adversarial review. The ledger stays at 235 typed objects and Q06=0; physical promotion remains 0. The next mathematical target is a stated interaction-locality constraint for the complete production/capture/renewal gates, followed by either a finite local decomposition with a controlled clock cost or a precise obstruction. The source certificate can be reused only while its isolation, margins, gate extensions and whole-bank assumptions remain unchanged.

title: M6 — Bounded controller and Paper IV proof review
note: Development addendum 0.1 · 4 October 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Supplied finite production/capture/renewal word, full-joint padding tail and reversible exhaustion. Constructor checks; native apparatus and independent review remain open. Physical promotion 0. M6 development addendum 0.1. Conditional finite scheduled-word construction. Same-constructor review; independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. Existing manuscript editions remain unchanged.Bounded controller and Paper IV reviewComplete readable report · Source, replay and hash release · Paper IV 0.1Fresh M6 replay: 101 exact checks and 79 numerical checks passed. Paper IV replay: 378 exact and 71 numerical checks passed on rerun. These are constructor checks.Status: development — no registry entry. Exact conditional finite-matrix construction; same-constructor review. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. No new ledger coefficient, physical scale, novelty claim or native apparatus is introduced. Paper IV 0.1 and Papers I–III 1.1.1 remain unchanged. 1. The gap and the narrower result Paper IV Section 10 asks for a bounded production-to-capture trigger and finite router on one complete domain. We answer a restricted version: a supplied finite gate word can order production, output exchange, record creation and fresh-donor renewal under one time-independent Hamiltonian after a supplied launch. Identity padding supplies a pointwise interval during which the completed word is close to a clock-independent body target. The controller does not detect an arbitrary external readiness event. Its trigger is a designated clock edge, encoded in supplied couplings. Native acquisition, local synthesis, launch and permanent exhaustion remain open. The ingredients are the prefix-dressed perfect-transfer clock already proved in Paper IV IV.4, the matched SWAP identity IV.12, and Duhamel comparison IV.1. The new work is their complete finite-domain composition, an explicit padding tail, refusal/return accounting and a replayable two-attempt example. This is not an independent or comprehensive literature comparison. 2. Complete domain and ordered slots All spaces are finite. The active module is A=(S,R,F,L)A=(S,R,F,L), with source SS, reference RR, fuel FF and bare-degenerate flag LL. For aa attempts supply separate output slots OiO_i, donor modules DiD_i matched to all of AA, and bare-degenerate records Mi,EiM_i,E_i, i=1,…,ai=1,\ldots,a. A degenerate exhaustion witness ZZ and one global clock QQ complete the controller. Arbitrary spectator/history YY retains all old correlations and waste. There is no separate production or capture clock in this architecture; QQ is never renewed. The additive comparison bare generator is H‾B\bar H_B on the body B=(A,D1,…,Da,O1,…,Oa,M1,E1,…,Ma,Ea,Z)B=(A,D_1,\ldots,D_a,O_1,\ldots,O_a,M_1,E_1,\ldots,M_a,E_a,Z). Donors match AA under a specified identification; outputs match SS. Supply a complete initial body/history state σBY\sigma_{BY}. It specifies fresh donor states independent of the old active module and history, independent output blanks, and L,Mi,Ei,Z=0L,M_i,E_i,Z=0. Fresh coherent fuel and any needed reference states are included. A production word has unitary gates Vi,1,…,Vi,biV_{i,1},\ldots,V_{i,b_i} acting on S,R,FS,R,F, each commuting with H‾B\bar H_B. The word’s correctness on the supplied input is a separate hypothesis; it is not inferred from the clock. For attempt ii, append these production gates, then Ki=SWAPSOiXLXMiXEi,Ri=SWAPADi. K_i=\mathrm{SWAP}_{S O_i}\,X_L X_{M_i}X_{E_i},\qquad R_i=\mathrm{SWAP}_{A D_i}. The factors in KiK_i commute because their registers are disjoint. Both KiK_i and RiR_i are matched-energy involutions commuting with H‾B\bar H_B. Each KiK_i is unconditional at its designated word position: in the ideal path the production word has already completed. The flag and record mean scheduled transfer, not detector-confirmed production quality. A failed production or bad supply is still exchanged and consumes its slot. No branch is discarded. Append XZX_Z after the final renewal. Let the resulting gates be G1,…,GkG_1,\ldots,G_k, with k=∑i=1a(bi+2)+1. k=\sum_{i=1}^a(b_i+2)+1. There is no modulo slot index: only slots 11 through aa occur, each once in the forward word. Append m≥0m\ge0 identity gates, so n=k+mn=k+m. Let Pj=Gj⋯G1P_j=G_j\cdots G_1 for j≤kj\le k, and Pj=PkP_j=P_k for k≤j≤nk\le j\le n, with P0=IP_0=I. All gates must be supplied as unitaries on the full finite domain, including their complements; correctness only on a populated subspace is insufficient. After KiK_i, later ideal gates in this forward word do not act on Oi,Mi,EiO_i,M_i,E_i. At RiR_i, all old A/YA/Y correlations move into Di/YD_i/Y, while the supplied independent fresh module occupies AA. In particular, no output is reused as a blank and no consumed donor is refilled. Successive forward attempts begin from supplied modules; XZX_Z creates a reversible witness of reaching the last designated edge. 3. One constant post-launch generator Let QQ have n+1n+1 addresses, initially |0⟩|0\rangle. With κ>0\kappa>0, define HQ=κ∑j=0n−1(j+1)(n−j)(|j+1⟩⟨j|+|j⟩⟨j+1|),𝒲=∑j=0n|j⟩⟨j|⊗Pj, H_Q=\kappa\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\sqrt{(j+1)(n-j)} (|j+1\rangle\langle j|+|j\rangle\langle j+1|), \quad \mathcal W=\sum_{j=0}^{n}|j\rangle\langle j|\otimes P_j, Hd=𝒲(HQ⊗IB)𝒲†,H0=IQ⊗H‾B+Hd. H_d=\mathcal W(H_Q\otimes I_B)\mathcal W^\dagger, \quad H_0=I_Q\otimes\bar H_B+H_d. Its edge jj to j+1j+1 carries Gj+1G_{j+1} and the reverse edge carries Gj+1†G_{j+1}^\dagger. All edge couplings are constant after launch. Routing is encoded in these supplied multi-register gates; address-neighbor coupling does not prove spatial locality on BB. Theorem M6.1 (finite ordered controller). For every body/history input ρBY\rho_{BY}, the comparison evolution from Q=0Q=0 is ρ0(t)=𝒲(|χ(t)⟩⟨χ(t)|⊗e−itH‾BρBYeitH‾B)𝒲†, \rho_0(t)=\mathcal W\left(|\chi(t)\rangle\langle\chi(t)|\otimes e^{-it\bar H_B}\rho_{BY}e^{it\bar H_B}\right)\mathcal W^\dagger, where |χ(t)⟩=∑j=0ncj(t)|j⟩|\chi(t)\rangle=\sum_{j=0}^nc_j(t)|j\rangle and cj(t)=(−i)j(nj)sinj(κt)cosn−j(κt). c_j(t)=(-i)^j\sqrt{\binom nj}\sin^j(\kappa t)\cos^{n-j}(\kappa t). At T=π/(2κ)T=\pi/(2\kappa) the complete word PkP_k has executed, every designated slot has been used in the forward word, and Z=1Z=1 for a supplied blank ZZ. At 2T=π/κ2T=\pi/\kappa the clock and gate word return to their initial prefix up to a common phase, with common free body evolution retained. In particular, all transfers and records can reverse. Proof. Each GjG_j commutes with H‾B\bar H_B, so [𝒲,IQ⊗H‾B]=0[\mathcal W,I_Q\otimes\bar H_B]=0 and H0=𝒲(HQ⊗I+I⊗H‾B)𝒲†H_0=\mathcal W(H_Q\otimes I+I\otimes\bar H_B)\mathcal W^\dagger. Paper IV IV.4 gives the spin-clock amplitudes. Initially P0=IP_0=I; at TT only address nn has weight and Pn=PkP_n=P_k. At 2T2T only address 0 has weight and P0=IP_0=I. The tensor identity on arbitrary YY preserves the full history. ▫\square Renewal inside PkP_k follows IV.12 at each forward prefix. If the full initial bank violates independence, the gate identity still holds, but it need not produce a fresh active module. That discrepancy is charged on the whole bank below. Energy-preserving gates can reorganize supplied coherence but do not prepare coherence from a stationary complete supply. 4. Padding tail and complete retention bound For p(t)=sin2(κt)p(t)=\sin^2(\kappa t) define the incomplete-prefix weight rn,k(t)=∑j=0k−1(nj)p(t)j[1−p(t)]n−j. r_{n,k}(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\binom nj p(t)^j[1-p(t)]^{n-j}. The completed target keeps the clock and all history: τ(t)=|χ(t)⟩⟨χ(t)|⊗e−itH‾BPkρBYPk†eitH‾B. \tau(t)=|\chi(t)\rangle\langle\chi(t)|\otimes e^{-it\bar H_B}P_k\rho_{BY}P_k^\dagger e^{it\bar H_B}. Write f(r)=1−[max{0,1−2r}]2f(r)=\sqrt{1-[\max\{0,1-2r\}]^2}. For 0≤r≤1/20\le r\le1/2, this is 2r(1−r)2\sqrt{r(1-r)}; for 1/2≤r≤11/2\le r\le1, it is 1. Theorem M6.2 (joint versus marginal tail). For every body/history input, $$ D_{\rm tr}(\rho_0(t),\tau(t))\le f(r_{n,k}(t))\le\min\{1,2\sqrt{r_{n,k}(t)}\}. $$ After tracing only QQ, the distance from the corresponding completed body/history target is at most rn,k(t)r_{n,k}(t). Proof. Purify ρBY\rho_{BY} without discarding any named register. The overlap between actual comparison purification and the product target is z=1−r+∑j<k|cj|2⟨ψ|Pk†Pj|ψ⟩, z=1-r+\sum_{j<k}|c_j|^2\langle\psi|P_k^\dagger P_j|\psi\rangle, where the common free evolution cancels. Each expectation has modulus at most one, so |z|≥max{0,1−2r}|z|\ge\max\{0,1-2r\}. Pure trace distance is 1−|z|2\sqrt{1-|z|^2}; reduction contracts it, yielding f(r)f(r). Tracing QQ removes all address cross terms. The body is a mixture with completed weight 1−r1-r, so convexity yields the separate rr bound. ▫\square This proof also tightens the conservative IV.10 bound on its stated domain. The old 2r2\sqrt r remains valid and is left unchanged. Neither it nor f(r)f(r) may be replaced by the marginal rr in a complete joint reuse ledger. For a one-edge gate G1=−IG_1=-I, the reduced body is unchanged, but the retained clock has a relative phase; its distance from the product target is 2r(1−r)2\sqrt{r(1-r)} when r≤1/2r\le1/2. Thus clock coherence can saturate the joint bound even when body error is zero. This phase control tests a general clock comparison; it is not a transfer-record implementation. Corollary M6.3 (uniform pointwise window). On π3κ≤t≤2π3κ,p(t)≥34, \frac{\pi}{3\kappa}\le t\le\frac{2\pi}{3\kappa}, \quad p(t)\ge\frac34, one has rn,k(t)≤Rn,k=14n∑j=0k−1(nj)3j. r_{n,k}(t)\le R_{n,k}=\frac{1}{4^n}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\binom nj3^j. The same uniform joint bound is f(Rn,k)f(R_{n,k}), and the uniform marginal bound is Rn,kR_{n,k}. Proof. Couple nn Bernoulli trials using common uniform variables; increasing pp increases their success count pointwise. Hence the lower binomial tail is decreasing in pp. Substitution of p=3/4p=3/4 yields the fraction. The function ff is nondecreasing. ▫\square For fixed kk, increasing nn by identity padding decreases this conservative tail; it also increases clock dimension and ∥Hd∥=κn\|H_d\|=\kappa n. The window duration is π/(3κ)\pi/(3\kappa). At fixed duration, padding costs norm and prepared addresses. The bounds are pointwise for an unmonitored evolution, not first-entry probabilities, a continuously monitored survival law or a stopping-time guarantee. If a supplied classical launch/readout timing offset obeys |s|≤σ|s|\le\sigma, choose nominal readout times in [π/(3κ)+σ,2π/(3κ)−σ][\pi/(3\kappa)+\sigma,2\pi/(3\kappa)-\sigma]. This interval is nonempty when σ≤π/(6κ)\sigma\le\pi/(6\kappa), and every actual elapsed time remains in the certified window. The target retains its actual free phase and clock at that elapsed time. A mixture over offsets preserves the bound when actual and target use the same offset distribution. Comparing instead to one fixed nominal-time target requires an additional full-generator timing bound, at most σ∥H0∥\sigma\|H_0\| for the ideal evolution, capped at one; bare body energies cannot be omitted from that new comparison. 5. Actual generator, supply, gates and record events Supply an actual complete generator HaH_a with ∥Ha−H0∥≤δ \|H_a-H_0\|\le\delta on the same domain. The actual initial full state ωQBY\omega_{QBY} obeys $$ D_{\rm tr}(\omega_{QBY},|0\rangle\langle0|_Q\otimes\sigma_{BY})\le\epsilon_F. $$ This includes clock initialization, all bank correlations, blank records and prior histories. It is charged once. If an intended replacement gate word P̃k\widetilde P_k has uniform per-gate operator deviations gj=∥Gj−G̃j∥g_j=\|G_j-\widetilde G_j\|, its product deviation is bounded by eG=∑j=1kgje_G=\sum_{j=1}^kg_j by telescoping. Use matching complete-domain unitaries and compare targets with the same H‾B\bar H_B free evolution. Production target certificates on a particular supplied state may instead add their corresponding full-joint target error η\eta; they are not automatically uniform channel bounds. Corollary M6.4 (actual full-joint budget). Relative to the completed scheduled word target on σBY\sigma_{BY}, $$ D_{\rm tr}(\rho_a(t),\tau_\sigma(t))\le \min\{1,\epsilon_F+t\delta+f(r_{n,k}(t))\}. $$ A separately specified production/semantic target adds its admitted η\eta; an alternative ideal gate word adds eGe_G. Do not count a gate implementation defect twice if it was already included in δ\delta on the same comparison. Proof. Contractivity transports the initial discrepancy. IV.1 bounds actual/comparison evolution by tδt\delta. M6.2 supplies the comparison/complete-word discrepancy. Triangle inequality proves the claim. For product gate deviations, insert one differing gate at a time; other unitary factors have norm one. ▫\square On the uniform window the state debit is at most min{1,ϵF+2πδ3κ+f(Rn,k)}. \min\left\{1,\epsilon_F+\frac{2\pi\delta}{3\kappa}+f(R_{n,k})\right\}. This whole-word perturbation replaces separate pulse and renewal contact debits for this architecture. The old timed and static apparatus norm terms are not copied into it. Corollary M6.5 (unconditional exhaustion diagnostics). Under the supplied blank ZZ hypothesis, comparison Z=0Z=0 probability is exactly rn,k(t)r_{n,k}(t). With the admitted actual generator and supply discrepancy, Pra(Z=0)≤min{1,ϵF+[rn,k(t)+tδ]2}. \Pr_a(Z=0)\le\min\{1,\epsilon_F+[\sqrt{r_{n,k}(t)}+t\delta]^2\}. The false exhaustion event is PQ<kPZ1P_{Q<k}P_{Z1}. It annihilates the comparison on blank ZZ, so Pra(Q<k,Z=1)≤min{1,ϵF+(tδ)2}. \Pr_a(Q<k,Z=1)\le\min\{1,\epsilon_F+(t\delta)^2\}. Proof. Prefixes j<kj<k never acted on ZZ; all j≥kj\ge k flipped it once. The projected comparison norm for Z=0Z=0 is r\sqrt r. Duhamel adds at most tδt\delta to each projected amplitude. The false event has zero comparison amplitude. Initial trace-distance discrepancy changes any event probability by at most ϵF\epsilon_F. ▫\square These are diagnostics of the supplied sequence, not detector certification. They are already controlled by a joint ledger and are not additional additive state charges. An operational measurement of ZZ changes the retained coherent state; apply the same specified measurement channel to both states when comparing. A normalized accepted state may need the posterior denominator from IV.8 and cannot silently discard failures. 6. Finite refusal, recurrence and resource ownership The word contains no (a+1)(a+1)st output or donor gate, and its padding carries identity. This is exact structural absence of another forward attempt. It is not a permanently absorbing END_OF_SUPPLY state. M6.1 returns the prefix at 2T2T, reversing the exchanges. Even during a high-weight padding window, backward coherent amplitudes exist and can revisit earlier prefixes; their effect is bounded by the tail, not forbidden by irreversible policy. Paper IV IV.9 excludes exact permanent first entry into a reducing subspace in a closed finite constant Hamiltonian. To freeze records beyond the window requires an owned external off-switch, export process, open reservoir or a different finite approximate design with its own ledger. The present controller needs none of the old timed capture switches during its post-launch interval, but requires a supplied launch and externally chosen readout window. It replaces pulse timing with engineered gate-dependent edge couplings and a finite prepared clock. It does not solve native event readiness, native coherent supply or local realization. The conserved comparison mean energy is that of H0H_0. Because [Hd,IQ⊗H‾B]=0[H_d,I_Q\otimes\bar H_B]=0, comparison body bare energy is also conserved. This does not establish conservation of the actual bare energy when native/comparator mismatch is present. If the clock energy is defined by HQH_Q, the interaction is V=Hd−HQV=H_d-H_Q and ∥V∥≤2κn\|V\|\le2\kappa n. Clock address 0 is a prepared nonstationary state, not a free timing resource. Global energy origins change no trajectory; address/flag-conditioned offsets change the operator. Required inputs: all complete gates and their complement action; n+1n+1-address clock state, norm and launch; aa fresh matched modules; aa independent output blanks; 2a+12a+1 blank records; coherent production resources; full supply correlation certificate; complete generator mismatch; and a readout/export policy compatible with the bounded interval. The count aa is freely specified, with no prime restriction. 7. Exact example and retained limitations Take a=2a=2 and b1=b2=1b_1=b_2=1, so k=7k=7. Independent human review: pending. Abstract We consolidate symmetry, radial refinement and prepared collective developments on declared tetrahedral carriers. Signed filled-tetrahedron chains have commutant dimensions 13, 10 and 3 for the full, self-adjoint and skew-adjoint families. Explicit annulus and center-filled shell constructions retain exact topology and representation decompositions. A confining depth operator has compact resolvent and fixed-index finite-shell convergence; four low spectral enclosures are repaired with new rational polynomials, exact root counts and an explicit infinite min-max proof. Scalar Weyl descriptions are restricted to visible modes pending infinite cyclicity. The six-edge relation algebra and minimum context dimension three are retained, with an explicit compatible basis proving covariance of the supplied context tensor. Prepared shape, burden, renewal, finite controller, timed capture and static capture-window results are integrated with their resource ledgers and no-gos. No universal relation strength, native preparation, perpetual storage or physical Hamiltonian is derived. 1. Scope and contribution boundary The purpose of this paper is to collect a set of post-companion mathematical results that enlarge the finite tetrahedral carrier while preserving a narrow claim boundary. The results concern finite S4S_4 representation theory, pure simplicial shell constructions, a declared radial operator family, and its infinite-volume spectral reduction. The basic chain conventions and skew Hodge–Dirac setup are those of the companion finite-carrier paper; the deterministic reconstruction problem is treated separately in the companion projective-receipt paper. Neither companion is logically required for the new shell triangulation once the tetrahedral vertex action is fixed. The ordinary background is standard. Finite-group characters and Schur’s lemma are used in the usual sense [1]. Simplicial boundary operators and combinatorial Laplacians follow the familiar discrete-exterior-calculus and simplicial-Laplacian setting [2-4]. The infinite radial reduction belongs to the general spectral theory of Jacobi-type difference operators and Weyl functions [5]. What is not claimed. The shell index is not a principal quantum number; the declared Hr,βH_{r, eta} is not asserted to be a physical Hamiltonian; EE and T2T_2 are representation labels, not particle names; the radial depth is an internal combinatorial function, not a physical radius; and no energy, action, mass, charge, or time unit is supplied. Any later correspondence to a physical system would require an independently specified carrier map and empirical test. 2. Representation theory of the filled tetrahedron Chain decomposition Let P≅ℝ4P\cong\mathbb{R}^4 be the natural permutation representation of S4S_4 on the vertices of a tetrahedron. With the increasing-order orientation convention, the chain spaces identify with exterior powers, C0≅Λ1P,C1≅Λ2P,C2≅Λ3P,C3≅Λ4P.C_0\cong\Lambda^1P,\qquad C_1\cong\Lambda^2P,\qquad C_2\cong\Lambda^3P,\qquad C_3\cong\Lambda^4P. We use the conventional irreducible labels A1,A2,E,T1,T2A_1,A_2,E,T_1,T_2 for the five real irreducible representations of S4S_4. Theorem 1 (Oriented-chain decomposition). Under the natural S4S_4 action, C0=A1⊕T2,C1=T2⊕T1, oxed{C_0=A_1\oplus T_2},\qquad  oxed{C_1=T_2\oplus T_1}, C2=T1⊕A2,C3=A2. oxed{C_2=T_1\oplus A_2},\qquad  oxed{C_3=A_2}. Equivalently, the decomposition follows directly from the character table of S4S_4 and the character formula for exterior powers. The dimensions 4,6,4,14,6,4,1 provide the independent dimension check. ▫\square Corollary 2 (Symmetry typing of adjacent Hodge channels). The equivariant boundary maps couple only common irreducible sectors. Thus the three adjacent-degree exchange channels are T2:C0↔C1,T1:C1↔C2,A2:C2↔C3, oxed{T_2:\ C_0\leftrightarrow C_1},\qquad  oxed{T_1:\ C_1\leftrightarrow C_2},\qquad  oxed{A_2:\ C_2\leftrightarrow C_3}, with an isolated harmonic A1A_1 vertex mode. The resulting pure 3-ball has f=(19,80,122,60), oxed{f=(19,80,122,60)}, Betti numbers (1,0,0,0), oxed{(1,0,0,0)}, and vertex representation 5A1⊕E⊕4T2. oxed{5A_1\oplus E\oplus4T_2}. Independent human review: pending. Abstract We give sufficient recorded statistics for reconstruction of real and complex chain states up to positive real scale. The real parity-degree and component-sign obstructions, exact forest reconstruction, frozen filled-tetrahedron 14/14 prediction split and covariance pushforward are retained. A separate twelve-incidence sign code detects single errors without unique correction. A new general complex forest proof uses normalized stocks, full complex incidence receipts and one supplied root phase per nonzero component; real-part currents alone remain insufficient. Exact tree-count arithmetic is separated from an unavailable alternative-tree optimization certificate. Correlated residual covariance, joint feasible-state tests, detector references, backaction and finite reuse remain explicitly qualified. A linear invariant-kernel criterion explains why unsigned interface memory need not close visible dynamics. The result is mathematical identifiability after sufficient data are supplied, with acquisition, units, physical carrier identification and original-release provenance maintained as separate obligations. 1. Problem and related work The problem is deterministic reconstruction from finite data. A state c∈ℝN\{0}c\in\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\} is indexed by oriented simplices. We wish to determine its positive ray [c]+={λc:λ>0}. [c]_+=\{\lambda c:\lambda>0\}. Unlike a real projective line, this convention distinguishes cc from −c-c. The distinction is why one absolute sign per connected support component is required. Squared coefficients determine magnitudes but lose signs. Adjacent bilinear products constrain relative signs but can leave magnitude ambiguities. A recording of measurements is useful only if the reconstruction map and its assumptions are stated. We call the resulting finite data a projective support receipt (PSR). “Sufficient statistic” here means sufficient for this deterministic reconstruction problem. No Fisher-Neyman statistical sufficiency claim is made without an additional sampling model. Graph-based recovery from relative observations has a substantial literature. Singer [1, arXiv version p. 1] explicitly describes noiseless phase recovery along a spanning tree, up to a root reference, and explains why noisy tree integration can accumulate error. Our sign propagation is the elementary two-element-group case, not a new general synchronization method. Its role here is to make the required sign data and zero-support cases explicit. The simplex-incidence graph and its operators are standard in combinatorial Hodge and Dirac constructions [2, pp. 1-2; 3, arXiv pp. 4-6]. We use the filled tetrahedron’s bipartite degree structure to expose a second ambiguity: opposite rescaling on even and odd degrees. That multiplicative ambiguity is distinct from the component sign ambiguity. Normalization by the total squared norm does not generally remove both. The contribution is the explicit reconstruction data structure on this carrier, a scoped identifiability counterexample, and a frozen-tree formulation that keeps full-state reconstruction separate from held-out magnitude prediction. Linear covariance pushforward is standard. Its useful specialization here is the exact integer matrix determined by the declared tree, together with a clear boundary between covariance and coverage. We make no priority claim for graph sign synchronization or covariance propagation in general. The companion finite-carrier paper establishes the chain conventions and exact A/B/C operators. This paper is independently readable: only the incidence signs, support graph and Euclidean norm are needed for its principal reconstruction theorem. What this paper does not claim. Algebraic consistency does not authenticate the origin of data or identify a mathematical state with a physical field. The receipt is sufficient under stated assumptions; it is not claimed globally minimal among every possible measurement design. A spanning tree is not claimed statistically optimal. Fourteen held-out channels are not fourteen independent confirmations. No device session or experimental success is reported. 2. The parity-degree identifiability obstruction 2.1 Observables and domain Let KK be a finite oriented simplicial complex. content: Preserved original text/PDF before M4 label and scope repairs. Current reading draft is 1.1.1. Consolidated draft 1.1 · 3 October 2026. Public portal reconciliation: 4 October 2026. Edition record, open gates and archives.Paper I · Consolidated draft 1.1Finite Tetrahedral Complexes, Skew Support Flow and Contact ReadinessPaper I PDF · 25 pages · Editable manuscript · Complete coordinated releaseIndependent researcher ORCID: 0009-0002-5813-0724 Edition status. Integration draft for independent review. Source baseline: portal version 161, commit 62a7c594e0c7ab02f1c87702d0586a39352170d5. Mathematical assertions retain the premises of their declared carriers and maps. Source-audited calculations are distinguished from new derivations. Physical promotion: zero. Independent human review: pending. Abstract We consolidate finite tetrahedral chain algebra with ambient jump comparisons, signed seed readiness and supplied multi-copy contact dynamics. The unit-weight skew Hodge-Dirac baseline, matching-indexed binary carrier, unique-simplex ownership identities, exact A/B/C spectra and receipt-conditioned affine maps are retained. A common ambient comparison exhibits incompatible linear chain/isometry/boundary contracts. A fixed-coupling theorem distinguishes immediate, fourth-order and absent recipient population, while candidate face-readiness coefficients require prepared polarity. Reciprocal endpoint charts give conditional conservation and continuation on supplied contact graphs. Legal distinct-face contacts need not commute, and symmetry obstructs deterministic exclusive progress at a symmetric tie. These results separate carrier geometry, amplitude population, event receipts and admission. Historical constitutive, winding, clock, engineering and empirical updates are integrated with their source limits. No native geometry-creation law, physical coupling or empirical validation is inferred. 1. Scope and mathematical question A finite complex, a linear evolution on its chain space, and a rule for changing the complex are different mathematical objects. This paper keeps them separate. It asks what follows exactly from a specified tetrahedral complex and a fixed skew generator, and what additional information is needed to define a discrete event map. The starting point is conventional: oriented simplices form bases of real chain spaces; signed incidence defines the boundary; the boundary and its adjoint define a Hodge Laplacian. We use the skew combination of these maps to obtain an orthogonal flow. Norm preservation is a standard consequence of skew symmetry, not a new unification principle. The specific calculations concern a matching-indexed binary state, three finite glued complexes, and conditional maps determined by recorded finite data. The notation is chosen to make each object recognizable before introducing any project terminology. A finite oriented tetrahedral simplicial complex is sometimes called a packet complex in the wider Unified Dynamics project. The Euclidean squared chain norm is denoted SμS_\mu, or support. A receipt means only recorded finite data supplied to a stated map. None of these names changes the mathematical type of the object. What this paper does not claim. The finite chain space is not identified with physical space, a physical field, matter or energy. The evolution parameter has no assigned physical unit. The binary coordinates are labels, not measured degrees of freedom. No microscopic source of the event receipts is derived. No physical coupling, action scale, experimental validation or universal recurrence is inferred from the calculations. A structural or numerical correspondence with another construction would not, by itself, identify the two objects. The original result sequence is retained and extended. Section 3 defines the labeled state set and its symmetries. Section 4 fixes the chain convention and records standard operator identities. Section 5 establishes local norm balance and gluing accounting. Section 6 gives the exact A/B/C spectra, recurrence obstruction and ambient linear-jump incompatibilities. Section 7 is one conditional argument: given event receipts, the affine binary map is exact; the pre-event source of those receipts remains open. Section 8 now treats signed readiness, contact charts and admission. Appendix C retains the preservation distinctions. The claim table and executable checks provide a finite review surface. Projective reconstruction is developed in the separate companion paper. Optical acquisition is a separate proposed protocol. Neither is required to prove a statement here. 2. Related work and the contribution boundary Discrete exterior calculus, combinatorial Hodge theory, Dirac operators on complexes, lattice gauge theory and bistellar moves already supply much of the relevant mathematical language. They are the starting point, rather than discoveries of this paper. Hirani’s discrete exterior calculus [1] develops discrete forms and metric-dependent operators using primal and dual complexes. The present work uses a much narrower choice: an orthonormal simplex basis and ordinary transposes. It introduces neither a circumcentric Hodge star nor a convergence theorem for a continuum equation. The comparison is to the discrete incidence/adjoint construction; the thesis abstract and the author’s overview [2, PDF pp. 1-3] identify this setting. We do not infer that the unit-weight matrices here approximate an externally specified metric. Horak and Jost [3, arXiv version pp. 4-6, Definition 2.1] define the up, down and total combinatorial Laplacians using coboundaries and adjoints. Our block Laplacian is the unweighted, nonaugmented specialization of that familiar construction. Our calculation adds the explicitly listed spectra of the selected A/B/C complexes and their consequences for exact periods, not a new general Hodge theory. Knill [4, pp. 1-2] describes D=d+d*D=d+d^*, its square, and the simplex-incidence graph. His Section 17, p. 18, also uses d−d*d-d^* and its relation to the Laplacian. Accordingly, the skew operator and norm conservation below are standard setup. We apply them to a declared finite family and state exactly which inclusion is an isometry and which relabeling is a dynamical intertwiner. Pachner’s theorem [5] concerns equivalence of triangulations of piecewise-linear manifolds under elementary changes. Lickorish [6, p. 302, Definition 2.3; p. 315, Theorem 5.9] states the local bistellar replacement and the global equivalence theorem. We use the three-dimensional 2-to-3 replacement and verify its oriented boundary identity. We claim neither a new move nor the global equivalence theorem. Equality of the exterior boundary does not imply equality of the interior chain operator or its spectrum. Wilson’s lattice gauge theory [7, Section III, pp. 2448-2450] introduces gauge variables and gauge-invariant lattice constructions. A binary label permutation or a change of serialization forest is not thereby a lattice gauge field. There is no Wilson action or gauge-field dynamics in this paper. Kraus’s operator formalism [8] is relevant only to the final distinction between an operator contraction and a norm-preserving map; no new dilation theorem is asserted. The cited article is the original operator-theoretic source, not a source for any physical interpretation of our chain coefficients. The reviewable differences from these literatures are therefore restricted to the following constructions and calculations: the explicit opposite-edge indexing of Θ≅𝔽23\Theta\cong\mathbb F_2^3, distinguished from the matching stabilizer; the selected unique-simplex A/B/C matrices, their exact spectra, and the irrational-frequency obstruction; the receipt-conditioned affine Θ\Theta-map and its exact transition counts; a typed comparison of Euclidean norm, a second quadratic form, sector mixing and contraction effects. title: Paper IV — Finite Prepared Quantum Controllers, Capture Windows and Correlation-Preserving Renewal
note: Current draft 0.1 · 4 October 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Scoped written proofs and retained source dependencies. Independent review pending; physical promotion 0. Papers I–III review drafts 1.1.1 · Paper IV development draft 0.1 · 4 October 2026. Current edition, corrections, source contracts and preserved archives.Paper IV · draft 0.1Finite Prepared Quantum Controllers, Capture Windows and Correlation-Preserving RenewalPaper IV PDF · 14 pages · Editable manuscript · Complete four-paper releaseIndependent researcher ORCID: 0009-0002-5813-0724 Edition status. A mathematical development draft for independent review. This paper consolidates the prepared mechanisms PT11-PT16, previously summarized in Paper III Section 13, without changing their source premises. Finite apparatus is supplied. No empirical validation, native preparation, local implementation or complete autonomous cycle is established. Physical promotion: zero. Independent human review: pending. Abstract We formulate complete joint-system contracts for finite history controllers, capture and matched-register renewal. A supplied gate word is implemented by prefix dressing of an engineered perfect-transfer clock; its native/comparator mismatch is charged over the whole propagation interval. Coherent binary fuel produces a finite reference packet by energy-preserving exchanges, while stationary complete inputs under covariant processing obey a sharp preparation obstruction. A supplied timed terminal exchange protects output after pulse-off under a factorized background. A separate constant post-launch Hamiltonian supplies a finite retention interval, with a complete joint bound distinguished from its smaller marginal error. Matched renewal exports old correlations into a retained donor register; whole-bank supply admission and unconditional telescoping bounds prevent marginal-fidelity and postselection discounts. We state finite exhaustion, recurrence, energy conventions, implementation debits and acquisition limitations explicitly. These are conditional operator constructions, not a derivation of native apparatus or permanent autonomous storage. 1. Question, contribution and established ingredients The question is whether a finite prepared controller can execute a supplied word, export its output and replace its consumed module while preserving a complete account of errors, energy and correlations. A propagation Hamiltonian, a capture operation, and the supply/trigger/router that repeats them are different objects. We construct the first two conditionally and state a finite renewal identity. We do not infer the third from their composition. Engineered perfect state transfer is established prior art. Christandl et al. [1, Eqs. (13)-(15)] use a spin representation of a chain with square-root couplings. Our clock has n+1n+1 addresses and corresponds to their N=n+1N=n+1 sites with their rate parameter 2κ2\kappa. Prefix-dressed history propagation is a standard circuit-to-Hamiltonian ingredient. Caha, Landau and Nagaj [2, Sections 2 and 4] study history clocks and idling; their Theorem 2 concerns amplified ground-state history weight, whereas the retention estimate here is a real-time comparison on a supplied finite spin clock. We claim neither a new perfect-transfer principle nor the general history-clock construction. Finite-clock resource and backreaction analysis has a substantial existing literature, including Woods, Silva and Oppenheim [3]. Their Quasi-Ideal clock is a different construction; no equivalence or superiority theorem is established here. Lostaglio and Mueller [4, Theorem 1] prohibit coherence broadcasting under their finite-reference covariant contract. Our fuel is consumed and renewal uses fresh donors; retaining an outgoing correlated donor is not an unchanged coherence catalyst. Unitary flag premeasurement is standard [5]. Duhamel estimates, swap identities and finite-dimensional analyticity are also established mathematical ingredients. The contribution of this draft is a coordinated, source-traceable set of conditional contracts: actual native operators remain distinct from comparators; timed and static capture have different storage guarantees; complete joint error includes clock and spectator; renewal preserves exported correlations; and finite resource admission is charged at its full-bank domain. A comprehensive theorem-level novelty assessment is pending. The proofs below are supplied to make the stated comparisons reviewable, not to establish a priority claim. Paper I supplies finite tetrahedral chain conventions, Paper II distinguishes complete receipts from incomplete observations, and Paper III supplies the operator comparisons in which these mechanisms arose [6]. None is a proof that the apparatus defined here occurs natively. Our Hilbert spaces are arbitrary declared finite carriers; apparatus address dimensions are not new spatial dimensions. 2. Joint domains, distances and error ownership All spaces in this paper are finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. Tensor identities are suppressed when their domain is declared. Hamiltonians are Hermitian. We use ℏ=1\hbar=1 as a mathematical convention; no laboratory unit or action normalization is inferred. The operator norm is ∥A∥=sup∥v∥=1∥Av∥\|A\|=\sup_{\|v\|=1}\|Av\|. For states, $$ D_{\rm tr}(\rho,\sigma)=\frac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\in[0,1]. $$ A joint state includes every named register and arbitrary spectator YY, possibly correlated with the active body. Any free spectator dynamics is common to actual and comparison channels. A marginal statement explicitly names the traced registers. Probabilities, state distances and Hamiltonian norms have different types. The work module is W=(S,R,F)W=(S,R,F): source bank SS, reference RR and fuel FF. Production clock CC has n+1n+1 addresses. Capture adds a matched output bank OO and degenerate flag LL; optional degenerate memory/witness registers are M,EM,E. Static capture adds address clock QQ of dimension N+1N+1. Donor DD matches the complete module being exchanged. YY includes prior outputs, records, waste and every retained external correlation. Matched means equal carrier dimensions and equal bare energy operators under the declared identification. It is stronger than equal mean energy. A blank output or fresh donor state is a supplied resource, not a state created by exchange. Lemma IV.1 (joint perturbation). If H,KH,K are Hermitian and ∥H−K∥≤d\|H-K\|\le d, then for any t≥0t\ge0, $$ \|e^{-itH}-e^{-itK}\|\le td, \quad D_{\rm tr}(U_H\rho U_H^\dagger,U_K\rho U_K^\dagger)\le\min\{1,td\}, $$ including arbitrary spectator extensions. For a time-dependent extra contact V(u)V(u) on the same domain, replace tdtd by ∫0t∥V(u)∥du\int_0^t\|V(u)\|\,du. Proof. Duhamel writes the propagator difference as an integral of unitary factors around H−KH-K; submultiplicativity bounds it by tdtd. On a purification, the vector difference has that bound, and pure-state trace distance is at most vector distance. Reduction contracts trace distance. The time-dependent proof uses the corresponding propagator identity. ▫\square If an event projector PP annihilates the comparison vector, its actual probability is at most min{1,(td)2}\min\{1,(td)^2\} on that purification. If comparison event amplitude is at most aa, the actual probability is at most min{1,(a+td)2}\min\{1,(a+td)^2\}. An initial full-joint state discrepancy instead changes any event probability by at most its trace distance; it is not automatically an amplitude-square debit. All budgets below refer to a fixed pair of actual and ideal contracts. Additional supplied-state, contact, thermal, detector, storage and implementation errors must be admitted on matching domains. Shared errors are charged once, not repeated for each marginal or each quoted diagnostic. 3. Finite reference and coherent binary fuel 3.1 Source operator and finite shift margins The source packages [7-9] use an actual oriented-ring spectrum Ek=2Jsin(2πk/K)E_k=2J\sin(2\pi k/K), a prepared packet, a declared cutoff and tail probability qbq_b. A comparator E‾k=Δak\bar E_k=\Delta a_k on the admitted cutoff uses certified integer labels; outside that cutoff it agrees with the actual operator. A source cell mismatch is bounded by Δ/2\Delta/2, so for mm admitted cells a sufficient work mismatch is d≤mΔ/2d\le m\Delta/2. This is an assumption/certificate of that source example, not a property of every Hamiltonian. The actual HSH_S is never rounded. Let C*=max|ak|C_* =\max|a_k|. To avoid collision with clock CC, we write the source’s shift margin as C*C_*. A finite ladder has MR=L+2(m+1)C*,n0=(m+1)C*,HR=Δ∑a=0MR−1a|a⟩⟨a|. M_R=L+2(m+1)C_*,\qquad n_0=(m+1)C_*,\qquad H_R=\Delta\sum_{a=0}^{M_R-1}a|a\rangle\langle a|. The packet occupies n0,…,n0+L−1n_0,\ldots,n_0+L-1. Up to m+1m+1 shifts of magnitude at most C*C_* remain inside the declared window. Every gate extension outside its disjoint admitted exchange pairs is specified separately; reference wraparound is not used. The native receipt determining these shifts and packet coefficients is supplied. The parent source’s isolated production overlap yields a full source/reference bank bound $$ \eta_{\rm bank}=\sqrt{1-(1-q_b)^m A_m^2},\qquad A_m\ge\left(1-\frac{m\mu}{L}\right)_+, $$ where μ\mu and the signed-word overlap AmA_m have their source definitions [7-8]. This is an inherited certificate, not newly proved for arbitrary interleaved contacts. A later contact on the same reference, fuel or clock needs its integrated joint channel bound. Isolation is an explicit dependency. 3.2 Energy-preserving producer Theorem IV.2 (binary fuel; PT12 producer). Let L=2qL=2^q, Δ>0\Delta>0, and supply independent fuel qubits FjF_j in |+⟩|+\rangle, with HFj=Δ2j|1⟩⟨1|H_{F_j}=\Delta2^j|1\rangle\langle1|. Supply reference seed |n0⟩|n_0\rangle. There are disjoint energy-preserving exchanges that send |+⟩F⊗q|n0⟩R↦|0⟩F⊗q|ηL⟩R,|ηL⟩=1L∑r=0L−1|n0+r⟩. |+\rangle_F^{\otimes q}|n_0\rangle_R\longmapsto |0\rangle_F^{\otimes q}|\eta_L\rangle_R,\qquad |\eta_L\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt L}\sum_{r=0}^{L-1}|n_0+r\rangle. The seed energy n0Δn_0\Delta and all fuel coherence are inputs. Proof. At step jj pair |1⟩|n0+r⟩|1\rangle|n_0+r\rangle with |0⟩|n0+r+2j⟩|0\rangle|n_0+r+2^j\rangle whenever the jjth bit of rr is zero in the declared packet block. Pairs are disjoint, preserve the sum of the two bare energies, and define a unitary permutation with identity on the complement. By induction, before step jj the populated reference labels are r=0,…,2j−1r=0,\ldots,2^j-1, so the current bit is zero. The next exchange doubles the uniform reference support and leaves fuel bit jj in ground state. After qq steps every binary label occurs once. ▫\square For the bit rule write r=2j+1u+vr=2^{j+1}u+v and r≡v(mod2j+1)r\equiv v\pmod{2^{j+1}}, with 0≤v<2j0\le v<2^j. Transfer replaces vv by v+2jv+2^j on the declared pair. The modulus is a power of the prime 2. This rule defines pairs, not a recycling reservoir. For ideal independent fuel, elementary geometric sums give ⟨HF⟩=Δ(L−1)2,VarHF=Δ2(L2−1)12. \langle H_F\rangle=\frac{\Delta(L-1)}2,\qquad \operatorname{Var}H_F=\frac{\Delta^2(L^2-1)}{12}. For a pure state and the specified time-translation generator, FQ=4VarHFF_Q=4\operatorname{Var}H_F. Correlated pure fuel requires the variance of the complete sum, including covariance terms. For mixed fuel this equality is not generally valid. Arbitrary correlated fuel is transformed to its corresponding joint output; the producer does not replace it by an ideal independent packet. 3.3 Stationary complete-supply limitation Theorem IV.3 (stationary supply; PT12 obstruction). Let the complete input be stationary under a declared additive total free-energy generator. Let the complete production channel be covariant for its input/output generators, and let the output reference generator have nondegenerate packet energies (n0+r)Δ(n_0+r)\Delta, Δ>0\Delta>0. Its reduced reference ωR\omega_R then obeys $$ D_{\rm tr}(\omega_R,|\eta_L\rangle\langle\eta_L|)\ge1-\frac1L. $$ Proof. Covariance preserves total stationarity. Partial trace under an additive output generator leaves a stationary reference. Its matrix is diagonal in the nondegenerate energy basis, so ⟨ηL|ωR|ηL⟩=L−1∑r=0L−1(ωR)n0+r,n0+r≤1/L\langle\eta_L|\omega_R|\eta_L\rangle=L^{-1}\sum_{r=0}^{L-1}(\omega_R)_{n_0+r,n_0+r}\le1/L. The two-outcome measurement of the target projector gives the distance lower bound. The uniform diagonal packet has eigenvalues 1/L1/L on the packet block; its difference from the pure uniform packet has trace norm 2(1−1/L)2(1-1/L), attaining the bound. ▫\square Any coherent fuel, reference, interacting controller or spectator that breaks complete stationarity must be counted. The theorem does not forbid preparation from admitted nonstationary resources, nor does it give a universal approximate-QFI cost. Degeneracy across packet energies would invalidate the diagonal step and requires a different statement. 4. Supplied history word and finite clock Supply gates U1,…,UnU_1,\ldots,U_n commuting with a comparison work Hamiltonian H‾W\bar H_W. Define prefixes P0=IP_0=I, Pj=Uj⋯U1P_j=U_j\cdots U_1, and 𝒲=∑j=0n|j⟩⟨j|C⊗Pj,HC=κ∑j=0n−1(j+1)(n−j)(|j+1⟩⟨j|+|j⟩⟨j+1|), \mathcal W=\sum_{j=0}^n|j\rangle\langle j|_C\otimes P_j, \quad H_C=\kappa\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\sqrt{(j+1)(n-j)} (|j+1\rangle\langle j|+|j\rangle\langle j+1|), with κ>0\kappa>0. Let Hp=𝒲(HC⊗I)𝒲†H_p=\mathcal W(H_C\otimes I)\mathcal W^\dagger and $$ H_{\rm act}=I_C\otimes H_W+H_p,\qquad H_{\rm comp}=I_C\otimes\bar H_W+H_p, \quad \|H_W-\bar H_W\|\le d. $$ Gate-dependent hopping edges contain Uj,Uj†U_j,U_j^\dagger. Their synthesis is supplied; a nearest-neighbor address graph does not establish locality on the work registers. Theorem IV.4 (history propagation; PT11). The clock has spectrum κ(n−2j)\kappa(n-2j), j=0,…,nj=0,\ldots,n, norm κn\kappa n and amplitudes cj(t)=(−i)j(nj)sinj(κt)cosn−j(κt). c_j(t)=(-i)^j\sqrt{\binom nj}\sin^j(\kappa t)\cos^{n-j}(\kappa t). From address 0, the comparator applies PnP_n at T=π/(2κ)T=\pi/(2\kappa) with terminal probability one, and returns to prefix P0P_0 at 2T2T. Actual/comparator propagator difference is at most tdtd. Proof. Identify address jj with the normalized symmetric sum of nn binary spin states of weight jj. The operator κ∑a=1nXa\kappa\sum_{a=1}^n X_a has the displayed adjacent matrix elements and restricts to HCH_C. Tensor products of single-spin rotations give cj(t)c_j(t); symmetric products of XX eigenstates give the spectrum. Since [H‾W,𝒲]=0[\bar H_W,\mathcal W]=0, $$ e^{-itH_{\rm comp}}|0\rangle|\psi\rangle =\sum_j c_j(t)|j\rangle e^{-it\bar H_W}P_j|\psi\rangle. $$ At TT only j=nj=n survives; at 2T2T only j=0j=0 survives. The actual difference is HW−H‾WH_W-\bar H_W, so Lemma IV.1 gives the last bound. The identity extends to mixed inputs and arbitrary spectators by purification. ▫\square The endpoint return is projective: the common factor at 2T2T is (−1)n(-1)^n. Free work evolution is retained; the full work state need not recur. At integer endpoint index ℓ=2u+r\ell=2u+r, ℓ≡r(mod2)\ell\equiv r\pmod2, the address is start for r=0r=0 and terminal for r=1r=1. The modulus 2 is prime. Returning the address does not refill a donor or provide a stopping rule. Corollary IV.5 (completion window). Start the actual machine at address 0 with arbitrary work/spectator state. For t=T+s≥0t=T+s\ge0 and |s|≤σ|s|\le\sigma, define aC=nκσ+(T+σ)d. a_C=\sqrt n\,\kappa\sigma+(T+\sigma)d. Its nonterminal probability is at most min{1,aC2}\min\{1,a_C^2\}. Proof. The comparison terminal probability is cos2n(κs)\cos^{2n}(\kappa s). The inequality 1−(1−z)n≤nz1-(1-z)^n\le nz for z∈[0,1]z\in[0,1], together with |sin(κs)|≤κ|s||\sin(\kappa s)|\le\kappa|s|, bounds the nonterminal amplitude by nκσ\sqrt n\kappa\sigma. Lemma IV.1 adds at most td≤(T+σ)dtd\le(T+\sigma)d to this projected amplitude. ▫\square If the source terminal-branch target has its inherited isolated bank error $\eta_{\rm bank}$ and the native/comparator post-endpoint free phases differ by at most |s|d|s|d, a complete target bound is $$ \eta_{\rm window}\le\min\{1,\eta_{\rm bank}+\sqrt n\kappa\sigma+(T+2\sigma)d\}. $$ Here the comparator is compared to its normalized terminal branch, whose purification overlap has magnitude |cn||c_n|, hence trace distance 1−|cn|2\sqrt{1-|c_n|^2}. Triangle inequality then supplies the displayed bound. The branch-target premise is essential: a generic arbitrary word is not a packet producer. The whole propagation mismatch replaces the earlier separately timed pulse debit; both are not charged for the same comparison interval. 5. The original paper PDF remains unchanged; independent review of the supplement is pending.Review edition 1.0 · 16 September 2026Finite Tetrahedral Complexes and Skew Hodge–Dirac Support FlowBenjamin Walker MayesIndependent researcher ORCID: 0009-0002-5813-0724 Abstract We study dimensionless linear algebra on finite oriented tetrahedral simplicial complexes. The setup is the standard simplicial boundary complex with its Euclidean inner products and skew Hodge–Dirac generator. We distinguish an eight-element binary space indexed by the three perfect matchings of K4K_4 from a matching stabilizer of the same order. An explicitly defined edge projection partitions the labeled state set S4×𝔽23S_4\times\mathbb F_2^3 into six fibers of size 32; this count carries no sequential interpretation. We give exact unique-simplex gluing identities and compute the spectra of three specified tetrahedral complexes. Irrational ratios of their nonzero frequencies exclude a positive exact period for each full flow. Recorded event data define affine maps on the binary space, with exact Hamming-sector transition ranks and a commutator identity. These conditional maps do not supply a pre-event source law. We separate norm preservation, changes of a second quadratic form, sector mixing and contraction effects. Proofs and a standard-library Python reproduction package identify precisely which statements are general and which concern the declared finite examples. These results are finite identities and no-gos on a declared simplicial carrier. They are not a derivation of spacetime geometry, gauge theory, or empirical couplings. 1. Scope and mathematical question A finite complex, a linear evolution on its chain space, and a rule for changing the complex are different mathematical objects. This paper keeps them separate. It asks what follows exactly from a specified tetrahedral complex and a fixed skew generator, and what additional information is needed to define a discrete event map. The starting point is conventional: oriented simplices form bases of real chain spaces; signed incidence defines the boundary; the boundary and its adjoint define a Hodge Laplacian. We use the skew combination of these maps to obtain an orthogonal flow. Norm preservation is a standard consequence of skew symmetry, not a new unification principle. The specific calculations concern a matching-indexed binary state, three finite glued complexes, and conditional maps determined by recorded finite data. The notation is chosen to make each object recognizable before introducing any project terminology. A finite oriented tetrahedral simplicial complex is sometimes called a packet complex in the wider Unified Dynamics project. The Euclidean squared chain norm is denoted SμS_\mu, or support. A receipt means only recorded finite data supplied to a stated map. None of these names changes the mathematical type of the object. What this paper does not claim. The finite chain space is not identified with physical space, a physical field, matter or energy. The evolution parameter has no assigned physical unit. The binary coordinates are labels, not measured degrees of freedom. No microscopic source of the event receipts is derived. No physical coupling, action scale, experimental validation or universal recurrence is inferred from the calculations. A structural or numerical correspondence with another construction would not, by itself, identify the two objects. The result sequence is deliberately short. Section 3 defines the labeled state set and its symmetries. Section 4 fixes the chain convention and records standard operator identities. Section 5 establishes local norm balance and gluing accounting. Section 6 gives the exact A/B/C spectra and their recurrence obstruction. Section 7 is one conditional argument: given event receipts, the affine binary map is exact; the pre-event source of those receipts remains open. Section 8 distinguishes several often-confused notions of preservation. The claim table and executable checks provide a finite review surface. Projective reconstruction is developed in the separate companion paper. Optical acquisition is a separate proposed protocol. Neither is required to prove a statement here. 2. Related work and the contribution boundary Discrete exterior calculus, combinatorial Hodge theory, Dirac operators on complexes, lattice gauge theory and bistellar moves already supply much of the relevant mathematical language. They are the starting point, rather than discoveries of this paper. Hirani’s discrete exterior calculus [1] develops discrete forms and metric-dependent operators using primal and dual complexes. The present work uses a much narrower choice: an orthonormal simplex basis and ordinary transposes. It introduces neither a circumcentric Hodge star nor a convergence theorem for a continuum equation. The comparison is to the discrete incidence/adjoint construction; the thesis abstract and the author’s overview [2, PDF pp. 1–3] identify this setting. We do not infer that the unit-weight matrices here approximate an externally specified metric. Horak and Jost [3, arXiv version pp. 4–6, Definition 2.1] define the up, down and total combinatorial Laplacians using coboundaries and adjoints. Our block Laplacian is the unweighted, nonaugmented specialization of that familiar construction. Our calculation adds the explicitly listed spectra of the selected A/B/C complexes and their consequences for exact periods, not a new general Hodge theory. Knill [4, pp. 1–2] describes D=d+d*D=d+d^*, its square, and the simplex-incidence graph. His Section 17, p. 18, also uses d−d*d-d^* and its relation to the Laplacian. Accordingly, the skew operator and norm conservation below are standard setup. We apply them to a declared finite family and state exactly which inclusion is an isometry and which relabeling is a dynamical intertwiner. Pachner’s theorem [5] concerns equivalence of triangulations of piecewise-linear manifolds under elementary changes. Lickorish [6, p. 302, Definition 2.3; p. 315, Theorem 5.9] states the local bistellar replacement and the global equivalence theorem. We use the three-dimensional 2-to-3 replacement and verify its oriented boundary identity. We claim neither a new move nor the global equivalence theorem. Equality of the exterior boundary does not imply equality of the interior chain operator or its spectrum. Wilson’s lattice gauge theory [7, Section III, pp. 2448–2450] introduces gauge variables and gauge-invariant lattice constructions. A binary label permutation or a change of serialization forest is not thereby a lattice gauge field. There is no Wilson action or gauge-field dynamics in this paper. Kraus’s operator formalism [8] is relevant only to the final distinction between an operator contraction and a norm-preserving map; no new dilation theorem is asserted. The cited article is the original operator-theoretic source, not a source for any physical interpretation of our chain coefficients. The reviewable differences from these literatures are therefore restricted to the following constructions and calculations: the explicit opposite-edge indexing of Θ≅𝔽23\Theta\cong\mathbb F_2^3, distinguished from the matching stabilizer; the selected unique-simplex A/B/C matrices, their exact spectra, and the irrational-frequency obstruction; the receipt-conditioned affine Θ\Theta-map and its exact transition counts; a typed comparison of Euclidean norm, a second quadratic form, sector mixing and contraction effects. The companion paper treats the reconstruction statistic, its parity-degree ambiguity and the frozen-tree covariance map. We do not assert a priority claim for general graph synchronization, linear covariance propagation, or sufficient data for sign reconstruction. 3. Labeled tetrahedral states 3.1 Vertices, edges and perfect matchings Let V={0,1,2,3}V=\{0,1,2,3\} and let K4K_4 be the complete graph on this vertex set. Its six edges are the two-element subsets of VV. Every permutation of VV preserves adjacency, so Aut(K4)=S4\operatorname{Aut}(K_4)=S_4. The three perfect matchings are M1={01,23},M2={02,13},M3={03,12}. M_1=\{01,23\},\qquad M_2=\{02,13\},\qquad M_3=\{03,12\}. Each partitions the four vertices into two disjoint edges. A vertex permutation induces a permutation of this three-element set. Write π:S4→S3 \pi:S_4\longrightarrow S_3 for that action. Proposition P3.1 (matching action). The map π\pi is onto and has kernel V4={1,(01)(23),(02)(13),(03)(12)}. V_4=\{1,(01)(23),(02)(13),(03)(12)\}. Proof. Each listed double transposition preserves all three matchings. A transposition of vertices fixes one matching and exchanges the other two, and suitable vertex permutations therefore generate all permutations of the three matchings. The kernel of a surjection from a group of order 24 onto one of order 6 has order 4. The four listed elements exhaust it. ▫\square Assign one bit to each matching: Θ=𝔽2{M1,M2,M3}≅𝔽23. \Theta=\mathbb F_2^{\{M_1,M_2,M_3\}}\cong\mathbb F_2^3. For p∈S3p\in S_3, use the coordinate action (Ppθ)p(j)=θj(P_p\theta)_{p(j)}=\theta_j. This convention fixes the direction of later composition formulas. Proposition P3.2 (equal order is not group identity). The stabilizer of one matching in S4S_4 has order 8 and is nonabelian. It is not the additive group of Θ\Theta. Proof. Orbit-stabilizer gives order 24/3=824/3=8. In the stabilizer of M1M_1, independently swap the two vertices of each edge, and also exchange the edges. Thus the group is (C2×C2)⋊C2(C_2\times C_2)\rtimes C_2, with the last factor exchanging the first two. For example, the within-edge swap (01)(01) and edge exchange (02)(13)(02)(13) do not commute. The additive group 𝔽23\mathbb F_2^3 is abelian. ▫\square The distinction is structural, not merely terminological. A matching indexes a coordinate; its stabilizer is a group of vertex permutations. The coordinate space is not obtained by identifying those two objects. 3.2 The edge projection and its fibers Define the labeled state set 𝒳=S4×Θ. \mathcal X=S_4\times\Theta. This is a product of sets. It has 192 elements. To make a fiber count meaningful, a projection must be declared. Fix the reference edge e0={0,1}e_0=\{0,1\} and define pE(g,θ)=g(e0). p_E(g,\theta)=g(e_0). The second coordinate does not enter this projection. Proposition P3.3 (uniform edge fibers). Every edge has 32 inverse images under pEp_E. Consequently |𝒳|=192=6×32. |\mathcal X|=192=6\times32. Proof. A permutation sending e0e_0 to a specified edge can assign its two vertices in two orders and assign the two complementary vertices in two orders. There are four such permutations. Each can be paired with any of the eight binary vectors, giving 4×8=324\times8=32 states. The six fibers partition 𝒳\mathcal X. ▫\square The integer factors are 192=26⋅3192=2^6\cdot3, 6=2⋅36=2\cdot3, and 32=2532=2^5. They record the specified counting construction, not a dynamical scale. In quotient/remainder notation, 192=6(32)+0192=6(32)+0 and 192≡0(mod32)192\equiv0\pmod{32}: six complete groups leave no remainder. No-go NG3.4 (cardinality does not specify depth). The size 32 of a fiber does not imply 32 successive update stages, a 32-cycle, or a required duration. Proof. On the same 32-element fiber one may define the identity map, a transposition, or a 32-cycle. Their update histories differ while the underlying cardinality is unchanged. No transition map is included in the fiber definition. Therefore no sequential depth follows from that definition alone. ▫\square 3.3 Hamming sectors On the eight-dimensional vector space with basis eθe_\theta, define Weθ=wH(θ)eθ,wH(θ)=θ1+θ2+θ3. W e_\theta=w_H(\theta)e_\theta, \qquad w_H(\theta)=\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3. These eigenspaces are called Hamming sectors; “branch” will not be used to imply a physical process. Oriented chains and the standard skew generator 4.1 Chain convention A simplicial complex in this paper contains each nonempty simplex once, including all faces of every maximal simplex. Along the closed flow, dSRds=Jin(R)−Jout(R), \frac{dS_R}{ds}=J_{\mathrm{in}}(R)-J_{\mathrm{out}}(R), where only adjacent-degree incidences crossing RR and its complement contribute. Proof.
