Both contradict two. ▫\square This excludes one particular auxiliary labeling condition. It does not obstruct the Pachner move itself or rule out another state representation. 6.4 Exact recurrence and its limits No-go NG6.6 (no positive full-flow period). For each K∈{A,B,C}K\in\{A,B,C\}, there is no T>0T>0 for which eT𝒜K=Ie^{T\mathcal A_K}=I. Proof. For AA, a full period requires integers n,m>0n,m>0 with T3=2πn,T5=2πm. T\sqrt3=2\pi n,\qquad T\sqrt5=2\pi m. Thus 5/3=m/n\sqrt{5/3}=m/n. If this were rational in lowest terms, 3m2=5n23m^2=5n^2, contradicting the even valuations of squares at primes 3 and 5. The same argument using primes 2 and 5 rules out 5/2\sqrt{5/2} for B and C. ▫\square The clock form of the required equalities is T3≡T5≡0(mod2π)T\sqrt3\equiv T\sqrt5\equiv0\pmod{2\pi} for A, and analogously for B/C: both spectral pointers would have to return to zero after integer full rotations. The irrational ratio forbids a common nonzero exact return. This statement is about the identity of the entire evolution operator. A harmonic state is fixed. A state supported in a single frequency subspace is periodic. Approximate returns are not excluded; simultaneous rational approximation of phases can bring a bounded finite-dimensional orthogonal flow close to its initial operator. We make no claim about a minimum approximate-return time. The single-cell period π\pi therefore cannot be assigned to all glued complexes, but recurrence of selected states remains possible. 7. Recorded events determine affine binary maps 7.1 What data are supplied Fix pre- and post-event labeled states (g−,θ−)(g^-,\theta^-) and (g+,θ+)(g^+,\theta^+). Define the relative vertex permutation and binary offset r=g+(g−)−1,a=θ+⊕Pπ(r)θ−. r=g^+(g^-)^{-1},\qquad a=\theta^+\oplus P_{\pi(r)}\theta^-. The pair (r,a)(r,a) is the recorded event data. If those endpoints are observed only after the event, the pair is retrospective. To predict an event, a separate pre-event process must supply (r,a)(r,a) without using the held-out endpoint. Definition D7.1. For supplied r∈S4r\in S_4, a∈Θa\in\Theta, define the affine map Fr,a(θ)=a⊕Pπ(r)θ, F_{r,a}(\theta)=a\oplus P_{\pi(r)}\theta, and its permutation operator Ur,aeθ=eFr,a(θ)U_{r,a}e_\theta=e_{F_{r,a}(\theta)}. Proposition T7.2 (exact receipt-conditioned map). The map is a bijection, its permutation operator is orthogonal, and endpoint-derived data satisfy Fr,a(θ−)=θ+F_{r,a}(\theta^-)=\theta^+. Proof. Coordinate permutation and translation in 𝔽23\mathbb F_2^3 are both bijections. The inverse is θ↦Pπ(r)−1(θ⊕a)\theta\mapsto P_{\pi(r)}^{-1}(\theta\oplus a). A bijection of an orthonormal basis gives an orthogonal matrix. Substituting the endpoint definition of aa cancels the repeated binary vector. ▫\square For consecutive supplied events, the maps compose as Fr2,a2∘Fr1,a1=Fr2r1,a2⊕Pπ(r2)a1. F_{r_2,a_2}\circ F_{r_1,a_1} =F_{r_2r_1,\ a_2\oplus P_{\pi(r_2)}a_1}. This is an affine-group identity. It does not say which events occur or assign probabilities to them. 7.2 Exact Hamming-sector consequences Theorem T7.3 (sector transition counts). Let h=wH(a)h=w_H(a). For weights w,w′w,w', rank(Pw′Ur,aPw)=(ht)(3−hw−t),t=w+h−w′2, \operatorname{rank}(P_{w'}U_{r,a}P_w) =\binom ht\binom{3-h}{w-t}, \qquad t=\frac{w+h-w'}2, when tt is an integer satisfying 0≤t≤h0\le t\le h and 0≤w−t≤3−h0\le w-t\le3-h; otherwise the rank is zero. Furthermore, 18∥[Ur,a,W]∥F2=h. \frac18\|[U_{r,a},W]\|_F^2=h. Proof. Coordinate permutation preserves weight. Of the hh coordinates flipped by the offset, let tt initially contain a one. The output weight is w+h−2tw+h-2t. There are (ht)(3−hw−t)\binom ht\binom{3-h}{w-t} input basis vectors with these properties. Distinct inputs have distinct outputs, so counting them gives the block rank. For the commutator, its squared norm is the sum of squared weight changes over the eight basis vectors. For a uniformly selected binary vector, each flipped coordinate contributes independently either +1+1 or −1-1, equally often. The expected square of their sum is hh, since the cross terms cancel. Multiply by eight. ▫\square Thus a map may mix Hamming sectors while preserving the Euclidean norm of every vector on the eight-state space. For example, a one-bit flip has normalized commutator square one but remains a permutation matrix. Hamming-sector preservation for this affine family occurs exactly when a=0a=0. 7.3 Recovering a relative frame when an edge map is supplied A specified edge map can sometimes determine the vertex permutation in the receipt without reference to the post-event binary endpoint. This remains a conditional extraction problem: the edge map itself must already be available. Proposition P7.4 (unique relative-frame extraction). Let M:C1(Δ3)→C1(Δ3)M:C_1(\Delta^3)\to C_1(\Delta^3) be a supplied real matrix, and let J4=𝟏𝟏TJ_4=\mathbf1\mathbf1^T. Form P̂=14(B1MB1T+J4). \widehat P=\frac14(B_1MB_1^T+J_4). If P̂\widehat P is a vertex permutation matrix and B1M=P̂B1B_1M=\widehat P B_1, there is a unique r∈S4r\in S_4 with P0(r)=P̂P_0(r)=\widehat P. With the induced signed edge map P1(r)P_1(r), the residual R=P1(r)−1MR=P_1(r)^{-1}M satisfies B1R=B1B_1R=B_1. If MM is orthogonal, RR fixes the cut space pointwise and preserves the cycle space. Proof. A permutation matrix uniquely specifies its vertex permutation. Boundary equivariance gives B1P1(r)=P0(r)B1B_1P_1(r)=P_0(r)B_1, so substitution gives B1R=B1B_1R=B_1. Transposing yields RTB1T=B1TR^TB_1^T=B_1^T. If RR is orthogonal, multiply by RR to obtain RB1T=B1TRB_1^T=B_1^T; hence it fixes the cut space. Orthogonality then preserves its orthogonal complement, the cycle space. Conversely, if an edge map satisfies B1M=P0B1B_1M=P_0B_1 for a permutation P0P_0, multiplication by B1TB_1^T and use of B1B1T=4I−J4B_1B_1^T=4I-J_4, P0J4=J4P_0J_4=J_4, recovers the stated formula. ▫\square The two admission checks are essential. The formula alone may yield a matrix that is not a permutation, and a visually nearby permutation is not an exact substitute. Even successful extraction leaves the parity offset aa unspecified. This illustrates the distinction between recovering a frame from sufficient recorded data and deriving an event source. 7.4 The unresolved source question The logical conclusion is deliberately conditional: supplied (r,a)⇒an exact affine Θ-map. \text{supplied }(r,a)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{an exact affine }\Theta\text{-map}. It is not a derivation of (r,a)(r,a) from the chain state or from a microscopic law. Extracting an offset from observed endpoints always fits that pair of endpoints by definition; it cannot count as a successful prediction of them. Many different offset-selection rules are compatible with the same carrier, group action and closed norm conservation. Later conditional constructions in the research archive introduce finite update interfaces, source packets, recovery criteria and event-admission rules. They specify what a source would have to provide. They are not used as premises of the theorems above and are not stacked into the main argument. In particular, an executable rule that accepts source terms as input is not a derivation of those terms. The source of predictive receipts remains outside this paper. 8. Four preservation statements with different types Let TT be a linear map between Euclidean chain spaces. Its Gram defect is GT=TTT−I. G_T=T^TT-I. It measures a change in squared chain norm: ∥Tc∥2−∥c∥2=cTGTc\|Tc\|^2-\|c\|^2=c^TG_Tc. This must not be confused with Hamming-sector mixing on the separate eight-state space. Suppose a second quadratic form is specified by a symmetric matrix QQ. The change of that form is cT(TTQT−Q)c. c^T(T^TQT-Q)c. A project may call such a second functional burden, but the word supplies no physical meaning and no relation to SμS_\mu. The matrix QQ and its carrier must be stated before the expression is meaningful. Proposition P8.1 (norm preservation does not imply preservation of another form). Choosing L=E1/2L=E^{1/2} gives KTK+LTL=I. K^TK+L^TL=I. This is the elementary finite operator identity behind a retained/lost split. In a complex quantum-operation setting it is familiar from Kraus representations. Here it is only linear algebra. A permutation mixing Hamming sectors can have zero Gram defect and zero complementary effect; a contraction can have nonzero complementary effect without any binary-state interpretation. These examples explain why numerical agreement between four diagnostics would not make them one object. Each has a domain, codomain and defining map. Calling all of them “leakage,” “transport” or “burden” would erase premises needed by a referee to check the claim. 9. Limitations and operational checks The results depend on fixed finite carriers, unit simplex inner products and the stated event maps. The relay spectra are calculations for three complexes, not a classification of all tetrahedral complexes. Norm conservation is too weak to select the skew generator uniquely. The matching-labeled state set is a chosen representation, not a derived ontology. The receipt-conditioned map leaves constitutive dynamics open. The contribution relative to existing Hodge and graph-operator work is correspondingly narrow, and no general novelty is asserted for the standard lemmas. Referee checks. A nonzero B1B2B_1B_2 or B2B3B_2B_3 refutes the supplied chain construction. Unequal fibers under the declared pEp_E refute P3.3. A nonzero commutator refutes a claim of exact Hamming-sector preservation for that operator. Different exact nullities refute the spectral certificate. A verified positive period for the full A, B or C operator would contradict the recurrence argument; a period for one state would not. A failure of the ownership weights to sum to one refutes the stated gluing partition. These are operational internal checks. They do not require cosmological, particle or optical observations. The companion reconstruction paper supplies its own data-consistency and held-out falsifiers. 10. The original paper PDF remains unchanged; independent review of the supplement is pending.Review edition 1.0 · 16 September 2026Projective Reconstruction from Simplex Stocks and Incidence CurrentsBenjamin Walker MayesIndependent researcher ORCID: 0009-0002-5813-0724 Abstract Let a nonzero real vector be indexed by the simplices of a finite oriented complex. Squared coefficients and adjacent-degree bilinear incidence currents do not generally determine its positive ray: parity-degree rescaling preserves every current and can preserve total squared norm while changing the ray. We construct a sufficient finite reconstruction statistic consisting of normalized squared coefficients, relative signs on a spanning forest of nonzero support, and one reference sign per component. The statistic reconstructs the normalized signed vector, independently of forest choice. For the fully supported filled tetrahedron, the 28 incidence channels split into a frozen 14-edge spanning tree and 14 complementary checks. An integer alternating-path matrix maps training log-current magnitudes to held-out log-current magnitudes, yielding exact covariance pushforward without an independence assumption. The covariance describes predicted log magnitudes; it supplies neither a coverage probability nor the uncertainty of an independently measured residual without further assumptions. We state exact consistency tests, interval feasibility conditions, and the limits of the reconstruction claim. No experimental optical result is reported. 1. Problem and related work The problem is deterministic reconstruction from finite data. A state c∈ℝN\{0}c\in\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\} is indexed by oriented simplices. We wish to determine its positive ray [c]+={λc:λ>0}. [c]_+=\{\lambda c:\lambda>0\}. Unlike a real projective line, this convention distinguishes cc from −c-c. The distinction is why one absolute sign per connected support component is required. Squared coefficients determine magnitudes but lose signs. Adjacent bilinear products constrain relative signs but can leave magnitude ambiguities. A recording of measurements is useful only if the reconstruction map and its assumptions are stated. We call the resulting finite data a projective support receipt (PSR). “Sufficient statistic” here means sufficient for this deterministic reconstruction problem. No Fisher–Neyman statistical sufficiency claim is made without an additional sampling model. Graph-based recovery from relative observations has a substantial literature. Singer [1, arXiv version p. 1] explicitly describes noiseless phase recovery along a spanning tree, up to a root reference, and explains why noisy tree integration can accumulate error. Our sign propagation is the elementary two-element-group case, not a new general synchronization method. Its role here is to make the required sign data and zero-support cases explicit. The simplex-incidence graph and its operators are standard in combinatorial Hodge and Dirac constructions [2, pp. 1–2; 3, arXiv pp. 4–6]. We use the filled tetrahedron’s bipartite degree structure to expose a second ambiguity: opposite rescaling on even and odd degrees. That multiplicative ambiguity is distinct from the component sign ambiguity. Normalization by the total squared norm does not generally remove both. The contribution is the explicit reconstruction data structure on this carrier, a scoped identifiability counterexample, and a frozen-tree formulation that keeps full-state reconstruction separate from held-out magnitude prediction. Linear covariance pushforward is standard. Its useful specialization here is the exact integer matrix determined by the declared tree, together with a clear boundary between covariance and coverage. We make no priority claim for graph sign synchronization or covariance propagation in general. The companion finite-carrier paper establishes the chain conventions and exact A/B/C operators. This paper is independently readable: only the incidence signs, support graph and Euclidean norm are needed for its principal reconstruction theorem. What this paper does not claim. Algebraic consistency does not authenticate the origin of data or identify a mathematical state with a physical field. The receipt is sufficient under stated assumptions; it is not claimed globally minimal among every possible measurement design. A spanning tree is not claimed statistically optimal. Fourteen held-out channels are not fourteen independent confirmations. No device session or experimental success is reported. 2. The parity-degree identifiability obstruction 2.1 Observables and domain Let KK be a finite oriented simplicial complex. For each simplex σ\sigma, let cσc_\sigma be a real coefficient and define qσ=cσ2,S=∑σqσ>0. q_\sigma=c_\sigma^2,\qquad S=\sum_\sigma q_\sigma>0. e B, there is a nonidentity GλG_\lambda that also preserves SS and changes [c]+[c]_+. Proof. Each adjacent product gains the factor λλ−1=1\lambda\lambda^{-1}=1. Set (c0,c01)=(2,1)(c_0,c_{01})=(2,1), all other coefficients zero. The vector (1,2)(1,2) has the same total norm 5 and the same products, but a different positive ray. With the canonical boundary sign, the nonzero current is −4-4 in both cases. Even where A=BA=B, stocks and currents cannot distinguish simultaneous sign reversal on a connected support component. The theorem establishes noninjectivity of the observation map; it does not say every state has the same ambiguity. Additional metadata cannot repair it unless that metadata is specified to constrain the ambiguous state coordinates. Labels describing an event or route, by themselves, are not such a constraint. 2.2 A second ambiguity: component signs Form a graph whose vertices are simplex coordinates with qσ>0q_\sigma>0, and whose edges are their adjacent-degree incidences. Multiplying all coefficients in one connected component by minus one leaves all stocks and currents unchanged. Edges to zero coordinates still have zero current. There is therefore one undetermined common sign per connected support component. Fixing one global sign suffices only when that graph is connected. A zero coordinate can split the graph and increase the number of required reference signs. An isolated nonzero coordinate is a component and needs its own reference. 3. Suppose it agrees at uu. Since χuv=sgn(cucv)\chi_{uv}=\operatorname{sgn}(c_uc_v), multiplication gives sv=sgn(cv)s_v=\operatorname{sgn}(c_v). Induction along the unique root-to-vertex path covers each tree. Multiplying by cσ2/S\sqrt{c_\sigma^2/S} yields cσ/Sc_\sigma/\sqrt S. It does not reconstruct the unknown absolute scale SS. If SS is also supplied, multiplying by S\sqrt S recovers cc. Proposition P3.3 (exact current consistency). Every exact receipt satisfies Jστ2=4qσqτ. J_{\sigma	au}^2=4q_\sigma q_	au. On a connected nonzero graph, compatible relative signs have product one around every cycle. Conversely, positive stocks, compatible edge signs and root signs define a state realizing the corresponding signed products. Proof. The squared-current identity follows from Bστ2=1B_{\sigma	au}^2=1. A cycle product of coefficient-pair signs contains every coefficient sign twice, giving one. For the converse, propagate from a root along a tree. Cycle compatibility makes the result consistent with every non-tree edge. Multiply the assigned signs by the square roots of the stocks. ▫\square An exact packet violating the squared-current identity is rejected. Approximate measurements require the interval or probabilistic specification of Section 7; they cannot be repaired by silently relaxing this exact equation after viewing the target. 3.3 A reference-sign measurement model One possible ideal reference uses a separately calibrated real probe α≠0\alpha
e0 at a root coordinate: qr+=(cr+α)2,qr−=(cr−α)2. q_r^+=(c_r+\alpha)^2,\qquad q_r^-=(c_r-\alpha)^2. Then qr+−qr−=4αcr. q_r^+-q_r^-=4\alpha c_r. The sign of the difference relative to the known sign of α\alpha identifies the root sign. These equations describe a measurement model, not evidence that a device has implemented it. They require the same underlying state for the two probe conditions, or a validated equivalent preparation, and separate treatment of probe uncertainty. 4. Forest choice and event maps Proposition T4.1 (forest independence). Any spanning forest and root choices with data derived from the same state reconstruct the same normalized signed vector. Proof. Theorem T3.2 holds for each forest separately, with the same right-hand side. Equivalently, cycle-consistent pair signs make each path product agree with the endpoint coefficient signs. ▫\square Forest choice is therefore a serialization convention for exact data. It is sometimes called a gauge in the broader project, but it is not a physical gauge field. With noisy data, different trees can have different conditioning and uncertainty. Exact equivalence is not a claim of equal statistical performance. Let TT be the canonical zero-extension from the A complex to B, and PP the signed B-to-C isomorphism defined in Paper I. Both preserve the Euclidean norm on their source domains. Proposition P4.2 (event-level reconstruction covariance). ℛB(PSR(Tc))=TℛA(PSR(c)), \mathcal R_B(\operatorname{PSR}(Tc))=T\mathcal R_A(\operatorname{PSR}(c)), ℛC(PSR(Pc))=PℛB(PSR(c)). \mathcal R_C(\operatorname{PSR}(Pc))=P\mathcal R_B(\operatorname{PSR}(c)). Proof. Apply T3.2 to the transformed vector and use ∥Tc∥=∥c∥\|Tc\|=\|c\|, or ∥Pc∥=∥c∥\|Pc\|=\|c\|, respectively. ▫\square The statistic on the transformed state may use a newly computed forest. Its edge list need not be the image of the previous list. These are event-level reconstruction identities. They do not assert that the dimension-changing A-to-B inclusion intertwines the continuous flows; Paper I gives an explicit nonzero residual for that claim. 5. The filled tetrahedron and the frozen 14/14 split 5.1 The incidence graph The filled tetrahedron has 15 nonempty simplices: four vertices, six edges, four faces and one cell. Its graph of adjacent-degree containments has 12+12+4=28 12+12+4=28 incidences. It is connected and bipartite by simplex-degree parity. On full nonzero support, a spanning tree uses 14 incidences, leaving 14 chords. Thus 28=14tree+14heldout. 28=14_{\mathrm{tree}}+14_{\mathrm{held\ out}}. This is a channel partition. It does not mean a PSR consists only of fourteen current readings: normalized stocks and root references remain necessary for its full reconstruction theorem. The supplement supplies the ordered 28-channel list and one specific frozen tree. Channel identities, not a path-length histogram, define the split. A tree must be chosen before examining held-out measurements if they are to remain held out. 5.2 Signless incidence and the parity gauge For nonzero currents, define xσ=log|cσ|,ze=log(|Je|/2). x_\sigma=\log|c_\sigma|,\qquad z_e=\log(|J_e|/2). Then zuv=xu+xvz_{uv}=x_u+x_v. Equivalently, using log stocks would insert a factor of one half; the convention here is log amplitude. Let S∈ℤ14×15S\in\mathbb Z^{14	imes15} have a one in each of the two endpoint columns of a training incidence, and zeros elsewhere. Let HH be the analogous matrix for held-out chords. Theorem T5.1 (tree rank and its unresolved direction). The connected tree matrix SS has rank 14. Its nullspace is spanned by the parity vector pσ=(−1)dimσp_\sigma=(-1)^{\dim\sigma}. Every held-out row annihilates pp. Proof. The equation Sx=0Sx=0 forces xv=−xux_v=-x_u along each tree edge. Connectivity determines every coordinate from one root value, with sign alternating by parity. Thus the kernel is one-dimensional. Every adjacent-degree chord also has opposite-parity endpoints, so its row has zero dot product with pp. ▫\square The gauge is x↦x+tpx\mapsto x+tp, not uniform translation. Exponentiating gives opposite multiplicative scales on the two parity classes. A known root log amplitude fixes it. A total norm can admit the two values exhibited in NG2.1 and is not a generally unique substitute. 5.3 Alternating-path synthesis Theorem T5.2 (held-out magnitudes from tree data). There is a unique matrix C∈ℤ14×14C\in\mathbb Z^{14	imes14} satisfying H=CS,zH=CzT. H=CS,\qquad z_H=Cz_T. For a chord’s unique tree path, its row has alternating entries +1,−1,+1,…,+1+1,-1,+1,\ldots,+1 on the path edges, and zero elsewhere. Proof. The endpoints of a chord have opposite parity, so their tree path has odd length. In the alternating sum of endpoint-sum rows along this path, each interior vertex cancels and the two endpoints have coefficient one. This is the chord row. Uniqueness follows from independence of the 14 training rows. ▫\square For the declared split, eight paths have length 3, five have length 5 and one has length 7. The mean is exactly 4. The held-out row matrix has rank 10, checked over the rationals in the supplement. Accordingly, four of the fourteen log relations are linearly redundant. They are still useful consistency checks, but not independent evidence. The sign of a held-out coefficient product is also determined by multiplying the recorded pair signs along its path. The incidence orientation sign then determines the signed current. Root signs cancel from pair products. Full signed-vector reconstruction and signed-current prediction therefore have different reference requirements. 6. Exact covariance transport and what it does not imply Let a random training log-current estimate have a finite covariance matrix ΣT\Sigma_T. Define its predicted held-out log vector by the fixed linear map ẑH=CẑT\widehat z_H=C\widehat z_T. Proposition T6.1 (covariance pushforward). ΣHpred=CΣTCT. \Sigma_H^{\mathrm{pred}}=C\Sigma_TC^T. For rows ch,ckc_h,c_k of CC, Var(ẑh)=chΣTchT,Cov(ẑh,ẑk)=chΣTckT. \operatorname{Var}(\widehat z_h)=c_h\Sigma_Tc_h^T,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\widehat z_h,\widehat z_k)=c_h\Sigma_Tc_k^T. Proof. Center the training vector about its expectation, multiply by CC, and take the expectation of the resulting outer product. Linearity and finite second moments give the formula. ▫\square No independence or Gaussian assumption is required. If, additionally, ΣT=σ2I\Sigma_T=\sigma^2I, each predicted variance equals its path length times σ2\sigma^2. This specialization is exact for that log-space covariance model. It is not an assumption about untransformed detector readings. If the input consists of signed nonzero currents with covariance ΣJ\Sigma_J, differentiating ze=log(|Je|/2)z_e=\log(|J_e|/2) gives D=diag(1/Je)D=\operatorname{diag}(1/J_e) and the first-order approximation ΣT≈DΣJDT. \Sigma_T\approx D\Sigma_JD^T. The first-order map must not be relabeled exact. When possible, covariance estimated directly from declared transformed replicates avoids this extra approximation, although its own estimation uncertainty still remains. No-go NG6.2 (covariance is not a coverage certificate). Covariance alone does not imply that a chosen interval ẑh±kuh\widehat z_h\pm k u_h has a specified coverage probability for an unknown data-generating law. Proof. Different distributions can have the same variance and different tail probabilities. For instance, a mean-zero variable taking ±1\pm1 equally often and one taking 0 with probability 3/43/4, ±2\pm2 with probability 1/81/8 each, both have variance one but different probabilities outside [−3/2,3/2][-3/2,3/2]. ▫\square Distribution-free inequalities can provide conservative bounds under their own assumptions, but do not turn an arbitrary multiplier into an exact 95-percent interval. A coordinate condition number also supplies no such probability. It measures sensitivity of a specified inversion in specified norms. Neither κ(S)\kappa(S) nor κ(C)\kappa(C) is a substitute for a simultaneous coverage rule. Prediction covariance also differs from measurement-residual covariance. If r=z̃H−CẑTr=\widetilde z_H-C\widehat z_T, then Cov(r)=ΣHH+CΣTTCT−ΣHTCT−CΣTH. \operatorname{Cov}(r)=\Sigma_{HH}+C\Sigma_{TT}C^T -\Sigma_{HT}C^T-C\Sigma_{TH}. The cross terms vanish only under an appropriate uncorrelatedness assumption. Comparing predicted intervals to independently noisy held-out readings must account for that additional measurement uncertainty. 7. Exact consistency, uncertainty and prospective tests 7.1 Feasible sets For an exact receipt, the reconstruction theorem and squared-current constraints can be checked directly. For measurements with certified strictly positive magnitude intervals, write xσ=log|cσ|x_\sigma=\log|c_\sigma|. Stock intervals give 12logqσmin≤xσ≤12logqσmax, 	frac12\log q_\sigma^{\min}\le x_\sigma\le	frac12\log q_\sigma^{\max}, and current-magnitude intervals give log(|Je|min/2)≤xu+xv≤log(|Je|max/2). \log(|J_e|^{\min}/2)\le x_u+x_v\le\log(|J_e|^{\max}/2). Together these define a linear feasible set in log amplitudes, subject to separately compatible signs. If sign or support cannot be qualified because an interval crosses zero, this log construction is unavailable and the declared procedure returns an indeterminate result; it must not invent a sign or an epsilon cutoff after inspection. For a frozen feasible set ℱ\mathcal F, the predicted range of a held-out signed current is Ihpred={2Bhcucv:c∈ℱ}. I_h^{\mathrm{pred}}=\{2B_hc_uc_v:c\in\mathcal F\}. Optimizing the linear log-magnitude functional over the feasible set gives its endpoints before exponentiation, with the sign convention then applied. Marginal ranges alone need not guarantee a single jointly compatible state. A protocol claiming joint compatibility must use the joint feasible-set test. 7.2 A small operational decision rule Internal falsifiers. An exact receipt with Je2≠4quqvJ_e^2
e4q_uq_v is inconsistent. Incompatible products of relative signs around a cycle are inconsistent. A claimed reconstruction differing from the normalized input state refutes T3.2’s implementation. A nonzero H−CSH-CS refutes the supplied tree map. Once the training feasible set and held-out measurement model are fixed, an observed held-out vector incompatible with that set fails the declared protocol. Acceptance of the finite model on a data set is conditional on the acquisition and uncertainty assumptions. Device authentication, same-state preparation and independent scoring are external procedures. They cannot be inferred from an algebraically valid receipt, and are kept out of the mathematical sufficiency claim. A numerical noise sweep may check an implementation or illustrate a stipulated stochastic model. It is not needed for the exact map H=CSH=CS or the covariance theorem. The earlier 1,500-trial sweep is therefore omitted from this paper’s evidence for the exact claims. Any future protocol report using it should label it as a numerical check under the specified noise distribution. 8. Limits and claim table The reconstruction theorem assumes real coefficients, a correct support graph, normalized stocks and valid reference signs. Complex coefficients require phase data and a different specification. Sparse support changes both the forest and the number of references. Exact tree prediction can be sensitive to noise; the chosen tree is not claimed optimal. No redundancy count is a count of independent replications. No uncertainty model or acquisition calibration has been derived from the finite algebra. The main result is best understood as an explicit complete invariant for positive rays under a chosen observation scheme. It solves an identifiability problem after sufficient data have been supplied. It does not provide an endogenous source of those data or establish that a physical apparatus measures the intended coefficients. ID Statement Status Proof / artifact Depends on NG2.1 Currents and total norm can leave two rays No-go Quadratic equation; rational witness Both parity sectors nonzero T3.2 PSR reconstructs c/Sc/\sqrt S Theorem Forest induction; fixtures D3.1 P3.3 Current square and cycle consistency Proposition Products and sign cancellation Incidence signs T4.1 Exact forest choice is immaterial Proposition T3.2 in two forests Valid root data P4.2 Reconstruction commutes with isometries Proposition Norm identity Event isometry T5.1 Tree rank 14; parity kernel Theorem Tree propagation; exact rank Full support T5.2 H=CSH=CS, integer path map Theorem Alternating path cancellation Frozen tree T6.1 ΣH=CΣTCT\Sigma_H=C\Sigma_TC^T Standard proposition Centered outer products Finite covariance NG6.2 Covariance alone is not coverage No-go Equal-variance distributions No fixed distribution law 9. Reproduction The shared supplement includes the canonical ordered incidence list, frozen training and held-out identities, all 196 entries of CC, SS, HH, an exact finite-distribution covariance example, and signed-state fixtures with full, sparse and disconnected support. Run python verify.py with Python 3.10 or later; no third-party package is required. The checks regenerate the artifacts rather than reading a stored PASS flag. Rational arithmetic verifies matrix identities and squared amplitudes. The general square-root reconstruction follows the written proof; fixtures check its signs and normalized squared coefficients without floating-point approximation. The same package contains Paper I’s exact matrices. A package README maps each check family to its paper and states the measured runtime. Appendix A. The declared training tree Here vv, ee, ff, and tt label a vertex, edge, face and tetrahedron, respectively. The fourteen tree incidences, in their frozen order, are Index Training incidence Index Training incidence 1 v0–e01 8 v1–e13 2 v1–e01 9 v2–e23 3 v0–e02 10 e01–f012 4 v2–e02 11 e01–f013 5 v0–e03 12 e02–f023 6 v3–e03 13 e12–f123 7 v1–e12 14 f012–t0123 The complementary chord list is e12–v2, e13–v3, e23–v3, e02–f012, e12–f012, e03–f013, e13–f013, e03–f023, e23–f023, e13–f123, e23–f123, f013–t0123, f023–t0123, f123–t0123. Reversing the written order of endpoints here does not change a signless row; the boundary orientation used for signed currents remains fixed by the simplex bases. For example, the chord v2–e12 follows the path v2–e02–v0–e01–v1–e12. Its prediction is zv2,e12=zv2,e02−zv0,e02+zv0,e01−zv1,e01+zv1,e12. z_{v2,e12}=z_{v2,e02}-z_{v0,e02}+z_{v0,e01}-z_{v1,e01}+z_{v1,e12}. Every interior log amplitude cancels. Jost, “Spectra of combinatorial Laplace operators on simplicial complexes,” Advances in Mathematics 244, 303–336 (2013). doi:10.1016/j.aim.2013.05.007; arXiv:1105.2712, pp. 4–6. [4] B. W. Running the script with a different Python version may change the environment field in the results; keep the original release separate if preserving its hashes. Definitions Use one basis vector per unique simplex, sorted lexicographically by increasing vertex labels within each degree. Shared simplices occur once. The inner product is Euclidean with unit simplex weights. For an oriented simplex, [ k[v_0,,v_k] ={j=0}k(-1)j[v_0,,v_j,,v_k]. ] Let (B_k) be its boundary matrix, and let (d) be the degree-raising block operator with (B_k^) in degree ((k-1)k). Define [ D=d+d,A=d-d,L=D2=-A2. ] The last identity uses (d^2=0), checked through (B_1B_2=B_2B_3=0). The complexes, specified by their maximal tetrahedra, are: [ K_A=,0124, K_B=,0124,0134, K_C=,0234,1234. ] The September note’s (K_-) is A and its (K_+) is C. Exact replay results Complex Simplex counts Boundary ranks Laplacian eigenvalues (multiplicities) Skew characteristic polynomial A (5,9,7,2) (4,5,2) 0 (1), 3 (8), 5 (14) ((2+3)4(2+5)7) B (5,10,9,3) (4,6,3) 0 (1), 2 (4), 5 (22) ((2+2)2(2+5){11}) C (5,10,9,3) (4,6,3) 0 (1), 2 (4), 5 (22) ((2+2)2(2+5){11}) All three reconstructed boundary systems obey the chain identities. The verifier uses exact rational row reduction, not floating-point eigenvalue fitting. The eigenspace dimensions exhaust the relevant chain-space dimensions. Grading anticommutation checks supply the paired real Dirac multiplicities; real skew symmetry supplies conjugate imaginary pairs. Implementation note for reviewers: the original script describes its Gershgorin step as applying to a “symmetric nonnegative matrix.” Here the needed condition is positive semidefiniteness, not entrywise nonnegativity. It follows from (L=D2=DD). The absolute row-sum bound and exact nullity exhaustion remain applicable to these integer matrices. The comment is retained unchanged in the source snapshot. The spectrum result is a finite benchmark under these inner products. This package does not establish novelty or generalize the factors to arbitrary weighted complexes. Continuity identity: short proof and execution evidence For real amplitudes (c) evolving by (c=Ac) and a fixed subset R of the simplex coordinates, define [ S_R(c)={iR}c_i^2. ] Since (A^=-A), [ =2{iR,j}c_iA_{ij}c_j =2{iR,jR}A{ij}c_ic_j. ] The terms with both indices in R cancel in pairs, including zero diagonal terms. This argument applies to every R and every real state. For the full coordinate set, the derivative is zero. With outgoing signed current (J_{ij}=2A_{ji}c_ic_j), the same statement is [ =-{iR,jR}J{ij}. ] These are signed mathematical currents; no physical energy, action, clock or material carrier is identified. The supplemental verifier compares exact coefficients of these quadratic polynomials, rather than sampling numeric amplitudes: - A: 31 scheduled regions; - B: 35 scheduled regions; - C: 35 scheduled regions. The regions include the empty/full sets, every singleton, each complete degree, and two mixed cuts. The script does not enumerate all subsets; the proof above covers the general identity. Frozen face gates For each of A’s 128 binary face masks, the supplement masks the rows of (B_3), then rebuilds both transposed operator blocks with the same mask. All 128 masked generators remain skew and pass the same 31 scheduled continuity-region checks. Scope: fixed-mask continuity only. Row-masking (B_3) can destroy the chain identity (B_2B_3=0); the gated systems are not asserted to retain the original Hodge factorization or spectrum. These controls show that the selected checks detect these specific errors. They do not establish comprehensive fault coverage. Recurrence scope The source note’s absence of a positive exact full-operator period follows from the simultaneous frequencies (,) for A and (,) for B/C. Their ratios are irrational: the prime exponents in (5/3) and (5/2) are not all even, so neither ratio is a rational square. This is an analytic consequence of the exact spectral certificate, not a numerical search over time. Stationary states and single-frequency periodic states remain possible; approximate recurrences are not excluded. The script does not verify this corollary in a formal proof assistant. Run from the complete release package; imports its preserved historical verifier. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact replay supplement. Standard library only; no independent peer review."""
import importlib.util
import json
import platform
import sys
from fractions import Fraction as Q
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SOURCE = ROOT / 'sources' / 'verify_bistellar_hodge_dirac_note_v1_2.py'
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('historical_verifier', SOURCE)
v = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(v)

def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(message)

def assemble(tets):
    simplices = v.closure(tets)
    dims = [len(simplices[k]) for k in range(4)]
    boundaries = [v.boundary(simplices[k-1], simplices[k]) for k in range(1,4)]
    return simplices, dims, boundaries, v.block_operator(boundaries, dims, True)

def quadratic_coefficients(A, selected):
    # Coefficients of d/ds sum_{i in R} c_i^2, for arbitrary real c.
    coefficients = {}
    for i in selected:
        for j, a in enumerate(A[i]):
            key = tuple(sorted((i,j)))
            coefficients[key] = coefficients.get(key,Q(0)) + 2*a
    return {k:a for k,a in coefficients.items() if a}

def cut_coefficients(A, selected):
    coefficients = {}
    for i in selected:
        for j,a in enumerate(A[i]):
            if j not in selected:
                key = tuple(sorted((i,j)))
                coefficients[key] = coefficients.get(key,Q(0)) + 2*a
    return {k:a for k,a in coefficients.items() if a}

def check_continuity(A, dims):
    n = len(A)
    require(v.add(A,v.transpose(A)) == v.zeros(n,n), 'skew symmetry failed')
    require(not quadratic_coefficients(A,set(range(n))), 'global norm derivative nonzero')
    regions = [set(),set(range(n))] + [{i} for i in range(n)]
    offset = 0
    for d in dims:
        regions.append(set(range(offset,offset+d)))
        offset += d
    regions += [set(range(n//2)), {0,n-1}]
    for region in regions:
        require(quadratic_coefficients(A,region)==cut_coefficients(A,region),
                'polynomial cut identity failed')
    return len(regions)

def main():
    require(__debug__, 'Run without -O: historical verifier uses assertions')
    cases = {'A':v.K_MINUS,
             'B':[(0,1,2,3),(0,1,2,4),(0,1,3,4)],
             'C':v.K_PLUS}
    expected = {'A':([5,9,7,2],{0:1,3:8,5:14}),
                'B':([5,10,9,3],{0:1,2:4,5:22}),
                'C':([5,10,9,3],{0:1,2:4,5:22})}
    results = {}
    matrices = {}
    for name,tets in cases.items():
        result = v.verify(name,tets)
        require(result['dims']==expected[name][0], 'unexpected simplex count')
        require(result['laplacian_spectrum']==expected[name][1], 'spectrum mismatch')
        simplices,dims,boundaries,A = assemble(tets)
        result['polynomial_cut_regions_checked'] = check_continuity(A,dims)
        result['arbitrary_real_amplitude_identity'] = 'PASS within the tested regions'
        results[name] = result
        matrices[name] = {'simplices':simplices,
                          'boundaries':[[[int(x) for x in row] for row in b] for b in boundaries],
                          'skew_operator':[[int(x) for x in row] for row in A]}

    simplices,dims,boundaries,A = assemble(cases['A'])
    mask_count = 0
    for mask in range(1 << dims[2]):
        gated = [[x for x in row] for row in boundaries[2]]
        for f in range(dims[2]):
            if not ((mask >> f) & 1):
                gated[f] = [Q(0) for _ in gated[f]]
        Ag = v.block_operator(boundaries[:2]+[gated],dims,True)
        check_continuity(Ag,dims)
        mask_count += 1
    # Frozen face gates preserve skew symmetry. No gate-transition law is inferred.

    broken = [row[:] for row in A]
    edge = dims[0]
    require(broken[0][edge] != 0,'mutation location must be an incidence')
    broken[0][edge] *= -1
    bad_norm = quadratic_coefficients(broken,set(range(len(A))))
    require(bool(bad_norm), 'one-sided sign mutation was not detected')
    bad_b2 = [row[:] for row in boundaries[1]]
    bad_b2[0][0] *= -1
    require(v.matmul(boundaries[0],bad_b2)!=v.zeros(dims[0],dims[2]),
            'boundary mutation was not detected')
    local_direct_sum_dimension = sum(sum(len(x) for x in v.closure([t]).values()) for t in cases['A'])
    require(local_direct_sum_dimension==30 and sum(dims)==23,
            'shared-simplex duplication control failed')

    output = {'status':'PASS','python':platform.python_version(),
              'scope':'Exact finite replay; constructor/self-check, not formal verification or independent peer review',
              'cases':results,'frozen_A_face_masks_checked':mask_count,
              'negative_controls':{
                  'one_sided_operator_sign_flip':{'detected':True,'norm_derivative_coefficients':{str(k):str(a) for k,a in bad_norm.items()}},
                  'single_boundary_incidence_sign_flip':{'detected':True},
                  'cell_local_duplicate_assembly':{'detected':True,'wrong_dimension':30,'unique_simplex_dimension':23}},
              'physical_promotion':0}
    out = ROOT / 'results'
    out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (out/'replay_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(output,indent=2)+'\n')
    (out/'exact_matrices.json').write_text(json.dumps(matrices,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps(output,indent=2))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

What incidence determines For a supplied labeled tetrahedral complex, define its potential face-contact graph by connecting two distinct tetrahedra precisely when their vertex sets intersect in three vertices. Put p=(0,1,2,3),q=(0,1,3,2), p=(0,1,2,3),\qquad q=(0,1,3,2), and use contacts e=(0,1,p,p,+1), f=(0,2,q,p,+1). The derivative of each readiness coefficient is zero in every direction at this preparation: for g=zᵀPz/(zᵀFz), Pz=Fz=z gives ∇g=0; for the other channel Pz=0 and g=0 also gives ∇g=0. Thus the bracket at this state can be calculated from the fixed standard-channel matrices, without assuming the full two-contact trajectory keeps constant gates. Let C be the signed chart matrix of q and B the standard face channel. Then BCBv=−2v,C𝖳=C. B C Bv=-2v,\qquad C^{\mathsf T}=C. This is an obstruction to universal interchange of sequential exact contact subflows on distinct central faces, not only repeated use of one face. A conservative conflict relation for this candidate therefore connects contact occurrences sharing an endpoint copy. Its graph is the line graph of the contact graph. Disjoint endpoint sets guarantee commutation because each contact field depends on and changes only its two endpoint copies. Overlap is a conservative dependency warning, not proof that every overlapping pair fails at every preparation. More permissive independence requires a separate operator proof on the admitted domain. Symmetry obstruction to exclusive progress Add the following conditional round contract, without adopting it as native UD: A deterministic selector uses the complete current preparation and supplied candidate contacts. Selection is covariant under copy relabeling and signed tetrahedral chart changes. A round executes at most one contact incident to any copy. In the legal geometry above, reflect central vertices2 and3 and exchange the leaves, including their external apex labels4 and5. The corresponding signed chart action fixes v, the leaf exchange fixes their equal states, and both prepared polarities are positive. The full preparation is unchanged while e and f are exchanged. For any deterministic equivariant selector S and any symmetry σ that fixes its input X, S(X)=S(σX)=σS(X). S(X)=S(\sigma X)=\sigma S(X). The selected set must therefore be invariant under the input stabilizer. Here the only invariant subsets are ∅ and {e,f}. The former violates progress; the latter violates per-copy exclusivity. No nonempty exclusive invariant selection exists. Enumeration retains all four subsets; this is not a best-fit choice. NO-GO scope: these four additional requirements cannot all hold at this symmetric checkpoint. This is not a contradiction of the source theory and does not rule out every admission mechanism. It identifies which requirement must change or which new sourced data must break the symmetry. Candidate escape Extra source obligation or changed assumption Admit both as one simultaneous batch Explicit batch admission, event grouping and simultaneous field contract; no exclusive round Return no event Explicit contact-domain hold/defer rule and liveness conditions; do not reuse Theta hold without a bridge Use distinct pre-event histories or priorities Their state carrier, provenance, covariance and selection rule; equality must still be handled Use covariant stochastic arbitration A stochastic primitive/protocol and law; distributional covariance is different from deterministic covariance Treat identifiers as a physical priority A source-defined ordering role for those identifiers; numeric serialization labels alone do not supply it A sorted contact list is used only to serialize the diagnostic output. Its ordering is not a derived dynamical priority. Fair service can establish liveness for a declared scheduling model, but does not select that model, a physical rate or an event clock. 5. After consistent records have been merged, the associated amplitude fields can still fail to commute. AUTO_FREEZE applies to stronger native formation, universal order independence, binding and physical claims. The supplied two-copy readiness rule extends consistently to a fixed contact graph if every contact retains signed endpoint charts and reciprocal cross blocks. Total support and global continuation survive. Universal pair-sector conservation and arbitrary sequential contact-order independence do not survive. Extending the graph does not add dissipative selection. 1. Source and new choices Parent archive: UD_SEED_CAPABLE_FACE_READINESS_v0.1_RELEASE.zip, SHA-256 9cc55d9c93665ee2fa3693e77839ee6a4ab0cc6c762dbeccef72e545326f9bc3. Copied seed_runtime.py and exact_gluing.py retain their original bytes. This packet retains hashes for those files, the original parent archive, and this audit’s frozen protocol. Each copy retains all 15 real coordinates of a filled tetrahedron and the unit inner product. There are 15n coordinates, including independently stored coordinates on corresponding faces. This is not the unique-simplex glued chain space. Copies, contacts, face correspondence, charts and polarity are supplied data. An empty amplitude copy already exists; populating it is not creating a carrier. The new witness choice is simultaneous summation of the parent’s contact contributions over a fixed finite graph, with inherited flow applied once per copy. It does not follow as a selected native law from the pair audit. It preserves the parent’s face-support denominator and identity coefficient response, themselves supplied choices. No threshold, denominator regularizer, fit or physical rate is added. PROTOCOL_v0.1.md was written before the verifier’s first execution. The graphs, generic rational preparation and obstruction preparations were declared there before probing. Exact fixtures test identities, without matching an empirical target. 2. Endpoint charts and reciprocal contact law Let A=Dᵀ−D for one copy, and let B01,B12 be the parent’s skew channels on reference face012. Let F be its seven-coordinate face projector. The channels satisfy B_jᵀB_j=3P_j, where P01 and P12 are orthogonal projectors of ranks4 and2, and P01+P12≤F. Each edge e={i,k} supplies signed permutation charts C_i,e and C_k,e on the full 15 coordinates. The reference vertices012 map to corresponding ordered endpoint-face vertices; vertex3 maps to the local apex. Signed simplex maps include the sign of the induced permutation on each simplex. Thus CᵀC=I and AC=CA in the local ascending basis. Put u=C_i,eᵀx_i, v=C_k,eᵀx_k and define Te=∥Fu∥2+∥Fv∥2,Re,j=∥Bju∥2+∥Bjv∥23. T_e=\|Fu\|^2+\|Fv\|^2,\qquad R_{e,j}=\frac{\|B_ju\|^2+\|B_jv\|^2}{3}. Set g_e,j=R_e,j/T_e for T_e>0 and zero otherwise. Then 0≤g_e,j and g_e,01+g_e,12≤1. With prepared constant χ_e∈{−1,+1}, write Kik,e=Ci,e(ge,01B01+ge,12B12)Ck,e𝖳. K_{ik,e}=C_{i,e}(g_{e,01}B_{01}+g_{e,12}B_{12})C_{k,e}^{\mathsf T}. The candidate field is xi′=Axi+∑e={i,k}χeKik,exk,χe′=0. x_i'=Ax_i+\sum_{e=\{i,k\}}\chi_e K_{ik,e}x_k,\qquad \chi_e'=0. Scope of the collective comparison The retained star and two chain representatives each have four tetrahedra, seven vertices, fifteen unique edges, and three compatible closure classes A/B/C. Each class contains five unique edges and one opposite-edge pair in every cell. The representatives are histories 0, 1, and 4 in the frozen carrier census. All comparisons here use passing integrity and singleton current-state scores in a fixed one-closed-class sector. These conditions define the test scope; conservation does not derive the chosen closure budget. For edge weight w_e = (b_i - b_j)^2, define the global class coefficient W_p = sum[e in class p] w_e. The unique-edge Q162 relaxation score for class p closed is R_p = (sum(W) - W_p)/4. Therefore its conditional optimum closes a class of minimum global coefficient. The optimal endpoint set retains all exact ties. The strict diagnostic wrapper requests a different class only when that minimum is unique. It does not automatically apply to the whole assembly. Imposing a global objective requires a collective authorization and publication rule in addition to a compatible target. A global preference can appear while every cell is tied Prepare a uniform burden plus a localized contrast: b = a*1 + h*e_v, with h nonzero and burdens nonnegative. In a cell containing v, exactly one edge of each opposite pair is incident on v. Every local pair score is therefore h^2. A cell not containing v has three zero pair scores. Every local cell returns NO_EVENT under the strict address rule, for every baseline closure class. The unique-edge global coefficient is instead W_p = h^2*d_p(v), where d_p(v) counts class-p edges incident on v. Those class degrees need not agree. The assembly can therefore create a strict global objective preference without creating a local event receipt. content: Norm-preserving local rotations give an unambiguous same-history lift under full shared-face observation. Real amplitude, step, schedule, launch, embedding and clock remain supplied choices. The top-sector construction is not a full physical propagation law. Physical promotion 0; independent review pending. Recovered source, original scientific status preserved. Norm-preserving local rotations give an unambiguous same-history lift under full shared-face observation. Real amplitude, step, schedule, launch, embedding and clock remain supplied choices. The top-sector construction is not a full physical propagation law. Constructor replay passed; independent review remains pending; physical promotion 0.UD collective four face history lift audit A collective rotation of each tetrahedron’s amplitude and its four oriented face amplitudes gives a connected candidate that preserves locality, source-independent event ordering, and the original squared-amplitude norm. It repairs the specific failures of the previous overlapping two-coordinate assignment. Its small-step aggregate recovers the native face-and-tetrahedron generator and its tetrahedron-based acoustic branch, whose leading metric is compatible with the supplied BCC embedding. This is a conditional construction, not a source-derived law. The current binary event branch does not supply its real amplitude state, rational rotation, step size, launch, or aggregate schedule. The new replay passes 53 exact checks and 730 numerical checks, including five directions for every one of the 720 six-type schedules. Physical promotion remains 0. Exact algebra and finite sampling have different scopes throughout this report. Operator from the oriented four face boundary For tetrahedron t, let b_t be its column in the oriented boundary matrix B3. Its four entries are signs of unit magnitude, so b_t* b_t=4. Let f contain the face amplitudes and u the tetrahedron amplitudes. Define J_t by coupling only u_t and b_t: J_t(f,u) = (-b_t u_t, e_t b_t* f) J_t* = -J_t J_t³ = -4 J_t Here e_t selects that tetrahedron’s coordinate, and star denotes adjoint. For a supplied real step ε, choose the local rational rotation: U_t(ε) = I + [ε/(1+ε²)] J_t + [ε²/(2(1+ε²))] J_t² It is the Cayley transform of J_t. On the normalized pair (b_t/2,u_t), its cosine is (1-ε²)/(1+ε²) and its sine is 2ε/(1+ε²). Therefore U_t*U_t=I for every real ε. There is no stability restriction on this local rotation and no modified norm is needed. The rational formula is an added choice. The decomposition J_t uses the inspected chain incidence grammar, while choosing Cayley evolution and a common ε does not follow from that grammar. No value is fitted to a physical target. The ε=1/8 exact witness and refinement resolutions are computational controls. Locality and chain closure U_t changes only the four face coordinates in b_t and the cell coordinate u_t. It leaves every other coordinate unchanged, including disconnected spectators. Its face-to-face terms stay within the same tetrahedral star; a stage spans at most two face-cell incidence hops. The boundary identity B2B3=0 gives B2b_t=0. Hence every update leaves B2f unchanged and preserves the subspace f in the image of B3. Together with arbitrary tetrahedron amplitudes, that subspace is the native top coexact sector. The original full chain generator preserves it as well: the edge update from such f vanishes because B2f=0. The replay verifies these identities exactly on a connected five-tetrahedron witness and verifies the periodic Laurent boundary and column-norm identities. The periodic columns each use four distinct face types. Thus translates of one tetrahedron type form disjoint update stars and can be grouped into one matching layer. Causal history lift Use the inspected readiness, binary flip, and active recording-buffer rules with every shared face observed. Two different tetrahedra that share no face have disjoint amplitude update supports. Their U operators commute exactly. Tetrahedra sharing a face have overlapping operations; the source’s full observed-face buffers order their commits and preserve that order in receipt parents. For a supplied initial amplitude c0 and a complete retained causal event set E, apply the actors’ U operators in any linear order consistent with its parent relation. Incomparable events cannot share a face under the full observation contract. Exchanging adjacent incomparable events therefore exchanges commuting operators and leaves the result unchanged. Since any two linear orders of the same finite partial order can be connected by such exchanges, this defines an unambiguous formal amplitude Φ(E). Appending an enabled commit applies its U_t, preparations leave amplitude unchanged in this proposed lift, and each commit still contributes one source event unit. The real amplitude state or the retained history carries phase information that the recurrent binary state lacks. The previous current-control obstruction remains valid; this construction escapes it by explicitly adding that information. The proposed amplitude update occurs at commit and publication. An observer can replay only its parent-closed known event set, which may lag published evolution. Readiness and pending buffers still govern source enablement; Φ alone is not a complete source state or a claim of instantaneous global knowledge. The exact source witness has a central tetrahedron and four neighbors, one across each face. All 24 leaf orders followed by the center give the same retained causal record and the same amplitude, using a dense rational launch. The replay also checks the complete operator commutators, not only this launch. The norm identity applies to every amplitude. This lift does not turn the binary receipts into measurements of real amplitudes. Given the extra law and launch, actors inferred from receipts can determine a mathematical replay. A physical amplitude measurement, state implementation, precision policy, and receipt accounting interpretation remain open. Full observation is a material condition An arbitrary identifying subgraph is insufficient for this operator family. Three tetrahedra can form a triangle in their full dual graph while the observed graph is only a three-actor path. The path has nonempty, distinct actor signatures and meets the source’s component-size condition. Its endpoint actors use disjoint observed buffers, yet their tetrahedra share an unobserved face. Their U operators do not commute. The replay constructs this triangle and checks the nonzero commutator exactly. A lift that relies on source independence must therefore observe every amplitude-sharing face, introduce separately justified dependencies, or change the operator support. Full observation is an admitted choice here, not an internally selected detector graph. Its buffers retain the source’s backpressure; the construction does not claim passive observation. Aggregate native generator Summing the collective generators gives precisely the native top block: A23 = sum_t J_t = [[0, -B3], [B3*, 0]] u_double_dot = -B3* B3 u For the periodic six-tetrahedron translation cell, supply a palindromic schedule: the six type layers in order, followed by the reverse order. Each layer uses U_t(δ/2). A full macro update Sδ consequently has: Sδ = I + δ A23 + δ² A23²/2 + O(δ³) The exact replay checks both coefficients at the zero character and one nontrivial sign character. The general result follows from consistent first-order generators and the symmetric composition: the palindrome makes the quadratic coefficient half the square of their sum. Each factor conserves the original norm, so the complete macro update does too. The schedule is supplied. On a proper finite periodic carrier with N translation cells, it contains 12 actor-type layers and 12N individually completed commits. The appearance of δ/2 in an amplitude operation does not make a fractional event tick: every commit counts one. Neither 12 layers nor 12N activity units are automatically a native or physical duration. A complete macro layer ordering is an additional contract beyond the source’s local readiness and buffer rules. Which propagation branch survives This construction addresses the face-and-tetrahedron sector, not all 26 chain coordinates. Its native top Laplacian has one acoustic branch and five optical pairs at generic nonzero wavevector. At the zero character it has five oscillating pairs and eight stationary coordinates in the full 18-dimensional top block. The aggregate retains the stationary dimension in the exact checked characters, but its stationary cell vector differs from the native one at finite δ. The prior full-mode audit gives the leading top squared frequency Q/24, where Q=qᵀ(2I+2J)q. Under the previously supplied embedding E=4^(-1/3)(J-2I), the long-wavelength continuum squared speed is κ/24, with κ=2^(5/3). It is 0.132283420997 in the declared units, or speed 0.363707878657. It is slower than the vertex branch by the factor 1/√24. A common shape does not make those speeds equal. Extending these operators as identity on degree zero and one coordinates leaves a vertex-only amplitude readout unchanged. A state launched solely in this top sector stays invisible to the prior vertex array. Binary face mismatch receipts identify event actors but do not replace a face or cell amplitude readout. This is a concrete observation requirement for using the branch, not evidence for a physical field identification. Finite resolution and schedule scan All 720 permutations of the six type layers were tested at macro δ=1/8, wave magnitude 0.0002, and five Cartesian directions after applying E. The sampled squared speeds range from 0.132282075280 to 0.132282579917. Within any tested schedule, the largest directional spread is about 3.23 times 10^-11. These numerical samples support compatibility with the BCC long-wavelength metric shape; they are not an exact proof of isotropy for arbitrary wavevector or schedule. Different dependent schedules have different exact macro operators, despite equal total commit counts. Their sampled common speeds also differ slightly. Those schedules correspond to different ordered causal histories, so this is not a failure of the same-history commutation theorem. It shows why counts alone do not specify amplitude evolution and why a schedule cannot be silently imported as a selected clock. For the displayed order 0,1,2,3,4,5 and its reverse: Macro δ One-step operator error at declared nonzero q Departure of native normalized cell harmonic vector at q=0 1/8 0.000909120416 0.000643239026 1/16 0.000114044055 0.000080657496 1/32 0.000014268189 0.000010090101 Both errors decrease by approximately eight when δ halves, as expected for a cubic local error. The native cell harmonic representative is changed, although an eight-dimensional stationary space remains at q=0. Thus a finite-step macro is not exactly the native continuous flow. A controlled refinement limit Each J_t has operator norm 2. Replacing its Cayley half-step by the corresponding exponential costs at most δ³/12, using the angle bound |2 atan(x)-2x|≤2|x|³/3. Twelve factors cost at most δ³ by unitary telescoping. The exponential palindrome and exp(δA23) have equal terms through degree two. Bounding their Taylor tails by the sum of generator norms gives: ||Sδ - exp(δA23)|| ≤ [1 + 576 exp(12|δ|)] |δ|³ This bound is intentionally loose; at the displayed larger resolutions it is much larger than the measured error. It is useful for establishing the refinement order and does not estimate an experimental tolerance. Supply spatial scale a and the same type of refinement clock Δt=aδ used previously. At an integer-step horizon t=n aδ, unitary telescoping gives: ||Sδ^n - exp(nδA23)|| ≤ [1 + 576 exp(12|δ|)] |t| δ²/a Therefore δ²/a tending to zero is a sufficient joint-refinement condition. The declared example δ=a meets it. This preserves convergence to the native top flow and then its low-wavevector BCC branch under the separately supplied embedding and clock. Neither refinement relation nor its units are derived from the source’s commit count. Every macro update has a strict support bound of at most 24 face-cell incidence hops. Under Δt=aδ, this bound does not provide a uniform physical speed as δ tends to zero. The bound alone does not prove that no sharper cone exists; a uniform cone or appropriate observable-tail statement needs a separate analysis. No Lorentzian or relativistic causal interpretation is established. Source selection remains open Two compatible local laws already demonstrate nonuniqueness: U_t(ε) and U_t(ε/2) squared both conserve the norm, stay in the same star, preserve chain closure, commute for nonadjacent cells, and have the same first derivative J_t. They differ exactly at finite ε. The replay verifies this alternative. Four-face incidence and these compatibility gates do not select the rational law or its scale. The binary field is also not simply the sign of the new cell amplitude. With cell amplitude 1 and face amplitudes zero, a commit at ε=1/8 gives cell amplitude 63/65, still positive, while the declared source binary bit flips. This exactly rejects that particular sign identification. The source defines x as a binary decoration, so it does not require the rejected sign map in the first place; any alternative readout map needs its own law. Zero real amplitude remains zero under every rotation while the source can still perform binary commits. Consequently, event counts and a nonzero wave launch are not linked by this construction alone. The source needs an amplitude initialization or resource and readiness relationship before commits can be interpreted as amplitude-driven occurrences. Admission requirement This audit Remaining obligation Connected local operators Constructed from oriented four-face columns Justify the operator as a native commit action Common conserved support Original unit norm conserved exactly Identify its source meaning and amplitude readout Independent event ordering Formal lift is well-defined with full shared-face observation Derive or admit that graph and memory contract Aggregate wave structure Native top generator recovered to second order Select event grouping and schedule; audit finite resolution Other branches Top acoustic branch shares the conditional BCC metric Full four-branch law and a common physical interpretation remain open State and enablement Real amplitudes provide the missing phase state Tie binary decoration and readiness to amplitudes or retained resources Metric and time Embedding and refinement clock supplied Independent metric selection and empirical correspondence remain open The next bounded source target is the state-and-enablement relationship: whether an inspected support, burden, or resource law ties real face and cell amplitudes to readiness and the binary interface record. If no such map is supplied, retain this as a formal history lift with an explicit new axiom rather than a derived UD mechanism. The global scale and schedule questions remain independent. Replay and scope Run python verify_ud_collective_face_rotation_v0_1.py --out replay_results with NumPy and the three unchanged helper files beside it. Their complete prior audits are not rerun. The release preserves source bytes, candidate choices, exact certificates, numerical samples, rejected interpretations, and a SHA256 manifest. The inspected minimum time model v0.11 was checked again against its current retained source, which continues to distinguish the real chain and binary event branches. No canonical source was amended. The construction and its general algebraic proofs concern internal mathematical compatibility. The 720-schedule scan is finite numerical evidence at a declared wave magnitude, not a proof of all-wavevector symmetry. No independent review, physical experiment, duration calibration, or external physical correspondence is promoted. content: Sixteen scoped statements and proofs with preserved source releases. Constructor replay passed; independent review pending. Correspondence not proposed; physical promotion 0. Download supplement and nine original replay packages · Typed claim register · Dependency hashes · Release SHA-256UD public theorem supplement Version 1.0 · 3 October 2026 · Benjamin Walker Mayes This supplement promotes the scoped mathematical results below into the public theorem layer at Benjamin Mayes’s explicit direction. It extends the public review surface beyond Papers I–II without changing their frozen PDFs, original releases, source proposals, or coefficient ledger. Constructor proofs and replays are available; independent review is pending. Publication is not a completed CRL review or empirical validation. Physical promotion remains 0. Each statement has three independent fields: internal claim bin EXACT_CONDITIONAL_MATHEMATICAL_RESULT, correspondence status NOT_PROPOSED, physical promotion 0. The publication status is PUBLIC_THEOREM_SUPPLEMENT. A theorem conditional on a proposed primitive proves an implication; it does not admit that primitive as bedrock. Original candidate/development labels remain visible in the preserved sources. The equations use dimensionless source or apparatus units. Observer grids, programmed gates, apparatus scales, initial carriers and supplied resources retain their declared roles. Assertion counts measure replay coverage, not scientific confidence or independent evidence. Public statements and proofs PT01 — The four-vertex projection fixes a tetrahedral frame For P=I−𝟏𝟏T/4P=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/4, the projected coordinate vectors satisfy P2=PP^2=P, squared norms 3/43/4, distinct inner products −1/4-1/4, and pair cosine −1/3-1/3 in the three-dimensional zero-sum subspace. Proof. Multiply the projector and inspect its diagonal and off-diagonal entries. Dividing −1/4-1/4 by 3/43/4 gives the cosine. This is a representation theorem conditional on four coordinates; it supplies neither their creation nor a physical embedding or radius. Dependency: shape screen. PT02 — Capped coface extension terminates at a unique multiplicity class For an alphabet of size qq, counts ci∈{0,1,2}c_i\in\{0,1,2\}, and the proposed rule that every extension adds one vertex of an unsaturated label and connects it to the existing simplex, every maximal extension-only history terminates after D=∑i(2−ci)D=\sum_i(2-c_i) steps at (2,…,2)(2,\ldots,2). Its terminal simplex has 2q2q vertices and dimension 2q−12q-1; the binary case gives balanced K4K_4. Proof. Every legal step decreases the nonnegative integer deficit by one. A positive deficit always leaves a legal label. At zero deficit no extension is legal. Idling or interposed retraction is outside the statement. The alphabet and cap are assumptions, and A3 remains a proposed primitive. Dependency: native shape growth. PT03 — Fresh boundary growth preserves a ball but selects no unique cluster Beginning with one tetrahedron, repeatedly attach a tetrahedron along exactly one boundary triangle using a fresh vertex. After mm cells, the complex is a stacked three-ball with f=(m+3,3m+3,3m+1,m),|∂2|=2m+2.f=(m+3,3m+3,3m+1,m),\qquad |\partial_2|=2m+2. Its face-dual graph is a tree. Under the balanced binary restoration rule, every frontier triangle has a unique restoring label. Both a four-cell chain and a four-cell star are legal from the same seed; no finite stopping size follows from extension alone. Proof. A step adds (1,3,3,1)(1,3,3,1) simplices, preserves Euler characteristic, replaces one boundary triangle by three, and adds one dual leaf. Boundary gluing preserves the ball. The replay supplies chain/star witnesses with degree lists (1,1,2,2)(1,1,2,2) and (1,1,1,3)(1,1,1,3), which cannot be isomorphic. Since 2m+2>02m+2>0, further extension remains possible.
