content: Scoped exact mathematics is promoted through PT01–PT16. Native primitive admission and empirical claims remain separate; independent review pending; physical promotion 0. Preserved source release. Its historical development status remains unchanged. Scoped results are now stated in the public theorem supplement; independent review is pending and physical promotion remains 0.UD shape selection and clustering evidence 2026-10-02, America/Chicago. Development research. Independent review pending. Internal claim bin: CANDIDATE_DEVELOPMENT_MATHEMATICS. Correspondence status: NOT_PROPOSED. Physical promotion: 0. The research focus is now which configurations UD selects from alternatives, rather than whether a chosen cube supports compatible dynamics. The cube remains one comparison carrier. Its dispersion work is deferred while the selection mechanism is investigated. The first exact screen identifies tetrahedral directions forced by the active four-vertex projection and distinguishes several propagation and closure motifs. It does not identify a shape that the inspected dynamics naturally assembles or attracts. That distinction is the starting result, not a conclusion about every historical UD model. What counts as a shape discovery Three objects must be recorded independently. An activity pattern is a distribution of chain amplitudes or event counts on a supplied carrier. A cluster is a collection of cells with a recorded incidence structure. A metric shape additionally has lengths, angles and an embedding. A pattern moving across an existing cube does not establish cube formation. For this programme, “snaps to” means an admitted rule maps a range of different initial states to the same configuration class, or produces attraction toward that class. A cluster formation claim requires an actual creation, deletion, attachment or rearrangement transition, or an explicitly defined emergent activity cluster. These are proposed operational definitions for testing; they are not new UD laws. A preferred motif must outperform declared alternatives under the same rule and preparation ensemble. Relabeling covariance, robustness to perturbation and independence from a chosen drawing or display threshold are required checks. No geometric ranking, damping, energy minimization or attachment preference is introduced merely to obtain a desired shape. Evidence stages Stage Question Current evidence Status 0 Source admissibility Which variables and transitions can change shape? Inspected fixed chain flow and phase-agreement commits retain the supplied incidence. The manuscript explicitly leaves spatial genesis open. Tested scope established; growth law not identified 1 Primitive geometry Does a local rule force geometric relations? The active four-vertex projection fixes equal directional norms and pair cosine −1/3. Exact conditional representation result 2 Coupling and propagation Which supplied attachments communicate activity? Face-shared top cells couple. Vertex- and edge-shared pairs do not exchange top amplitude in the tested top/face sector. Exact screening result 3 Collective closure Which motifs admit closed or static sectors? The abstract boundary of a four-simplex has one top cycle; the finite coordinate-order cube has none. Exact topology result; formation unproved 4 Attraction and persistence Does a pattern survive perturbation or attract nearby states? The fixed skew flow preserves pair separation. The historical positive-coherence Genesis branch has only the zero static amplitude equilibrium under its stated assumptions. Attraction unavailable in the fixed flow; other source branches open 5 Assembly and competition Do different seeds converge to the same cluster class? No topology-changing source rule was identified in the inspected contracts. No assembly simulation is claimed. Open 6 Reproducibility Does a selected class survive seed, size and boundary changes? Exact replay covers nine supplied motifs and a complete small combinatorial universe. No selection ensemble has yet run. Baseline captured; selection tests pending Stages are evidence checkpoints, not an observed temporal formation sequence. A future run must record the actual ordered transitions and their source receipts before any formation story is written. The first exact comparison The verifier builds the oriented simplicial boundaries, checks the chain identity, computes exact ranks and Betti numbers, and constructs the full unit-norm chain generator A=B transpose−B. It verifies skewness entry by entry. It also computes exact top Gram characteristic polynomials and Taylor derivative orders for top-cell propagation from each cell seed. All motifs below are supplied abstract carriers. The cube name comes from its declared coordinate-order construction. The other names specify incidence, not recovered Euclidean shapes. Supplied motif Cells Vertices Face components Top cycles Single tetrahedron 1 4 1 0 Disjoint pair 2 8 2 0 Vertex-shared pair 2 7 2 0 Edge-shared pair 2 6 2 0 Face-shared pair 2 5 1 0 Three-cell face chain 3 6 1 0 Three-cell ring around an edge 3 5 1 0 Six-cell coordinate-order cube 6 8 1 0 Abstract boundary of a four-simplex 5 5 1 1 For the vertex- and edge-shared pairs, G=B3 transpose B3=4I. A top seed in one cell therefore never produces top amplitude in the other under the closed top/face sector. This does not assert absence of all lower-degree interactions or protocol dependence: shared vertices still matter to the discrete commit guards. The face-shared pair instead has characteristic polynomial (lambda−3)(lambda−5). Its neighboring top amplitude begins at source derivative order 2. In the three-cell face chain, a seed reaches the adjacent cell at order 2 and the next at order 4. In the supplied cube, the tested seed reaches other top cells at orders 2, 4 and 6 according to the exact Gram powers. These are local Taylor orders, not finite arrival times or a physical causal cone. The abstract boundary of a four-simplex has Betti vector (1,0,0,1). The alternating top chain z=(1,−1,1,−1,1) has B3 z=0, so it supplies a static top mode. The finite cube has Betti vector (1,0,0,0). A closed top cycle is therefore a useful discriminator. It is not automatically a retained attractor: its amplitude is preparation dependent and remains constant under the fixed flow. The four-simplex boundary is an abstract triangulated three-sphere, not a filled polyhedron in ordinary three-dimensional Euclidean space. A genuinely constrained tetrahedral relation For the supplied four-vertex representation, let P=I−11 transpose/4. Its projected coordinate directions obey: P squared = P norm squared of each direction = 3/4 inner product of distinct directions = −1/4 pair cosine = −1/3 Those directions form a regular tetrahedral frame within the three-dimensional zero-sum space. This is stronger than a visual resemblance: the angular relation follows exactly from the projection. It does not derive the existence of the four vertices, their physical embedding, a common absolute radius, or an assembly process. Removing label bias A complete enumeration of nonempty subsets of the five tetrahedral facets on five ambient vertices gives 31 labeled carriers and five isomorphism classes, distinguished by cell count. Unused vertices are removed. The labeled counts are 5, 10, 10, 5 and 1 for one through five cells. This is a bounded combinatorial baseline, not a catalogue of all three-dimensional shapes. It provides no dynamical preference among the classes. A selector still needs an admitted rule rather than multiplicity or visual familiarity. What the sources exclude and leave open The current manuscript proves that two solutions of the same fixed skew generator maintain their Euclidean separation. This excludes contracting phase or configuration selection from that flow itself. Its discrete phase-agreement candidate updates vertex and reference bits on a supplied carrier; it does not create or rearrange cells. The inspected historical Genesis audit gives the positive-coherence equilibrium identity: Omega kappa a transpose L a + 2 Omega Phi norm(a) squared + delta sum(a_i to the fourth) = 0. With positive Omega, Phi and delta and nonnegative coupling on a positive-semidefinite Laplacian, only a=0 is static. That conditional no-go does not rule out periodic, statistically stationary, driven or other nonlinear branches. The historical numerical coupling is not adopted as a current fundamental coefficient. The next investigation must recover the actual update rules and estimator histories before replaying that branch. Next bounded investigation Inventory source-complete rules that can alter adjacency, retain a local cluster or feed retained burden back into amplitudes. For each, record state variables, guards, updates, conserved quantities, external inputs and admitted source lineage. Start with historical Genesis and the retained-burden feedback frontier; do not combine their rules silently. If a source-complete topology-changing rule is found, run it from differently labeled and differently shaped seeds and record every attachment or rearrangement. If it is absent, distinguish the two remaining experiments: activity-pattern selection on a fixed carrier, and a separately labeled candidate assembly rule. A candidate rule must retain its new assumptions and cannot count as native UD selection. Each run will capture the initial carrier and preparation, rule version, event ordering, stage changes, connectivity, closure rank, support distribution, persistence, perturbation response, failed alternatives and exact replay receipts. Numerical thresholds, if required for an activity cluster readout, must be declared and varied; a zero/nonnull readout alone is not a robust cluster definition. A successful next milestone is a source-complete selection experiment with a falsifier, even if it shows that no preferred shape forms. No “winning shape” is declared by this initial comparison. Scoped results are now stated in the public theorem supplement; independent review is pending and physical promotion remains 0.UD native coface growth and cluster selection audit 2026-10-02, America/Chicago. The broader UD source record contains a local cell-forming coface candidate, boundary growth, retraction and conditionally admitted Pachner actions. This advances the previous fixed-carrier screen: growth rules are present, although a universal cluster selector is still unproved. The recovered coface rule conditionally selects the balanced four-vertex cell for a binary alphabet. It does not select a unique cluster type or a finite stopping size. Exact replay from one fixed tetrahedral seed admits both a four-cell chain and a four-cell star. These conclusions distinguish a local closure normal form from a global preferred shape. Persistence and clustering onset The primary question is now: which configurations achieve coherent agreement, persist, and enable further clustering? Which of those configurations receive a persistence or growth preference from the source rules? The investigation proceeds in this order: Checkpoint Evidence required Coherent agreement A typed agreement predicate and its actual source receipt Persistence onset Survival, recurrence or retained state over a declared window and perturbation Clustering availability At least one lawful attachment or collective closure transition Growth preference A source drive or rate favoring one available transition over alternatives Cluster persistence The resulting collective pattern retains or recovers its defining relations The order is an investigation sequence, not a theorem that one checkpoint causes the next. Balanced binary label admissibility is not automatically phase agreement or completed triadic closure. The retrieved receipt kernel emits a candidate and leaves closure to its next owner. Those predicates must remain separately recorded. For the tested growth branch, local balanced completion and lawful clustering availability are established. Persistent cluster selection is not established. The exact growth history is therefore a baseline for identifying where persistence and availability begin, rather than an answer declaring which shape wins. “Prefers persistence” will mean a measured or proved source-law advantage in survival, recovery or retention under matched initial conditions and perturbations. A visually stable prepared pattern or a larger count of legal histories does not establish that advantage. Source boundaries The August graph-first coface audit introduces a new vertex on an admissible simplex when its chosen label has multiplicity below two. Each new vertex connects to all vertices of that simplex. Extension preserves the per-label cap of two. Its boundary propagation branch introduces a fresh vertex only on a frontier facet and connects it exclusively to that facet. This is a retrieved primitive candidate with explicit historical target exposure: the binary alphabet and tetrahedral spatial target are declared. The source also states that the older global edge-saturation and lexicographic preference route was moved to the analysis sandbox. We do not revive that preference to force a winning cluster. The graph-seed audit keeps the first nonempty graph as boundary data. The new tests therefore begin with declared admissible seeds. They do not narrate creation from an empty state. The spatial manifold candidate applies to the ordinary spatial three-dimensional branch, not all UD topology or internal fibers. Face incidence at most two alone is insufficient for a manifold certificate. The fresh-vertex boundary construction used here is stronger: it glues a tetrahedron along exactly one boundary triangle of a stacked three-ball. Local completion result For alphabet size q and label counts c_i in {0,1,2}, define the deficit D=sum_i(2−c_i). Every legal extension reduces D by one. If D is positive, at least one legal label remains. Thus every maximal extension history terminates after D steps at counts (2,…,2). The terminal cardinality is 2q and dimension 2q−1. For q=2 this is a balanced K4 cell. It is unique as a label-multiplicity class, up to relabeling of vertices within label classes. It is not a unique labeled history, metric tetrahedron, physical scale or origin. The exact replay checks all nonempty multiplicity seeds for q=1 through q=6, verifies the unique terminal count vector and counts every legal label-completion order through an exact recurrence and multinomial check. Larger alphabets terminate at larger simplices; tetrahedral size is conditional on the binary alphabet and cap, not an alphabet-independent selection theorem. These are mathematical termination statements for the extension branch. They assume that legal extensions continue rather than arbitrary idling or intervening retractions. Observed growth stages For cluster growth, use the fixed completed seed (0,1,2,3) with labels (0,0,1,1). Enumerate every legal frontier triangle choice through five cells. Each triangle has exactly one deficient label, so the next vertex label is uniquely fixed once the face is selected. title: Uniform burden persistence and recovery
note: Public theorem dependencies · original development release preserved · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Scoped exact mathematics is promoted through PT01–PT16. Native primitive admission and empirical claims remain separate; independent review pending; physical promotion 0. Preserved source release. Its historical development status remains unchanged. Scoped results are now stated in the public theorem supplement; independent review is pending and physical promotion remains 0.UD shape discovery scientific gap analysis and repairs 2026-10-02, America/Chicago. Development evidence. Independent review pending. Internal claim bin: CANDIDATE_DEVELOPMENT_MATHEMATICS. Correspondence status: NOT_PROPOSED. Physical promotion: 0. The approach is now a testable programme for agreement, persistence and clustering onset. Its largest scientific gap is a missing source-connected bridge between a closure decision, a retained formation amount and a growth or recovery law. That gap cannot be closed by motif counting or naming a persistent-looking pattern. This audit repairs definitions, comparisons, availability gates, concurrency controls and falsifiers. It also executes an existing burden-mixing branch: uniform burden persists, same-total contrast perturbations relax, and concentration decreases. This is a positive persistence result for a mode on supplied K4, with spreading rather than compact cluster formation. Main gaps and repairs Gap Repair completed Remaining limit Label balance, phase agreement and closure treated as one predicate Separate typed predicates and source-owned receipts Agreement-to-formation update remains open Persistence treated as one outcome Separate stock, recurrence, retained history, recovery and structural survival A persistent stock need not preserve a pattern Frontier face treated as full clustering availability Require topology, label, coherence, resource, lineage, freshness/conflict and event gates Only topology and binary-label controls are replayed here No fair basis for shape comparisons Match size, stock, boundary, receipt stratum, perturbation and native clock No full cross-shape persistence ensemble has run Legal history multiplicity treated as preference Retain outcome sets; require a source measure for probabilities No native attachment rates are inferred Reversible recurrence treated as attraction Test perturbation separation and pattern recovery separately Fixed skew flow supplies no contraction Spreading treated as clustering Add exact concentration and participation observables Geometric assembly requires incidence transitions Concurrency ignored Test same-facet stale aborts and distinct-facet commutation Connection/resource transaction controls remain separate Coface sufficiency treated as bedrock Read the explicit A3 proposal record A3 is a locked proposal, not admitted bedrock Small motif census treated as natural geometry Separate representation, incidence and metric shape Universality and metric selection remain open Retention decision used as formation amount Enforce ledger decision–amount separation Source magnitude and coupled scheduler remain open Criteria could change after seeing outcomes Freeze a future protocol, nulls and falsifiers Present checks are retrospective source-derived controls The machine-readable gap register retains thirteen individual gaps, their repairs, status and falsifiers. A method repair is not reported as a completed theory law. The corrected experimental sequence First identify a typed agreement predicate. A binary balanced cell, a phase-agreement state, a triadic candidate and a completed closure are different objects. A receipt must identify its source owner and current dependencies. Then measure persistence. Report conserved stock, repeated return, retained identity, perturbation recovery and structural survival separately. The order “agreement then persistence then clustering” is an investigation order; the sources must prove or implement each causal arrow. Next evaluate clustering availability. A frontier triangle establishes a topological opportunity. Full availability also needs all required source gates. At least one failed gate yields FAIL. If none fails but a gate is unmeasured or unsourced, the result is UNKNOWN. A native HOLD is recorded only when the rule actually issues one. UNKNOWN is neither PASS nor a native HOLD. Only then compare preference. A valid preference must arise from source drives, sourced transition rates, a proved survival advantage or explicitly declared exogenous sampling. It cannot be inferred from drawing familiarity, an arbitrary scheduler, or the number of enumerated histories. Exact persistence control from the burden source Ledger Q163 gives the isolated K4 relaxational burden equation: rho_perp' = −(4/3)rho_perp. P0 = 11 transpose/4 Pperp = I−P0 T(s) = P0 + exp(−4s/3)Pperp. The rate is an existing dimensionless source result, not a fitted physical damping constant. This branch is unprotected relaxational burden on a supplied K4. It is not the reversible support lane, a protected burden sector, or an implemented agreement-driven growth process. Write b(0)=mean(b)1+delta with sum(delta)=0. The uniform component remains unchanged. The contrast evolves as exp(−4s/3)delta. Consequently: total burden is preserved contrast norm squared = exp(−8s/3) times its initial value same-total contrast perturbations decay toward the same uniform state a perturbation of total burden shifts the final uniform state. This gives an attracting family of uniform states within the stated lane. It does not choose an absolute amplitude or attract all initial totals to one state. For nonnegative burden with positive total B, use the exact concentration observable: IPR(s) = sum_i b_i(s)^2 / B^2 = 1/4 + exp(−8s/3) norm(delta)^2/B^2. effective participation = 1/IPR. IPR decreases toward 1/4 while participation increases toward four. A seed b=(1,0,0,0) spreads to all four vertices. In propagator coordinate r=exp(−4s/3): b(r) = ((1+3r)/4,(1−r)/4,(1−r)/4,(1−r)/4) IPR(r) = 1/4 + 3r^2/4. The uniform limit is reached only asymptotically unless the preparation is already uniform. Persistence preference here concerns a burden mode, not a preferred polyhedron or compact cluster. The exact replay checks the projection identities, propagator semigroup, positivity, total preservation, contrast contraction and concentration formula. It uses all eighty nonzero preparations on the declared nonnegative three-level grid, all twenty-four vertex permutations and two amplitude-scaling controls at each propagator fixture. Grid values are test preparations, not internal coefficients. r=0 is explicitly the infinite-time limit. Attachment conflict controls The retrieved serializability source is conditional on TX0, seam innovation and flat/path-compatible transport. We replay only its topology and binary-label snapshot requirements, not the full connection or resource transaction. Four same-facet tests commit one newborn and reject the stale second proposal. Four changed-label snapshot tests abort. Six pairs of distinct frontier facets commute under both serial orders, up to fresh-vertex renaming, while preserving labels and old vertex identities. These fourteen cases repair an omitted control in the earlier serial growth census. They do not settle curved inherited facets, non-Abelian innovation, resource debits, phase changes or surgery. Source admission and retention corrections The explicit A3 source reads “PROPOSED_AXIOM / LOCKED PROPOSAL RECORD / NOT BEDROCK.” Its local completion theorem is conditional on that primitive. A3 is independent of the older static grammar; sufficiency for cell generation does not establish its primitive necessity or physical admission. The earlier growth candidate classification is therefore retained. Ledger Q368–Q370 provides another persistence avenue: an isolated symmetry-compatible winding-to-burden output lies in the uniform mode and is annihilated by the stated mixing operator. But Q369 leaves its scalar formation law open, and Q384 explicitly prohibits inferring a source amount from a binary retention decision. Retaining a zero mode is not proof that the dynamics creates a nonzero value in it. The pure-lineage defect source provides a third, topological persistence notion: odd boundary endpoint counts are conserved while endpoints propagate through fresh cofaces. This is a conditional defect invariant, not burden amplitude persistence or an attachment preference. It is retained as a distinct source result, not replayed in the new burden controls. These distinctions prevent three false substitutions: conserved defect for stable spatial shape, binary retained decision for source amount, and persistent uniform burden for compact clustering. Frozen next study The future study protocol asks three questions: Does a source-owned closure receipt predict retention or recovery beyond label admissibility under matched preparations? At which event cuts do all required gates first permit a cluster attachment? Do the resulting source drives favor persistent configurations over competing legal outcomes? Each hypothesis lists its prerequisites, primary observable and null result. If an agreement-to-evolution bridge, full availability gate or coupled scheduler is missing, that experiment remains not executable rather than receiving a synthetic replacement. Matched comparisons require the same cell count when comparing shapes, stock within the same typed lane, boundary contract, receipt/transport stratum, source clock and admissible perturbation class. Relabeling, scaling, reversible-support, uniform-mixing, zero-formation and transaction controls are required where relevant. Primary exact tests use no tolerance. Future approximate tests must declare tolerances and observation windows before outcomes and report sensitivity. A finite window cannot prove eternal persistence. No p-value or shape probability is reported without a valid sampling measure. The current results are retrospective source-derived checks; the future frozen protocol has not yet run. What is filled and what is still missing The definitions and analysis controls are filled to an executable level. The burden branch now has exact retention, recovery and spreading tests. The topology/label transaction branch has explicit race controls. Source admission and unknown-gate handling are corrected, and the next study has falsifiers. The unresolved theory work is specific: the typed coherent-agreement-to-formation update, source amplitude, full resource/lineage/event availability, and the coupled growth/retraction or preference law. No attracting compact cluster or metric shape is established by this audit. The highest-value next task is to identify one source-complete closure receipt and follow it into the first persistence update, before adding a larger motif catalogue. An exact non-result at that boundary is useful: it identifies which primitive must be derived or separately proposed. Evidence The new replay passes 12244 exact assertions over eighty nonnegative burden preparations and fourteen attachment-conflict cases. Earlier growth and fixed-carrier results remain unchanged. Source read packets, gap register, future study protocol, controls, results and risks are included in the release. Sources include the coefficient ledger, Q163 and Q368–Q384; the A3 proposal; the coface serializability theorem; and the pure-lineage defect theorem. Scoped results are now stated in the public theorem supplement; independent review is pending and physical promotion remains 0.UD collective motif agreement and retention The controlled four-cell comparison separates collective agreement, retained burden memory and persistent gate configuration. Three tetrahedral complexes have different agreement counts. More decisively, a chain and a star start with the same active propagation operator and the same burden, then make matching local gate proposals whose integrated retention changes in opposite directions. The chain initially loses memory faster after its swap, but later retains more, with a certified curve crossing between source-clock values 1 and 2. The generated replays make one candidate collective swap and then keep the gate fixed. Exact local score ties explain that quiescence under the declared unanimous commit contract. Burden contrast still decays. We have evidence for conditional carrier-dependent retention and gate quiescence, not a native clustering onset, preferred Euclidean shape or sustained burden formation. Exact rational propagation enclosures certify the difference is negative at s=1 and positive at s=2. Continuity proves at least one crossing in (1,2). The proof does not establish a unique crossing or all-time ordering for the star. The figure uses floating eigendecomposition only to display curves; rational receipts supply the sign evidence. Wider preparation and robustness controls A retrospective follow-up tests the earlier two-cell preparation extended as (1,0,0,5,2,a,b), with a and b from 0 through 6, all three initial classes, and one representative of each complex. Generated propagation and gate quiescence Three representative traces start from the wider witnesses. They each execute one candidate complete-target swap at s=0 and then propagate under the published global generator. Exact rational uniformization encloses the continuous semigroup at eight successive observer intervals of length 1/4, through s=2. This is not an Euler update or a recovered native event cadence. Squared-gradient score differences are linear functionals on the 49-dimensional burden tensor-square carrier. Forty-nine vanishing integer moments certify an identically zero difference by Cayley-Hamilton. The two chains have tied open-pair scores in every cell after C closes. It does not supply a source-owned distributed implementation or resolve partial proposals. The source supplies a conditional local first-admissibility rule. It does not fill the complete clock, integrity and shared-authorization contract in the passages and releases read here. It then defines the next local event index as the minimum observed n after the previous completed event for which the predictive receipt is nonzero. The earlier B2 theorem is conditional on fixed Hamming weight, a one-close/one-reopen event, the burden-relaxation objective and passing integrity gates. Use the twelve vertices (0,±1,±φ),(±1,±φ,0),(±φ,0,±1). (0,\pm1,\pm\varphi),\quad(\pm1,\pm\varphi,0),\quad(\pm\varphi,0,\pm1). The signs are independent within each pair. Join vertices at squared distance 4. This gives 30 exterior edges and 20 triangular faces. The exact verifier checks each triangle is a supporting facet of the convex hull and is nondegenerate. Add the origin as labeled vertex 12 and cone each face to it. Convexity places the origin inside, so these twenty tetrahedra fill the polyhedron with shared faces and disjoint interiors. Object Vertices Edges Triangular faces Tetrahedra Exterior icosahedral sphere 12 30 20 0 Filled center-cone carrier 13 42 50 20 Added radial generators 1 12 30 20 Total chain dimension is 125. The 20 exterior faces belong to one tetrahedron each; the 30 radial faces belong to two. Every radial edge belongs to five tetrahedra. This carrier is neither a single filled tetrahedron, the K4 graph, the K5-e bench carrier, nor the SER incidence star. Exact geometry and the regularity obstruction The exterior edges have length 2. The center-to-vertex squared length is r2=1+φ2=5+52≠4.r^2=1+\varphi^2=\frac{5+\sqrt5}{2}\ne4. Each constituent has three equal exterior edges and three equal radial edges. The twenty tetrahedra are congruent by icosahedral symmetry, but are not regular. Their coordinates and all geometric comparisons are calculated exactly in Q(√5), represented as rational pairs [a,b] for a+b√5. The interior dihedral angle at each radial edge is 2π/5, or 72 degrees. The verifier checks the face-normal dot products exactly, including their positive sign, using cos(2π/5)=5−14,cos2(2π/5)=3−58.\cos(2\pi/5)=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4},\qquad \cos^2(2\pi/5)=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{8}. Thus five sectors close: 5(2π/5) = 2π. Five regular Euclidean tetrahedra instead leave the strictly positive angular gap δ=2π−5arccos(1/3)>0,\delta=2\pi-5\arccos(1/3)>0, because cos(2π/5) < 1/3. They do not assign physical distance or select the chain-space inner product H. A unit simplex metric and a metric weighted by this embedding would be distinct operator choices. Comparator gaps are bar E_k=Δa_k with certified nearest-integer labels, a_-k=-a_k, and native mismatch d_S≤Δ/2 on each admitted cell; comparator and native energies coincide outside the cutoff. Actual native H_S is never rounded. Ledger baseline 235, source-selected Q06=0, action normalization, gauge limits and LC thresholds remain unchanged. The ladder has M=L+2(m+1)C levels, C=max|a_k|, initial support n_0,…,n_0+L-1 with n_0=(m+1)C, and H_R=Δn. Parent q_b and the full signed-word comparator overlap A_m remain charged jointly, once: ηbank=1−(1−qb)mAm2,Am≥(1−mμL)+. \eta_{\mathrm{bank}}=\sqrt{1-(1-q_b)^m A_m^2},\qquad A_m\geq\left(1-\frac{m\mu}{L}\right)_+. Apparatus admissions here are Δ,L,m, the controller scale κ, its programmed gate list and the capture/reset durations. Binary fuel gaps, controller couplings and phase precompensation are supplied apparatus laws, not native coefficients or fitted physical constants. Native donor production remains open. 2. Explicit upstream ladder production from finite coherent fuel For L=2^q, supply q qubits F_j with H_Fj=Δ2^j|1><1| and initial |+>=(|0>+|1>)/√2. Supply the reference seed |n_0>, with its energy n_0Δ explicitly loaded. Within the admitted reference window, define the reversible swaps |1⟩Fj|n0+r⟩R↔|0⟩Fj|n0+r+2j⟩R |1\rangle_{F_j}|n_0+r\rangle_R\ \longleftrightarrow\ |0\rangle_{F_j}|n_0+r+2^j\rangle_R for r with its j-th binary bit zero. All other states act as identity. These pairs are disjoint; each preserves H_Fj+H_R exactly. Process j=0,…,q-1. Previously populated lower bits leave the current bit zero, so on the admitted input |+⟩F⊗q|n0⟩R↦|0⟩F⊗q1L∑r=0L−1|n0+r⟩R. |+\rangle^{\otimes q}_F|n_0\rangle_R\ \longmapsto\ |0\rangle^{\otimes q}_F\frac{1}{\sqrt L}\sum_{r=0}^{L-1}|n_0+r\rangle_R. No outcome is discarded. Fuel energy and coherence are transferred into R; they are not created. Gate extensions outside the supported window are identity, never reference wraparound. This map works for arbitrary coherent fuel amplitudes and correlations, but then produces their corresponding joint output rather than silently replacing them by independent |+> qubits. The integer bit rule has clock notation: r=2^(j+1)u+v and r≡v (mod 2^(j+1)); require 0≤v<2^j, then transfer to r+2^j. For instance r=5=1·4+1 and 5≡1 (mod 4); transferring bit j=1 takes it to 7=1·4+3 and 7≡3 (mod 4). These residue labels specify disjoint finite pairs, not resource refilling. Moduli are powers of the prime 2; 5 and 7 are prime. For independent ideal fuel, ⟨HF⟩=Δ(L−1)2,VarHF=Δ2(L2−1)12,FQ=4VarHF. \langle H_F\rangle=\frac{\Delta(L-1)}2,\qquad\operatorname{Var}H_F=\frac{\Delta^2(L^2-1)}{12},\qquad F_Q=4\operatorname{Var}H_F. For general correlated pure fuel, retain 4 Var(Σ_j H_Fj), including every covariance. For mixed fuel, QFI is generally not 4 Var; no marginal-QFI sum is substituted. The ideal output fuel is ground-state waste with no energy or coherence; its outgoing carrier remains part of the ledger. Installing fresh fuel requires a new supplied nonstationary bank. 3. Finite static history controller Take a programmed list U_1,…,U_n. The first q gates may be the binary producer above, followed by m finite parent preparation lifts. Each gate commutes with the comparison work Hamiltonian bar H_W=H_R+Σ_j H_Fj+Σ_i bar H_Si. Define prefix products P_0=I and P_j=U_j…U_1 and 𝒲=∑j=0n|j⟩⟨j|C⊗Pj. \mathcal W=\sum_{j=0}^{n}|j\rangle\langle j|_C\otimes P_j. Choose a controller clock HC=κ∑j=0n−1(j+1)(n−j)(|j+1⟩⟨j|+|j⟩⟨j+1|), H_C=\kappa\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\sqrt{(j+1)(n-j)}\bigl(|j+1\rangle\langle j|+|j\rangle\langle j+1|\bigr), and the actual constant machine Hamiltonian Hact=HW+𝒲(HC⊗I)𝒲†. H_{\mathrm{act}}=H_W+\mathcal W(H_C\otimes I)\mathcal W^\dagger. Tensor identities are implicit. Actual H_W contains every native H_S, exact ladder/fuel energies and any independent free spectator dynamics. Gate-dependent edges contain U_j and U_j†. Their synthesis is supplied and generally nonlocal; a nearest-neighbor clock graph is not a proof of local system/reference interactions. In the symmetric subspace of n abstract spin-1/2 systems, H_C equals κΣX. Acting on |0>^n therefore gives e−itHC|0⟩=∑j=0n(−i)j(nj)sinj(κt)cosn−j(κt)|j⟩. e^{-itH_C}|0\rangle=\sum_{j=0}^n(-i)^j\sqrt{\binom nj}\sin^j(\kappa t)\cos^{n-j}(\kappa t)|j\rangle. Thus its spectrum is κ(n-2j), norm κn, and derived completion time T=π/(2κ). At T the comparator reaches (-i)^n|n>⊗P_nψ for every work input ψ, including arbitrary spectators and correlations, up to common comparison free evolution. Since [bar H_W,mathcal W]=0, this identity follows by unitary conjugation, not by assuming instantaneous physical gates. Each preparation gate is programmed with V_i|g>=Σ_k c_k exp(i bar E_k T)|k>. At the common endpoint, comparison source phases cancel and the output clocks are the admitted packets; R has the common free phase and the signed history displacement. The fuel ends in |0>^q. Subsequent output evolution uses actual native H_S. All phases reside in the supplied initial fuel and static edge program. No free external phase ruler is inferred. The four-level controller, n=m=3, assumes R was already supplied. The integrated producer/controller has q=20, m=3, n=23, hence 24 clock levels. Adding the producer changes clock precision and resource costs even though this engineered spin clock’s exact T is independent of n. 4. Native-dynamics and capture budget The actual/comparison machine difference is Σ_i(H_Si-bar H_Si), with norm d≤mΔ/2. Duhamel’s identity gives a uniform operator and full-joint trace-distance bound ∥e−itHact−e−itHcomp∥≤|t|d. \|e^{-itH_{\mathrm{act}}}-e^{-itH_{\mathrm{comp}}}\|\leq |t|d. Unlike the earlier separately timed pulse construction, this comparison runs over the whole controller interval. The old mτΔ/2 pulse debit is replaced by Td; it is not also added. At exactly T the source/reference/native comparison is bounded by η_bank+Td. Additional implementation, supplied-state, parent thermal, acquisition and reset debits remain separate. At time t=T+s the comparator’s terminal probability is p_n(t)=cos^(2n)(κs). For |s|≤σ, 1−pn(t)≤nκ2σ2,1−pn(t)≤nκσ. 1-p_n(t)\leq n\kappa^2\sigma^2,\qquad \sqrt{1-p_n(t)}\leq\sqrt n\,\kappa\sigma. Compare the endpoint branch with the desired native freely evolved packet at the actual capture time. Besides the controller evolution debit td, comparison/native phases after T cost at most |s|d. Hence a conservative complete-record state budget is ηwindow≤min{1,ηbank+nκσ+(T+2σ)d}. \eta_{\mathrm{window}}\leq\min\{1,\eta_{\mathrm{bank}}+\sqrt n\,\kappa\sigma+(T+2\sigma)d\}. Before supply or capture errors, the actual probability of controller-completion failure obeys pFAIL_C≤min{1,nκ2σ2+(T+σ)d}. p_{\mathrm{FAIL\_C}}\leq\min\{1,n\kappa^2\sigma^2+(T+\sigma)d\}. Use the full instrument with P_n=|n><n| and I-P_n. Append the two unnormalized output branches as SUCCESS_C and FAIL_C records, preserving all prior acquisition failures and histories. This CPTP record map contracts the unconditional joint comparison. Successful posterior precision needs its own acceptance-probability bound; it is not obtained by renormalizing away FAIL_C. The word-overlap formula covers isolated bank production. Downstream maps can interleave on emitted systems and separate resources. Contacts on this same R, fuel or controller require their integrated channel bound or actual joint replay, as held correction LB02 requires. Native running does not make detector backaction disappear. 5. Recurrence and absence of autonomous stop At 2T=π/κ the comparison clock is (-1)^n|0> and the circuit prefix returns to P_0=I, with common comparison free evolution. Preparation is undone by coherent reverse traversal if the output is not captured. At integer multiples ℓT: ℓ=2u+r and ℓ≡r (mod 2); r=0 gives the starting endpoint and r=1 the completion endpoint. This two-state endpoint clock is not a cyclic energy reservoir. The relevant modulus 2 is prime; n=23 is prime, while its 24-level carrier has 24=2^3·3 levels. A bounded timing window and a supplied capture/export map remain necessary. This is autonomous one-shot propagation under a constant engineered Hamiltonian, not permanent shutdown or an autonomous prepare/acquire/export/reset cycle. An irreversible latch, finite dissipative memory or output routing must carry its own resource, backaction and recurrence accounting. No success plateau is asserted. 6. Constant-machine first law and interaction receipts Use bare H_C+κnI if a nonnegative controller energy convention is required. Write H_act=H_free+V, where H_free=H_W+H_C and V=mathcal W(H_C⊗I)mathcal W†-H_C⊗I. The additive offset cancels from all differences. During the constant machine evolution, Δ⟨Hact⟩=0,Δ⟨Hfree⟩=−Δ⟨V⟩,∥V∥≤2κn. \Delta\langle H_{\mathrm{act}}\rangle=0,\qquad\Delta\langle H_{\mathrm{free}}\rangle=-\Delta\langle V\rangle,\qquad\|V\|\leq2\kappa n. The controller/interaction energy replaces the earlier external timed-pulse switching receipt for this different architecture. No per-edge switched mean-work debit is inherited without a physical switch. Initializing the static device, capturing outputs and resetting it still require supply/contact accounting. Do not claim exact conservation of the bare native free energy alone. The initial |0> clock has mean κn in the nonnegative convention and variance κ²n; at the ideal completion |n> the same moments hold. During the run it is correlated with circuit prefixes and work states. Return to the initial state has not happened merely because the mean energies agree. Actual first-law equality is checked on arbitrary spectator-entangled inputs, without a two-point measurement of coherent fuel. 7. Matched supply/reset with outgoing correlations Let A include the consumed reference, fuel and controller; include source cells as well when fresh selected input cells are needed for the next bank. Supply one independent matched donor D with H_D=H_A and declared initial state σ_D. For the integrated producer, σ_A consists of reference |n_0>, q coherent |+> fuel qubits, controller |0>, and fresh source eigenstates |g> as required. The thermal/eigenstate supply errors retain their parent full-joint admission. Prephase the donor for the actual reset endpoint under H_D. D’s source-cell partition can be retained as output data; its consumed reference/fuel/controller partitions are outgoing resource waste. None is traced away to claim a free reset. The ideal exchange is implemented in duration τ_r by G_r=π(I-SWAP)/(2τ_r), norm π/τ_r, commuting with the matched bare free Hamiltonian. Native independent Y dynamics continues. If the production machine’s V remains active during reset, compare the actual reset to that matched exchange with a full-joint contact debit ηreset,contact≤τr∥V∥≤2κnτr. \eta_{\mathrm{reset,contact}}\leq\tau_r\|V\|\leq2\kappa n\tau_r. An actual disconnect instead needs a switching/controller receipt. There is no silent assumption that the static machine stops for reset. This reset is still a specified supplied finite-duration control, not a derived autonomous trigger. Small replays exchange a reference/controller module while retaining an entangled spectator; the algebraic full-module extension covers arbitrary finite matched A, including all source cells and fuel. For N runs, supply N actual donor slots. Refuse the next exchange and preserve END_OF_SUPPLY in the record. Donors are consumed once; outgoing coherent waste is not presumed reusable. Marginal fuel fidelities do not determine the joint supply admission: three mutually exclusive single-slot errors have marginal fidelity 2/3 in each slot but joint target fidelity 0, not (2/3)^3=8/27. Here 8=2^3, 27=3^3; 8=0·27+8 and 8≡8 (mod 27). With joint pure-bank fidelity f and fixed ω_Y, a conservative gentle-measurement bound is ε_F≤min{1,√(1-f)+(1-f)/2}. The projected Y deficit is positive with trace 1-f; this also charges supply/history correlations. Direct full-joint admission is preferred. An unconditional telescoping budget across supplied runs is bounded by ε_F plus the sum of declared production/capture/contact/reset and other matching apparatus errors, capped at 1. Joint source thermal admission is charged once on its held bank domain. In a repeated ideal comparison, matched reset restores fresh inputs and exports each old correlated state; it does not remove correlation from the complete universe. 8. Stationary-supply obstruction and resource frontier If all input resources are stationary under the admitted free-energy generator and the production map is energy covariant, the reference output is stationary. Against the uniform pure L-level reference packet, any stationary reference has overlap at most 1/L. Measuring the target projector therefore gives D_tr≥1-1/L, achieved by the uniform diagonal mixture. For L=1048576 the minimum is exactly 1048575/1048576. Define b=4Ω+2κ+2κb. b=4\Omega+2\kappa+2\kappa_b. Let J_fin,T be the complete finite-pulse instrument, with its N-bin record, and J_id,T the just-defined lifted ideal instrument. It is uniform over arbitrary retained quantum memory; all records, including no receipt, reverse and OTHER, participate. A finite counter with N+1 ordinal states is bookkeeping, not a demonstrated clock. The coordinates p_i do not occur in any B_k. Thus B_k, the unweighted skew generator, the Hodge Laplacian, and all their chain-coordinate trajectories are identical for every r>0. This follows by literal equality of the matrices, rather than by a numerical spectral coincidence. For the nonaugmented filled tetrahedron the blocks are L0=4I4−J4,L1=4I6,L2=4I4,L3=(4). L_0=4I_4-J_4,\quad L_1=4I_6,\quad L_2=4I_4,\quad L_3=(4). Hence the full 15-coordinate Laplacian spectrum is one zero and fourteen copies of 4, and the skew generator has characteristic polynomial lambda(lambda²+4)^7. The parameter r does not split these modes. This conclusion concerns fixed chain coordinates; a separately chosen geometry-dependent preparation or readout can introduce shape dependence without changing the generator and must be declared as such. For SER, the vertex–cell incidence graph and firing predicates are also unchanged. Legal event sequences, local commit counts and target bounds are identical under the same labeled event sequence. A single tetrahedral cell still has B_c=5. A scheduler chosen to depend on shape would be an added rule, not a consequence of the original source. Conditional nonidentifiability statement. Any observable determined solely by this unchanged incidence structure, fixed source operator, fixed initial chain coordinates and fixed readout cannot distinguish r=1 from r=2. The shape-sensitive normal frame can do so precisely because it adds geometric data absent from those inputs. 5. The angle and frame conclusions are independent of overall scale; an equal-volume comparison can be obtained by a uniform rescaling and gives the same dihedral cosines and F. No physical length unit is selected. 6. A possible next interface, not an adopted dynamics To let geometry affect the chain operator, a future source addendum must specify positive-definite chain inner products H_k from declared geometric data, including normalization and gluing compatibility. For B_k:C_k→C_(k-1), the consistent adjoint is Bk†=Hk−1BkTHk−1,Lk=Bk†Bk+Bk+1Bk+1†. B_k^{\dagger}=H_k^{-1}B_k^T H_{k-1},\qquad L_k=B_k^{\dagger}B_k+B_{k+1}B_{k+1}^{\dagger}. These identities specify how to use a chosen inner product; they do not choose one. The boundary identities remain B_(k-1)B_k=0. Changing one coupling block without consistent adjoints is not this construction. H_k=I restores the current baseline. No circumcentric or other metric-weight choice is selected in this audit, and no new frequency ratio is fitted. The affine map from the regular reference to this family is diag(1,1,r). Its pullback of the assumed Euclidean metric is diag(1,1,q). This is an explicitly assigned internal positive-definite metric, not an emergent spacetime metric or a Lorentzian signature. Dihedral geometry supplies neither seconds nor a law for r to change. 7. Verification and limits The bundled Python script uses the standard library and exact Fraction arithmetic. It reconstructs outward normals from independent vertex cross products; verifies edge lengths, face-area squares, volume, the cosine identities, normal closure, frame eigenvectors, face-data reconstruction, and metric symmetry counts; and constructs all boundary matrices from oriented simplex lists to verify the chain identities and Hodge blocks. The chosen rational cases are reproducibility checks; the all-r results are established by the algebraic arguments above, not inferred from sampling. Falsifiers for overextended readings are explicit: unchanged unit weights must not split the Hodge spectrum; the fixed 3/4 frame inverse must fail away from the regular point for appropriate centered data; arbitrary six dihedral cosines need not satisfy the family’s geometric constraint; and neither a frame eigenvalue nor a shape coordinate is an elapsed time. Source basis: the retained Paper I snapshot, Section 4 (oriented chain convention and single-cell identity), and the retained 18 September angular review, Sections 2–4 (regular face frame and weighted-chain limitation). The unavailable Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was not used. No registry status is advanced under the supplied CRL-2 governance proposal. The frozen LC bench, its target sqrt(5/3), Stage 0 acquisition proposal, SER manuscript and coefficient ledger remain unchanged. Physical promotion remains 0.

content:
Run within the complete package with its dependencies. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact finite replay of the shape audit. No empirical data or physical scoring."""
from fractions import Fraction as Q
from itertools import combinations, permutations
from pathlib import Path
import json

checks = []
def check(label, condition):
    if not condition: raise AssertionError(label)
    checks.append(label)
def sub(a,b): return [x-y for x,y in zip(a,b)]
def dot(a,b): return sum(x*y for x,y in zip(a,b))
def cross(a,b): return [a[1]*b[2]-a[2]*b[1],a[2]*b[0]-a[0]*b[2],a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0]]
def tr(a): return [list(v) for v in zip(*a)]
def mm(a,b): return [[dot(row,col) for col in tr(b)] for row in a]
def plus(a,b): return [[x+y for x,y in zip(u,v)] for u,v in zip(a,b)]
def scale(c,a): return [[c*x for x in row] for row in a]
def diag(xs): return [[v if i==j else Q(0) for j in range(len(xs))] for i,v in enumerate(xs)]
def zero(a): return all(x==0 for row in a for x in row)
def encode(obj):
    if isinstance(obj,Q): return str(obj)
    if isinstance(obj,dict): return {str(k):encode(v) for k,v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj,(tuple,list)): return [encode(x) for x in obj]
    return obj

def geometry(r):
    r=Q(r)
    if r<=0: raise ValueError('Nondegenerate family requires r > 0')
    q=r*r; D=2*q+1
    P=[[Q(1),Q(1),r],[Q(1),Q(-1),-r],[Q(-1),Q(1),-r],[Q(-1),Q(-1),r]]
    M=[[-x*r,-y*r,-z/r] for x,y,z in P]
    distances={(i,j):dot(sub(P[i],P[j]),sub(P[i],P[j])) for i,j in combinations(range(4),2)}
    tag=f'r={r} '
    check(tag+'squared edges',all(v==(8 if (i,j) in ((0,3),(1,2)) else 4*(1+q)) for (i,j),v in distances.items()))
    crosses=[]
    for i in range(4):
        a,b,c=[P[j] for j in range(4) if j!=i]
        v=cross(sub(b,a),sub(c,a))
        if dot(v,sub(P[i],a))>0: v=[-x for x in v]
        crosses.append(v)
        check(tag+f'face {i}: outward normal from cross product',v==[4*x for x in M[i]])
        check(tag+f'face {i}: area squared',dot(v,v)/4==4*D)
        check(tag+f'face {i}: supporting plane',all(dot(M[i],P[j])==(r if j!=i else -3*r) for j in range(4)))
    volume=abs(dot(sub(P[1],P[0]),cross(sub(P[2],P[0]),sub(P[3],P[0]))))/6
    check(tag+'volume',volume==8*r/3)
    check(tag+'area-normal closure',all(sum(v[j] for v in crosses)==0 for j in range(3)))
    cosines={(i,j):-dot(crosses[i],crosses[j])/(16*D) for i,j in combinations(range(4),2)}
    a=(2*q-1)/D;b=1/D
    check(tag+'six interior cosines',all(v==(a if (i,j) in ((0,3),(1,2)) else b) for (i,j),v in cosines.items()))
    check(tag+'cosine domain',all(-1<v<1 for v in cosines.values()))
    check(tag+'cosine constraint and reconstruction',a+2*b==1 and (1-b)/(2*b)==q)
    F=scale(1/D,mm(tr(M),M)); G=scale(1/D,mm(M,tr(M)))
    eigen=[4*q/D,4*q/D,4/D]
    check(tag+'frame operator',F==diag(eigen))
    check(tag+'Gram eigenvectors',mm(G,M)==mm(M,diag(eigen)))
    check(tag+'Gram null vector',zero(mm(G,[[Q(1)]]*4)))
    left=mm(diag([1/(4*q),1/(4*q),Q(1,4)]),tr(M))
    check(tag+'scaled frame left inverse',mm(left,M)==diag([1,1,1]))
    projector=[[Q(int(i==j))-Q(1,4) for j in range(4)] for i in range(4)]
    check(tag+'centered-data reconstruction',mm(M,left)==projector)
    check(tag+'regular-only 3/4 inverse',(scale(Q(3,4),F)==diag([1,1,1]))==(r==1))
    def dist(i,j):return distances[tuple(sorted((i,j)))]
    sym=[p for p in permutations(range(4)) if all(dist(i,j)==dist(p[i],p[j]) for i,j in distances)]
    check(tag+'metric symmetry count',len(sym)==(24 if r==1 else 8))
    return dict(r=r,vertices=P,squared_edge_lengths={f'{i}{j}':v for (i,j),v in distances.items()},
                face_index_dihedral_cosines={f'{i}{j}':v for (i,j),v in cosines.items()},
                each_face_area_squared=4*D,volume=volume,normal_frame=F,normal_gram=G,
                frame_eigenvalues=eigen,metric_permutation_count=len(sym))

def boundary(k,simplices):
    low=simplices[k-1];high=simplices[k];a=[[0]*len(high) for _ in low]
    for j,tet in enumerate(high):
        for pos in range(len(tet)):
            face=tet[:pos]+tet[pos+1:];a[low.index(face)][j]=(-1)**pos
    return a

def main():
    cases=[geometry(r) for r in ('1/3','1/2','1','3/2','2','3')]
    try: geometry(0)
    except ValueError: check('degenerate input rejected',True)
    else: raise AssertionError('Degenerate input accepted')
    S={k:list(combinations(range(4),k+1)) for k in range(4)}
    B={k:boundary(k,S) for k in range(1,4)}
    check('boundary of boundary 1-2',zero(mm(B[1],B[2])))
    check('boundary of boundary 2-3',zero(mm(B[2],B[3])))
    L=[mm(B[1],tr(B[1])),plus(mm(tr(B[1]),B[1]),mm(B[2],tr(B[2]))),
       plus(mm(tr(B[2]),B[2]),mm(B[3],tr(B[3]))),mm(tr(B[3]),B[3])]
    check('vertex Laplacian',L[0]==[[4*int(i==j)-1 for j in range(4)] for i in range(4)])
    for k in range(1,4):check(f'L{k}=4I',L[k]==diag([4]*len(S[k])))
    A=[[0]*15 for _ in range(15)];offset=[0,4,10,14]
    for k in range(1,4):
        for i,row in enumerate(B[k]):
            for j,v in enumerate(row):
                A[offset[k-1]+i][offset[k]+j]=-v;A[offset[k]+j][offset[k-1]+i]=v
    full=[[0]*15 for _ in range(15)]
    for k in range(4):
        for i,row in enumerate(L[k]):
            for j,v in enumerate(row):full[offset[k]+i][offset[k]+j]=v
    check('skew adjoint generator',tr(A)==scale(-1,A))
    check('minus A squared equals full L',scale(-1,mm(A,A))==full)
    check('A cubed plus 4A vanishes',zero(plus(mm(mm(A,A),A),scale(4,A))))
    report={'status':'PASS','evidence_class':'EXACT_RATIONAL_CONSTRUCTOR_CHECKS',
            'check_count':len(checks),'checks':checks,'rational_cases':cases,
            'boundary_matrices':B,'laplacian_blocks':L,
            'full_hodge_spectrum':{'0':1,'4':14},'single_cell_SER_target_bound':5,
            'all_r_proof_location':'UD_TETRAHEDRAL_SHAPE_AUDIT_v0.1.md sections 1-4',
            'independent_review':False,'empirical_data_used':False,'physical_promotion':0}
    Path(__file__).with_name('EXACT_SHAPE_RESULTS.json').write_text(json.dumps(encode(report),indent=2)+'\n')
    print(f'PASS: {len(checks)} exact checks; {len(cases)} rational geometries; no empirical data.')

if __name__=='__main__':main()

Its Riesz map sends a vector to the covector H_k x; H_k^{-1} reverses that map in the declared bases. Proof: x^T H_k B_k† y=(B_k x)^T H_(k-1)y for all x,y. Positivity makes H_k invertible. Importantly, uniqueness of the adjoint does not imply uniqueness of H. Let B be the full degree-lowering boundary on the direct sum and H the block-diagonal matrix of the H_k. Define AH=B†−B,DH=B+B†,LH=BB†+B†B. A_H=B^{\dagger}-B,\qquad D_H=B+B^{\dagger},\qquad L_H=BB^{\dagger}+B^{\dagger}B. Since B²=0, (B†)²=0. Therefore −AH2=DH2=LH,AHTH+HAH=0. -A_H^2=D_H^2=L_H,\qquad A_H^T H+HA_H=0. Its determinant equals (k!)² times its squared Euclidean k-volume and is independent of the chosen base vertex. For the regular reference with squared edge length 8, these determinants are 8,48,256 for k=1,2,3. Define a dimensionless ratio Rσ=detGσdetGregular,k. R_\sigma=\frac{\det G_\sigma}{\det G_{\mathrm{regular},k}}. The assumed Euclidean coordinate geometry and reference scale are input. Neither is derived from incidence. On a nondegenerate simplex R_sigma>0; for rational coordinates it is rational. Rule B (squared Gram ratio): H_0=I, with (H_k)_(sigma,sigma)=R_sigma². All off-diagonal entries are zero. H_0=I_4,\quad H_1=\operatorname{diag}(a,a,1,1,a,a),\quad H_2=bI_4,\quad H_3=(c). Both are positive for every r>0 and recover H_k=I at r=1. With the reference held fixed, uniformly scaling the coordinates by t changes H_k by t^(2kp) and the Laplacian blocks by t^(-2p). Simultaneously rescaling both actual and reference coordinates leaves the ratios unchanged. These rules require explicit reference/scale discipline; dihedral angles alone cannot select an absolute frequency scale. 4. Direct multiplication by the uniform vector and the three sign vectors of the tetrahedral coordinates gives specL0={0,u,v,v},u=4/a,v=2+2/a. \operatorname{spec}L_0=\{0,u,v,v\},\qquad u=4/a,\quad v=2+2/a. For the higher blocks define x=4a/b,y=2(a+1)/b,z=4b/c. x=4a/b,\qquad y=2(a+1)/b,\qquad z=4b/c. Then specL1={u,v,v,x,y,y},specL2={x,y,y,z},specL3={z}. \begin{aligned} \operatorname{spec}L_1&=\{u,v,v,x,y,y\},\\ \operatorname{spec}L_2&=\{x,y,y,z\},\\ \operatorname{spec}L_3&=\{z\}. \end{aligned} Proof: B_2†B_2=(1/b)B_2^T H_1B_2 on the four face coordinates. Result and status The current finite-chain papers already specify what their amplitudes mean mathematically: real coefficients in an orthonormal oriented-simplex basis. They do not identify those coefficients with geometric densities, integrated fields, or electrical measurements. Shape alone does not supply that interpretation. This note proves a compatibility constraint and gives a conditional extension of the observation contract. Keeping the existing generator and a diagonal, additive, conserved support forces equal weights on each connected Hasse component. A shape-sensitive diagonal support therefore requires a changed generator if it is to remain conserved. For a declared fixed positive diagonal weight matrix, the corresponding local current and positive-ray receipt can be written exactly. Status: internal mathematical development; elementary algebra, no independent novelty claim, no independent human review. No canonical geometric weighting is selected. No physical promotion, spacetime metric, time unit, bench result, or retriangulation equivalence is asserted. The frozen LC acquisition and scoring contracts are unaffected. 2. Baseline and notation Let KK be a finite oriented simplicial complex, using nonaugmented real chains. Stack its simplex coordinates by degree into cc. Let BB be the total degree-lowering boundary matrix, so B2=0B^2=0. For a codimension-one incidence σ⊂η\sigma\subset\eta, Bση=±1B_{\sigma\eta}=\pm1. The existing source uses the dimensionless evolution parameter ss and ċ=A0c,A0=BT−B,S0=cTc. \dot c=A_0c,\qquad A_0=B^T-B,\qquad S_0=c^Tc. Its per-simplex stocks and signed incidence currents are qσ0=cσ2,Jση0=2Bσηcσcη. q^0_\sigma=c_\sigma^2,\qquad J^0_{\sigma\eta}=2B_{\sigma\eta}c_\sigma c_\eta. A positive current transfers stock from the lower-degree coordinate to the upper-degree coordinate. This is an algebraic convention, not a physical identification. The Hasse graph has one vertex per simplex coordinate and an undirected edge per nonzero boundary entry. Connectedness below refers to this graph, not the graph of currently nonzero amplitudes. The latter can have more components when amplitudes vanish. 3. Fixed-source diagonal-support theorem Proposition 1. Let H=diag(hσ)H=\operatorname{diag}(h_\sigma) be fixed, with hσ>0h_\sigma>0. Then SH=cTHcS_H=c^THc is conserved by ċ=A0c\dot c=A_0c for every initial state if and only if hσ=hηh_\sigma=h_\eta on every Hasse incidence. Consequently, HH is a positive scalar multiple of the identity on each connected Hasse component. Fixing a reference weight to one in each component gives H=IH=I. Proof. Conservation for every initial state is equivalent to A0TH+HA0=0. A_0^TH+HA_0=0. Indeed the derivative is the associated symmetric quadratic form, whose vanishing for all real vectors implies the symmetric matrix is zero. Since A0T=−A0A_0^T=-A_0, the matrix is HA0−A0HHA_0-A_0H. Its (σ,η)(\sigma,\eta) entry is (hσ−hη)(A0)ση. (h_\sigma-h_\eta)(A_0)_{\sigma\eta}. Every incidence has nonzero (A0)ση(A_0)_{\sigma\eta}; nonincidences impose no condition. Equality propagates along paths. Conversely, constant weights on components commute with A0A_0. ▫\square This theorem does not force regular tetrahedra. It says that an unchanged incidence-only generator cannot conserve arbitrary relative geometric reweightings of its existing independent stocks. A common overall weight may still depend on externally fixed geometry; it contributes no relative shape weighting within a component. Scope check: non-diagonal metrics are not excluded. Put ℒ=−A02=A0TA0\mathcal L=-A_0^2=A_0^TA_0. Then H×=I+ℒH_\times=I+\mathcal L is positive definite and commutes with A0A_0, hence is conserved by the same generator. Proposition 1 is not a uniqueness theorem for all conserved quadratic forms. 4. Declared weighted dynamics and local continuity For a fixed positive diagonal HH, retain the same boundary matrix and define its weighted adjoint and a candidate generator: B†H=H−1BTH,AH=B†H−B. B^{\dagger_H}=H^{-1}B^TH,\qquad A_H=B^{\dagger_H}-B. Then AHTH+HAH=0A_H^TH+HA_H=0. Set qσ=hσcσ2,SH=∑σqσ,JσηH=2Bσηhσcσcη. q_\sigma=h_\sigma c_\sigma^2,\qquad S_H=\sum_\sigma q_\sigma,\qquad \boxed{J^H_{\sigma\eta}=2B_{\sigma\eta}h_\sigma c_\sigma c_\eta.} The weight in this expression belongs to the lower-degree simplex. Proposition 2. Under ċ=AHc\dot c=A_Hc, q̇σ=∑ξ:ξ⊂σJξσH−∑η:σ⊂ηJσηH, \dot q_\sigma= \sum_{\xi:\,\xi\subset\sigma}J^H_{\xi\sigma} -\sum_{\eta:\,\sigma\subset\eta}J^H_{\sigma\eta}, where both sums are over codimension-one incidences. Proof. An upper neighbor contributes −Bσηcη-B_{\sigma\eta}c_\eta to ċσ\dot c_\sigma; multiplication by 2hσcσ2h_\sigma c_\sigma gives −JσηH-J^H_{\sigma\eta}. A lower neighbor contributes hσ−1Bξσhξcξh_\sigma^{-1}B_{\xi\sigma}h_\xi c_\xi, giving +JξσH+J^H_{\xi\sigma}. Summing over coordinates cancels every incidence pair. Summing over a subset cancels internal incidences and gives the corresponding cut balance. ▫\square In normalized coordinates y=H1/2cy=H^{1/2}c, this is JσηH=2Bσηhσ/hηyσyη. J^H_{\sigma\eta}=2B_{\sigma\eta} \sqrt{h_\sigma/h_\eta}\,y_\sigma y_\eta. Neither a zero state nor an uncertain forest-current sign can be normalized into a valid exact receipt. The exact current consistency test becomes (JσηH)2=4hσhηqσqη,(JσηHSH)2=4hσhηpσpη. \boxed{(J^H_{\sigma\eta})^2 =4\frac{h_\sigma}{h_\eta}q_\sigma q_\eta,}\qquad \left(\frac{J^H_{\sigma\eta}}{S_H}\right)^2 =4\frac{h_\sigma}{h_\eta}p_\sigma p_\eta. Signs must still have product one around every cycle of the nonzero support graph. Given positive stocks, compatible signs, root signs, and known weights, reconstruction realizes currents with these magnitudes and signs. At zero endpoints the current must be zero. The legacy unit-weight test cannot be retained unchanged where endpoint weights differ and both stocks are nonzero. These formulas are a conditional extension of the existing PSR contract, not evidence of a measured device. The weight matrix is supplied metadata; no inverse problem establishing its recovery from observations is solved here. One could instead report rescaled currents J̃ση=hη/hσJσηH\widetilde J_{\sigma\eta}=\sqrt{h_\eta/h_\sigma}J^H_{\sigma\eta}, which satisfy the legacy product identity for yy. Those rescaled quantities are not the currents in the local continuity law above. 6. Explicit nonregular counterexample Use the previous disphenoid family p0=(1,1,r),p1=(1,−1,−r),p2=(−1,1,−r),p3=(−1,−1,r). p_0=(1,1,r),\quad p_1=(1,-1,-r),\quad p_2=(-1,1,-r),\quad p_3=(-1,-1,r). At r=2r=2, the previous squared-volume-ratio candidate (Rule A) gives h0=1h_0=1, h01=5/2h_{01}=5/2. Set c0=2c_0=2, c01=−3c_{01}=-3, all other coordinates zero, with B0,01=−1B_{0,01}=-1. Then q0=4,q01=45/2,SH=53/2,J0,01H=12. q_0=4,\quad q_{01}=45/2,\quad S_H=53/2,\quad J^H_{0,01}=12. The correct squared current is 144144, while the legacy expression 4q0q014q_0q_{01} gives 360360. Multiplication by h0/h01=2/5h_0/h_{01}=2/5 restores 144144. Under the old generator A0A_0, this same weighted support has instantaneous derivative 1818; under AHA_H, its derivative is zero. This is an exact algebraic witness that geometry-dependent weights cannot simply be inserted into the old support and receipt formulas. 7. What an amplitude interpretation would add The existing source definition is complete for its abstract algebra. A geometric interpretation is additional structure. Three distinct contracts should be distinguished: Interpretation of a coefficient Declared norm Geometric implication Existing abstract chain amplitude ∑cσ2\sum c_\sigma^2 Unit weights; dihedral angles can accompany the state as geometry metadata Constant scalar density on a cell of measure VV ∫ρ2dV=ρ2V\int\rho^2\,dV=\rho^2V Relative weight V/VrefV/V_{\mathrm{ref}} after reference normalization Integrated scalar quantity Q=ρVQ=\rho V on that cell ∫ρ2dV=Q2/V\int\rho^2\,dV=Q^2/V Relative weight Vref/VV_{\mathrm{ref}}/V after reference normalization The last two rows are conditional derivations for constant scalar densities, with separately chosen reference units for each interpretation. They do not establish a norm for all simplex degrees at once. Mixing dimensions requires explicit reference measures and amplitude units. In particular, the two squared-volume candidates in the previous interface note are not selected by either scalar-density calculation. For differential forms, simplex integrals are cochain degrees of freedom. A Whitney reconstruction ω=∑iaiWi\omega=\sum_i a_iW_i has ∥ω∥L22=aTMa,Mij=⟨Wi,Wj⟩L2. \|\omega\|_{L^2}^2=a^TMa,\qquad M_{ij}=\langle W_i,W_j\rangle_{L^2}. Overlapping basis forms generally produce off-diagonal terms. An inverse-volume diagonal rule is not automatically the Whitney mass matrix. This chain/cochain distinction is standard in finite element exterior calculus [3]; adopting that route requires a specified interpolation and inner product, beyond the present diagonal-stock contract. 8. Consequence for dihedral-angle research The prior shape audit showed that the disphenoid’s two interior-dihedral cosine classes determine its dimensionless shape parameter r2r^2, but not its scale. That information is already a legitimate geometric observable. It does not by itself select a meaning for chain amplitudes or a transport law. The next well-defined modelling decision is therefore an amplitude-to-geometry contract: state the represented quantity, its units or reference normalization, its interpolation if applicable, the conserved quadratic form, and the resulting observable currents. This note supplies the exact checks for a diagonal contract. Until such a contract is adopted, preserve the existing orthonormal-amplitude model and report shape observables separately. If geometry varies with ss, the fixed-weight proof no longer suffices: dds(cTH(s)c)=cTḢ(s)c \frac{d}{ds}(c^TH(s)c)=c^T\dot H(s)c when the instantaneous generator is AH(s)A_{H(s)}. An additional transport or exchange law would be needed to remove or interpret this term. No such law is chosen here. The parameter ss remains dimensionless and is not identified with a sink-reversal count or an LC period. 9. It builds the oriented filled tetrahedron directly, checks the 28-incidence constraint matrix has rank 14, and verifies a non-diagonal conserved-form counterexample. It evaluates both previous geometric rules at r=1/2,1,3/2,2,3r=1/2,1,3/2,2,3, with dense, sparse incident-pair, and disconnected-support states. The script checks weighted skew-adjointness, per-coordinate continuity, global balance, reconstruction of squared magnitudes and signs, forest sizes, weighted current consistency, the explicit legacy-contract failure, and zero-state rejection. Current session checkpoint.Markdown source · LaTeX source · Complete package1. Decision and exact result This development note supplies a concrete, reversible amplitude-to-geometry interface. It interprets an existing abstract amplitude through normalized simplex measures, while keeping the original finite-chain evolution as the reference model. It is a candidate source addendum, development — no registry entry. No coefficient, frozen manuscript, LC bench rule, or physical claim is promoted. The central result is that density and integrated-quantity coordinates can represent the same state and the same dynamics. Their norms look different, but their spectra, stocks, currents, and positive-ray receipts agree when every operator is transformed consistently. Choosing a density interpretation therefore does not, by itself, create a shape-dependent frequency prediction. The candidate is useful as a baseline: any proposed shape-sensitive dynamics can be compared against it to determine whether the change survives removal of coordinate effects. It is elementary change-of-basis algebra, with no independent novelty claim. 2. Explicit semantic assumptions Use the existing nonaugmented oriented simplex chain coordinates aa, boundary BB, generator A0=BT−BA_0=B^T-B, and conserved support S=aTaS=a^Ta. The evolution parameter ss is dimensionless. No identification with SER ticks or laboratory duration is made. For each simplex σ\sigma of degree kk, supply a positive geometric measure VσV_\sigma, a fixed positive reference VσrefV^{\mathrm{ref}}_\sigma, and the dimensionless ratio vσ=Vσ/Vσref,V=diag(vσ),D=V1/2. v_\sigma=V_\sigma/V^{\mathrm{ref}}_\sigma,\qquad V=\operatorname{diag}(v_\sigma),\qquad D=V^{1/2}. For vertices use counting measure, hence vσ=1v_\sigma=1. Reference measures are part of the declared convention; they are not fitted to spectra. Require compatible values for an identified shared simplex. Degenerate simplices with zero measure are excluded. Define signed scalar amplitude densities, not material densities, by a=Dρ=D−1m,m=Vρ. \boxed{a=D\rho=D^{-1}m,\qquad m=V\rho.} Here ρ\rho is a normalized density coordinate and mm its normalized integrated coordinate. For one scalar field constant on a simplex, let ρphys\rho^{\mathrm{phys}} denote its dimensional value, with reference value ρref\rho^{\mathrm{ref}}. Run within the complete package with its dependencies. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact rational coordinate-contract checks; synthetic basis scales, no measurements."""
from pathlib import Path
from itertools import combinations
from fractions import Fraction as Q
import sys,json
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path(__file__).parent/'dependencies'))
from shape_helpers import mm,tr,plus,scale,diag,zero,boundary,encode
checks=[]
def check(label,x):
    if not x:raise AssertionError(label)
    checks.append(label)
def mv(M,x):return [sum(a*b for a,b in zip(row,x)) for row in M]
def inverse(M):
    n=len(M);a=[list(row)+[Q(i==j) for j in range(n)] for i,row in enumerate(M)]
    for j in range(n):
        p=next(k for k in range(j,n) if a[k][j]);a[j],a[p]=a[p],a[j]
        v=a[j][j];a[j]=[x/v for x in a[j]]
        for k in range(n):
            if k!=j:
                f=a[k][j];a[k]=[x-f*y for x,y in zip(a[k],a[j])]
    return [row[n:] for row in a]
def minus(a,b):return plus(a,scale(-1,b))
S={k:list(combinations(range(4),k+1)) for k in range(4)}
n=15;offset=[0,4,10,14];I=diag([Q(1)]*n)
B=[[Q(0)]*n for _ in range(n)]
for k in range(1,4):
    for i,row in enumerate(boundary(k,S)):
        for j,x in enumerate(row):B[offset[k-1]+i][offset[k]+j]=Q(x)
A=minus(tr(B),B);edges=[(i,j,B[i][j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if B[i][j]]
def conjugate(A,d):return mm(mm(diag([1/x for x in d]),A),diag(d))
def run():
    check('boundary nilpotency',zero(mm(B,B)))
    check('source skew',zero(plus(tr(A),A)))
    check('filled-tet minimal polynomial',zero(plus(mm(mm(A,A),A),scale(4,A))))
    # A Cayley transform is an exact orthogonal test step; NOT an exact-time exponential.
    t=Q(1,5);U=mm(inverse(minus(I,scale(t,A))),plus(I,scale(t,A)))
    check('exact rational orthogonal test step',mm(tr(U),U)==I)
    scales=[[Q(1)]*n,[Q(1)]*4+[Q(i+2,3) for i in range(11)],
            [Q(i+1,5) for i in range(n)]]
    a=[Q((-1)**i*(i+1),7) for i in range(n)]
    total=sum(x*x for x in a);records=[]
    for k,d in enumerate(scales):
        tag=f'basis case {k}: ';v=[x*x for x in d];V=diag(v);Vi=diag([1/x for x in v])
        R=conjugate(A,d);M=conjugate(A,[1/x for x in d]);Br=conjugate(B,d)
        rho=[x/y for x,y in zip(a,d)];m=[x*y for x,y in zip(a,d)]
        check(tag+'coordinate identity',m==mv(V,rho))
        check(tag+'three equal supports',sum(v[i]*rho[i]**2 for i in range(n))==total==sum(m[i]**2/v[i] for i in range(n)))
        check(tag+'density weighted skew',zero(plus(mm(tr(R),V),mm(V,R))))
        check(tag+'integral weighted skew',zero(plus(mm(tr(M),Vi),mm(Vi,M))))
        check(tag+'coordinate conjugacy',M==mm(mm(V,R),Vi))
        check(tag+'transformed boundary nilpotency',zero(mm(Br,Br)))
        check(tag+'transformed adjoint generator',R==minus(mm(mm(Vi,tr(Br)),V),Br))
        check(tag+'same minimal polynomial',zero(plus(mm(mm(R,R),R),scale(4,R))))
        check(tag+'same squared-generator trace',sum(mm(R,R)[i][i] for i in range(n))==-56)
        for label,c,h,gen,dd in [('density',rho,v,R,d),('integral',m,[1/x for x in v],M,[1/x for x in d])]:
            currents=[2*b*dd[i]*dd[j]*c[i]*c[j] for i,j,b in edges]
            check(tag+label+' currents unchanged',currents==[2*b*a[i]*a[j] for i,j,b in edges])
            dr=mv(gen,c);balance=[Q(0)]*n
            for (i,j,b),flow in zip(edges,currents):balance[i]-=flow;balance[j]+=flow
            check(tag+label+' local continuity',balance==[2*h[i]*c[i]*dr[i] for i in range(n)])
            check(tag+label+' current consistency',all(flow**2==4*h[i]*c[i]**2*h[j]*c[j]**2 for (i,j,b),flow in zip(edges,currents)))
            step=conjugate(U,dd);new=mv(step,c)
            check(tag+label+' finite-step intertwining',mv(diag(dd),new)==mv(U,a))
            check(tag+label+' finite-step support',sum(h[i]*new[i]**2 for i in range(n))==total)
        # d' is an arbitrary local coordinate-scale velocity, not a shape evolution law.
        dprime=[Q((-1)**i,11) for i in range(n)];g=[x/y for x,y in zip(dprime,d)]
        Vdot=diag([2*d[i]*dprime[i] for i in range(n)])
        Rmoving=minus(R,diag(g));Mmoving=plus(M,diag(g))
        check(tag+'moving density conservation',zero(plus(plus(mm(tr(Rmoving),V),mm(V,Rmoving)),Vdot)))
        Vidot=diag([-2*dprime[i]/d[i]**3 for i in range(n)])
        check(tag+'moving integral conservation',zero(plus(plus(mm(tr(Mmoving),Vi),mm(Vi,Mmoving)),Vidot)))
        check(tag+'moving coordinate relation',Mmoving==plus(mm(mm(V,Rmoving),Vi),mm(Vdot,Vi)))
        fixed=minus(mm(mm(Vi,tr(B)),V),B)
        check(tag+'fixed B differs except unit case',(fixed==R)==(k==0))
        records.append({'case':k,'sqrt_volume_ratios':d,'volume_ratios':v,'interpretation':'synthetic positive coordinate scales; not claimed tetrahedron geometry'})
    d0,d1,d2=scales
    T01=diag([a/b for a,b in zip(d0,d1)]);T12=diag([a/b for a,b in zip(d1,d2)]);T20=diag([a/b for a,b in zip(d2,d0)])
    check('pure coordinate roundtrip identity',mm(mm(T20,T12),T01)==I)
    check('density support preserving expansion changes integral',Q(4)*Q(1,2)==2)
    check('integral preserving expansion changes squared support',Q(4)*Q(1,4)**2==Q(1,4))
    # These are squared actual measure ratios from the exact disphenoid family.
    geometry=[]
    for r in map(Q,['1/2','1','2','3']):
        q=r*r;e=(1+q)/2;f=(2*q+1)/3
        check(f'r={r}: positive geometric measures',min(e,f,q)>0)
        check(f'r={r}: regular reference iff r=1',(e==f==q==1)==(r==1))
        geometry.append({'r':r,'edge_03_12_ratio_squared':Q(1),'other_edge_ratio_squared':e,'face_ratio_squared':f,'cell_ratio':r})
    for ell in map(Q,['1/2','1','5/2']):
        W=[[Q(0)]*4 for _ in range(4)]
        for i,j in combinations(range(4),2):
            w=Q(1) if (i,j) in ((0,3),(1,2)) else 1/ell
            W[i][i]+=w;W[j][j]+=w;W[i][j]-=w;W[j][i]-=w
        modes=[([1,1,1,1],Q(0)),([1,-1,-1,1],4/ell),([1,0,0,-1],2+2/ell),([0,1,-1,0],2+2/ell)]
        for j,(vector,value) in enumerate(modes):
            check(f'weighted vertex mode ell={ell}, branch={j}',mv(W,vector)==[value*x for x in vector])
    report={'status':'PASS','check_count':len(checks),'checks':checks,'coordinate_cases':records,'disphenoid_measure_data':geometry,
            'physical_promotion':0,'canonical_rule_selected':False,'empirical_data_used':False,'independent_review':False,
            'finite_test_step':'Cayley transform, not exact exponential at a claimed time'}
    Path(__file__).with_name('EXACT_CONTRACT_RESULTS.json').write_text(json.dumps(encode(report),indent=2)+'\n')
    print(f'PASS: {len(checks)} exact rational checks; 3 coordinate cases and 4 disphenoid measure cases.')

Their chain spaces have dimensions 23 and 27. Their labeled union has dimension 30 and is the boundary of a 4-simplex, giving integral coordinate inclusions into a common space. The difference of the zero-extended skew operators has rank 18, certified by a determinant-one minor and a twelve-dimensional kernel. Both local triangulations have trivial reduced integer homology and the same oriented exterior boundary, but their operator spectra differ. We specify the changes in incidence receipts and show that the overlap projection is neither a chain map nor a norm-preserving jump rule.
