E=\{01,12,23,30\}. This is C4C_4. It is: reciprocal; connected; vertex-transitive, hence non-privileged at the vertex level; internally mediated by paths; incomplete, with four rather than six edges. Therefore non-privilege, reciprocity, and connectedness do not force complete pairwise coupling. Ruling: G3 is false without a stronger coupling axiom. 3.5 Five-role case A fifth independent role is not inconsistent. It is excluded only by minimality if four roles have already been proved sufficient and carrier-distinct. Conversely, a fifth redundant or derived role does not refute four-function sufficiency. Ruling: five-role systems are admissible nonminimal extensions; they do not establish or defeat four-role minimality by themselves. 4. Paper IV draft 0.1 supplies a dedicated treatment of prepared controllers, capture and renewal. Section numbering and PT identifiers in this paper remain stable. Abstract We consolidate symmetry, radial refinement and prepared collective developments on declared tetrahedral carriers. Signed filled-tetrahedron chains have commutant dimensions 13, 10 and 3 for the full, self-adjoint and skew-adjoint families. Explicit annulus and center-filled shell constructions retain exact topology and representation decompositions. A confining depth operator has compact resolvent and fixed-index finite-shell convergence; four low spectral enclosures are repaired with new rational polynomials, exact root counts and an explicit infinite min-max proof. Scalar Weyl descriptions are restricted to visible modes pending infinite cyclicity. The six-edge relation algebra and minimum context dimension three are retained, with an explicit compatible basis proving covariance of the supplied context tensor. Prepared shape, burden, renewal, finite controller, timed capture and static capture-window results are integrated with their resource ledgers and no-gos. No universal relation strength, native preparation, perpetual storage or physical Hamiltonian is derived. 1. Scope and contribution boundary The purpose of this paper is to collect a set of post-companion mathematical results that enlarge the finite tetrahedral carrier while preserving a narrow claim boundary. The results concern finite S4S_4 representation theory, pure simplicial shell constructions, a declared radial operator family, and its infinite-volume spectral reduction. The basic chain conventions and skew Hodge–Dirac setup are those of the companion finite-carrier paper; the deterministic reconstruction problem is treated separately in the companion projective-receipt paper. Neither companion is logically required for the new shell triangulation once the tetrahedral vertex action is fixed. The ordinary background is standard. Finite-group characters and Schur’s lemma are used in the usual sense [1]. Simplicial boundary operators and combinatorial Laplacians follow the familiar discrete-exterior-calculus and simplicial-Laplacian setting [2-4]. The infinite radial reduction belongs to the general spectral theory of Jacobi-type difference operators and Weyl functions [5]. What is not claimed. The shell index is not a principal quantum number; the declared Hr,βH_{r, eta} is not asserted to be a physical Hamiltonian; EE and T2T_2 are representation labels, not particle names; the radial depth is an internal combinatorial function, not a physical radius; and no energy, action, mass, charge, or time unit is supplied. Any later correspondence to a physical system would require an independently specified carrier map and empirical test. 2. Representation theory of the filled tetrahedron Chain decomposition Let P≅ℝ4P\cong\mathbb{R}^4 be the natural permutation representation of S4S_4 on the vertices of a tetrahedron. With the increasing-order orientation convention, the chain spaces identify with exterior powers, C0≅Λ1P,C1≅Λ2P,C2≅Λ3P,C3≅Λ4P.C_0\cong\Lambda^1P,\qquad C_1\cong\Lambda^2P,\qquad C_2\cong\Lambda^3P,\qquad C_3\cong\Lambda^4P. We use the conventional irreducible labels A1,A2,E,T1,T2A_1,A_2,E,T_1,T_2 for the five real irreducible representations of S4S_4. Theorem 1 (Oriented-chain decomposition). Under the natural S4S_4 action, C0=A1⊕T2,C1=T2⊕T1, oxed{C_0=A_1\oplus T_2},\qquad  oxed{C_1=T_2\oplus T_1}, C2=T1⊕A2,C3=A2. oxed{C_2=T_1\oplus A_2},\qquad  oxed{C_3=A_2}. Consequently, 𝒞=C0⊕C1⊕C2⊕C3=A1⊕2A2⊕2T1⊕2T2.\mathcal C=C_0\oplus C_1\oplus C_2\oplus C_3 =A_1\oplus2A_2\oplus2T_1\oplus2T_2. In particular, EE is absent from the linear chain carrier. Proof. The natural permutation representation decomposes as P=A1⊕T2P=A_1\oplus T_2. Taking exterior powers and reducing the corresponding characters gives the displayed sequence. Equivalently, the decomposition follows directly from the character table of S4S_4 and the character formula for exterior powers. The dimensions 4,6,4,14,6,4,1 provide the independent dimension check. ▫\square Corollary 2 (Symmetry typing of adjacent Hodge channels). The equivariant boundary maps couple only common irreducible sectors. Thus the three adjacent-degree exchange channels are T2:C0↔C1,T1:C1↔C2,A2:C2↔C3, oxed{T_2:\ C_0\leftrightarrow C_1},\qquad  oxed{T_1:\ C_1\leftrightarrow C_2},\qquad  oxed{A_2:\ C_2\leftrightarrow C_3}, with an isolated harmonic A1A_1 vertex mode. Proof. Equivariance of each boundary map with the vertex-permutation action and Schur’s lemma imply that inequivalent irreducible sectors cannot couple. The dimensions in Theorem 1 then identify the active channel in each adjacent pair. In particular, kerB1≅T1\ker B_1\cong T_1 and the uniform vertex vector spans the A1A_1 harmonic sector. ▫\square Quadratic traceless parent Proposition 3 (Quadratic E⊕T2E\oplus T_2 sector). For the standard three-dimensional T2T_2 representation, Sym2(T2)=A1⊕E⊕T2,\operatorname{Sym}^2(T_2)=A_1\oplus E\oplus T_2, so after removing the scalar trace, Sym02(T2)=E⊕T2. oxed{\operatorname{Sym}^2_0(T_2)=E\oplus T_2}. Proof. The symmetric-square character is χsym2(g)=12(χ(g)2+χ(g2))\chi_{\mathrm{sym}^2}(g)= rac12(\chi(g)^2+\chi(g^2)). Reducing this character against the five irreducible characters of S4S_4 gives one copy each of A1,E,T2A_1,E,T_2. The A1A_1 summand is the trace. ▫\square No-go 4 (No linear E→T2E	o T_2 intertwiner). There is no nonzero S4S_4-equivariant linear map J:E→T2J:E	o T_2: HomS4(E,T2)=0. oxed{\operatorname{Hom}_{S_4}(E,T_2)=0}. Proof. The two representations are inequivalent irreducibles, so the statement is Schur’s lemma. ▫\square The useful interpretation of Proposition 3 and No-go 4 is therefore representation-theoretic: EE and T2T_2 can appear as sibling summands of a common quadratic parent, but they cannot be identified by an S4S_4-equivariant linear isomorphism. 2.3 The full signed commutant Proposition III.S1 (equivariant family dimensions). On all fifteen signed filled-tetrahedron chain coordinates the decomposition is A1⊕2A2⊕2T1⊕2T2. A_1\oplus2A_2\oplus2T_1\oplus2T_2. The real commutant has dimension 13, its self-adjoint part dimension 10 and its skew-adjoint part dimension 3. Proof. All the listed irreducibles have real scalar endomorphism algebra. The existing nonuniform vertex-chain sector provides a source-native T2T_2 context. Problem The self-consistent Reynolds parent operator has the form H[ψ]=λE[ψ]PE+λT2[ψ]PT2, H[\psi] = \lambda_E[\psi]P_E + \lambda_{T_2}[\psi]P_{T_2}, so it cannot move population between the inequivalent EE and T2T_2 sectors. The minimum possible context dimension is 3. \boxed{3}. The two co-minimal choices are T1orT2. \boxed{T_1\quad\text{or}\quad T_2}. Their S4S_4 permutation representation is A1⊕E, \boxed{ A_1\oplus E, } not T1T_1 or T2T_2. Consequently E⊗(A1⊕E) E\otimes(A_1\oplus E) contains no T2T_2. For a current vertex-chain state c0c_0, define ξT2=(I−14J)c0. \xi_{T_2} = \left( I-\frac14J \right)c_0. If nonzero, normalize ξ̂=ξT2∥ξT2∥. \widehat\xi = \frac{\xi_{T_2}}{\|\xi_{T_2}\|}. The T2T_2 lane is used below as the simplest orientation-even mainline; T1T_1 remains an equally minimal oriented-cycle alternative. 5. Fix the normalization 𝒞𝒞†=IT2. \boxed{ \mathcal C\mathcal C^\dagger=I_{T_2}. } This removes any adjustable amplitude from the representation map itself. For context coordinates ξ=(ξ1,ξ2,ξ3), \xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3), define Γξ=∑a=13ξaΓa:E→T2. \Gamma_\xi = \sum_{a=1}^3 \xi_a\Gamma_a: E\to T_2. For nonzero generic context, [Kξ,PE]≠0, \boxed{ [K_\xi,P_E]\ne0, } so it permits population transfer between the two symmetry sectors. It transforms covariantly: Kgξ=ρW(g)KξρW(g)−1. \boxed{ K_{g\xi} = \rho_W(g) K_\xi \rho_W(g)^{-1}. } Thus no preferred labeled vertex or edge is introduced. Numerical residuals are at floating-point scale. The replay verifies: unitarity; involution; S4S_4 covariance; noncommutation with the sector projector; actual population transfer for generic context. The recommended publication posture is: \[  oxed{ ext{small Review 1.1 delta} + ext{separate future symmetry/radial/context paper(s)}} \] This follows the existing review-preparation rule: preserve a small review surface, compress the theorem spine, and add theorem growth only when it materially strengthens the scoped paper. ## Recommended Review edition 1.1 delta ### Paper I Only three post-source additions are recommended for serious consideration: 1. **D01 — exact \(S_4\) decomposition of \(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3\)**. 2. **D02 — exact symmetry typing of the adjacent Hodge channels**. 3. **D12 — exact six-edge adjacent/opposite relation algebra and the no-go that symmetry alone does not determine the \(E/T_2\) ordering**. These are all finite, source-adjacent results on carriers already present in Paper I. They can be written without atomic-orbital language. ### Paper II \[  oxed{ ext{No Sep-20 theorem addition is recommended for Paper II Review 1.1.}} \] Paper II is already tightly scoped around deterministic reconstruction, the parity-degree identifiability obstruction, the frozen 14+14 tree/chord split, covariance pushforward and its limitations. The orbital/radial/context work does not materially strengthen that theorem spine. ## Do not merge the following into Review 1.1 The pure shell/radial carrier, central binding family, infinite-r convergence, block-Jacobi/Weyl analysis, Reynolds constitutive closure, self-consistent parent dynamics and context-transfer program are mathematically substantial but collectively define a **new research program**. Merging them into Paper I/II would materially enlarge carrier, operator and interpretation scope. The correct posture is to preserve them as append-only research objects and promote only exact pieces into a future dedicated paper. ## Target-exposure firewall The following must not be used as retrospective atomic evidence: - the opposite-only relation operator; - any \(w_{ m opp}/w_{ m adj}\) choice motivated by known tetrahedral orbital ordering; - the later \(E/T_2\) ancestry rule as a repair of the first ordering comparison; - Reynolds closure or polar-swap response as a retroactive held-out success. content: Paper III draft, independently reconstructed finite checks, and explicit release corrections. Candidate context response and physical acquisition remain separate. Symmetry, radial shells and context transfer Supporting mathematical review · 20 September 2026 The new draft extends the finite mathematics into symmetry-resolved shell complexes and a declared radial operator family. Papers I and II remain Review edition 1.0. Paper III is available here as Review draft 0.1, with a partial independent reproduction and a release-readiness assessment. Publication in this record does not adopt every developmental claim into the two-paper edition. Read the supplied Paper III PDF · Download the review and partial reproduction · Verification results 1. What the new mathematics adds The natural vertex-permutation action gives the oriented tetrahedron a precise symmetry decomposition: C0=A1⊕T2,C1=T2⊕T1,C2=T1⊕A2,C3=A2. C_0=A_1\oplus T_2,\quad C_1=T_2\oplus T_1,\quad C_2=T_1\oplus A_2,\quad C_3=A_2. Here T2T_2 denotes the standard three-dimensional representation of S4S_4, and T1T_1 its sign twist. These are representation labels. The two-dimensional representation EE is absent from the linear chain, but appears in the traceless symmetric square: Sym02(T2)=E⊕T2. \operatorname{Sym}^2_0(T_2)=E\oplus T_2. An annulus built by coning triangulated prism boundaries provides a larger, symmetry-preserving simplicial carrier. Adding a central vertex and filling the inner boundary gives a ball. Repeated annulus attachment then supplies a family of finite shell complexes. This is a construction in discrete geometry; shell depth has no physical length unit. 2. What was independently reproduced The accompanying verifier uses exact SymPy arithmetic. It reconstructs the tetrahedra from the draft’s written construction rather than claiming recovery of the missing author archive. Object Independent result Scope Oriented tetrahedron All four chain decompositions and the symmetric-square decomposition agree Character calculations Annulus f=(18,76,116,56)f=(18,76,116,56), boundary ranks (17,59,56)(17,59,56), Betti numbers (1,0,1,0)(1,0,1,0) Eight boundary triangles; invariance under all 24 vertex permutations Center-filled ball f=(19,80,122,60)f=(19,80,122,60), boundary ranks (18,62,60)(18,62,60), Betti numbers (1,0,0,0)(1,0,0,0) Four outer boundary triangles Annulus vertex Laplacian Characteristic polynomial agrees with the two displayed multiplicity blocks and the EE eigenvalue 6 Spectral factorization; not a supplied basis-intertwiner replay Six-edge relations Projector, adjacent/opposite Laplacian and pair-aggregate formulas agree Exact finite algebra Minimum context T1T_1 and T2T_2 are the co-minimal irreducible choices Linear equivariant coupling Supplied transfer tensor CCT=I3CC^T=I_3 and tr(ΓaTΓb)=δab\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_a^T\Gamma_b)=\delta_{ab} Exact normalization Polar response Symmetry and involution pass at ranks two, one and zero Representative exact cases, supported by the general algebra below Boundary incidence and homology alone do not characterize a 3-manifold. The annulus/ball interpretation also uses the described geometric prism subdivision and coning construction. Each annulus attachment adds (14,70,112,56)(14,70,112,56) simplices after identifying the common boundary. Starting from the four-tetrahedron central fill gives f(Kr)=(14r−9,70r−60,112r−102,56r−52),r≥1. f(K_r)=(14r-9,70r-60,112r-102,56r-52),\qquad r\ge1. This recurrence follows from the declared gluing construction. The verifier checks the annulus and the first filled annulus; it does not exhaustively generate arbitrary radial depth. 3. Context transfer: the result and the modeling choice A nonzero equivariant linear map R⊗E→T2R\otimes E\to T_2 requires a T1T_1 or T2T_2 component in RR. The exact products are E⊗E=A1⊕A2⊕E,E⊗T1=E⊗T2=T1⊕T2. E\otimes E=A_1\oplus A_2\oplus E,\qquad E\otimes T_1=E\otimes T_2=T_1\oplus T_2. Consequently, the smallest possible context has dimension three. The three-state matching shells transform as A1⊕EA_1\oplus E; their dimension alone does not make them suitable. This is a selection rule for the stated linear equivariant channel, not a prohibition on every nonlinear construction. The nonuniform vertex sector supplies a possible T2T_2 input. Once bases and representation actions are fixed, multiplicity one determines an equivariant channel up to scale; a real normalized channel still has an overall sign choice. In the complex setting there is an overall phase choice. The supplied matrices obey the declared normalization, so ∥Γξ∥F2=∥ξ∥2. \|\Gamma_\xi\|_F^2=\|\xi\|^2. Thus every nonzero ξ\xi gives a nonzero off-diagonal direction KξK_\xi, and [Kξ,PE]≠0[K_\xi,P_E]\ne0. The covariance identity for these specific matrix entries additionally requires the corresponding context, EE, and parent action matrices. Those basis-specific matrices and the original random-replay script are absent from this batch; normalization alone does not verify covariance. The polar partial isometry VV gives the proposed block response U=(I−V†VV†VI−VV†). U=\begin{pmatrix}I-V^\dagger V&V^\dagger\\V&I-VV^\dagger\end{pmatrix}. Let P=V†VP=V^\dagger V and Q=VV†Q=VV^\dagger. Since P,QP,Q are projections and VP=QV=VVP=QV=V, direct block multiplication gives U†=UU^\dagger=U and U2=IU^2=I. This identity holds for every such partial isometry. At zero context, the specified response is the identity. Choosing this involution as a response law remains a model proposal. The representation theorem supplies neither its occurrence rule nor a continuous coupling strength. Normalizing a matrix does not derive a rate. The response also need not vary continuously when rank changes: along a positive ray approaching zero, the nonzero polar factor is unchanged, while the definition sets U0=IU_0=I. 4. Radial spectra: conditional mathematics Paper III declares Hr,β=L0(Kr)+βDrH_{r,\beta}=L_0(K_r)+\beta D_r, where DrD_r records combinatorial depth. The exact consequences concern this chosen operator. They do not select it uniquely as a constitutive law or identify it with a physical Hamiltonian. The compact-resolvent argument has a standard structure: depth tends to infinity with finite multiplicity, and the bounded graph Laplacian perturbs the depth operator. The finite-to-infinite comparison uses the boundary correction 7PSr7P_{S_r}. The draft’s outer-vertex degrees 10 and 17 apply from r≥2r\ge2; at r=1r=1 they are 4 and 11, with the same correction of seven. The singular, rank-one intercell blocks permit Schur-complement recursions where the required inverses exist. For a submission, state the resolvent domains explicitly and justify any assertion that a scalar Weyl component detects the entire sector spectrum: a scalar entry can miss modes orthogonal to its observation vector. The present review does not certify that completeness assertion. The printed high-precision eigenvalue intervals have not been independently certified here. The draft refers to exact polynomials and Sturm certificates, but their JSON files are not in this upload. The new partial verifier is not a substitute for those certificates and makes no claim to reproduce them. 5. Corrections before a review release Item Required correction Publication metadata PDF/TeX say “Radial Block-Jacobi Spectra,” Review draft 0.1; the metadata draft says “Radial Jacobi-Type Spectral Theory,” Review edition 1.0. Reconcile before deposition. No Zenodo publication is inferred. Claim-table numbering Use generated theorem references. For example, P3.1 in the table is Proposition 2.3 in the text; T5.1 is Theorem 4.1; NG3.2 is No-go 2.4. Compact resolvent and convergence are separate Theorems 7.1 and 7.2. Reproduction availability Supply the advertised author archive, complete tetrahedron lists, spectral certificate files and verifier. The delta ledger names 13 distinct archives; none was available in the upload folder or published site files examined during this intake. Tensor covariance Add the basis conventions and explicit S4S_4 generator matrices alongside the CSV. Spectral claims Make inverse domains and spectral-detection assumptions explicit; replay the exact enclosures from their certificates. Source-summary wording In the current-state refresh, replace “stocks + currents + norm are not generally sufficient” with the precise currents-and-norm ambiguity statement. The parity rescaling changes individual squared coefficients qσq_\sigma; it does not preserve a supplied complete stock vector. Sparse-support sign ambiguities are a separate issue. Historical terminology “Current public canon” in the refresh describes the two-paper edition. Making a later draft accessible does not itself revise that edition. The supplied PDF is preserved unchanged. Its cover and claim-table page were visually inspected; the detected numbering problems are recorded here, not silently repaired inside the author’s original. 6. What remains open Papers I and II continue to provide finite carrier identities and reconstruction results. Paper III develops additional mathematics on declared carriers. The context response, source-law choices, acquisition calibration, and physical carrier identification remain separate questions. No new hardware session, optical result, atomic identification or physical unit is supplied by this batch. Physical promotion remains 0. 7. Reproduction and provenance The supplement includes all ten supplied files unchanged, an intake hash inventory, this review, the bounded verifier and its results. With Python 3 and SymPy installed, run: python verify-symmetry-radial.py It completes in seconds on the review environment; runtime varies by machine. The gate may: strengthen a context label discover a new exact theorem identify a typed collision produce a scoped no-go leave the result unchanged It may not: reverse engineer a target create a physical bridge from arithmetic resemblance override source provenance weaken AUTO_FREEZE raise physical promotion PHYSICAL_PROMOTION remains 0 unless a separate explicit bridge closes.
