The nine inductor branches are 01,02,03,04,12,13,14,23,24. 01,02,03,04,12,13,14,23,24. Use node fluxes Φ=(Φ0,…,Φ4)⊤ \Phi=(\Phi_0,\ldots,\Phi_4)^\top as physical generalized coordinates. The dimensionless operator is not fitted. 5. Frozen primary prediction The two nonzero frequency classes obey ω3=Ω*3,ω5=Ω*5. \omega_3=\Omega_*\sqrt3,\qquad \omega_5=\Omega_*\sqrt5. Then the held-out prediction is Rω=ω5ω3=53=1.2909944487358056… \boxed{ R_\omega = \frac{\omega_5}{\omega_3} = \sqrt{\frac53} = 1.2909944487358056\ldots } Equivalently, ω52ω32=53. \boxed{ \frac{\omega_5^2}{\omega_3^2}=\frac53. } No second spectral scale may be fitted. title: Static LC Benchmark and Finite Counting Checks
note: Supporting review · 19 September 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Exact carrier spectra and two arithmetic remarks; the supplied LC target and tolerance remain untested in hardware. Procurement and governance sources are preserved with their scope. 29 September: event counts and measured periods remain separate. The SER reference is an expository draft; the LC bench awaits three K4 frequencies. Stage 0 is UNSCORED; the new estimator addendum is proposed and pre-acquisition adoption is unconfirmed. Physical promotion remains 0.Read the session checkpoint · Event-time reference · Stage 0 acquisition addendumA static LC benchmark and two finite counting checks Supporting review · 19 September 2026 The new experimental focus is a five-node inductor–capacitor network with one missing branch. Its ideal graph Laplacian predicts two nonzero frequency classes with ratio 5/3\sqrt{5/3}. The supplied priority note fixes an absolute ratio tolerance of 0.0150.015; the procurement manifest still records the preliminary hardware test as not executed. This is a proposed classical linear-network benchmark. The finite mathematics can be checked now; component receipt, metrology, wiring, and measured spectra require physical acquisition. No hardware result is reported in this review. Download sources and exact replay · Verification results · Source inventory 1. Why the missing branch makes a useful test The two-tetrahedron complex K−={0123,0124}K_-=\{0123,0124\} has five vertices and nine edges. Its vertex graph is K5K_5 without edge 3434. With oriented incidence matrix B1B_1, the unit-weight vertex Laplacian is L0=B1B1T=(4−1−1−1−1−14−1−1−1−1−14−1−1−1−1−130−1−1−103). L_0=B_1B_1^T= \begin{pmatrix} 4&-1&-1&-1&-1\\ -1&4&-1&-1&-1\\ -1&-1&4&-1&-1\\ -1&-1&-1&3&0\\ -1&-1&-1&0&3 \end{pmatrix}. Its characteristic polynomial is x(x−3)(x−5)3x(x-3)(x-5)^3. In particular, L0(0,0,0,−1,1)T=3(0,0,0,−1,1)T, L_0(0,0,0,-1,1)^T=3(0,0,0,-1,1)^T, L0(−1,1,0,0,0)T=5(−1,1,0,0,0)T. L_0(-1,1,0,0,0)^T=5(-1,1,0,0,0)^T. These are the proposed apex-difference and base-difference excitations. Their definitions precede any measured spectrum. For equal ideal shunt capacitors CC and equal branch inductors LbL_b, node fluxes obey CΦ̈+Lb−1L0Φ=0. C\ddot\Phi+L_b^{-1}L_0\Phi=0. The predicted ratio is therefore R=ω5ω3=53. R=\frac{\omega_5}{\omega_3}=\sqrt{\frac53}. A single scale is estimated from the first mode; the second mode is held out. Adding the missing edge makes the vertex graph complete, with spectrum 0,5,5,5,50,5,5,5,5, eliminating this split in the ideal model. The four-node K4K_4 control instead has spectrum 0,4,4,40,4,4,4. Circuit Laplacians are established electrical-network tools; see Lee et al., Topolectrical circuits. The proposed contribution here is the declared finite carrier, excitation pair, and test procedure. It is not the invention of a circuit–graph correspondence. What a successful ratio check would establish A result within the predeclared interval would support this spectral prediction for the assembled network and measurement procedure. One ratio does not uniquely identify a matrix, verify every eigenspace, or demonstrate the entire Hodge–Dirac construction. Different operators can share eigenvalues or a selected ratio. The circuit addresses the degree-zero, five-coordinate operator. It does not realize the full 23-coordinate chain space of K−K_-, execute a Pachner move, or establish a constitutive event law. The full K+K_+ carrier has 27 coordinates, even though its vertex graph alone is K5K_5. 2. The supplied bench sequence and its evidence boundary Stage Supplied specification Evidence still needed Component pools 25 inductors and 25 capacitors of the named parts Receipt, lot information, and labeled physical components Pre-power metrology Measurements at 1 kHz; selection by pool median and label order Raw readings, instrument settings and calibration, and selected-part record Repeatability Ten readings each of one selected inductor and capacitor; coefficient of variation at most 0.0005 Actual readings and a stated estimator Four-node control Six branches and four shunt capacitors; relative frequency spread at most 0.015 Frozen differential-mode definitions, acquisition procedure, and three measured frequencies Five-node score Add node 4 and branches 04, 14, 24; keep 34 absent Raw waveforms or spectra, scale estimate, held-out result, and uncertainty record The manifest states median-relative eligibility limits of 0.00750.0075 for inductors and 0.00250.0025 for capacitors. The first nine eligible inductors and first five eligible capacitors are selected by labels assigned before measurement. The specified branch assignment is preserved in the original handoff. The documents use two different quantities with the same numerical threshold: Primary score: |Rmeas−5/3|≤0.015|R_{\mathrm{meas}}-\sqrt{5/3}|\le0.015, an absolute dimensionless ratio tolerance. Stage-zero score: (maxfj−minfj)/meanfj≤0.015(\max f_j-\min f_j)/\operatorname{mean}f_j\le0.015, a relative frequency spread. They are distinct tests. Passing the control does not itself establish the uncertainty of the held-out ratio. The initial preregistration calls for a tolerance derived from pre-power uncertainty propagation. Later supplied records fix it at 0.015. This review records that later threshold without changing it. The referenced uncertainty-propagation and component-selection scripts are not included in this batch, so their implementation and the numerical justification for the threshold cannot be audited here. At the stated nominal values of 10 mH and 100 nF, ideal frequencies are approximately 8.72 kHz, 10.07 kHz and 11.25 kHz for eigenvalues 3, 4 and 5. These are calculated design values, not measurements. The measurement record must account for the difference between 1 kHz component characterization and operation in this band, as well as losses, probe and drive loading, and the frequency estimator used. A ring-down frequency and a driven-response peak need not be interchangeable in a lossy network. The supplied handoff permits stopping when matching or repeatability fails and requires a new pre-power version after hardware repair. No component purchase, substitution, post-exposure fit, or threshold change is performed by this publication update. Source presentation and procurement status The handoff Markdown contains damaged escape sequences in several equations. Its bytes remain unchanged. The readable numerical criteria above are taken from its companion JSON manifest and the separate priority/preregistration documents; the damaged source is displayed as raw text with a notice. Vendor stock, price and lifecycle statements in the handoff are historical source snapshots, not current availability claims verified here. The checklist remains a proposed physical procedure; its presence is not evidence that an order or measurement occurred. 3. Two arithmetic remarks, with their scope made explicit Equal tree and complement counts For the nonempty face Hasse graph of a simplex on n≥2n\ge2 vertices, Vn=2n−1,En=n(2n−1−1),Tn=2n−2,Cn=En−Tn. V_n=2^n-1,\quad E_n=n(2^{n-1}-1),\quad T_n=2^n-2,\quad C_n=E_n-T_n. There are n2n−1n2^{n-1} covers in the full Boolean lattice; deleting the empty face removes nn of them. The remaining graph is connected, so a spanning tree has Vn−1V_n-1 edges. Consequently Tn=Cn⇔2=n−2⇔n=4. T_n=C_n\iff 2=n-2\iff n=4. The factor canceled here is positive for n≥2n\ge2. The single-vertex case n=1n=1 has the trivial equality T=C=0T=C=0, so the domain restriction matters. The short source remark omits that restriction in its opening statement; the longer audit supplies it. For the tetrahedron, the count is (V,E,T,C)=(15,28,14,14)(V,E,T,C)=(15,28,14,14). This explains the equal sizes of a spanning tree and its complement within this family of graphs. It does not select a unique tree, establish optimal noise performance, or prove an optical uniqueness claim. The graph arithmetic alone is not a general PSR reconstruction theorem for every support pattern. Spectral trace counts incidences For the unit-weight skew Hodge–Dirac matrix A=d−dTA=d-d^T in an orthonormal simplex basis, each incidence contributes two squared unit entries. Hence 12tr(−A2)=∑ω>0mωω2=EH. \frac12\operatorname{tr}(-A^2)=\sum_{\omega>0}m_\omega\omega^2=E_H. The reproduction script builds boundaries directly from simplex lists, checks consecutive boundary products vanish, and verifies these full characteristic polynomials: Carrier Chain dimension Hasse incidences Skew characteristic polynomial Filled tetrahedron 15 28 x(x2+4)7x(x^2+4)^7 K−K_- 23 47 x(x2+3)4(x2+5)7x(x^2+3)^4(x^2+5)^7 K+K_+ 27 59 x(x2+2)2(x2+5)11x(x^2+2)^2(x^2+5)^{11} This is an exact trace identity and consistency check, not a physical energy law. With weights, squared matrix entries must be retained; the unweighted incidence count cannot simply be reused. Repeated counts such as 14 or 7 do not identify the different spaces or objects they count. 4. Governance and parity reconciliation The supplied v1.2R1 governance source explicitly narrows the earlier arithmetic rule to numerical labeling, provenance collisions, and interpretation risks. It retains v1.2 beneath the repair as historical source. Routine proofs need not become factorization exercises. The finite arithmetic remarks are therefore presented here as conventional mathematical statements, without adding internal governance machinery to Papers I or II. The reconciliation note reaffirms the supplied CRL-2d ruling, reports the reciprocal-family repair, and keeps the self-containment amendment pending independent review. It also states that retained-basis source objects remain open. None of those scopes changes the LC target. That note reports additional replication documents and hash checks from another ingest. Those referenced bytes are not included in this batch. It therefore adds a reported reconciliation, not an independent replay of the missing replication package. The parity execution review remains the account of what was actually replayed here, and the earlier theorem-wording corrections remain visible. 5. Current conclusion The finite carrier calculations are reproducible. The supplied bench documents specify a target, a threshold, component selection criteria and a staged acquisition path. Hardware execution remains open, and the supporting uncertainty and selection implementations still need to accompany the bench record. The supplement preserves 13 uploads plus two JSON files recovered from the procurement archive. All three entries in its included hash manifest match. The finite checks are exact; nominal frequency calculations are explicitly separated from experimental evidence. Physical promotion remains zero. note: Preserved source · 2026-09-19 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content:
Read with the execution and replication review. Historical statuses are preserved; the supplied CRL-2d ruling and independently replayable evidence are distinguished. #!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, sys, hashlib
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

TOL = 1e-10
CONTROL_TOL = 1e-8

R = np.diag([1,1,1,-1,-1,-1]).astype(float)
J = np.block([[np.zeros((3,3)), -np.eye(3)],
              [np.eye(3), np.zeros((3,3))]])
S = np.block([[np.zeros((3,3)), np.eye(3)],
              [np.eye(3), np.zeros((3,3))]])

def infnorm(M):
    return float(np.max(np.abs(M)))

def classify(case):
    W = np.array(case["W"], dtype=float)
    T = np.array(case["T_H"], dtype=float)
    Theta = np.array(case["Theta_H"], dtype=float)
    Ic = np.array(case["I_c"], dtype=float)

    residuals = {
        "W_orthogonality": infnorm(W.T @ W - np.eye(6)),
        "TH_definition": infnorm(T - W.T),
        "Theta_definition": infnorm(Theta - W @ R @ W.T),
        "parity_intertwining": infnorm(T @ Theta - R @ T),
        "event_antisymplectic": infnorm(R.T @ J @ R + J),
        "Q121_commutation": infnorm(R @ Ic - Ic @ R),
        "copy_swap_sign": infnorm(S @ R @ S.T + R),
    }

    premise_ok = (
        residuals["W_orthogonality"] <= TOL and
        residuals["TH_definition"] <= TOL and
        residuals["Theta_definition"] <= TOL and
        residuals["Q121_commutation"] <= TOL
    )

    if premise_ok:
        result = "IN_SCOPE_PASS" if (
            residuals["parity_intertwining"] <= TOL and
            residuals["event_antisymplectic"] <= TOL and
            residuals["copy_swap_sign"] <= TOL
        ) else "IN_SCOPE_FAIL"
    else:
        result = "CONTROL_FAIL"

    return result, residuals

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        raise SystemExit("usage: runner.py CASES.json OUTPUT.json")
    cases_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
    out_path = Path(sys.argv[2])
    doc = json.loads(cases_path.read_text())
    results = []
    for case in doc["cases"]:
        cls, residuals = classify(case)
        results.append({
            "case_id":case["case_id"],
            "classification":cls,
            "residuals":residuals
        })

    payload = {
        "schema":"UD_PARITY_CARRIER_CRL2C_RUN_OUTPUT_v0.1",
        "input_sha256":hashlib.sha256(cases_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "tolerance":TOL,
        "results":results
    }
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    print(hashlib.sha256(out_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest())

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Response Hessians and transported parity Supporting mathematical review · 19 September 2026 This batch connects a symmetric response operator to a quadratic potential and gives parity identities between declared six-dimensional coordinate spaces. The useful advances are a precise candidate coupling and an explicit transport construction. Neither selects a constitutive source law, establishes a physical identification, nor supplies a completed custodian ruling. Papers I and II remain unchanged. Independent exact checks confirm the basic algebra and identify three corrections needed in the presentation: a Hessian leaves affine freedom; the composite parity map needs a correctly typed embedding; and a plain exchange of coordinate and momentum copies is anti-symplectic. The original documents remain available unchanged below. Download the review and reproduction supplement · Independent check results · Source inventory 1. A response operator defines a candidate quadratic coupling Let m∈ℝ3m\in\mathbb R^3, let Y=YTY=Y^T be a declared response matrix, and let λ\lambda be a scalar amplitude. If both are independent of mm, the proposed contribution ΔH(m)=λ2mTYm \Delta H(m)=\frac{\lambda}{2}m^TYm has Euclidean gradient λYm\lambda Ym and Hessian λY\lambda Y. These are standard quadratic identities. They make a proposed coupling explicit; they do not derive why this matrix or amplitude governs a particular system. State dependence of YY or λ\lambda introduces additional derivative terms. The uniqueness statement needs a qualification. Prescribing the Hessian alone determines a potential only up to an affine term: ΔH(m)=λ2mTYm+ℓTm+C. \Delta H(m)=\frac{\lambda}{2}m^TYm+\ell^Tm+C. Prescribing the gradient as well, or imposing zero gradient at the origin, removes ℓ\ell. Only then is the remaining freedom an additive constant. The amplitude is an independent input, and a rescaling of the response map can be absorbed into it. In a non-Euclidean metric GG, the gradient is G−1λYmG^{-1}\lambda Ym; the Hessian bilinear form and its associated operator must be distinguished. The displayed boundary correction has a different trace The supplied source displays S∂=(2/9−1/31/3−1/35/9−4/91/3−4/95/9). S_{\partial}=\begin{pmatrix} 2/9&-1/3&1/3\\ -1/3&5/9&-4/9\\ 1/3&-4/9&5/9 \end{pmatrix}. Exact arithmetic gives rank two, trace 4/34/3, and eigenvalues 0,1/9,11/90,1/9,11/9. First separate S∂=49I+(S∂−49I). S_{\partial}=\frac49I+\left(S_{\partial}-\frac49I\right). Any further comparison of the traceless part requires a common representation and basis. Matching eigenvalues alone cannot establish that correspondence. Nor does positivity of the displayed matrix fix the sign of a spectral-parameter-dependent coefficient multiplying it. For a positive-definite base Hessian KK, stability of the candidate correction requires K+λY≻0K+\lambda Y\succ0. A sufficient condition is |λ|∥K−1/2YK−1/2∥op<1|\lambda|\,\|K^{-1/2}YK^{-1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1. This is a mathematical bound, not a supplied calibration. Compatibility with the declared retained Hessian and its normalization remains a separate obligation. 2. A normalized real map still has a sign choice unless an orientation convention fixes it. This conclusion does not select the action on an arbitrary retained coordinate chart. The construction needs the retained representation matrices or an explicit change of basis to the tetrahedral representation. A proposed projection of a boundary tensor onto the V3V_3 sector must be nonzero and satisfy the declared equivariance conditions. A zero projection rejects that particular construction, not every possible transfer. The reproduction script includes an exact counterexample to using spectrum as an alignment substitute: two orthogonally conjugate traceless matrices have the same spectrum, while one has zero projection onto the fixed V3V_3 sector and the other does not. title: Fixed-Event Spectra, Orbit Averaging and Transported Parity
note: Supporting review · 19 September 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: A verified spectral obstruction, conditional response averaging and frame-dependent parity transport. State-level dynamics and constitutive identity remain open. Fixed-event spectra, orbit averaging and transported parity Supporting mathematical review · 19 September 2026 The new calculations clarify which structures can be identified and which require a change of model. The declared fixed B/C action has two distinct frequencies, so it cannot be identified with a single-frequency event action by a canonical coordinate change. Uniform orbit averaging can instead produce a scalar response operator. A proposed cotangent Hamiltonian then supplies an oscillator and a parity—but the averaging step and the response-to-state interpretation remain separate assumptions. This is a supporting extension to Paper I, not a revision of its theorem spine. It follows the event-exchange and parity review and the normalization and event-phase review. No physical field identification or physical time-reversal claim follows. Review and reproduction supplement · Independent checks · Source inventory 1. The fixed-event spectral obstruction The uploaded audit specifies two three-dimensional response Hessians: KB=diag(4/3,1,5/3),KC=diag(4/3,5/3,1). K_B=\operatorname{diag}(4/3,1,5/3),\qquad K_C=\operatorname{diag}(4/3,5/3,1). For KBC=diag(KB,KC)K_{BC}=\operatorname{diag}(K_B,K_C) and the declared symplectic matrix JJ, the paired generator GBC=JKBCG_{BC}=JK_{BC} has characteristic polynomial χGBC(λ)=(λ2+5/3)2(λ2+16/9). \chi_{G_{BC}}(\lambda) =(\lambda^2+5/3)^2(\lambda^2+16/9). Its squared frequencies are 5/3,5/3,16/95/3,5/3,16/9. Their nontrivial ratio is 16/1516/15. By contrast, the permutation-equivariant named-event quadratic family KE=(aIcIcIbI) K_E=\begin{pmatrix}aI&cI\\cI&bI\end{pmatrix} satisfies (JKE)2=−(ab−c2)I(JK_E)^2=-(ab-c^2)I: every positive member has a single frequency with multiplicity three. An invertible change of state coordinates conjugates the generator and preserves its spectrum. A common rescaling of the generator changes all frequencies by the same factor and preserves their ratios. Neither operation removes this split. Thus the stated fixed B/C action cannot be identified with this single-frequency family while preserving the dynamics. This also clarifies “mode-dependent normalization”: a genuine coordinate change still preserves eigenvalues. Forcing unequal frequencies to coincide requires changing the dynamical operator, not merely renaming its coordinates. Carrier-level symplectic equivalence can remain valid even when action-preserving equivalence fails. 2. What uniform orbit averaging changes The proposed response-level operation is the Reynolds average ℛ(K)=1120∑g∈S5UgTKUg. \mathcal R(K)=\frac1{120}\sum_{g\in S_5}U_g^TKU_g. It is a projection on operators. It can map distinct response Hessians to the same symmetric operator, so it loses information and is not an invertible canonical transformation of the original state. The source reports a five-dimensional response carrier W5=kerNW_5=\ker N and normalized spectra {2/3,1,1,5/3,5/3}\{2/3,1,1,5/3,5/3\}, with trace six. In an explicit unsigned five-vertex edge-incidence realization, the averaging result can be derived without fitting: Take the ten edges of K5K_5, with Nve=1N_{ve}=1 when vertex vv belongs to edge ee. Its kernel has dimension five. Under vertex permutations, matrix entries fall into three classes: equal edges, adjacent edges and disjoint edges. On kerN\ker N, the corresponding invariant matrices restrict to I,−2I,II,-2I,I. Every averaged symmetric operator is therefore scalar there. Trace preservation fixes that scalar to 6/56/5 for a response Hessian with trace six. Under this declared carrier realization and the supplied spectral premise, ℛ(KB)=ℛ(KC)=65κloopP5. \mathcal R(K_B)=\mathcal R(K_C) =\tfrac65\kappa_{\mathrm loop}P_5. An odd component proportional to their difference averages to zero. Restricting the scalar result to the standard three-dimensional subspace gives the same coefficient. The independent replay constructs this carrier explicitly and checks all 120 permutations on a labeled control operator. The batch does not supply executable full matrices for the original DB,DCD_B,D_C or their embeddings. This is an independent derivation of the conditional averaging identity, not a replay of the original full B/C matrix calculation. The edge-response kernel here is also distinct from the five-dimensional vertex-permutation carrier discussed in an earlier candidate screen. 3. An averaged operator is not an averaged trajectory Uniform weights over the permutation group are part of the proposed construction. Symmetry averaging alone does not establish that an event process visits those configurations uniformly or evolves according to the averaged operator. In general, 1n∑ietGi≠et(∑iGi/n). \frac1n\sum_i e^{tG_i}\ne e^{t(\sum_iG_i/n)}. For example, let G1=Jdiag(1,4)G_1=J\operatorname{diag}(1,4) and G2=Jdiag(4,1)G_2=J\operatorname{diag}(4,1). Their mean squared generator is −4I-4I, whereas the square of their mean is −25I/4-25I/4. Their averaged flows already disagree at second order in time. A dynamical coarse-graining claim therefore needs a state map and a closure or limiting argument, with the sampling, switching or time-scale assumptions stated. The present result establishes an operator average. It does not recover fixed-event trajectories or prove native microscopic isotropy. 4. The conditional route to a single-frequency event After averaging, the source proposes the cotangent Hamiltonian Hneutral(Q,P)=12(∥P∥2+k∥Q∥2),k=65κloop>0. H_{\mathrm neutral}(Q,P)=\tfrac12(\|P\|^2+k\|Q\|^2), \qquad k=\tfrac65\kappa_{\mathrm loop}>0. The kinetic coefficient one and the interpretation of the response variable as a configuration coordinate are part of this model assignment. They are not consequences of the response average alone. Its generator squares to −kI-kI. Within the positive diagonal squeeze family Q′=rQ,P′=r−1P, Q'=rQ,\qquad P'=r^{-1}P, equal transformed coefficients require uniquely r=k1/4r=k^{1/4}. The resulting generator is kJ\sqrt{k}J. The qualifier “within this squeeze family” matters: symplectic rotations of the normalized oscillator still provide other valid coordinate frames. If the separate response-to-retained Hamiltonian identification is imposed, matching Q=cq,P=c−1m,Hret=12(32∥q∥2+114∥m∥2) Q=cq,\quad P=c^{-1}m,\qquad H_{\mathrm ret}=\tfrac12\left(\tfrac32\|q\|^2+\tfrac{11}{4}\|m\|^2\right) gives c2=4/11c^2=4/11 and k=33/8k=33/8. Comparing its normalized frequency with the supplied selected-Hodge frequency 5\sqrt5 then gives the common generator factor 33/40\sqrt{33/40}. The coefficient arithmetic is exact under these assumptions. It is a compatibility calculation, not independent evidence that the response and retained-state coordinates are the same dynamical variables. Nor does it select a physical clock. The source names this still-open identification SA-023. 5. Separate parity existence from parity descent An orthogonal source involution UU, if retained on the neutral response space, preserves a scalar response Hessian. Its cotangent action diag(U,U)\operatorname{diag}(U,U) is symplectic. The alternative diag(U,−U)\operatorname{diag}(U,-U) is anti-symplectic and preserves the proposed block-scalar Hamiltonian, but the additional sign does not follow from the operator average. Equal averaged Hessians do not themselves define a map from the original B/C state copies to the new configuration and momentum coordinates. Thus there is no supplied state map through which the original copy-exchange parity has been shown to descend. This is a missing construction, not a theorem that no possible parity-compatible coarse-graining can ever exist. Independently, a declared cotangent structure has fiber inversion (Q,P)↦(Q,−P)(Q,P)\mapsto(Q,-P). On the present linear phase space it has two rank-three Lagrangian eigenspaces. A Hamiltonian is invariant under it only if it is even in momentum. The proposed natural quadratic Hamiltonian satisfies that condition; cotangent geometry alone does not require every Hamiltonian to satisfy it. 6. Parity inside the selected Hodge sector Given the source’s stated orthonormal Darboux frame WW, with WTW=I6W^TW=I_6, define PH=WWT,R=diag(I3,−I3),ΘH=WRWT. P_H=WW^T,\qquad R=\operatorname{diag}(I_3,-I_3),\qquad \Theta_H=WRW^T. Then ΘH2=PH\Theta_H^2=P_H, so it is an involution on the selected sector. If WTJHW=JW^TJ_HW=J and the selected generator is represented by 5J\sqrt5J, it is anti-symplectic, has rank-three even and odd Lagrangian halves, and reverses that generator: ΘH𝒜HΘH=−𝒜H. \Theta_H\mathcal A_H\Theta_H=-\mathcal A_H. The quadratic Hamiltonian is invariant. A trajectory x(s)x(s) is consequently paired with ΘHx(−s)\Theta_Hx(-s). Anti-symplecticity by itself should not be described as invariance of the first-order action at fixed time; the time reversal and endpoint conventions must be included. This construction is exact for a chosen frame. The oscillator alone does not select it uniquely: replacing WW by WVWV, for an orthogonal symplectic VV, generally changes WRWTWRW^T while preserving the oscillator. Calling it canonical therefore requires an independently specified frame or polarization rule. The zero extension also squares to the sector projector, not the identity on the entire ambient space. The batch gives the frame identities but not the full numerical or symbolic frame. The replay verifies their algebraic consequences and a frame-dependence counterexample; it does not reconstruct the original selected Hodge frame. 7. What the remaining map must supply Established within the stated model Still needed for the stronger identification Fixed B/C spectrum and its obstruction A different source-derived action or an explicit coarse dynamical model. Scalar response after uniform operator averaging A justified averaging rule and state-level evolution closure. Neutral oscillator after cotangent assignment A source law selecting the configuration, momentum and kinetic structure. Conditional coefficient matching A constitutive map from response data to retained-state coordinates. Parity in a selected Darboux frame Frame-selection provenance and, for descent, a compatible state map. An equivariant map unique up to scalar does not identify its input and output as the same state variable. On two copies of the standard representation, general equivariant symplectic maps can also mix those copies; the diagonal scaling family is a restricted assignment, not the full set of possibilities. A response-to-attitude norm relation alone does not complete the response-to-retained-state map. The next useful artifact is that explicit map, with its dynamics, normalization, reduction limits and falsification conditions—not another numerical coincidence between carriers. Source completeness All 20 uploaded files are preserved unchanged. Of 14 references in the three supplied manifests, 12 match and two files are absent: UD_NEUTRAL_COTANGENT_FIBER_INVERSION_PARITY_AUDIT_v0.1.md UD_NEUTRAL_EVENT_TRIANGLE_AND_FIBER_PARITY_EXACT_CHECKS_v0.1.csv Five orbit-averaging documents are included as supplied supporting sources; this batch contains no corresponding orbit-package hash manifest. The new inventory records their hashes without presenting that as original package certification. The supplement distinguishes exact checks of declared matrices, general transport identities, independently reconstructed controls and unreplayed source embeddings. The supplied statements about earlier source searches are retained as reported audits, not independently repeated archival searches. Physical identification remains unclaimed. """
UD_BIDIRECTIONAL_SUPPORT_BURDEN_CURRENT_RUNTIME_PROBE_v0.1

Executes the preregistered immediate-response probes against the CURRENT
locked support/burden equations only:

support: dc/ds = A_K c            (no burden->support cross term)
burden:  db/ds = -R_B b           (no support->burden cross term)

Q164 may modify burden transport as a function of burden/support state,
but it does not add a reciprocal support update. At b=0 its burden-side
contribution vanishes.

Therefore the bidirectional vertical cross slopes are exact zeros.
"""

from fractions import Fraction
import math
import csv
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path(__file__).with_name("UD_BIDIRECTIONAL_SUPPORT_BURDEN_CURRENT_RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_v0.1.csv")

sqrt = math.sqrt
basis = {
    "u0": [Fraction(1,2)]*4,

    "u2": [1/sqrt(6), 1/sqrt(6), -2/sqrt(6), 0.0],
    "u3": [1/sqrt(12), 1/sqrt(12), 1/sqrt(12), -3/sqrt(12)],
}
sector = {"u0":"uniform","u1":"contrast","u2":"contrast","u3":"contrast"}

eps = [Fraction(1, 2**m) for m in range(6)]

rows = []
for bid in ["u0","u1","u2","u3"]:
    for e in eps:
        # Forward B->S: c=0 => dc0=A*c=0 because current runtime has no cross term.
        f_plus = Fraction(0,1)

        g_plus = Fraction(0,1)
        g_minus = Fraction(0,1)
        g_slope = -(g_plus-g_minus)/(2*e)

        rows.append([sector[bid],bid,"B_to_S",str(e),str(f_plus),str(f_minus),str(f_slope),"EXACT_ZERO"])
        rows.append([sector[bid],bid,"S_to_B",str(e),str(g_plus),str(g_minus),str(g_slope),"EXACT_ZERO"])

with OUT.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    w=csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["sector","basis_id","direction","epsilon","response_plus","response_minus","central_odd_slope","status"])
    w.writerows(rows)

print(f"Wrote {OUT}")

print("f_perp = 0")
print("g_perp = 0")
print("RATE-SB: UNIDENTIFIED/INACTIVE in current runtime")
print("NORM-SB: UNIDENTIFIED (0/0; do not compute)")

title: Coupling Rate, State Normalization and Event Phase
note: Supporting review · 19 September 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Exact factor separation and corrected phase-symmetry scope. The zero-response script is an algebraic fixture, not a runtime acquisition. Coupling rate, state normalization and event phase Supporting mathematical review · 19 September 2026 This update separates the speed of a reciprocal exchange from the scaling of its state coordinates. It also distinguishes a fixed coordinate rotation from the periodic phase generated by an oscillator’s own Hamiltonian. Both distinctions sharpen the proposed tests without supplying a new event-source law or a physical measurement. Read this alongside the event-exchange and parity review. The theorem statements in Paper I and Paper II are unchanged. All quantities below belong to declared finite-dimensional models; no physical units or field identification are inferred. Review and reproduction supplement · Independent verification · Source inventory 1. Two quantities, two directional measurements In a scalar reciprocal exchange, let b̂=κb\widehat b=\kappa b, with positive scaling κ\kappa, and let the normalized coupling rate be γ>0\gamma>0. The raw cross terms are ċ=k+b,ḃ=−k−c,k+=γκ,k−=γ/κ. \dot c=k_+b,\qquad \dot b=-k_-c,\qquad k_+=\gamma\kappa,\quad k_-=\gamma/\kappa. Thus, for independently determined positive directional coefficients, γ=k+k−,κ=k+/k−. \gamma=\sqrt{k_+k_-},\qquad \kappa=\sqrt{k_+/k_-}. The product determines the rate; the ratio determines the relative scaling. One directional coefficient alone determines neither. In the isolated, undamped scalar subsystem, c̈=−γ2c\ddot c=-\gamma^2c, so the period of a nonzero state is 2π/γ2\pi/\gamma. That period does not identify κ\kappa. This recurrence statement is scoped to the isolated exchange. Additional support evolution, damping, forcing, unobserved modes or a partial observation can change what an observed recurrence identifies. A zero state has no informative oscillation period. If both coefficients are negative, their product still determines a positive frequency magnitude and their ratio a positive scaling, but the normalized generator has a negative signed rate. A positive product alone does not justify the positive-rate convention. Sector comparisons must retain these signs. 2. Conservation uses the transformed metric For a constant invertible matrix NN, write b̂=Nb\widehat b=Nb. Transforming the normalized equations gives ċ=𝒜c+γI0Nb,ḃ=−γN−1I0Tc−N−1RB̂Nb, \dot c=\mathcal Ac+\gamma I_0Nb, \qquad \dot b=-\gamma N^{-1}I_0^Tc-N^{-1}R_{\widehat B}Nb, where I0I_0 includes vertex coordinates in the support chain. The raw storage is H=12∥c∥2+12bTNTNb. H=\tfrac12\|c\|^2+\tfrac12 b^TN^TNb. The reciprocal cross terms cancel in Ḣ\dot H. If 𝒜\mathcal A is skew and the symmetric part of RB̂R_{\widehat B} is positive semidefinite, the remaining derivative is Ḣ=−b̂TRB̂b̂≤0. \dot H=-\widehat b^TR_{\widehat B}\widehat b\le0. Total conservation therefore requires the dissipation contribution to vanish; cancellation of cross terms alone is not full conservation of a dissipative model. If NN varies with time, the transformed equations also require its derivative. For scalar N=κIN=\kappa I, ordinary unweighted raw storage instead has cross derivative γ(κ−κ−1)cTb\gamma(\kappa-\kappa^{-1})c^Tb. For an active coupling, it vanishes for all states only when κ=1\kappa=1. The general matrix exception is an orthogonal normalization, for which NTN=IN^TN=I; “nonidentity normalization” alone is not a universal test for loss of Euclidean conservation. In equal-dimensional cross coordinates, F=γNF=\gamma N and G=γN−1G=\gamma N^{-1} imply FG=GF=γ2IFG=GF=\gamma^2I. Conversely, FG=λIFG=\lambda I, λ>0\lambda>0, reconstructs an invertible N=F/λN=F/\sqrt\lambda. It does not by itself prove that NN is symmetric positive definite. For example, F=G=−IF=G=-I passes the product test but produces N=−IN=-I. Positivity is an additional assumption or check when that normalization class is required. 3. The directional protocol and its limits The proposed protocol uses positive and negative impulses along a fixed uniform direction and three orthonormal contrast directions. Immediate odd response slopes estimate the forward and reverse cross terms separately. For the reverse map, the estimator includes the minus sign in ḃ=−Gc\dot b=-Gc. Under an independently justified permutation-equivariant model, F=f0P0+f⊥P⊥,G=g0P0+g⊥P⊥, F=f_0P_0+f_\perp P_\perp,\quad G=g_0P_0+g_\perp P_\perp, with P0=𝟏𝟏T/4P_0=\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/4, P⊥=I−P0P_\perp=I-P_0. Positive sector coefficients give γr=frgr,νr=fr/gr. \gamma_r=\sqrt{f_rg_r},\qquad \nu_r=\sqrt{f_r/g_r}. A common positive rate additionally requires equal products. Different sector rates must remain distinct. Equal diagonal probe slopes are necessary but not sufficient to establish full equivariance; record cross-direction responses or independently verify the operator symmetry, as explained in the preceding review. Odd differencing cancels constant and even contamination. It does not remove odd nonlinear terms: a cubic response contributes a term proportional to the squared probe amplitude. The zero-amplitude limit, numerical error envelope, timing and source controls must therefore be specified and tested. A finite sequence of six amplitudes is not, by itself, a proof of convergence. The synthetic controls (f0,g0,f⊥,g⊥)=(2,1/2,3,1/3)(f_0,g_0,f_\perp,g_\perp)=(2,1/2,3,1/3) yield γ=1\gamma=1 and N=2P0+3P⊥N=2P_0+3P_\perp. We independently reconstructed their directional slopes and matrix identities. These values demonstrate the method; they are not recovered coefficients of a UD event. 4. What the supplied zero-response script establishes The supplied script produces 48 rows: four basis labels, six amplitudes and two directions. Replaying it reproduces the uploaded CSV byte for byte. Its implementation assigns every response to zero explicitly. It does not import or call a support/burden runtime, apply the stored basis vectors to an operator, or evaluate a source term. This is a reproducible algebraic fixture for a declared uncoupled model, not an independent runtime measurement or a software integration test. For ċ=𝒜c\dot c=\mathcal Ac and ḃ=−RBb\dot b=-R_Bb, immediate cross responses are indeed zero in the specified initial states. If a general burden source sBs_B is included, the reverse conclusion also requires its support-dependent odd response to vanish or be excluded. Absence of an explicit symbol GG does not establish that property of an unspecified source. The fixture therefore demonstrates the expected inactive case. It supplies no nonzero exchange coefficient and no normalization: the ratio 0/00/0 is undefined. It does not establish physical zero coupling or verify the behavior of every archived implementation. A meaningful next implementation check should call an actual right-hand-side function, run disabled and nonzero synthetic controls through that same interface, record full response vectors, and then apply the frozen identification rules. The current uploaded script is preserved as supplied. 5. A fixed rotation is not every phase action In grouped coordinates z=(q,p)z=(q,p), with q,p∈ℝ3q,p\in\mathbb R^3, the declared permutation-equivariant quadratic family has H=12(a∥q∥2+2χqTp+b∥p∥2),K=(aIχIχIbI). H=\tfrac12\left(a\|q\|^2+2\chi q^Tp+b\|p\|^2\right),\qquad K=\begin{pmatrix}aI&\chi I\\\chi I&bI\end{pmatrix}. Assume a,b>0a,b>0 and Δ=ab−χ2>0\Delta=ab-\chi^2>0. The standard coordinate rotation generated by J=(0I−I0) J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix} preserves HH exactly when a=ba=b and χ=0\chi=0. The source’s example a=1,b=33/8,χ=0a=1,b=33/8,\chi=0 correctly shows that a frequency constraint alone does not force this fixed rotation symmetry. The number 33/833/8 is a supplied internal baseline here, not a newly derived physical value. However, for every positive member of this quadratic family, its Hamiltonian generator A=JKA=JK satisfies A2=−ΔI,ATK+KA=0. A^2=-\Delta I,\qquad A^TK+KA=0. Consequently JH=A/ΔJ_H=A/\sqrt\Delta is a complex structure, and RH(θ)=cosθI+sinθJH R_H(\theta)=\cos\theta\,I+\sin\theta\,J_H is a periodic circle action preserving HH. This remains true when the mixed coefficient is nonzero. The strongest correct distinction is therefore: Not forced: the specified raw-coordinate rotation, a uniquely source-selected Hamiltonian, or identity with the Hodge complex structure. Available conditionally: a generator-defined periodic phase action for each chosen positive quadratic Hamiltonian in this family. The broad wording “no internal U(1)” in the preserved sources should be read with this qualification. A coordinate-normalized oscillator phase is not an electromagnetic gauge field or an additional independent conserved quantity. The source writes a tensor product in interleaved-coordinate order while displaying grouped coordinates. The block matrix above fixes the ordering; a permutation relates the two conventions. A global sign change of JJ reverses phase orientation without changing these invariance conditions. 6. The proposed natural Hamiltonian is a conditional subclass The source’s “natural cotangent lift” proposes a natural Hamiltonian on a cotangent phase space, HE=12μE∥p∥2+12kE∥q∥2,μE,kE>0. H_E=\tfrac12\mu_E\|p\|^2+\tfrac12 k_E\|q\|^2, \qquad \mu_E,k_E>0. Its equations give frequency ωE=μEkE\omega_E=\sqrt{\mu_Ek_E}. The canonical squeeze Q=rq,P=p/r,r=(kE/μE)1/4 Q=rq,\quad P=p/r,\quad r=(k_E/\mu_E)^{1/4} preserves pTdqp^Tdq and produces HE=ωE(∥Q∥2+∥P∥2)/2H_E=\omega_E(\|Q\|^2+\|P\|^2)/2. These are exact conditional identities. The phase construction is not exclusive to this mixed-term-free subclass, as the preceding calculation shows. Neither symmetry alone nor this change of coordinates derives the kinetic coefficient, eliminates a mixed term from the original source law, or identifies the resulting complex structure with the independently constructed Hodge operator. The supplied five-seat response ratio 5/65/6 is not imported as a kinetic/potential ratio without a map establishing that interpretation. 7. What comes next Review target Evidence needed A nontrivial reciprocal event Source-defined forward and reverse maps, recorded through an executable runtime interface. Rate and normalization Signed directional slopes, convergence and symmetry checks, then a pulled-back storage check. A selected event action A source statement fixing the quadratic coefficients and coordinate convention. An event/Hodge identification An independently constructed map preserving the specified dynamical and symplectic structures. The upload supplies 20 files. Two earlier files complete its three manifests, giving 22 preserved originals and 16 matching manifest references. This batch is complete against those manifests. It does not supply the four missing references named in the previous review. The reproduction supplement contains exact symbolic checks, the isolated zero-fixture replay and unchanged originals. Historical source searches are the authors’ reported audits; they were not independently repeated in this review. No acquired physical session or physical identification is claimed. SOURCE_ADDENDUM_GATE_TO_BURDEN_EXCHANGE_RECEIPT_v0.1_AUDIT Date: 2026-09-18 Status: CANDIDATE SAME-EVENT STORAGE RECEIPT / EXACT IDENTIFIABILITY RESULTS Physical promotion: 0 1. Purpose Construct the narrowest lawful packet event that could convert support storage into burden storage without silently identifying their raw units. The conversion metric remains symbolic until independently derived. 2. Same-event state packet For one declared gate event ee, record pre/post states ce−,ce+ c^-_e,\ c^+_e for the support carrier and be−,be+ b^-_e,\ b^+_e for raw burden. Use support storage HS(c)=12∥c∥2 \boxed{ H_S(c) = \frac12\|c\|^2 } within the declared event control region. Use raw burden storage HB(b)=12b⊤MBb,MB≻0. \boxed{ H_B(b) = \frac12 b^\top M_B b, \qquad M_B\succ0. } No value of MBM_B is inserted. 3. General same-event receipt Define ΔeHS=HS(ce+)−HS(ce−), \Delta_e H_S = H_S(c_e^+)-H_S(c_e^-), ΔeHB=HB(be+)−HB(be−). \Delta_e H_B = H_B(b_e^+)-H_B(b_e^-). Let WeextW_e^{ext} be declared external storage injected during the event; De≥0D_e\ge0 be declared dissipative storage loss. The event receipt is ℜe=ΔeHS+ΔeHB+De−Weext. \boxed{ \mathfrak R_e = \Delta_eH_S + \Delta_eH_B + D_e - W_e^{ext}. } PASS ℜe=0. \boxed{ \mathfrak R_e=0. } For a closed, nondissipative internal support→burden conversion event, Weext=0,De=0, W_e^{ext}=0, \qquad D_e=0, so ΔeHB=−ΔeHS. \boxed{ \Delta_eH_B=-\Delta_eH_S. } This is the minimal common-event conservation statement. 4. K4 burden-metric decomposition On K4, MB=m0P0+m⊥P⊥,m0,m⊥>0. \boxed{ M_B = m_0P_0+m_\perp P_\perp, \qquad m_0,m_\perp>0. } Define event burden-sector increments Δq0,e=∥P0be+∥2−∥P0be−∥2, \Delta q_{0,e} = \|P_0b_e^+\|^2 - \|P_0b_e^-\|^2, Δq⊥,e=∥P⊥be+∥2−∥P⊥be−∥2. \Delta q_{\perp,e} = \|P_\perp b_e^+\|^2 - \|P_\perp b_e^-\|^2. Then ΔeHB=12(m0Δq0,e+m⊥Δq⊥,e). \boxed{ \Delta_eH_B = \frac12 \left( m_0\Delta q_{0,e} + m_\perp\Delta q_{\perp,e} \right). } For a closed nondissipative conversion event, m0Δq0,e+m⊥Δq⊥,e=−2ΔeHS. \boxed{ m_0\Delta q_{0,e} + m_\perp\Delta q_{\perp,e} = -2\Delta_eH_S. } 5. One-event identifiability theorem A generic single event supplies one scalar equation for the two unknown metric coefficients m0,m⊥. m_0,\ m_\perp. Therefore a mixed-sector event cannot uniquely determine the full K4 burden metric. AUTO_LOCK ONE_MIXED_GATE_TO_BURDEN_EVENT_CANNOT_IDENTIFY_BOTH_K4_BURDEN_METRIC_SECTORS_v0.1 6. Sector-isolating closure routes Uniform-only event If Δq⊥,e=0 \Delta q_{\perp,e}=0 and Δq0,e≠0, \Delta q_{0,e}\neq0, then m0=−2ΔeHSΔq0,e \boxed{ m_0 = -\frac{2\Delta_eH_S}{\Delta q_{0,e}} } for a closed nondissipative event. Contrast-only event If Δq0,e=0 \Delta q_{0,e}=0 and Δq⊥,e≠0, \Delta q_{\perp,e}\neq0, then m⊥=−2ΔeHSΔq⊥,e. \boxed{ m_\perp = -\frac{2\Delta_eH_S}{\Delta q_{\perp,e}}. } Thus two independent sector-isolating same-event receipts would be sufficient to identify MB=m0P0+m⊥P⊥ \boxed{ M_B=m_0P_0+m_\perp P_\perp } without target fitting. AUTO_LOCK — conditional TWO_SECTOR_ISOLATING_GATE_TO_BURDEN_RECEIPTS_CAN_IDENTIFY_K4_RAW_BURDEN_METRIC_v0.1 7. Q173 cannot be silently reused as support-storage loss Current hard-gated support receipt J23h=2hfB3,fτc2,fc3,τ J_{23}^h = 2h_fB_{3,f\tau}c_{2,f}c_{3,\tau} is an internal support throughput object. It transfers support between support-chain degrees. By itself it does not establish a net loss of total support storage: ΔeHS<0. \Delta_eH_S<0. Therefore it cannot serve as the support-loss leg of the gate→burden receipt without an additional source/sink theorem. AUTO_LOCK Q173_GATE_TRANSITION_CURRENT_IS_NOT_BY_ITSELF_SUPPORT_STORAGE_LOSS_v0.1 8. Q158 cannot be silently reused as gate-generated burden Current sB=Δρ−B1jB s_B = \Delta\rho-B_1j_B is a residual burden source receipt. Its predictive constitutive source remains open. Therefore it cannot be identified with the burden-gain leg of the gate event without a common-event tag. AUTO_LOCK Q158_BURDEN_RESIDUAL_IS_NOT_BY_ITSELF_GATE_TO_BURDEN_CONVERSION_v0.1 9. Same-event tagging requirement A lawful gate→burden source packet must carry the same event identifier on: support storage change; burden state change; external input receipt; dissipation receipt; gate transition state. Without that common tag, temporal coincidence is insufficient to infer conversion. 10. Relation to the primitive KXK_X generator A finite same-event receipt can determine storage conversion and, with enough independent events, the metric MBM_B. It does not by itself determine the infinitesimal exchange generator KXK_X. To identify KXK_X, one additionally needs immediate directional response telemetry or a source law for the event rate. Thus: same-event storage receipt⇒MBcandidate \boxed{ \text{same-event storage receipt} \Rightarrow M_B\ \text{candidate} } but not automatically KX. K_X. 11. Current source has separately typed support throughput and burden source receipts, but no common-event storage-conversion identity. A pre/post burden change across a finite gate window therefore contains both: any candidate gate→burden conversion; ordinary burden evolution. Because the raw burden metric is itself the object being inferred, generic dissipation cannot simply be subtracted afterward without risking circularity. Repair: primary identification uses a matched immediate-response pair: TREAT: candidate gate event active; CTRL: same initial state/source tick/exogenous inputs, candidate gate event absent or conversion leg disabled in development/simulation mode. Define attributable derivatives/increments by TREAT minus CTRL at the same source tick. Finite-window receipts become held-out validation, not primary metric identification. Severity: MATERIAL. M3 — support control volume was under-specified v0.1 required direct ΔHS\Delta H_S but did not freeze the exact Hasse control region. Q170 already provides a control-volume support object. M8 — finite mixed events should remain held out v0.1 already prohibited refitting after mixed-event exposure. Retain this rule, but use TREAT−CTRL attributable changes when native background dynamics are active. Severity: PASS / retained. Read with the event-exchange and parity review. Original status labels are retained; templates and symbolic controls are not acquired data. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Target-blind analyzer for UD_GATE_TO_BURDEN_SECTOR_ISOLATING_PREREG_v0.1.
No target values are embedded. Computes sector metric estimates only for
qualified sector-isolating events.
"""
import csv, math, sys

def fnum(x):
    return float(x) if x not in ("", None) else None

def analyze_row(r):
    cls=r["event_class"]
    dHs=fnum(r["delta_H_S"])
    dq0=fnum(r["delta_q0"])
    dqp=fnum(r["delta_qperp"])
    W=fnum(r["W_ext"]) or 0.0
    D=fnum(r["D_diss"]) or 0.0
    if dHs is None:
        return None, "MISSING_DELTA_HS"
    if cls=="U":
        if dq0 in (None,0.0): return None,"NO_UNIFORM_SIGNAL"
        if dqp is None or abs(dqp)>0.0: return None,"NOT_UNIFORM_ISOLATED"
        m=2.0*(W-D-dHs)/dq0
        return m, "PASS_CANDIDATE" if m>0 else "NONPOSITIVE_METRIC"
    if cls=="C":
        if dqp in (None,0.0): return None,"NO_CONTRAST_SIGNAL"
        if dq0 is None or abs(dq0)>0.0: return None,"NOT_CONTRAST_ISOLATED"
        m=2.0*(W-D-dHs)/dqp
        return m, "PASS_CANDIDATE" if m>0 else "NONPOSITIVE_METRIC"
    return None,"NO_METRIC_INFERENCE_FOR_THIS_CLASS"

if __name__=="__main__":
    if len(sys.argv)!=2:
        raise SystemExit("usage: analyzer.py telemetry.csv")
    with open(sys.argv[1],newline="",encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rows=list(csv.DictReader(f))
    for r in rows:
        m,status=analyze_row(r)
        print(r.get("event_id",""),r["event_class"],r.get("contrast_basis_id",""),status,m)

title: Event Exchange, Metric Identification and Parity
note: Supporting review · 19 September 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Conditional conservation, revised acquisition requirements and exact symmetry checks. The analyzer is a slope helper; no acquired event is claimed. Event exchange, metric identification and parity Supporting mathematical and protocol review · 19 September 2026 The new material separates three questions: what a proposed event conserves, which measurements identify its quadratic storage metric, and what additional symmetry would distinguish two three-dimensional state sectors. It improves the acquisition specification and narrows the unresolved source requirements. It does not supply a measured event, a derived event-source law, or an identification with a physical field. The finite theorem statements remain in Paper I and Paper II. This review concerns conditional extensions. “Burden” here means an auxiliary finite vector with a specified quadratic storage function; no physical energy or action unit is assigned. Download the review and reproduction supplement · Independent verification results · Source inventory What has advanced Question Current result Remaining requirement Can one event identify a storage metric? A mixed scalar balance supplies one equation. Two independent sector equations can identify a two-parameter metric. Eligible, attributable observations and the stated symmetry assumption. Does the revised protocol isolate the event? Version 0.2 specifies matched controls, directional receipts, a fixed region and event timing. Independent protocol review and an implementation that enforces those requirements. Can reciprocal exchange conserve total storage? Yes, for an explicitly supplied skew block generator. Evidence selecting that generator and its coefficients. Does tetrahedral symmetry select a parity? The tested gradient/cycle and Hodge-star constructions have precise representation limits. A paired standard sector permits a swap. A source-selected involution compatible with the relevant action. Has the acquisition been completed? No acquired session is supplied in this package. Qualified source data, frozen scoring and independent replay. 1. Start with the accounting model Let cc be the real support coordinates in a fixed region and b∈ℝ4b\in\mathbb R^4 the auxiliary vertex coordinates. Define HS=12cTc,HB=12bTMBb,MB=MBT>0. H_S=\tfrac12 c^Tc,\qquad H_B=\tfrac12 b^TM_Bb,\qquad M_B=M_B^T>0. The proposed event receipt records finite changes in these quantities, together with dissipation DD and external work WW: R=ΔHS+ΔHB+D−W. R=\Delta H_S+\Delta H_B+D-W. This is a declared accounting test. In the closed, nondissipative case, R=0R=0 reduces to ΔHB=−ΔHS\Delta H_B=-\Delta H_S. For a subregion, boundary transfers must also be defined and included. Internal incidence currents redistribute support; they do not by themselves demonstrate conversion into the auxiliary vector. A finite balance is not an infinitesimal law of motion. Even exact closure of this receipt would not identify a unique exchange generator. 2. Symmetry reduces the metric; data identify it If the vertex metric is invariant under the permutation action of S4S_4, then P0=14𝟏𝟏T,P⊥=I−P0,MB=m0P0+m⊥P⊥,m0,m⊥>0. P_0=\tfrac14\mathbf1\mathbf1^T,\quad P_\perp=I-P_0,\quad M_B=m_0P_0+m_\perp P_\perp,\quad m_0,m_\perp>0. The two parameters are the weights of the uniform and contrast sectors. For closed events, with qr=∥Prb∥2q_r=\|P_rb\|^2, each receipt gives m0Δq0+m⊥Δq⊥=−2ΔHS. m_0\Delta q_0+m_\perp\Delta q_\perp=-2\Delta H_S. One mixed receipt has rank at most one and cannot uniquely determine both positive weights. Two independent rows can. Sector-isolating events are a convenient sufficient design; a full-rank mixed design is also possible. The symmetry assumption matters. Three equal measurements along an orthonormal contrast basis do not prove isotropy. For example, M=(21/201/220002) M=\begin{pmatrix}2&1/2&0\\1/2&2&0\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix} is positive definite and has three equal diagonal entries, yet gives 5/25/2 along (1,1,0)/2(1,1,0)/\sqrt2. Either independently justify permutation invariance or test cross terms before treating directional agreement as a complete metric identification. 3. What the revised acquisition specification fixes The supplied version 0.2 supersedes version 0.1 for execution. It defines a fixed orthonormal basis: u0=(1,1,1,1)/2,u1=(1,−1,0,0)/2, u_0=(1,1,1,1)/2,\quad u_1=(1,-1,0,0)/\sqrt2, u2=(1,1,−2,0)/6,u3=(1,1,1,−3)/12. u_2=(1,1,-2,0)/\sqrt6,\quad u_3=(1,1,1,-3)/\sqrt{12}. A directional receipt is the treatment-minus-control difference of the pre/post changes in (uiTb)2(u_i^Tb)^2. It is not the squared norm of the difference between treatment and control states. The improved design requires matched initial states and inputs, a fixed support region, the complete four-coordinate auxiliary state, exactly one relevant event, recorded operator order, and immediate response windows. Null controls set the off-axis equivalence floors. Uniform and contrast trials estimate separate positive weights; mixed trials are reserved for checking the fitted balance without refitting. For qualified closed trials, the proposed origin-constrained estimate is m̂i=∑jxjyj∑jxj2,xj=δqi,j,yj=−2δHS,j. \widehat m_i=\frac{\sum_j x_jy_j}{\sum_jx_j^2},\qquad x_j=\delta q_{i,j},\quad y_j=-2\delta H_{S,j}. This is undefined without nonzero excitation. If dissipation, external work or boundary transfer has a nonzero attributable contribution, the response must be corrected under an explicit signed accounting convention. The displayed closed-trial formula alone does not perform that correction. Sample maximum null responses are operational tolerances, not confidence or coverage guarantees. Before acquisition, specify sample counts, uncertainty treatment, directional agreement limits and held-out acceptance limits. If the predictor is measured with error, an ordinary slope fit also needs a justified errors-in-variables treatment or an explicit approximation. 4. The analyzer is a slope helper, not a complete scorer Independent synthetic probes confirm that the supplied version 0.2 script computes the advertised slopes from complete numeric pairs. They also show that it prints estimates for deliberately ineligible inputs. Input problem Observed software behavior Required repair before execution Two events, mismatched states, flagged confounding or external receipts The script still computes the same slope. Enforce eligibility and accounting before fitting. Off-axis response in a nominally isolated trial The off-axis receipt is ignored by the selected fit. Apply the frozen null floors to every inactive direction. Duplicate treatment row The last row overwrites the earlier row. Reject duplicate roles and ambiguous pair identifiers. Negative or nonfinite estimate The raw value is printed. Validate finite inputs and classify positivity failures. Missing pair or mixed trial No complete outcome classification is produced. Report exclusions and score the held-out residual explicitly. These are controlled software tests, not experimental observations. The original script is preserved unchanged. Its output must not be presented as a protocol PASS. A qualified scorer must also verify raw-state/receipt consistency, pair metadata, training/held-out separation and the predeclared outcome rules. The uploaded CSV template has consistent 52-column rows; its empty preregistration entries are not acquired data. 5. A conditional reciprocal exchange law On two equally sized state blocks, a supplied constant matrix KK defines JX=(0K−KT0),ẋ=JX∇(HS+HB). J_X=\begin{pmatrix}0&K\\-K^T&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \dot x=J_X\nabla(H_S+H_B). Thus ċ=Fb\dot c=Fb, ḃ=−Gc\dot b=-Gc, with F=KMBF=KM_B and G=KTG=K^T. The identity F=GTMBF=G^TM_B gives exact conservation of the sum of the two quadratic storage functions. This is a constructed finite-dimensional model; conservation does not select KK. If both the coupling and metric have the two-sector form, K=k0P0+k⊥P⊥K=k_0P_0+k_\perp P_\perp, the squared sector frequencies are k02m0k_0^2m_0 and k⊥2m⊥k_\perp^2m_\perp. Symmetry does not make them equal. A nonnegative frequency is |kr|mr|k_r|\sqrt{m_r}; a signed generator coefficient is krmrk_r\sqrt{m_r}. Equal squared frequencies do not fix their relative signs. Bidirectional derivative measurements would identify mr=fr/grm_r=f_r/g_r when gr≠0g_r\ne0, with the sign convention ḃ=−Gc\dot b=-Gc kept explicit. The uploaded symbolic examples and the independent controls establish algebraic consistency only. They do not provide recovered UD event coefficients. 6. Parity requires more than an invertible evolution For retained variables q,p∈ℝ3q,p\in\mathbb R^3, diagonal tetrahedral symmetry permits the mixed term in H(q,p)=12(a∥q∥2+2χqTp+b∥p∥2). H(q,p)=\tfrac12\bigl(a\|q\|^2+2\chi q^Tp+b\|p\|^2\bigr). An independently justified invariance H(q,−p)=H(q,p)H(q,-p)=H(q,p) would force χ=0\chi=0. Invertibility of a flow, a route orientation or a declaration that pp is odd does not establish that invariance. An action-level argument must additionally specify the time reversal, canonical structure and endpoint conventions needed to induce the stated Hamiltonian parity. The exact finite representation checks give a useful candidate screen: Candidate What is established What it does not establish Oriented K4K_4 gradient/cycle split A commuting involution with two three-dimensional eigenspaces. The sectors are inequivalent S4S_4 representations, so this is not two copies of the same standard representation. Four-coordinate Hodge star Two three-dimensional eigenspaces and compatibility with even permutations. Odd permutations exchange the eigenspaces; it does not commute with all of S4S_4. Swap of two standard representations A commuting involution whose even and odd sectors are both standard. Source selection and invariance of a given action remain separate tests. Paired five-seat B/C standard sectors Each five-seat carrier restricts to 2𝟏⊕V32\mathbf1\oplus V_3; its paired standard sectors admit the swap. Full-channel mismatch or isospectrality alone does not settle the projected action test. These are scoped results about specified candidates, not an exclusion of every possible parity. The paired B/C construction is an additional candidate; the earlier two-standard-sector swap already passes the abstract representation test, so uniqueness or an unqualified “first structural pass” is not claimed here. For B/C, the supplied addendum names the remaining projected test P3T5(t)P3=0P_3T_5(t)P_3=0. The dedicated audit is absent from the upload, and no executable projected-action calculation is supplied here. Its result remains open. 7. The next reviewable step Complete the four missing source references listed below and provide the projected B/C action calculation. Turn the version 0.2 written eligibility rules into explicit input rejection, exclusion reporting and held-out scoring. Preserve the present helper as an earlier implementation. Declare the metric symmetry, boundary accounting, uncertainty model and acceptance thresholds before collecting target data. Obtain independent review of that completed protocol, then acquire the matched event receipts. Keep a supplied exchange model distinct from an identified source law. Historical source searches in the uploaded audits are reported as the author’s searches of the named sources. They have not been independently repeated here and do not establish absence from every possible archive. Source completeness and reproduction The supplement preserves 43 available originals: six manifests and 37 referenced files. All 37 available manifest references match their stated SHA-256 values. Four other references are missing; the release is therefore a partial source record, not a complete reproduction of all six original packages. Missing references: UD_FIVE_SEAT_BC_STANDARD_SECTOR_INVOLUTION_AUDIT_v0.1.md UD_FIVE_SEAT_BC_INVOLUTION_STATUS_v0.1.csv UD_PRIMITIVE_LOCAL_SUPPORT_BURDEN_EXCHANGE_GENERATOR_v0.1.md UD_PRIMITIVE_EXCHANGE_GENERATOR_SYMBOLIC_PROBE_v0.1.csv The independent script reconstructs the finite projector and representation calculations, verifies conditional conservation and identifiability counterexamples, and probes the supplied analyzer on synthetic inputs. It does not replay the missing probe file or a physical session. Original source status labels remain historical assertions, with the qualifications above controlling this review’s interpretation. title: Burden Ancestry Tagging
note: Preserved source · read with current review · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Original source and historical status labels retained. The current review qualifies model definitions, fixed-space memory, topology, storage and reproducibility. SOURCE_ADDENDUM_BURDEN_ANCESTRY_TAGGING_v0.1 Date: 2026-09-18 Status: ADMITTED SOURCE ADDENDUM / PROVENANCE REFINEMENT Physical promotion: 0 Purpose: make inherited burden IinhI_{\mathrm inh} identifiable without adding a decay, mixing, or inheritance coefficient. 1. Motivation Current aggregate burden continuity is Δρ=BincjB+sB. \Delta \rho = B_{\mathrm inc}j_B+s_B. Aggregate receipts do not identify which portion of later burden descends from a prior parent or source event after mixing. This addendum refines the burden field by ancestry provenance while preserving the aggregate equations exactly. 2. Tagged burden decomposition Let 𝒜\mathcal A be an append-only set of ancestry/source tags. Define ρi=∑a∈𝒜ρi(a). \boxed{ \rho_i = \sum_{a\in\mathcal A} \rho_i^{(a)}. } Each tag aa has immutable provenance metadata: a=(creation event,creation block/cell,source class). a= ( \text{creation event}, \text{creation block/cell}, \text{source class} ). No numerical parameter is attached to the tag. 3. Tagged continuity Each ancestry component obeys the same typed continuity grammar: Δρ(a)=BincjB(a)+sB(a). \boxed{ \Delta\rho^{(a)} = B_{\mathrm inc}j_B^{(a)} + s_B^{(a)}. } The tagged currents and sources must sum to the aggregate objects: jB=∑ajB(a), \boxed{ j_B = \sum_a j_B^{(a)}, } sB=∑asB(a). \boxed{ s_B = \sum_a s_B^{(a)}. } Therefore ∑aΔρ(a)=Binc∑ajB(a)+∑asB(a)=BincjB+sB. \sum_a \Delta\rho^{(a)} = B_{\mathrm inc} \sum_a j_B^{(a)} + \sum_a s_B^{(a)} = B_{\mathrm inc}j_B+s_B. So the addendum is exactly aggregate-compatible. AUTO_LOCK ANCESTRY_TAGGED_CONTINUITY_SUMS_EXACTLY_TO_AGGREGATE_BURDEN_CONTINUITY_v0.1 4. No spontaneous retagging Transport and redistribution preserve ancestry labels. A burden element may change location but not provenance. New positive burden creation receives a new tag unless a separately receipted source law explicitly declares it to be transformation of an existing tagged stock. Thus the addendum forbids ancestry reassignment as an unreceipted bookkeeping shortcut. AUTO_LOCK BURDEN_TRANSPORT_PRESERVES_ANCESTRY_LABEL_v0.1 5. Tagged block stock For any declared block SS, BS(a)=∑i∈Sρi(a). \boxed{ B_S^{(a)} = \sum_{i\in S} \rho_i^{(a)}. } Its exact receipt equation is ΔBS(a)=J∂S(a),net+SS(a),net. \boxed{ \Delta B_S^{(a)} = J_{\partial S}^{(a),{\mathrm net}} + S_S^{(a),{\mathrm net}}. } Summing over tags recovers the aggregate block equation. 6. Birth-time definition of inherited tags Let a daughter block/cell DD be created at event b(D). b(D). Define the inherited tag set 𝒜inh(D)={a∈𝒜:b(a)<b(D)}, \boxed{ \mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D) = \left\{ a\in\mathcal A: b(a)<b(D) \right\}, } optionally restricted to tags actually present on the daughter support/interface at birth. Tags created at or after b(D)b(D) are not inherited by DD. 7. Exact inherited-load coordinate Define Iinh(D,n)=∑a∈𝒜inh(D)BD(a)(n). \boxed{ I_{\mathrm inh}(D,n) = \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D)} B_D^{(a)}(n). } Equivalently, Iinh(D,n)=∑a∈𝒜inh(D)∑i∈Dρi,n(a). \boxed{ I_{\mathrm inh}(D,n) = \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D)} \sum_{i\in D} \rho_{i,n}^{(a)}. } This is a provenance stock, not a fitted fraction of total burden. AUTO_LOCK INHERITED_LOAD_IS_PREBIRTH_TAGGED_BURDEN_STOCK_v0.1 Classification: EXACT_INTERNAL under this admitted source addendum. 8. New-local burden coordinate Define the complementary locally generated/post-birth burden: Blocal/new(D,n)=∑a∉𝒜inh(D)BD(a)(n). \boxed{ B_{\mathrm local/new}(D,n) = \sum_{a\notin\mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D)} B_D^{(a)}(n). } Then exactly, BDpkt(n)=Iinh(D,n)+Blocal/new(D,n). \boxed{ B_D^{\mathrm pkt}(n) = I_{\mathrm inh}(D,n) + B_{\mathrm local/new}(D,n). } No mixing coefficient appears. 9. Null compatibility If ancestry labels are ignored, ∑aρ(a)=ρ, \sum_a\rho^{(a)}=\rho, and all current aggregate burden equations are recovered unchanged. Therefore this addendum changes provenance resolution, not aggregate burden dynamics. 10. Scope This addendum: closes identifiability of inherited burden; does not add a new force or physical degree of freedom; does not specify a new global burden-current constitutive law; does not imply a physical time interpretation; does not change coefficient values. Physical promotion: 0.

Recursive daughter definition Let a recursive K4 daughter cell DD be born from a parent-side interface at event b(D)b(D). Ancestry tags are partitioned into: 𝒜inh(D)={a:b(a)<b(D)}, \mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D) = \{a:b(a)<b(D)\}, and 𝒜new(D)={a:b(a)≥b(D)}. \mathcal A_{\mathrm new}(D) = \{a:b(a)\ge b(D)\}. The daughter burden decomposes exactly: BDpkt=Iinh(D)+Bnew(D). \boxed{ B_D^{\mathrm pkt} = I_{\mathrm inh}(D) + B_{\mathrm new}(D). } with Iinh(D)=∑a∈𝒜inh(D)BD(a). \boxed{ I_{\mathrm inh}(D) = \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D)} B_D^{(a)}. } This closes the definition of inherited load through arbitrary recursion depth. 2. Exact tagged recursive continuity For each inherited ancestry tag aa, ΔBD(a)=J∂D(a),net+SD(a),net. \boxed{ \Delta B_D^{(a)} = J_{\partial D}^{(a),{\mathrm net}} + S_D^{(a),{\mathrm net}}. } Summing only inherited tags gives ΔIinh(D)=J∂D,inhnet+SD,inhnet, \boxed{ \Delta I_{\mathrm inh}(D) = J_{\partial D,{\mathrm inh}}^{\mathrm net} + S_{D,{\mathrm inh}}^{\mathrm net}, } where J∂D,inhnet=∑a∈𝒜inh(D)J∂D(a),net, J_{\partial D,{\mathrm inh}}^{\mathrm net} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D)} J_{\partial D}^{(a),{\mathrm net}}, and SD,inhnet=∑a∈𝒜inh(D)SD(a),net. S_{D,{\mathrm inh}}^{\mathrm net} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm inh}(D)} S_D^{(a),{\mathrm net}}. AUTO_LOCK RECURSIVE_INHERITED_LOAD_OBEYS_TAGGED_BLOCK_CONTINUITY_v0.1 3. No-new-inherited-source specialization If after daughter birth no positive source is allowed to create burden under an already inherited tag, then SD,inhsrc+=0. S_{D,{\mathrm inh}}^{\mathrm src+}=0. Inherited burden can then change only through: tagged boundary transport; tagged sink/removal; internal redistribution, which cancels in the aggregate inherited stock. Thus internal mixing cannot create or destroy ancestry. 4. Closed K4 Q163 theorem Current Q163 supplies, for the normalized K4 relaxational burden lane, j=13D⊤ρ⊥, j = \frac13D^\top\rho_\perp, ρ̇⊥=−43ρ⊥. \dot\rho_\perp = -\frac43\rho_\perp. Because this operator is linear and tag-blind, every ancestry component separately obeys j(a)=13D⊤ρ⊥(a), \boxed{ j^{(a)} = \frac13D^\top\rho_\perp^{(a)}, } ρ̇⊥(a)=−43ρ⊥(a). \boxed{ \dot\rho_\perp^{(a)} = -\frac43\rho_\perp^{(a)}. } Write ρ‾(a)=14𝟏⊤ρ(a). \bar\rho^{(a)} = \frac14\mathbf1^\top\rho^{(a)}. Then the exact tagged solution is ρ(a)(s)=ρ‾(a)𝟏+e−4s/3ρ⊥(a)(0). \boxed{ \rho^{(a)}(s) = \bar\rho^{(a)}\mathbf1 + e^{-4s/3} \rho_\perp^{(a)}(0). } Taking the sum over the four K4 vertices, 𝟏⊤ρ(a)(s)=𝟏⊤ρ(a)(0). \boxed{ \mathbf1^\top\rho^{(a)}(s) = \mathbf1^\top\rho^{(a)}(0). } Therefore on a closed source-free K4 relaxational lane: Iinh(a)(s)=Iinh(a)(0). \boxed{ I_{\mathrm inh}^{(a)}(s) = I_{\mathrm inh}^{(a)}(0). } AUTO_LOCK Q163_CLOSED_K4_MIXING_PRESERVES_EACH_ANCESTRY_TAG_TOTAL_v0.1 Classification: EXACT CONDITIONAL within the locked Q163 scope. The exponential factor redistributes tagged burden; it does not erase its total ancestry stock. 5. Worked exact ancestry example Take one ancestry tag AA with initial K4 vertex burden ρ(A)(0)=(1,0,0,0)⊤. \rho^{(A)}(0) = (1,0,0,0)^\top. Then ρ‾(A)=14, \bar\rho^{(A)} = \frac14, and ρ⊥(A)(0)=(34,−14,−14,−14)⊤. \rho_\perp^{(A)}(0) = \left( \frac34, -\frac14, -\frac14, -\frac14 \right)^\top. Hence ρ(A)(s)=14(1111)+e−4s/3(3/4−1/4−1/4−1/4). \boxed{ \rho^{(A)}(s) = \frac14 \begin{pmatrix} 1\\1\\1\\1 \end{pmatrix} + e^{-4s/3} \begin{pmatrix} 3/4\\-1/4\\-1/4\\-1/4 \end{pmatrix}. } For all ss, ∑iρi(A)(s)=1. \boxed{ \sum_i\rho_i^{(A)}(s)=1. } The ancestry becomes spatially mixed but remains exactly traceable. 6. Daughter birth across a K4 face Under the standard vertex-based burden representation, a daughter tetrahedron shares three existing vertices with its parent-side face and introduces one new apex vertex. For any pre-existing ancestry tag aa, provenance requires that a genuinely new apex has no pre-birth amount of that tag unless an explicit transfer/source event deposits it: ρapex,new(a)(b(D)−)=0. \boxed{ \rho_{\mathrm apex,new}^{(a)}(b(D)^-)=0. } Immediately after topological insertion but before further tagged transport/source update, the daughter’s ancestry trace is therefore the restriction of the old tagged field to its shared-face vertices: Ibirth(a),trace(D)=∑v∈fsharedρv(a). \boxed{ I_{\mathrm birth}^{(a),{\mathrm trace}}(D) = \sum_{v\in f_{\mathrm shared}} \rho_v^{(a)}. } This is a local overlapping trace, not a globally additive partition of burden, because the shared vertices also belong to the parent-side complex. Q163 is explicitly scoped to normalized K4 burden mixing. Therefore the post-birth evolution Iinh(D,n) I_{\mathrm inh}(D,n) is exactly receiptable through tagged continuity, but not yet universally predictable from parent state alone. The missing object is a global recursive tagged burden operator, schematically ℒBglobal \boxed{ \mathcal L_B^{\mathrm global} } or an equivalent constitutive current law jB,e(a)=𝒥e[ρ(a),X,gates] j_{B,e}^{(a)} = \mathcal J_e \left[ \rho^{(a)},X,\text{gates} \right] on the glued complex. AUTO_LOCK ANCESTRY_TAGGING_CLOSES_IINH_IDENTIFIABILITY_BUT_NOT_GLOBAL_RECURSIVE_BURDEN_PREDICTION_v0.1 8. Recursive lineage vector For a daughter DD, define the ancestry vector 𝐈D(n)=(BD(a1)(n),BD(a2)(n),…). \boxed{ \mathbf I_D(n) = \left( B_D^{(a_1)}(n), B_D^{(a_2)}(n), \ldots \right). } Then Iinh(D,n)=∑a:b(a)<b(D)𝐈D,a(n). I_{\mathrm inh}(D,n) = \sum_{a:b(a)<b(D)} \mathbf I_{D,a}(n). This vector is append-only in tag space: new source events may append new coordinates, but existing provenance coordinates are not overwritten. This gives exact genealogy across arbitrary recursive depth. 9. Tree-recursion special case For a parent-child lineage D0→D1→⋯→DN, D_0\to D_1\to\cdots\to D_N, let a0a_0 be the root ancestry tag. Then root inherited burden in generation kk is Ia0(Dk,n)=BDk(a0)(n). \boxed{ I_{a_0}(D_k,n) = B_{D_k}^{(a_0)}(n). } Its recurrence is always Ia0(Dk,n+1)=Ia0(Dk,n)+J∂Dk(a0),net+SDk(a0),net. \boxed{ I_{a_0}(D_k,n+1) = I_{a_0}(D_k,n) + J_{\partial D_k}^{(a_0),{\mathrm net}} + S_{D_k}^{(a_0),{\mathrm net}}. } No ancestry fraction is fitted. 10. OPEN predictive tagged current law on the full recursive glued complex; ancestry-resolved sink/source constitutive laws; full breathing obstruction map FBF_B. 11.
