Physical promotion: 0. manuscript/UD_JOP_v2.40_LEHIGH_ISOLATION_LEAK_QUALIFICATION_ADDENDUM_v0.1.mdJOP v2.40 Addendum — Lehigh Isolation / Leak Qualification Gate v0.1 The prospective Lehigh tank-side physical comparator is supplemented by a pretarget hydraulic isolation qualification gate. The Bitlismen source confirms manual valves on all tank outlets, independently controlled pumps, pump-inlet solenoids, and four tank-level pressure sensors. These control states do not by themselves prove zero residual flow. For each of the two future comparator states, a matched-level no-pump hold is therefore required. Using source-authored tank geometry Vi(hi)V_i(h_i), the no-pump drift is estimated as the OLS volume slope ℓ̂i,r=∑n(tn−t‾)(Vi(hi,n)−V‾i)∑n(tn−t‾)2. \hat\ell_{i,r} = \frac{\sum_n(t_n-\bar t)(V_i(h_{i,n})-\bar V_i)} {\sum_n(t_n-\bar t)^2}. Each tank/state must be statistically or deterministically compatible with zero under a pretarget source-authored metrology band. Detectable drift blocks comparator scoring. A passed no-drift test is not promoted to exact zero leakage. The maximum undetected leak is retained as Li,r=|ℓ̂i,r|+frozen drift band, L_{i,r}=|\hat\ell_{i,r}|+\text{frozen drift band}, and contributes conservatively BR14leak=14∑i,rLi,r B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm leak} = \frac14\sum_{i,r}L_{i,r} to the final Lehigh comparator tolerance. Thus imperfect manual-valve closure cannot silently enter the physical comparator as an unmodeled assumption. Purpose Qualify the actual Lehigh/Bitlismen hydraulic isolation before the preregistered tank-side physical comparator is allowed to score. The comparator assumes that, during a fresh filling window, tank storage change is attributable to delivered pump inflow on the declared branch. Manual valve closure and pump-off commands cannot silently be equated with zero residual hydraulic flow. This protocol therefore measures the residual no-pump storage drift directly. 1. Source-authored hardware basis The Bitlismen Quadruple Tank Process Control Research Platform source states that: the system contains two coupled-tank subsystems; the upper-tank bottom outlet can feed the lower tank; lower tanks drain to the main reservoir; upper tanks have another direct outlet to the reservoir; all outlets have manual valves; each tank has a pressure sensor for level measurement; couplings may be changed using 3/8″3/8'', 5/16″5/16'', and 1/4″1/4'' tubes; water is delivered by two independently controlled pumps; pump inlet flow can be opened/closed using solenoid valves. Bitlismen separately identifies the April 2024 Lehigh installation as a custom quadruple-tank platform. These source statements establish that hydraulic isolation is physically configurable. They do not establish that a commanded/manual CLOSED state has zero leakage. 2. Qualification principle For each future comparator state r∈{0,1}, r\in\{0,1\}, perform a matched-level no-pump hold before the fresh target score is opened. At the matched state: bring all four tanks to the predeclared state-rr level band; set both pump drives to the source-declared OFF state; close both pump-inlet solenoid paths; set every non-pump outlet/intertank/bypass path required by the comparator to the declared CLOSED/isolation state; wait the predeclared settling interval; record a fixed, predeclared hold window; do not alter the hold window after observing drift. The same tank geometry and level-metrology receipts required by the comparator are used here. 3. General storage-drift estimator For tank ii, use the source-authored geometry Vi=Vi(hi). V_i=V_i(h_i). For each hold-window level sample, transform vi,n=Vi(hi,n). v_{i,n}=V_i(h_{i,n}). Let the frozen hold window have sample times tnt_n. Define the OLS-with-intercept volume slope ℓ̂i,r=∑n(tn−t‾)(vi,n−v‾i)∑n(tn−t‾)2. \boxed{ \hat\ell_{i,r} = \frac{ \sum_n(t_n-\bar t)(v_{i,n}-\bar v_i) }{ \sum_n(t_n-\bar t)^2 }. } Units: [ℓ̂i,r]=volume/time. [\hat\ell_{i,r}]={\mathrm volume/time}. Interpretation: ℓ̂i,r>0 \hat\ell_{i,r}>0 means net unmeasured inflow/storage gain, while ℓ̂i,r<0 \hat\ell_{i,r}<0 means net unmeasured outflow/storage loss. Both signs are isolation failures when detectably nonzero. Constant-area specialization Only if source-authored geometry supplies constant area AiA_i, Vi=Aihi+Vi,0, V_i=A_i h_i+V_{i,0}, then ℓ̂i,r=Aim̂i,rhold. \boxed{ \hat\ell_{i,r}=A_i\hat m_{i,r}^{\mathrm hold}. } No generic geometry is admitted. 4. Matched-level requirement Leakage through imperfect valves can depend on hydrostatic head. One no-pump test at an unrelated level is therefore insufficient. For each comparator state rr, the hold test must be performed at levels matched to that state. Define the hold and comparator mean levels h‾i,rhold,h‾i,rfill. \bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm hold}, \qquad \bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm fill}. The matched-level gate is not assigned an arbitrary tolerance. It passes only if the authenticated level metrology establishes compatibility: Hard-bound route |h‾i,rhold−h‾i,rfill|≤BΔhi,rmatch. \boxed{ |\bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm hold}-\bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm fill}| \le B_{\Delta h_{i,r}}^{\mathrm match}. } Standard-uncertainty route |h‾i,rhold−h‾i,rfill|≤kmatchu(Δhi,rmatch). \boxed{ |\bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm hold}-\bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm fill}| \le k_{\mathrm match}\, u(\Delta h_{i,r}^{\mathrm match}). } Both BΔhmatchB_{\Delta h}^{\mathrm match} or kmatchk_{\mathrm match} must be frozen from source/metrology before target scoring. No post-hoc level-match tolerance is allowed. 5. Zero-drift metrology gate The no-pump isolation test uses the same two allowed metrology routes as the comparator. Route H — hard error bound Let Bℓi,r B_{\ell_{i,r}} be the authenticated propagated absolute bound on the hold-slope estimate. Tank ii, state rr qualifies only if |ℓ̂i,r|≤Bℓi,r. \boxed{ |\hat\ell_{i,r}| \le B_{\ell_{i,r}}. } Route C — standard covariance Let u(ℓi,r) u(\ell_{i,r}) be the source-propagated standard uncertainty and let khold k_{\mathrm hold} be a pretarget coverage factor. Tank ii, state rr qualifies only if |ℓ̂i,r|≤kholdu(ℓi,r). \boxed{ |\hat\ell_{i,r}| \le k_{\mathrm hold}u(\ell_{i,r}). } No value of kholdk_{\mathrm hold} is set in this protocol. 6. OLS hold-slope uncertainty For fixed sample times, define wn=tn−t‾Stt,Stt=∑n(tn−t‾)2. w_n = \frac{t_n-\bar t}{S_{tt}}, \qquad S_{tt}=\sum_n(t_n-\bar t)^2. Then ℓ̂i,r=∑nwnvi,n. \hat\ell_{i,r} = \sum_n w_n v_{i,n}. For a source-authored volume-sample covariance matrix ΣV,i,r\Sigma_{V,i,r}, u2(ℓi,r)=wTΣV,i,rw \boxed{ u^2(\ell_{i,r}) = w^T\Sigma_{V,i,r}w } is exact for fixed timing. If timing uncertainty is material, the already frozen slope timing-sensitivity law must be included; it cannot be silently ignored. For hard volume-sample bounds BV,i,nB_{V,i,n}, Bℓi,r≤∑n|wn|BV,i,n+Bℓi,rtiming \boxed{ B_{\ell_{i,r}} \le \sum_n |w_n| B_{V,i,n} + B_{\ell_{i,r}}^{\mathrm timing} } with the timing term source-derived or explicitly proven negligible. 7. Qualification is not a zero-leak claim Even when |ℓ̂i,r| |\hat\ell_{i,r}| lies inside its no-drift band, the actual residual leak is not set to zero. Define a conservative undetected leak allowance. Hard-bound route Li,r=|ℓ̂i,r|+Bℓi,r. \boxed{ L_{i,r} = |\hat\ell_{i,r}|+B_{\ell_{i,r}}. } Standard-uncertainty route Li,r=|ℓ̂i,r|+kholdu(ℓi,r). \boxed{ L_{i,r} = |\hat\ell_{i,r}|+k_{\mathrm hold}u(\ell_{i,r}). } This quantity is carried forward as a bounded contamination term. 8. Leak contribution to the Lehigh R14R_{14} comparator Let the signed residual non-pump storage drifts during the matched fill states be λi,r. \lambda_{i,r}. The contamination of the two-state branch-contrast residual is R14leak=14[(λ1,1+λ4,1−λ1,0−λ4,0)−(λ2,1+λ3,1−λ2,0−λ3,0)]. \boxed{ R_{14}^{\mathrm leak} = \frac14 \left[ (\lambda_{1,1}+\lambda_{4,1}-\lambda_{1,0}-\lambda_{4,0}) - (\lambda_{2,1}+\lambda_{3,1}-\lambda_{2,0}-\lambda_{3,0}) \right]. } If each matched-state drift obeys |λi,r|≤Li,r, |\lambda_{i,r}|\le L_{i,r}, then by the triangle inequality, BR14leak=14∑r∈{0,1}∑i=14Li,r. \boxed{ B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm leak} = \frac14 \sum_{r\in\{0,1\}} \sum_{i=1}^4 L_{i,r}. } This is a conservative bound. No cancellation between tank leaks is assumed. 9. Integration with the main comparator gate Let the main comparator’s pre-leak metrology band be: Hard-bound comparator BR14meas. B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm meas}. Then the final allowed band becomes BR14total=BR14meas+BR14leak. \boxed{ B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm total} = B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm meas} + B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm leak}. } The physical comparator PASS condition is |R14(LEHIGH)|≤BR14total. \boxed{ |R_{14}^{(\mathrm{LEHIGH})}| \le B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm total}. } Standard-uncertainty comparator If the ordinary measurement contribution is kcovu(R14), k_{\mathrm cov}u(R_{14}), the bounded isolation nuisance is added conservatively: TR14total=kcovu(R14)+BR14leak. \boxed{ T_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm total} = k_{\mathrm cov}u(R_{14}) + B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm leak}. } PASS requires |R14(LEHIGH)|≤TR14total. \boxed{ |R_{14}^{(\mathrm{LEHIGH})}| \le T_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm total}. } The leak allowance is not placed in quadrature unless a future source establishes a probabilistic leak model and a separately frozen version permits it. 10. Isolation failure rule If any tank/state fails the no-drift metrology gate, |ℓ̂i,r|>frozen zero-drift band, |\hat\ell_{i,r}|>\text{frozen zero-drift band}, then: ISOLATION_QUALIFICATION := FAIL LEHIGH_PHYSICAL_COMPARATOR := NOT_SCORED v0.1 does not repair a detected leak by subtracting the observed hold drift. Why: leak may be head-dependent; leak may change between hold and fill; manual-valve hysteresis/reseating may matter; subtraction would introduce an additional constitutive assumption. A future leak-correction protocol would require independent source derivation and preregistration. 11. Pump-off / valve-state source receipt The hold test requires a pretarget operator/hardware receipt containing: pump1_drive_state := OFF pump2_drive_state := OFF pump1_inlet_solenoid := CLOSED pump2_inlet_solenoid := CLOSED tank1_to_reservoir_path := CLOSED tank2_to_reservoir_path := CLOSED tank3_to_tank1_path := CLOSED tank4_to_tank2_path := CLOSED tank3_direct_reservoir_path := CLOSED tank4_direct_reservoir_path := CLOSED all_other_bypass_paths := NONE_OR_CLOSED overflow_possible := FALSE If the custom Lehigh build uses different path names, the source operator must supply an equivalent typed map. Unknown path: SOURCE_BLOCKED_CONFIGURATION 12. Hold-window controls Before fresh target acquisition, freeze: state0 hold target level band state1 hold target level band settling duration hold duration sample interval OLS estimator geometry receipt level metrology receipt timing metrology receipt k_hold or hard-bound route k_match or hard matched-level bound No hold window may be lengthened because the initial result is inconvenient. No drift segment may be dropped. 13. Optional repeated-hold diagnostic A repeated hold may be preregistered before target exposure to test manual-valve reseating repeatability. If used, the repeat count and aggregation rule must be frozen beforehand. v0.1 does not require a repeat and does not authorize adding repeats after seeing the first drift. 14. Current source disposition At freeze time: MANUAL_OUTLET_VALVES := SOURCE_CONFIRMED PUMP_INLET_SOLENOIDS := SOURCE_CONFIRMED TANK_LEVEL_SENSORS := SOURCE_CONFIRMED CUSTOM_LEHIGH_PLATFORM := SOURCE_CONFIRMED RUN_SPECIFIC_VALVE_STATE := OPEN TANK_GEOMETRY := OPEN LEVEL_METROLOGY := OPEN HOLD_METROLOGY_BAND := OPEN MATCHED_LEVEL_BAND := OPEN ISOLATION_PROTOCOL := PRETARGET_FROZEN EXECUTION := SOURCE_BLOCKED PHYSICAL_PROMOTION := 0

A future fresh run is bound before scoring to pump-flow provenance, source-only extraction, two fill windows, two matched-level no-pump hold windows, source-authored tank geometry, run-specific hydraulic-isolation receipts, and a hard-bound metrology manifest. Execution chain This package binds the entire future Lehigh physical-comparator lane under one immutable pre-score freeze: pump-flow source provenance→authenticated G14/G23 source stream→matched-level no-pump isolation qualification→independent tank-storage comparator→cross-platform report \boxed{ \text{pump-flow source provenance} \rightarrow \text{authenticated }G_{14}/G_{23}\text{ source stream} \rightarrow \text{matched-level no-pump isolation qualification} \rightarrow \text{independent tank-storage comparator} \rightarrow \text{cross-platform report} } No stage may be redefined after fresh physical outcomes are available. 1. Frozen source theorem For delivered pump-flow changes Δq1,Δq2, \Delta q_1,\qquad \Delta q_2, G14=Δq1−Δq24,G23=−G14. \boxed{ G_{14} = \frac{\Delta q_1-\Delta q_2}{4}, \qquad G_{23}=-G_{14}. } The 14/2314/23 subchannel is independent of the unknown valve-split fractions. The integrated harness therefore contains no γ1,γ2\gamma_1,\gamma_2 scoring parameter. 2. Required future raw files Exactly three fresh physical data files are bound by the master freeze. A. fill_raw.csv Required columns: sample_index timestamp_s pump1_command pump2_command h1_cm h2_cm h3_cm h4_cm Optional only when directly source-authenticated: q1_delivered q2_delivered The pump-source stage reads only source columns. The tank comparator reads only the tank level columns plus the independently generated delivered-flow realization. B. hold_state0.csv Required: timestamp_s h1_cm h2_cm h3_cm h4_cm C. hold_state1.csv Same schema. These are the matched-level no-pump isolation holds for the two future fill states. 3. Single master run manifest The master run manifest freezes before scoring: run ID; Lehigh configuration ID; fill state-0 indices; fill state-1 indices; hold-state indices; source-only canonical extraction identity; source/operator receipt; isolation operator/configuration receipts; all files used by the experiment. Exactly two non-overlapping fill windows are used. No window search or target-aware adjustment exists in this package. 4. Pump-flow source stage The embedded source scorer is the already frozen Lehigh v0.1A implementation. It accepts only source-authored: DIRECT_FLOW_CHANNELS AFFINE_COMMAND POLYNOMIAL_COMMAND PIECEWISE_LINEAR_TABLE and rejects unsupported hidden-state calibration. Its adjacent-row source stream remains unchanged: Δqi[n]=qi[n]−qi[n−1]. \Delta q_i[n]=q_i[n]-q_i[n-1]. The integrated tank comparator additionally constructs the two flow states by the arithmetic mean of the authenticated delivered qiq_i samples over the exact two fill windows. This state-mean aggregation is frozen here before any fresh Lehigh physical data arrive. 5. Tank geometry implementation The integrated v0.1 harness supports two source-authored geometry modes. CONSTANT_AREA For tank ii, Vi(h)=Aih. V_i(h)=A_i h. The source receipt supplies AiA_i and its volume-sample uncertainty adapter. PIECEWISE_LINEAR_VOLUME The source receipt supplies strictly increasing source knots (hi,j,Vi,j) (h_{i,j},V_{i,j}) in cm and cm3. Volume is linearly interpolated inside the source knots. Extrapolation is forbidden. Any other geometry form returns: SOURCE_BLOCKED_UNSUPPORTED_GEOMETRY_FORM No generic cylindrical or Johansson geometry is inserted. 6. Frozen storage-rate estimator For every fill or hold window: transform each measured tank level through the source-authored Vi(h)V_i(h); estimate volume rate by OLS with intercept: V̇i=∑n(tn−t‾)(Vi(hi,n)−V‾i)∑n(tn−t‾)2. \boxed{ \dot V_i = \frac{ \sum_n(t_n-\bar t)(V_i(h_{i,n})-\bar V_i) }{ \sum_n(t_n-\bar t)^2 }. } No smoothing, polynomial fitting, robust fitting, tank removal, or window movement is allowed. 7. Isolation qualification For each state r∈{0,1}r\in\{0,1\} and tank ii, the matched no-pump hold yields ℓ̂i,r. \hat\ell_{i,r}. The integrated v0.1 metrology route is deliberately conservative: HARD_BOUND_ONLY No covariance/coverage-factor route is available in v0.1. The source metrology manifest supplies: BVi B_{V_i} as an absolute per-sample volume error bound and, if timing is material, Bt. B_t. The OLS hard slope bound is Bℓi,r≤∑n|wn|BVi+Bℓi,rtiming. B_{\ell_{i,r}} \le \sum_n|w_n|B_{V_i} + B_{\ell_{i,r}}^{\mathrm timing}. Isolation passes only if all eight tank/state conditions satisfy |ℓ̂i,r|≤Bℓi,r. |\hat\ell_{i,r}|\le B_{\ell_{i,r}}. Any detectable drift returns: ISOLATION_QUALIFICATION_FAIL LEHIGH_COMPARATOR_NOT_SCORED No leak subtraction is performed. 8. Matched-level gate For each tank and state, compare the fill-window and hold-window mean levels. The source metrology manifest supplies a frozen absolute match bound Bhimatch. B_{h_i}^{\mathrm match}. Pass requires |h‾i,rfill−h‾i,rhold|≤Bhimatch. \boxed{ |\bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm fill}-\bar h_{i,r}^{\mathrm hold}| \le B_{h_i}^{\mathrm match}. } Failure returns: MATCHED_LEVEL_QUALIFICATION_FAIL LEHIGH_COMPARATOR_NOT_SCORED 9. Undetected leak allowance A passed hold does not set leakage to zero. For each tank/state, Li,r=|ℓ̂i,r|+Bℓi,r. \boxed{ L_{i,r} = |\hat\ell_{i,r}|+B_{\ell_{i,r}}. } The conservative contamination bound is BR14leak=14∑i=14∑r=01Li,r. \boxed{ B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm leak} = \frac14 \sum_{i=1}^{4} \sum_{r=0}^{1} L_{i,r}. } No cancellation is assumed. 10. Independent tank-side comparator For fill state rr, q1,rtank=V̇1,r+V̇4,r, q_{1,r}^{\mathrm tank} = \dot V_{1,r}+\dot V_{4,r}, q2,rtank=V̇2,r+V̇3,r. q_{2,r}^{\mathrm tank} = \dot V_{2,r}+\dot V_{3,r}. The tank target is G14,tank=(q1,1tank−q1,0tank)−(q2,1tank−q2,0tank)4. G_{14,\mathrm tank} = \frac{ (q_{1,1}^{\mathrm tank}-q_{1,0}^{\mathrm tank}) - (q_{2,1}^{\mathrm tank}-q_{2,0}^{\mathrm tank}) }{4}. The independently authenticated flow prediction is G14,flow=(q1,1flow−q1,0flow)−(q2,1flow−q2,0flow)4. G_{14,\mathrm flow} = \frac{ (q_{1,1}^{\mathrm flow}-q_{1,0}^{\mathrm flow}) - (q_{2,1}^{\mathrm flow}-q_{2,0}^{\mathrm flow}) }{4}. Primary residual: R14(Lehigh)=G14,tank−G14,flow. \boxed{ R_{14}^{(\mathrm Lehigh)} = G_{14,\mathrm tank}-G_{14,\mathrm flow}. } 11. Main hard-bound metrology The source metrology manifest supplies: BViB_{V_i}: per-sample tank-volume hard bounds after geometry/level propagation; Bf1,Bf2B_{f_1},B_{f_2}: delivered-flow sample hard bounds; timing hard bound or source receipt that timing is negligible; matched-level hard bounds. For each fill-window volume slope, BV̇i,r B_{\dot V_{i,r}} is propagated with the same frozen OLS hard-bound law. Then BΔV̇i=BV̇i,0+BV̇i,1. B_{\Delta\dot V_i} = B_{\dot V_{i,0}}+B_{\dot V_{i,1}}. The conservative pump-flow state-mean hard bound remains BfiB_{f_i}; averaging does not reduce a source hard maximum error without a stochastic model. Therefore BΔqiflow=2Bfi. B_{\Delta q_i}^{\mathrm flow}=2B_{f_i}. The pre-leak comparator band is BR14meas=14[∑i=14BΔV̇i+2Bf1+2Bf2]. \boxed{ B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm meas} = \frac14 \left[ \sum_{i=1}^{4}B_{\Delta\dot V_i} + 2B_{f_1} + 2B_{f_2} \right]. } Final threshold: BR14total=BR14meas+BR14leak. \boxed{ B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm total} = B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm meas} + B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm leak}. } PASS iff |R14(Lehigh)|≤BR14total. \boxed{ |R_{14}^{(\mathrm Lehigh)}| \le B_{R_{14}}^{\mathrm total}. } 12. Master freeze freeze_all.py runs before scoring. The frozen QPB1 candidate η𝒜=2\eta_{\mathcal A}=2 is therefore equivalent, on this engineered oscillator, to the hardware impedance condition Z⊥=πRQ. Z_\perp=\pi R_Q. Because Z⊥Z_\perp is designable, a custom device built after target exposure cannot independently validate QPB1 merely by landing near this impedance. Blind analysis cannot remove target information already available during device design. The current project-designed device is therefore restricted to quantitative correspondence testing. Independent QPB1 scoring requires either hardware/data predating target exposure or a target-isolated external selection protocol that does not use the QPB1 relation and reports the entire selection frame or a preregistered random sample. The scoring packet measures all three transverse modes, preserves common capacitance covariance, verifies static/dynamic frequency consistency and mode degeneracy, requires at most ten-percent relative one-sigma uncertainty on the combined action ratio, freezes the combined score before target unblinding, and prohibits all post-result parameter tuning. Physical promotion remains zero.

The current audit corpus includes the classic 2010 JRM literature, the 2017 JPC/JRM experimental literature, the 2019/2020 Kerr-free JRM experiment, and independent four-junction CSFQ literature. 2. Selected primary Class-A source Chien et al. — Kerr-free Josephson Ring Modulator Publication: - T.-C. On a native Hodge JJ-plane, the locked dimensionless action 12adϕ̃\frac12a\,d\widetilde\phi is the canonical one-form 12(x1dx2−x2dx1)\frac12(x_1dx_2-x_2dx_1). Multiplication by the native action unit therefore makes the dimensional symplectic form ΩUD=𝒜0dx1∧dx2. \Omega_{\mathrm UD}=\mathcal A_0\,dx_1\wedge dx_2. For a frequency-matched physical oscillator, the dynamical intertwiner has form T=λRT=\lambda R. Pulling back the dimensional native symplectic form and demanding equality with the physical canonical form gives 𝒜0λ2=1. \mathcal A_0\lambda^2=1. Thus canonical symplectic preservation fixes the scale of TT only relative to the still-open native action unit. The simultaneous transformation (𝒜0,T)↦(c𝒜0,c−1/2T)(\mathcal A_0,T)\mapsto(c\mathcal A_0,c^{-1/2}T) leaves both dynamics and symplectic matching unchanged. This is an exact action-scale gauge. For an exactly degenerate mm-mode multiplet, dynamics plus symplectic preservation strengthens the result considerably. Consequently the symmetric engineered three-mode carrier no longer admits independent mode-by-mode normalization. Its only unresolved normalization is the single common 𝒜0\mathcal A_0. Setting a symplectic matrix to unit determinant by first dividing physical coordinates by an external action reference merely imports that reference. In particular, using ℏ\hbar to normalize this bridge would make the QPB1 test circular because QPB1 itself proposes 𝒜0=2ℏ\mathcal A_0=2\hbar. The remaining physical closure therefore requires one independent non-QPB1 action-dimensional normalization receipt. Physical promotion remains zero. Result Canonical symplectic preservation does not independently determine the remaining physical-to-Hodge scale. It determines only the product 𝒜0λ2=1 \boxed{ \mathcal A_0\lambda^2=1 } for the one-mode dynamical intertwiner T=λR, T=\lambda R, where RR is an orientation-compatible phase rotation. Therefore: dynamics + canonical symplectic preservation⇏absolute 𝒜0. \boxed{ \text{dynamics + canonical symplectic preservation} \;\not\Rightarrow\; \text{absolute }\mathcal A_0. } Instead they leave the exact gauge (𝒜0,T)↦(c𝒜0,c−1/2T),c>0. \boxed{ (\mathcal A_0,T) \mapsto (c\mathcal A_0,c^{-1/2}T), \qquad c>0. } The physical action unit is therefore the unavoidable remaining scale. 2. Native Hodge symplectic form from the locked action theorem On one active Hodge JJ-plane, let x=(x1x2),a=x12+x22. x= \begin{pmatrix} x_1\\ x_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad a=x_1^2+x_2^2. The locked native lifted action is ℐHodge=12aΔϕ̃. \mathcal I_{\mathrm Hodge} = \frac12a\,\Delta\widetilde\phi. In polar coordinates x1=rcosϕ̃,x2=rsinϕ̃,a=r2. x_1=r\cos\widetilde\phi, \qquad x_2=r\sin\widetilde\phi, \qquad a=r^2. Define the dimensionless Hodge one-form ϑH=12(x1dx2−x2dx1)=12adϕ̃. \boxed{ \vartheta_{\mathrm H} = \frac12 \left( x_1dx_2-x_2dx_1 \right) = \frac12a\,d\widetilde\phi. } Its integral along a constant-amplitude phase arc is exactly the locked Hodge action: ∫ϑH=12aΔϕ̃. \int\vartheta_{\mathrm H} = \frac12a\,\Delta\widetilde\phi. Therefore dϑH=dx1∧dx2. \boxed{ d\vartheta_{\mathrm H} = dx_1\wedge dx_2. } The dimensional native action is 𝒮native=𝒜0ℐHodge. \mathcal S_{\mathrm native} = \mathcal A_0\mathcal I_{\mathrm Hodge}. Hence the dimensional native canonical one-form is ΘUD=𝒜0ϑH \boxed{ \Theta_{\mathrm UD} = \mathcal A_0\vartheta_{\mathrm H} } and the dimensional native symplectic two-form is ΩUD=dΘUD=𝒜0dx1∧dx2. \boxed{ \Omega_{\mathrm UD} = d\Theta_{\mathrm UD} = \mathcal A_0\,dx_1\wedge dx_2. } In matrix notation, ΩUD↔𝒜0J0,J0=(01−10). \boxed{ \Omega_{\mathrm UD} \leftrightarrow \mathcal A_0J_0, \qquad J_0= \begin{pmatrix} 0&1\\ -1&0 \end{pmatrix}. } Thus 𝒜0\mathcal A_0 is not an optional later multiplier: it is the dimensional scale of the native symplectic form itself. 3. Physical oscillator symplectic form For a conservative physical oscillator, mq̈+kq=0,ω=k/m, m\ddot q+kq=0, \qquad \omega=\sqrt{k/m}, with canonical momentum p=mq̇, p=m\dot q, the physical symplectic form is Ωphys=dq∧dp. \boxed{ \Omega_{\mathrm phys} = dq\wedge dp. } Define the balanced coordinates z1=mωq,z2=pmω. z_1=\sqrt{m\omega}\,q, \qquad z_2=\frac{p}{\sqrt{m\omega}}. Since the transformation determinant is exactly one, dz1∧dz2=dq∧dp. \boxed{ dz_1\wedge dz_2 = dq\wedge dp. } Therefore in balanced coordinates Ωphys↔J0. \Omega_{\mathrm phys} \leftrightarrow J_0. The balanced coordinates each carry square-root-action units; their product carries action units. The physical generator is ż=ωJ0z. \dot z = \omega J_0z. 4. Dynamical intertwiner recap The parent theorem gives an invertible dynamical intertwiner only when ω=2τ0. \boxed{ \omega=\frac2{\tau_0}. } On the orientation-preserving branch the complete family is T=aI+bJ0. \boxed{ T = aI+bJ_0. } Define λ2=a2+b2. \lambda^2=a^2+b^2. Then T𝖳T=λ2I. \boxed{ T^\mathsf TT = \lambda^2I. } Equivalently, T=λR, T=\lambda R, where R∈SO(2) R\in SO(2) is a phase rotation. 5. Symplectic normalization theorem The physical-to-native map is x=Tz. x=Tz. Canonical symplectic preservation requires T*ΩUD=Ωphys. \boxed{ T^\ast\Omega_{\mathrm UD} = \Omega_{\mathrm phys}. } In matrix form, T𝖳(𝒜0J0)T=J0. \boxed{ T^\mathsf T (\mathcal A_0J_0) T = J_0. } For T=aI+bJ0, T=aI+bJ_0, one has exactly T𝖳J0T=(a2+b2)J0=λ2J0. T^\mathsf TJ_0T = (a^2+b^2)J_0 = \lambda^2J_0. Hence 𝒜0λ2J0=J0. \mathcal A_0\lambda^2J_0 = J_0. Therefore: 𝒜0λ2=1. \boxed{ \mathcal A_0\lambda^2=1. } Symplectic Normalization Theorem For a frequency-matched physical oscillator and one native Hodge JJ-plane, a dynamical intertwiner is canonically symplectic if and only if λ=𝒜0−1/2. \boxed{ \lambda = \mathcal A_0^{-1/2}. } Thus symplecticity fixes the map scale conditional on 𝒜0\mathcal A_0. It does not determine 𝒜0\mathcal A_0 itself. 6. Exact action-variable equality The physical oscillator action is Iphys=Eω=12(z12+z22). I_{\mathrm phys} = \frac{E}{\omega} = \frac12 (z_1^2+z_2^2). Under x=Tz, x=Tz, the native active amplitude is aUD=x𝖳x=λ2(z12+z22)=2λ2Iphys. a_{\mathrm UD} = x^\mathsf Tx = \lambda^2 (z_1^2+z_2^2) = 2\lambda^2I_{\mathrm phys}. The dimensional native action variable is IUD=𝒜02aUD. I_{\mathrm UD} = \frac{\mathcal A_0}{2} a_{\mathrm UD}. Therefore IUD=𝒜0λ2Iphys. I_{\mathrm UD} = \mathcal A_0\lambda^2I_{\mathrm phys}. With canonical symplectic preservation, 𝒜0λ2=1, \mathcal A_0\lambda^2=1, so IUD=Iphys. \boxed{ I_{\mathrm UD} = I_{\mathrm phys}. } Thus action equality is not an additional numerical coincidence. It follows exactly once the symplectic condition is satisfied. 7. Action-scale gauge theorem The pair (𝒜0,T) (\mathcal A_0,T) enters the canonical bridge only through 𝒜0T𝖳J0T. \mathcal A_0T^\mathsf TJ_0T. For any c>0, c>0, define 𝒜0′=c𝒜0, \mathcal A_0' = c\mathcal A_0, T′=c−1/2T. T' = c^{-1/2}T. Then 𝒜0′T′𝖳J0T′=𝒜0T𝖳J0T. \mathcal A_0' T'^\mathsf TJ_0T' = \mathcal A_0 T^\mathsf TJ_0T. The dynamical intertwining relation is also unchanged because it is homogeneous in TT. Therefore: (𝒜0,T)∼(c𝒜0,c−1/2T) \boxed{ (\mathcal A_0,T) \sim (c\mathcal A_0,c^{-1/2}T) } is an exact one-parameter bridge gauge. Therefore one independent action-dimensional normalization receipt remains necessary. 8. Why setting λ=1\lambda=1 is not a derivation Suppose one declares normalized dimensionless physical balanced coordinates ẑ=z𝒜ref \widehat z = \frac{z}{\sqrt{\mathcal A_{\mathrm ref}}} using an external action reference 𝒜ref. \mathcal A_{\mathrm ref}. Then Ωphys=𝒜refdẑ1∧dẑ2. \Omega_{\mathrm phys} = \mathcal A_{\mathrm ref} \,d\widehat z_1\wedge d\widehat z_2. If the dimensionless map x=T̂ẑ x=\widehat T\widehat z is chosen with detT̂=1, \det\widehat T=1, canonical symplectic preservation gives 𝒜0=𝒜ref. \boxed{ \mathcal A_0 = \mathcal A_{\mathrm ref}. } Hence a unit-normalized symplectic matrix does not derive 𝒜0\mathcal A_0. It imports an external action normalization through 𝒜ref\mathcal A_{\mathrm ref}. This is the normalization firewall. 9. QPB1 firewall The frozen QPB1 candidate proposes ℏ↔𝒜02, \hbar \longleftrightarrow \frac{\mathcal A_0}{2}, equivalently 𝒜0=2ℏ. \mathcal A_0=2\hbar. Using physical quantum symplectic normalization to set 𝒜ref=2ℏ \mathcal A_{\mathrm ref}=2\hbar would therefore reproduce QPB1 by assumption. It is not an independent test. Thus: ℏ-based symplectic normalization is forbidden as the independent 𝒜0 anchor for QPB1. \boxed{ \hbar\text{-based symplectic normalization is forbidden as the independent }\mathcal A_0\text{ anchor for QPB1}. } The independent action receipt must be non-QPB1 and non-ℏ\hbar-targeted. 10. UJ_m=J_mU. Therefore U∈Sp(2m,ℝ)∩GL(m,ℂ)=U(m). \boxed{ U\in Sp(2m,\mathbb R) \cap GL(m,\mathbb C) = U(m). } Hence T=𝒜0−1/2U,U∈U(m). \boxed{ T = \mathcal A_0^{-1/2}U, \qquad U\in U(m). } Consequently, T𝖳T=1𝒜0I2m. \boxed{ T^\mathsf TT = \frac1{\mathcal A_0}I_{2m}. } Important repair The parent dynamical theorem left a positive Hermitian metric freedom inside an exactly degenerate multiplet. Canonical symplectic preservation removes that freedom completely except for: a unitary basis rotation UU, which leaves the metric invariant; the single common action scale 𝒜0\mathcal A_0. A conservative physical oscillator can be written in balanced phase-space coordinates with generator ωJ0\omega J_0. The filled-K4K_4 active Hodge carrier has complex structure JJ and physical-time phase rate 2/τ02/	au_0. A linear invertible physical-to-Hodge map must therefore satisfy (2/τ0)JT=TωJ0. (2/	au_0)JT=T\omega J_0. Similarity of the generators proves that such a map exists on one oscillator plane if and only if ω=2/τ0\omega=2/	au_0. When this condition is met, the one-plane intertwiner is complex-linear up to orientation and its pullback metric has isotropic shape, TTT=λ2IT^TT=\lambda^2I. Dynamics therefore fixes the conformal metric shape but cannot fix the absolute normalization because the intertwining equation is homogeneous in TT. For a multimode physical system, every injectively mapped mode must share the same native frequency. The current filled-K4K_4 Hodge active sector has real dimension 14=2⋅714=2\cdot7 and a common active phase frequency. Consequently a physical carrier with unequal mode frequencies cannot map as a whole into this native carrier. This strengthens the prior Chien-2020 result: the measured aa and bb JRM modes have unequal frequencies, so they cannot both dynamically intertwine with one native Hodge clock regardless of amplitude metric choice. The earlier metric-conditional no-go therefore has a stronger metric-independent spectral obstruction. The symmetric engineered four-junction A-mode avoids the spectral obstruction at model level because its three transverse modes are degenerate, but dynamics alone still leaves complex-linear mixing freedom inside that degenerate multiplet. Historical statements that must be reconciled The historical source states all three of the following: the genesis rate is Γi=|ȧi|Δa; \Gamma_i=\frac{|\dot a_i|}{\Delta a}; the integral ∫Γidt \int\Gamma_i\,dt is described as the total number of distinction events; the construction is described as an absolute-value action of a Poisson process, followed by a smooth slow-genesis/diffusion limit. These statements are not all simultaneously exact under one ordinary smooth-variable interpretation. 2. Poisson counting distinction For a genuine Poisson counting process, let Ni(t)∈ℕ0 N_i(t)\in\mathbb N_0 be the realized event count. Its increments are discrete: dNi∈{0,1,2,…}. dN_i\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}. Let λi(t)≥0 \lambda_i(t)\ge0 be the predictable event intensity. Then 𝔼[dNi(t)∣ℱt−]=λi(t)dt. \boxed{ \mathbb E[dN_i(t)\mid\mathcal F_{t^-}] = \lambda_i(t)\,dt. } The cumulative intensity is Λi(T)=∫0Tλi(t)dt. \boxed{ \Lambda_i(T) = \int_0^T\lambda_i(t)\,dt. } For an inhomogeneous Poisson process, 𝔼[Ni(T)]=Λi(T). \boxed{ \mathbb E[N_i(T)] = \Lambda_i(T). } In general, Λi(T)∉ℕ0. \Lambda_i(T) \notin \mathbb N_0. Thus a smooth rate integral is naturally an expected count / compensator, not the realized integer event count. 3. Exact-count branch The historical wording can remain literally exact only if Γidt \Gamma_i\,dt is interpreted as the counting measure itself: dNi \boxed{ dN_i } rather than a smooth ordinary function times dtdt. Then Ni(T)=∫0TdNi \boxed{ N_i(T) = \int_0^T dN_i } is exactly integer. But in that interpretation the amplitude ai(t)a_i(t) is fundamentally a jump/staircase process at event resolution, and ȧi \dot a_i is distributional rather than an ordinary smooth derivative. The later slow-genesis smooth action is then a coarse-grained limit, not the same microscopic path object. 4. Smooth Poisson-intensity branch To preserve the historical slow-genesis language as an ordinary smooth trajectory, define Γi(t)=λi(t) \boxed{ \Gamma_i(t) = \lambda_i(t) } as the Poisson intensity. Then the historical continuum object becomes Λgen(T)=∫0T∑iΓi(t)dt \boxed{ \Lambda_{\mathrm gen}(T) = \int_0^T\sum_i\Gamma_i(t)\,dt } with Λgen=𝔼[Ngenreal] \boxed{ \Lambda_{\mathrm gen} = \mathbb E[N_{\mathrm gen}^{\mathrm real}] } under the Poisson model. The corresponding continuum action is Sgenesismean=ℏdΛgen. \boxed{ S_{\mathrm genesis}^{\mathrm mean} = \hbar_d\Lambda_{\mathrm gen}. } The realized microscopic action is instead Sgenesisreal=ℏdNgenreal. \boxed{ S_{\mathrm genesis}^{\mathrm real} = \hbar_d N_{\mathrm gen}^{\mathrm real}. } Therefore 𝔼[Sgenesisreal]=Sgenesismean. \boxed{ \mathbb E[S_{\mathrm genesis}^{\mathrm real}] = S_{\mathrm genesis}^{\mathrm mean}. } 5. Literal-triple no-go The following three claims cannot all hold exactly for the same ordinary smooth object: ai(t)a_i(t) is smooth; Γi=|ȧi|/Δa\Gamma_i=|\dot a_i|/\Delta a is an ordinary Poisson intensity; ∫Γidt\int\Gamma_i dt is always the realized integer event count. Thus: smooth amplitude+Poisson intensity+exact integer integral \boxed{ \text{smooth amplitude} + \text{Poisson intensity} + \text{exact integer integral} } is a typed incompatibility. Classification: AUTO_LOCK_LITERAL_TRIPLE_INCONSISTENCY. 6. Canonical source repair The least destructive append-only repair is: Microscopic layer Ngenreal=∑i∫dNi∈ℕ0. \boxed{ N_{\mathrm gen}^{\mathrm real} = \sum_i\int dN_i \in\mathbb N_0. } Mesoscopic/continuum layer Λgen=∫∑iΓidt=𝔼[Ngenreal] \boxed{ \Lambda_{\mathrm gen} = \int\sum_i\Gamma_i\,dt = \mathbb E[N_{\mathrm gen}^{\mathrm real}] } when Γi\Gamma_i is the Poisson intensity. Action Sreal=ℏdNgenreal, \boxed{ S_{\mathrm real} = \hbar_dN_{\mathrm gen}^{\mathrm real}, } Scont=ℏdΛgen=𝔼[Sreal]. \boxed{ S_{\mathrm cont} = \hbar_d\Lambda_{\mathrm gen} = \mathbb E[S_{\mathrm real}]. } Slow-genesis quadratic action The diffusion/quadratic expression is typed as an effective continuum action associated with the coarse/mean process, not an exact pathwise integer-event ledger. This preserves: the historical Poisson language; the slow-genesis continuum limit; the action quantum ℏd\hbar_d; exact microscopic integer counting. 7. Impact on the prior integrality obstruction The earlier integrality obstruction remains valid for a claim that the smooth Hodge variation itself equals an exact integer event history. However, under the repaired Poisson branch, the Hodge-induced continuous functional may lawfully correspond to the cumulative intensity Λgen \Lambda_{\mathrm gen} rather than to the realized integer count. Therefore: GH-3 is closed for the EXPECTED/INTENSITY branch \boxed{ \text{GH-3 is closed for the EXPECTED/INTENSITY branch} } but remains open for a pathwise exact event ledger. This is a scope split, not a deletion. 8. GH-1 + Poisson-repair combined formula Using the source-typed GH-1 node map, ΛgenHodge=1ΔaG∫0π∥q̇(s)∥1ds. \boxed{ \Lambda_{\mathrm gen}^{\mathrm Hodge} = \frac1{\Delta a_{\mathrm G}} \int_0^\pi \|\dot q(s)\|_1\,ds. } On the exact vertex-gradient Hodge subcarrier, ΛgenHodge=4ΔaG∑i=14q0,i2+14q̇0,i2. \boxed{ \Lambda_{\mathrm gen}^{\mathrm Hodge} = \frac4{\Delta a_{\mathrm G}} \sum_{i=1}^4 \sqrt{ q_{0,i}^2 + \frac14\dot q_{0,i}^2 }. } This quantity is allowed to be noninteger because it is now typed as cumulative expected count. The remaining scale gate is ΔaG\Delta a_{\mathrm G}. 9. In the homogeneous triangular lattice this collapses to six scalar inputs: current and previous means, current same-site and nearest-neighbor covariances, and current/previous same-site and nearest-neighbor cross covariances. The functional itself performs strongly. On eight fresh candidate-model seeds, after the formula was frozen, the mean relative discrepancy from the exact historical triangle-ratio calculation is about 0.18%, with worst selected discrepancy about 1.04%. Yet a fully autonomous Gaussian-Hartree moment evolution drifts badly at late time. Supplying the actual nonlinear first and second moments restores the Φ\Phi prediction. The surviving dynamics gap is therefore not the triadic ratio functional but the low-order autonomous moment hierarchy under quartic evolution. A temporal cluster-admission law was then derived from the source-driven covariance. The final-epoch same-site temporal covariance reaches e−1e^{-1} after 35 source steps, corresponding to 7/47/4 source time units, and crosses zero at 38 steps. Strict local peaks were tracked one-to-one between consecutive source states within the previously derived correlation radius r+=2r_+=2. A peak is admitted temporally only if its lifetime exceeds one e-fold coherence lag. This rule was frozen before eight new candidate-model seeds were executed. The e-fold lag remains exactly 35 steps across all eight seeds, demonstrating a stable temporal coherence scale, but the admitted final-object count is approximately 102 rather than 38. The combined result is another useful narrowing. Spatial covariance supplies a stable length scale and temporal covariance supplies a stable lifetime scale, but neither alone defines the historical cluster ontology. A future cluster law must operate on a joint spatiotemporal object—most plausibly including basin mass/energy, lifetime, and closure/admissibility—rather than on raw peaks alone. Physical promotion remains zero. Purpose This packet converts the frozen E2 state-qualification protocol into a laboratory-facing acquisition and custody workflow. It is designed for a superconducting-ring collaboration able to resolve metastable winding branches and adjacent phase-slip events. The scientific target is deliberately split into three independent questions: Carrier: did a genuine physical 2→32\to3 adjacent winding event occur? Burden: did an independently typed source channel return ε2\varepsilon_2? Leakage: did a separate provider return Λ2\Lambda_2? No model score is allowed to influence event admission or state labeling. 2. Experimental feasibility boundary Public experiments establish relevant capabilities but not UD identity. Ring winding/phase-slip analogue Petković et al., Nature Communications 7, 13551 (2016), DOI 10.1038/ncomms13551: isolated flux-biased superconducting rings access multiple metastable states; smooth persistent-current branches are labeled by winding number nn; jumps between branches are phase slips; in the reported operating regime the flux spacing was one superconducting flux quantum and nn changed by unity at each jump; the paper also notes that lower-temperature regimes can exhibit |Δn|>1|\Delta n|>1, making the explicit single-slip gate mandatory. Individual fluxoid-transition imaging analogue Polshyn, Naibert & Budakian, Physical Review B 97, 184501 (2018), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.97.184501: experimentally resolves individual fluxoid transitions in micron-scale superconducting rings. Phase-slip calorimetry analogue Gümüş et al., Nature Physics 19, 196–200 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41567-022-01844-0: time-resolved electron thermometry detects heat released by an individual phase slip in a Josephson junction. High-fidelity state-readout analogue Nambisan et al., Nature 653, 63–67 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10441-7: demonstrates coherent manipulation and quantum non-demolition readout of superconducting vortex states in granular aluminium. These are EXPERIMENTALLY_REALIZED_ANALOGUE receipts only. They do not establish a UD physical identity. 3. Required collaborator capabilities Minimum: isolated or otherwise individually state-resolved superconducting ring; controllable flux bias; metastable branches that include independently calibratable n=2n=2 and n=3n=3; readout capable of distinguishing those branches before and after the event; phase-slip detection with a calibrated voltage/phase or fluxoid-transition receipt; synchronized timestamps across state and phase channels. Preferred: single-event calorimetry; independent environment/leakage telemetry; common clock for all acquisition channels; blind event-control automation. A device that resolves only parity or an unlabeled two-state manifold is insufficient for E2. 4. The preferred evidence hierarchy is: direct/calibrated fluxoid or persistent-current branch readout; multi-branch fit/calibration with a predeclared physical model; repeated adjacent-flux-period indexing anchored to a frozen reference state. Jack Harris - Yale To: jack.harris@yale.edu Subject: Feasibility question: state-resolved n=2 -> 3 phase-slip experiment in an isolated ring Professor Harris, I am developing a target-blind superconducting phase-slip experiment whose first requirement is deliberately narrow: independently qualify consecutive winding states n=2 and n=3 in an isolated flux-biased ring, then admit only a verified single 2 -> 3 phase-slip event before any energetic or model analysis. Your group’s isolated-ring phase-slip work is the closest experimental carrier match I have found, and Yale’s current materials still list persistent-current work and in-situ electron thermometry in your program. I attached a one-page proposal describing the state, phase, thermal, and custody requirements. The experiment is preregistered so that state labels and event admission are frozen before downstream comparisons. I am not asking for endorsement of a theory - only whether this measurement is technically clean and feasible with an existing or adapted ring platform. If it looks plausible, the next step would be a short apparatus-specific feasibility discussion before any data are acquired. Best regards, Benjamin Mayes Unified Dynamics 2. Clemens Winkelmann - Grenoble To: clemens.winkelmann@grenoble-inp.fr CC candidate: herve.courtois@neel.cnrs.fr Subject: Feasibility question: single-event calorimetry for a state-resolved superconducting-ring phase slip Professor Winkelmann, I am assembling a target-blind experiment that combines two independently qualified capabilities: an isolated superconducting ring with explicit n=2 and n=3 winding-state readout, and a synchronized single-event thermal receipt for an admitted 2 -> 3 phase slip. Your phase-slip calorimetry work and the current Grenoble superconducting-nanoelectronics program are directly relevant to the thermal side of the experiment. The protocol intentionally keeps winding-state labeling, phase-slip admission, calorimetry, and model scoring separate. I attached a one-page experimental proposal. My immediate question is technical: could the RF electron-thermometry / nanocalorimetry approach be adapted to a ring-state platform, either through a hybrid device or a collaboration with a group providing the winding-state carrier? No theoretical endorsement is being requested; the objective is a clean falsifiable measurement with frozen raw-data custody. Best regards, Benjamin Mayes Unified Dynamics 3. Jukka Pekola - Aalto PICO To: jukka.pekola@aalto.fi Subject: Feasibility question: electronic thermometry for a blinded n=2 -> 3 phase-slip experiment Professor Pekola, I am developing a blinded superconducting phase-slip experiment in which an isolated ring is first qualified in consecutive winding states n=2 and n=3, followed by an admitted single 2 -> 3 phase-slip event. PICO’s work in electronic thermometry, superconducting/hybrid nanostructures, Josephson devices, and its contribution to single-phase-slip calorimetry makes your group highly relevant to the thermal, cryogenic, and uncertainty side of the experiment. I attached a one-page proposal. The protocol requires winding labels to come from an independent state readout; calorimetry is measured separately and cannot be used to select or relabel the event. I would value a technical assessment of whether PICO’s present thermometry methods could be integrated with a state-resolved superconducting-ring platform, either directly or through a collaboration. Best regards, Benjamin Mayes Unified Dynamics First-contact rule Send only the one-page proposal initially. The technical gate sheet and full custody packet are held for follow-up unless requested. A partner with a NO or unresolved CONDITIONAL field is not silently composed with another partner. UD_E2_YALE_GRENOBLE_AALTO_CONSORTIUM_RESPONSIBILITY_AND_HANDOFF_PROTOCOL_v0.1.mdUD E2 Yale–Grenoble–Aalto Consortium Responsibility and Handoff Protocol v0.1 Date: 2026-09-14 Status: FROZEN PROTOCOL TEMPLATE / NO EXECUTION OWNERS ASSIGNED YET Physical promotion: 0 1. Purpose Permit complementary carrier and calorimetry capabilities to compose without silently merging: different physical events; different clock domains; incompatible calibrations; post hoc state labels; burden and leakage providers; unfrozen raw data. The protocol inherits the immutable E2 scientific core unchanged. 2. Hard architecture rule One scored E2 event must terminate in one integrated acquisition host. Allowed: SINGLE_HOST_INTEGRATED; TRANSFERRED_METHOD_INTEGRATED_HOST. Forbidden: DISTRIBUTED_INDEPENDENT_EVENT_STITCHING. AUTO_LOCK / NO-GO E2_STATE_PHASE_AND_THERMAL_CHANNELS_FROM_DIFFERENT_PHYSICAL_EVENTS_CANNOT_BE_STITCHED_INTO_ONE_E2_EVENT_v0.1 A state transition from one apparatus and a heat pulse from a different event are two correspondence records, not one E2 event. 3. Method ownership versus event ownership A partner may own a method without owning the scored event acquisition. Examples: Grenoble/Aalto may own thermometer design or thermal calibration while the thermometer is integrated into a Yale-hosted event apparatus. A carrier/state method may be transferred to a Grenoble/Aalto-hosted integrated apparatus. For one scored event, the same integrated host must own raw acquisition of: state/winding; phase/flux-slip; thermal event; master clock; raw origin custody. No host is preselected by this template. 4. Candidate method roles — nonbinding Yale: carrier/state/phase method candidate. Grenoble: single-event calorimetry, thermal calibration, nanofabrication candidate. Aalto: RF electron thermometry, thermal calibration/integration candidate. UD: preregistration, SHA-256 custody, provider firewall, joint-merge governance. These are not execution assignments. 5. Calibration authorities Name exactly one primary owner for: state-label calibration; phase/flux calibration; thermal response/covariance calibration; timing-delay calibration. The thermal channel may never define the state-label map. 6. Common event identity and clock All scientific event channels must use one frozen event-ID namespace and one common acquisition epoch. The common-event relation is provenance, not nearest-timestamp matching. No post hoc nearest-event matching is permitted. 7. Required handoffs H01_STATE_LABEL_MAP H02_PHASE_RECEIPT_CALIBRATION H03_THERMAL_RESPONSE_CALIBRATION H04_COMMON_CLOCK_AND_DELAY_MAP H05_RAW_STATE_PHASE_EVENT_DATA H06_RAW_THERMAL_EVENT_DATA H07_BURDEN_PROVIDER_RETURN H08_LEAKAGE_PROVIDER_RETURN H09_JOINT_MERGE_MANIFEST Every handoff carries: producer; consumer; SHA-256 artifact hash; parent manifest hash; freeze timestamp; event-ID namespace; PASS/REJECT status. H09 may be created only after H01–H08 pass and are frozen. 8. Provider firewall Burden and leakage must have different provider IDs, separate request files, separate executable hashes, and forbidden cross-channel inputs. They may be hosted by one institution only if the provider identities and information flows remain separately frozen. 9. Consortium composition rule Complementary partner replies do not auto-compose. Before execution, freeze: one integrated host; method-transfer responsibilities; calibration ownership; synchronized acquisition design; raw custody; provider firewall; H01–H09. Only then may the consortium become: CONSORTIUM_MAP_EXECUTION_READY. 10. No-go conditions Return CONSORTIUM_MAP_NOT_EXECUTION_READY for: cross-lab event stitching; no common event namespace; no common epoch; state/phase/thermal raw acquisition split across hosts; missing primary role; burden/leakage provider collision; unhashed or rejected handoff; event-namespace mismatch. Any immutable-core change returns: NEW_VERSION_REQUIRED_BEFORE_DATA_EXPOSURE. 11. Type firewall Calorimetry remains distinct from: winding-state labels; native UD burden identity; leakage; physical carrier identity. Physical promotion remains 0. Problem The previous localized-event audit found that, for a fixed nonzero anchor receipt a⋆a_\star, minimizing the matching-defect support alone gives six exact minimizers: 6=2⋅3. 6=2\cdot3. Exactly one minimizer has one active facet; five activate all five facets. This appeared to require an additional principle: minimize the number of active facets. The current source package allows a sharper result. 2. Two held scope statements A. Delta4-to-K4 operational reduction The normalized reduction is a five-member equivariant family {RF}F∈∂Δ4. \{R_F\}_{F\in\partial\Delta^4}. Bare S5S_5 symmetry does not select one member. A unique operational reduction requires an independently derived facet-selection receipt. Therefore, once a selector passes and returns F⋆, F_\star, the active operational branch is RF⋆. \boxed{ R_{F_\star}. } The other four RFR_F remain alternative charts/branches, not simultaneous copies of the selected K4 packet. B. Directed-parity source domain The directed-parity source law is explicitly scoped to the three opposite-edge pairs of one tetrahedral packet. \boxed{ \text{the three opposite-edge pairs of one tetrahedral packet}. } Its one-pair locality is internal to that selected tetrahedral packet: |cΘ|≤1,|oΘ|≤1. |c_\Theta|\le1, \qquad |o_\Theta|\le1. The source operator does not define a simultaneous five-facet event field. 3. Branch-domain typing theorem Assume: a lawful selector returns one unique facet F⋆; F_\star; the operational reduction is therefore RF⋆; R_{F_\star}; the directed-parity source operator is applied according to its declared one-tetrahedral-packet scope. Then the only type-correct location for its nonzero event receipt is the selected operational packet: ai=δi⋆a⋆. \boxed{ a_i = \delta_{i\star}a_\star. } For every i≠⋆, i\neq\star, FiF_i is not the selected operational K4 branch. Assigning an additional nonzero parity event aia_i there would require: a second operational facet selection; or a new multi-facet source law; or explicit defect/associated-bundle semantics. None is supplied by the current one-packet source operator. Therefore the five fully active defect-minimizing fields found previously are mathematical completions of the local coordinate field, but they are not in the domain of the selected-branch source law. AUTO_LOCK — CONDITIONAL ON UNIQUE FACET SELECTION UNIQUE_OPERATIONAL_FACET_OWNERSHIP_PLUS_ONE_PACKET_SOURCE_SCOPE_FORCES_SINGLE_FACET_EVENT_LOCALITY_THEOREM_v0.1 4. Minimum-active-facet rule is not an independent axiom Once assumptions 1–3 hold, Nactive=1 N_{\mathrm active}=1 is not selected by a new variational principle. It follows from domain typing: one selected K4 branch+one-packet source operator⇒one active event facet. \boxed{ \text{one selected K4 branch} + \text{one-packet source operator} \Rightarrow \text{one active event facet}. } Accordingly, the previous proposed rule MINIMUM_ACTIVE_FACET_LOCALITY is repaired as follows: AUTO_REPAIR retain its numerical consequence: ai=δi⋆a⋆; a_i=\delta_{i\star}a_\star; retire it as an independent primitive source axiom whenever a unique operational facet has already been lawfully selected; retain it only as a descriptive equivalent of selected-branch scope. 5. What one-pair locality does not prove by itself Without a unique operational facet receipt, the local one-pair condition |cΘ|≤1,|oΘ|≤1 |c_\Theta|\le1, \qquad |o_\Theta|\le1 places no restriction on how many of the five facet charts independently receive local events. Thus: one-pair locality alone⇏Nactive=1. \boxed{ \text{one-pair locality alone} \not\Rightarrow N_{\mathrm active}=1. } The branch selector is load-bearing. AUTO_LOCK / NO-GO ONE_PAIR_LOCALITY_ALONE_DOES_NOT_DERIVE_SINGLE_FACET_LOCALITY_THEOREM_v0.1 This prevents conflating: pair locality inside one tetrahedron; facet locality inside Delta4. 6. First-admissible trigger The held source law defines the event index as the first later update where the local source operator is nonzero. Once F⋆F_\star owns the operational K4 branch, the trigger is evaluated on that selected packet. The first-admissible trigger therefore determines when the selected local event occurs; it does not independently select additional facet copies. No global simultaneous-replication rule follows. 7. Exact downstream defect section The earlier defect theorem remains unchanged. For ai=δi⋆a⋆, a_i=\delta_{i\star}a_\star, the source-compatibility residual is supported on the four edges incident to F⋆F_\star: |suppS|=4=22. \boxed{ |\operatorname{supp}S|=4=2^2. } And ∑{i,j}|Sj←i|H=4|a⋆|H. \boxed{ \sum_{\{i,j\}}|S_{j\leftarrow i}|_H = 4|a_\star|_H. } The new result changes the authority for localization, not these exact counts. 8. Remaining anchor authority This theorem does not promote the current candidate anchor rules. A unique F⋆F_\star must still be supplied lawfully. Current options remain: exact C3-exclusive receipt used as a candidate selector; MRR used as a candidate selector; conservative consensus when both are unique and agree; a future independently derived primitive selector. If no unique facet passes, this theorem does not create one. 9. Ruling EXACT / AUTO_LOCK CONDITIONAL unique selected operational facet + one-packet source scope implies one active event facet; the localized field is ai=δi⋆a⋆a_i=\delta_{i\star}a_\star; the four-edge matching-defect star follows as previously proved. AUTO_REPAIR MINIMUM_ACTIVE_FACET_LOCALITY_SOURCE_ADDENDUM is no longer independently required after lawful unique facet selection. NO-GO one-pair locality by itself cannot choose one Delta4 facet; first-admissible timing by itself cannot choose one facet; the theorem cannot manufacture a unique anchor from a tie. OPEN primitive facet-selection authority; physical correspondence. Physical promotion remains 0.

The local carrier is the tetrahedral graph K4K_4 with automorphism group S4S_4, together with an opposite-edge binary fiber Θ≅𝔽23\Theta\cong\mathbb F_2^3. On the filled tetrahedron we use the oriented simplicial chain complex of dimensions 4,6,4,14,6,4,1 and a real skew Hodge–Dirac generator. The single-cell carrier satisfies the exact identity 𝒜2=−4(I−PH0), \mathcal A^2=-4(I-P_{H_0}), which yields one harmonic zero mode, fourteen nonzero directions at frequency magnitude 22, and exact conservation of the quadratic chain support. It has been adversarially reviewed only by its own author (two passes), which this session demonstrates is insufficient — two material and four minor errors survived construction and were caught only on hostile re-read. It is not CRL-2b until a non-constructor reviews it. 2. Anti-erosion rule (support depth) Define, for any claim X: depth(X) = 0 if X is exact-substrate or empirical depth(X) = 1 + max over dependencies D of depth(D) otherwise Rule E1 — status is capped by depth. A claim cited only by other conditional claims gets deeper, never firmer. Citation is not evidence. Status improves only by re-derivation against a lower-depth anchor, never by accumulating dependents. Rule E2 — dependency expiry. If X depends on assumption A and A is revised or demoted, X auto-demotes to “pending re-derivation” with no ruling required. Append-only. Rationale. This is the specific mechanism that prevents the failure seen in the abandoned exploratory thread, where a “structural choice” became “canonicalized” across a chain in which no single step was individually wrong. Each step raised apparent firmness by citation. E1 makes that impossible; E2 makes revision propagate. 3. Asymmetric promotion / demotion PROMOTION (any rung): requires non-constructor adversarial review, then custodian ruling. Slow by design. DEMOTION on falsify: automatic, immediate, no ruling. Append-only. The custodian is removed from the demotion path entirely. This is what makes a faster promotion path safe to offer: safety never waits on custodian availability. 4. DEVELOPMENT LANE analysis reaching no registry conclusion. Requires only a label: "development — no registry entry." Frozen frontiers do NOT apply. Analysis that promotes nothing (e.g. showing a frozen family fails to discriminate) belongs in the development lane and does not require frontier re-entry. Promotion from development to registry requires the §3 procedure. 5. Retractions and provenance as first-class objects Retraction registry. Every correction is a registry object with the same standing as a claim: what was wrong, what replaced it, found-by (construction / self-review / external). The session-level retraction ratio is published as a diagnostic. A framework with zero recorded retractions after substantial development is unaudited, not clean. Provenance field on every claim: origin, constructor, reviewer(s), dependency list, lane. This is the field that catches contamination — content entering the lineage from outside the substrate — at entry rather than downstream. 6. A predictive source requires pre-update source custody. For event ee, define a typed burden packet 𝒮eB=(e,𝒞ρ,Ae,δρesrc,κe,Πe,te−). \mathscr S_e^B = (e,\mathcal C_\rho,A_e,\delta\rho_e^{src},\kappa_e,\Pi_e,t_e^-). Q158 becomes verification After the update, ϵB=Δρobs−BjBpred−sBpred. \boxed{ \epsilon_B = \Delta\rho^{obs} - Bj_B^{pred} - s_B^{pred}. } A closed tested packet batch gives ϵB=0. \epsilon_B=0. A separate bridge into the burden carrier is required. 6. Perturbation-class consequence Realized Q153/Q158 source packets and realized O05 context packets are now RECEIPT-CONDITIONED EXECUTABLE. Observation Graphene and diamond should not be described as the same structure at different stacking depths. Graphene is a planar three-connected honeycomb network. Diamond is a three-dimensional four-connected tetrahedral network. The structural invariant worth testing is instead: shortest closed bond cycle length=6 \boxed{\text{shortest closed bond cycle length}=6} in both nets. Thus the promising object is a hexacycle, not necessarily a planar hexagon. In graphene the six-cycle is planar. In diamond the six-membered rings are puckered in the tetrahedral network. 2. Exact bipartite-cycle theorem Represent a bipartite nearest-neighbor net by bond vectors viv_i, with alternating steps +vi,−vj,+vk,−vl,…. +v_i,-v_j,+v_k,-v_l,\ldots . Both the honeycomb and diamond nets are bipartite, so odd cycles are excluded. A nontrivial four-cycle would require vi−vj+vk−vl=0, v_i-v_j+v_k-v_l=0, equivalently vi+vk=vj+vl. v_i+v_k=v_j+v_l. For the graphene three-direction bond set, all unordered two-vector sums are distinct. For the tetrahedral diamond bond set t0=(1,1,1),t1=(1,−1,−1),t2=(−1,1,−1),t3=(−1,−1,1), t_0=(1,1,1),\quad t_1=(1,-1,-1),\quad t_2=(-1,1,-1),\quad t_3=(-1,-1,1), the six unordered pair sums are (2,0,0),(0,2,0),(0,0,2),(0,0,−2),(0,−2,0),(−2,0,0), (2,0,0),\ (0,2,0),\ (0,0,2),\ (0,0,-2),\ (0,-2,0),\ (-2,0,0), all distinct. Therefore no nontrivial four-cycle exists. A six-cycle exists for any three distinct bond labels i,j,ki,j,k: vi−vj+vk−vi+vj−vk=0. v_i-v_j+v_k-v_i+v_j-v_k=0. Hence ghcb=gdia=6 \boxed{ g_{\mathrm hcb}=g_{\mathrm dia}=6 } where gg is graph girth. AUTO_LOCK HONEYCOMB_AND_DIAMOND_BIPARTITE_NO_SQUARE_NETS_HAVE_GIRTH_SIX_THEOREM_v0.1 within the declared canonical bond-vector models. 3. Dimensional lift The local coordination changes: zgraphene=3,zdiamond=4. z_{\mathrm graphene}=3, \qquad z_{\mathrm diamond}=4. But the minimal cycle length does not: 6→6. \boxed{6\to6}. The number of unordered local branch-pair sectors is Npair(z)=(z2). N_{\mathrm pair}(z)=\binom z2. Thus (32)=3,(42)=6. \binom32=3, \qquad \binom42=6. Interpretation: graphene: three local branch-pair sectors around a three-connected site; diamond: six local branch-pair sectors around a four-connected tetrahedral site. The dimensional transition therefore changes closure multiplicity 3→6 3\to6 while preserving the shortest closure word length 6. 6. 4. K4 relation For a tetrahedral four-branch frame, (42)=6=E(K4). \binom42=6=E(K_4). This equality is exact combinatorics: four local directions define six unordered direction pairs, just as four K4 vertices define six edges. However, diamond six-ring vertices≠K4 six edges \boxed{ \text{diamond six-ring vertices} \neq \text{K4 six edges} } as typed objects. The useful correspondence is instead: tetrahedral local frame→6branch-pair sectors→6-step minimal network closure. \boxed{ \text{tetrahedral local frame} \longrightarrow 6\ \text{branch-pair sectors} \longrightarrow 6\text{-step minimal network closure}. } Whether UD dynamics makes these two appearances of six causally related is OPEN. 5. Frozen-matter hypothesis CANDIDATE FROZEN_MATTER_HEXACYCLE_SHELL_CANDIDATE_v0.1 A stable 3D retained-matter network may use: a tetrahedral local coordination frame; bipartite / alternating transport; exclusion of triangular and square local return loops; a shortest nontrivial retained closure cycle of length six. In this interpretation the fundamental extended frozen-matter motif is not a planar six-vertex polygon but a puckered six-cycle wrapped through tetrahedral local frames. This reconciles: K4local volumetric closure K_4\ \text{local volumetric closure} with C6extended retained closure. C_6\ \text{extended retained closure}. 6. Why the candidate is interesting The carbon comparison supplies a real structural analogue: 2D honeycomb carbon: degree 3, six-rings; 3D diamond carbon: degree 4 tetrahedral, six-rings. So a dimension lift does not require replacing the six-cycle. It can preserve the cycle while changing local coordination and embedding. This is materially stronger than a bare numerical match. 7. Falsifiers / no-go boundaries The following would falsify a universal six-cycle frozen-matter law: a claimed UD frozen phase whose source-complete minimal retained cycle is not six; a derivation showing stable frozen retention with unavoidable shorter primitive cycles; a bridge in which ring length is representation-dependent rather than invariant. Existing materials with other ring sizes already show that C6C_6 cannot be promoted as a universal law of all ordinary solids from carbon alone. Therefore the present status is: EXACT: the graph-theoretic honeycomb/diamond girth-six result. DERIVED: z=3→4z=3\to4 gives branch-pair multiplicity 3→63\to6. CANDIDATE: six-cycle as an extended UD frozen-matter closure shell. NO-GO: “diamond is simply stacked graphene.” OPEN: derive C6C_6 from UD source/admissibility dynamics rather than from the carbon analogy. Physical promotion remains 0.

Classification: STRONG STRUCTURAL ANALOGUE / DIA NET / C6 Silicon and germanium Both elemental Si and Ge adopt the diamond-cubic structure at ordinary conditions. Therefore their bond-network topology inherits the diamond-net six-ring structure. Classification: STRONG STRUCTURAL ANALOGUE / DIA NET / C6 Zincblende / cubic SiC-type branch Zincblende is topologically the binary diamond net (dia-b). Both zincblende and wurtzite networks have shortest circuits of length six; cubic 3C-SiC is zincblende-type, while SiC polytypes retain tetrahedral bonding with different stacking sequences. Classification: STRONG STRUCTURAL ANALOGUE / TETRAHEDRAL BINARY NET / C6 Ice I branch Ordinary hexagonal ice is characterized by six-membered rings in the tetrahedral hydrogen-bond network; cubic ice is the corresponding diamond-like branch. Classification: STRUCTURAL ANALOGUE / TETRAHEDRAL H-BOND NET / C6-DOMINANT Alpha-quartz and beta-cristobalite Shortest-path topology analyses of crystalline silica report regular six-membered rings in both alpha-quartz and beta-cristobalite, arranged into different three-dimensional tetrahedral networks. Classification: STRUCTURAL ANALOGUE / CORNER-SHARING SiO4 / C6 3. Counterexamples Zeolite frameworks The International Zeolite Association defines zeolite frameworks as 3D networks of corner-sharing TO4TO_4 tetrahedra. Yet IZA vertex symbols explicitly contain 4-rings, 5-rings, 6-rings, 8-rings, 12-rings, and other combinations depending on framework topology. For example, the IZA explanatory material gives FAU with 4⋅4⋅4⋅6⋅6⋅12. 4\cdot4\cdot4\cdot6\cdot6\cdot12. Therefore tetrahedral coordination⇏g=6. \boxed{ \text{tetrahedral coordination} \not\Rightarrow g=6. } High-pressure ice Ice I is six-ring rich, but higher-pressure ice polymorphs change network topology and ring sizes. Ice V contains smaller and larger rings, and other phases contain mixed ring populations. Again: z≈4⇏C6-only topology. \boxed{ z\approx4 \not\Rightarrow C_6\text{-only topology}. } Vitreous silica Amorphous/vitreous silica retains local SiO4SiO_4 tetrahedral coordination while exhibiting a broad distribution of ring sizes, including four-, six-, and larger-membered rings. Thus local tetrahedral geometry survives while long-range ring topology changes. 4. What the audit selects The data discriminate two hypotheses. H0 — universal tetrahedral C6 tetrahedral local coordination⇒minimal extended cycle 6. \text{tetrahedral local coordination} \Rightarrow \text{minimal extended cycle }6. FALSIFIED. H1 — constrained tetrahedral C6 branch tetrahedral local coordination+additional network admissibility⇒C6. \text{tetrahedral local coordination} + \text{additional network admissibility} \Rightarrow C_6. SUPPORTED AS A CANDIDATE CLASS. The missing admissibility is plausibly related to some combination of: bipartite/alternating site type; exclusion of short square closures; low-strain tetrahedral angle compatibility; stacking/retention rules; absence of topology-changing high-pressure/interpenetrating channels. The materials audit does not decide which mechanism is fundamental. 5. UD consequence The strongest current UD formulation is therefore not frozen matter=C6. \text{frozen matter}=C_6. It is: diamond-like frozen branch=local K4/tetrahedral frame+derived retained-net constraints+girth 6. \boxed{ \text{diamond-like frozen branch} = \text{local K4/tetrahedral frame} + \text{derived retained-net constraints} + \text{girth }6. } This retains the graphene/diamond intuition while respecting the counterexamples. Scientific Reports / ACS crystal-structure tutorial — zincblende as diamond topology and six-membered zincblende/wurtzite rings. Purpose The aggregate OP03 / viable-lane event packet can contain Γ∈{0,1,2,3} \Gamma\in\{0,1,2,3\} simultaneous address changes. Treating every aggregate event as one primitive retained graph edge destroys the native Z2Z_2 alternation whenever Γ\Gamma is even. The source receipts already provide a canonical finer factorization. This artifact makes that factorization the retained-carrier primitive. 1. Primitive address atoms Let 𝒫={A,B,C}. \mathcal P=\{A,B,C\}. For event nn, define the active source-address set Pn={p∈𝒫:γn,p=An,p+Sn,p=1}. \boxed{ P_n = \{p\in\mathcal P:\gamma_{n,p}=A_{n,p}+S_{n,p}=1\}. } For each p∈Pn p\in P_n define the address-atomic lineage object αn,p=(n,p,ξn,p),ξn,p=Sn,p−An,p∈{−1,+1}. \boxed{ \alpha_{n,p} = (n,p,\xi_{n,p}), \qquad \xi_{n,p}=S_{n,p}-A_{n,p}\in\{-1,+1\}. } Each αn,p\alpha_{n,p} carries exactly one source address and exactly one unit lineage change. Aggregate event as a higher-order object Define the event bundle ℌn={αn,p:p∈Pn}. \boxed{ \mathfrak H_n = \{\alpha_{n,p}:p\in P_n\}. } Its rank is rankℌn=|Pn|=Γn. \boxed{ \operatorname{rank}\mathfrak H_n = |P_n| = \Gamma_n. } Classification: Γ=0:hold / no source-lineage event, \Gamma=0: \quad \text{hold / no source-lineage event}, Γ=1:atomic event, \Gamma=1: \quad \text{atomic event}, Γ=2:rank-2 simultaneous event bundle, \Gamma=2: \quad \text{rank-2 simultaneous event bundle}, Γ=3:rank-3 simultaneous event bundle. \Gamma=3: \quad \text{rank-3 simultaneous event bundle}. Carrier rule Only rank-1 source objects are eligible to instantiate one primitive retained graph edge. Rank-2 and rank-3 packets remain higher-order event objects. They may create, destroy, or coordinate multiple primitive relations, but are not collapsed into one graph edge. AUTO_LOCK — CARRIER DEFINITION MULTI_ADDRESS_EVENT_PACKET_IS_HIGHER_ORDER_RETAINED_EVENT_NOT_PRIMITIVE_GRAPH_EDGE_v0.1 This is a carrier choice / source amendment, not a newly discovered physical law. 3. Source-state Z2Z_2 is exact on atoms Define the viable-lane source parity qω(ω)=ωA⊕ωB⊕ωC. \boxed{ q_\omega(\omega) = \omega_A\oplus\omega_B\oplus\omega_C. } For one address atom, ω+=ω−⊕ep, \omega^+ = \omega^-\oplus e_p, hence qω(ω+)=qω(ω−)⊕1. \boxed{ q_\omega(\omega^+) = q_\omega(\omega^-)\oplus1. } Therefore every address-atomic source edge flips qωq_\omega. AUTO_LOCK ADDRESS_ATOMIC_VIABLE_LANE_TRANSITION_HAS_EXACT_SOURCE_Z2_COLOR_FLIP_v0.1 This result does not require POC-1. 4. Relation to the Θ\Theta quotient The separately derived Θ\Theta quotient is qΘ(θ)=θA⊕θB⊕θC. q_\Theta(\theta) = \theta_A\oplus\theta_B\oplus\theta_C. If the POC-1 saturation relation holds, θ=𝟏−ω, \theta = \mathbf1-\omega, then over 𝔽2\mathbb F_2, θ=𝟏⊕ω. \theta = \mathbf1\oplus\omega. Since there are three coordinates, qΘ(θ)=1⊕qω(ω). \boxed{ q_\Theta(\theta) = 1\oplus q_\omega(\omega). } Thus the two colorings differ by a global color swap and have identical edge alternation. This is: EXACT_CONDITIONAL_ON_POC1 and does not promote POC-1 itself. 5. Material retained graph requires an endpoint map A source-lineage atom is not yet a spatial or material bond. Introduce an independently sourced endpoint map β:αn,p↦{u,v} \boxed{ \beta: \alpha_{n,p} \longmapsto \{u,v\} } where u,vu,v are retained material sites / packet-center sites / whatever retained-site carrier is ultimately admitted. Then define ER(1)={β(α):αis retained and source-authenticated}. E_R^{(1)} = \{\beta(\alpha):\alpha\ \text{is retained and source-authenticated}\}. The primitive retained graph is ΓR(1)=(VR,ER(1)). \boxed{ \Gamma_R^{(1)} = (V_R,E_R^{(1)}). } Without β\beta, no material ring length may be inferred from source-address atoms. AUTO_LOCK TYPE GUARD SOURCE_ADDRESS_ATOM_DOES_NOT_EQUAL_MATERIAL_BOND_WITHOUT_ENDPOINT_MAP_v0.1 6. Hypergraph / event-bundle sidecar Preserve simultaneity by attaching an event hypergraph sidecar ℋR={ℌn}. \boxed{ \mathcal H_R = \{\mathfrak H_n\}. } The graph ΓR(1) \Gamma_R^{(1)} stores primitive pairwise retained relations. The hypergraph/event sidecar ℋR \mathcal H_R stores which primitive relations were created/removed/coordinated in the same completed event. Thus simultaneity is preserved without turning a multi-address aggregate into one primitive edge. 7. Why no arbitrary sequentialization is introduced For Γ=2 \Gamma=2 there are 2!=2 2!=2 possible serial orders. For Γ=3 \Gamma=3 there are 3!=6 3!=6 possible serial orders. No current source receipt selects one. Therefore introducing one sequence would invent intermediate states. However it does not yet prove a diamond-like C6C_6 material graph. Thus the topology chain becomes source atoms→β→ΓR(1)→X4→R6→C6candidate branch. \boxed{ \text{source atoms} \to \beta \to \Gamma_R^{(1)} \to X_4 \to R_6 \to C_6\ \text{candidate branch}. } No material ring claim is promoted merely from the address-atomic decomposition. 9. Its physical derivation is instead a coupling-to-mismatch resonance: α=w2ℏvFkDsin(θ/2) \alpha = \frac{w}{2\hbar v_F k_D\sin(\theta/2)} and the first symmetric continuum approximation has v*vF=1−3α21+6α2. \frac{v_*}{v_F} = \frac{1-3\alpha^2}{1+6\alpha^2}. The transport slope vanishes when 3α2=1⇒α*=13. 3\alpha^2=1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \alpha_*=\frac1{\sqrt3}. Using 2ℏvFkD=19.81eV 2\hbar v_Fk_D=19.81\ {\mathrm eV} and w=0.110eV, w=0.110\ {\mathrm eV}, sinθ*2=3w2ℏvFkD, \sin\frac{\theta_*}{2} = \frac{\sqrt3\,w}{2\hbar v_Fk_D}, so θ*=2arcsin(3(0.110)19.81)=0.0192355907rad=1.102118165∘. \theta_* = 2\arcsin\!\left( \frac{\sqrt3(0.110)}{19.81} \right) = 0.0192355907\ {\mathrm rad} = 1.102118165^\circ. Thus the familiar experimental number 1.1° emerges naturally from the first-star velocity-cancellation condition with standard graphene parameters. A chiral continuum model with α1≃0.586 \alpha_1\simeq0.586 gives θ1≃1.085849713∘. \theta_1\simeq 1.085849713^\circ. A commonly used realistic full-model value near α≃0.605 \alpha\simeq0.605 corresponds to approximately 1.051747675∘. 1.051747675^\circ. Therefore 1.1° is not a universal pure-geometry number; its precise physical value depends on the continuum model and material parameters. 1. Geometric derivation Take two identical reciprocal-lattice vectors of magnitude kDk_D, rotated relative to one another by θ\theta. The vector difference has magnitude kθ=2kDsinθ2. k_\theta = 2k_D\sin\frac{\theta}{2}. This is the new small momentum scale generated by the twist. Question The exact quadratic face→pairing map requires a centered scalar field xf. x_f. Current support dynamics offers at least two source-bound candidates: interface support stock; face-to-cell support current. Which object should source the persistent pairing state? 1. Candidate S — interface stock Current exact face state: Sfiface=c2,f2. \boxed{ S_f^{\mathrm iface} = c_{2,f}^2. } Define its centered anisotropy xf(S)=Sfiface−14∑gSgiface. \boxed{ x_f^{(S)} = S_f^{\mathrm iface} - \frac14 \sum_gS_g^{\mathrm iface}. } Properties: state variable; nonnegative before centering; invariant under sign reversal of the face amplitude c2,fc_{2,f}; does not require a clock or event integration; survives when instantaneous transport current is zero; directly attached to the unique shared face reservoir. Q_{\mathrm pair}^{(S)}=0. This is consistent with the existing equal-cell pairing-source zero. 2. Candidate J — face current Current exact support flux: J23(f,τ)=2(B3)fτc2,fc3,τ. \boxed{ J_{23}(f,\tau) = 2(B_3)_{f\tau}c_{2,f}c_{3,\tau}. } A centered current adapter would be xf(J)=Jf−14∑gJg. x_f^{(J)} = J_f-\frac14\sum_gJ_g. The current manuscript explicitly types the sign of incidence current as orientation dependent. The resulting quadratic pairing diagnostic Qpair(J)=ℐQ←F(x(J)) Q_{\mathrm pair}^{(J)} = \mathcal I_{Q\leftarrow F} \left(x^{(J)}\right) has several distinct properties: it is a rate/flux-derived object, not a support state; it depends on event/time orientation; instantaneous current can vanish while face anisotropy remains nonzero; because ℐ\mathcal I is quadratic, ℐ(−x(J))=ℐ(x(J)), \mathcal I(-x^{(J)})=\mathcal I(x^{(J)}), so global current direction is discarded by the pairing projection; using an integrated current as a stock replacement requires an event interval and clock normalization. Thus current anisotropy can provide a useful dynamic modulation signal but is not automatically the persistent pairing state. 3. But Siface=(4,1,1,0), S^{\mathrm iface} = (4,1,1,0), whose centered face pattern has a nonzero pairing-22 component. Therefore Qpair(S)≠0,Qpair(J)=0. \boxed{ Q_{\mathrm pair}^{(S)}\ne0, \qquad Q_{\mathrm pair}^{(J)}=0. } AUTO_LOCK NO-GO INSTANTANEOUS_FACE_CURRENT_ALONE_CANNOT_UNIVERSALLY_REPRESENT_PERSISTENT_PAIRING_ANISOTROPY_v0.1 A useful control also emerged: the pattern S=(4,1,1,1) S=(4,1,1,1) is anisotropic but maps to zero pairing tensor. Q_{\mathrm pair}^{(S)}=0. For a canonical oriented tetrahedron with B3=(−1,+1,−1,+1)⊤ B_3=(-1,+1,-1,+1)^\top and c3=1, c_3=1, the face currents are J23=(−2,+2,−2,+2). J_{23}=(-2,+2,-2,+2). AUTO_LOCK FACE_STOCK_PAIRING_AND_FACE_CURRENT_PAIRING_ARE_INDEPENDENT_TYPED_ANISOTROPY_DIAGNOSTICS_v0.1 5. Therefore event-integrated J23J_{23} alone does not reconstruct the face stock unless the J12J_{12} contribution is independently known or vanishes. AUTO_LOCK NO-GO EVENT_INTEGRATED_J23_ALONE_DOES_NOT_DETERMINE_FACE_INTERFACE_STOCK_THEOREM_v0.1 So a universal replacement Sfiface↦∫J23ds S_f^{\mathrm iface} \mapsto \int J_{23}\,ds is not admitted. 6. Adjudication For a persistent pairing state / static cross-carrier coupling, the strongest current source candidate is xf=xf(S)=Sfiface−S‾. \boxed{ x_f = x_f^{(S)} = S_f^{\mathrm iface}-\bar S. } Status: PREFERRED MAINLINE CONSTITUTIVE CANDIDATE. It is not promoted to a physical material law; rather, it is the source choice best aligned with the current carrier typing. For transition-induced modulation, retain xf(J) \boxed{ x_f^{(J)} } as an independently typed sidecar. Status: DYNAMIC MODULATION CANDIDATE. AUTO_FREEZE Do not use x(S)+λx(J) x^{(S)}+\lambda x^{(J)} with an arbitrary coefficient λ\lambda. The two terms have different state/rate provenance and cannot be combined until a lawful clock/action normalization supplies the conversion. The remaining dynamical gap is narrower: derive why the exact face-mediated support transfer is weighted by the rank-two pairing overlap KQK_Q, and derive the coupling/detuning ratio that selects a transport-null angle. Current face currents may then modulate that baseline but should not silently replace it. Final status EXACT: interface stock is the face state. EXACT: J23J_{23} is face↔︎cell support flux. Equating gives 1−32γ2=1−ε+O(ε2,γ4), 1-\frac32\gamma^2 = 1-\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^2,\gamma^4), so γ*2=23ε+O(ε2). \boxed{ \gamma_*^2 = \frac23\varepsilon + O(\varepsilon^2). } Thus γ*∼23(α−1). \boxed{ \gamma_* \sim \sqrt{\frac23(\alpha-1)}. } AUTO_LOCK — EXACT ASYMPTOTIC CONDITIONAL SMALL_MAGIC_ANGLE_IS_SQUARE_ROOT_RESOLUTION_OF_NEAR_CRITICAL_COUPLING_EXCESS_THEOREM_v0.1 This is the strongest current mathematical explanation for why a very small transport magic angle can arise without being a primitive small angular constant. 4. Question Does the Hodge–Dirac / Projective Support Receipt (PSR) bridge repeat the §7.26 winding error: an internal law written in one functional class but measured through a silently different observation map? Ruling: no current map-class conflation was found. The Hodge–Dirac/PSR manuscript explicitly separates quadratic stocks, bilinear signed currents, root-sign probes, and covariance transport. 1. Internal Hodge–Dirac observables are already typed by map class The chain state is c=(cσ). c=(c_\sigma). Current internal observables include: simplex support stock qσ=cσ2 \boxed{ q_\sigma=c_\sigma^2 } and total support Sμ=∑σcσ2. \boxed{ S_\mu=\sum_\sigma c_\sigma^2. } These are quadratic/even in the chain amplitudes. Hasse current Jστ=2Bστcσcτ. \boxed{ J_{\sigma\tau} = 2B_{\sigma\tau}c_\sigma c_\tau. } This is bilinear and signed through the incidence orientation and amplitude signs. The manuscript does not infer the signed current from support squares alone. Indeed, the pre-PSR no-go proves that currents plus total support still do not identify the chain ray.
