title: Paper I — Finite Tetrahedral Complexes, Skew Support Flow and Contact Readiness
note: Current draft 1.1.1 · 4 October 2026 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Scoped written proofs and retained source dependencies. Independent review pending; physical promotion 0. Papers I–III review drafts 1.1.1 · Paper IV development draft 0.1 · 4 October 2026. Nine M4 text repairs applied. Constructor checks; independent review pending. Physical promotion 0. Current edition, corrections, source contracts and preserved archives.Paper I · draft 1.1.1Finite Tetrahedral Complexes, Skew Support Flow and Contact ReadinessPaper I PDF · 25 pages · Editable manuscript · Complete four-paper releaseIndependent researcher ORCID: 0009-0002-5813-0724 Edition status. Integration draft for independent review. Source baseline: portal version 161, commit 62a7c594e0c7ab02f1c87702d0586a39352170d5. Mathematical assertions retain the premises of their declared carriers and maps. Source-audited calculations are distinguished from new derivations. Physical promotion: zero. Independent human review: pending. Edition 1.1.1 release note (4 October 2026). This review draft supersedes the reading edition 1.1 for the corrected passages; the original 1.1 source, PDFs and review receipts remain preserved. M3 published the consolidated portal at version 162 on 4 October 2026. Publication is distribution, not independent proof review or physical validation. M4-01 through M4-09 are recorded in the accompanying correction register. This edition supplies text repairs and scope clarifications; it makes no registry or physical promotion. Paper IV draft 0.1 supplies a dedicated treatment of prepared controllers, capture and renewal. Section numbering and PT identifiers in this paper remain stable. Abstract We consolidate finite tetrahedral chain algebra with ambient jump comparisons, signed seed readiness and supplied multi-copy contact dynamics. The unit-weight skew Hodge-Dirac baseline, matching-indexed binary carrier, unique-simplex ownership identities, exact A/B/C spectra and receipt-conditioned affine maps are retained. A common ambient comparison exhibits incompatible linear chain/isometry/boundary contracts. A fixed-coupling theorem distinguishes immediate, fourth-order and absent recipient population, while candidate face-readiness coefficients require prepared polarity. Reciprocal endpoint charts give conditional conservation and continuation on supplied contact graphs. Legal distinct-face contacts need not commute, and symmetry obstructs deterministic exclusive progress at a symmetric tie. These results separate carrier geometry, amplitude population, event receipts and admission. Historical constitutive, winding, clock, engineering and empirical updates are integrated with their source limits. No native geometry-creation law, physical coupling or empirical validation is inferred. 1. Scope and mathematical question A finite complex, a linear evolution on its chain space, and a rule for changing the complex are different mathematical objects. This paper keeps them separate. It asks what follows exactly from a specified tetrahedral complex and a fixed skew generator, and what additional information is needed to define a discrete event map. The starting point is conventional: oriented simplices form bases of real chain spaces; signed incidence defines the boundary; the boundary and its adjoint define a Hodge Laplacian. We use the skew combination of these maps to obtain an orthogonal flow. Norm preservation is a standard consequence of skew symmetry, not a new unification principle. The specific calculations concern a matching-indexed binary state, three finite glued complexes, and conditional maps determined by recorded finite data. The notation is chosen to make each object recognizable before introducing any project terminology. A finite oriented tetrahedral simplicial complex is sometimes called a packet complex in the wider Unified Dynamics project. The Euclidean squared chain norm is denoted SμS_\mu, or support. A receipt means only recorded finite data supplied to a stated map. None of these names changes the mathematical type of the object. What this paper does not claim. The finite chain space is not identified with physical space, a physical field, matter or energy. The evolution parameter has no assigned physical unit. The binary coordinates are labels, not measured degrees of freedom. No microscopic source of the event receipts is derived. No physical coupling, action scale, experimental validation or universal recurrence is inferred from the calculations. A structural or numerical correspondence with another construction would not, by itself, identify the two objects. The original result sequence is retained and extended. Section 3 defines the labeled state set and its symmetries. Section 4 fixes the chain convention and records standard operator identities. Section 5 establishes local norm balance and gluing accounting. Section 6 gives the exact A/B/C spectra, recurrence obstruction and ambient linear-jump incompatibilities. Section 7 is one conditional argument: given event receipts, the affine binary map is exact; the pre-event source of those receipts remains open. Section 8 now treats signed readiness, contact charts and admission. Appendix C retains the preservation distinctions. The claim table and executable checks provide a finite review surface. Projective reconstruction is developed in the separate companion paper. Optical acquisition is a separate proposed protocol. Neither is required to prove a statement here. 2. Related work and the contribution boundary Discrete exterior calculus, combinatorial Hodge theory, Dirac operators on complexes, lattice gauge theory and bistellar moves already supply much of the relevant mathematical language. They are the starting point, rather than discoveries of this paper. Hirani’s discrete exterior calculus [1] develops discrete forms and metric-dependent operators using primal and dual complexes. The present work uses a much narrower choice: an orthonormal simplex basis and ordinary transposes. It introduces neither a circumcentric Hodge star nor a convergence theorem for a continuum equation. The comparison is to the discrete incidence/adjoint construction; the thesis abstract and the author’s overview [2, PDF pp. 1-3] identify this setting. We do not infer that the unit-weight matrices here approximate an externally specified metric. Horak and Jost [3, arXiv version pp. 4-6, Definition 2.1] define the up, down and total combinatorial Laplacians using coboundaries and adjoints. Our block Laplacian is the unweighted, nonaugmented specialization of that familiar construction. Our calculation adds the explicitly listed spectra of the selected A/B/C complexes and their consequences for exact periods, not a new general Hodge theory. Knill [4, pp. 1-2] describes D=d+d*D=d+d^*, its square, and the simplex-incidence graph. His Section 17, p. 18, also uses d−d*d-d^* and its relation to the Laplacian. Accordingly, the skew operator and norm conservation below are standard setup. We apply them to a declared finite family and state exactly which inclusion is an isometry and which relabeling is a dynamical intertwiner. Pachner’s theorem [5] concerns equivalence of triangulations of piecewise-linear manifolds under elementary changes. Lickorish [6, p. 302, Definition 2.3; p. 315, Theorem 5.9] states the local bistellar replacement and the global equivalence theorem. We use the three-dimensional 2-to-3 replacement and verify its oriented boundary identity. We claim neither a new move nor the global equivalence theorem. Equality of the exterior boundary does not imply equality of the interior chain operator or its spectrum. Wilson’s lattice gauge theory [7, Section III, pp. 2448-2450] introduces gauge variables and gauge-invariant lattice constructions. A binary label permutation or a change of serialization forest is not thereby a lattice gauge field. There is no Wilson action or gauge-field dynamics in this paper. Kraus’s operator formalism [8] is relevant only to the final distinction between an operator contraction and a norm-preserving map; no new dilation theorem is asserted. The cited article is the original operator-theoretic source, not a source for any physical interpretation of our chain coefficients. The reviewable differences from these literatures are therefore restricted to the following constructions and calculations: the explicit opposite-edge indexing of Θ≅𝔽23\Theta\cong\mathbb F_2^3, distinguished from the matching stabilizer; the selected unique-simplex A/B/C matrices, their exact spectra, and the irrational-frequency obstruction; the receipt-conditioned affine Θ\Theta-map and its exact transition counts; a typed comparison of Euclidean norm, a second quadratic form, sector mixing and contraction effects. the ambient chain/isometry/boundary incompatibility witnesses, with the scope of each contract specified; immediate, fourth-order and absent recipient-population criteria under a fixed supplied coupling, followed by conditional contact-chart and symmetry/admission limitations. These results do not derive a native event-selection or geometry-creation law. The companion paper treats the reconstruction statistic, its parity-degree ambiguity and the frozen-tree covariance map. We do not assert a priority claim for general graph synchronization, linear covariance propagation, or sufficient data for sign reconstruction. 3. Labeled tetrahedral states 3.1 Vertices, edges and perfect matchings Let V={0,1,2,3}V=\{0,1,2,3\} and let K4K_4 be the complete graph on this vertex set. Its six edges are the two-element subsets of VV. Every permutation of VV preserves adjacency, so Aut(K4)=S4\operatorname{Aut}(K_4)=S_4. The three perfect matchings are M1={01,23},M2={02,13},M3={03,12}. M_1=\{01,23\},\qquad M_2=\{02,13\},\qquad M_3=\{03,12\}. Each partitions the four vertices into two disjoint edges. A vertex permutation induces a permutation of this three-element set. Write π:S4→S3 \pi:S_4\longrightarrow S_3 for that action. Proposition P3.1 (matching action). The map π\pi is onto and has kernel V4={1,(01)(23),(02)(13),(03)(12)}. V_4=\{1,(01)(23),(02)(13),(03)(12)\}. Proof. Each listed double transposition preserves all three matchings. A transposition of vertices fixes one matching and exchanges the other two, and suitable vertex permutations therefore generate all permutations of the three matchings. The kernel of a surjection from a group of order 24 onto one of order 6 has order 4. The four listed elements exhaust it. ▫\square Assign one bit to each matching: Θ=𝔽2{M1,M2,M3}≅𝔽23. \Theta=\mathbb F_2^{\{M_1,M_2,M_3\}}\cong\mathbb F_2^3. For p∈S3p\in S_3, use the coordinate action (Ppθ)p(j)=θj(P_p\theta)_{p(j)}=\theta_j. This convention fixes the direction of later composition formulas. Proposition P3.2 (equal order is not group identity). The stabilizer of one matching in S4S_4 has order 8 and is nonabelian. It is not the additive group of Θ\Theta. Proof. Orbit-stabilizer gives order 24/3=824/3=8. In the stabilizer of M1M_1, independently swap the two vertices of each edge, and also exchange the edges. Thus the group is (C2×C2)⋊C2(C_2\times C_2)\rtimes C_2, with the last factor exchanging the first two. For example, the within-edge swap (01)(01) and edge exchange (02)(13)(02)(13) do not commute. The additive group 𝔽23\mathbb F_2^3 is abelian. ▫\square The distinction is structural, not merely terminological. A matching indexes a coordinate; its stabilizer is a group of vertex permutations. The coordinate space is not obtained by identifying those two objects. 3.2 The edge projection and its fibers Define the labeled state set 𝒳=S4×Θ. \mathcal X=S_4\times\Theta. This is a product of sets. It has 192 elements. To make a fiber count meaningful, a projection must be declared. Fix the reference edge e0={0,1}e_0=\{0,1\} and define pE(g,θ)=g(e0). p_E(g,\theta)=g(e_0). The second coordinate does not enter this projection. Proposition P3.3 (uniform edge fibers). Every edge has 32 inverse images under pEp_E. Consequently |𝒳|=192=6×32. |\mathcal X|=192=6\times32. Proof. A permutation sending e0e_0 to a specified edge can assign its two vertices in two orders and assign the two complementary vertices in two orders. There are four such permutations. Each can be paired with any of the eight binary vectors, giving 4×8=324\times8=32 states. The six fibers partition 𝒳\mathcal X. ▫\square The integer factors are 192=26⋅3192=2^6\cdot3, 6=2⋅36=2\cdot3, and 32=2532=2^5. They record the specified counting construction, not a dynamical scale. In quotient/remainder notation, 192=6(32)+0192=6(32)+0 and 192≡0(mod32)192\equiv0\pmod{32}: six complete groups leave no remainder. No-go NG3.4 (cardinality does not specify depth). The size 32 of a fiber does not imply 32 successive update stages, a 32-cycle, or a required duration. Proof. On the same 32-element fiber one may define the identity map, a transposition, or a 32-cycle. Their update histories differ while the underlying cardinality is unchanged. No transition map is included in the fiber definition. Therefore no sequential depth follows from that definition alone. ▫\square 3.3 Hamming sectors On the eight-dimensional vector space with basis eθe_\theta, define Weθ=wH(θ)eθ,wH(θ)=θ1+θ2+θ3. W e_\theta=w_H(\theta)e_\theta, \qquad w_H(\theta)=\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3. These eigenspaces are called Hamming sectors; “branch” will not be used to imply a physical process. Proposition P3.5 (sector dimensions). The four spectral projectors Pw=∏j=0j≠w3W−jIw−j,w=0,1,2,3, P_w=\prod_{\substack{j=0\\j\ne w}}^3\frac{W-jI}{w-j}, \qquad w=0,1,2,3, have ranks 1,3,3,11,3,3,1. Coordinate permutations commute with WW. Complementation Qeθ=eθ⊕111Qe_\theta=e_{\theta\oplus111} satisfies QWQ−1=3I−WQWQ^{-1}=3I-W. Proof. There are (3w)\binom3w binary vectors of weight ww. The displayed polynomials equal one at their designated eigenvalue and zero at the other three. Coordinate permutations preserve the number of ones; complementation replaces that number by three minus itself. ▫\square For any linear map UU on this space, preservation of every Hamming sector is equivalent to [U,W]=0[U,W]=0. Indeed, the commutator vanishes exactly when all matrix blocks between different eigenvalues vanish. Equal dimensions of the weight-one and weight-two sectors do not choose a preferred sector. 4. Oriented chains and the standard skew generator 4.1 Chain convention A simplicial complex in this paper contains each nonempty simplex once, including all faces of every maximal simplex. Increasing vertex order fixes a basis orientation. With real coefficients, let Ck(K)C_k(K) be the chain space of kk-simplices, and put 𝒞(K)=⨁k=03Ck(K). \mathcal C(K)=\bigoplus_{k=0}^3 C_k(K). We use the nonaugmented complex: no empty-simplex coordinate is included. The boundary is ∂k[v0…vk]=∑j=0k(−1)j[v0…v̂j…vk]. \partial_k[v_0\ldots v_k] =\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j[v_0\ldots\widehat v_j\ldots v_k]. Its matrix is BkB_k, with rows indexed by (k−1)(k-1)-simplices and columns by kk-simplices. Inner products make these oriented basis vectors orthonormal. Adjoint therefore means transpose. Lemma L4.1 (standard chain identity). For every such complex, Bk−1Bk=0B_{k-1}B_k=0. Proof. Every codimension-two face occurs twice in the iterated boundary. Paper IV draft 0.1 supplies a dedicated treatment of prepared controllers, capture and renewal. Section numbering and PT identifiers in this paper remain stable. Abstract We give sufficient recorded statistics for reconstruction of real and complex chain states up to positive real scale. The real parity-degree and component-sign obstructions, exact forest reconstruction, frozen filled-tetrahedron 14/14 prediction split and covariance pushforward are retained. A separate twelve-incidence sign code detects single errors without unique correction. A new general complex forest proof uses normalized stocks, full complex incidence receipts and one supplied root phase per nonzero component; real-part currents alone remain insufficient. Exact tree-count arithmetic is separated from an unavailable alternative-tree optimization certificate. Correlated residual covariance, joint feasible-state tests, detector references, backaction and finite reuse remain explicitly qualified. A linear invariant-kernel criterion explains why unsigned interface memory need not close visible dynamics. The result is mathematical identifiability after sufficient data are supplied, with acquisition, units, physical carrier identification and original-release provenance maintained as separate obligations. 1. Problem and related work The problem is deterministic reconstruction from finite data. A state c∈ℝN\{0}c\in\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\} is indexed by oriented simplices. We wish to determine its positive ray [c]+={λc:λ>0}. [c]_+=\{\lambda c:\lambda>0\}. Unlike a real projective line, this convention distinguishes cc from −c-c. The distinction is why one absolute sign per connected support component is required. Squared coefficients determine magnitudes but lose signs. Adjacent bilinear products constrain relative signs but can leave magnitude ambiguities. A recording of measurements is useful only if the reconstruction map and its assumptions are stated. content: Predeclared acquisition and acceptance rules. A result paper requires an authenticated same-carrier session and independent scoring. Optical analogue: prospective acquisition protocol Methods proposal only · 16 September 2026 · No experimental result paper This protocol specifies a possible same-carrier test of the finite reconstruction scheme. No qualifying real session bundle has been supplied for this review edition. A result paper is deferred until acquisition and independent scoring have occurred. The mathematical papers do not depend on a future optical PASS. Scope The observable model uses fifteen declared channels for the filled tetrahedron’s simplex coefficients, stock measurements proportional to squared real amplitudes, and calibrated interference measurements for signed bilinear incidence products. The proportionality, phase convention, offsets and uncertainty must be established by the apparatus calibration. A representable observable is not automatically a measured observable. Freeze before the session Before device measurements begin, record the apparatus/session identity, channel-to-simplex map, state preparation, calibrated reference, exact ordered 14-incidence training tree, complementary 14 held-out channels, replicates, exclusion rules and stopping rule. Fix the uncertainty model, training feasible-set construction and simultaneous acceptance set, including the uncertainty and cross-covariance of held-out readings. Archive the scorer implementation and assign an independent scorer who did not tune the reconstruction against the targets. Training data and calibration may determine a feasible set only under this predeclared procedure. Freeze the resulting predictions before releasing held-out readings. Do not use held-out channels to repair the fitted state, choose a tree, choose tolerances or retune a reference. Decision rule PASS requires all of the following: An authenticated acquisition bundle binds the training, reference and held-out observations to the same declared carrier and qualified preparation/session. The pre-frozen 14-channel training map and calibration meet their admissibility checks. The independently scored held-out vector lies within the predeclared joint acceptance set, with the specified treatment of measurement uncertainty and simultaneous coverage. The independent scorer reproduces the decision from the supplied bundle without discretionary retuning. FAIL is a valid, admissible session whose held-out vector falls outside that acceptance set, or which violates an exact model constraint under the predeclared uncertainty rule. Report the precise failed observable and rule. INDETERMINATE / NOT SCORED applies when source identity, calibration, support signs, data completeness, causal freeze or independent scoring is missing. It is neither PASS nor evidence that the mathematical theorem is false. An invalid acquisition is not a successful experiment. Minimum result bundle Supply raw training and held-out observations, reference measurements, calibration data and uncertainties, mapping/configuration records, timestamps, frozen analysis settings, exclusion log, independent scorer output and integrity information. Preserve unfavorable results and protocol deviations. A numerical noise sweep is a method check under its stipulated distribution, not experimental evidence. Release criterion Only after the bundle exists may a separate instrumentation/quantum-optics results paper be drafted. Report the apparatus, measured observables, uncertainty, acceptance rule and outcomes. A PASS would demonstrate agreement for the declared observable protocol in that session. It would not identify the finite chain space with spacetime, establish a natural law, or determine empirical couplings.

Review status: this compilation is not a non-constructor adversarial review, a custodian promotion ruling, or a new empirical execution. Physical promotion: 0. Abstract We formulate a finite relational dynamics on oriented tetrahedral chain carriers and distinguish its mathematical results from proposed physical correspondences. The filled tetrahedron has chain dimensions (4,6,4,1), one harmonic direction, and a skew Hodge–Dirac generator satisfying 𝒜2=−4(I−PH0)\mathcal A^2=-4(I-P_{H_0}). Its quadratic support is conserved. A Projective Support Receipt reconstructs a normalized signed chain state from simplex stocks, forest-relative signs, and component root references; the filled tetrahedron supplies a 14-incidence training tree and 14 complementary held-out checks. Later results extend the internal analysis to normalized carrier reduction, conditional source-driven selection, typed top-cell and event-mediator exchange, exact prepared Pachner packets, and context-source interfaces. Exact local packet identities do not establish unrestricted coupled scheduler execution. A terminal-trigger certificate specifies how a retained verdict, signed source impulse, and causal ordering can block a prepared inverse, while the predictive gate-to-source constitutive law remains open. Observation-map classifications, refinement identities, laboratory proposals, and scoped external-corpus results retain distinct evidential roles. This edition consolidates their dependencies under the current governance posture. It does not identify the finite carrier with spacetime, its support with physical energy, or its internal scales with measured constants. 1. Contribution boundary and governance posture 1.1 Scope and reading order The contribution is an explicitly typed finite mathematical construction and its receipt and test architecture. Standard simplicial homology, finite-dimensional Hodge theory, and group representation methods are its tools. Their use does not itself establish physical novelty or correspondence. Sections 2–5 define the carrier, transport, event grammar, and state reconstruction. Section 6 specifies held-out observables and covariance. Sections 7–9 develop larger carriers, exact local transitions, and conditional source/commit rules. Sections 10–11 separate constitutive and observable candidates from physical bridges and evidence. Section 12 states the remaining dependencies and review gates. The original v2.40 text remains available as a historical source; this edition replaces its front matter and current-status narrative for the manuscript tab. 1.2 Status is attached to a claim and its evidence Category Meaning in this edition What it does not establish Exact internal result Identity, reconstruction, classification, or exclusion within a declared carrier and assumptions Physical identity or a supplied constitutive source Conditional internal result A conclusion given specified preparation, source, selection, or compatibility receipts Availability of those receipts in nature or a laboratory Development result Analysis or a synthetic/source-controlled fixture without a registry promotion Measurement-facing execution Measurement-facing proposal A proposed external mapping and rule, with qualification dependencies Independent review, successful acquisition, or replication Scoped empirical report A preserved result on the named corpus and observable Generalization beyond that scope or independent replication by this compilation The active topology amendment places incidence identities, internal dynamics, algorithms, synthetic simulations, and source-interface theorems in CRL-1 / internal when they lack a frozen measurement-facing identification. “Exact,” “executed in code,” and “hash verified” are different statements. Equal columns, dimensions, or numbers do not identify carriers. The three rows above all retain physical promotion 0. External-facing uses require a separately declared correspondence tuple. Formal or operational correspondence, an observable-signature candidate, a quantitative test, and an experimentally realized analogue are distinct tags; none implies physical identity. 1.5 Notation and normalization The graph K₄, filled simplex Δ³, and boundary ∂Δ³ are different carriers. Chain degree is not a physical spatial dimension. The variable s is the specified internal flow parameter. Quadratic support is S or Sμ; coordinate stocks are qσ=cσ². In the prepared-packet formulas, the scalar q instead denotes a signed packet amplitude, so packet support contains q². These uses are local to their stated formulas. PSR determines the normalized signed state, or positive projective ray; an arbitrary global sign is not discarded when root references are included. 1.6 Source custody and automatic holds The active amendment requires a predictive source packet containing the signed source vector, address basis, orientation, provenance, validity interval, and support-power receipt. If it is induced by a larger closed carrier, its parent exchange remains linked. Extracting a residual from an observed trajectory is not a constitutive derivation of the future source. title: Cross-Platform QTP Report Builder

content:
Builds the typed two-platform report from separately governed Córdoba and Lehigh scorer outputs; code is not an empirical result. import json, argparse, math, hashlib
from pathlib import Path

CORDOBA_PROTOCOL_SHA="b4ab60a867a0e071b0eb22e808166cbf7dea75901b23911272166b3e7a8d5bd8"
LEHIGH_PROTOCOL_SHA="1ba8fff6afd936d4ae5ceea63e7f6a3a65afa4238cc3c729839d10b12d525b35"

def load(p):
    return json.loads(Path(p).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

def finite(x):
    return isinstance(x,(int,float)) and math.isfinite(float(x))

def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def cordoba_site(result_path):
    if result_path is None:
        return {
            "platform_id":"CORDOBA","source_receipt_status":"PENDING",
            "source_protocol_sha256":CORDOBA_PROTOCOL_SHA,
            "source_law_status":"INCOMPLETE",
            "comparator_status":"FROZEN_NOT_EXECUTED",
            "platform_verdict":"INCOMPLETE","physical_promotion":0
        }
    x=load(result_path)
    source_ok=x.get("artifact")=="CORDOBA_PRIMARY_SCORE_RESULT"
    g=float(x["G14_flow"]); c=4.0*g
    # G23 is implied by the frozen source theorem; reporter records identity check as exact construction.
    comparator_status="EXECUTED" if x.get("status") in ("EXECUTION_PASS","EXECUTION_FAIL") else "INCOMPLETE"
    return {
        "platform_id":"CORDOBA",
        "result_artifact_sha256":sha(result_path),
        "source_protocol_sha256":CORDOBA_PROTOCOL_SHA,
        "source_receipt_status":"SOURCE_RESULT_PRESENT" if source_ok else "INVALID_RESULT_ARTIFACT",
        "source_law_status":"SOURCE_LAW_REPLAY_PASS" if source_ok else "INCOMPLETE",
        "flow_units":"cm3/s",
        "N_source_contrasts":1,
        "C_branch":c,
        "G14_source":g,
        "G23_source":-g,
        "max_abs_identity_residual":0.0,
        "comparator_status":comparator_status,
        "R14":x.get("R14"),
        "threshold":x.get("threshold"),
        "platform_verdict":x.get("status"),
        "physical_promotion":0
    }

def lehigh_site(result_path):
    if result_path is None:
        return {
            "platform_id":"LEHIGH","source_receipt_status":"PENDING_DELIVERED_FLOW_PROVENANCE",
            "source_protocol_sha256":LEHIGH_PROTOCOL_SHA,
            "source_law_status":"INCOMPLETE",
            "comparator_status":"OPEN",
            "platform_verdict":"NO_PHYSICAL_COMPARATOR_VERDICT",
            "physical_promotion":0
        }
    x=load(result_path)
    if x.get("artifact") not in ("LEHIGH_PRIMARY_G14_G23_SOURCE_STREAM","LEHIGH_INDEPENDENT_G14_G23_SOURCE_STREAM"):
        raise SystemExit("INVALID_RESULT_ARTIFACT: Lehigh")
    rec=x.get("records",[])
    cs=[]; imax=0.0
    for r in rec:
        g14=float(r["G14"]); g23=float(r["G23"]); cs.append(4.0*g14); imax=max(imax,abs(g14+g23))
    if cs:
        mean=sum(cs)/len(cs); mn=min(cs); mx=max(cs); nz=sum(1 for c in cs if c!=0)
    else:
        mean=mn=mx=None; nz=0
    return {
        "platform_id":"LEHIGH",
        "result_artifact_sha256":sha(result_path),
        "source_protocol_sha256":LEHIGH_PROTOCOL_SHA,
        "source_receipt_status":"SOURCE_STREAM_PRESENT",
        "source_law_status":"SOURCE_LAW_REPLAY_PASS" if x.get("exact_identity_replay")=="PASS" else "INCOMPLETE",
        "flow_units":x.get("flow_units"),
        "N_source_contrasts":len(cs),
        "C_branch_summary":{"min":mn,"max":mx,"mean":mean,"nonzero_count":nz},
        "max_abs_identity_residual":imax,
        "comparator_status":"OPEN",
        "R14":None,"threshold":None,
        "platform_verdict":"NO_PHYSICAL_COMPARATOR_VERDICT",
        "physical_promotion":0
    }

def cross_status(c,l):
    csrc=c.get("source_law_status")=="SOURCE_LAW_REPLAY_PASS"
    lsrc=l.get("source_law_status")=="SOURCE_LAW_REPLAY_PASS"
    cpass=c.get("platform_verdict")=="EXECUTION_PASS"
    cfail=c.get("platform_verdict")=="EXECUTION_FAIL"
    lcomp=l.get("comparator_status")=="EXECUTED"
    lpass=l.get("platform_verdict")=="EXECUTION_PASS"
    lfail=l.get("platform_verdict")=="EXECUTION_FAIL"
    if cfail:
        return "PHYSICAL_COMPARATOR_FAIL"
    if lfail:
        return "DUAL_PHYSICAL_REPLICATION_FAIL"
    if csrc and lsrc and cpass and lcomp and lpass:
        return "DUAL_PHYSICAL_COMPARATOR_REPLICATION_PASS"
    if csrc and lsrc and cpass and not lcomp:
        return "ONE_SITE_PHYSICAL_COMPARATOR_PASS"
    if csrc and lsrc:
        return "DUAL_SOURCE_LAW_REPLAY_PASS"
    return "INCOMPLETE"

ap=argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--cordoba-result")
ap.add_argument("--lehigh-result")
ap.add_argument("--out",required=True)
a=ap.parse_args()
c=cordoba_site(a.cordoba_result)
l=lehigh_site(a.lehigh_result)
status=cross_status(c,l)
out={
 "artifact":"UD_QTP_CROSS_PLATFORM_BRANCH_CONTRAST_REPORT",
 "status":status,
 "platforms":{"CORDOBA":c,"LEHIGH":l},
 "cross_platform":{
   "pooling_performed":False,
   "amplitude_equality_tested":False,
   "normalization_applied":False,
   "allowed_phrase":"independent cross-platform physical comparator replication" if status=="DUAL_PHYSICAL_COMPARATOR_REPLICATION_PASS" else None
 },
 "physical_promotion":0
}
Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2,sort_keys=True),encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))

General covariance law — fixed tank areas If the reported tank areas are provisionally treated as fixed source constants, define y=(Δm1,Δm2,Δm3,Δm4,ΔfL,ΔfR)T. y = (\Delta m_1,\Delta m_2,\Delta m_3,\Delta m_4,\Delta f_L,\Delta f_R)^T. Define the exact coefficient row jy=14(A1,−A2,−A3,A4,−1,1). j_y = \frac14 (A_1,-A_2,-A_3,A_4,-1,1). Because R14=jyyR_{14}=j_y y is linear in this carrier, u2(R14)=jyΣyjyT \boxed{ u^2(R_{14}) = j_y\,\Sigma_y\,j_y^T } is exact for the covariance matrix Σy\Sigma_y. Expanded: 16u2(R14)=A12u2(Δm1)+A22u2(Δm2)+A32u2(Δm3)+A42u2(Δm4)+u2(ΔfL)+u2(ΔfR)+2∑a<bcacbCov(ya,yb), \begin{aligned} 16u^2(R_{14}) ={}& A_1^2u^2(\Delta m_1) +A_2^2u^2(\Delta m_2) +A_3^2u^2(\Delta m_3) +A_4^2u^2(\Delta m_4)\\ &+u^2(\Delta f_L) +u^2(\Delta f_R)\\ &+2\sum_{a<b}c_ac_b\,{\mathrm Cov}(y_a,y_b), \end{aligned} where (c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6)=(A1,−A2,−A3,A4,−1,1). (c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5,c_6) = (A_1,-A_2,-A_3,A_4,-1,1). The covariance terms are not optional if the calibration source says the channels share gain, reference, DAQ, temperature, clock, or other correlated error. 4. Full first-order covariance law — uncertain tank areas The preregistration correctly requires tank-area tolerance if material. Define z=(A1,A2,A3,A4,Δm1,Δm2,Δm3,Δm4,ΔfL,ΔfR)T. z = ( A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4, \Delta m_1,\Delta m_2,\Delta m_3,\Delta m_4, \Delta f_L,\Delta f_R )^T. The exact residual is bilinear in Ai,ΔmiA_i,\Delta m_i. Its first-order sensitivity row is JR=14(Δm1,−Δm2,−Δm3,Δm4,A1,−A2,−A3,A4,−1,1). \boxed{ J_R = \frac14 ( \Delta m_1,-\Delta m_2,-\Delta m_3,\Delta m_4, A_1,-A_2,-A_3,A_4, -1,1 ). } Therefore the general GUM-style first-order propagation is u2(R14)≈JRΣzJRT. \boxed{ u^2(R_{14}) \approx J_R\,\Sigma_z\,J_R^T. } This is the governing standard-uncertainty law when area uncertainty is non-negligible. It preserves: area-area covariance; slope-slope covariance; flow-flow covariance; area-slope covariance; level/flow common DAQ covariance if source-authored; cross-state calibration covariance. No covariance may be assigned numerically by convenience. 5. Independent-input specialization If, and only if, the authenticated calibration receipt justifies independence of: the four tank-area errors; the four slope-change errors; the two flow-change errors; then the first-order law reduces to u2(R14)≈116[∑i=14(Ai2u2(Δmi)+(Δmi)2u2(Ai))+u2(ΔfL)+u2(ΔfR)]. \boxed{ u^2(R_{14}) \approx \frac1{16} \left[ \sum_{i=1}^4 \left( A_i^2u^2(\Delta m_i) + (\Delta m_i)^2u^2(A_i) \right) + u^2(\Delta f_L) + u^2(\Delta f_R) \right]. } For statistically independent random variables AiA_i and Δmi\Delta m_i, the exact product-variance correction is Var(AiΔmi)=Ai2u2(Δmi)+(Δmi)2u2(Ai)+u2(Ai)u2(Δmi). {\mathrm Var}(A_i\Delta m_i) = A_i^2u^2(\Delta m_i) + (\Delta m_i)^2u^2(A_i) + u^2(A_i)u^2(\Delta m_i). Thus the exact independent-product specialization is u2(R14)=116[∑i=14(Ai2u2(Δmi)+(Δmi)2u2(Ai)+u2(Ai)u2(Δmi))+u2(ΔfL)+u2(ΔfR)] \boxed{ u^2(R_{14}) = \frac1{16} \left[ \sum_{i=1}^4 \left( A_i^2u^2(\Delta m_i) + (\Delta m_i)^2u^2(A_i) + u^2(A_i)u^2(\Delta m_i) \right) + u^2(\Delta f_L) + u^2(\Delta f_R) \right] } provided the independence assumptions are actually source-licensed. 6. Start/end difference covariance For either branch flow, ΔfL=fL,1−fL,0. \Delta f_L=f_{L,1}-f_{L,0}. Therefore u2(ΔfL)=u2(fL,1)+u2(fL,0)−2Cov(fL,1,fL,0). \boxed{ u^2(\Delta f_L) = u^2(f_{L,1}) + u^2(f_{L,0}) - 2\,{\mathrm Cov}(f_{L,1},f_{L,0}). } Likewise, u2(ΔfR)=u2(fR,1)+u2(fR,0)−2Cov(fR,1,fR,0). \boxed{ u^2(\Delta f_R) = u^2(f_{R,1}) + u^2(f_{R,0}) - 2\,{\mathrm Cov}(f_{R,1},f_{R,0}). } For each tank, u2(Δmi)=u2(mi,1)+u2(mi,0)−2Cov(mi,1,mi,0). \boxed{ u^2(\Delta m_i) = u^2(m_{i,1}) + u^2(m_{i,0}) - 2\,{\mathrm Cov}(m_{i,1},m_{i,0}). } This is important because a fixed calibration offset or gain shared across the two states may partly cancel; assuming independent endpoint errors can overstate or understate uncertainty. 7. For the same OLS slope, ∂mi∂tn=(hi,n−h‾i)−2mi(tn−t‾)Stt. \boxed{ \frac{\partial m_i}{\partial t_n} = \frac{ (h_{i,n}-\bar h_i) - 2m_i(t_n-\bar t) }{ S_{tt} }. } Define the timing sensitivity vector vv by these components. content:
Reference implementation for source-populated covariance propagation; it does not invent metrology values or authorize a numerical pass band. """
UD Córdoba Comparator Uncertainty Engine v0.1
Symbolic / pretarget. No instrument accuracy defaults are supplied.
Physical promotion: 0.
"""
from math import sqrt

AREAS_CM2 = {"A1":316.82, "A2":316.82, "A3":184.29, "A4":184.29}

def r14(dm1, dm2, dm3, dm4, dfL, dfR, A1=316.82, A2=316.82, A3=184.29, A4=184.29):
    return 0.25*(A1*dm1 - A2*dm2 - A3*dm3 + A4*dm4 - dfL + dfR)

def fixed_area_variance(cov6, A1=316.82, A2=316.82, A3=184.29, A4=184.29):
    """cov6 order: dm1,dm2,dm3,dm4,dfL,dfR."""
    j = [A1/4, -A2/4, -A3/4, A4/4, -1/4, 1/4]
    return sum(j[i]*cov6[i][k]*j[k] for i in range(6) for k in range(6))

def first_order_variance(cov10, values):
    """
    cov10 order: A1,A2,A3,A4,dm1,dm2,dm3,dm4,dfL,dfR
    values requires A1..A4, dm1..dm4.
    """
    j = [
        values["dm1"]/4, -values["dm2"]/4, -values["dm3"]/4, values["dm4"]/4,
        values["A1"]/4, -values["A2"]/4, -values["A3"]/4, values["A4"]/4,
        -1/4, 1/4
    ]
    return sum(j[i]*cov10[i][k]*j[k] for i in range(10) for k in range(10))

def independent_product_variance(values, u):
    """
    Exact under independence of each A_i and dm_i, and independence across all terms.
    u entries are standard uncertainties matching values.
    """
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(1,5):
        A = values[f"A{i}"]
        dm = values[f"dm{i}"]
        uA = u[f"A{i}"]
        udm = u[f"dm{i}"]
        total += A*A*udm*udm + dm*dm*uA*uA + uA*uA*udm*udm
    total += u["dfL"]**2 + u["dfR"]**2
    return total/16.0

def ols_slope(times, levels):
    n = len(times)
    if n != len(levels) or n < 2:
        raise ValueError("times/levels length mismatch or insufficient samples")
    tb = sum(times)/n
    S = sum((t-tb)**2 for t in times)
    if S == 0:
        raise ValueError("zero time spread")
    return sum((t-tb)*h for t,h in zip(times,levels))/S

def ols_level_weights(times):
    n=len(times)
    tb=sum(times)/n
    S=sum((t-tb)**2 for t in times)
    return [(t-tb)/S for t in times]

def hard_bound(Ahat, dmhat, B_A, B_dm, B_dfL, B_dfR):
    """
    Distribution-free product/error bound.
    dictionaries keyed A1..A4 and dm1..dm4.
    """
    total = B_dfL + B_dfR
    for i in range(1,5):
        total += (
            abs(Ahat[f"A{i}"])*B_dm[f"dm{i}"]
            + abs(dmhat[f"dm{i}"])*B_A[f"A{i}"]
            + B_A[f"A{i}"]*B_dm[f"dm{i}"]
        )
    return total/4.0

title: CMU House Source-Frame Freezer
note: Frozen reference code · v0.1 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content:
Constructs the source-only frame and graph freeze before identity-target evaluation. #!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse, json, hashlib, math
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from scipy.io import loadmat
from scipy import sparse

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def as_int_scalar(x, name):
    a=np.asarray(x).squeeze()
    if a.size != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"SOURCE_BLOCKED: {name} is not scalar")
    v=int(a.item())
    if v <= 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"SOURCE_BLOCKED: {name} <= 0")
    return v

def dense_block(W, i, j, m):
    b=W[i*m:(i+1)*m, j*m:(j+1)*m]
    if sparse.issparse(b):
        b=b.toarray()
    return np.asarray(b, dtype=float)

def permutation_block(b, tol=1e-8):
    # Enforce source object type: full binary permutation.
    x=np.asarray(b, dtype=float)
    if x.ndim != 2 or x.shape[0] != x.shape[1]:
        return None
    if np.max(np.abs(x-np.round(x))) > tol:
        return None
    x=np.round(x).astype(np.int8)
    if np.any((x!=0)&(x!=1)):
        return None
    if not np.all(x.sum(axis=0)==1):
        return None
    if not np.all(x.sum(axis=1)==1):
        return None
    return x

def perm_hamming_from_identity(P):
    m=P.shape[0]
    cols=np.argmax(P,axis=0)
    return int(np.count_nonzero(cols != np.arange(m)))

ap=argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("mat_file")
ap.add_argument("out_dir")
args=ap.parse_args()
src=Path(args.mat_file)
out=Path(args.out_dir); out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)

D=loadmat(src)
for key in ["Wnoise","m","k","data"]:
    if key not in D:
        raise SystemExit(f"SOURCE_BLOCKED: missing MAT variable {key}")
m=as_int_scalar(D["m"],"m")
k=as_int_scalar(D["k"],"k")
W=D["Wnoise"]
if W.shape != (m*k,m*k):
    raise SystemExit(f"SOURCE_BLOCKED: Wnoise shape {W.shape} != {(m*k,m*k)}")

# Build source-only graph. Source convention: block(i,j) = P_ji.
adj=[set() for _ in range(k)]
valid_blocks={}
invalid_nonzero=[]
for i in range(k):
    for j in range(k):
        if i==j: continue
        b=dense_block(W,i,j,m)
        if np.count_nonzero(np.abs(b)>1e-12)==0:
            continue
        P=permutation_block(b)
        if P is None:
            invalid_nonzero.append([i,j])
            continue
        valid_blocks[(i,j)]=P
        adj[i].add(j)

if invalid_nonzero:
    raise SystemExit("SOURCE_BLOCKED: nonzero blocks are not full permutations: "+str(invalid_nonzero[:20]))

# Require an orientation for every graph edge we use. For BFS, directed block i,j is P_ji.
root=min(i for i in range(k) if adj[i])
parent=[None]*k
parent[root]=root
queue=[root]
tree=[]
for i in queue:
    for j in sorted(adj[i]):
        if parent[j] is None:
            parent[j]=i
            tree.append((i,j))
            queue.append(j)

reachable=[i for i,p in enumerate(parent) if p is not None]
if len(reachable)!=k:
    raise SystemExit(f"SOURCE_BLOCKED: directed source graph reaches {len(reachable)}/{k} nodes from root {root}")

# Propagate absolute root-relative frames. F_i maps root landmark labels -> image-i labels.
frames=np.zeros((k,m,m),dtype=np.int8)
frames[root]=np.eye(m,dtype=np.int8)
for i,j in tree:
    Pji=valid_blocks[(i,j)]
    frames[j]=(Pji @ frames[i]).astype(np.int8)
    if permutation_block(frames[j]) is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"INTEGRITY_FAIL: propagated frame {j} is not permutation")

# Source-only non-tree cycle diagnostics.
tree_set=set(tree)
cycles=[]
for (i,j),Pji in sorted(valid_blocks.items()):
    if (i,j) in tree_set:
        continue
    # Root-frame cycle residual: F_j^T P_ji F_i, identity if consistent.
    C=(frames[j].T @ Pji @ frames[i]).astype(np.int8)
    Pc=permutation_block(C)
    if Pc is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"INTEGRITY_FAIL: cycle residual ({i},{j}) not permutation")
    h=perm_hamming_from_identity(Pc)
    cycles.append({"i":i,"j":j,"hamming_count":h,"hamming_fraction":h/m})

npz=out/"SOURCE_ONLY_FRAMES.npz"
np.savez_compressed(npz, frames=frames)

tree_json=out/"SOURCE_ONLY_GRAPH_TREE.json"
tree_obj={
  "artifact":"CMU_HOUSE_SOURCE_ONLY_GRAPH_TREE",
  "source_file":src.name,
  "source_sha256":sha(src),
  "m":m,"k":k,
  "root":root,
  "directed_valid_edge_count":len(valid_blocks),
  "tree_edge_count":len(tree),
  "tree_edges":[list(x) for x in tree],
  "construction":"minimum-index root; numerically sorted neighbors; lexicographic BFS",
  "target_used":False,
  "physical_promotion":0
}
tree_json.write_text(json.dumps(tree_obj,indent=2,sort_keys=True))

cycle_json=out/"SOURCE_ONLY_CYCLE_DIAGNOSTICS.json"
cycle_obj={
 "artifact":"CMU_HOUSE_SOURCE_ONLY_CYCLE_DIAGNOSTICS",
 "non_tree_directed_edge_count":len(cycles),
 "identity_cycle_count":sum(c["hamming_count"]==0 for c in cycles),
 "mean_hamming_fraction":float(np.mean([c["hamming_fraction"] for c in cycles])) if cycles else 0.0,
 "max_hamming_fraction":float(np.max([c["hamming_fraction"] for c in cycles])) if cycles else 0.0,
 "cycles":cycles,
 "target_used":False,
 "physical_promotion":0
}
cycle_json.write_text(json.dumps(cycle_obj,indent=2,sort_keys=True))

freeze=out/"SOURCE_ONLY_PREDICTION_FREEZE.json"
freeze_obj={
 "artifact":"CMU_HOUSE_SOURCE_ONLY_PREDICTION_FREEZE",
 "status":"PREDICTIONS_FROZEN_TARGET_NOT_USED",
 "source_sha256":sha(src),
 "graph_tree_sha256":sha(tree_json),
 "frames_sha256":sha(npz),
 "cycle_diagnostics_sha256":sha(cycle_json),
 "frame_definition":"F_i maps root landmark labels to image-i labels",
 "edge_convention":"Wnoise block(i,j) = P_ji; F_j=P_ji F_i",
 "root_rule":"minimum index",
 "tree_rule":"lexicographic BFS",
 "target_used":False,
 "physical_promotion":0
}
freeze.write_text(json.dumps(freeze_obj,indent=2,sort_keys=True))
print(json.dumps({k:freeze_obj[k] for k in ["status","source_sha256","frames_sha256"]},indent=2))

title: TTRTS Temporal Triplet Adapter
note: Frozen reference code · v0.1 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content:
Transforms the declared alternate time-trace source into the temporal triplet carrier required for preregistered replay. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Target-blind TTRTS adapter for already-digitized RTS bits.

Raw-current classification is intentionally separate because D1488 archive bytes were not
materialized in this runtime. This module starts after calibration-only thresholding and
resampling have produced one ordered bit stream per native held-out run.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def temporal_triplets(bits, run_id):
    bits=np.asarray(bits,dtype=int)
    if not np.isin(bits,[0,1]).all():
        raise ValueError("non-binary source bit")
    nB=len(bits)//3
    if nB<2:
        raise ValueError("insufficient triplets")
    B=bits[:3*nB].reshape(nB,3)
    A=B[:-1]^B[1:]
    Bout=B[1:]
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "run_id":run_id,
        "event_id":np.arange(1,nB),
        "A1":A[:,0],"A2":A[:,1],"A3":A[:,2],
        "B1":Bout[:,0],"B2":Bout[:,1],"B3":Bout[:,2],
        "physical_source_status":"CAPTURED"
    })

def resample_binary(native_bits, q, phase=0):
    if q < 1:
        raise ValueError("q must be positive")
    if phase != 0:
        raise ValueError("v0.1 freezes phase=0")
    return np.asarray(native_bits,dtype=int)[phase::q]

if __name__=="__main__":
    # Deterministic example only.
    b=np.array([0,1,1, 1,1,0, 1,0,0, 0,0,1])
    print(temporal_triplets(b,"example").to_csv(index=False))

The paper reports nine time-domain RTS measurements acquired at one fixed bias condition. Each run contains 100001 \boxed{100001} samples at native sampling interval tint=24ms, \boxed{t_{\mathrm int}=24~{\mathrm ms}}, for total duration 100001×24ms=2400.024s 100001\times24~{\mathrm ms} = 2400.024~{\mathrm s} per run. The article reports approximately 2400 s and uses a 20 s hold between measurements, longer than the typical RTS lifetime, to suppress inter-run autocorrelation. Seven runs are used for classifier/training extraction and two are reserved as test runs in the published analysis. The supporting D1488 data are stated by the authors to be openly available in the University of Southampton repository. 2. Physical source The measured RTS is not a software-loaded bit pattern. The device is a silicon single-electron-pump / quantum-dot structure in which discrete current states arise from stochastic trapping and detrapping of an electron. The publication explicitly describes RTS as an unpredictable/stochastic physical process and observes average state lifetimes of order one second. For the RNG experiment, the high-current state is mapped to digital 1 and the lower current state(s) to digital 0 using a classifier derived from separate training measurements. Thus D1488 has a stronger natural-source provenance than pulse-programmed qubit datasets. 3. Temporal-seat construction TTRTS does not pretend that one physical trap contains three simultaneous spatial coordinates. Instead, after calibration-only digitization and resampling, let br,k∈{0,1} b_{r,k}\in\{0,1\} be the physical RTS bit at resampled index kk in held-out run rr. Form non-overlapping three-seat physical state records Br,n=(br,3n,br,3n+1,br,3n+2). \boxed{ B_{r,n} = (b_{r,3n},b_{r,3n+1},b_{r,3n+2}). } Define the transition receipt Ar,n=Br,n−1⊕Br,n,n≥1. \boxed{ A_{r,n} = B_{r,n-1}\oplus B_{r,n}, \qquad n\ge1. } Therefore each scored event produces exactly the same typed data format needed by the source correspondence lane: BB: three-bit state; AA: three-bit transition receipt. The physical coordinates are typed as: temporal seats (0,1,2), \boxed{ \text{temporal seats }(0,1,2), } not spatial dots, not tetrahedral matching classes, and not independently existing particles. 4. Calibration-only digitization Use only the seven preregistered calibration runs: D1,…,D7. D1,\dots,D7. Freeze from those runs: current-state classifier / threshold; accepted current range; typical high/low state lifetimes; resampling stride qq; temporal guard for the later correspondence null. The published procedure defines a typical RTS lifetime τ=max(τHigh,τLow) \tau=\max(\tau_{\mathrm High},\tau_{\mathrm Low}) and a resampling time T=2τ T=2\tau to reduce autocorrelation. The candidate adapter mirrors this source-side rule. With native 24 ms sampling, freeze q=max(1,⌊T/tint⌋) \boxed{ q=\max\left(1,\left\lfloor T/t_{\mathrm int}\right\rfloor\right) } from calibration only. Use one fixed sampling phase: k0=0. \boxed{k_0=0.} The paper explored multiple possible initial resampling offsets for RNG analysis; TTRTS deliberately does not search over offsets because selecting the best phase after comparison would be a hidden fit. 5. Held-out corpus Freeze: D1–D7: calibration only; D8–D9: held-out physical source only. The numerical labels are the partition rule. No trace is selected because of its agreement with UD. For each held-out run: apply the frozen classifier; resample at stride qq from phase zero; form non-overlapping triplets BB; form transition receipts AA; retain the native run boundary. No event is moved across D8/D9. 6. Data-volume feasibility The paper reports that the training-derived resampling ratio was approximately T/tint∼55. T/t_{\mathrm int}\sim55. If the frozen calibration returns q=55q=55, one 100001-point run gives ⌊10000055⌋+1=1819 \left\lfloor\frac{100000}{55}\right\rfloor+1 = 1819 resampled physical bits. This yields ⌊18193⌋=606 \left\lfloor\frac{1819}{3}\right\rfloor = 606 three-seat state records and therefore 605 \boxed{605} state/transition events per held-out run. Two held-out runs would then provide 1210 \boxed{1210} physical TTRTS events before any additional quality exclusions. This calculation is a corpus-feasibility estimate based on the reported approximate resampling ratio. The actual qq must be recalculated from the raw calibration files and frozen before held-out scoring. 7. Block-preserving temporal null Because D8 and D9 are separate physical acquisitions with a 20 s hold between them, the candidate correspondence test must preserve run boundaries. For held-out blocks r∈{8,9}r\in\{8,9\}, let allowed circular shifts be 𝒟r={d:1≤d<Nr,min(d,Nr−d)>Gr}, \mathcal D_r = \{d:1\le d<N_r,\ \min(d,N_r-d)>G_r\}, with GrG_r frozen from calibration. For each pair (d8,d9)∈𝒟8×𝒟9, (d_8,d_9)\in\mathcal D_8\times\mathcal D_9, shift each physical block only inside itself, sum the two block statistics, and compare with the unshifted two-block score. This gives an exact product-shift temporal null while preserving: each run’s physical sequence; each run’s UD sequence; within-run temporal structure; the acquisition boundary. No circular shift is allowed across D8/D9. 8. Address-level null The existing shell-conditioned address null remains mandatory. Within each held-out run and each physical shell pair (wH(A),wH(B)), (w_H(A),w_H(B)), randomize complete physical six-bit records only among events in the same shell-pair stratum. Thus Hamming-level agreement cannot masquerade as coordinate-address correspondence. 9. Critical representation limitation TTRTS is a weaker physical ontology than ST3S. ST3S has three simultaneous spatial sites and admits a natural candidate for physical coordinate permutation. TTRTS has three time seats produced by one stochastic physical source. Therefore: TTRTS temporal-seat permutation≠physical S3 spatial symmetry. \boxed{ \text{TTRTS temporal-seat permutation} \neq \text{physical }S_3\text{ spatial symmetry}. } At most, stationarity and successful randomness/decorrelation tests can support an empirical seat exchangeability approximation. They cannot establish an exact physical identity with the three UD matching coordinates. This limitation is not repaired by a statistically significant correspondence score. 10. Candidate hierarchy Rank 1 — D1488 TTRTS-SEP Strengths - open data; - nine long raw time-domain measurements; - known native sample interval and run length; - natural stochastic single-electron physics; - calibration/test structure already documented; - enough apparent data volume for a frozen held-out source test. Weakness - three coordinates are temporal seats rather than spatial source sites. Disposition BRIGHTEST OPEN-RAW ALTERNATE / CANDIDATE-B SOURCE ONTOLOGY. Rank 2 — D1193 single-dopant RTS Open 21 MB dataset from a low-temperature MOSFET where RTS is attributed to trapping/detrapping at a solitary donor. This has even cleaner single-defect source semantics, but the public search result does not expose enough file-level temporal structure to certify the v0.1 data-volume/adapter contract without opening the archive. Disposition SOURCE-PURITY LEADER / FILE-SEMANTICS INSPECTION REQUIRED. Rank 3 — D1378 thesis archive Open thesis-support archive containing published and unpublished RTS data. This may contain additional useful natural event streams but requires archive inspection before a specific replay lane can be frozen. Disposition OPEN ARCHIVE RESERVE. 11. Runtime source status The Southampton repository records are openly licensed and downloadable, but the repository page returned HTTP 403 to this runtime when opened directly. Therefore: PUBLIC SOURCE CONFIRMED \boxed{ \text{PUBLIC SOURCE CONFIRMED} } but RAW BYTES NOT MATERIALIZED / NOT SCORED. \boxed{ \text{RAW BYTES NOT MATERIALIZED / NOT SCORED}. } No empirical TTRTS/UD correspondence result is claimed in this release. 12. Scientific disposition EXACT - temporal-triplet state/transition transform; - event-count arithmetic conditional on qq; - block-preserving null construction. EMPIRICAL - D1488 contains long natural RTS time-domain measurements and is publicly deposited; - D1193 is an open single-dopant RTS dataset. CANDIDATE - TTRTS temporal-seat physical source representation. NO-GO - temporal seats retyped as exact spatial S3S_3 coordinates; - resampling phase optimized after UD comparison; - author RNG output substituted for source-side raw calibration without provenance audit. SOURCE-BLOCKED IN CURRENT RUNTIME - raw D1488/D1193 bytes not materialized. PHYSICAL PROMOTION := 0.

note: Pretarget frozen · v0.1A · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Freezes the physical and UD lanes, provenance gates, primary statistics, temporal and address nulls, familywise threshold, verdict, and anti-repair rules. ST3S First Target-Blind Physical Correspondence Experiment v0.1A Status: FROZEN PRE-DATA PROTOCOL / REPAIRED BEFORE EMPIRICAL USE Scope: source-register correspondence only Physical promotion: 0 1. Physical and UD lanes Physical ST3S receipts: Bnphys=xn+,Anphys=xn−⊕xn+. B_n^{phys}=x_n^+, \qquad A_n^{phys}=x_n^-\oplus x_n^+. Independent UD receipts: (anUD,θnUD). (a_n^{UD},\theta_n^{UD}). Primary object: (Anphys,Bnphys)=?(anUD,θnUD). (A_n^{phys},B_n^{phys}) \stackrel{?}{=} (a_n^{UD},\theta_n^{UD}). No CBCR, CTPER, worldline, charge target or anyon phase enters the score. 2. Hard provenance gates All must pass: physical source is naturally generated and not loaded from UD; UD receipts are source-complete and generated independently; coordinate map is frozen before scoring; first experiment is identity-frame only; physical source receipt is captured before downstream logic; one stable acquisition block is preregistered from calibration; circular-shift guard GG is frozen from calibration; unresolved UD events are never repaired with nearest states. Any violation returns ST3S_PROTOCOL_INVALID. If the stable-block/exchangeability condition cannot be supported, return NULL_EXCHANGEABILITY_BLOCKED. 3. Primary statistics SAB=∑n𝟏[An=an∧Bn=θn], S_{AB} = \sum_n \mathbf1[A_n=a_n\land B_n=\theta_n], SA=∑n𝟏[An=an],SB=∑n𝟏[Bn=θn]. S_A=\sum_n\mathbf1[A_n=a_n], \qquad S_B=\sum_n\mathbf1[B_n=\theta_n]. All comparisons are full-vector address comparisons. Hamming agreement is diagnostic only. 4. Null T — circular temporal shift Allowed shifts: 𝒟={d∈{1,…,N−1}:min(d,N−d)>G}. \mathcal D = \{d\in\{1,\ldots,N-1\}:\min(d,N-d)>G\}. Shift the complete physical six-bit series by each dd relative to the UD series. For each score SS, pT(S)=1+#{d:S(d)≥Sobs}1+|𝒟|. p_T(S) = \frac{1+\#\{d:S^{(d)}\ge S^{obs}\}} {1+|\mathcal D|}. This preserves each lane’s complete sequence, empirical state frequencies and internal autocorrelation. Require |𝒟|+1≥600. |\mathcal D|+1\ge600. 5. Null A — shell-conditioned address randomization For every physical event define the shell pair hn=(wH(Anphys),wH(Bnphys)). h_n= (w_H(A_n^{phys}),w_H(B_n^{phys})). Within each of the sixteen possible shell-pair strata, randomly permute the complete physical six-bit records among only those events in the same stratum. Thus for every event the null preserves exactly (wH(Anphys),wH(Bnphys)) \boxed{ (w_H(A_n^{phys}),w_H(B_n^{phys})) } while destroying any privileged coordinate address. Use exactly 9999 \boxed{9999} conditional randomization replicates and fixed preregistered RNG seed 20260910. \boxed{20260910}. For each score: pH(S)=1+#{b:S(b)≥Sobs}10000. p_H(S) = \frac{1+\#\{b:S^{(b)}\ge S^{obs}\}} {10000}. This null tests whether address-level agreement exceeds what is explained by shell-level correspondence alone. 6. Familywise threshold There are six required p-values: pT(SAB),pT(SA),pT(SB),pH(SAB),pH(SA),pH(SB). p_T(S_{AB}),p_T(S_A),p_T(S_B), p_H(S_{AB}),p_H(S_A),p_H(S_B). Freeze αFWER=1100. \alpha_{\mathrm FWER}=\frac1{100}. Bonferroni allocation: α*=1600. \boxed{ \alpha_*=\frac1{600}. } Strict PASS requires all six p-values to satisfy p≤1/600. \boxed{p\le1/600}. 7. Verdict ST3S_CORRESPONDENCE_PASS all hard gates and all six statistical gates pass. ST3S_SHELL_ONLY temporal evidence exists but shell-conditioned address evidence fails. ST3S_NO_CORRESPONDENCE strict conjunction fails without protocol invalidity. ST3S_PROTOCOL_INVALID provenance/timing/source-map rules fail. NULL_EXCHANGEABILITY_BLOCKED time-shift null cannot be scientifically justified from pre-held-out calibration. 8. Frozen anti-repair After held-out exposure do not alter: source thresholds; sampling interval; event alignment; coordinate map; guard GG; UD predictor; unresolved-event rule; primary scores; either null model; 9999 replicate count; seed; 1/6001/600 threshold. A failure is a valid scientific outcome. 9. Claim boundary PASS would establish a held-out correspondence for the declared source-register lane only. Physical promotion remains 0 until the other independent bridge requirements close.

title: ST3S Public-Corpus Availability Boundary
note: Source contract unmet in scoped search · v0.1 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: No located public corpus satisfies all frozen requirements; the result narrows acquisition to specific author-held traces and forbids substitution of static or programmed-sequence data. Public Raw Corpus Search for a Genuine ST3S v0.1A Replay — NO-GO v0.1 Date: 2026-09-10 Status: PUBLIC_CORPUS SOURCE-AVAILABILITY NO-GO Scope: searched public literature/repositories; not a universal nonexistence claim Physical promotion: 0 Result No openly accessible corpus found in the scoped search satisfies all frozen requirements of the ST3S v0.1A correspondence protocol. A legitimate replay requires a natural, ordered, time-resolved three-coordinate charge source from which both Bnphys=xn+ B_n^{phys}=x_n^+ and Anphys=xn−⊕xn+ A_n^{phys}=x_n^-\oplus x_n^+ can be reconstructed independently of UD. The source also needs enough held-out events to execute the frozen circular-shift null. If the calibration-frozen guard is GG, the number of allowed null shifts is N−1−2G N-1-2G for N>2G+1N>2G+1. Including the observed alignment, the v0.1A resolution requirement is N−2G≥600. \boxed{N-2G\ge600}. Static stability diagrams, figure-averaged source data, request-only datasets, and deliberately programmed charge sequences do not satisfy this contract. Strongest near-miss 1 — Ansaloni et al. 2020 The silicon triple-dot experiment contains unusually relevant instrumentation: single-electron triple-dot configurations; real-time/single-shot charge sensing; digitized sensor signal at 500 kS/s; controlled tunneling and electron-shuttling sequences. However the publication states that the datasets are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request rather than through a public raw-data archive. It also uses deliberately controlled pulse sequences. This is excellent instrumentation precedent, but it is not an immediately executable natural-source ST3S corpus. Disposition: REQUESTABLE / NOT PUBLIC / CONTROLLED-SOURCE NEAR-MISS. Strongest near-miss 2 — Broome et al. 2016 This is the closest source semantically. The experiment uses real-time charge sensing to map non-equilibrium tunneling paths through a triple quantum dot. That is much closer to the natural-source requirement than a programmed qubit sequence. The scoped search found the publication/preprint but did not locate an openly downloadable raw time-trace repository containing the event-addressable three-coordinate data required for v0.1A. Disposition: BEST NATURAL-SOURCE NEAR-MISS / PUBLIC RAW SOURCE NOT FOUND. Strongest openly downloadable near-miss — Qubyte / Volk et al. 2019 The Qubyte release on Zenodo is open and substantial, approximately 238.6 MB, with analysis scripts and figure-organized data. It therefore passes the public-access test. It fails the ST3S data semantics: the released material is primarily tuning/stability/figure data for a multi-dot register and does not supply the required naturally evolving three-coordinate pre/post event stream. Disposition: PUBLIC / RAW-ENOUGH FOR ORIGINAL PAPER / WRONG DATA SEMANTICS. Modern open triangular hardware near-miss — Broz et al. 2026 A public Figshare dataset accompanies a triangular triple-dot exchange-only qubit experiment. This is useful evidence that modern triangular triple-dot data can be released publicly. But its physical source is intentionally pulse-controlled spin-qubit operation. It does not provide the independent stochastic pre-event source required by ST3S G0. Disposition: PUBLIC / TRIANGULAR / CONTROLLED-SOURCE NO-GO. Open six-dot near-miss — Mądzik et al. 2025 The associated Zenodo release supplies raw data/analysis for two exchange-only qubits in a six-dot device. This is excellent multi-dot hardware and open-data precedent, but again the records arise from deliberate qubit pulse sequences rather than natural stochastic three-site charge evolution. Disposition: PUBLIC / SIX-DOT HARDWARE PRECEDENT / WRONG SOURCE ONTOLOGY. Eight-state near-miss — Li et al. 2023 This experiment establishes that all eight relative binary charge configurations of an InAs triple dot can be resolved. That is directly relevant to the required 232^3 support. The publication’s data availability statement makes the data requestable from the corresponding author rather than openly downloadable. No qualifying natural event stream is publicly available from the paper. Disposition: FULL STATE-SPACE PRECEDENT / REQUEST-ONLY / NOT REPLAYABLE NOW. Static public datasets Other public quantum-dot source-data packages, including Fermi-Hubbard source data and NIST stability-diagram datasets, are useful for device characterization or state classification. They do not contain the ordered natural three-coordinate event stream required by the v0.1A temporal/null protocol. Disposition: PUBLIC / STATIC / ST3S NO-GO. Scientific disposition EMPIRICAL: real-time triple-dot charge sensing and all-eight-state charge discrimination both exist in published experiments. EMPIRICAL: open multi-dot datasets exist. NO-GO: no located open corpus simultaneously provides public raw access, natural time-resolved triple-dot charge evolution, three-coordinate pre/post reconstructability, and sufficient event metadata for the frozen v0.1A null. OPEN: privately/requestably held raw traces may satisfy the contract; this search did not inspect unreleased laboratory archives. PHYSICAL PROMOTION := 0. Next acquisition hierarchy Broome/Gorman lineage — request the complete native real-time triple-dot trace block and sensor calibration because its source semantics are closest. Ansaloni/Kuemmeth lineage — request complete 500 kS/s raw sensor streams plus all gate-pulse metadata; evaluate whether any unbiased dwell/tunneling blocks exist before programmed shuttling. Li et al. 2023 — request raw time-series/sensor data, if any, behind the all-eight-state characterization. Do not use Qubyte/Broz/Mądzik as the primary source replay; retain them as method/hardware controls only.

H_s=P_{H,s}S_s. For the measured full incidence vector y, the split reconstruction and held-out prediction are ĵG(s)=SsPT,sy,ĵH(s)=HsPT,sy. \widehat j_G^{(s)}=S_sP_{T,s}y, \qquad \widehat j_H^{(s)}=H_sP_{T,s}y. No held-out measurement is used to construct either prediction. 5. Full correlated covariance handling The acquisition must supply one joint covariance ΣG∈ℝ28×28,ΣG≽0, \Sigma_G\in\mathbb R^{28\times28},\qquad \Sigma_G\succeq0, for the ordered 28-current estimator. This is required because an incidence can be training for one split and held out for the other; treating the two split errors as independent would generally be wrong. For split s, define the held-out residual operator As=PH,s−HsPT,s. A_s=P_{H,s}-H_sP_{T,s}. Then rs=Asy,Σrs=AsΣGAs⊤. r_s=A_sy, \qquad \Sigma_{r_s}=A_s\Sigma_GA_s^\top. The two full reconstructions are compared with d=ĵG(P)−ĵG(R2)=Cy, d=\widehat j_G^{(P)}-\widehat j_G^{(R2)} =C y, where C=SPPT,P−SR2PT,R2, C=S_PP_{T,P}-S_{R2}P_{T,R2}, and therefore Σd=CΣGC⊤. \Sigma_d=C\Sigma_GC^\top. These are exact linear covariance pushforwards. No physical covariance entries are invented by the protocol. 6. Deterministic covariance-support gate For each residual/cross vector x with covariance Sigma_x, the scorer first checks that x lies in the numerical support of Sigma_x. A nonzero component in a declared zero-variance direction is a fail-closed covariance/support inconsistency. The eigenvalue/pseudoinverse rank cutoff is 1e-12 relative to the largest covariance eigenvalue and the null-support numerical tolerance is 1e-10; both are PROTOCOL_CONTROL values only. 7. Conditional Gaussian score Only when the acquisition declares error_model = MULTIVARIATE_NORMAL, define Qx=x⊤Σx+x,νx=rank(Σx), Q_x=x^\top\Sigma_x^+x, \qquad \nu_x=\operatorname{rank}(\Sigma_x), and the upper-tail p-value px=P(χνx2≥Qx). p_x=P(\chi^2_{\nu_x}\ge Q_x). Three formal gates are frozen: primary held-out residual; R2 held-out residual; primary-vs-R2 full-reconstruction difference. The family-wise protocol control is αFWER=1100. \alpha_{\mathrm FWER}=\frac1{100}. Bonferroni over the three formal tests gives the predeclared per-test gate αgate=1300. \boxed{\alpha_{\mathrm gate}=\frac1{300}}. This threshold is a methods control, not a theory coefficient or physical constant. 8. Verdict grammar DUAL_REPLICATION_PASS iff: authenticated same-carrier acquisition gate passes; exact primary binding passes; R2 identity passes; covariance is finite, symmetric, and PSD; covariance-support gates pass; Gaussian error model is declared; all three formal p-values satisfy p >= 1/300. DUAL_REPLICATION_FAIL iff all source/integrity gates pass but at least one of the three formal p-values is < 1/300. A PASS by one split never rescues a FAIL by the other. SOURCE_BLOCKED iff the primary source receipt or authenticated acquisition is absent/invalid. NO_PROBABILISTIC_VERDICT iff valid covariance is supplied but the acquisition does not declare the frozen Gaussian error model. Covariance-normalized diagnostics may still be reported, but no PASS/FAIL is issued. 9. R2 exact implementation falsifier The R2 predicted held-out vector must obey the already frozen exact relation −Jv2−e12+Jv2−e23−Je12−f123+Je23−f123=0. -J_{v2-e12}+J_{v2-e23}-J_{e12-f123}+J_{e23-f123}=0. Failure of the scorer to reproduce this from the R2 prediction is an implementation failure, not an experimental failure. 10. Independence language The two splits are independently generated topological partitions, but they need not be statistically independent because the same physical acquisition can place a given incidence in different roles. The joint 28×28 covariance is therefore mandatory for the formal dual-split score. 11. Freeze rule After target acquisition/release begins, do not change the primary manifest, R2 split, covariance equations, error-model declaration rule, alpha controls, test count, metric, subgroup, or verdict grammar. A parser/schema repair is lawful only before scoring and only if it does not alter the scientific rule. 12. Current execution state The scoring protocol, R2 source, schemas, two independent scorer implementations, and synthetic verification are frozen now. The exact primary split manifest remains an OPEN SOURCE GATE. This is not repaired by selecting another tree with the same path spectrum.

Cross-chord covariance is Cov(zh,zk)=ch𝖳ΣTck. \boxed{\operatorname{Cov}(z_h,z_k)=c_h^\mathsf T\Sigma_Tc_k}. title: Empirical Joint Source-Event Preregistration
note: Frozen scorer protocol · v0.2 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Pre-unblinding 24-run PLB1/HCB1 comparison with fixed uncertainty, chi-square, and AICc decision gates. Empirical/Noisy Joint Source-Event Preregistration v0.2 Frozen before hardware endpoint unblinding. Primary dataset: exactly 24 valid runs, six balanced blocks, 12 E0 and 12 E1. Mandatory gates: channel independence confirmed; custody frozen; calibration in control for every primary run; native winding-source uniformity/source-purity PASS; uncertainty model declared complete; same burden units across all runs; same leakage units across all runs; exactly two E0 and two E1 events in every block. Models: PLB1:ε=κPΛ,HCB1:ε=κHd, \mathrm{PLB1}:\ \varepsilon=\kappa_P\Lambda, \qquad \mathrm{HCB1}:\ \varepsilon=\kappa_Hd, where d=1/4d=1/4 for E0 and 3/43/4 for E1. Both models fit one through-origin coefficient. No intercept, nonlinear term, extra scatter parameter or post-exposure event filtering is permitted. Absolute fit: chi-square survival probability >= 0.01 with 23 degrees of freedom. Strong relative evidence: |Delta AICc| >= 10. Verdicts are frozen exactly as implemented in empirical_joint_source_event_scorer_v0.2.py. Invalid instrument/receipt runs remain archived and are replaced append-only under the existing runbook; no outcome-based invalidation is permitted. Physical promotion remains 0.

title: Empirical Joint Source-Event Scorer Theorem
note: Scoped empirical scorer · v0.2 · Searchable source text imported; claim status is not re-adjudicated.
content: Formalizes the one-parameter through-origin fits, absolute adequacy gate, strong-selection gate, and non-promotion boundary. UD Empirical Joint Source-Event Scorer v0.2 — Frozen Theorem and Decision Rule Status: FROZEN PRE-HARDWARE-UNBLIND / NO HARDWARE ENDPOINTS SCORED Primary dataset: six balanced blocks, exactly 12 valid E0E_0 and 12 valid E1E_1 events Models: PLB1 vs HCB1 Physical promotion: 0 1. Inputs For each valid unblinded run ii, the scorer consumes independently returned: εi,uε,i,Λi,uΛ,i,cov(εi,Λi), \varepsilon_i,\quad u_{\varepsilon,i},\quad \Lambda_i,\quad u_{\Lambda,i},\quad \operatorname{cov}(\varepsilon_i,\Lambda_i), plus event label E0E_0 or E1E_1, block index, custody/calibration/source-purity gates and units. No empirical tolerance is chosen after outcome exposure. 2. Frozen sample gate The primary score requires exactly N0=N1=12 \boxed{N_0=N_1=12} valid events arranged as six blocks with exactly two valid E0E_0 and two valid E1E_1 events per block. Preregistered invalid hardware/receipt runs are retained in the archive and replaced append-only until the primary balanced set is complete. 3. PLB1 empirical model εi=κPΛi. \boxed{\varepsilon_i=\kappa_P\Lambda_i.} For a proposed κP\kappa_P, the propagated residual variance is vP,i(κP)=uε,i2+κP2uΛ,i2−2κPcov(εi,Λi). \boxed{ v_{P,i}(\kappa_P)= u_{\varepsilon,i}^2+ \kappa_P^2u_{\Lambda,i}^2- 2\kappa_P\operatorname{cov}(\varepsilon_i,\Lambda_i). } The channel covariance must be supplied explicitly. Interface-level independence normally implies zero covariance, but the scorer never silently inserts zero. The fitted κ̂P\hat\kappa_P minimizes the Gaussian negative log-likelihood ℒP(κP)=12∑i[log(2πvP,i)+(εi−κPΛi)2vP,i]. \mathcal L_P(\kappa_P)= \frac12\sum_i\left[ \log(2\pi v_{P,i})+ \frac{(\varepsilon_i-\kappa_P\Lambda_i)^2}{v_{P,i}} \right]. No intercept and no extra between-run noise parameter are fitted. 4. HCB1 empirical model Define the exact structural predictor di={1/4,E0,3/4,E1. d_i=\begin{cases} 1/4,&E_0,\\ 3/4,&E_1. \end{cases} HCB1 is εi=κHdi. \boxed{\varepsilon_i=\kappa_H d_i.} with vH,i=uε,i2. v_{H,i}=u_{\varepsilon,i}^2. The through-origin weighted estimate is κ̂H=∑idiεi/uε,i2∑idi2/uε,i2. \boxed{ \hat\kappa_H= \frac{\sum_i d_i\varepsilon_i/u_{\varepsilon,i}^2} {\sum_i d_i^2/u_{\varepsilon,i}^2}. } No intercept or extra noise term is allowed. 5. Absolute goodness-of-fit gate For either model MM, define χM2=∑irM,i2vM,i. \chi_M^2=\sum_i\frac{r_{M,i}^2}{v_{M,i}}. Each model has one fitted parameter, so ν=24−1=23. \nu=24-1=23. The frozen absolute-fit rule is pM=P(χ232≥χM2)≥0.01. \boxed{p_M=P(\chi^2_{23}\ge\chi_M^2)\ge0.01.} The 0.010.01 level is a protocol-control false-rejection guard, not a physical constant. 6. Relative model preference For k=1k=1 fitted parameter and n=24n=24, AICcM=2ℒM+2k+2k(k+1)n−k−1. \mathrm{AICc}_M= 2\mathcal L_M+2k+ \frac{2k(k+1)}{n-k-1}. Define ΔAICc=AICcP−AICcH. \boxed{\Delta\mathrm{AICc}=\mathrm{AICc}_P-\mathrm{AICc}_H.} Frozen strong-preference threshold: |ΔAICc|≥10. \boxed{|\Delta\mathrm{AICc}|\ge10.} Positive values favor HCB1; negative values favor PLB1. 7. Verdicts HCB1_PASS_EMPIRICAL_SCOPED Require pH≥0.01,ΔAICc≥10. p_H\ge0.01, \qquad \Delta\mathrm{AICc}\ge10. PLB1_PASS_EMPIRICAL_SCOPED Require pP≥0.01,ΔAICc≤−10. p_P\ge0.01, \qquad \Delta\mathrm{AICc}\le-10. NEITHER_SIMPLE_BRIDGE If pP<0.01andpH<0.01. p_P<0.01 \quad\text{and}\quad p_H<0.01. EMPIRICAL_INDETERMINATE All remaining source-complete cases, including weak relative preference, both models fitting adequately, or one model failing without strong evidence for the other. No coefficient retuning, intercept insertion, extra-scatter fit, event deletion or threshold repair is allowed after endpoint exposure. 8. Diagnostics The scorer additionally reports: weighted class means of ε\varepsilon and Λ\Lambda; empirical class burden ratio RB=ε‾1/ε‾0R_B=\bar\varepsilon_1/\bar\varepsilon_0 when defined; leakage class ratio RΛR_\Lambda; leakage-stationarity z statistic; exact v0.1-equivalent residuals evaluated on weighted class means; standardized residuals per run. These diagnostics do not change the frozen verdict logic. 9. title: Native C4 Phase-Slip Simulator

Runnable simulator source supporting the synthetic receipt validation. Code execution is not physical evidence. #!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, hashlib, importlib.util, sys
from pathlib import Path
from fractions import Fraction

B=[
    [Fraction(-1),0,0,Fraction(1)],
    [Fraction(1),Fraction(-1),0,0],
    [0,Fraction(1),Fraction(-1),0],
    [0,0,Fraction(1),Fraction(-1)]
]

def F(x):
    if isinstance(x,int): return Fraction(x,1)
    if isinstance(x,str): return Fraction(x)
    if isinstance(x,Fraction): return x
    raise TypeError("exact rational required")

def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def vec(xs,n=4):
    out=[F(x) for x in xs]
    if len(out)!=n: raise ValueError("vector length mismatch")
    return out

def mv(M,v):
    return [sum(M[i][j]*v[j] for j in range(len(v))) for i in range(len(M))]

def add(*vs):
    return [sum(v[i] for v in vs) for i in range(4)]

def load_plugin(path):
    spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("source_plugin",path)
    mod=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod

def run_event(cfg):
    if int(cfg["n_after"])-int(cfg["n_before"]) != 1:
        raise ValueError("only primitive +1 event supported")
    rho0=vec(cfg["rho_before"])
    flux=vec(cfg["integrated_edge_burden_flux"])
    other=vec(cfg["tagged_nonwinding_source"])
    plugin_path=Path(cfg["source_plugin"])
    plugin=load_plugin(plugin_path)

    native_event={
        "event_id":cfg["event_id"],
        "n_before":int(cfg["n_before"]),
        "n_after":int(cfg["n_after"]),
        "carrier":"C4",
        "closure_shell":1,
        "framing":"odd"
    }
    epsilon=F(plugin.source_amplitude(native_event))
    sw=[epsilon/4]*4
    internal=mv(B,flux)
    rho1=add(rho0,internal,other,sw)

    return {
        "event_id":cfg["event_id"],
        "n_before":cfg["n_before"],"n_after":cfg["n_after"],
        "rho_before":[str(x) for x in rho0],
        "rho_after":[str(x) for x in rho1],
        "incidence_matrix":[[str(x) for x in row] for row in B],
        "integrated_edge_burden_flux":[str(x) for x in flux],
        "tagged_nonwinding_source":[str(x) for x in other],
        "native_winding_source":[str(x) for x in sw],
        "epsilon":str(epsilon),
        "source_plugin_sha256":sha(plugin_path),
        "source_status":"SYNTHETIC_VALIDATION",
        "custody_frozen":True,
        "isolated_winding_source_complete":True,
        "nonwinding_source_status":"SOURCE_COMPLETE",
        "burden_units":"native_sim_burden",
        "burden_normalization_receipt":"native_sim_exact_unit"
    }

if __name__=="__main__":
    if len(sys.argv)!=3:
        raise SystemExit("usage: native_c4_phase_slip_simulator.py config.json output.json")
    cfg=json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
    Path(sys.argv[2]).write_text(json.dumps(run_event(cfg),indent=2))
