# Gibbs-flag receipt apparatus and its joint error state

2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Outcome and source qualification

An explicit candidate apparatus now supplies a joint receipt-error state, including a shared-error mechanism, instead of merely assuming an error distribution. Its unitary, flag Gibbs state, marginalization, joint moments and accuracy bounds are checked exactly.

This is a conditional apparatus derivation, not a native UD source closure. The supplied carrier_definition.md, coherence_equation.md and master_action.md are placeholders; ledger G05/G06 still do not supply an apparatus Hamiltonian, its thermal preparation, calibrated gaps or coupling law. Native face projector A=P_f anchors the signal. The flag state and controlled interactions below are newly declared physical candidates. G is unused.

## 1. Declare state, Hamiltonian and interaction

Hold the binary carrier observable A with the prior four-incidence coupling suspension. Let R=0 or 1 denote its held eigenlabel. Use three degenerate blank receipt bits S_1,S_2,S_3.

Supply one shared flag C and three private flags Z_i with Hamiltonian

\[
H_F=\Delta_c n_C+\Delta_p\sum_{i=1}^3 n_{Z_i}.
\]

At temperature T, declare the initially independent Gibbs flag state

\[
\tau_F=\tau_c\otimes\tau_p^{\otimes3},\quad
\tau_r=(1-r)|0\rangle\langle0|+r|1\rangle\langle1|,
\]

where

\[
c=\frac1{1+e^{\beta\Delta_c}},\qquad
p=\frac1{1+e^{\beta\Delta_p}},\quad\beta=1/(k_BT).
\]

For each receipt apply carrier-to-receipt CNOT, private-flag-to-receipt CNOT, and shared-flag-to-receipt CNOT. They commute during acquisition because they have unchanged controls and target bit flips. Their combined action is

\[
U|R,c,z,s\rangle
=|R,c,z,s\oplus R\mathbf1\oplus c\mathbf1\oplus z\rangle.
\]

The shared flag interacts with all three receipts; each private flag interacts only with its corresponding receipt. A product initial flag state therefore does not imply independent receipt errors. Correlation is generated by a shared control path.

The checker verifies the acquisition permutation and inverse on all source/flag/receipt basis states. With source held and receipt targets degenerate, these controlled operations commute with the free held-source-plus-flag Hamiltonian. Their ideal net free-energy expectation change is zero. Timing, target isolation, coupling switches, preparation and routing are additional controller resources.

The private/common flags model controlled perturbations of acquisition. They are an explicit realization of the declared noise channel; nothing here proves these perturbations are intrinsic to native UD or unavoidable in a physical recorder.

## 2. Derive the joint state

From blank receipts the recorded bits are

\[
S_i=R\oplus C\oplus Z_i,
\qquad E_i=S_i\oplus R=C\oplus Z_i.
\]

Tracing the flag registers gives, conditional on R,

\[
\rho_{S|R}=\sum_{e\in\{0,1\}^3}w_e
|R\mathbf1\oplus e\rangle\langle R\mathbf1\oplus e|,
\]

with k=sum_i e_i and

\[
\boxed{w_e=(1-c)p^k(1-p)^{3-k}
+c\,p^{3-k}(1-p)^k.}
\]

After carrier uncopies, the receipt error-state diagonal is the same w_e on |e>. Equivalently,

\[
\rho_E=(1-c)\tau_p^{\otimes3}
+c\,X^{\otimes3}\tau_p^{\otimes3}X^{\otimes3}.
\]

The eight probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one. This is the apparatus's derived joint error state under the declared Gibbs preparation and interactions. The symbolic form precedes choosing test probabilities.

## 3. Exact moments and majority

Write p_bar for each receipt marginal error, a for each pair joint error, b for the triple joint error. Direct marginalization gives

\[
\bar p=p+c(1-2p),\quad a=p^2+c(1-2p),
\]
\[
b=(1-c)p^3+c(1-p)^3.
\]

Thus the local flag probability p is not the receipt marginal p_bar when c is nonzero. The mean pair covariance is

\[
a-\bar p^2=c(1-c)(1-2p)^2\ge0.
\]

Using the exact majority identity,

\[
m=3a-2b=(3p^2-2p^3)+c[1-2(3p^2-2p^3)].
\]

The checker independently obtains these moments from the full flag-state sum and verifies the earlier sharp bounds

\[
\max(0,2a-\bar p)\le b\le\min(a,1-3\bar p+3a).
\]

In particular the shared perturbation creates a majority-error component that is not quadratically suppressed by independent private flags.

## 4. Decision flag state and final-error test

Supply four further independent Gibbs flag bits D_j with gap Delta_q and excitation q=1/(1+exp(beta Delta_q)). Couple them as target XOR controls after the three forward majority gates and the seed-copy gate. They give a parity fault

\[
u_4=\frac{1-(1-2q)^4}{2},
\quad p_{\rm seed}=m+u_4-2mu_4.
\]

The replay explicitly enumerates both the sixteen acquisition flag states and sixteen decision flag states to verify this effective error. Reverse cleanup and downstream fanout are ideal, and storage uses the previously specified fresh independent Gibbs stream.

For the prior 32-update ideal-seed storage error e0, final error is exactly

\[
e_{\rm final}=e_0+(1-2e_0)p_{\rm seed}.
\]

Test points p=1/100 and q=1/10000 are declared Gibbs excitation probabilities, not measured UD values. They correspond to beta Delta_p=ln99 and beta Delta_q=ln9999 within this candidate model. These gap assignments are test inputs, not canonical UD constants.

| Shared excitation c | Receipt pair joint error a | Exact final error | Exact model passes 1% | Broad robust gate passes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 0 | 1/10000 | 0.00992358 | yes | yes |
| 1/100000 | 549/5000000 | 0.00993338 | yes | yes |
| 1/20000 | 149/1000000 | 0.00997259 | yes | no |
| 1/10000 | 99/500000 | 0.01002160 | no | no |

Passing and failing comparisons are exact rational checks. A failed sufficient bound does not prove that the particular apparatus fails: the c=1/20000 row demonstrates this distinction. Its exact joint state contains triple coincidences which the broader bound conservatively discards.

## 5. Two different shared-error ceilings

Let s*=(1/100−e0)/(1−2e0). Without relying on decision independence, the sufficient gate 3a+4q<=s* gives

\[
c\le\frac{s_*-4q-3p^2}{3(1-2p)}
\approx2.567950424\times10^{-5}.
\]

For the fully specified independent decision flags, use the exact u4 and m. The exact passing region is

\[
c\le\frac{s_*-u_4-(1-2u_4)(3p^2-2p^3)}
{(1-2u_4)[1-2(3p^2-2p^3)]}
\approx7.796483800\times10^{-5}.
\]

Both are conditional source requirements, with exact fractions in results.json. The first offers a guarantee under a broader decision-error class; the second depends on the explicitly prepared product decision state. UD must select or bound actual flag gaps and interactions before either becomes a native prediction.

## 6. Energy, entropy, renewal and latency

The eight flag occupations are unchanged by their controlled-X interactions, so their marginal energies do not change. Receipt and decision targets are degenerate during those operations. Ideal net acquisition/decision heat and endpoint work are zero under the held-source control assumptions. Pure blank targets and the clock still supply resources.

For a fixed classical source label, receipt entropy grows from zero to H(w). The flags retain their original marginal entropy, while the combined unitary preserves total entropy. Receipt/flag correlations account for the local increase: I(receipts:flags|R)=H(w). Thus this explicit apparatus again shows that local record entropy need not equal heat divided by T. It does not close the horizon Clausius identification.

Blind workspace reset must use H(w), not 3h(p_bar). The output garbage also depends on decision flags. Their joint state and correlations determine any accessible-side-information reduction. The pure-blank reset protocol remains open; its free-energy bound is not a finite exact preparation recipe.

After use, matched-energy swaps with eight fresh Gibbs flag cells restore the required independent flag state, exporting correlations into the outgoing cells. These swaps need no net free-energy change of matched pairs. They require a fresh source and routing. A finite closed flag bank is not made cyclic by this export. Incoming energy inventory is Delta_c c+3 Delta_p p+4 Delta_q q, not extra dissipated work.

The apparatus also changes primitive locality and timing. Decomposing every declared flag interaction into separate CNOTs adds six acquisition flag gates and four decision flag gates to the earlier twenty-four-gate sequence. The explicit decomposed write therefore has 34 primitive gates and a 23-gate carrier hold, before eleven memory fanout gates complete it. Refresh/reset durations are additional. The accuracy table fixes 32 storage updates after the completed write; it does not reuse the previous 44-slot common-deadline schedule. A combined multi-control pulse could reduce gate count only by declaring a different interaction and duration.

## Disposition

The source task is now specific: recover a UD-authored law for the apparatus gaps and shared coupling, or derive those quantities in a new source programme. 2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Result and scope

The next controlled comparison changes the memory encoding while preserving the prior binary carrier test, boundary graph, Ising Hamiltonian and thermal update rule. A complementary ground-state encoding substantially improves finite-step retention over the one-hot word. It has zero net endpoint work for the real carrier test states, but a 10J single-bit transition barrier, a prepared orientation resource, and a driven carrier control. ## 1. Complementary ground-state write

Let A=P_f be the projector onto the exposed face used in the earlier binary test. R=0 prepares the interior core cell and R=1 prepares that face, each with probability 1/2. The twelve-bit blank is |0^12>. Let F=product_i X_i, the global bit complement. Declare

\[
U_g=(I-A)\otimes I+A\otimes F.
\]

As before, a pulse generator (pi hbar/2 tau) A tensor (I−F) implements this controlled unitary in the interaction picture. Its laboratory implementation requires timed drive control; the collective operator F is not a local single-bit interaction.

The memory Hamiltonian is H_M=J sum_edges(1−Z_iZ_j)=2J k(m). Complementing both ends of every edge leaves each product Z_iZ_j unchanged, hence

\[
[F,H_M]=0.
\]

Both written ground words have H_M=0. More generally the global complement preserves memory energy for every input word. The controlled write can therefore bypass a memory barrier if its collective generator is available, but this availability is an added control assumption.

The carrier marginal is pinched into A and I−A. With H_C=i epsilon B_K and real test inputs, its mean energy change is zero. Consequently the net endpoint pulse work is exactly zero for this test. For general rho it is the carrier backaction term

\[
W_g=\operatorname{Tr}\{[AH_CA+(I-A)H_C(I-A)-H_C]\rho\}.
\]

The write remains noncommuting with native carrier energy and requires a control resource. Zero net endpoint work is not zero drive strength, zero resource preparation, zero full-cycle cost, or a native energy-conserving recorder.

For the connected boundary graph, the only zero-disagreement words are all-zero and all-one. Therefore, among XOR writes from the fixed blank, all-one is the unique nontrivial codeword minimizing endpoint memory energy. This is an exact endpoint-energy optimization, not a claim that this encoding is globally optimal for logical lifetime or capacity.

## 2. Exact local energy barrier

Restrict implementation to paths of single-bit flips from blank to all-one. A configuration S has energy 2J times the number of boundary graph edges crossing S and its complement.

For monotone paths, dynamic programming computes

\[
b(\varnothing)=0,\qquad
b(S)=\max\{k(S),\min_{i\in S}b(S\setminus\{i\})\}.
\]

The optimum is b(all)=5, corresponding to peak memory energy 10J. A witness flip order and each intermediate energy are included in results.json. An independent threshold-reachability calculation allows arbitrary single-bit flips, revisits and nonmonotone paths. The all-one word is unreachable within energies at most 8J and reachable within at most 10J. Thus the unrestricted single-bit path barrier is also exactly 10J.

This is a classical configuration-path barrier. It is not a lower bound for arbitrary coherent collective control, and no Arrhenius lifetime or physical time is inferred from it. Sequential writes can require transient positive work and later recover energy even when net endpoint work is zero. Their dissipative losses and intermediate carrier backaction are not supplied by this graph calculation.

## 3. Retained distinguishability under the same bath

Use the previous uniform-site Gibbs resampling kernel at x=exp(−2 beta J)=1/3. Its per-update probabilities have denominator 336. Global complement is an exact symmetry of the kernel, so if p_r(m) is the distribution after r updates from all-zero, the distribution from all-one is p_r(complement(m)). The replay checks the symmetry for every memory word.

The optimal full-word readout error is

\[
D_r=\frac12\sum_m|p_r(m)-p_r(\bar m)|,
\quad P_{\rm err}^{\rm opt}=(1-D_r)/2.
\]

A feasible alternative measures all bits and uses majority vote, breaking ties randomly. Its error is computed exactly and is always at least the optimum. The replay uses integer path weights, reports exact rational probabilities and energies, and checks monotonicity of D_r through 128 updates. Logarithmic information is reported as a floating display value.

| Thermal updates | Ground encoding optimal error | Majority error | Earlier one-hot optimal error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 1/24 |
| 2 | 0 | 0 | 0.079383 |
| 4 | 0 | 0 | 0.144307 |
| 8 | 0.00001274 | 0.00001375 | 0.236741 |
| 16 | 0.00075667 | 0.00077078 | 0.332874 |
| 32 | 0.00923883 | 0.00934834 | 0.411147 |
| 64 | 0.04717227 | 0.04749628 | not computed previously |
| 128 | 0.13624588 | 0.13659575 | not computed previously |

Finite-step zero error has a direct support proof: after r single-site updates, no word can be more than r Hamming flips from its initial word. The radius-r supports about all-zero and all-one are disjoint for r<=5. The first overlap is possible at r=6. This protects distinguishability while configurations may already have changed; static configuration survival and logical retention are different quantities.

The calculation gives zero error for updates 0 through 5, and nonzero error thereafter. At 32 updates, I(R:M) is approximately 0.667610 nats, compared with approximately 0.028799 for the earlier one-hot encoding. Exact rational errors rather than display logarithms certify the retention comparison.

The finite thermal chain remains irreducible. Both initial codewords eventually converge to the same Gibbs state, so D_r tends to zero, error tends to 1/2, and recorded reference information tends to zero. There is no indefinitely stable finite-temperature memory here.

## 4. Energy and preparation accounting

The two conditional distributions have equal mean memory energy by complement symmetry. Initial memory energy is zero and, with energy-conserving bath collisions, cumulative mean bath heat is minus the memory energy increase. At equilibrium the memory energy is 11J/2, so cumulative mean bath heat tends to −11J/2. Thermalization supplies energy to the memory while eventually erasing the logical label. A sign of mean heat does not determine retention.

The finite-temperature Gibbs memory is exactly invariant under F, so using that pointer produces identical outputs for R=0 and R=1: D=0 and I(R:M)=0. The collective encoding requires preparation that selects an orientation. Even a zero-temperature equal mixture of the two ground words would be invariant and would not record the label under this XOR write. Low mean energy alone is insufficient.

A pure oriented blank has higher free energy than the finite-temperature Gibbs state by k_B T ln P(x). This preparation resource remains separate from the zero endpoint write work. Exact pure preparation with a finite full-rank bath is not furnished by this candidate. Resetting an unknown fair ground-encoded logical bit to the same oriented blank, without usable source-label information, raises memory free energy by k_B T ln2 under isothermal accounting. A reusable apparatus cannot infer zero cycle cost from zero write work.

## 5. Implication for entropy and area

This encoding improves retention by spending twelve memory factors on a single label. Its logical record entropy is at most k_B ln2, regardless of assigning all twelve exposed faces to that one code. It therefore does not provide a positive extensive record density as the boundary grows. The Gibbs entropy and the logical record entropy must remain typed separately.

The next comparison should jointly constrain logical capacity, readout error at a declared horizon of updates, and complete resource cost. Independent small encoding patches might provide extensive capacity, but their coupling, boundary interfaces and source-selected write rules must be derived. The present result supplies a controlled retention benchmark, not that construction.

## Disposition

CHECKED: collective write; unique minimum endpoint-energy nontrivial XOR codeword; exact 10J local path barrier; thermal complement symmetry; retained optimal and majority readout errors; preparation dependence; eventual information loss.

CANDIDATE: collective drive, symmetry-breaking pointer preparation, memory and bath Hamiltonians, clock and routing. OPEN: native autonomous source law, physical calibration and retention, many-bit density, refinement consistency and horizon map. Ledger, registry, repositories and site unchanged. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN. The unavailable Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was unused.

# Local write control, Gibbs renewal and repeated resource comparison

2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Outcome and source scope

A local memory-gate sequence now implements the complementary ground encoding from a blank. A matched-energy Gibbs-cell SWAP gives an exact bath-refresh rule. These protocols reproduce the earlier storage kernel, so the retained-information comparison remains valid. Switching work, gate count, latency and consumed reservoir cells are now explicit.

The protocols are declared physical candidates. Native boundary incidence determines allowed neighbor gates. Native UD does not select the coupling-switch law, pulse clock, Gibbs source, transport, recovery efficiency or reset apparatus. G05/G06 remain source-open. The work below supplies concrete conditional mechanisms rather than interpreting the previous ideal collective gate as already local or autonomous.

## 1. Local seed and neighbor fanout

Use the earlier fair binary carrier input: core cell for R=0 and exposed face f for R=1. Reserve the same twelve-bit memory, initially all-zero, and disconnect its thermal bath during writing.

First write P_f into memory bit 0. Then apply eleven neighbor CNOTs, copying an already written parent bit into a still-blank child. The checked target order is

\[
0,2,6,1,4,8,3,5,7,9,10,11.
\]

Every child has a parent sharing a boundary edge. The gate-parent pairs are in results.json. For R=0 all bits remain zero; for R=1 all become one. This implements the same encoded isometry on the declared blank input. It is not asserted to equal the collective complement gate on arbitrary dirty memory.

For a memory CNOT from parent p to target t, use pulse

\[
K_{p,t}=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\tau_g}n_p\otimes(I-X_t),\qquad n_p=|1\rangle\langle1|.
\]

Temporarily switch off the three Ising bonds incident to the target. The remaining memory Hamiltonian commutes with this pulse, so it produces the intended gate, apart from diagonal free phases that do not change the test's pointer statistics. Restore those bonds after the pulse. This gives a local two-memory-bit gate with local target-bond switching; it does not require a twelve-bit pulse operator.

The carrier seed needs an explicit hold. Set A=P_f and temporarily remove its native cross-incidence terms AH_C(I−A)+(I−A)H_CA. The exposed face has four incidence neighbors: three edges and its attached cell. Removing these four couplings makes A commute with the held carrier Hamiltonian. Apply the analogous A-controlled seed pulse while the target memory bonds are off, then restore the carrier couplings. This records the initial binary label without assuming native carrier evolution stops everywhere.

For the declared real basis inputs the mean carrier coupling-switch work is zero. General coherences need the carrier backaction account. Switching four carrier couplings, three memory bonds, and supplying timed pulses are resource requirements, not native emergent controls. Once the seed is written, the carrier can resume native evolution while fanout acts only on memory.

No independent thermal updates are applied during either write. Gate errors and thermal leakage during isolation are omitted by declaration; they are not asserted physically absent.

## 2. Signed switching work and pulse ledger

Along the R=1 fanout path, the post-gate memory energies in J units are

\[
0,6,8,6,8,10,8,10,8,10,8,6,0.
\]

For each target flip, removing its incident bonds contributes −E_inc(before), and restoring contributes +E_inc(after). Summing over the twelve flips gives −36J and +36J on the R=1 branch. The R=0 branch contributes zero. Thus the fair ensemble gives

\[
W_{\rm off}=-18J,\quad W_{\rm restore}=18J,
\quad W_{\rm net}=0.
\]

The largest conditional memory energy is 10J, matching the independently certified optimal local path barrier. Gross restoration work is not just the maximum energy barrier. The one-hot write instead gives zero bond-removal work and 3J mean bond-restoration work.

For each ideal controlled pulse, let kappa=pi hbar/(2 tau_g). Switching on the pulse contributes kappa/2 mean interaction energy for the fair, perfectly encoded branch ensemble; switching it off recovers the same amount. This cancels in the ideal net pulse work, but its recovery and control hardware are additional requirements. The ground sequence uses twelve such pulses, while one-hot uses one. Losses in pulse control are kept separate from memory-bond recovery below.

Both protocols are externally scheduled. A fixed gate list supplies a reproducible local-control specification, not a source-derived autonomous clock or a proof of zero controller-reset cost.

## 3. Local thermal collision and bath refresh

At each storage step choose a site uniformly. Its three neighbor labels define a memory gap 2J or 6J. Swap the site's energy-ordered bit with the matching bath qubit, leaving the other qubit unchanged. The previously verified conditional swap is an energy-conserving unitary V_i supported on a local star: target, three neighbors and two bath qubits.

An exact pulse generator is pi hbar(I−V_i)/(2 tau_b). Since V_i is an involution commuting with memory-plus-bath energy, so does this generator. This is geometrically local to the star, but it is not a derived two-local Hamiltonian. Resolving it into lower-body couplings is a further control question.

Renew both bath qubits by swapping them with fresh, independent Gibbs cells having the same respective Hamiltonians 2J n and 6J n. A matched-energy SWAP commutes with the sum of those two identical Hamiltonians and has zero net free-energy change of the pair. More strongly, for any correlated old memory/bath state,

\[
\mathrm{SWAP}_{B,R}(\rho_{MB}\otimes\tau_R)
\mathrm{SWAP}_{B,R}^\dagger=\rho_{MR}\otimes\tau_B.
\]

Thus the refreshed bath is exactly Gibbs and independent of the retained memory. All old correlations move into the outgoing stream cell. The proof holds quantum mechanically, not only for diagonal inputs. The checker additionally verifies classical factorization examples at probabilities 1/4 and 1/28.

Site selection is represented by a degenerate twelve-state control in the uniform Gibbs state. Refresh it by the same SWAP rule with a fresh independent uniform degenerate cell. This removes old control/memory correlations by export; it does not erase them within a closed finite apparatus.

For 32 storage updates the specified refresh implementation consumes 64 Gibbs qubit cells and 32 uniform twelve-state cells. It requires 64 bath-qubit swaps and 32 site-control swaps, in addition to 32 local thermal collisions. This is a per-run finite stream requirement. Indefinite operation needs continued reservoir supply or a separately specified rethermalization apparatus.

At beta J=(ln3)/2, incoming bath-pair mean energy is

\[
2J(1/4)+6J(1/28)=5J/7.
\]

Thirty-two pairs therefore carry energy inventory 160J/7. This shared incoming inventory is not extra dissipated work to add to the cost ledger. Bath heat is determined by outgoing-minus-incoming energy. Pulse/transport losses, preparing and moving stream cells, and returning the reservoir to its starting state are not determined by the ideal SWAP identity.

## 4. Repeated information and cost comparison

The local write produces the same blank or encoded word as before, and refreshed collisions induce exactly the previous memory kernel. At 32 storage updates:

| Quantity | One-hot | Local ground fanout |
|---|---:|---:|
| Retained information, nats | 0.02879899 | 0.66761023 |
| Information density | 0.00239992/a0 | 0.05563419/a0 |
| Optimal error | 0.41114666 | 0.00923883 |
| Write pulses | 1 | 12 |
| Memory bond off/on rounds | 1 target round | 12 target rounds |
| Mean bond-removal work | 0 | −18J |
| Mean bond-restoration work | 3J | 18J |
| Storage bath/control cells | 64 / 32 | 64 / 32 |
| Ideal memory-cycle work bound | 2.56731 kBT | 1.49719 kBT |

Localizing the write does not change the retained-information numbers under perfect isolated gates. It changes latency and recovery requirements. With durations tau_g and tau_b, total write-plus-storage times are tau_g+32 tau_b and 12 tau_g+32 tau_b. This is a same-storage-horizon comparison, not a same-wall-clock-deadline comparison. Neither duration has a native physical calibration; the extra eleven write slots must not disappear from a performance claim.

To expose sensitivity, declare eta in [0,1] as recovery efficiency for negative memory bond-switch work. Let gamma kBT be the same additional implementation work per local write gate, covering pulse/timing/switch-actuator losses other than the already counted memory bond-recovery loss. Let c0 kBT be common nonnegative excess work from storage, refresh, readout and reset under the stated blind-memory-reset/export convention. Then the corresponding cost floors are

\[
\frac{C_h}{k_BT}\ge b_h+\gamma+c_0,
\qquad
\frac{C_g}{k_BT}\ge b_g+12\gamma+18\beta J(1-\eta)+c_0,
\]

where b_h=2.567311... and b_g=1.497188... are the derived ideal memory-cycle bounds. The eta and gamma laws are declared engineering assumptions; they are not coefficients recovered from UD. Actual reset may exceed its free-energy floor and finite exact pure reset is not supplied.

Comparing these floors, ground has lower total work when

\[
11\gamma+18\beta J(1-\eta)<b_h-b_g.
\]

At gamma=0 this requires eta approximately greater than 0.89177. At eta=1 it requires gamma approximately less than 0.097284 kBT per gate. If neither is met, ground can cost more net work even while retaining much more information.

For the costs assigned by this common-overhead model, retained information per work still favors ground for all nonnegative gamma,c0 and eta in [0,1]. Algebraically let R=I_g/I_h=23.18173...; then R>12 and R b_h>b_g+18 beta J. Therefore

\[
R(b_h+\gamma+c_0)-[b_g+12\gamma+18\beta J(1-\eta)+c_0]>0.
\]

This conclusion concerns the parameterized cost floors or an implementation whose excess costs equal the declared terms. Lower bounds alone cannot rank unknown actual costs. Different costs per gate, technology-dependent readout/renewal, or different reset excesses require a revised ledger. The retained-information advantage does not prove a universal apparatus-efficiency advantage.

## 5. Closure boundary

SPECIFIED and CHECKED under declared protocols: neighboring fanout gates; local target-bond switching; four-incidence carrier seed hold; signed switching work; matched Gibbs refresh; correlation export; exact unchanged storage statistics; latency and recovery sensitivity.

OPEN: source-selected autonomous coupling switches and clock, practical local-star Hamiltonian decomposition, physical control/transport losses, equilibrium stream supply, readout and pure-reset implementation, extensive record density, refinement and horizon normalization. A finite closed reservoir with cyclic restoration is not obtained by relabeling fresh-stream export as renewal.

This step closes the mathematical gate-list and refresh-channel definitions. It does not close native UD provenance or physical apparatus cost. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN. No ledger, registry, site or repository entries changed. Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png remained unavailable and unused.

# Native propagation and a declared record-entropy rate

2026-10-12, America/Chicago. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Outcome

The independent-bit boundary assumption is replaced by an explicitly derived **correlated record process**. Under a declared fresh-memory projective recording interaction, native tetrahedral propagation fixes a Markov transition kernel and its information-entropy rate. The sampling interval and record observable remain candidate source choices. No physical heat, universal area normalization, metric horizon or G has been derived.

The sharp new distinction is that the stationary carrier-label chain has positive record-history entropy rate but zero path-reversal entropy production. Record-information accumulation is therefore not interchangeable with thermodynamic entropy production.

## 1. Exact native generator and candidate recording operation

Use the filled tetrahedron, unit metric, fifteen oriented simplex coordinates, and B=D^T−D. Let P0 project onto the uniform four-vertex zero mode. The exact checker verifies

D²=0, B^T=−B, B P0=0, B²=−4(I−P0).

Hence the native propagator at sampling gap Delta is exactly

U_Delta=P0+cos(2 Delta)(I−P0)+(sin(2 Delta)/2)B.

Delta is measured in the declared dimensionless native evolution parameter. A physical clock calibration or a preferred sampling gap is not assumed.

Declare the recording instrument on carrier and a fresh blank record:

R(rho)=sum_j Pj rho Pj tensor |j><j|.

One cycle first applies U_Delta to the carrier, then applies this instrument and retains the new record. This is a mathematical CPTP projection-and-write channel. It may be implemented by coherent copying plus an additional record dephasing/environment operation. Neither that dephasing nor the supply of fresh memory is supplied by the closed skew native generator. This is a declared candidate **open-system interaction**, not a reclassification of native reversible dynamics as irreversible.

The conditional carrier state after a rank-one readout is the indicated basis state. Thus outcome probabilities over repeated cycles are derived from the generator and the instrument, rather than inserted as independent Bernoulli occupations.

## 2. Degree recording in the top-cell/face oscillator

Let e be the unit top-cell vector, f=Be/2. The native invariant plane has B e=2f and B f=−2e. With e labelled 0 and coherent face vector f labelled 1, the propagator is a rotation by 2 Delta. Chain-degree recording restricted to this plane distinguishes these two labels and retains the coherent face superposition.

The recorded transition kernel is

P_degree=[[1−q,q],[q,1−q]], q=sin²(2 Delta).

Starting at e, the final label probability after n cycles is

Pr(Rn=1)=[1−(1−2q)^n]/2.

The history is generally correlated. Nonetheless its Markov conditional entropy is constant:

H(Rn|R1,...,Rn−1)=h(q),
H(R1,...,Rn)=n h(q),

with deterministic R0=0 and h(q)=−q ln q−(1−q)ln(1−q). Thus q and the information-entropy rate are now derived **conditional on the specified native propagator, observable and sampling gap**.

| Gap Delta | q | Information entropy per record, in nats |
|---|---|---|
| pi/12 | 1/4 | 2 ln 2−(3/4)ln 3 |
| pi/8 | 1/2 | ln 2 |
| pi/4 | 1 | 0 |
| pi/2 | 0 | 0 |

The full-transfer clock at pi/4 produces a deterministic alternating sequence and zero history entropy. The return clock at pi/2 also produces zero. The quarter-ray-period sampling pi/8 gives independent fair records. The native oscillation frequency does not by itself select the entropy-maximizing clock.

As Delta→0, q=4 Delta²+O(Delta⁴) and h(q)=q[1−ln q]+O(q²). Therefore h(q)/Delta→0. Arbitrarily frequent recording does not yield an unbounded information-entropy rate in this candidate interaction; the repeated projection suppresses transitions. This is a scoped recording-backaction result, not a physical time law.

## 3. Resolving individual simplices changes the recorded dynamics

Now take rank-one projectors onto all fifteen simplex coordinates. The conditional state after a record is a simplex basis vector, and

P_ij=|(U_Delta)_ji|².

These projectors destroy coherence between the four face coordinates. Unlike degree recording, the conditioned carrier is no longer restricted to the two-dimensional top-cell/face plane. Future propagation explores the full fifteen-dimensional register. The change in entropy rate is an intervention effect, not merely a passive renaming of the same recorded history.

Put c=cos(2 Delta), s²=1−c². The transition probabilities have a simple native form:

- For a vertex, its own probability is (1+3c)²/16; each of the other three vertices has probability (1−c)²/16; each of its three incident edges has probability s²/4.
- For a nonvertex simplex, its own probability is c²; each of its four incident adjacent-degree simplices has probability s²/4.
- All other entries vanish.

The matrix is symmetric and doubly stochastic. When sin(2 Delta) is nonzero, the incidence edges give an irreducible chain; vertex self-loops give aperiodicity for the tested gaps. The unique stationary label distribution is uniform 1/15. This equilibrium is selected by the **candidate unital recording channel**; it is not a derived thermal Gibbs state.

Let Hv be the vertex-row entropy and Hnv the common nonvertex-row entropy. The stationary record-information entropy rate is

h_star=(4 Hv+11 Hnv)/15.

For Delta=pi/4 the row entropies are Hv=(5/2)ln 2 and Hnv=2 ln 2, so

h_star=(32/15)ln 2.

For Delta=pi/6, exact rational probabilities give

h_star=(58/15)ln 2−(7/10)ln 3−(5/24)ln 5.

Both kernels, every row and column sum, the exact entropy log coefficients and finite-history chain-rule calculations are checked. At the same gap pi/4, degree recording has zero rate while simplex recording has a positive rate. A source law choosing the record observable is indispensable.

## 4. Controlled stationary limit from a fixed native initial state

Start from the top-cell basis state rather than assume a stationary ensemble. For the tested simplex kernels, the exact sixth power P^6 has strictly positive entries. Its minimum m gives a Doeblin coefficient alpha=15m, because P^6_ij≥alpha/15 for all i,j.

Total variation distance to uniform contracts by at least 1−alpha every six steps. Therefore, with Hn the n-record history entropy,

|Hn−n h_star|≤(6/alpha) ln 15.

The bound follows by summing deviations of the expected row entropy; each row entropy lies between 0 and ln 15. It is conservative but explicit and does not assume independent records.

For Delta=pi/4, alpha=135/1024, and the transient bound is (2048/45)ln 15. For Delta=pi/6, alpha=24324705/33554432. This proves the limiting information-entropy rate from a declared native pure initial state under the recording intervention.

If the initial label is stationary and included as the first of N records, the exact joint entropy is ln 15+(N−1)h_star. These conventions differ only by initial/transient terms; they must not be mixed when assigning an exact finite-area intercept.

## 5. Positive record entropy does not establish irreversible carrier thermodynamics

At the stationary distribution pi_i=1/15, symmetry gives pi_i P_ij=pi_j P_ji. Consequently the stationary Markov path-reversal relative-entropy rate

sigma_path=k_B sum_ij pi_i P_ij ln[(pi_i P_ij)/(pi_j P_ji)]

is exactly zero; zero-probability terms are omitted. Yet h_star is strictly positive for both tested simplex channels. The current label entropy stays fixed at ln 15 while the retained history entropy grows.

Thus history randomness, storage growth and the stationary label chain's time-reversal irreversibility are distinct quantities. The result does **not** say that the complete measurement, dephasing, memory preparation or erasure apparatus dissipates no energy. Its energetic/environmental bookkeeping is not present in the candidate channel and remains OPEN. Neither sigma_path nor Hn has been identified with a physical horizon Clausius entropy.

For classically dephased records with consistent retained histories, each cycle raises the carrier-plus-retained-record information entropy by the relevant conditional record entropy. A unitary dilation including the omitted environment can instead preserve total von Neumann entropy. The statistical increase cannot be used as a heat law without deriving that environment and its energy exchange.

## 6. Conditional area coefficient with derived correlations

If a source independently assigns one distinct retained record slot to each equal-area boundary tile, and N tiles have A=N a0, then the derived correlated process gives

S_rec(A)=k_B h_star A/a0+O(1), eta_phys=k_B h_star/a0.

For stationary label initialization, the O(1) term is explicitly k_B(ln 15−h_star). For the deterministic top-cell start, it is bounded by k_B(6/alpha)ln 15.

This advances the previous product-bit example: h_star is computed from native propagation and a recording interaction, and correlations are retained. The one-slot-per-tile placement, record sampling gap, observable, physical a0 and identification of the boundary with a causal horizon remain candidate inputs. Recording repeatedly on one fixed patch produces a temporal history, not automatically additional spatial horizon area.

At Delta=pi/4 and equilateral triangular patch area a0=sqrt(3)ell²/4,

eta_phys=128 k_B ln 2/(15 sqrt(3)ell²).

# Receipt dependence and a robust accuracy gate

2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Result

The previous independent-receipt majority formula is replaced by sharp bounds using joint error probabilities. Full three-way independence is not necessary for the declared one-percent final-error guarantee. A sufficiently small pair joint-error sum suffices, even when decision faults depend on one another and on receipt errors.

The bounds identify source quantities that UD must independently derive; they do not establish those quantities. Native action normalization and recording-source provenance remain open under G05/G06. G was unused. The prior physical gates, thermal kernel, ideal reverse cleanup and ideal downstream fanout retain their declared scope.

## 1. Exact majority identity

Let E_i indicate that receipt i disagrees with the original binary carrier label. Do not assume that the three errors are independent. Define

\[
p=\frac13\sum_iP(E_i=1),\qquad
a=\frac13\sum_{i<j}P(E_i=E_j=1),\qquad
b=P(E_1=E_2=E_3=1).
\]

These are mean marginal, mean pair joint, and triple joint error probabilities. The identity

\[
\mathbf1_{E_1+E_2+E_3\ge2}
=E_1E_2+E_1E_3+E_2E_3-2E_1E_2E_3
\]

holds on all eight binary patterns. Therefore majority error is exactly

\[
\boxed{m=3a-2b.}
\]

No permutation symmetry is required. Quantities may be averaged over the fair source label; conditional source-specific statistics can instead be treated separately.

## 2. Sharp joint-moment bounds

Let Q_k=P(sum_i E_i=k). The moments give

\[
Q_0=1-3p+3a-b,\quad Q_1=3p-6a+3b,
\quad Q_2=3a-3b,\quad Q_3=b.
\]

Nonnegativity is equivalent to

\[
b_{\min}=\max(0,2a-p)\le b\le
b_{\max}=\min(a,1-3p+3a).
\]

Thus, for feasible moments,

\[
\boxed{3a-2b_{\max}\le m\le3a-2b_{\min}.}
\]

The bounds are sharp. Choose b at either endpoint, construct the nonnegative Q_k, and distribute Q_k uniformly among the binomial(3,k) patterns of weight k. This gives an explicit law attaining each bound. The checker verifies normalization, moments and majority error of those witnesses using fractions.

With only marginal mean p=1/100, majority error can be anywhere from zero to 3/200. The worst case puts mass 3p/2 on exactly-two-error patterns. Therefore a quoted one-percent receipt error alone does not certify a majority advantage; the resulting majority can be worse than a single receipt.

| p | Mean pair joint a | Sharp majority-error interval |
|---|---|---|
| 1/100 | 1/10000 | [1/10000, 3/10000] |
| 1/100 | 1/1000 | [1/1000, 3/1000] |
| 1/100 | 1/100 | {1/100} |

For pairwise independent equal-marginal receipts, a=p². Triple independence need not hold, and m need not equal 3p²−2p³. Nonetheless the worst-case m<=3p² is small enough for the current criterion.

## 3. Decision faults without an independence assumption

Let L denote the parity of the three forward majority-target faults and the seed-copy fault. Suppose each of those four event probabilities is bounded by q. By the union bound,

\[
P(L=1)\le4q.
\]

This remains valid for correlated decision events. The final seed is wrong when receipt-majority error and L disagree. Consequently

\[
p_{\rm seed}\le m+P(L=1)\le3a-2b_{\min}+4q\le3a+4q.
\]

No independence between acquisition and decision errors is required for these upper bounds. They are sufficient guarantees, not exact formulas for every joint law. The previous parity formula [1−(1−2q)^4]/2 remains exact only under its independent decision-fault model.

Storage is still assumed to use fresh independent bath states and to depend only on the written seed. If its ideal-seed error is e0 and the average seed error is s, the final equal-prior error is e0+(1−2e0)s while s<=1/2. The formula also allows unequal errors conditional on R=0 and R=1: s is their average. It follows by subtracting the two binary-mixture memory distributions.

For the current 32-update ground storage and target epsilon=1/100, define

\[
s_*=\frac{\epsilon-e_0}{1-2e_0}.
\]

The replay's exact rational e0 gives s* approximately 0.000775497742. A robust sufficient source gate is

\[
\boxed{3a+4q\le s_*.}
\]

A tighter version uses 3a−2b_min+4q if p is also available. These gates retain ideal reverse cleanup and ideal fanout; faults outside the four stated decision events need their own terms.

## 4. Conditional guarantee at the current test point

For p=1/100, a=p²=1/10000 and q=1/10000,

\[
p_{\rm seed}\le\frac7{10000},
\quad e_{\rm final}\le e_0+(1-2e_0)\frac7{10000}
\approx0.009925897279<\frac1{100}.
\]

The final inequality is checked exactly using fractions. Thus pairwise independent receipt errors, together with four bounded decision-event marginals, suffice for the accuracy target. Neither three-way receipt independence nor decision-event independence is needed for this guarantee.

With q fixed at 1/10000, the looser sufficient pair-joint ceiling is

\[
a\le\frac{s_*-4q}{3}
\approx0.000125165914.
\]

If all receipt marginals equal p=1/100, define the average pair correlation coefficient by

\[
\bar\rho=\frac{a-p^2}{p(1-p)}.
\]

The ceiling corresponds to bar rho approximately 0.00254201153. This is an average bound, not an individual bound on every pair. Unequal marginals require their actual pair probabilities rather than this equal-marginal correlation conversion.

The bounds are requirements for a declared source model, not measured or native UD correlation values. A small change in shared error can consume the prior margin, so repeating acquisition without a joint-state source law remains insufficient.

## 5. Entropy/resource correction

The receipt workspace contains the joint error flags after carrier uncopies. Under correlated errors its entropy is H(E1,E2,E3), not automatically 3h(p). The general inequality is

\[
H(E_1,E_2,E_3)\le\sum_i h(p_i).
\]

Equality requires error independence. Similarly the output parity garbage can correlate with the receipt flags, so the previous additive 3h(p)+h(u3) expression remains scoped to its independent fault channels. A correlated source can have smaller garbage entropy while producing larger majority error. Reset cost and source fidelity must therefore be derived from different functionals of the same joint state.

The earlier majority release is preserved as an independent-model result. This report adds the correlated-model scope; it does not overwrite its exact conditional formulas or change any registry status.

## 6. What a native source derivation must supply

A source-complete apparatus model must define the receipt-error flags and their pre-decision joint state. If F_i are commuting error projectors on distinct flag registers with state rho_F, then

\[
p_i=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_F F_i),\quad
a_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_F F_iF_j),\quad
b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_F F_1F_2F_3).
\]

The inequality gate can be tested directly on those source-derived quantities. Declaring product flag states and factorized conditional interactions can establish independence within a candidate apparatus, but it does not derive product preparation from native incidence motion. Shared control, carrier drift, bath reuse and coupling errors must be included in the actual joint-state evolution if present.

The supplied source copies and coefficient ledger do not provide this current apparatus joint-state law. The next source task is therefore precise: derive or bound the pair joint-error sum and the four decision-event probabilities using an energetically specified flag environment. The thermodynamic record-to-horizon bridge remains open even if the accuracy gate passes.

Disposition: exact conditional joint-probability theorem and robust accuracy gate checked. Native moments, clock, fault energy, full reset and apparatus area OPEN. # Record energy balance and spatial boundary entropy

2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Result and source scope

The supplied Pasted text(1).txt proposes analogies between adaptive transport networks and GR/QFT, including the candidate conductance rule dC_ij/dt=f(|I_ij|)−gamma C_ij. Pasted text(2).txt includes that material and the earlier entropy calculation. These texts do not specify a quantum recording interaction, Gibbs reservoir, energy calibration, or horizon map. The supplied carrier_definition.md, master_action.md and coherence_equation.md copies are placeholders. Ledger G05 remains source-blocked and G06 lacks a recovered current normalization receipt. This report derives conditional mathematics without replacing those missing sources.

The previous candidate record channel can be dilated explicitly. It nevertheless fails energy covariance for the declared native Hamiltonian. Separately, the five-tetrahedron spatial boundary supplies a categorical record alphabet, not a tensor product of independent face bits. These results prevent promoting the earlier conditional temporal entropy rate to a native thermodynamic horizon-area coefficient.

## 1. Explicit reversible copying and reduced record entropy

For the filled tetrahedron let C have the fifteen simplex basis states |j>, with B=D^T−D. Let memory M and environment E each have fifteen states, initially |0>. Let X be the cyclic shift on either pointer. Define the unitary

\[
W=\sum_{j=0}^{14}|j\rangle\langle j|_C\otimes X_M^j\otimes X_E^j.
\]

Each controlled block is unitary. In particular W|j,0,0>=|j,j,j>. For any carrier density matrix rho,

\[
\operatorname{Tr}_E W(\rho\otimes|00\rangle\langle00|)W^\dagger
=\sum_j\rho_{jj}|j\rangle\langle j|_C\otimes|j\rangle\langle j|_M.
\]

Tracing E yields exactly the earlier dephased projective instrument. For a pure input sum_j a_j|j>, the global output sum_j a_j|j,j,j> remains pure. C+M has entropy H(p), E has entropy H(p), and their mutual information is 2H(p), where p_j=|a_j|² and all information entropies use natural logarithms. Thus reduced record entropy arises from entanglement and discarding environmental information; the complete unitary does not create total von Neumann entropy.

The pure pointer blanks are resources. E is not hereby a finite-temperature Gibbs bath; the existence of this dilation does not derive heat or temperature. Returning W to its input would erase the apparent record reversibly if all coherent degrees of freedom remained controllable.

## 2. Exact obstruction to a stationary energy-conserving recorder

Declare a candidate physical-energy embedding

\[
H_C=i\epsilon B,\qquad \epsilon>0.
\]

This is Hermitian, and exp(−iH_C t/hbar)=exp(B epsilon t/hbar). The native dimensionless gap is Delta=epsilon t/hbar. Neither epsilon nor physical t is independently calibrated here.

Let D_s(rho)=sum_j P_j rho P_j denote simplex dephasing. Because B has zero diagonal, D_s^*(H_C)=0. Hence

\[
\Delta E_C=\operatorname{Tr}[H_C D_s(\rho)]-\operatorname{Tr}(H_C\rho)
=-\operatorname{Tr}(H_C\rho).
\]

For real pure native carrier states this mean is zero. That does not certify energy conservation of the operation: a complex superposition (|a>+i|b>)/sqrt(2) across an incidence B_ab=±1 has initial mean energy −epsilon B_ab and final mean zero. The mean energy change is state-dependent.

More strongly, a stationary apparatus and an energy-conserving unitary can only induce an energy-covariant carrier channel. Specifically, if [sigma_A,H_A]=0 and [V,H_C+H_A]=0, then the reduced channel Phi obeys

\[
\Phi(e^{-iH_Ct/\hbar}\rho e^{iH_Ct/\hbar})
=e^{-iH_Ct/\hbar}\Phi(\rho)e^{iH_Ct/\hbar}.
\]

Proof: insert the stationary apparatus evolution into the input, commute the joint evolution through V, and take the apparatus trace.

Simplex dephasing violates this identity. With rho=P_top,

\[
D_s([H_C,\rho])=0,\qquad[H_C,D_s(\rho)]=[H_C,\rho]\ne0.
\]

The derivative at t=0 already contradicts covariance. Native pre-evolution commutes with energy translations, so composing it with D_s does not cure the obstruction.

**Scoped NO-GO:** exact simplex dephasing for arbitrary carrier inputs cannot come from a stationary apparatus via an energy-conserving joint unitary under H_C=i epsilon B. Possible candidate extensions include an apparatus with energy coherence, a clock/work resource, a different observable, an approximate recorder, or a different energy embedding. The sources must select and account for the extension. This is not a universal impossibility of recording.

For the explicit copying dilation with degenerate pointers H_M=H_E=0, the operation is not energy conserving. With interaction switched off at both endpoints, its change in free energy expectation is supplied as work, not automatically heat: W_ext=Delta E_C. Work may vanish for the tested real inputs while the operation still requires a resource to violate covariance.

## 3. Exact entropy balance with a declared thermal reservoir

Let X denote the carrier plus all retained memory and apparatus degrees of freedom kept in the accounting. Declare a reservoir R initially independent of X and in tau_R=exp(−beta H_R)/Z, beta=1/(k_B T), with T positive and finite. Let the joint process be unitary. Define Q_R=Tr[H_R(rho_R'−tau_R)], heat deposited in R, and dimensionless entropy s(rho)=−Tr rho ln rho. Then

\[
\boxed{\Delta s_X+\beta Q_R=I(X':R')+D(\rho_R'\Vert\tau_R).}
\]

This is the equality form of Landauer's principle, with entropy decrease convention translated to Delta s_X; see Reeb–Wolf, Theorem 3, arXiv:1306.4352v3, DOI 10.1088/1367-2630/16/10/103011.

The proof is short: initial independence and global entropy conservation give I=Delta s_X+Delta s_R. The Gibbs identity gives D=beta Q_R−Delta s_R. Adding them proves the equation. Both terms on the right are nonnegative. Writing Q_X=−Q_R gives

\[
\Delta S_X=Q_X/T+k_B\Sigma,\qquad
\Sigma=I+D\ge0,\quad S_X=k_Bs_X.
\]

This equation supplies the missing conditional entropy balance; it does not identify X with a spacetime horizon or equate its joint entropy with the marginal history entropy. Work enters the energy balance separately. Initial bath correlations, nonthermal baths, unaccounted apparatus memory, or retained interactions require additional terms or revised definitions.

For a finite bath with full-rank tau_R, Sigma=0 forces rho_R'=tau_R and I=0, hence Q_R=0 and Delta s_X=0. Therefore a nontrivial finite process does not satisfy exact Clausius equality merely by setting its production term to zero. A controlled limiting construction would be required.

Blindly resetting a classical n-record memory with entropy H_n to a blank gives the formal bound Q_R>=k_B T H_n under these assumptions. If the latest carrier label is retained as usable side information, erasing history while preserving that label instead decreases joint entropy by H_n−H(R_n). In the stationary fifteen-label chain, H_n=ln 15+(n−1)h_star, so this joint entropy decrease is (n−1)h_star. At Delta=pi/4, h_star=(32/15)ln 2. Accessible side information and reset protocol must be declared; the random label process alone does not fix reset cost.

Exact pure reset of a mixed local memory is impossible with a finite full-rank thermal bath: input rank r*d_R exceeds d_R when r>1, but a final pure-memory product state has rank at most d_R. The heat bound is a necessary bound for permitted resets/limits, not an existence proof for finite exact erasure.

## 4. Five tetrahedra: an actual spatial record rule

Use core cell 0123 and attach one new apex to each core face, giving five cells total. Exact enumeration gives

\[
f=(8,18,16,5),\quad\dim C_\bullet=47,
\quad N_{\rm exposed}=12,\quad N_{\rm internal}=4.
\]

Every boundary edge belongs to two exposed faces and the boundary Euler characteristic is 2. Under a declared equilateral metric with edge ell, each exposed triangle has area a0=sqrt(3)ell²/4 and A=12a0=3sqrt(3)ell². The combinatorics do not fix ell or identify this spatial boundary as a causal horizon.

Declare face projectors P_f onto the twelve exposed face coordinates and P_out=I−sum_f P_f. For normalized rho on the 47-dimensional carrier,

\[
p_f=\operatorname{Tr}(P_f\rho),\quad
p_{\rm out}=1-\sum_f p_f,
\quad S_{\rm spatial}=-k_B\sum_{x\in\{f,\mathrm{out}\}}p_x\ln p_x.
\]

This is a simultaneous spatial coarse-graining with thirteen mutually exclusive outcomes. In an equivalent twelve-bit occupancy representation, at most one bit is 1. The bits are correlated by the single-carrier constraint. Consequently

\[
0\le S_{\rm spatial}\le k_B\ln13.
\]

For boundary-supported states p_out=0, the bound is k_B ln12. It is attained by a declared uniform superposition of the twelve faces. This example gives eta=k_B ln12/(12a0), but the uniform state is a candidate and the number is not universal.

For an N-face family using this same single-carrier rule, S_spatial<=k_B ln(N+1). With fixed a0 and growing area A=N a0, S_spatial/A tends to zero. Thus this rule cannot yield a positive extensive boundary-area density. A multi-carrier/tensor-product local memory construction, extensive temporal placement, or another physical record rule would be needed. This does not rule out an area law for a separately derived many-body boundary state.

Refinement adds another constraint. Splitting one outcome of probability p into m equiprobable resolved children increases entropy by k_B p ln m even though its total metric area remains fixed. Redundant copies add zero joint entropy. A coarse-to-fine state/readout map must distinguish these two operations. Geometric refinement alone does not choose one.

## 5. How the adaptive-conductance proposal can contribute

Changing incidence weights in a prescribed real skew generator B(C(t)) keeps each carrier evolution unitary. It does not by itself create total information entropy or supply a thermal bath. State-dependent feedback also needs a declared physical feedback implementation rather than assuming a linear quantum channel.

A separate classical candidate can be stated: nonnegative symmetric rates w_ij=w_ji=alpha_ij C_ij, with dot p_i=sum_j w_ij(p_j−p_i). For positive probabilities its Shannon entropy satisfies

\[
\dot H=\frac12\sum_{ij}w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)\ln(p_j/p_i)\ge0.
\]

This proves a conditional mixing law, not a UD heat law. To obtain heat accounting, independently declare energies and local detailed balance w_ij/w_ji=exp[−beta(E_j−E_i)], with w_ij now denoting i-to-j rates. Then for J_ij=p_iw_ij−p_jw_ji,

\[
\dot S-k_B\beta\dot Q_{\rm in}
=k_B\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}\ln\frac{p_iw_{ij}}{p_jw_{ji}}\ge0,
\quad\dot Q_{\rm in}=\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}(E_j-E_i).
\]

If energies change, sum_i p_i dot E_i is a work term. Conductance maintenance and feedback resources must also be included. The pasted adaptation equation does not specify f, the rates, energy gaps, or bath temperature, so no particular entropy production follows from it yet. Its other analogy claims are not used as evidence here.

## Disposition

DERIVED under declared choices: reversible copying dilation; energy-covariance obstruction; thermal entropy identity; five-tetrahedron spatial alphabet; logarithmic entropy bound; refinement dependence.

OPEN: source-derived recorder/resource, physical energy and clock normalization, many-body boundary state, extensive local record capacity, causal horizon, and gravitational normalization. G was not used. No ledger, registry, repo, or website entries were changed. The unavailable Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was unused.

Next source programme: construct local boundary memory coupled to the carrier with a declared conserved energy, clock/work source and Gibbs bath, and derive the coarse-to-fine state map. Test entropy production and area scaling together rather than fitting either coefficient independently.

## Exact external source

David Reeb and Michael M. Wolf, *An improved Landauer Principle with finite-size corrections*, New Journal of Physics 16 (2014) 103011. https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.4352 ; https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/16/10/103011 . Theorem 3 and Sections 3.2–3.3. This is an external statistical-mechanics theorem, not a native UD source derivation.

S_snap(rho;C)=−k_B sum_j p_j ln p_j.

This functional uses the standard statistical information-entropy convention. It is the entropy of the declared record state, not an independently derived thermodynamic entropy of spacetime. The isometry does not itself imply dissipation: the joint carrier/record state can remain pure. Physically irreversible storage, decoherence or exported entropy requires a source mechanism.

For the same carrier state, a different coarse-graining generally gives a different entropy. Therefore neither carrier support ||c||² nor its conservation determines S_rec without the channel and state statistics. The source ledger also distinguishes micro and coarse functionals; no such equality is introduced here.

## 2. Exact native counterexample to “entropy accumulation”

Let D be oriented incidence lowering the chain degree and B=D^T−D. The checker constructs all fifteen oriented simplices, verifies D²=0 and B^T=−B, and chooses the unit top-cell vector e. Direct calculation gives B²e=−4e and ||Be/2||=1, with Be/2 entirely in the face sector. Thus the exact native solution is

b(u)=cos(2u)e+sin(2u)Be/2.

Here u is the declared dimensionless evolution parameter, not calibrated proper time. Degree probabilities are p3=cos²(2u), p2=sin²(2u), p0=p1=0. Consequently

S_snap(u)=k_B h(sin²(2u)),
h(q)=−q ln q−(1−q)ln(1−q).

| u | Degree-record entropy |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| pi/8 | k_B ln 2 |
| pi/4 | 0 |

This is a source-bound reversible example. Hence S_snap is not a monotone “entropy generated per update.” At u=pi/4, all four face coordinates have equal squared weight. The degree record has entropy zero while the simplex-coordinate record has entropy k_B ln 4. The same state does not have a channel-independent record entropy.

For classical records retained as a growing history, define instead

S_hist(n)=k_B H(R1,...,Rn).

If old records are retained and the distributions have consistent prefixes, the chain rule gives

S_hist(n)−S_hist(n−1)=k_B H(Rn|R1,...,Rn−1)≥0.

That monotonicity belongs to the declared retained classical history. It is not a theorem about the closed native carrier, thermodynamic entropy production, or a resettable memory. Snapshot entropy and retained-history entropy must not be interchanged.

## 3. Single-register area-growth obstruction

For any orthogonal projective partition into m nonzero blocks in a d-dimensional register,

S_snap≤k_B ln m≤k_B ln d.

This follows from the nonnegative classical relative entropy to the uniform m-outcome distribution. For a single filled tetrahedron the degree channel has bound k_B ln 4 and full-coordinate pinching has bound k_B ln 15.

If a sequence of meshes uses one such normalized single register with d=O(L^3) and a boundary area A proportional to L², then S_snap/A≤O(ln L/L²)→0. A positive extensive area coefficient does not follow from this single-register representation. This obstruction is scoped to the stated orthogonal record channel; general instruments can introduce extra apparatus randomness, and a many-body/record-history state space is a separate extension.

In particular, C0⊕C1⊕C2⊕C3 is a direct sum. It is not a tensor product of independent thermodynamic cells. Turning a count of simplices into independent record bits is an additional state-space and dynamics assumption.

## 4. A conditional boundary-area theorem with no G input

Declare a boundary Gamma tiled by N patches, each of independently supplied physical area a0. Extend the model to N classical binary record slots, with joint distribution

p_Gamma(r1,...,rN)=product_i q^(ri)(1−q)^(1−ri), 0≤q≤1.

A micro-to-record rule is the marginal over unobserved variables: a micro-distribution p(r,b)=p_Gamma(r)p(b|r) is mapped to p_Gamma by summing b. The discarded conditional bulk state is arbitrary. This defines a coarse-graining; it does not prove the native carrier prepares that microstate.

The record density matrix is diagonal in the N-bit record basis. Tensor-product eigenvalues give exactly

S_Gamma=k_B N h(q), A_Gamma=N a0,

and therefore

S_Gamma=eta_phys A_Gamma,
eta_phys=k_B h(q)/a0.

At fixed q,a0, a discrete patch variation obeys Delta S=eta_phys Delta A. If these patches are independently shown to represent a local horizon cross-section, this becomes a conditional discretized horizon-area law. The horizon identification, continuum/local-equilibrium limit and local constancy of eta are not proved by counting boundary slots.

For a fair binary record q=1/2, eta_phys=k_B ln 2/a0. If the boundary patches are equilateral triangular faces with an independently given side length ell,

a0=sqrt(3) ell²/4,
eta_phys=4 k_B ln 2/(sqrt(3) ell²).

This is a derived coefficient for the **declared** state and metric convention. No G or Planck length entered. Neither ell nor q has been selected by the present native source, so this is a parameterized normalization, not a universal numerical constant.

## 5. Correlations and history defeat an unconditional law

For an arbitrary joint classical boundary distribution,

H(R1,...,RN)=sum_i H(Ri)−TC_N,

where TC_N=D(p_joint||product_i p_i)≥0 is total correlation. If the marginals all have entropy h(q),

S_Gamma=k_B[N h(q)−TC_N].

All N marginal records may be individually fair while the joint distribution puts probability 1/2 on all zeros and 1/2 on all ones. Then S_Gamma=k_B ln 2 for every N, whereas independent fair records give N k_B ln 2. The same marginal occupancy and patch area do not fix an area entropy density.

A weaker asymptotic theorem is available if an independently derived conditional entropy rate h_* exists: if H(Ri|R1,...,Ri−1)→h_* and A=N a0, the chain rule and Cesaro averaging imply S_Gamma/A→k_B h_*/a0. Finite correlation length alone does not set h_*=ln 2 or make total correlation subleading.

Accumulated records also need not be a function of instantaneous area. A fixed-area memory supplied with n fresh independent fair classical records has S_hist=n k_B ln 2. Thus identifying retained-history accumulation with horizon entropy requires a capacity, export/reset, occupancy or redundancy law that relates the retained state to the current area.

## 6. Physical normalization is not identifiable from these inputs

There are two independent freedoms.

Population freedom: q=1/2 yields h=ln 2, while q=1/4 yields h=2 ln 2−(3/4)ln 3. Both are allowed declared binary record states on the same patches and have different entropy densities. The difference is positive because 27>16. A source-selected equilibrium distribution is needed to choose one.

Scale freedom: rescaling the embedding ell→s ell leaves this dimensionless carrier, record channel and probability distribution unchanged, but a0→s²a0 and eta_phys→eta_phys/s². Thus incidence, simplex counts and dimensionless state probabilities do not determine entropy per square metre. An independent metric/length normalization is necessary.

If the other Jacobson bridge assumptions were also established, the candidate effective coupling would be

G_eff=k_B c³/(4 hbar eta_phys)=c³a0/(4 hbar h_*).

This would predict a coupling from independent source inputs rather than use measured G to choose eta. Here those inputs remain unclosed. Setting a0=4 ell_P² ln 2 with ell_P²=G hbar/c³ would insert G and is explicitly not done.

## 7. Exact source audit and name collision

The external manuscript read from Library is Harold D. Kirk III's *Unified Dynamics from Time Generation: Schrödinger, Yang–Mills, and Einstein as Regimes of Generative Contraction*, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18662525. This is not Benjamin Walker Mayes's tetrahedral programme. In its section 8.1–8.2, equations (43)–(45), the entropy uses a cutoff epsilon=kappa ell_P and imposes c0 N_eff=kappa²/4 by matching the Bekenstein–Hawking value. Those steps do not satisfy the present requirement of independently deriving an entropy normalization without using G. This is a scoped normalization audit, not a verdict on every claim of that manuscript.

An exact source for the previously vague Bochner-flat claim was also located: Kirk's *Unified Dynamics from the Product Flag Manifold Fl_(1,2)(C^3) x CP^1*, version 2.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19302283. Its repository description advertises both Bochner-flat and Jacobson routes. The downloadable PDF could not be read by the web retrieval service, so its full reduction equations are NOT certified here. Bibliographic recovery does not validate the claimed reduction.

Relevant primary references:

- T. Jacobson, *Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State*, Phys. Rev. Lett. 75, 1260–1263 (1995), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1260; arXiv gr-qc/9504004v2. The area law and Clausius relation are hypotheses of that construction.
- C. Eling, R. Guedens, T. Jacobson, *Non-equilibrium Thermodynamics of Spacetime*, Phys. Rev. Lett. 96, 121301 (2006), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.121301; arXiv gr-qc/0602001. Entropy-production terms are explicitly retained.
- R. L. Bryant, *Bochner-Kahler metrics*, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 14, 623–715 (2001); arXiv math/0003099v3. This is a geometric classification/construction source, not a UD-to-Einstein matter reduction.

No exact source is invented for the earlier homepage-only citations. Local carrier/master-action/coherence markdown copies inspected here are placeholders. The attached Mayes v2.2 manuscript contains historical gravitational claims, but its searched text did not supply this record-state/coarse-graining derivation. The current ledger leaves physical action normalization and coarse maps open.

## 8. Bochner-flatness alone: an exact counterexample

Take the Riemannian product S²(+k) x H²(−k), k>0, with its product complex structure. Each factor is a complex curve, so the product is Kahler. In an orthonormal product frame the Ricci eigenvalues are (k,k,−k,−k) and scalar curvature is zero. The four-dimensional Weyl formula gives W=0, hence the Kahler Bochner component also vanishes. Yet Ricci is not lambda*g for any scalar lambda.

The checker verifies every Weyl component for k=1 and the unequal Ricci eigenvalues exactly. Thus Bochner-flat Kahler does not imply an Einstein metric, even before addressing Lorentzian signature. This does not rule out a separately specified sourced reduction; it rules out treating Bochner-flatness alone as that reduction. A full claim needs the reduction map, signature, retained fields, matter action/stress tensor and all reduced equations.

## 9. Disposition and next source gate

EXACT under declared mathematics: record probabilities and entropy; reversible entropy counterexample; conditional product-boundary area coefficient; correlation correction; single-register bound; scale/population nonidentifiability; Bochner-flat non-Einstein counterexample.

OPEN: native irreversible recording dynamics; source-selected h_* and physical a0; thermodynamic identification of S_rec; local horizon and stress-energy/Unruh/Clausius bridge; normalization agreeing with physical gravity; full flag-manifold reduction.

The next task is to derive a many-record boundary state and its entropy rate from a specific UD interaction plus memory/export rule, and derive its physical patch metric without gravity calibration. Generic topology or a numerical match is insufficient. Registry and website are unchanged; physical promotion remains 0. The unavailable Genesis image was unused.
