# Retained information per boundary area and resource cost

2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Result and fair comparison

Compare the one-hot and complementary-ground encodings on the same twelve-face memory, at the same temperature beta J=(ln3)/2 and after the same number r of uniform-site thermal updates. Both begin with the same oriented pure blank and encode the same fair binary carrier label. Both reserve the full coupled boundary area A=12a0. A one-face area denominator for one-hot would require a different isolated apparatus and thermal kernel; it cannot be substituted into this comparison.

Exact conditional distributions and energy means determine retained information, readout error and a memory-cycle work bound. Complete apparatus cost remains OPEN because the drive, clock, bath renewal, readout, and controller reset have not been physically specified. This report provides a complete list of those resource categories, not a falsely complete numerical total.

## 1. Information density and retention target

Let R be the carrier label at write time and M_r the memory after storage. Define

\[
\mathcal I_r=I(R:M_r),\qquad
\rho_{\rm info}(r)=\frac{\mathcal I_r}{12a_0}.
\]

This is retained source information in nats per spatial area, not thermodynamic horizon entropy density. Multiplication by k_B gives entropy units without establishing a horizon identification.

| Quantity at r=32 | One-hot | Complementary ground |
|---|---:|---:|
| Retained information, nats | 0.02879899 | 0.66761023 |
| Information density | 0.00239992/a0 | 0.05563419/a0 |
| Optimal equal-prior error | 0.41114666 | 0.00923883 |
| Retained fraction of initial ln2 | 0.04155 | 0.96316 |

The density ratio is approximately 23.18173. Exact rational error probabilities and the underlying rational distributions certify the state evolution; logarithmic displays are ordinary floating evaluations, not rigorous numeric intervals.

For a candidate retention criterion of optimal error at most 1/100 after 32 updates, the ground encoding passes and the one-hot encoding fails. This threshold is an explicitly chosen comparison criterion, not a native UD constant. The optimal-error measurement may require full-word processing. The feasible majority decoder also passes for the ground encoding, with error approximately 0.00934834.

The two encodings each store one source bit, so this comparison measures retention density at finite time, not asymptotic code capacity or an extensive area law.

## 2. Typed energy ledger

Let E_r be the mean memory energy, H_r=H(M_r) its dimensionless marginal entropy, and E_w its energy immediately after the write. For these real carrier test inputs, the pulse work is W_w=E_w: 3J for one-hot and zero for ground. Subsequent memory collisions conserve energy with their baths, so cumulative bath heat is

\[
Q_B(r)=E_w-E_r.
\]

These are different quantities. Negative bath heat means the memory absorbs energy.

The storage entropy balance, with the outgoing baths and degenerate random-site controls included in the environment accounting, gives

\[
\sigma_r=H_r-\ln2+\beta Q_B(r)\ge0.
\]

It is the marginal memory entropy-production expression for the declared thermal process, not a count of lost carrier information. Conditional reference information requires a separate accounting.

Blind reset returns the full memory to the same pure zero-energy blank without using R. Under isothermal reset with a thermal reservoir and a work source,

\[
W_{\rm reset}\ge k_BT H_r-E_r.
\]

Proof: W=Delta E+Q_B, and the thermal entropy inequality gives Q_B>=−T Delta S. Combining gives W>=Delta E−T Delta S, the free-energy change. A pure blank has E=S=0, yielding the expression above.

Therefore the write–store–reset memory-cycle work obeys

\[
\boxed{W_{\rm mem,cycle}\ge
k_BT H_r+Q_B(r)
=k_BT[\ln2+\sigma_r].}
\]

This is a lower bound for a reusable memory with outgoing baths exported and source-label side information unavailable. It is not an attainable finite exact reset recipe. Exact pure reset is blocked with a finite full-rank thermal bath; bounds describe permitted approximations or limiting processes. It also is not a scalar total for returning every control and finite bath to its original state.

An independent relative-entropy evaluation verifies the same reset expression. For Gibbs memory tau_M with partition P,

\[
D(\rho_{M_r}\Vert\tau_M)=-H_r+\beta E_r+\ln P,
\quad W_{\rm reset}^{\rm bound}/(k_BT)=\ln P-D.
\]

The checker evaluates both expressions on the exact propagated states.

## 3. Comparison including reset

At r=32, the modeled ledger is:

| Quantity | One-hot | Complementary ground |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pulse work / J | 3 | 0 |
| Mean memory energy / J | 3.92355 | 3.24654 |
| Cumulative bath heat / J | −0.92355 | −3.24654 |
| Marginal memory entropy, nats | 3.07462 | 3.28057 |
| Storage sigma | 1.87416 | 0.80404 |
| Reset work bound / kBT | 0.91939 | 1.49719 |
| Memory-cycle work bound / kBT | 2.56731 | 1.49719 |

The ground memory has higher reset work at this time, but lower combined write–store–reset work bound. Net endpoint write work alone would hide this distinction.

At r=0, both memory-cycle bounds are exactly k_BT ln2. The one-hot write deposits 3J which can offset reset work; the ground encoding deposits no energy. Thus zero ground write work does not imply zero blind-reset cycle cost. At infinite storage time both memory states tend to the same Gibbs state and retain no source information. Their modeled memory-cycle bounds tend respectively to 3J+k_BT ln P and k_BT ln P, assuming the same blind reset convention.

Dividing retained information by a thermodynamic lower bound gives an optimistic score, not an actual efficiency. At 32 updates these scores are about 0.01122 and 0.44591 nats per k_BT of memory-cycle bound. Real control and reset costs can reduce achievable efficiencies and can change their ordering.

## 4. Preparation, side information and omitted costs

The oriented blank is common initial infrastructure. Preparing it from the declared Gibbs memory has free-energy work bound

\[
W_{\rm prep}\ge k_BT\ln P(1/3)
=k_BT[23\ln2-13\ln3]
\approx1.66043\,k_BT.
\]

Count this once at startup, then amortize over reuse only if each cycle actually returns the apparatus to the same blank. Adding it to a single startup-plus-memory-cycle job gives bounds approximately 4.22774 k_BT for one-hot and 3.15761 k_BT for ground. Re-adding it every cycle after already charging a return-to-blank reset would double-count preparation.

If R is physically available as usable reset side information, a separate ideal conditional-reset free-energy bound replaces H_r by H(M_r|R)=H_r−I_r. The modeled cycle bound is reduced by k_BT I_r. At 32 updates the corresponding bounds are about 2.53851 k_BT for one-hot and 0.82958 k_BT for ground. A bookkeeping reference label does not make that access free: retaining and controlling from the actual source system requires its own apparatus and cost. The blind-reset comparison does not assume it.

| Resource category | One-hot | Complementary ground | Current accounting |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reserved boundary memory | 12 bits, area 12a0 | Same | Exact state-space cost |
| Initial oriented blank | Same pure state | Same pure state | Free-energy lower bound; exact preparation OPEN |
| Carrier write | Controlled single memory flip for binary test | Controlled global 12-bit complement | Endpoint work derived; drive/clock cost OPEN |
| Single-bit implementation | Face flip reaches 6J | Best local path barrier 10J | Exact path energies; losses and controller OPEN |
| Storage for 32 updates | 64 fresh Gibbs bath qubits | Same | States and heat specified; renewal implementation OPEN |
| Site-selection control | 32 fresh uniform 12-state degenerate controls | Same | State entropy specified; routing/reset OPEN |
| Readout | Optimal full-word discrimination | Optimal full-word or majority | Error derived; apparatus and output-memory cost OPEN |
| Return to blank | Blind reset | Blind reset | Free-energy lower bound; protocol/excess cost OPEN |
| Native normalization | J, epsilon, T, clock, a0 | Same | Not derived; G05/G06 remain OPEN |

The fresh-bath count is the resource consumption of the declared replay implementation, not a theorem that every implementation needs 64 distinct qubits. Reuse needs a lawful renewal rule. The 10J barrier is a transient energy requirement for single-bit paths, not an extra 10J of irreversible net work to add to the ledger. A collective drive bypasses that particular path restriction while introducing a different control requirement.

## 5. What ranking is justified

Within this declared memory model, at the same area and 32-update horizon, ground encoding retains more information, has lower modeled cycle work bound, and passes the stated 1/100-error criterion. It is the better candidate for this retention task. No global encoding optimum or complete apparatus-cost advantage is proved.

For positive, consistently defined actual total costs C_g and C_h, retained information per cost favors ground exactly when

\[
\frac{C_g}{C_h}<\frac{I_g}{I_h}\approx23.18173.
\]

This threshold states how much cost overhead the information advantage can tolerate; it does not assign the unknown actual costs. A vector of preparation purity, physical memory, control locality, bath consumption and reset work must remain visible until a scalar objective is declared.

## Next gate and disposition

DERIVED: retained-information density; exact retained-error comparison; memory energies and heat; consistent blind-reset cycle bounds; preparation amortization rule; side-information dependence; explicit resource gaps.

OPEN: complete autonomous control/renewal/readout/reset apparatus, physical calibration, extensive logical code density, refinement consistency and horizon interpretation. The highest-priority mathematical continuation is a local-control write/retention design with specified bath renewal and output retention, followed by the same ledger. Further optimizing a zero-write-energy code without closing those source choices cannot establish a thermodynamic gravitational coefficient.

Development — no registry entry. No ledger, registry, site or repository updates. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN. The unavailable Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was unused.

# Reversible receipt majority and its resource gate

2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Result and source scope

A three-receipt majority module is constructed as a reversible gate sequence and integrated with the existing twelve-bit ground encoding. It reduces a declared independent receipt-error rate, but costs additional workspace, carrier hold time, gates and garbage reset. Faults in the majority/copy operation impose a second accuracy requirement. The calculation is conditional on source-receipt independence and specified fault channels; it does not derive their actual probabilities or energy environment from UD.

Native P_f supplies the carrier observable. The four-incidence hold and bath-isolated memory write are the prior candidate controls. Native autonomous timing, coupling switches, G05/G06 normalization and horizon map remain open. G is unused.

## 1. Acquire three receipts of the held observable

Use three distinct, initially blank receipt bits a,b,c and a separate initially blank output o. Hold A=P_f by removing its four cross-incidence couplings, so its binary label R is constant throughout acquisition and cleanup. Acquire A into each receipt by the corresponding controlled bit flip. Declare independent XOR acquisition errors E_i with probability p, giving

\[
(a,b,c)=(R\oplus E_1,R\oplus E_2,R\oplus E_3).
\]

These are independent errors conditional on R, not independent receipts marginally: all receipts share the source label. Their error environments must be independently supplied by a future physical model. Fresh bits and repetition alone do not prove that independence.

The native source is only copied as a binary observable during its hold. This is not a three-copy measurement of an arbitrary unknown quantum state.

## 2. Reversible majority and cleanup

Boolean majority satisfies

\[
\operatorname{maj}(a,b,c)=ab\oplus ac\oplus bc.
\]

Apply three Toffoli gates controlled respectively by (a,b), (a,c), and (b,c), each targeting o. From o=0, this computes the majority. Copy o into boundary-memory seed bit 0. Reverse the three majority gates. Finally apply the carrier-controlled receipt copy again to each receipt, converting its value R XOR E_i into E_i. The truth-table checker verifies all input and fault patterns.

With ideal decision gates the output o returns to zero, the three receipt bits retain their error flags, and the memory seed is

\[
S=R\oplus\operatorname{maj}(E_1,E_2,E_3).
\]

Fan the seed out along the previous eleven neighboring CNOTs, starting from the otherwise blank twelve-bit boundary. This generates the same conditional all-zero/all-one codeword family used in the earlier thermal replay.

Primitive counts are three acquisition gates, three majority Toffolis, one seed copy, three reverse Toffolis, three carrier receipt uncopies, and eleven fanout gates: 24 total. The carrier hold lasts through the first 13 gates; thereafter carrier and memory can decouple. The decision module uses four extra workspace bits. Its Toffolis are three-body gate primitives, not a proven two-local decomposition. Routing among receipt bits and the memory seed is declared local to an added decision module, whose physical geometry is not derived.

## 3. Receipt and decision fault laws

For independent acquisition errors the majority seed error is

\[
p_3=3p^2-2p^3.
\]

Exact enumeration gives p3=1499/500000000 at p=1/1000 and p3=149/500000 at p=1/100. This quadratic reduction is conditional on the independent error source.

Now declare an independent target XOR fault of probability q after each of the three forward majority gates and after the seed-copy gate. The four faults combine as a parity error

\[
u_4=\frac{1-(1-2q)^4}{2}.
\]

The effective seed error is therefore

\[
\boxed{p_{\rm eff}=p_3+u_4-2p_3u_4.}
\]

The receipt gates' p and the decision gates' q are different typed probabilities. Reverse computation, carrier uncopies and downstream fanout are ideal in this release. Adding their faults requires a new channel; it cannot be inferred from the four-event model above.

For storage error e_r conditional on a perfect seed, final error is exactly

\[
e_{\rm final}=p_{\rm eff}+(1-2p_{\rm eff})e_r.
\]

## 4. Retention and latency test

The replay derives the same Gibbs storage kernel on the twelve-face graph at beta J=(ln3)/2. Exact rational propagation gives e20 approximately 0.001912274 and e32 approximately 0.009238832. The gate clock again assigns one complete gate round and one collision/refresh round to one slot; this is a declared ratio.

At a common 44-slot deadline, the majority write takes 24 slots and leaves 20 storage updates. The previous single-seed ground write took 12 slots and left 32. The one-hot write took one slot and left 43. Receipt reset is deferred after readout in this schedule; charging its duration before the deadline requires a new time allocation.

| Acquisition p | Decision q | Error after 32 storage updates | Error at 44-slot deadline, 20 storage updates |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1/1000 | 0 | 0.00924177 | 0.00191526 |
| 1/1000 | 1/10000 | 0.00963426 | 0.00231361 |
| 1/1000 | 1/1000 | 0.01315608 | 0.00588800 |
| 1/100 | 0 | 0.00953133 | 0.00220913 |
| 1/100 | 1/10000 | 0.00992358 | 0.00260725 |
| 1/100 | 1/1000 | 0.01344332 | 0.00617953 |

All criterion comparisons use exact rationals. Decimal errors are displays. For the declared one-percent final-error target after 32 storage updates, acquisition p=1/100 combined with decision q=1/10000 passes; decision q=1/1000 fails. At the common deadline the lower thermal exposure improves the error, but spends more time in bath-isolated writing. It is not an intrinsic lifetime improvement at equal post-write age.

At 32 updates the seed ceiling remains (1/100−e32)/(1−2e32), approximately 0.000775498. Majority helps only if both the acquisition majority error and the added decision parity fit inside this ceiling.

## 5. Workspace, energy and reset

Declare the four workspace bits energetically degenerate during the decision stage. This permits ideal logic with zero workspace endpoint energy change, but requires pure blanks and driven control. It does not assign zero total controller cost.

After noisy forward decision gates and ideal reverse computation, o retains the parity of the three forward majority faults, with probability

\[
u_3=\frac{1-(1-2q)^3}{2}.
\]

The receipt uncopies leave E_1,E_2,E_3. The workspace's marginal entropy is

\[
H_{\rm garbage}=3h(p)+h(u_3).
\]

For a blind isothermal reset of that degenerate workspace to its original pure blanks, the necessary work bound is kBT H_garbage. At p=1/100,q=1/10000 this is approximately 0.170738 kBT; at q=0 it is approximately 0.168005 kBT. These are workspace-reset bounds additional to boundary memory reset, drive and source-hold resources. Exact finite pure reset is not provided; accessible side information can change the reset bound but must be physically specified.

The original carrier hold is used explicitly to uncopy R from the receipts. Error flags remain because their stochastic origins are not reversibly controlled in this model. They may correlate with the memory label. Logical uncomputation cannot silently erase an inaccessible noise environment or those flags.

The noise environments themselves still lack Hamiltonian, preparation and renewal laws. Therefore this calculation is not a complete energetic implementation of faulty majority. The twenty-four gate schedule, four workspace blanks, garbage entropy, hold duration and deferred reset are concrete new resource obligations.

The boundary-memory energy still ends at zero for either ideal ground codeword; the earlier 10J fanout path barrier remains. Those facts do not cancel the added decision-module resource costs. The nominal boundary remains 12a0, but the physical area occupied by added workspace is unknown. Retained information per total apparatus area cannot be computed by ignoring that workspace.

## 6. Independence and common-mode failure

To expose the source assumption, let every receipt error contain a shared XOR component C with probability c, plus independent components with probability p. Then

\[
p_{\rm maj}=c+(1-2c)(3p^2-2p^3).
\]

A perfectly shared error is not reduced by majority. The total single-receipt marginal error is c+(1−2c)p, so c and p cannot be conflated with one quoted receipt-error rate. A future source law must establish independent components or directly bound shared error; repeating the same faulty source mechanism is insufficient.

## Disposition and next gate

CANDIDATE: independent acquisition source, degenerate workspace, primitive Toffoli clock and ideal cleanup. # Write faults and a common deadline

2026-10-13. Benjamin Walker Mayes, AI-assisted development. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Result and declared scope

The next best step tests the retention comparison against two previously idealized choices: unequal write latency and faultless gate execution. Ground encoding still retains substantially more information on the same boundary at a common deadline. However, its nominal one-percent-error margin is narrow and places a strict requirement on the initial carrier-to-seed operation.

The clocks and error probabilities below are declared test inputs, not empirical rates or native UD predictions. The fault environment's energy and control costs are not derived, so earlier ideal cost thresholds are not silently applied to noisy gates. G05/G06 and the native recording source remain open. G is unused.

## 1. Common deadline rather than equal post-write exposure

Define one complete write-gate round and one complete thermal collision/refresh round to take one slot each. This equal-duration choice is a candidate clock ratio, not a physical calibration. Isolate the memory from its storage bath during writing, as in the prior local protocol.

At a deadline of 44 slots from the beginning of writing, one-hot finishes its one-gate write and then undergoes 43 storage updates. Ground fanout finishes its twelve-gate write and then undergoes 32 storage updates. Both occupy A=12a0.

| Ideal common-deadline result | One-hot | Ground |
|---|---:|---:|
| Write slots | 1 | 12 |
| Storage updates | 43 | 32 |
| Optimal readout error | 0.43482158 | 0.00923883 |
| Retained information, nats | 0.01666994 | 0.66761023 |
| Information density | 0.00138916/a0 | 0.05563419/a0 |
| Fresh bath qubits in the specified stream | 86 | 64 |
| Fresh uniform site-control cells | 43 | 32 |

The clock cost is explicit. Ground is thermally isolated longer during its write, which is part of this protocol, not an unqualified encoding advantage. If bath leakage during the write is allowed, or gate durations differ, a different kernel and deadline must be evaluated.

The replay independently propagates the one-hot state through 43 updates; it does not extrapolate the earlier 32-update result. Exact rational probabilities are stored, with logarithmic quantities displayed as floating values.

## 2. Exact seed bottleneck

Let R be the original fair carrier label and let the written seed be

\[
S=R\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}E_s,\qquad E_s\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_s),\quad0\le p_s\le1/2.
\]

After this initial operation all fanout, thermalization and memory readout act downstream of S. Let p_0 and p_1 be the final memory distributions conditional on a correct seed value. Then the distributions conditional on the original R are

\[
\tilde p_0=(1-p_s)p_0+p_sp_1,\qquad
\tilde p_1=p_sp_0+(1-p_s)p_1.
\]

Their difference is (1−2p_s)(p_0−p_1). Hence the full-memory trace distance and optimal equal-prior error obey exactly

\[
\boxed{D(p_s)=(1-2p_s)D(0),\quad
e(p_s)=p_s+(1-2p_s)e(0).}
\]

In particular e>=p_s. Also R→S→M is a Markov chain, so I(R:M)<=ln2−h(p_s). Subsequent copies cannot correct an incorrect source seed because they contain no independently acquired information about R.

With perfect fanout and 32 ground storage updates, e0 is the previous exact rational error. To meet the declared final-error criterion epsilon=1/100,

\[
p_s\le\frac{\epsilon-e_0}{1-2e_0}
\approx0.000775497742.
\]

The inequality is exact with the replay's rational e0; the decimal is display only. A seed error of 1/1000 already violates the criterion, yielding final error approximately 0.01022035. The earlier perfect-write pass is therefore conditional on a much better source write than one-percent or one-per-thousand errors.

## 3. Independent fanout errors and the entropy distinction

Declare an independent target-bit XOR error after each of the eleven memory CNOTs, before the target bonds are restored, with probability q. The seed bit is untouched by those eleven faults. In the tree encoding, each child-parent parity equals its own gate error. Thus the eleven independent error bits are in bijection with the resulting word at a fixed seed value.

Consequently, immediately after fanout,

\[
H(M\mid S)=11h(q),\quad
H(M)=\ln2+11h(q),\quad
I(R:M)=\ln2-h(p_s).
\]

The original label is accessed through the seed bit, so extra fanout randomness does not increase source information. It does increase marginal memory entropy. Counting that increase as additional record formation would count control noise as physical evidence about the carrier.

The noisy initial words are propagated through the same finite thermal kernel using exact integer probability weights. Global complement symmetry relates the distributions for S=0 and S=1. The checker verifies the fanout conditional entropy formula, the seed-error law, and exact criterion comparisons.

| Ground encoding, 32 storage updates | Seed error p_s | Fanout target error q | Final optimal error | Retained information, nats |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ideal | 0 | 0 | 0.00923883 | 0.66761023 |
| Seed stress | 1/1000 | 0 | 0.01022035 | 0.66071146 |
| Fanout stress | 0 | 1/100 | 0.01832168 | 0.64062030 |
| Larger fanout stress | 0 | 1/20 | 0.05786802 | 0.53769125 |
| Feasible declared budget | 1/10000 | 1/2000 | 0.00978596 | 0.66541124 |

The last row passes the one-percent criterion by exact rational comparison. It is a conditional gate-quality budget, not a measured performance claim. Non-independent or correlated faults require a new joint law.

## 4. A source-redundancy candidate, distinguished from copying

The mathematical bottleneck suggests three independently acquired seed receipts rather than a larger fanout of one receipt. Under an explicitly independent binary-error model with single-receipt error p, majority error is

\[
p_3=3p^2-2p^3.
\]

Enumerating the eight fault patterns gives, for p=1/1000, p3=1499/500000000; for p=1/100, p3=149/500000. Both are below the perfect-fanout seed ceiling above. This could make source acquisition more robust without pretending downstream copies add evidence.

This is a separate candidate source protocol, not an implemented part of the present retention replay. It needs a carrier hold/readout rule, genuinely independent receipt errors, a reversible majority/control circuit, additional time and apparatus resources, and a revised common deadline. Perfectly correlated receipt errors would give p3=p and remove the advantage. Its energy cost cannot be inferred from the binomial polynomial.

## 5. Cost and closure boundary

The common-deadline comparison changes thermal stream consumption: one-hot needs 43 collision/refresh rounds while ground needs 32. Gate noise additionally introduces an unspecified environment that stores error flags and may exchange work or heat. The marginal entropy 11h(q) is not evidence that its energetic cost is free, nor that every noisy operation dissipates kBT times that entropy. A Hamiltonian/resource model is required.

Therefore ideal write–store–reset cost laws from the previous release remain scoped to their faultless write. They cannot be declared complete cost laws for the noisy cases. This release closes exact information/error propagation under a declared noise channel and clock ratio, not autonomous apparatus cost or physical source calibration.

CHECKED: common deadline; exact seed error floor; fanout entropy; correlated finite-memory propagation; feasible declared error budget; independent three-receipt majority polynomial.

OPEN: native source write, independence of actual receipts, energetic fault model, gate-time calibration, thermal leakage during writing, controller/readout/reset costs, extensive logical density, refinement and horizon map. No registry, ledger, site or repository changes. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN. Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png was unavailable and unused.

Next best mathematical source task: construct the independent source-receipt/majority interaction and include its latency and resource state. The immediate bottleneck is fidelity of carrier acquisition, not the number of downstream copies.

# Receipt thermal-gap frontier and corrected deadline v0.1

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review OPEN.

## Declared inputs and clock

Retain the twelve-face Gibbs collision kernel, beta J=ln(3)/2, ground encoding, perfect downstream fanout, independent decision flags, and receipt state from UD_GIBBS_FLAG_RECEIPT_JOINT_STATE_v0.1. The explicit decomposed write takes 34 primitive slots. A 44-slot deadline leaves 10 storage rounds; 32 post-write rounds require 66 slots. Pure preparation, refresh/reset after readout, routing, controller reuse and gate-energy implementation remain separate costs. Shorter thermal exposure is not an intrinsic lifetime improvement.

## Exact error and gap gates

Let e_r=(1-TV(P_0 K^r,P_1 K^r))/2 and s_r=(0.01-e_r)/(1-2e_r). With p=0.01, q=0.0001, u=(1-(1-2q)^4)/2, m_0=3p^2-2p^3, the exact receipt-seed error is s(c)=u+(1-2u)[m_0+c(1-2m_0)]. Thus e_final=e_r+(1-2e_r)s(c), and

c_exact(r)=[s_r-u-(1-2u)m_0]/[(1-2u)(1-2m_0)].

The broader sufficient union/moment bound gives c_robust(r)=[s_r-4q-3p^2]/[3(1-2p)]. In this declared Gibbs family, c=(1+exp(beta Delta_c))^-1 is strictly decreasing. Therefore c<=c_star is equivalent to beta Delta_c>=ln[(1-c_star)/c_star] whenever 0<c_star<1/2. This conversion is a requirement on a candidate gap, not a source derivation of that gap.

| Total slots | Storage rounds | Ideal storage error | Exact c ceiling | Robust c ceiling | Exact minimum beta Delta_c | Robust minimum beta Delta_c |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|44|10|6.162706438e-05|0.00925486951|0.003142720419|4.673307471|5.75951881|
|66|32|0.009238831644|7.7964838e-05|2.567950424e-05|9.45917466|10.5697917|

All acceptance comparisons and collision propagation use exact rational arithmetic; logarithms are numerical displays. The 32-round result matches the preserved parent error exactly. At 66 slots c=10^-5 passes and c=10^-4 fails. At 44 slots both pass because storage age differs.

## Non-identifiability certificate

Fix the carrier incidence operator, coarse-graining, face graph and the declared controlled-XOR receipt interaction. Give the control flags Hamiltonian H_F=Delta_c n_C+Delta_p sum n_Z+Delta_q sum n_D and energetically degenerate targets. Every flag-controlled XOR leaves its flag unchanged, so it commutes with H_F. Both c=10^-5 and c=10^-4 define valid product Gibbs flag states, both use the same carrier and receipt permutation, and both respect this ideal energy-conservation condition. Yet they lie on opposite sides of the 66-slot accuracy gate. The supplied incidence/coarse-graining plus this conservation condition therefore do not uniquely select receipt performance. A source-authored state-preparation or gap/coupling selection rule is necessary. This is a no-go for inference from those inputs, not a no-go for all possible future UD completions.

There is also a scale freedom: multiply every apparatus and memory energy by alpha>0 and temperature by alpha. All beta Delta and beta J, Gibbs probabilities and dimensionless accuracy results stay fixed, while energies and work in joules scale by alpha. Separately, changing the geometric area unit a0 changes I/(12a0) without changing these finite probabilities. Neither dimensional full-resource cost nor physical entropy per boundary area is identified by the dimensionless apparatus model. No G matching has been used.

## Eight incoming flags and resource interpretation

At c=10^-5, p=0.01, q=0.0001 the incoming flag inventory has beta <H_F>=0.141652820805, S_F/kB=0.172213848417, and ln Z_F=0.0305610276118; S_F/kB=beta <H_F>+ln Z_F. The Gibbs reference free energy is -kBT ln Z_F. Preparing that same equilibrium state from the same equilibrium reference has zero free-energy difference. Its mean energy and entropy are not an extra per-use work bill. After use, matched swaps with eight fresh Gibbs cells export correlations. Their source, routing and finite-bank restoration must be included to establish a full cycle.

The source handoff requires: a native apparatus Hilbert space and embedding; an actual Hamiltonian with typed gaps and local couplings; a bath state and temperature rule; gate durations in relation to storage collisions; a reset channel and finite reservoir/controller accounting; and a geometric physical scale. These are the next dependencies to solve before claiming a complete retained-information-per-area efficiency or horizon normalization.

## Provenance and verification

Inputs: exact parent storage error, boundary face labels, and the explicitly declared prior apparatus equations. verify.py recomputes the collision kernel and corrected-clock errors, verifies the parent equality, constructs the gap frontier and checks the Gibbs energy/entropy identity. This is constructor verification. Native selection, physical promotion and independent review remain OPEN. The original twelve releases are immutable; this result extends their timing and gap analysis without superseding their fixed-age results.

"""Exact corrected-clock propagation and dimensionless Gibbs gap frontier."""
from pathlib import Path
from fractions import Fraction as F
from collections import defaultdict
import json,math
root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
faces=json.loads((root/'boundary_source.json').read_text())['boundary_face_labels']
N=len(faces);assert N==12;full=(1<<N)-1
neighbors=[[j for j in range(N) if j!=i and len(set(faces[i])&set(faces[j]))==2] for i in range(N)]
assert all(len(x)==3 for x in neighbors)
trans=[]
for m in range(1<<N):
 row=[]
 for i in range(N):
  ones=sum((m>>j)&1 for j in neighbors[i]);major=int(ones>=2)
  q=1 if abs(2*ones-3)==3 else 7
  w=q if (1-((m>>i)&1))!=major else 28-q
  row.append((m^(1<<i),w))
 row.append((m,336-sum(w for _,w in row)));assert all(w>=0 for _,w in row)
 assert sum(w for _,w in row)==336;trans.append(row)
def step(v):
 out=defaultdict(int)
 for m,w in v.items():
  for t,a in trans[m]:out[t]+=a*w
 return dict(out)
def gap(prob):
 return math.log(float((1-prob)/prob)) if 0<prob<F(1,2) else None
loc=F(1,100);q=F(1,10000);p3=3*loc**2-2*loc**3;u4=(1-(1-2*q)**4)/2
p={0:1};den=1;rows=[]
for r in range(33):
 if r in (10,32):
  d=F(sum(abs(p.get(m,0)-p.get(m^full,0)) for m in range(1<<N)),2*den)
  e0=(1-d)/2;assert sum(p.values())==den
  s=(F(1,100)-e0)/(1-2*e0)
  robust=(s-4*q-3*loc**2)/(3*(1-2*loc))
  exact=(s-u4-(1-2*u4)*p3)/((1-2*u4)*(1-2*p3))
  cases=[]
  for c in (F(1,100000),F(1,10000)):
   a=loc**2+c*(1-2*loc);m=p3+c*(1-2*p3)
   seed=m+u4-2*m*u4;err=e0+(1-2*e0)*seed
   bound=e0+(1-2*e0)*(3*a+4*q);assert err<=bound
   cases.append({'c_exact':str(c),'final_error_exact':str(err),'final_error':float(err),'exact_pass':err<=F(1,100),'robust_bound':float(bound),'robust_pass':bound<=F(1,100),'beta_Delta_c':gap(c)})
  rows.append({'storage_updates':r,'write_slots':34,'total_slots':34+r,'ideal_storage_error_exact':str(e0),'ideal_storage_error':float(e0),'seed_ceiling_exact':str(s),'robust_c_ceiling_exact':str(robust),'exact_c_ceiling_exact':str(exact),'robust_c_ceiling':float(robust),'exact_c_ceiling':float(exact),'robust_beta_Delta_c_min':gap(robust),'exact_beta_Delta_c_min':gap(exact),'cases':cases})
 if r<32:p=step(p);den*=336
assert rows[1]['ideal_storage_error_exact']==json.loads((root/'baseline.json').read_text())['storage_error_32_exact']
assert rows[1]['cases'][0]['exact_pass'] and not rows[1]['cases'][1]['exact_pass']
assert rows[0]['cases'][1]['exact_pass']
def h(x):return -float(x)*math.log(float(x))-(1-float(x))*math.log(1-float(x))
c=F(1,100000);energy=float(c)*gap(c)+3*float(loc)*gap(loc)+4*float(q)*gap(q)
entropy=h(c)+3*h(loc)+4*h(q)
logZ=-math.log(1-float(c))-3*math.log(1-float(loc))-4*math.log(1-float(q))
assert abs(entropy-energy-logZ)<1e-12
out={'status':'PASS conditional declared apparatus','physical_promotion':0,'independent_review':'OPEN','G_input':False,'clock':'one primitive gate or complete collision/refresh round per declared slot; post-readout reset excluded','beta_Delta_p':gap(loc),'beta_Delta_q':gap(q),'rows':rows,'incoming_flags':{'count':8,'beta_mean_energy':energy,'entropy_nats':entropy,'log_partition':logZ,'interpretation':'incoming equilibrium inventory, not dissipated work or complete cycle cost'},'native_gap_selection':'OPEN','dimensional_normalization':'OPEN'}
(root/'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2)+'\n');print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))

# Contribution to Unified Dynamics

Public contribution guide · 13 October 2026

Mathematicians, scientists, independent peer reviewers and research software contributors are invited to volunteer on a bounded task. Contributions may include checking a proof, finding a counterexample, independently reproducing a calculation, reviewing a physical correspondence, improving code or clarifying a manuscript.

## Starter tasks

1. Review a declared A/B/C spectrum or frozen-mask continuity argument in UD_REVIEW_REPLAY_v0.1.zip.
2. Audit the receipt thermal-gap frontier: exact error gates, corrected write/storage timing or the physical-scale non-identifiability proof.
3. Recover an exact paper and source equation for a proposed correspondence, including assumptions and units.
4. Submit a small reproducible correction to code, notation or a source citation.

## Volunteer review

Specify the artifact and version, hypotheses, scope and proposed deliverable. A review should state what was checked, describe discrepancies or missing proof steps, record reproduction commands when applicable, and distinguish established results from candidate interpretations.

Independent reviews and constructor checks retain separate status. Favorable and unfavorable findings are both useful. Reviewer attribution and publication of the review summary are agreed with the reviewer. A review of one artifact does not endorse the whole framework.

## How to start

- Open a contribution offer at https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/issues/new.
- Include relevant background, task or artifact of interest, proposed scope, availability and preferred acknowledgment.
- Agree a bounded review or coordinated task before beginning it.
- Return proof notes, code, a result receipt or a review report with assumptions and limitations.
- Use issues and focused pull requests for corrections; preserve original evidence and record the change.

Attribution, acknowledgments and any coauthorship are agreed according to the contribution. Referrals to suitable researchers and reviewers are welcome.

## Practical support

Suitable computing equipment, compute access, research hosting and support for a separately agreed independent review are additional contribution options. The historical 3 October 2026 planning brief estimated $6,500 for a laptop package and $4,000 for a paid mathematical review. These are preliminary USD estimates, subject to quotations and agreed terms; in-kind resources reduce the corresponding cash need.

No payments are collected on the site. Financial and paid-review arrangements require agreed terms; no charitable status or tax-deductibility is represented. Reviewer payment is for careful work regardless of conclusion.

## Status and links

Contribution

Mathematicians, scientists, research software contributors and independent peer reviewers are invited to volunteer their time on a clearly defined task. A checked proof, a counterexample, a corrected calculation or a sharper statement of an open question can all move the work forward.

Ways to contribute

Mathematics

Check, challenge or extend a result

Review definitions, proofs and assumptions in discrete geometry, algebraic topology, spectral operators or dynamical systems. Find counterexamples, repair gaps, simplify arguments or compare a construction with established mathematics.

Science

Assess a proposed physical bridge

Examine observables, units, source equations and measurement assumptions. Help define a falsifiable correspondence or review a proposed protocol against the evidence it would actually provide.

Reproducibility

Replay and improve the code

Independently run a frozen calculation, check exact arithmetic and failure controls, document dependencies, or submit a small code improvement with a reproducible result receipt.

Clarity and context

Improve the research record

Clarify notation, identify related work, supply an exact paper or source equation, review a manuscript section, or help make a bounded result easier for another researcher to inspect.

Volunteer independent peer review

If you are a mathematician or scientist willing to scrutinize one defined claim, your help is welcome. Start with a specific artifact and version, agree a manageable scope, then assess the reasoning on its own merits.

  • Proof review: identify the hypotheses, check each inference and report missing steps or counterexamples.
  • Independent reproduction: record the source version, environment, commands, results and any discrepancy.
  • Scientific assessment: separate established mathematics from a proposed physical interpretation; examine testability, dimensional consistency and the required evidence.

A useful review states what was checked, what remains unresolved and whether a correction is needed. Favorable and unfavorable findings are both valuable. Each review is recorded against its specific scope; the review summary and reviewer attribution are published with the reviewer's agreement. Constructor checks and independent reviews retain separate status.

Offer a volunteer review or join the repository discussion.

  4. Return a small correction.Open an issue with a reproducible discrepancy or submit a focused pull request. Preserve the original record and explain the correction, its scope and how it was checked.

Evidence you can inspect now

The finite review package includes a recovered September mathematical note and exact-arithmetic verifier. Its supplemental replay checks the declared A/B/C spectra, all 128 frozen face-gate masks and three deliberately introduced errors.

# Repository protection checklist

The installed connector can create files and commits but cannot write branch-protection or ruleset settings. Protection remains an owner configuration task; files alone cannot prevent direct pushes.

In repository Settings -> Rules -> Rulesets, protect main: require pull requests, at least one approval, the `UD capture integrity` status check, resolved review conversations, and prohibit force pushes and branch deletion. Limit bypass to the repository owner as needed. Review administrative file changes through CODEOWNERS. No collaborator invitations or access grants were made by this bootstrap.

The CI workflow checks immutable-path changes, event coverage and artifact hashes. These checks become a mandatory merge gate only after the owner enables protection. Keep contributor branches unique and use non-forced, head-checked updates.

content:
# Capture protocol

The frozen import scope is the public UD portal source at its captured commit, every current Library title matching UD_, the supplied session project-source attachments, and directly browseable copies of selected manuscript/replay sources. The exhaustive search has no next cursor. The inventory records any mismatch, unavailable file, excluded native Site projection or failed materialization.

Original files are imported as bytes, not executed. SHA-256 deduplication determines duplicate content but does not erase distinct source identities. Library path and current source IDs retain provenance. Historical Library versions not surfaced by the current inventory and unexported chats are outside the recoverable scope.

Archives are deterministic tar/gzip snapshots; split parts are ordered and hashed. A restore verifies them and refuses to replace any existing file. Verification of imported legacy code is inherited unless specifically rerun and logged; ingestion/hash checking is not a scientific replay.

Every future capture uses a new directory and event. Status records distinguish generated, verified, committed and merged. Accepted milestones can reference new manuscripts/claim ledgers, preserving prior versions. Development notes belong on the portal Updates page when portal updates are separately authorized.

# Repository structure and archive recovery

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| captures/ | Immutable per-session scientific files, source snapshots and manifests |
| events/ | One independent JSON event per contribution or amendment |
| state/ | Versioned checkpoints; new files supersede rather than overwrite |
| manuscripts/ | Versioned paper sources and PDFs |
| docs/ | Contribution and capture procedures |
| scripts/ | Import, integrity and reconstruction tools |
| .github/ | Review templates, ownership and CI |

The initial capture combines the complete accessible portal snapshot, current UD-named Library files and supplied session attachments. Each inventory item retains a source identity, original path, SHA-256 and byte size. The raw snapshots use deterministic gzip tar bundles, split into small binary parts for ordinary Git storage. `python3 scripts/restore_capture.py captures/<capture-id>/MANIFEST.json <destination>` verifies every part and restores the original snapshot tree. The tool refuses to replace an existing destination file or traverse outside the chosen destination.

The import does not contain hidden model state, deleted/unexported conversations, inaccessible versions or unavailable attachments. Those limitations are recorded in the capture receipt. Imported files are preserved evidence, not automatic canon or new physical results.

# UD native pre-event projection obstruction v0.1

**12 October 2026 UTC. EXACT formal factorization criterion and scoped source-interface countermodels; OPEN native dynamics. Constructor verification plus separate AI audit of the earlier comparison model. Physical promotion 0.** This does not assert that either formal completion occurs in nature.

## Source lock and typed question

The [Paper I review draft v1.1.1 §7.4](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-07T191951Z-codex-ud-bootstrap-5170f8b8/browse/dist/papers/UD_PAPER_I_REVIEW_DRAFT_v1.1.1.md) leaves the native source of an event receipt open. [Paper II review draft v1.1.1 §8.3, II.M1](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-07T191951Z-codex-ud-bootstrap-5170f8b8/browse/dist/papers/UD_PAPER_II_REVIEW_DRAFT_v1.1.1.md) proves the linear visible quotient criterion `PA=FP iff ker P is A-invariant`. The admitted `UD_THETA_FLIP_DIRECT_EVENT_INPUT_SOURCE_ADDENDUM_v0.1.md` (26 August 2026, local SHA-256 `afef7b56d187f4e6aa7dc7debd7d6fb36076f45b2630286d3716796afad93b06`, §§Event input–No claims) gives `Theta+ = P_g Theta- XOR xi`, with externally supplied `xi in F_2^3` and no flip rate, probability, or autonomous microdynamics; [the October 10 source audit](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-10T170752Z-codex-theta-closure-245626d6/REPORT.md) specifies provenance and separate edge transport limits. The supplied coefficient ledger v0.39(2) (22 August, SHA-256 `1281aa8454013fbbdbcf8ada07af0aefe81014003f25a27f3929ad43afffae63`, Q156/Q167/Q169/Q173) has a native global skew chain generator and conditional hard masks, but no source of `xi` or local factor transition. The attached CRL-2 subdivision v1.0 is a governance **proposal**, not an independent review receipt.

The mathematical question is whether the currently declared native **pre-event** packet/cochain state determines the next pair state or six-edge hard mask, before consulting an external flip receipt or a post-event closure/local-transport receipt. The native chain state, pair bits, closure predicates, transport predicates, their spaces and operators remain differently typed.

## General deterministic factorization criterion

Let `N` be a nonempty set of native pre-event states, `W` a set of source completions, and `R(n) subset W` the **nonempty** set of completions admitted by a declared source contract at every `n in N`. Let `O(n,w) in Z` be the requested next readout. A single deterministic function `f:N -> Z` agrees with **every admitted completion** exactly if

\[
\boxed{\forall n\in N,\quad |\{O(n,w):w\in R(n)\}|=1.}
\]

**Proof.** If `f` exists, every completion at a fixed `n` equals `f(n)`, giving a singleton. Conversely a singleton nonempty output at each `n` defines `f(n)` unambiguously. No metric, probability, physical time or regularity assumption enters. Outside this theorem's domain, `R(n)=empty` is a separate **hold/no-source** case, not a proved no-event physical outcome. This set-valued result is the nonlinear/relation counterpart of the fiber principle behind Paper II II.M1; it is not an amendment to that linear theorem.

If `j:N -> J` is any further statistic computed only from the same native state, two admitted completions at an identical `n` also have identical `j(n)` and cannot be separated by it. For a fixed native generator `A` and chain state `c`, all pre-event jets `c, Ac, A^2c, ...` and the same pre-event trajectory `exp(sA)c` are functions of `c`. Adding arbitrarily many of **those** jets cannot resolve a branch whose cause is an independently supplied event input. This says nothing about a new coupling that changes `A`, a new source state, or a new admissibility axiom.

## Application 1: pair-state event occurrence

Fix one labeled filled K4, oriented native chain state `c in C_0⊕C_1⊕C_2⊕C_3`, pre-event `Theta in F_2^3`, and sourced frame `g=id`. The direct-input interface admits the conditional calculation

\[
\Theta^+_\xi=\Theta\oplus\xi.
\]

Consider two **hypothetical, type-correct formal source completions**, `xi_0=(0,0,0)` and `xi_1=(1,1,1)`, with distinct stipulated external providers. The interface does not itself supply or authenticate either provider. If both completions are admitted at the same native pre-state, they give distinct next pair states despite identical pre-event cochain jets. Both constant masks are invariant under the matching `S4 -> S3` action, so pair-relabeling covariance alone does not choose one. This is a logical countermodel to **derivation from the currently stated interface**, not a demonstration that two actual provider receipts or physical histories exist for one preparation. A missing receipt instead produces `THETA_UPDATE_DEFERRED`, a third operational status that must not be silently identified with a zero-flip event.

Thus **NO-GO for a theorem from the currently stated native-only inputs across all type-correct formal source completions**: the interface does not force a unique pair endpoint. A future native causal theorem or verified provider constraint could restrict `R(n)` to a singleton and reopen this branch. This no-go is about logical entailment, not a physical impossibility theorem. Until then an endpoint-derived `xi=Theta XOR Theta+` is retrospective.

The stochastic alternative is also not determined. At one fully pair-symmetric input, **conditional on an applied receipt**, define solely as formal distributions over the type-correct masks, for `p in [0,1]`:

\[
\Pr_p(\xi=000)=1-p,\qquad
\Pr_p(\xi=100)=\Pr_p(\xi=010)=\Pr_p(\xi=001)=p/3.
\]

Every such distribution is normalized and invariant under the pair action at that input, but `p=0` and `p=1` give different **nonzero-switch probabilities conditional on a receipt**. A zero mask is an applied receipt, not `None`. To represent the separate missing-receipt status, one may also stipulate `Pr(receipt=None)=1-q` and multiply each displayed applied-receipt probability by `q`, with independently free `q in [0,1]`. This changes **receipt availability** and the operational rate of recorded switches (`qp`) without identifying a physical event rate. These fiberwise examples do **not** construct a globally defined stochastic UD evolution on all native states. They are **countermodels to stochastic identification**, not UD-approved physical kernels. The direct-input source explicitly defines no flip probability, receipt-arrival law, or physical clock. Admissibility and symmetry can restrict *what* may happen without supplying *how often* it happens.

## Application 2: edge-mask factor source is separate

For a local edge, the declared readout is `h_e=C_e T_e`, with `C_e` an edge closure predicate and `T_e` an edge transport-integrity predicate. The [mask-source readiness v0.1, adversarial fixtures](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-10T163105Z-codex-source-readiness-3c72f65b/REPORT.md) keeps the same **reduced pre-factors** `(C,T)=(1,1)` and unresolved primitive event token, while displaying formal completions `(C',T')=(1,1)` and `(0,1)`. They yield `h'=1` and `h'=0`. This proves no deterministic rule from **those reduced inputs alone**. It does not prove failure of a rule on a richer complete native state: a future sourced cochain-to-receipt mechanism might distinguish them. No such mechanism is defined in that audit. This is a **separate typed** obstruction; it is not obtained by identifying edge closure with `1-Theta_p` in every context. The [direct-Theta pushforward v0.1](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-10T170752Z-codex-theta-closure-245626d6/REPORT.md) proves a particular pair-lift formula only after `xi` is supplied and, for hard-mask counts, under fixed local `T`.

A **predeclared fixed-structure certificate** that all relevant closure receipts and local transport predicates remain constant through an interval does prove `h^+=h^-` there. Such a certificate is additional model information, not an inference from the current cochain value or negative signed source. [Structural eligibility boundary v0.1 §§The sourced negative certificate–Adversarial contrast](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-10T182115Z-codex-structural-veto-ef5beee2/REPORT.md). Nor can one universally substitute a compression of native `exp(sA)` for the internal edge map; the fixed-map countercompletion is documented in [native projection boundary v0.1 §§Why a local contractive step misses the return–Frozen-null test](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-11T010749Z-codex-native-projection-c9c95ae7/REPORT.md).

## What an admissible positive repair must supply

The next proposal must declare a new source state or source law with a **pre-event** domain, causal order and retained null windows, then show that the projected next pair/edge output is single valued on every in-domain input, or give a fully normalized stochastic transition kernel with its event-count/physical-time distinction. It must state how the source state is obtained from packet/cochain/defect variables (or label it an independent axiom), how local closure receipts and typed edge maps update, and what happens under simultaneous contacts and symmetry. A future observable dictionary needs units, uncertainty, baseline and falsifier. Simply appending `xi`, the next `C/T`, or an endpoint-derived address to the pre-state relabels the answer unless their independent prior source is demonstrated.

The [bounded comparison law v0.1](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-12T001121Z-codex-k4-pre-event-40c08e54/MODEL.md) is complete **after** preparing clock and fuel bits. Its independent finite audit below supports internal consistency, not the missing map from native UD state to those bits. The [OP03 producer handoff v0.1](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-11T020241Z-codex-op03-producer-handoff-23f7e091/PROVIDER_HANDOFF_v0.1.md) still needs an independently generated same-carrier endpoint and all null windows for any held-out score. No target was exposed here.

## Verification and disposition

`verify.py` checks the direct-input algebra and S4 pair action over all `8*24*8=1,536` state/action/flip cases; eight conditional endpoints for each fixed `Theta`; two distinct covariant deterministic completions; 72 invariance checks for three exact-fraction conditional flip kernels; 216 checks for receipt-availability/flip mixtures that keep `None` distinct from `000`; and a separate edge-factor ambiguity. These are finite formal checks of the written source-interface reasoning. They do not establish physical attainability or replace the general set-valued proof.

**EXACT scoped:** factorization criterion and the conditional algebra/covariance cases. **NO-GO scoped:** the current direct-input interface does not logically force a deterministic native-only next `Theta`; reduced pre-edge factors do not determine next `h`; symmetry does not identify a flip/receipt-availability probability. **OPEN_GATED:** whether a *complete* native cochain/defect state supplies either transition, and whether a new constitutive source axiom makes independent predictions and a physical bridge. No AUTO_LOCK of a UD event mechanism; no empirical score; physical promotion **0**.

# UD packet-action event-source and renewal audit v0.1

**12 October 2026 UTC. EXACT conditional two-branch kernel counterexample; NO-GO deriving a unique switch schedule from the available action/admissibility statements. OPEN native pair receipt, feedback/renewal and physical clock. Physical promotion 0.** This preserves the prior continuous contrast candidate as a candidate; no result is promoted to an autonomous UD law.

## Source and status lock

The attached March 2026 `distinction_dynamics_manuscript.pdf` (SHA-256 `909ac4bfbb07ab815d15463648278877a7452989797589bf630564a0afa9f1ef`) is a **historical packet proposal**, not the current accepted event source. Its §§2,4 define packet variables `X_i=(rho_i,theta_i,chi_i)`, link transport `U_ij`, and a proposed action consisting of loop-holonomy, burden and orientation-mismatch terms. Its §13 gives an illustrative Monte Carlo loop: choose a random node or edge, propose a local `X_i` or `U_ij` change, compute `Delta S`, and accept with `min(1,exp(-Delta S/T))`. It does not specify a proposal distribution, all admissible moves, graph-update/renewal dynamics, a physical attempt clock, or a map from its local `chi_i` to the current K4 pair bits `Theta_p`. Those are separately typed.

The current [Paper I review draft v1.1.1 §7.4](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-07T191951Z-codex-ud-bootstrap-5170f8b8/browse/dist/papers/UD_PAPER_I_REVIEW_DRAFT_v1.1.1.md) expressly leaves the pre-event binary offset/source outside its exact conditional map. The supplied `UD_COEFFICIENT_PROVENANCE_LEDGER_v0.39(2).md` (22 August 2026, SHA-256 `1281aa8454013fbbdbcf8ada07af0aefe81014003f25a27f3929ad43afffae63`) marks Q153's burden flux/source law as open, Q158's source/sink as a *residual receipt*, Q156/Q167/Q173's masks/currents as conditional on gates, and Q178/Q179's open-system renewal terms as unsourced. The [current UD portal](https://tetrahedral-packet-complexes.ben-w-mayes.chatgpt.site/) lists Papers I–III v1.1.1 and physical promotion 0. The earlier [continuous contrast v0.2](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-12T135643Z-codex-continuous-admission-0575daf6/PROTOCOL.md) is an explicit comparator, not a packet-source derivation.

The attachment `packet_modulation_layer.md` and `Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png` were unavailable this turn; neither was read. The available seam/transport and equation `.md` snapshots are one-line placeholders. The full-repository zip contains similarly short placeholder snapshots; it provides no executable packet source law. The two PDFs and ledger were inspected as source data, with present-version precedence assigned to the current reviewed Paper I and ledger.

## Conditional rate/clock counterexample inside the historical packet proposal

The displayed March action is

\[
S_{\rm packet}=\sum_C\kappa\operatorname{Tr}(I-U_C)
+\sum_i\lambda(\rho_i-\rho_0)^2
+\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\eta(\theta_i-\theta_j)^2.
\]

**Object and assumptions.** Hold graph, all `U`, `rho`, and `theta` fixed; consider one local binary branch `chi∈{0,1}`. **Condition on both `chi` values and a `chi`-only proposal being admissible** under some future explicit grammar. The displayed action contains no `chi`, so `Delta S=0` for this move and Metropolis acceptance equals 1 for any `T>0`. The source does not specify how often that move is proposed. For any `r∈[0,1]`, define a symmetric pre-event proposal kernel per **attempt**, independently across attempts,

\[
K_r=\begin{pmatrix}1-r&r\\r&1-r\end{pmatrix}.
\]

`r` is an illustrative **unsourced proposal probability**, not a UD coefficient or measured rate. Both `r=1/4` and `r=1/2` have the same displayed action, unit acceptance for a proposed branch flip, symmetry/detailed balance and uniform stationary distribution `(1/2,1/2)`. Yet the expected first-flip attempt counts are `4` and `2`; their three-attempt **strict null-window** probabilities are `(3/4)^3=27/64` and `(1/2)^3=1/8`. Their probabilities of an **unchanged endpoint after three attempts**, allowing two flips, are `9/16` and `1/2`. Thus equal stationary states and the same action/acceptance do not identify an event schedule, null frequency, or first-switch timing. `verify.py` checks all statements in exact `Fraction` arithmetic and compares powers through ten steps. An attempt index is not seconds.

**NO-GO scope.** This is a conditional logical counterexample to inferring a unique *primitive branch* update from the historical action plus acceptance formula. It does **not** prove that actual UD admits `chi`-only moves, that `chi` equals the current K4 `Theta`, or that either Markov kernel occurs physically. If an independently sourced proposal/eligibility rule prohibits these moves, that defines a narrower new branch; the action alone still did not supply that rule. Identifying `chi` with `Theta`, or inferring the pair flip receipt `xi`, would require a separate typed carrier/readout bridge.

## The source-complete feedback/renewal dependency cut

A future autonomous packet/defect law must supply, before endpoint exposure:

| Required typed item | Current status | What is needed to predict switches |
|---|---|---|
| State/carrier | Paper I closed K4 chains; historical `X_i,U_ij` proposal; ledger support/burden | Common labeled carrier and map from packet/defect variables to pair `Theta` and six local `C_e,T_e` |
| Proposal/admission | Historical Metropolis acceptance only, Paper I §7.4 receipt source OPEN | Explicit admissible move support and a normalized attempt/kernel law or deterministic event generator, including symmetry ties and simultaneous contacts |
| Feedback and renewal | Ledger Q153/Q158 and Q178/Q179 source/sink laws OPEN | Pre-event constitutive packet flux, support/burden source and sink, gate transition and post-event state map; initial/boundary data and conservation balance |
| Clock | Paper I `s` dimensionless; historical Monte Carlo attempt step | Source mapping from attempt/event parameter to any physical time, with units, calibration and uncertainty |
| Endpoint/readout | Conditional `Theta` receipt and `h_e=C_eT_e` | Causal `xi`, closure and local transport update generated before targets; no endpoint-derived source variable |
| Evaluation | OP03 producer handoff v0.1 reports zero complete targets | Independent same-carrier ordered positive **and null** windows, sealed pre-state/target chronology, baseline and falsifier |

Under the closed no-feedback continuous contrast v0.2, an active pair has two recurring switches per `π/2` internal period; affected `Theta` and pair-lift closure never terminally settle. To obtain settling **within that specific candidate**, at least one of its continuing fixed flow, no-feedback assumption, unbounded horizon, or every-crossing admission axiom must change. A source/sink or feedback law is a plausible repair, not derived by this necessity statement. Merely appending a fuel bit or gate whose initial value encodes a desired endpoint is not a source derivation.

## Execution and disposition

**Executed:** exact two-kernel comparison and manuscript/ledger source audit. **Not executed:** independent same-carrier event score, hardware/physical clock calibration, packet proposal/renewal derivation. A synthetic two-state branch kernel is a mathematical witness, **not** an OP03 target corpus or a reproduction of observed switches. No AUTO_LOCK of a source rule, no CRL advancement, physical promotion **0**. The independent provider assessment is captured separately in this versioned package if available; a missing provider is recorded as `NOT_RUN` rather than replaced with generated positives.

## Typed source audit

| Supplied `UD_GOVERNANCE_CRL2_SUBDIVISION_v1.0.md`, SHA-256 `8e9e8159fe2e5c4bdc234712e02db0151fc77f4a92c140372279a1e9717689a4`, §§1–4 | Governance **proposal** for development versus registry and independent review | Scientific event source; it is not an accepted source receipt |

The historical packet coordinate `chi_i`, Paper I §8.2's prepared polarity `chi`, and K4's three-bit pair `Theta` have distinct definitions. The matching Greek letter creates no map among them. Q158's `s_B=Delta rho-B j_B` is a residual after a change, not a predictive constitutive source.

## EXACT conditional mathematical criterion: visible Markov closure

**Object.** Let `Z` be a finite *complete* source state space, including any packet, graph, frame, source/sink, hidden history, previous completed-switch index, and renewal variables needed for the update. Let `K: Z x Z -> [0,1]` be a row-stochastic one-attempt transition kernel. Let `h: Z -> O` be a fixed, pre-event typed visible readout, for example `O=(oriented frame, three K4 pair bits, required switch-index memory)`. Its carrier map must be independently specified; it is not constructed by reading endpoints. For an output frame `r`, event receipt compares `Theta+` to the source bits transported to the output basis, `P_{pi(r)} Theta-`, using XOR. A frame-only transition and a bit switch remain separate tags.

**Claim.** A time-homogeneous Markov kernel `\bar K` on visible `O` gives the law of `h(Z_n)` for **every** initial complete state if and only if, for all `z,z'` with `h(z)=h(z')` and every visible `o'`, the row sums agree:

\[
\sum_{y:h(y)=o'}K(z,y)=\sum_{y:h(y)=o'}K(z',y).\tag{L}
\]

**Proof.** Necessity: start once from `z` and once from `z'`; both have the same visible initial value, so their one-step visible distributions must be equal. Sufficiency: define `\bar K(o,o')` to be the common row sum in (L). Conditional on any visible history, the complete current state is a mixture over the fiber `h^{-1}(o)`. Every point in that fiber has the same next visible distribution, so the mixture has distribution `\bar K(o,·)` independently of earlier visible history. This proves the Markov property for all initial laws. This elementary strong-lumpability criterion does not assert that UD supplies `K`, `h`, or (L). Special prepared ensembles may have weaker closure; that would be a separately stated preparation-dependent claim.

**Switch and strict-null calculus, if a source kernel exists.** Let `xi(z,y)` be the declared frame-aligned binary event receipt and let `N(z,y)=K(z,y) 1[xi(z,y)=000]` be the sub-stochastic null kernel. For initial complete state `z`,

\[
P_z(\text{switch next attempt})=\sum_y K(z,y)1[\xi(z,y)\ne000],\qquad
P_z(\text{no switch for }m\text{ attempts})=e_z^T N^m\mathbf1.\tag{N}
\]

The second identity multiplies kernels along all null paths and therefore includes feedback and renewal of hidden state. It reduces to `(1-r)^m` only under additional constant-hazard assumptions. If a normalized proposal `q(a|z)` and accepted update `T_a(z)` are supplied, and rejected moves stay in the same state, then the one-attempt switch chance is `sum_a q(a|z) Acc(z,a) 1[xi(z,T_a(z)) != 000]`. Metropolis acceptance alone supplies `Acc`, not `q`, `T_a`, or `xi`. An attempt count is not a calibrated physical time; a holding-time/clock map with units is a separate bridge.

## Exact constructed witnesses; not UD dynamics

The attached `verify.py` evaluates a four-state `Z={(h,theta): h,theta in {0,1}}` with hidden-state-specific switch proposals `r_0=1/4`, `r_1=1/2`. Holding `h` fixed, the two full states `(0,0)` and `(1,0)` have the **same visible bit** `theta=0` but next-bit distributions `(3/4,1/4)` and `(1/2,1/2)`. Hence (L) fails and no universal `theta`-only Markov law exists for this constructed kernel. Adding the hidden `h` makes the full law well defined. This is a counterexample to automatic projection, not a finding that UD itself is non-lumpable.

A second constructed kernel toggles `h` on every attempt while keeping the **same first-attempt** visible distribution from `(0,0)`. Equation (N) gives three-attempt strict-null probabilities `27/64` with fixed `h` and `9/32` with renewing `h`. Thus matching one-step switch chances do not determine null-window histories. The script checks row sums, probabilities, one-step equality, projection failure, and the exact rational null results. No endpoint target was opened or scored.

## Source-complete return and disposition

An actual UD source submission needs a versioned `Z` and initial/boundary preparation; admissible moves and a normalized generator/kernel with tie and simultaneous-contact semantics; predictive packet/support/burden sources and sinks; update and renewal maps; a fixed carrier/frame-aligned `h` and `xi`; the event/attempt observation schedule; and, for physical claims, a calibrated time/measurement bridge. Apply (L) to any proposed **compact** visible record. If it fails, retain the needed hidden state rather than fitting a visible rate. Then freeze its rule before independent full-endpoint and null-window exposure under OP03.

**Disposition:** EXACT conditional criterion (L) and identities (N); EXACT finite constructed witnesses; NO-GO recovery of a *source-complete UD* rule from these available files; OPEN source dynamics, K4 bridge, event clock and independent endpoint test. The [prior packet-action audit v0.1](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-12T141129Z-codex-packet-source-755aaa68/SOURCE_AUDIT.md) remains valid under its explicit conditional move grammar. `Gap2_FINAL_Finite_Genesis.png` was unavailable and was not used. The user-supplied statement declares `Theta={0,1}^3`, `q=1-theta`, integrity `T`, latent support `L=1[R>0]`, viable obligation `omega=T L`, a finite continuation index, POC-1 saturation `q=omega`, signed reversible support flux, and a burden address selector. For each coordinate, admissibility is `omega=T L`, `omega<=q<=T`. There are five `(T,L,q)` states per coordinate and therefore `5^3=125` complete states. Write `h=q-omega`, a nonnegative idle-open bit vector. For **frame-aligned** old receipts and new receipts,

\[

The last equality `ind F=dim L^- - dim L^+` holds for **any** linear map between these finite obligation spaces; it does not identify a causal continuation map or independently force `h=0`. \[

\qquad G_A^{S\pm}=\tfrac18>0.

The proposed monotone sign rule would assign `mu_flux=-1`. This is a genuine one-viable-pair, pre-event case; hard integrity suppresses B/C obligations while their reversible chain support may still flow. **NO-GO under unchanged T and this native flow:** signed support change alone is not a universal equality constraint on the discrete obligation index. ## 5. Frame provenance and corrected execution scope

The cardinal index is unaffected by relabeling, but address-level closures/reopenings are not. ## Source, version and typed question

[Paper I review draft v1.1.1 §§4.1–4.2, 7.4](https://github.com/ud-tetra/UD/blob/main/captures/2026-10-07T191951Z-codex-ud-bootstrap-5170f8b8/browse/dist/papers/UD_PAPER_I_REVIEW_DRAFT_v1.1.1.md) defines the unit-weight oriented filled-K4 chain space, skew generator `A=d-d^T`, its fixed-chain flow `exp(sA)`, and leaves event receipt admission open. The exact Fraction checker constructs the signed boundary independently of the prior candidate implementation and verifies `A²`, the closed Cayley formula, orthogonality, and the defining Cayley equation at `h=1,1/2`.

where `d_p=3 sum_{e∈p} c_{1,e}² - sum_{e}c_{1,e}²` and `α,β,γ` are exact quadratic expressions in the rational initial chain. This is a **constructed contrast proxy**, not the source-defined `G_p^{S±}` or a physical defect observable.

The frozen **endpoint** rule therefore emits `xi=(0,1,0)`. Yet continuity forces at least **two distinct strict zeros** of `d_A` and at least two of `d_C` inside `(0,π/4)`, one on each side of `π/8`.
