content:
# UD finite six-ratio calibration v0.1

**RESULT / STATUS — DERIVED CONDITIONAL; constructor verification PASS.**
Twelve scalar readings from three specified preparations suffice to estimate
the six effective directed ratios with

\[
\|\widehat q-q\|_2<6.189\times10^{-13}
 <2^{-40}<2^{-39}.
\]

The decimal is rounded upward; the exact interval expression below is the
certificate. The result is uniform on the declared ratio and gain box and
uses a finite interval, not a derivative oracle. Four auxiliary diagnostic
ports are required beyond the original 62-channel vertex-link observer.
This is a proposed protocol with sufficient deterministic input bounds;
apparatus performance has not been measured. Development lane; no registry
entry. Physical promotion = 0. Independent review pending.

## 1. Model and what is identified

Use the frozen real 2640-coordinate chain carrier with grade sizes
(120,720,1200,600) and skew incidence channels A1,A2,A3. In logger time,
let K scale the lower-grade rows of Ak by Dk and upper-grade rows by Uk,
retaining all signs of the frozen A. Equivalently, for the grade-scalar family,

\[
 D_k=\alpha w_k/h_{k-1},\qquad U_k=\alpha w_k/h_k,\qquad
 q=(D_1,U_1,D_2,U_2,D_3,U_3).
\]

Both true ratios and six positive sensor gains are assumed to lie in
\(\Omega=[15/16,17/16]^6\). Ratios, gains and the affine logger scale
are constant across the calibration runs. Sensor outputs are the declared
coordinate times its gain, plus bounded error. Offsets, cross-talk,
off-diagonal metric terms and extra generator terms are excluded by this
candidate family unless their selected-output effects are already bounded
within the stated error receipts. The twelve readings do not verify these
model restrictions.

The effective ratios absorb the constant clock scale. No independent alpha
or h0 reference is needed for their estimation or relative metric/rate shape.
Separating alpha from native rates, or determining an absolute metric scale,
remains unidentified by this protocol. Logger units do not identify physical
seconds. All coordinates below are zero-based and all preparations use real
chain coefficients; no finite-field SVD or exponential is invoked.

## 2. Finite acquisition: three preparations, twelve readings

Let e_j be the jth chain-coordinate vector and set h=1/32 in logger units.
Use a separately prepared initial state for each run:

1. Gain run: pG=e1+e133+e486+e878+e1680+e2040. At the preparation event,
   read these six coordinates. Clip each reading to [15/16,17/16] to obtain
   its gain estimate. The gain preparation has squared norm 6.
2. Run A: pA=e1+e1680, squared norm 2. At h, read 133,486,2040.
3. Run B: pB=e133+e2040, squared norm 2. At h, read 1,878,1680.

Each dynamic output is zero in its prepared initial state. Apply the sign in
the table and divide its reading by h times the corresponding gain estimate.
The resulting vector is z, in the ratio order below.

| Ratio feature | Run | Output | Sign | Oriented simplex | In original shell |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| D1 | B | 1 | + | vertex (1) | No |
| U1 | A | 133 | − | edge (1,11) | No |
| D2 | A | 486 | − | edge (33,34) | Yes |
| U2 | B | 878 | + | face (1,11,87) | No |
| D3 | B | 1680 | − | face (33,34,41) | Yes |
| U3 | A | 2040 | + | tetrahedron (0,33,34,41) | No |

Thus four auxiliary ports are **1,133,878,2040**. All six are available in the
previous 189-coordinate diagnostic layout, but the original 62-coordinate
shell alone does not implement this calibration. The scalar count is
6+3+3=12. It excludes the work needed to certify preparation amplitudes,
addressing, timing and error bounds. In particular, pG contains six known
amplitudes, rather than one unknown amplitude inferred from the same data.
Its error is bounded at its actual readout event, covering any initial
timing uncertainty affecting those prepared coefficients.

## 3. Uniform finite-map theorem

Let L extract the six signed coordinates from the direct-sum states of runs
A and B. Define the ideal finite map

\[
\Phi(q)=h^{-1}L\big(e^{hK(q)}p_A\oplus e^{hK(q)}p_B\big).
\]

The exact incidence jet is I6. K flips grade parity and the selected outputs
have opposite parity to their preparations. Every even Taylor power vanishes
in those outputs, so Phi=q plus odd terms beginning at order 3.

The frozen incidence channels satisfy Ai Aj=0 for i≠j, with orthogonal active
spaces. The inherited spectral certificate gives ||A||<4 and hence every
channel boundary block has norm <4. On each active pair, the directed block
norm is at most 4 max(Dk,Uk). Consequently, throughout Omega,

\[
\|K(q)\|\le\omega=17/4,\qquad
\|\partial K/\partial q_i\|\le4.
\]

For n≥1, differentiating K^n gives n product terms. The combined nominal
preparation norm is 2 and ||L||=1. Summing odd terms n≥3 and then taking the
Frobenius bound over six Jacobian columns gives

\[
\|D\Phi-I\|\le8\sqrt6[\cosh(17/128)-1]
 <0.173082<1/5.
\]

Integrating along segments in the convex box yields

\[
\tfrac45\|q-q'\|_2\le\|\Phi(q)-\Phi(q')\|_2
 \le\tfrac65\|q-q'\|_2.
\]

The finite map is globally injective on this box and its normalized Jacobian
condition number is <3/2. This is a condition number for normalized features,
not for arbitrary raw voltage scales. Finite-time normalization amplifies raw
errors and is explicitly included next. Unlike the older alpha-anchored
protocol, alpha is already absorbed in q, so the bound needs no separate
alpha error term.

## 4. Candidate deterministic precision contract

Let l=15/16 and u=17/16. These are sufficient design requirements, not measured
performance or theory constants. No stochastic averaging assumption is used.

| Error source | Exact ceiling | Norm and scope |
|---|---:|---|
| Gain preparation coefficients at readout | 2^-49 | Infinity norm over six ports |
| Gain-run additive raw noise | 2^-49 | Infinity norm over six readings |
| Dynamic preparation errors | 2^-49 | Combined two-run Euclidean state norm |
| Dynamic additive raw noise | 2^-49 | Euclidean norm of all six readings |
| Dynamic interval error | 2^-55 | Absolute logger-time error for each run |
| Computation of normalized data | 2^-60 | Six-vector Euclidean error |
| Numerical update error | 2^-60 | Euclidean error per projected iteration |
| Accepted projected fixed-point defect | 2^-44 | Six-vector Euclidean norm |

A sufficient per-reading dynamic noise ceiling is 2^-51, since
sqrt(6) times 2^-51 <2^-49. Individual preparation errors must respect the
combined two-run bound; giving each the full combined ceiling would not
suffice. Gain estimation by clipping cannot increase distance to a true gain
in the assumed box. Writing xiG=nuG=xi=nu=2^-49 and j=2^-55 gives

\[
 \epsilon_g=u\xi_G+\nu_G=33/2^{53},\qquad
 E=\exp[\omega(h+j)].
\]

The combined ideal dynamic state norm is at most 2E. Gain normalization error
contributes at most 2E epsilon_g/l. Preparation error contributes at most
u E xi/l. The variation of the exponential over the two interval errors is
at most 2 omega E j before the gain factor u/l. Raw additive noise contributes
at most nu/l, which is conservatively bounded by E nu/l. Therefore

\[
\|z-\Phi(q)\|_2\le B:=
\frac{E(\nu+2\epsilon_g+u\xi+2u\omega j)}{hl}+2^{-60}.
\]

256-bit Arb arithmetic encloses B below 4.382260 times 10^-13. This includes
both readout gain and finite-time normalization. A known constant clock-scale
offset is part of q; j measures error relative to the specified logger
interval. Arbitrary time variation of that scale is outside this model.

## 5. Finite inverse, including noisy data outside the image

Starting at q0=(1,...,1), perform **20 iterations**:

\[
 q_{n+1}=\Pi_\Omega[q_n+z-\Phi(q_n)].
\]

Projection is nonexpansive, and the map inside projection has derivative
I−D Phi of norm <1/5. The iteration is thus a contraction even if noisy z
is outside Phi(Omega). Its fixed point exists uniquely. If the computed
estimate has projected defect r, comparison with the true q gives

\[
\boxed{\|\widehat q-q\|_2\le\tfrac54(B+r).}
\]

For numerical updates with error at most epsilon_step=2^-60, the box diameter
D=sqrt(6)/8 gives the finite defect bound

\[
 r\le\tfrac65[(1/5)^{20}D+\tfrac54\epsilon_{step}]
 <3.855\times10^{-15}<2^{-44}.
\]

The implementation evaluates the exponential map by an **exact rational
degree-32 Taylor polynomial**. Exact incidence channel powers construct the
integer coefficients; all odd terms through degree 31 are retained. The
uniform vector remainder is at most

\[
 T=\frac{2e^{17/128}(17/128)^{33}}{33!h}
 <2^{-170}.
\]

Rounding each updated coordinate to the nearest 2^-64 costs at most
sqrt(6) times 2^-65. T plus this rounding error is <2^-60, so the specified
finite implementation meets the update contract. Exact rational division
followed by the same rounding also meets the normalized-data computation
contract. h and the box endpoints are exactly dyadic.

With the conservative accepted r=2^-44, the interval-certified final bound is

\[
 \tfrac54(B+2^{-44})
 \in (6.18836,6.18837)\times10^{-13}
 <1/2^{40}<1/2^{39}.
\]

In particular every individual ratio meets the requested absolute 2^-39
accuracy gate. The stopping rule uses the **projected fixed-point defect**,
rather than requiring an arbitrarily small raw forward residual. An explicit
boundary example in the replay adds −2^-43 to all six normalized features at
q=(l,...,l). Projection retains the boundary point with zero exact defect,
while the raw forward residual exceeds 2^-44. This distinction prevents an
unnecessary failure on valid noisy data.

## 6. Connection to the fitted-generator shape certificate

The new protocol supplies the previously missing bounded-estimate hypothesis
of `PARENT_SHAPE_GATE.json`, conditional on the family and precision receipts.
It does not supply measured estimates. Retaining the parent's declared
delta=2^-39 cap, define

\[
 \widehat q_0^{\rm frame}=1,\qquad
 (\widehat q_k^{\rm frame})^2=\prod_{j\le k}\widehat D_j/\widehat U_j,
 \quad \widehat s_k=\sqrt{\widehat D_k\widehat U_k},\quad
 \widehat c=(\widehat s_1\widehat s_2\widehat s_3)^{1/3}.
\]

If actual estimates also pass
|shat_k/chat−1|≤2^-38 and the separate common-scale gate 1±1/1024, the parent
propagation bounds imply metric and native-rate shape errors <2^-35. The
protocol alone does not force data to pass those acceptance gates. A measured
shape-gate evaluation must include its own interval arithmetic.

The bound on an additional skew J, full-domain acquisition readout error,
preparation receipts for the 37 history runs, acquisition timing, and stability
throughout the acquisition batch remain separate requirements. Calibrating six
diagonal gains does not certify all 62 or 189 sensor channels. The original
747-dimensional nominal kernel and 1893 historical signal rank are not altered
by this calibration theorem.

## 7. Verification and provenance

Constructor replay verifies identical frozen shell/calibration generators;
14880 sparse entries; all cross-channel directed products; orthogonal channel
identities; the exact I6 jet; parity; polynomial equality against full-carrier
rational powers at four parameter points; four synthetic inverse cases,
including imperfect gain readings and nonzero raw noise; and the noisy
out-of-image boundary case. Uniform interval comparisons establish the global
theorem; point tests alone would not establish it. An isolated fresh-directory
replay checks source hashes and identical certificate fields.

The coefficient ledger O03 treats every precision here as protocol control.
Q139's physical-clock gap remains open; Q165/Q169 supply the scoped real
support/generator framework. The CRL2 attachment is a governance proposal,
not silently adopted. No attachment is modified or republished. No independent
review or apparatus run is claimed. Local capture is separate from public
publication; no push, PR or merge is performed.

Recommended next gate: specify held-out checks for the assumed readout and
generator family at an error level compatible with this six-ratio budget,
and prove the detectable alternatives and blind directions before execution.

# UD fitted generator and common scale certificate

**RESULT — Known fitted offsets can be absorbed exactly into the coordinates, preparations, readout and sampling interval. An unknown common effective scale within 1±1/1024 preserves the parent temporal frame bounds. Residual shape limits can be relaxed eightfold to 2^-35 while retaining 1893 signal directions.** The resulting condition bounds are 19410, 3385 and 1930 for the three schedules.

This is a conditional certificate for an explicitly declared matched grade-metric family. The concrete centre below is an exact candidate example, not an empirical fit. Equal effective incidence rates are a model restriction used for this transfer theorem, not a derived physical unification law. Physical promotion is **0**, development lane, no registry entry; independent review is pending.

## General fitted-coordinate principle

For a known fitted H-skew generator Khat and SPD fitted metric Hhat, let `Q=Hhat^(1/2)`. The transformed generator `Q Khat Q^-1` is skew in Euclidean coordinates. Preparation and readout must be transformed consistently, and calibration uncertainty must be expressed around the fitted values.

A general fitted centre still needs its own modal rank and finite-frame certificate. The exactly transferable family is

\[
\widehat K=cQ^{-1}AQ,\qquad
\widehat H=Q^2,
\]

where A is the frozen unit-metric generator. For grade-scalar `Q=diag(q0 I120,q1 I720,q2 I1200,q3 I600)`, this is a native weighted-incidence model

\[
\widehat K=\widehat H^{-1}A(\widehat w),
\qquad \widehat w_k=cq_{k-1}q_k.
\]

The proof uses exact diagonal similarity; it does not approximate a large known offset by a small perturbation. A fitted generator outside this matched family requires a fresh modal or clustered-frequency calculation before numerical bounds can transfer.

## Explicit exact centre and preparation conversion

Choose the candidate centre

\[
(q_0,q_1,q_2,q_3)=
\left(1,\frac{65}{64},\frac{33}{32},\frac{67}{64}\right),
\qquad c=\frac{33}{32}.
\]

Then

\[
\widehat H_k=
\left(1,\frac{4225}{4096},\frac{1089}{1024},\frac{4489}{4096}\right),
\]

\[
(\widehat w_1,\widehat w_2,\widehat w_3)=
\left(\frac{2145}{2048},\frac{70785}{65536},\frac{72963}{65536}\right).
\]

All 14880 sparse generator entries pass exact rational similarity and H-skew checks. The six directed calibration ratios lie within `[15/16,17/16]`, the earlier local identification domain. This domain check is not an executed calibration receipt or the older nominal-unit acceptance gate.

Use the 37 parent sign preparations X, with entries±1/52, and set

\[
\widehat X=Q^{-1}X,\qquad
\widehat R=RQ,\qquad
\widehat\Delta=\frac 1{2c}=\frac{16}{33}.
\]

The complete rational input matrix is supplied in `FITTED_PREPARATIONS.npz`. Its entries preserve the parent sign pattern and are±1/52,±16/845,±8/429 or±16/871 according to grade. Each has exactly `xhat^T Hhat xhat=165/169`, and Euclidean squared norm no greater than 165/169.

For every integer j,

\[
\widehat R\exp(j\widehat\Delta\widehat K)\widehat X
=R\exp(jA/2)X.
\]

Thus the parent response Hankel matrix is reproduced exactly at the fitted centre. If raw sensors read R, multiply each observed output channel by its fitted grade factor to implement RQ in software. The maximum output factor is 33/32; the maximum state whitening factor is 67/64. Changing only the generator while keeping the old inputs, readout normalization and sampling interval does not satisfy this identity.

Sufficient conversions from raw-coordinate error ceilings to normalized fitted-coordinate ceilings are: multiply the normalized preparation ceiling by 64/67, the readout-operator and additive-output ceilings by 32/33, and the origin/jitter ceilings by 32/33. These factors follow from operator norms of the declared transformations. They do not establish hardware accuracy or an SI clock conversion.

## Common scale uncertainty without phase-error accumulation

In fitted coordinates and normalized time, allow a reference generator `q A`, with

\[
|q-1|\le d=\frac 1{1024}.
\]

The common q is constant throughout the acquisition batch; arbitrary time-varying scale drift is outside this allowance. Its spectral projectors and modal response blocks `R E_lambda X` are unchanged. Only the temporal frequencies scale. The reference family therefore contains the accumulated phase shift exactly; it is not charged as a growing unknown waveform mismatch against A.

The nominal frequencies satisfy `|omega|<4`, so every positive half-phase gap `x=|omega_i-omega_j|/4` is below 2. Since `sin x>=x/3` there, and sine is 1-Lipschitz,

\[
\sin(qx)\ge\sin x-dx
\ge(1-3d)\sin x>0.
\]

The parent's reciprocal-sine sum C is below 1786. Uniformly over this whole common-scale interval,

\[
C(q)\le\frac{C}{1-3d}
<\frac{1786\cdot 1024}{1021}<1792.
\]

This retains the previous temporal Gram allowances 7/8,1/2 and 1/4 for M2048,4096 and 8192. Consequently every reference-family Hankel matrix has rank 1893 and the same certified nonzero condition bounds 15360,3072 and 5120/3 as the unit-rate model.

The effective scale may combine common clock, native-rate and metric factors:

\[
q=\alpha\beta/\lambda.
\]

If each positive factor lies within 1±1/4096, exact interval multiplication and division place q inside 1±1/1024. Their separate identities remain unidentifiable from the response. The signal-rank certificate does not need to separate them. Physical clock and metric identifications still need independent evidence.

The effective common-scale allowance 1/1024 is 2^28 times the previous common clock bound 2^-38. The primitive common-factor allowance 1/4096 is 2^26 times the former rate/metric cap. These comparisons concern different sufficient protocol envelopes and declared normalized coordinates, not a universal hardware improvement or a new theory constant.

## Residual shape errors around the fitted family

The fitted centre and residual plant parameters are constant through the batch. Describe actual normalized dynamics by

\[
G=\widetilde H^{-1}(qA+\Delta A+J),
\]

with `||Htilde-I||<=eta`, `||Delta A||<=4r`, and skew J of norm at most sigma. Here r bounds absolute normalized coefficient errors in the native rate shape after the common scale has been removed. It is not a raw relative error on each unnormalized fitted rate.

Taking `qplus=1+1/1024`, the residual generator difference from its own common-scale reference satisfies

\[
e\le\frac{4r+\sigma+4q_{+}\eta}{1-\eta},
\qquad \|e^{tG}\|\le g=\sqrt{\frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}}.
\]

Preparation, readout, additional-output, origin and jitter limits remain respectively 2^-25,2^-25,2^-26,2^-29 and 2^-29 in normalized fitted coordinates. Set the three residual shape limits to

\[
\boxed{r=\eta=\sigma=2^{-35},}
\]

eight times the previous sufficient limits. With `a=sqrt(165/169)` and `tau=2^-28`, use

\[
u=g[(1+\rho)p+\rho a+a(4q_++e)\tau]+\nu,
\qquad v=gae.
\]

The response difference is bounded by u+vt relative to the appropriate member of the common-scale family. For the normalized finite Hankel matrix,

\[
\beta_M\le\sqrt{37}
\sqrt{u^2+2uv\frac{M-1}{2}
+v^2\frac{7M^2-12M+5}{24}}.
\]

Interval arithmetic certifies:

| M on each Hankel axis | Raw vectors per preparation | beta_M/s upper | Retained-signal condition bound |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 4095 | 0.209 | 19410 |
| 4096 | 8191 | 0.093 | 3385 |
| 8192 | 16383 | 0.116 | 1930 |

Every beta_M/s is below 1/4. Thresholding at half the declared reference-family signal lower bound selects 1893 directions. The condition numbers are looser than the prior tighter-residual certificate because this envelope permits larger residual errors. The relaxed result uses the Hankel-weighted bound directly; it does not require the older uniform per-raw-vector error ceilings.

Small additional observable singular values may occur under residual perturbations. No claim is made that the perturbed matrix has algebraic rank 1893 or that its dynamical kernel remains 747-dimensional.

## Shape calibration without separate common-scale anchors

The six effective directed ratios satisfy

\[
D_k=\alpha w_k/h_{k-1},\qquad U_k=\alpha w_k/h_k.
\]

Common clock and metric factors cancel from the relative metric reconstruction and the relative effective rates:

\[
q_k^2/q_0^2=\prod_{j=1}^k(D_j/U_j),\qquad
s_k=\sqrt{D_kU_k},\qquad
\frac{s_i}{s_j}=\sqrt{\frac{D_iU_i}{D_jU_j}}.
\]

Let the six estimated ratios lie in the earlier positive local domain, with each absolute estimation error at most 2^-39. Construct the fitted q values from the estimated metric ratios and take chat as the geometric mean of the three estimated s values. Require each estimated s_k/chat to lie within 1±2^-38. The separate common acquisition-scale interval must also hold.

With `ell=delta/(15/16-delta)`, delta=2^-39, the exact log error bound implies

\[
\|\widetilde H-I\|\le e^{6\ell}-1,
\]

\[
\max_k|\Delta a_k|\le
(1+1/1024)\left[(1+2^{-38})e^{7\ell}-1\right].
\]

The seven log-error contributions account for effective-rate normalization and the two neighboring fitted metric factors. Interval certification gives metric-shape error below 1.165e-11 and normalized native rate-shape error below 1.724e-11, both smaller than 2^-35. `SHAPE_CALIBRATION_GATE.json` records the proof bounds and exact reconstruction check for the candidate centre.

This is a sufficient gate on already bounded ratio estimates. It does not supply measurements at that precision, a bound on extra skew J, full-domain readout calibration or a physical clock correspondence. Common run-to-run scale changes must stay within the separately declared common-scale band, and noncommon changes must remain in the residual shape budget. Preserving correlated common-mode uncertainty may permit less restrictive absolute-ratio requirements than this simple gate.

## Calibration and interpretation limits

The older grade-calibration uncertainty bounds do not establish the new anisotropic shape limits: its metric uncertainty 5/10^10 and rate uncertainty 4/10^10 exceed 2^-35. They also do not establish the required correlation that would make most uncertainty a harmless common scale. The centre is illustrative, and no actual fitted data or calibration receipts were supplied.

The matched-family condition is a restriction on the three effective incidence rates. It is not a derivation that electromagnetic, weak or strong couplings unify, nor a theorem that measured rate ratios satisfy it. Generic unequal effective fitted rates require another certificate. Separate physical interpretation, full readout calibration and the hidden-generator obstructions from the preceding contract remain open.

Invertible Q and output rescaling do not add information: at an exact matched reference, the hidden space is Q^-1 N and still has dimension 747. The 37-input excitation limitations also persist under the similarity. A common-scale-tolerant rank certificate resolves neither those blind directions nor the coefficient ledger's Q139 clock bridge.

The next calibration task is to certify a finite measurement protocol delivering the six-ratio accuracy above while treating common scale as a nuisance parameter. Apply the matched-family gates explicitly; if the fitted effective rates are unequal beyond the allowed shape band, compute fresh modal or frequency-cluster bounds rather than transferring this certificate.

`validate_fitted.py` replays the exact construction and shape gate, verifies all source hashes and checks a small rational instance of the complete input/readout/retiming identity. Constructor verification is not independent review. No physical promotion or publication is claimed.

# UD full-state third-shell observability theorem v0.1

2026-10-16 UTC. Development — no registry entry. Constructor verification: exact finite arithmetic and certified interval bounds. Non-constructor independent review: pending. Physical promotion: 0.

## Result and fixed model

For the regular 600-cell boundary, the existing unit simplex metric and unweighted skew Hodge–Dirac generator A(1,1,1), three selected vertex-link shells, the retained tetrahedral port and three additional simplex ports give a **189-channel observer with history rank 2640 and zero dynamical kernel**. The previous observer's 142 hidden dimensions are all exposed.

For 8192 simultaneous snapshots at t_j=j/2, normalized by 1/sqrt(8192), the complete-state sample map satisfies

    sigma_min >= sqrt(3)/512, sigma_max <= 1,
    kappa_2 <= 512/sqrt(3) < 296.

A second sufficient protocol uses only **2048 snapshots** at the same spacing, with complete-state condition number less than **725**. These are mathematical sufficient bounds, not exact measured condition numbers, minimum sample counts or physically calibrated timing.

The carrier remains X=C0⊕C1⊕C2⊕C3 over R, dimensions (120,720,1200,600), total 2640, one sorted oriented simplex per coordinate. The generator has upper adjacent-degree blocks -Bk and lower blocks Bk^T. It is real skew in the identity metric. There is no gate, forcing, dissipation, rate change, retriangulation or change of state convention in this release. All simplex-amplitude readouts have unit gain and zero offset by declaration. The evolution parameter is internal model time.

## 1. Exact observation specification

Retain the two earlier centres 0 and 45 and the tetrahedral amplitude at global coordinate 2040, simplex (0,33,34,41). Add the link of vertex **66**. Exact unit-quaternion centre coordinates are

    v_0=(-1,0,0,0),
    v_45=(0,-1,0,0),
    v_66=(0,(1-phi)/2,-1/2,-phi/2), phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2.

Thus the third centre is orthogonal to the first; its inner product with the second is (phi-1)/2. Its label is a dataset index, not an inferred physical address. All vertices, edges and faces of all three links are observed. Together with the retained tetrahedral coordinate this gives 186 distinct channels.

The following additional readouts are selected in this order:

| Port | Global coordinate | Oriented simplex | Gain in history rank |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Triangle amplitude, degree 2 | 928 | (2,67,88) | 8 |
| Edge amplitude, degree 1 | 152 | (2,67) | 4 |
| Vertex amplitude, degree 0 | 4 | (4) | 2 |

The complete readout R has **36 vertex, 91 edge, 61 face and 1 tetrahedral channels**, all distinct coordinate rows. Its ordered coordinate list is in RESULTS.json and operators.npz. RR^T=I189. Its snapshot rank is 189 and its snapshot kernel has dimension 2451. Full reconstruction below uses the known evolution and measurement history; no static 189-to-2640 inverse is asserted.

## 2. Selection procedure and exact stage ranks

The finite-field design screen tested all **118 remaining third-centre vertices** against the previous observer's 142-dimensional hidden subspace. All three proposed additional port types were eligible in a subsequent greedy search across the 2640 coordinate readouts. At each step the search maximized the additional history rank; ties used the lowest coordinate. The selected third centre maximized screen rank, then minimized distinct channel count, then minimized index. Sixteen tested centres tied for highest third-shell screen rank; the channel-count/index rules selected 66.

This is an exhaustive third-centre screen for the fixed baseline followed by a greedy port construction. It is not a proof of a globally minimum sensor set or of optimal triples/port combinations. Screening used F1009; the chosen ranks are separately established over characteristic zero.

### Theorem FS1 — Complete observability

| Observer stage | Scalar channels | Exact history rank | Exact hidden dimension |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous two-shell observer plus tetrahedral port | 125 | 2498 | 142 |
| Add third shell | 186 | 2626 | 14 |
| Add triangle port | 187 | 2634 | 6 |
| Add edge port | 188 | 2638 | 2 |
| Add vertex port | 189 | **2640** | **0** |

The third shell exposes 128 dimensions, followed by increments 8,4,2. Port gains count recoverable state coordinates over histories, not instantaneous output dimensions. A single scalar oscillator readout can distinguish two initial quadratures through time.

There are two independent exact routes to the final rank:

1. Direct finite-field Krylov matrices stack R,RA,...,RA^31 and have full column rank 2640 over both F1009 and F1013. Each full modular rank certifies a nonzero integer minor. Rank over Q, R and C is at least 2640 and cannot exceed the 2640 columns, so it is exactly 2640. No rational upper-rank inference from merely matching deficient modular ranks is used.
2. Rational history-Gram ranks on coprime Laplacian components certify every selected intermediate stage, as detailed below. Their sums are 2626,2634,2638,2640.

Consequently

    intersection_(k=0)^31 ker(RA^k)={0},
    R exp(tA)x=R exp(tA)y for every t iff x=y.

The first identity is a finite derivative certificate, not a requirement to estimate 31 derivatives in the sampling protocol.

### Rational stage proof

Let L=-A² and let q be the same degree-53 squarefree polynomial used in the parent release. Exact integer multiplication verifies Rq(L)=0 on all 189 readouts. Full observability and commutation imply q(L)=0 on the entire carrier: all rows RA^j annihilate q(L), and those rows span the full dual space. This independently certifies the full-carrier annihilator.

For each irreducible factor f of q, use a rational Chinese-remainder projector P_f(L). For history rows R L^j P_f and R A L^j P_f, with j=0,...,deg(f)-1, the Gram blocks are

    [[G_(j+k), -J_(j+k)],
     [J_(j+k),  G_(j+k+1)]],

where G_s=R L^s P_f R^T and J_s=R A L^s P_f R^T. Because A is skew, L is symmetric and P_f is an orthogonal spectral-component projector, this is positive semidefinite and has the same rank as the history rows. A positive common denominator gives an integer matrix; FLINT exact integer rank establishes its rational rank. Selected sensor subsets give the intermediate-stage ranks. Components already fully observed by the parent remain full under inclusion of readouts. STAGE_RANKS.json records these dependencies and every component rank.

After adding the third shell the fourteen remaining hidden dimensions are:

| Squared frequency | Hidden dimension |
|---|---:|
| 14 | 4 |
| 8 | 2 |
| 7 | 4 |
| 4 | 2 |
| 3 | 2 |

The face port removes two dimensions at each of squared frequencies 8,7,4,3. The edge port removes two each at squared frequencies 14 and 7. The vertex port removes the final two at squared frequency 14. This is a typed statement about this generator and observation set, not a universal functional assignment to shapes.

FINAL_PORT_WITNESS.json provides an exact surviving oscillator pair just before the last port: A²x=-14x, all first 188 readouts vanish on x and Ax, but x_4 is nonzero. Thus the final vertex waveform recovers both quadratures of that particular ambiguity. The complete observer has no surviving hidden mode.

## 3. Theorem FS2 — Independent spectral-dimension certificate

The new conditioning computation does not simply assume prior modal multiplicities. The replay evaluates 240 quaternion left/right multiplication maps, with overlaps between the two families; this is an evaluation count, not the symmetry-group order. The replay verifies that each maps every simplex to a simplex and that their generated orbits are transitive separately on vertices, edges, faces and tetrahedra. Signed simplex actions are chain automorphisms by boundary naturality; they are orthogonal in the unit metric and commute with L.

It follows that every diagonal entry of L^k is constant within each chain degree. Since at least one simplex of every degree is observed, the exact observed moment matrices supply

    Tr L^k = 120 (L^k)_(v,v) + 720 (L^k)_(e,e)
             +1200 (L^k)_(f,f)+600 (L^k)_(tau,tau).

For a rational projector P_f(L), its trace equals its ambient dimension. Exact polynomial arithmetic and the stored integer moments compute all thirty dimensions. They sum to 2640 and match the prior characteristic-multiplicity record. The two harmonic dimensions and the signed nonzero-frequency dimensions used below are thereby independently checked. MODAL_DIMENSIONS.json stores the projectors, denominators, exact traces and dimensions.

This trace argument requires the actual unit-incidence model and verified grade transitivity. It is not imported into a nonuniform metric or gated complex without a new check.

## 4. Theorem FS3 — Complete finite-sample conditioning

Define

    F_M x=(1/sqrt(M)) stack_(j=0)^(M-1) R exp(jA/2)x.

All norms here are Euclidean chain-amplitude norms and average-time output norms. The 105 distinct frequencies are zero and the two signs of sqrt(mu) for every positive root of q. Their nodes exp(i omega/2) are distinct. The temporal Gram off-diagonal bound is

    |(V*V)_(a,b)| <= 1/[M |sin((omega_a-omega_b)/4)|].

Exact Sturm intervals and 256-bit Arb arithmetic certify a maximum reciprocal-sine row sum C less than 1786; its enclosed value is approximately 1785.76545033. Therefore temporal frame eigenvalues lie between 1-C/M and 1+C/M whenever the lower bound is positive.

For each squared frequency mu, the compressed positive-frequency spatial Gram is

    H_mu=[R P_mu R^T-i R A P_mu R^T/sqrt(mu)]/2.

At zero use H_0=R P_0 R^T. Synthetic division of q and exact moments evaluate the compressed projectors without singular matrix inversion. The full rank certificate shows that no frequency eigenspace has a hidden vector, so their nonzero dimensions follow from FS2.

Arb interval matrices enclose each H_mu at 256 bits. Approximate numerical eigenvectors U are treated as exact binary constants only to form a test congruence. Certified row-sum bounds on U*H_mu U-diag(d) and U*U-I, together with the exact modal ranks and Weyl/congruence bounds, certify all positive eigenvalues. No unverified numerical eigenvalue is used as proof.

Across all 53 zero/positive-root components,

    alpha² >= 1/65536 = 2^-16.

The smallest certified lower enclosure is approximately 2.32918827112×10^-5, at squared frequency three. The rational common bound is deliberately rounded down. Its power-of-two denominator is bookkeeping for a proved inequality, not a new structural coupling or physical constant.

For every state x and temporal bound epsilon_t<1,

    ||F_M x||² >= (1-epsilon_t) alpha² ||x||².

Also ||F_M x||<=||x|| because each propagator is orthogonal and R is a coordinate restriction. Thus the following sufficient profiles are certified:

| Snapshots M | Last internal time | Scalar samples | Certified sigma_min lower | Certified kappa_2 upper |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| **2048** | **2047/2** | **387072** | **1/(512 sqrt(2))** | **<725** |
| 4096 | 4095/2 | 774144 | 1/(256 sqrt(2)) | <363 |
| **8192** | **8191/2** | **1548288** | **sqrt(3)/512** | **<296** |

For these rows respectively, C/M is below 7/8, 1/2 and 1/4. The sample count, rational temporal bounds and common spatial bound are recorded in SCHEDULE_CERTIFICATES.json. All three finite sample operators have **rank 2640 and kernel zero**. The upper singular value bound is one.

The shorter 2048-snapshot profile uses one quarter as many scalar samples as the primary 8192-snapshot profile. These are sufficient choices; no globally shortest protocol or exact condition number is claimed. The earlier two-shell bound less than 1183 applied only to its observable subspace, whereas these new bounds apply to all 2640 state coordinates.

## 5. Reconstruction and deterministic error contract

For the selected profile, let measurements be y_j=R exp(jA/2)x+e_j and define

    delta=[(1/M) sum_j ||e_j||²]^(1/2).

Least squares using the normalized sample map now recovers the full initial state, with no hidden-state prior:

    ||x_hat-x|| < K delta,

where K=725,363,296 for M=2048,4096,8192 respectively. No zero-mean, Gaussian or independence assumption is needed. If every scalar error is bounded by epsilon, delta<=sqrt(189) epsilon.

For sampling-time errors bounded by |Delta t_j|<=tau, the full observed frequency band obeys |omega|<=sqrt(9+3sqrt(5))<4. Exact skew propagation gives the additional signal-error budget 4 tau ||x||, hence

    ||x_hat-x|| < K [delta+4 tau ||x||].

These bounds presume the declared generator, chain metric and coordinate gains. They do not estimate physical calibration, gain/offset error, bandwidth, rate/metric mismatch, instrument resources or seconds per internal time unit. Those require separate source and uncertainty contracts before hardware qualification. Recoverability of this finite model does not identify a fundamental physical substrate.

## 6. Provenance, reproducibility and limitations

- Immediate parent: local commit 506b7473cb43ef0aac974aae50936f28fe5aa3de, UD_TWO_SHELL_TETRAHEDRAL_OBSERVABILITY_v0.1. Its 2498-rank observer and exact component record are retained as dependency, not overwritten.
- Earlier baseline: local commit e215561fe155927e22d0997729f465b2604172aa, UD_600CELL_VERTEX_LINK_OBSERVABILITY_v0.1.
- Public main refreshed and unchanged at 3b4ccc26a65b5deef0e917fa8bbadf045649695d. Public source-data heads remain PR105 40d56f5f8a54b1ed7b6125209903504f66e9a2a4 and PR106 2c4e4c89d25817cb0120916e28014c8b77a5527f.
- All imported objects are JSON/matrix source data; no archived executable is run. The historical uploaded ledger and governance proposal are not changed or redistributed. The unavailable Genesis PNG is unread and unused.
- Project association remains REF01 (#136) and APP05 (#144). Native observer selection and measured apparatus correspondence are not closed by this ideal construction. Public GitHub publication remains pending authorization after the earlier approval-review block.

Run the new scripts in this order:

    python select.py
    python verify_rank.py
    python moments.py
    python modal_dimensions.py
    python stage_ranks.py
    python frequency_certificate.py
    python spatial_certificate.py
    python schedule_certificates.py
    python summarize.py
    python validate.py

requirements.txt pins the runtime versions. Exact full-rank checks use two primes, and selected intermediate ranks use rational PSD Gram calculations. Integer moments verify the observer annihilator. Exact quaternion automorphisms and trace projectors independently check modal dimensions. Interval temporal and spatial certificates establish rational final bounds. validate.py checks eighteen families and constructs the exact final-port witness. Clean replay reproduces the certificate pipeline from preserved integer moments; full field-rank and moment-generation runs are separate executed checks.

The full kernel result is scoped to A(1,1,1), the unit chain metric, this 189-coordinate readout and its known evolution. No minimality of sensor count or protocol length, physical calibration, independent review or registry promotion is asserted. Physical promotion remains 0.

## Next gate

Certify tolerances to generator/rate, metric and readout mismatch, using a declared state/noise budget, before turning this ideal full-state protocol into an experimental acceptance contract. A sensor/time-cost optimization can then compare the three sufficient profiles or search for smaller designs while retaining a specified reconstruction margin.

note: Recovered earlier package; original source scope retained. Independent review not established; physical promotion 0.
content:
# UD grade-metric and individual-gain calibration v0.1

**RESULT / STATUS — DERIVED CONDITIONAL; development — no registry entry.**
A specified three-preparation protocol identifies 189 individual gains, four
grade metric weights, three rates and one clock scale: **197 parameters**.
It uses 195 sensor scalars and two independent scale references. The normalized
six-ratio finite response map is globally one-to-one on the stated box, with
Jacobian condition number <3/2. This is an extension within an explicitly
chosen finite model. Physical promotion = 0. Constructor verification passed;
independent review pending. No apparatus data were supplied.

## 1. Candidate family and source assumptions

Retain the real 2640-coordinate 600-cell chain carrier, oriented incidence
maps, generator channels A1,A2,A3, and 189-coordinate readout R. The chain
grade dimensions are (120,720,1200,600). Write

\[
H=\operatorname{diag}(h_0 I_{120},h_1 I_{720},
                      h_2 I_{1200},h_3 I_{600}),\quad
A_w=\sum_{k=1}^3 w_k A_k,\quad K=H^{-1}A_w,
\]
\[
y(u)=D_g R e^{\alpha u K}p,\qquad
D_g=\operatorname{diag}(g_1,\ldots,g_{189}).
\]

All h, w, g and alpha are positive and fixed during calibration and subsequent
acquisition. u is logger time and t=alpha u is time in a chosen reference
unit after setting the preparation event to zero. This is an affine clock
with known origin; offsets, nonlinear drift and jitter are separately scoped.

**CANDIDATE choices:** H is scalar on each chain grade, the evolution rule is
K=H^(-1)A_w, readout errors are diagonal gains, offsets are zero, and known
chain-coordinate preparations are available. These choices are not derived
as native physical laws. H is a chain-space metric, not a spacetime metric.
The reference-time convention does not derive physical seconds from UD.

The exact identities Ai Aj=0 for i!=j follow from consecutive boundary maps
multiplying to zero. Their active subspaces are mutually orthogonal. On the
kth active subspace K has off-diagonal blocks -dk Bk and uk Bk^T, where

\[
d_k=\frac{w_k}{h_{k-1}},\qquad
u_k=\frac{w_k}{h_k},\qquad
q=(d_1,u_1,d_2,u_2,d_3,u_3).
\]

Consequently ||K(q)|| <=4 max_i qi, using the parent ||A||<4 bound and the
orthogonal active-subspace split. This norm bound is valid although K is
generally not skew in the Euclidean metric. It is H-skew. Replacing a dense
H by grade scalars is a substantive restriction, not a change of notation.

## 2. Two scale ambiguities and their references

Even exact knowledge of all directed slopes leaves these transformations:

1. (alpha,w)->(c alpha,w/c), leaving the generator in logger time unchanged.
2. (H,w)->(cH,cw), leaving K unchanged.

In logarithmic coordinates the six logger-time slope magnitudes are
log alpha+log wk-log htarget. Their 6 by 8 parameter matrix has rank 6.
The two independent null directions are

\[
(\delta\log\alpha,\delta\log h,\delta\log w)
=(1,0,-\mathbf1_3),\quad (0,\mathbf1_4,\mathbf1_3).
\]

An independent **clock-scale observation alpha** and an independent
**metric-scale observation h0** remove these two ambiguities. Appending their
logarithms gives an integer 8 by 8 matrix of determinant -1. The reference
for h0 may be replaced by another independent scale constraint transverse to
the same null direction, such as an independently known rate. A convention
h0=1 selects a mathematical representative; it is not a measured physical
metric receipt. This protocol requires the declared h0 uncertainty if its
numerical metric-error guarantee is to be used.

Given alpha, the six reference-time ratios q and h0 determine every weight:

\[
\boxed{h_k=h_0\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{d_i}{u_i},\qquad
w_k=h_0d_k\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{d_i}{u_i}.}
\]

The transformation between (h0,h1,h2,h3,w1,w2,w3) and (h0,q) is a smooth
bijection on positive parameters. These are identifiability equations for
the chosen family, not physical estimates from existing data.

## 3. Three known preparations and the actual sensor coordinates

Let e_j denote the chain coordinate vector with coefficient 1 at coordinate j.
The fixed observed coordinates used dynamically are:

| Coordinate | Grade | Oriented simplex |
|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 0 | (1) |
| 133 | 1 | (1,11) |
| 486 | 1 | (33,34) |
| 878 | 2 | (1,11,87) |
| 1680 | 2 | (33,34,41) |
| 2040 | 3 | (0,33,34,41) |

All are in the existing 189-coordinate readout. Use these independent runs:

**Gain preparation:** pG=R^T 1_189. At the known preparation event u=0,
read all 189 outputs. The ideal vector is exactly g, independent of H and w.
The initial gain map has identity Jacobian. pG has 189 unit coefficients and
norm sqrt(189). Realizing and verifying this input is an external requirement:
one run here contains **189 known coordinate amplitudes**, not one unverified
scalar amplitude assumption. Unknown individual preparation amplitudes would
be confounded with the individual gains.

**Dynamic preparations:** pA=e1+e1680 and pB=e133+e2040. Their norms are
sqrt(2); the combined norm of pA direct-sum pB is 2. Choose logger h=1/32.
After independently preparing each, read the following at u=h, divide by its
calibrated individual sensor gain, and apply the indicated sign:

| Ratio feature | Preparation | Output coordinate | Sign |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| d1 | B | 1 | +1 |
| u1 | A | 133 | -1 |
| d2 | A | 486 | -1 |
| u2 | B | 878 | +1 |
| d3 | B | 1680 | -1 |
| u3 | A | 2040 | +1 |

Every named dynamic output has zero prepared coefficient. The six signed
initial slopes, divided by alpha, are exactly q. The full-carrier integer
jet matrix is I6. The preparations were chosen to avoid first-order mixing
of the directed channels in these six outputs. Higher-order mixing is retained
in the finite exponential map; it is not discarded.

The sensor count is 189 initial gain values plus six finite response values,
total 195. The clock and metric scale references add two scalars, total 197.
These counts assume the specified known preparations and model. They do not
establish globally minimal experimental effort or count the effort needed
to verify 189 preparation amplitudes. Optional initial/off-channel readings
would be additional model checks, not part of the rank count.

## 4. Finite-map theorem: no derivative oracle

Let L extract the six signed coordinates from the direct-sum states for runs
A and B. For known alpha define

\[
\Psi_\alpha(q)=\frac{1}{h\alpha}\mathcal L
 \left(e^{h\alpha K(q)}p_A\oplus
       e^{h\alpha K(q)}p_B\right).
\]

Each preparation is supported on one grade parity, while its extracted outputs
have the opposite parity. Since K flips parity, every even Taylor power
vanishes in these outputs. Thus Psi=q plus odd-power terms starting at order 3.
Let gains, alpha and q_i lie in [15/16,17/16]; let h0 and its estimate also
lie in that interval. This box is in **directed ratios**, not independently
in all h and w. Reconstructed h and w can span a wider range before acceptance.

For a directed generator derivative Ti, ||Ti||<4. The derivative of K^n is
the sum of n products K^r Ti K^(n-1-r), so its norm is <=4n||K||^(n-1).
The combined preparation has norm 2. Summing the odd powers n>=3 gives
each Jacobian error column norm <=8[cosh(z)-1], with
z=4h alpha max qi. A Frobenius bound over six columns yields

\[
\|D\Psi_\alpha-I_6\|
\le8\sqrt6[\cosh(289/2048)-1]
<\frac15.
\]

The interval-enclosed expression is approximately 0.195430324. Integrating
the Jacobian along segments in the convex ratio box proves the **global**
inequalities

\[
\boxed{\frac45\|q-q'\|\le
\|\Psi_\alpha(q)-\Psi_\alpha(q')\|
\le\frac65\|q-q'\|.}
\]

Hence Psi is one-to-one and the normalized six-ratio Jacobian has condition
number <3/2 throughout the box. Its determinant magnitude is >(4/5)^6.
This does not give a condition number <3/2 for raw sensor voltages, the log
metric reconstruction, or the entire 197-parameter problem. Dividing by
sensor gain and h alpha amplifies raw errors, and scale references contribute
their own uncertainty.

With all gain readings, the two scale references and the six finite responses,
the full parameter map is globally identifiable on this domain and has
Jacobian rank **197**. The proof is block triangular: 189 gain coordinates,
the two scale observations, and the invertible six-ratio map, followed by the
smooth metric/rate reconstruction. At the jet level the ranks are 195 without
scale anchors, 196 with clock anchor only, and 197 with both anchors.

## 5. Constructive inverse and uncertainty propagation

For normalized finite data z, use

\[
q_{n+1}=\Pi_\Omega[q_n+z-\Psi_{\widehat\alpha}(q_n)],
\quad \Omega=[15/16,17/16]^6.
\]

This is a contraction with factor <1/5. It is defined even when noisy z is
outside the model image. If its certified fixed-point residual is <=rs and
||z-Psi_alphahat(q)||<=B, then

\[
\|\widehat q-q\|\le\epsilon_q:=\frac54(B+r_s).
\]

The same nonexpansive-projection argument as in the preceding calibration
applies. From any starting point in the box, 17 iterations suffice for a
residual below 10^(-12) in exact arithmetic, using the box diameter sqrt(6)/8.
Actual arithmetic/evaluation error must be enclosed in a certified residual.

Let epsilon0 bound the error in log h0, and let epsilon_log=epsilon_q/(15/16).
The mean-value theorem for log gives componentwise log-ratio errors at most
epsilon_log. Reconstruction then gives

\[
|\Delta\log h_k|\le\epsilon_0+2k\epsilon_{\log},\quad
|\Delta\log w_k|\le\epsilon_0+(2k-1)\epsilon_{\log}.
\]

The exact 7 by 7 log reconstruction matrix is integer, with Frobenius norm
squared 28. Its rows explicitly accumulate the ratio uncertainties; no
claim that reconstruction is perfectly conditioned is made.

If h0 and h0hat are in the declared box, both true and estimated weights obey
hmax=83521/54000 and wmax=83521/57600. Uniform absolute ceilings are therefore

\[
\epsilon_H=h_{\max}[e^{\epsilon_0+6\epsilon_{\log}}-1],\quad
\epsilon_w=w_{\max}[e^{\epsilon_0+5\epsilon_{\log}}-1].
\]

## 6. Candidate precision contract

These are sufficient proposed requirements, not measured apparatus performance
or theory constants. Let l=15/16, u=17/16, OmegaK=4u, h=1/32.

| Quantity | Exact ceiling | Norm/type |
|---|---:|---|
| Gain preparation error at its readout | 1/10^13 | Infinity norm of observed prepared coefficients |
| Initial gain-read noise | 1/10^13 | Infinity norm, 189 outputs |
| Dynamic preparation error | 1/10^13 | Combined two-run Euclidean state norm |
| Dynamic sensor noise | 1/10^13 | Euclidean norm of six scalars |
| Clock-scale estimate error | 1/10^12 | Absolute alpha error |
| Dynamic calibration interval jitter | 1/10^15 | Absolute reference-time interval error |
| Metric-scale reference error | 1/10^11 | Absolute error in log h0 |
| Certified projected solver residual | 1/10^12 | Normalized ratio-feature norm |

Clip gain and clock estimates to their known box. The individual gain error
is <=epsilon_g=u xiG+nuG=33/(16 times 10^13). No independent-noise assumption
or stochastic averaging is used. Constant gains and stable clock/rates/metric
are required across the different runs and later acquisition.

For dynamic combined preparation error xi, raw six-value noise nu, clock error
epsilon_alpha and calibration jitter jcal, set
E=exp[OmegaK(uh+jcal)]. A valid feature-error ceiling is

\[
B=\frac{E(\nu+2\epsilon_g+u\xi)/l
       +2\Omega_K E(h\epsilon_\alpha+j_{\rm cal})}{hl}.
\]

The factor 2 is the combined nominal preparation norm. The exponential factor
is retained because K is not Euclidean-skew. The gain error is diagonal, so
its operator norm is the maximum relative gain error; a factor sqrt(189) is
not required for this particular operator bound.

256-bit interval arithmetic gives these conservative ceilings:

| Recovered quantity | Exact declared error ceiling | Enclosed bound, display only |
|---|---:|---:|
| Four metric weights, maximum absolute error | 5/10^10 | 4.821588 times 10^(-10) |
| Three rates, maximum absolute error | 4/10^10 | 3.791033 times 10^(-10) |
| Six-ratio vector error | Exact expression above | 4.714638 times 10^(-11) |

They are deterministic conditional bounds, not confidence intervals. The
very small input ceilings and reference requirements are experimental design
burdens; satisfying the mathematical inequalities does not demonstrate their
feasibility in a particular device.

**Acceptance rule:** require each estimated metric weight and each estimated
rate to be within 2/10^9 of 1. The error ceilings then imply
||H-I||<3/10^9 and max|wk-1|<3/10^9. Merely estimating parameters accurately
does not show that these parameters are near nominal values; measurements
must pass this gate. No feedback or physical parameter adjustment is assumed.

After dividing future sensor readings by their individual gain estimates,
the residual readout error is <=epsilon_g/l, below 1/100000. This conclusion
uses diagonal gains. It does not control an arbitrary matrix of cross-talk.

Schedule logger times at tj/alphahat for tj=j/2. For the 8192-snapshot profile,
clock-scale error contributes at most 4.368534 times 10^(-9) reference-time
units. Separately certifying acquisition jitter <=1/10^6 keeps total error
below the parent 3/10^6 ceiling for all three profiles. A short clock reference
does not itself certify long-term clock stability.

Under these accepted checks and the declared family, the parent full-state
conditions apply to gain-normalized data: rank 2640, kernel 0, condition
numbers <748,<375,<306 for M=2048,4096,8192. Additive-noise receipts must also
be normalized by the individual estimated gains. The combined noiseless
calibration-plus-unknown-state inverse has Jacobian rank 197+2640=2837,
conditional on these parent observation bounds and a stable plant.

## 7. What this result leaves open

**General metric NO-GO remains.** The previously constructed harmonic metric
family H=I+eta u0u0^T/120 leaves H^(-1)A=A at unit rates. That family is
excluded by the grade-scalar restriction. This extension therefore does not
invalidate the general-metric obstruction. It identifies a declared finite
family using a new independent metric-scale reference.

**Readout-family validation remains.** The initial gain vector can absorb an
unknown contribution E pG if actual readout is Dg R+E. These 195 sensor values
do not establish that E=0, nor that offsets, drift and nonlinearities vanish.
Off-diagonal metric terms may also violate the finite family. Held-out probes
with explicit detectable alternatives and thresholds are required to test
model discrepancy before applying this calibration as an experimental claim.

**Preparation and scale references remain external.** Known vector amplitude,
relative coefficients and addresses are not supplied by topology. An h0
normalization convention is not an empirical metric identification. No
native law selecting these apparatus quantities is derived here.

## 8. Verification, source status and governance

`python certify_grade_calibration.py` reproduces the exact observed simplex
selection, full-carrier cross-channel identities, gain map and directed jet,
symbolic two-scale ranks, the parity-based finite bound, precision propagation,
three rational forward evaluations and one synthetic inverse round trip.
Integer weighted incidence powers produce exact rational Taylor sums. Degree
32 and the general exponential remainder give feature-vector error <10^(-50)
throughout the box. The finite rank theorem is analytical and uniform; three
point checks alone would not prove it. Clean replay uses a fresh directory
with identical frozen inputs. Constructor checks are not independent review.

A pre-release interval residual evaluation needed repair near exact zero;
CORRECTIONS.json records it. It did not change an earlier capture or the
analytic rank/uncertainty theorems. All source versions and prior captures
remain immutable.

The attached coefficient ledger's O03 controls, Q139 clock gap, Q165 support
carrier and Q169 generator remain scoped. No ledger entry is edited. The
attached CRL-2 amendment labels itself a proposal; this work remains in its
development distinction and makes no registry promotion. Attachments were
read for provenance and are not redistributed. The unavailable Genesis image
was not used. Repository main and the parent local captures are source-bound
in PROVENANCE.json. Local capture is separate from public publication.

**Next gate:** specify held-out tests for off-diagonal metric terms, sensor
cross-talk and temporal drift, prove what those probes can detect, and attach
explicit rejection thresholds. An independent reviewer and an apparatus
implementation are still required before experimental qualification.
