content:
# UD Hankel excitation and coefficient field audit

**RESULT — The proposed Hankel indexing is valid, but adding shifted columns from one initial state cannot produce rank 1893. Its rank is at most 105. Furthermore, the canonical characteristic-13 observability rank is 1877, which remains 1877 over the degree-12 extension.** Multiple preparation columns address excitation; a larger coefficient field cannot undo rank loss caused by reduction modulo thirteen.

Physical promotion remains **0**. This is a development calculation with no registry entry and independent review pending. The earlier real conditioning certificates are not changed or reverified here.

## Three ranks that must remain distinct

Let A be the frozen real unit-metric 2640-by-2640 generator and R the original 62-channel coordinate observer. The exact observability operator is

\[
O_{105}=\begin{bmatrix}R\\RA\\\vdots\\RA^{104}\end{bmatrix}
\in\mathbb R^{6510\times2640},\qquad \operatorname{rank}O_{105}=1893.
\]

For a single unknown state x, the history `Y=O105 x` is a 6510-entry column. That column can encode all **1893 observable state coordinates** when the operator O105 is known. Its matrix rank of one does not mean it contains only one state degree of freedom. What fails is using the SVD of one data column to infer the dimension or basis of the whole observable space.

The same distinction applies to a time-shifted Hankel matrix. Its rank measures the subspace excited by the selected preparations and visible in the outputs; it need not equal the system's observability rank. A single trajectory can reveal vector-valued amplitudes at many frequencies while providing only one temporal column-space direction per distinct eigenvalue.

## Exact factorization and the one-trajectory obstruction

For `y_k=R A^k x0`, define the block Hankel matrix by

\[
H_{L,M}(x_0)_{(k,c),j}=(R A^{k+j}x_0)_c,
\quad0\le k<L,\quad0\le c<62,\quad0\le j<M.
\]

It has dimensions `62L by M` and factors exactly:

\[
H_{L,M}(x_0)=O_L K_M(x_0),\qquad
K_M(x_0)=[x_0,Ax_0,\ldots,A^{M-1}x_0].
\]

The frozen real generator has degree-105 minimal polynomial. Hence its powers above order104 reduce to lower powers, so

\[
\operatorname{rank}H_{105,M}(x_0)
\le\operatorname{rank}K_M(x_0)
\le\min(M,105).
\]

This bound holds even for 1893 columns or arbitrarily many columns. A generic real initial state can reach the temporal bound105 when all visible eigenvalues are excited, but it cannot span repeated-eigenvalue state directions merely through time shifts. `M>=1893` is only a necessary column-count condition for rank 1893 in an arbitrary matrix, and is insufficient for this structured matrix.

The supplied code also checks a small exact counterexample: A consists of three identical two-dimensional rotation blocks, and R is the six-dimensional identity. The system is fully observable with rank 6. A single-state Hankel matrix with 12 rows and 7 columns has rank 2. Three independent preparations raise the corresponding block Hankel rank to6. This illustrates why observable state dimension and one-trajectory Hankel rank differ.

The frozen recurrence can be written `p(A)=0`, where

\[
p(t)=t\,\left(q_L(x)/x\right)\big|_{x=-t^2},
\qquad\deg q_L=53,\quad\deg p=105.
\]

The real annihilator follows from the earlier exact full-carrier certificate and real skew-adjoint semisimplicity. In this audit, the reduced row identity `R p(A)=0 mod13` is checked directly as well. It makes the 105-column bound and finite history stabilization valid for the reduced output sequences without assuming finite-field semisimplicity.

## Correct multi-preparation structure

Choose p independently prepared states and collect them as

\[
X=[x_1,\ldots,x_p]\in\mathbb R^{2640\times p}.
\]

The corrected response Hankel matrix is

\[
H_{L,M}(X)=\left[RA^{k+j}X\right]_{k,j}
=O_L[X,AX,\ldots,A^{M-1}X].
\]

Its dimensions are `62L by pM`. A fully explicit flattened index is

\[
i=62k+c,\quad \ell=pj+a,\quad
H_{i,\ell}=(R A^{k+j}x_{a+1})_c,
\]

with `0<=a<p`. The block Hankel consistency condition relates the same preparation and channel: increasing k by one is equivalent to increasing j by one, whenever both indices remain in range. To build L-by-M windows, each preparation needs the derivative sequence through order `L+M-2`, or `L+M-1` vectors in total. The proposed L=105,M=1893 matrix would therefore require 1997 derivative vectors, not 1893.

The real rank 1893 condition is

\[
\operatorname{im}[X,AX,\ldots,A^{M-1}X]+\ker O_{105}
=\mathbb R^{2640}.
\]

This is the missing excitation condition. Column count alone is not a substitute.

For unrestricted real preparations, the frozen modal rank table sharpens the requirement. On each nonzero irreducible L-factor of degree d, divide its real observable dimension by2d to obtain the observable multiplicity of each complex A-eigenvalue. The maximum is **37**, attained by the squared-frequency factor `L-4`, whose real observable dimension is74. A single preparation supplies at most one direction within each complex eigenspace, so **at least37 preparations** are necessary.

For the semisimple real observable quotient,37 generic preparations are also sufficient when M=105: degree104 interpolation isolates every distinct eigenvalue, and the projected preparations generically span each visible eigenspace. The resulting sufficient layout has dimensions **6510 by 3885**, using 209 derivative vectors per preparation. This is an existence and genericity theorem; no specific 37 preparations or their conditioning are certified in this audit. It does not claim that M=105 is the smallest possible shift horizon.

A straightforward guaranteed alternative is `X=I2640`, M=1: the response matrix is exactly O105, with dimensions 6510 by 2640 and real rank 1893. This uses 2640 known basis preparations. Neither derivative design replaces the earlier bounded-error finite-sampling protocol.

## Exact characteristic thirteen calculation

The follow-up assumes that real rank 1893 carries into the degree-12 field. It does not. Reducing the actual integer A and R modulo13 and stacking the 105 derivative blocks gives:

| Coefficient field | Rows | Columns | Rank | Kernel dimension |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Real numbers, frozen parent result | 6510 | 2640 | 1893 | 747 |
| F13, computed in this audit | 6510 | 2640 | **1877** | **763** |
| F_(13^12), same matrix after scalar extension | 6510 | 2640 | **1877** | **763** |

The modular rank was computed by exact elimination and rechecked by reduced row echelon form. A full 763-column kernel basis is included. Its free-coordinate submatrix is the identity, proving independence, and exact multiplication verifies `O105 N=0`. The reduced recurrence proves stabilization for all further formal power observations.

Field extension preserves the rank of a fixed matrix. Thus even all basis preparations cannot reach rank 1893 over this canonical reduced model. The drop of16 is a coefficient-field effect, not an extra physical loss or a contradiction of the real result. A redesigned field-valued generator would be a new model requiring its own calculation.

## Field indexing does not supply SVD or an exponential clock

Each field entry can validly be expanded as

\[
H_{(k,c),(j,a)}=\sum_{r=0}^2\sum_{s=0}^3
C_{k,c,j,a,r,s}\,b^r g^s,\qquad C_{k,c,j,a,r,s}\in\mathbb F_{13}.
\]

Use equality in the polynomial extension field. Integer congruence modulo13^12 denotes a different ring. The four powers `1,g,g^2,g^3` are a coefficient basis, not four or ten separate character sectors. The ten sectors are selected by the projectors P_m. The cubic powers likewise have no demonstrated identification as color or gauge components.

Ordinary real SVD and positive singular-value thresholds are not finite-field rank procedures. Use exact elimination over the stated field. A full restriction-of-scalars representation of an F_(13^12)-linear map uses12-by 12 multiplication blocks and multiplies both its domain/codomain dimensions and rank by 12. Merely listing twelve coefficients in each entry is not that construction and supplies no new observable state information.

Also distinguish derivative sequences from actual sampled dynamics. Over the reals, uniformly sampled data use `T=exp(Delta A)` and `y_j=R T^j x0`; their Hankel factorization uses T, not A. Since T is a function of the frozen semisimple A, one real trajectory still has at most105 temporal directions, potentially fewer under aliasing. Over characteristic13 the usual exponential series is not defined as written: factorials from 13 onward are noninvertible. A discrete transition matrix or another explicit valid construction must be supplied before using finite-field time samples.

There is still no derived nonabelian gauge spectrum or revived 1146 index theorem. Correct data layout and exact arithmetic answer excitation and rank questions. They do not select physical symmetries or calibrate an observation clock.

## Recommended next step

Use the real model for the existing finite-sample physical-bridge candidate. Select and certify independent preparations against the actual modal excitation condition, with explicit error bounds and conditioning. Keep the finite-field layer as a separate algebraic verification model with its measured rank 1877. A specific 37-preparation construction is a candidate next task, not an achieved result here.

title: HELD OUT DISCREPANCY CONTRACT v0.1
note: Recovered earlier package; original source scope retained. Independent review not established; physical promotion 0.
content:
# UD held-out discrepancy contract v0.1

**RESULT / STATUS — DERIVED CONDITIONAL; development — no registry entry.**
This contract separates a compact fault screen from a complete-basis coverage
benchmark. It gives explicit rejection thresholds for cross-talk, departures
from the fitted dynamics and observable drift. Under a repeatable linear
time-invariant plant, passing the complete-basis frame test would certify the
actual finite observer's rank 2640, kernel 0 and condition number <748. This
does not require the actual metric to be grade scalar or actual readout to be
diagonal. No experiment has been run. Physical promotion = 0; constructor
checks passed; independent review pending.

## 1. Freeze the predictor before taking held-out data

Retain the prior 197-parameter calibration and the 189-coordinate observer.
Freeze fitted gains ghat, clock scale alphahat, metric Hhat and generator
Khat=Hhat^(-1) A_what before acquiring the probes below. Do not refit these
parameters on held-out measurements. A rejection may motivate a new version
and a new held-out dataset; reusing the same data after refitting is not an
independent validation test.

Use reference-time coordinates t=alphahat u and gain-normalized outputs.
The fitted predictor is R exp(t Khat)p. Under the declared null family, the
true normalized readout C differs from R by at most gamma, and the true
effective generator in these reference-time coordinates differs from Khat
by at most epsilon. From the preceding candidate precision contract, take

\[
\eta=3/10^9,\quad r_{\rm fit}=2/10^9,\quad
\Delta_H=5/10^{10},\quad\Delta_w=4/10^{10},\quad l=15/16,
\]
\[
\epsilon_g=33/(16\cdot10^{13}),\quad
\gamma=\epsilon_g/l,\quad
\Gamma=\sqrt{(1+\eta)/(1-\eta)},\quad
K_{\max}=4(1+\eta)/(1-\eta),
\]
\[
\epsilon=\frac{4\Delta_w}{1-\eta}
 +\frac{4(1+r_{\rm fit})\Delta_H}{(1-\eta)^2}
 +K_{\max}\frac{1/10^{12}}{l}.
\]

The final term accounts for constant clock-scale uncertainty. Both null
propagators have norm <=Gamma for all real time. Their Duhamel difference
is <=Gamma^2 epsilon t for t>=0. The frozen model itself has a certified
2048-snapshot normalized minimum singular-value lower bound

\[
s_{\rm fit}=\frac{97}{100}\frac1{512\sqrt2}.
\]

These are conditional mathematical inputs. If the calibration model is false,
they need not describe the actual plant. Their role is to bound discrepancies
under the null and to certify the frozen predictor, not to assume the actual
plant belongs to the null while testing it.

## 2. Instrument contract and decision rule

The candidate validation error ceiling is

\[
e_{\rm col}=1/10^{13}.
\]

It bounds the Euclidean error in each complete 189-output, gain-normalized,
blank-corrected response vector for a specified unit preparation at a
specified reference time. It includes sensor noise, preparation contamination,
timing error, normalization arithmetic and blank correction. This is a
**total response error requirement**, not a claim that a preparation error of
the same size remains bounded under an arbitrary unstable plant. An apparatus
must independently justify this ceiling. No independent-noise assumption or
statistical averaging is used.

The zero-preparation blank is also bounded by ecol in response norm under the
zero-offset null. A blank response tests additive offsets; subtracting it
does not make an offset-free model empirically true. The total corrected
response error must include uncertainty in that subtraction.

For every statistic use a verified interval enclosure. Reject when its lower
bound is above the threshold, pass when its upper bound is at or below the
threshold, and refine or report inconclusive when the interval straddles it.
Numerical prediction error must be enclosed. The thresholds are deterministic
error budgets, not significance levels or estimated false-positive rates.

## 3. Compact targeted screen

Prepare the blank p=0 and six separate unit coordinate states

\[
p\in\{e_0,e_4,e_{120},e_{152},e_{928},e_{2040}\}.
\]

These are held out from the three mixed calibration preparations. Coordinates
0 and 120 are outside the readout; coordinate 120 is edge (0,33). The other
roles include all four chain degrees. Read all 189 outputs at reference times
0,1/32,1/16,1/2. Repeat the seven-preparation block at an early and a late
wall-clock epoch using the same preparation and relative-time schedule.
Cost: 2 times 7 times 4 times 189 = **10584 scalar outputs**.

For unit inputs let z(t,p) be corrected normalized data. Reject the frozen
prediction when

\[
\|z(t,p)-R e^{t\widehat K}p\|>
T(t):=\gamma\Gamma+\Gamma^2\epsilon t+e_{\rm col}+e_{\rm eval},
\quad e_{\rm eval}=1/10^{20}.
\]

| Reference time | Null residual threshold, display approximation |
|---:|---:|
| 0 | 3.200001 times 10^(-13) |
| 1/32 | 1.129534 times 10^(-10) |
| 1/16 | 2.255867 times 10^(-10) |
| 1/2 | 1.802454 times 10^(-9) |

The exact expressions and interval enclosures, not rounded values, define the
thresholds. A true response discrepancy above the null allowance plus twice
the instrument/evaluation error is guaranteed to reject. At time zero, for an
input outside the readout, the null response is exactly zero for every metric,
rate and diagonal gain; use the sharper ecol threshold for cross-talk leakage.
For the blank use threshold ecol and guaranteed offset detection above 2ecol.

**Observable drift:** compare the two blocks directly, with no model refit:

\[
D(t,p)=\|z_{\rm late}(t,p)-z_{\rm early}(t,p)\|.
\]

Reject stationarity if D>2ecol. A true response change >4ecol is guaranteed
to reject. Calibration uncertainty cancels because the same frozen predictor
and normalization are used in both blocks. The statistic does not identify
whether gain, generator, clock, offsets or preparation changed. It detects
response drift at the tested epochs and inputs, not every parameter drift.

## 4. Two actual-carrier synthetic fault demonstrations

These are mathematical fault injections, not empirical results.

**Cross-talk missed by the calibration.** Add
E=epsilon times output_row4 times input_column0^T to the readout, with
epsilon=1/10^9. The original gain preparation has zero coefficient at input0,
and none of its six dynamic calibration outputs was row4. Thus all 197
original calibration scalars are exactly unchanged. The new input e0 at time
zero produces leakage epsilon in observed coordinate4, far above the 2ecol
guaranteed-detection threshold.

**Excluded metric accepted by the calibration.** At unit rates and clock take

\[
H_\rho=I+\rho(e_0e_4^T+e_4e_0^T),\qquad \rho=1/10^6.
\]

This is SPD with eigenvalues 1+rho,1-rho and 1 elsewhere, and
||Hrho-I||=rho. It is not grade scalar. For K=Hrho^(-1)A,

\[
K[4,120]=-\frac{\rho}{1-\rho^2},
\]

where every grade-scalar candidate has zero direct incidence entry there.
Exact rational Taylor evaluation of the six original finite calibration
responses, followed by the prescribed projected fit, gives fitted q,h,w all
equal to 1 at the stored rational precision. The certified feature residual
is <10^(-12) (enclosed expression approximately 5.54 times 10^(-19)), so the
original estimated-parameter acceptance gates pass. The independent metric
reference at a diagonal unit coefficient also agrees with 1 in this example.

The held-out edge input e120, output4, at t=1/32 instead has a certified
prediction-residual magnitude **>3/10^8**, exceeding twice the screen threshold.
The signal lower bound is approximately 3.112296433 times 10^(-8).
This certifies detection of this alternative; it is not a universal lower
bound on the observability of every metric perturbation of that norm.

## 5. Complete-basis coverage benchmark

The compact screen cannot validate arbitrary readout columns or arbitrary
generator directions. For a complete benchmark, prepare every e_l,
l=0,...,2639, on the same repeatable linear time-invariant plant. Collect all
189 outputs at both schedules

\[
t_j=j/2,\quad t_j+\delta,\qquad j=0,\ldots,2047,
\quad\delta=1/32.
\]

Include a zero-input run for blank correction. Gain normalization is fixed
from the preceding calibration. The last reference time is 2047/2+1/32.
Each relative-time response block is an empirical 189 by 2640 unit-response
matrix. Form the normalized operators

\[
F=2048^{-1/2}\operatorname{stack}_j C e^{t_jK},\qquad
G=2048^{-1/2}\operatorname{stack}_j C e^{(t_j+\delta)K}.
\]

K here denotes the actual effective generator in the frozen reference-time
coordinates, with no grade-metric or diagonal-readout assumption. Let Fm,Gm
be their measured estimates. The response-error contract implies

\[
\|F_m-F\|,\|G_m-G\|\le
\varepsilon_V:=\sqrt{2640}\,e_{\rm col}.
\]

Proof: the normalized stacked error in each input column is <=ecol; sum
squared column bounds to obtain a Frobenius bound, hence an operator bound.
The normalized sample count does not introduce another sqrt(2048) factor.

**Cost:** 2640 times 4096 times 189 = **2043740160 sensor scalars**, or
2044514304 including one blank run. This is a complete-coverage benchmark,
not a practical sensor-minimal design. No such dataset was allocated or
generated. A streamed/sharded implementation can accumulate Gram statistics;
verified operator-norm bounds are required. Substituting a Frobenius residual
into the same null threshold without changing its uncertainty bound is invalid.

### 5.1 Arbitrary static cross-talk

At t=0, the full unit-response matrix is C. Mask out, in each output row, its
single allowed coordinate from R. Let Lm be the Frobenius norm of all remaining
measured entries. Under diagonal readout the true masked matrix is zero.
Reject if

\[
L_m>\varepsilon_V.
\]

Passing implies masked cross-talk Frobenius norm <=2epsilonV, hence operator
norm <=2epsilonV. The enclosed bound is <1.028 times 10^(-11). Cross-talk
operator norm >2/10^11 is therefore guaranteed to reject. These units refer
to gain-normalized readout. Unknown diagonal gain changes are not called
cross-talk by this statistic; they are tested by the frozen-frame comparison.

### 5.2 Direct validation of the finite observer

Let Fhat be the exact frozen-model history operator. Test

\[
\|F_m-\widehat F\|\le T_A:=1/400000.
\]

Under the null, the residual is bounded by

\[
\gamma\Gamma+\Gamma^2\epsilon T_{\rm rms}+\varepsilon_V<T_A,
\quad T_{\rm rms}^2=2047\cdot4095/24.
\]

If the test passes, irrespective of whether the actual H and C belong to the
calibration family,

\[
\sigma_{\min}(F)\ge s_*:=s_{\rm fit}-T_A-\varepsilon_V>0,
\quad\sigma_{\max}(F)\le\Gamma+T_A+\varepsilon_V.
\]

The interval calculation gives s_*>0.0013371358889 and
(Gamma+TA+epsilonV)/s_*<748. Thus the actual finite observer has **rank2640,
kernel0 and condition<748**, conditional on linearity, repeatability and the
response-error contract. A simulated or proposed pass is not an empirical pass.

### 5.3 Short-step dynamical consistency

Let Qhat=exp(delta Khat). Test the held-out shift residual

\[
\|G_m-F_m\widehat Q\|\le T_B:=1/(8\cdot10^9).
\]

Using measured Fm here cancels the long-duration prediction error. Under a
constant null plant, G=FQ with Q=exp(delta K), and

\[
\|G_m-F_m\widehat Q\|
\le(1+\gamma)\Gamma^3\epsilon\delta
    +\varepsilon_V(1+\Gamma)<T_B.
\]

The enclosed expression is approximately 1.229095211 times 10^(-10).
If both frame and shift tests pass, then

\[
\boxed{\|Q-\widehat Q\|\le
\frac{T_B+\varepsilon_V(1+\Gamma)}{s_*}}
\]

with enclosed upper-bound expression approximately 1.011686151 times 10^(-7).
This bound permits arbitrary constant actual C and K. It follows from
F(Q-Qhat)=G-F Qhat and the independently established lower singular bound.
Comparing Gm only with the frozen Ghat would retain a long-horizon parameter
uncertainty and give a much weaker result.

### 5.4 Continuous generator: an extra bandwidth assumption

To infer a continuous generator, additionally require ||K||<=5 in the fixed
coordinates. The fitted generator also satisfies this ceiling. Then
||exp(delta K)-I||<=r=exp(5/32)-1<1. The convergent logarithm series gives

\[
\|K-\widehat K\|\le
\frac{32}{2-e^{5/32}}\|Q-\widehat Q\|,
\quad \frac{32}{2-e^{5/32}}<40.
\]

Proof: for ||X||,||Y||<=r<1, expand log(I+X)-log(I+Y); each nth difference
is bounded by n r^(n-1)||X-Y||, canceling the factor1/n and summing to
1/(1-r). The same convergent series satisfies log(exp(delta K))=delta K
on this norm ball, for example by differentiating along sK where the series
converges and all terms commute. The combined interval ceiling is

\[
\boxed{\|K-\widehat K\|<1/250000.}
\]

Thus a constant bounded generator discrepancy above this ceiling cannot pass
both tests under the instrument contract. This is an operator validation
bound, not a direct metric-norm bound. It is looser than the original
generator calibration budget. The direct frame test certifies finite
observability without needing to turn this generator bound into a long-time
perturbation estimate.

## 6. Exact blind spots and scope limits

**Metric shadow:** u0 is uniform on the 120 vertex coordinates and zero
elsewhere. Au0=0 exactly. H=I+eta u0u0^T/120 is SPD for eta>-1 and satisfies
H^(-1)A=A. Every dynamical probe, including a complete basis sweep, gives the
same histories. A metric norm/energy measurement is needed to distinguish
this family; it must not be dismissed as gauge without an independent rule.

**Few-input blind directions:** under the nominal skew generator there are
105 distinct temporal frequencies. Each prepared vector spans at most105
dimensions under all powers of A. The original three preparations therefore
span at most315 dimensions over all time. At least2325 input directions per
readout row can support an added E annihilating all those trajectories. This
is a lower bound on blindness, not a computed exact dimension. A handful of
successful probe histories cannot validate arbitrary cross-talk.

**Sampling alias:** on the active space define the real complex structure
J=A(-A^2)^(-1/2), and J=0 on ker A. It commutes with A and J^2=-I on the
active space. The real skew generator Kprime=A+64 pi J has exactly the same
propagators as A at every multiple of1/32, since its extra exponential is
exp(2 pi n J)=I. All specified rational-grid probes miss this high-frequency
alternative. The generator norm ceiling above is essential; a finite-grid
pass alone cannot establish it.

**Drift between epochs:** finite tests cannot exclude unsampled bursts. For an
externally justified response Lipschitz constant L in wall-clock time and
maximum sampling gap Delta, passing sampled paired-drift tests implies a
continuous response bound <=4ecol+L Delta/2 inside the bracketed interval.
Without L, only sampled-epoch claims follow. Common time-dependent metric/rate
rescaling can also leave K unchanged, so independent scale references must
be monitored if parameter stability itself is claimed.

**Linearity and repeatability:** basis response matrices identify an LTI
operator only when the same linear plant is used across runs. Finite probes
cannot establish unrestricted linearity, exclude arbitrary nonlinearities
vanishing on the tested trajectories, or certify a time-varying plant by
silently assembling different runs into one matrix. Amplitude/superposition
checks and stability receipts are additional requirements with their own
detectable alternative classes.

## 7. Reproduction and remaining gate

Run `python certify_discrepancy.py` with the pinned requirements. It certifies
the null thresholds, conditional frame rank/conditioning, generator bound,
actual-carrier cross-talk blindness and harmonic witness, and exact rational
finite responses for the excluded-metric fault followed by calibration refit
and held-out rejection. Taylor remainders are enclosed; no decimal fit is
treated as proof. The complete-basis acquisition is a compact schedule, not a
generated or executed dataset. Constructor verification is not independent
adversarial review.

Ledger entries O03, Q139, Q165 and Q169 remain scoped; no coefficient ledger
entry is modified. The attached CRL-2 amendment labels itself a proposal.
This work stays in the development distinction and makes no registry claim.
Attachments are not redistributed; the unavailable Genesis image was unused.
Source hashes, clean replay, parent captures and publication status accompany
the contract. Public publication is separate from local capture.

**Next gate:** reduce the complete-basis cost for an explicitly restricted
discrepancy family, while retaining certified coverage and detection limits;
then map preparations, error receipts and scale references to a concrete
apparatus and obtain independent review. A smaller probe set is defensible
only after its remaining blind directions are quantified.

title: HELD OUT VALIDATION v0.1
note: Recovered earlier package; original source scope retained. Independent review not established; physical promotion 0.
content:
# UD held-out sampled validation v0.1

**RESULT / STATUS — REPAIRED PROPOSAL; DERIVED CONDITIONAL certificate.**
The supplied script cannot validate the fitted UD generator. It does not
parse as written, substitutes random dense matrices for the frozen model,
and constructs its purported truth directly from its prediction. Its residual
therefore measures the injected noise. Its thresholds also omit the certified
parameter uncertainty. The replacement package provides three frozen rational
probes, the actual 600-cell incidence generator, a finite propagator with
certified numerical error, exact residual decisions and synthetic fault controls.

The correct sampled threshold is

\[
 \boxed{\tau(t)=\frac{11}{2^{49}}+\frac5{2^{39}}t,\qquad
 t=j/32,\quad j=0,\ldots,24.}
\]

This is a sufficient null envelope under the stated model and metrology
receipts. A pass means consistency at the selected samples. No experimental
pass, unrestricted model identification, asymptotic stability or physical
promotion is claimed. Constructor verification passed; independent review
pending. Development lane; no registry entry.

## 1. Repairs to the synthesis and script

The previous six-ratio certificate proves a nonzero parameter-error bound by
exact arithmetic and interval inequalities. It does not make estimated
parameters exact. Three preparations and twelve readings were sufficient;
global minimality was not proved. The twelve readings consist of six initial
gain values and six outputs after one positive interval h=1/32. They are not
twelve time steps. The four auxiliary ports provide additional readout access,
not an invariant separation of shell and bulk. Inversion defect in normalized
ratio coordinates and raw measurement noise have different scaling.

The proposed code contains an invalid decimal literal `822d407`. Interpreting
the commit prefix as hexadecimal would fix syntax but would not make a random
matrix the certified UD operator. The real source is a sparse 2640-dimensional
incidence generator with 14880 signed entries and a fixed coordinate selector
R of norm 1. A generic fitted grade-scalar generator is skew with respect to
its fitted positive metric; it need not be Euclidean-skew.

The sign preparations already have squared norm 2640/52^2=165/169; floating
square-root rescaling is unnecessary. Gaussian draws do not obey a deterministic
hard noise bound. The draft evaluates the spectral norm but specifies a
Frobenius gate; it then compares the peak against 2^-39 instead of 2^-49.
The copied value 2^-55 bounds logger-interval error in the calibration contract,
not integrated residual energy. No transfer between these typed quantities was
proved.

Euler stepping is not exponential propagation: for real skew A,

\[
 \|(I+hA)x\|^2=\|x\|^2+h^2\|Ax\|^2.
\]

It increases the Euclidean stock on every active input. Finally,
`range(24)` reports states at times0,...,23/32. Twenty-four intervals through
24/32 require **25 snapshots**. This is a short finite horizon, rather than
a test of long-term recurrence or asymptotic stability. `AUDIT.json` records
18 scoped findings. The supplied script was statically inspected, not executed.

## 2. Frozen probes and acquisition plan

The new preparations X=[x38,x39,x40] have exactly 2640 coefficients each,
all ±1/52. Signs come from SHAKE256 using the domain recorded in DESIGN.json,
little-bit order and a2640x3 row-major layout. The numbering is a label;
freshness comes from the separate design and its frozen hash, not the numbers.
There is no assertion of statistical independence merely from different labels.

Each input has squared norm165/169; the combined squared Frobenius norm is
495/169. An exact modulo1009 Gram check proves that the three new inputs,
the previous37 history inputs and the three calibration inputs are jointly
linearly independent: rank43. This does not prove full dynamical excitation.

Use the original62-coordinate shell readout, at t_j=j/32 for j=0,...,24.
This requires **25x62x3=4650 scalar readings**. The first13 snapshots cover
0 through12/32; all25 cover0 through24/32=3/4. Those horizons are new protocol
choices. They do not inherit a twelve-step calibration horizon.

Freeze the actual six fitted effective ratios, probes, time grid, source hashes
and thresholds before examining validation outputs. Validation outputs must not
be used for parameter selection. The prediction file binds the fitted ratios,
source operator, design, engine and certificate through hashes. Hardware data
must be independently supplied. Synthetic controls are always labelled as such.

Only two of these62 channels were among the six diagnostic ports calibrated
previously. All62 gain corrections therefore require uncertainty receipts;
the twelve-value calibration alone does not supply them. Blank/offset correction
is included in the required noise receipt. No blank run is included in4650.

## 3. Null model and uniform propagator bound

Let K=K(q) and Khat=K(qhat) use the frozen incidence signs, with positive
effective ratios D1,U1,D2,U2,D3,U3 in Omega=[15/16,17/16]^6. These are
logger-time ratios, with the constant clock scale absorbed. Use the previous
uniform vector error delta=2^-40, conservatively above its tighter interval
bound. On the orthogonal incidence channel spaces,

\[
 \|K-Khat\|\le4\|q-qhat\|_\infty\le4\delta=:e=2^{-38},
 \qquad\|K\|,\|Khat\|\le\omega=17/4.
\]

Recover representative grade metrics h0=1 and
h_k=product_(j<=k)(D_j/U_j). The logarithmic metric spread across at most
three grade steps is bounded by3 log(17/15). Both propagators are thus bounded,
uniformly at every signed time, by

\[
 \|e^{tK}\|,\|e^{tKhat}\|
 \le g=(17/15)^{3/2}<1.206526.
\]

This uses metric skewness, avoiding an unnecessary exponentially growing
error estimate. Duhamel's identity gives

\[
 \|e^{tK}-e^{tKhat}\|\le g^2 e t\quad(t\ge0).
\]

It is a bound for the declared positive grade-scalar family; it cannot be
assumed for arbitrary extra generators or arbitrary time-varying systems.

## 4. Predictive thresholds from the complete error budget

Let b=||X||F=sqrt(495)/13. Under the joint null, gain-normalized readout is
C=R+E with ||E||≤rho. In the diagonal readout family, the external individual
gain uncertainties yield this modeled operator bound. Cross-talk beyond the
null is an alternative being tested, not something that three probes certify
absent. The remaining required ceilings are:

| Quantity | Exact ceiling | Scope |
|---|---:|---|
| Modeled62-channel gain/readout uncertainty rho | 2^-47 | Operator norm under the readout null |
| Preparation error xi | 2^-49 | Frobenius norm, all three runs combined |
| Corrected output noise nu | 2^-49 | Frobenius norm of62x3 matrix, at each sample |
| Timing error j | 2^-55 | Each validation run, logger units |
| Prediction numerical error eps | 2^-70 | Frobenius norm at each sample |

The parameters, gain corrections and model family must remain valid throughout
all calibration and validation runs. Receipt identifiers are external evidence
references; the module checks their presence and does not claim to verify their
truth. Missing receipts leave the result incomplete.

Separating generator, gain, preparation, timing, noise and numerical errors
gives, at each selected node,

\[
 \|R e^{tKhat}X-Y(t)\|_F\le a_0+a_1t,
\]
\[
 a_0=g[(1+\rho)\xi+\rho b+(1+\rho)b\omega j]+\nu+\epsilon,
 \qquad a_1=b g^2 e.
\]

The timing term allows different interval errors in the three runs; their
combined Frobenius contribution uses b. Uniform256-bit interval arithmetic
verifies

\[
 a_0<11/2^{49},\qquad a_1<5/2^{39}.
\]

Hence the boxed affine threshold strictly covers the null envelope. It includes
calibration uncertainty, rather than demanding raw noise-level prediction from
an uncertain fitted generator.

| Logger time | Exact gate | Approximate gate, display only |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 11/2^49 | 1.953993e-14 |
| 1/32 | 171/2^49 | 3.037570e-13 |
| 12/32 | 1931/2^49 | 3.430145e-12 |
| 24/32 | 3851/2^49 | 6.840751e-12 |

The module compares exact rational squared Frobenius norms with exact squared
thresholds. A node at or above threshold rejects the joint contract. This
does not assign a cause: preparation, timing, readout, generator, drift or
other model discrepancies can produce the same rejection.

## 5. Finite numerical implementation and controls

`validation_engine.py` uses the actual sparse incidence data. It forms integer
weighted powers, evaluates a degree80 Taylor series in256-bit Arb arithmetic,
and rounds predictions to exact dyadic rationals. At T=3/4, the uniform vector
Taylor remainder is bounded by

\[
 b e^{\omega T}(\omega T)^{81}/81!<2^{-100}.
\]

For every entry, an interval check certifies error from series evaluation and
dyadic rounding <2^-79. Combining186 entries and the vector remainder keeps
prediction error below2^-70. Alternative controls also pass an explicit
generator-norm certificate. No Euler stepping or random dense replacement is
used. The ordinary real norm and exponential remain separate from mod13 field
arithmetic; p=13 in the draft did not define its real propagator.

Ten gate tests pass, including these substantive controls:

| Control | Result and scope |
|---|---|
| Nominal fitted model | Consistent at every sample |
| True D1=1+2^-45, fitted D1=1; others1 | Realizable within the calibration noise budget; passes corrected gate but fails proposed2^-49 gate at12/32 |
| Readout C=R+2^-30 e_output0 e_input0^T | Rejected at t=0; twelve calibration readings unchanged because this output is uncalibrated |
| Generator A+2^-20(e33 e0^T−e0 e33^T) | Rejected at t=1/32; positive control of the response gate, with no claim it passes calibration first |

The allowed-ratio control has residual about3.16e-15 at12/32, exceeding the
proposed2^-49 gate despite being a legitimate calibrated null member. This is
a concrete counterexample, not merely an oversized conservative bound. The
six raw response changes can be canceled by calibration noise with combined
norm below2^-49, leaving observed data equal to the unit-ratio finite response.
The parent finite-map polynomial and its remainder certify this realization.

The cross-talk control has exact t0 signal norm2^-30 sqrt(3)/52, approximately
3.1021e-11, well above the t0 threshold and its bounded measurement uncertainty.
For the restricted single-coefficient fault family, its static singular value
is sqrt(3)/52. Conditional passage bounds that one coefficient below2^-39;
the interval-enclosed bound is1.153e-12. This does not bound arbitrary cross-talk.

The engine additionally rejects mismatched locks, modified predictions, malformed
dimensions and float-valued decision inputs. Synthetic controls never generate
an empirical validity claim. A source-hash check and isolated fresh-directory
replay reproduce the certificate, probe arrays, audit and control results.

## 6. Sampled energy and continuous-time limit

Report the explicitly sampled diagnostic

\[
 E_{grid}=\sum_{j=0}^{24}w_j\|r(t_j)\|_F^2,
 \quad w_0=w_{24}=1/64,\quad w_j=1/32\ (1\le j\le23).
\]

Its threshold is the exact rational sum of w_j tau(t_j)^2, approximately
1.174258e-23. It is redundant when all node gates pass, and is not an
independently measured continuous integral or a conserved stock.

Finite sampled passage does not control the continuum. For any unit output
matrix V, the smooth discrepancy

\[
 r(t)=2^{-20}\sin(32\pi t)V
\]

vanishes at every grid node, yet its squared Frobenius integral on[0,3/4]
is3/2^43, which exceeds2^-55. Independent regularity or quadrature control is
required to infer a continuous energy inequality. Under the null and only
if the same error receipts hold at every intermediate time, integrating the
affine envelope gives a separate conditional upper bound1.165e-23. The finite
test does not establish those all-time receipts.

## 7. What three probes cannot certify

At the frozen nominal A, its degree105 minimal polynomial bounds the cyclic
span of three validation inputs by315. At least2325 input directions per
arbitrary readout row can therefore remain blind, even with every possible
time sample on these inputs. Adding the three calibration inputs gives a
span upper bound630 and at least2010 blind directions per row. These counts
use nominal A; the same polynomial is not asserted for generic unequal rates.

The original62-channel observer also has its inherited747-dimensional nominal
dynamical kernel. A skew generator perturbation supported entirely in that
invariant kernel remains invisible to this readout for all preparations.
Distinct preparations and many samples do not remove that obstruction.

Consequently, this package tests specified predictive alternatives. It does
not establish full-domain readout or generator bounds required by the history
instrument certificate. To derive those bounds, restrict the fault family and
prove an observation lower bound for that family, or enlarge the independent
input/readout design. A short finite grid also leaves unsampled drift and
arbitrary nonlinear alternatives unresolved.

## 8. Governance and next action

The previous commit822d407 remains an immutable source. This audit corrects
the newly supplied proposal and supersedes none of that commit's certified
calibration inequalities. Exact construction, conditional derivation, proposed
metrology and empirical execution remain separate. The source coefficient
ledgerO03 keeps all thresholds as protocol controls; Q139's physical time gap
remains open; Q165/Q169 retain the scoped support/generator interpretation.
The CRL2 amendment is a proposal, and no registry promotion is made. Independent
review is pending. Physical promotion stays0. No public push, PR or merge occurs.

Recommended next step: freeze a restricted readout/generator fault family and
derive a detection lower bound that turns held-out passage into the specific
operator-error bounds needed for the subsequent history acquisition.

title: IDENTIFIABLE CALIBRATION v0.1
note: Recovered earlier package; original source scope retained. Independent review not established; physical promotion 0.
content:
# UD identifiable calibration protocol v0.1

**RESULT / STATUS — DERIVED CONDITIONAL; development — no registry entry.**
One known two-coordinate preparation, two sample instants and an independent
clock-scale observation identify a common gain and three rates in the declared
unit-metric model. The finite calibration map has parameter rank 5. Its
normalized three-rate Jacobian has condition number <47/33 throughout the
specified parameter box. Physical promotion = 0. Constructor checks passed;
independent review pending. No apparatus data were supplied.

This extends the prior robustness result. It does not infer an arbitrary
metric, calibrate arbitrary cross-talk, select a native preparation mechanism,
or identify UD internal time with seconds.

## 1. Source-bound model and references

Retain the 2640-coordinate real chain carrier and the 189-coordinate readout R
from the preceding 600-cell observer. Let A1,A2,A3 denote its adjacent-grade
skew channels. The exact identities Ai Aj=0 for i!=j imply mutually orthogonal
active subspaces and ||A_w|| <= 4 max_i |wi| for A_w=sum_i wi Ai.

For this protocol **H=I is known**. The candidate calibration model is

\[
y(u)=g R e^{\alpha u A_w}p,
\quad w=(a,b,c),\quad g>0,\quad\alpha>0.
\]

u is logger time; reference time is t=alpha u after resetting the preparation
event to zero. Rates are defined per chosen reference-time unit. An external
clock compares an interval of logger time with that chosen reference unit;
it supplies a measurement of alpha. This is a laboratory convention and
calibration assumption, not a derivation of a UD physical clock. An unknown
time offset, nonlinear clock drift and sample jitter require separate checks.

Two external anchors are indispensable here:

1. A known prepared chain vector, including its amplitude, coordinate address
   and relative signs. Its realization in an apparatus is OPEN.
2. A clock-scale reference independent of the generator rates. At least two
   clock events are needed to measure an interval.

The shape of R, common-gain form gR and unit metric must be selected or
independently established. These are model assumptions, not outputs of four
sensor values. Nominal sensor gain does not set the physical units of support.

## 2. Concrete preparation inside the existing readout

The sorted oriented simplices and global coordinate numbers are:

| Role | Simplex | Coordinate |
|---|---|---:|
| v | (33) | 33 |
| e | (33,34) | 486 |
| f | (33,34,41) | 1680 |
| tau | (0,33,34,41) | 2040 |

All four belong to the retained 189-coordinate observer. Prepare

\[
p=e_{486}+e_{1680},\qquad \|p\|=\sqrt2.
\]

Here e_j denotes a chain coordinate vector, not a geometric coframe. Let P
select coordinates (33,486,2040), and S=diag(1,-1,1). Exact integer checks on
the full carrier give

\[
SP[A_1p\ A_2p\ A_3p]=I_3,\qquad Pp=(0,1,0)^T.
\]

Thus the initial scalar readout at coordinate 486 gives g, and the signed
initial slopes give g alpha (a,b,c). The orientation signs used here are
A[33,486]=1, A[486,1680]=-1 and A[2040,1680]=1.

**Scoped minimality.** A single coordinate preparation lies in one chain
degree and excites at most two adjacent channels. Since different channels
annihilate each other, no later sample can recover a rate whose channel was
not excited. At least two nonzero coordinate components are therefore needed
to identify all three rates in one preparation of this form. The selected
two-component vector achieves this. This is not a sensor-minimality theorem
for every possible intervention architecture.

## 3. Exact jet rank and the necessary clock anchor

For theta=(g,alpha,a,b,c), the unanchored ideal jet is

\[
J_0(\theta)=(g,g\alpha a,g\alpha b,g\alpha c).
\]

Its Jacobian has rank 4 and null direction
(0,alpha,-a,-b,-c). The exact nonlinear ambiguity is
(alpha,w)->(q alpha,w/q), q>0. Arbitrarily many preparations or time samples
cannot separate alpha from w without a scale reference, because the entire
generator in logger time is alpha A_w.

With an independent alpha observation, arrange the outputs as
(g,alpha,g alpha a,g alpha b,g alpha c). The Jacobian determinant is
g^3 alpha^3, so its rank is 5. This is a structural check; the protocol below
does not assume that an exact derivative can be measured.

If the prepared amplitude were also unknown, the further change
(g,p)->(qg,p/q) would leave every sensor history unchanged. A preparation
address without an amplitude reference does not remove the gain ambiguity.

## 4. Finite two-instant protocol and uniform inverse theorem

Choose the rational logger interval h=1/256. Record only:

| Instant/source | Scalar value(s) |
|---|---|
| u=0 | y486(0) |
| u=h | y33(h), y486(h), y2040(h) |
| Independent interval reference | alpha |

There are four sensor scalars and one clock-scale scalar. No derivative
oracle is used. In the noiseless model g=y486(0). For known g and alpha define

\[
\Phi_\alpha(w)=\frac{SP(e^{h\alpha A_w}-I)p}{h\alpha}.
\]

The observed finite feature is S[Py(h)/g-Pp]/(h alpha), where Py(h) here
means the three named sensor channels. Its model value is Phi_alpha(w).
One must fit this finite exponential map; simply setting w equal to the
feature would retain a finite-step bias.

Let g,alpha,a,b,c lie in [15/16,17/16]. For each rate derivative the integral
formula for the exponential gives

\[
\left\|\frac{\partial\Phi_\alpha}{\partial w_i}
       -e_i\right\|
\le 4\sqrt2\,h\,\|\alpha A_w\|.
\]

For completeness, subtract h alpha Ai from the derivative of
exp(h alpha A_w), express the derivative as its integral, and bound the
two propagator differences by time times ||alpha A_w||. Both propagators
are orthogonal. Divide by h alpha, use ||Ai||<4 and ||p||=sqrt2.
Taking a Frobenius bound over three columns yields

\[
\|D\Phi_\alpha-I\|\le16\sqrt6\,\alpha\max_i w_i\,h
\le\frac{289\sqrt6}{4096}<\frac7{40}.
\]

The last inequality can also be checked by squaring positive rationals:
501126/16777216 < 49/1600. The box is convex, so integration of the Jacobian
along a line gives the **global** bound

\[
\boxed{\frac{33}{40}\|w-w'\|
\le\|\Phi_\alpha(w)-\Phi_\alpha(w')\|
\le\frac{47}{40}\|w-w'\|.}
\]

Consequently Phi is one-to-one on the box and every rate Jacobian has
sigma_min>33/40, sigma_max<47/40, hence condition number <47/33. The
five-feature raw parameter map has determinant magnitude bounded below by
(g h alpha)^3 (33/40)^3, so it has rank 5 at every point in the box. Since
g and alpha are separately read, the finite full map is globally identifiable
on this box as well.

The condition number <47/33 belongs to the **normalized rate map**, not to
raw voltages or the full five-parameter map. Normalization divides sensor
errors by g h alpha, approximately multiplying them by 256 near nominal
parameters. The raw determinant carries h^3. This precision cost remains.

## 5. A constructive inverse that also handles noisy data

Let Omega=[15/16,17/16]^3 and let q be the normalized measured feature.
The iteration

\[
w_{n+1}=\Pi_\Omega\bigl(w_n+q-\Phi_{\widehat\alpha}(w_n)\bigr)
\]

is a contraction with factor <7/40. It has one fixed point even if noisy
q lies outside the image of Phi. From any initial point in the box,
(7/40)^n sqrt(3)/8 bounds distance to that fixed point; n=14 suffices for
distance <10^(-11). This is an a priori iteration bound, not a physical
convergence claim for a UD dynamical process.

If ||q-Phi_alphahat(w)||<=B and a computed point has certified projected
fixed-point residual <=rsolve, then

\[
\boxed{\|\widehat w-w\|\le\frac{40}{33}(B+r_{\rm solve}).}
\]

Proof: projection is nonexpansive. Compare the noisy fixed-point equation
with the noiseless one, use the 7/40 Lipschitz bound for Phi-I, and absorb
that term. The same argument with a residual gives the displayed result.
No assumption that noisy data admit an exact exponential fit is needed.

For certified evaluations at rational candidate parameters, write A_w=G/d
with integer sparse G. Integer powers G^n p give exact rational Taylor sums.
The skew-exponential integral remainder after degree N is bounded by
sqrt(2)||h alpha A_w||^(N+1)/(N+1)!. Degree 20 makes the coordinate error
<10^(-50) throughout the parameter box. Remainders must be included in the
residual bound. The included synthetic round trip verifies this procedure
on the actual 2640-coordinate operator; it is not experimental data.

## 6. Candidate measurement contract and acceptance rule

This contract is a sufficient design example, **not measured instrument
performance**. Assume the actual calibration preparation is p+delta_p with
||delta_p||<=xi; common readout gain is constant g; initial scalar noise is
bounded by nu0 and later three-channel vector noise by nu. The later true
reference-time interval differs from alpha h by at most jcal. Clip the gain
and clock estimates to [15/16,17/16]; clipping preserves their error bounds
when the true parameters are in this box.

Let |ghat-g|<=epsilon_g, |alphahat-alpha|<=epsilon_alpha. The initial reading
supplies epsilon_g <= (17/16)xi+nu0. With l=15/16 and u=17/16, a rigorous
feature-error ceiling is

\[
B=\frac{\nu+\sqrt2\epsilon_g+u\xi}{l^2h}
 +\frac{4\sqrt2u}{l}
   \left(\epsilon_\alpha+\frac{j_{\rm cal}}h\right).
\]

The first term accounts for additive sensor noise, gain normalization and
preparation error. The second uses the orthogonal propagator's Lipschitz
bound for clock-scale and interval-jitter errors.

| Declared ceiling | Exact value |
|---|---:|
| nu0, nu, xi | 1/10^12 each |
| epsilon_g, derived | 33/(16 times 10^12) |
| epsilon_alpha | 1/10^11 |
| jcal, reference-time units | 1/10^14 |
| Certified projected solver residual | 1/10^11 |

256-bit interval arithmetic then proves

\[
\|\widehat w-w\|<\frac2{10^9}.
\]

The enclosed upper-bound expression is approximately 1.867702043 times
10^(-9), including the solver residual. This is a deterministic norm bound,
not a confidence interval. It is conditional on the stated precision ceilings.

**Rate acceptance rule.** Accept compatibility with the prior r=3/10^9
envelope only if max_i |what_i-1|<=1/10^9. Triangle inequality then certifies
max_i |wi-1|<3/10^9. Calibration precision alone cannot show that the actual
rates are near 1; data must pass this acceptance rule. No rate adjustment or
feedback actuator is assumed. A failed check requires a new baseline
certificate or a separately authorized physical adjustment.

For common gain, dividing future readings by ghat leaves a scalar operator
error at most epsilon_g/(15/16), below the prior rho=1/100000 ceiling. This
does not certify unknown relative gain or arbitrary cross-talk.

If later samples are scheduled at logger times tj/alphahat, clock-scale
uncertainty causes absolute timing error <= tj epsilon_alpha/(15/16).
For the longest M=8192 schedule this is <=4.368534 times 10^(-8) reference
time units. Separately bounded per-sample jitter <=1/10^6 leaves total error
below the prior tau=3/10^6 ceiling for all three schedules. This requires the
clock calibration to remain valid over acquisition; drift is not inferred
from a short interval.

Under these accepted checks, H=I, stable rates and common gain, the parent
robustness bounds apply to gain-normalized data: rank 2640 and conditions
<748,<375,<306 for M=2048,4096,8192 respectively. The parent's additive-noise
bound must be applied after gain normalization. The calibration and subsequent
unknown-state experiment are distinct runs on the same stable plant.

In the noiseless joint inverse problem the calibration block has rank 5 and
the subsequent state-history block has rank 2640. Their block-triangular
Jacobian therefore has rank 2645, provided the plant passes the parent
observability conditions. This statement does not add unknown metric or
arbitrary readout parameters to the model.

## 7. What the protocol cannot identify

**EXACT NO-GO — general metric.** Let u0 equal 1 on all 120 vertex coordinates
and 0 elsewhere. The exact incidence operator gives Au0=0 and ||u0||^2=120.
For every eta>-1 the SPD matrix

\[
H_\eta=I+\eta\,u_0u_0^T/120
\]

satisfies H_eta A=A, hence H_eta^(-1)A=A. Its distance from I is |eta|,
yet every coordinate history for every known preparation is unchanged at
the unit-rate plant. Thus even complete knowledge of K cannot bound a general
metric error using dynamics alone in the candidate rule K=H^(-1)A_w.
This is an exact counterexample, not a small-rank numerical observation.

There are additional common metric/rate scale ambiguities when H is unknown.
The present rank-5 theorem expressly assumes H=I. A selected metric family
with independently measured references is necessary before claiming broader
identification. A known norm convention and a measured physical metric remain
different types of objects.

**OPEN — relative readout.** Four sensor scalars cannot certify an arbitrary
189 by 2640 readout error matrix. Either the common-gain structure must be
validated independently or richer calibration preparations and sensors must
be specified. Time-dependent gain, timing drift and nonlinear generator
terms are also outside the rank-5 model and require explicit discrepancy
receipts.

## 8. Governance, reproducibility and provenance

Attached ledger v0.39 entries O03, Q139, Q165 and Q169 are relevant: tolerances
remain protocol controls, frequency does not acquire physical units from
geometry, and the chain generator/support carrier remain mathematically
typed. No ledger entry is modified. The attached CRL-2 amendment describes
itself as a governance proposal; its development-lane distinction and
non-constructor-review warning are respected without assuming formal adoption.
This output is not registered or promoted. The unavailable Genesis image was
not used. No private attachment is redistributed.

Run `python certify_calibration.py` with the pinned requirements. The code
verifies the actual observed flag, integer jet identities and metric
counterexample, symbolic parameter ranks, uniform finite-time inequalities,
precision budgets, three rational forward evaluations and a synthetic inverse
round trip. The rank-5 conclusion is supported by the analytic uniform proof;
point evaluations alone are not a uniform rank certificate. Source hashes
and a fresh-directory byte-identical replay accompany the result.

**Next gate:** formulate a richer readout and metric calibration model with
explicit admissible parameter families, then certify what additional reference
measurements make those parameters identifiable. Apparatus implementation and
independent review remain required before experimental qualification.

content:
# UD observer robustness v0.1

**RESULT / STATUS — DERIVED, CONDITIONAL, CONSTRUCTOR VERIFIED.** The retained
189-coordinate observer remains injective under the joint operator tolerances
below, for each of the three previously certified finite sampling protocols.
This adds a model-mismatch theorem to the known-model observer. It does not
measure an apparatus or establish a native metric-dependent physical law.
Physical promotion = 0. Independent review pending. Local append-only capture;
public publication pending. Parent local commit:
`0c0158fef1cb6b75ad4c7d057c0b72abdbcce3c0`.

## 1. Frozen carrier and nominal inputs

The carrier is the real simplicial chain space of the regular 600-cell boundary
S3, with grade dimensions (120,720,1200,600), total 2640. Ordered oriented
simplices carry the identity metric. The real generator A has upper adjacent
blocks -Bk and lower blocks Bk^T. Thus A^T = -A. Write A = A1+A2+A3 for the
three adjacent-grade channels. B1 B2 = B2 B3 = 0 implies
Ai Aj = 0 for i != j. The parent exact annihilator and spectral certificate give
||A|| < 4. All norms in this note are Euclidean operator/vector norms unless
an H subscript is present.

R selects 189 distinct chain coordinates: three vertex links centred at vertices
0,45,66, retained tetrahedral coordinate 2040, and coordinates 928 (face),
152 (edge), and 4 (vertex). There are 36 vertex, 91 edge, 61 face and one
tetrahedral channels. Consequently ||R|| = 1. A snapshot still has nullity 2451;
the full finite history is injective. This note does not change the observer
or its historical selection.

At times tj = j/2, j = 0,...,M-1, define

\[
F_M=M^{-1/2}\operatorname{stack}_j R e^{t_j A}.
\]

The frozen parent certificate supplies sigma_min(F_M) >= sM and
sigma_max(F_M) <= 1:

| M | Last nominal time | Exact sM | Parent condition bound |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 2047/2 | 1/(512 sqrt(2)) | <725 |
| 4096 | 4095/2 | 1/(256 sqrt(2)) | <363 |
| 8192 | 8191/2 | sqrt(3)/512 | <296 |

These are lower bounds, not measured singular values. The 105 distinct temporal
frequencies and common spatial certificate are inherited; this addendum checks
their hashes and spectral band input without recomputing the parent proof.

## 2. General perturbation theorem

**DERIVED.** In common fixed state coordinates let the actual constant generator
be K, the actual sample times tj+dj with |dj| <= tau, and the actual readouts
Cj = R+Ej with ||Ej|| <= rho. No statistical independence is assumed. Let
||K-A|| <= epsilon. The normalized actual map is

\[
\widetilde F_M=M^{-1/2}\operatorname{stack}_j
 (R+E_j)e^{(t_j+d_j)K}.
\]

First suppose one fixed SPD H satisfies ||H-I|| <= eta < 1 and
K^T H + H K = 0. Put

\[
g=\sqrt{\frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}},\quad
\overline t=\frac{M-1}{4},\quad
T_{\rm rms}^2=\frac{(M-1)(2M-1)}{24},\quad
b=\rho+(4+\epsilon)\tau.
\]

Then a sufficient mismatch bound is

\[
\boxed{\|\widetilde F_M-F_M\|\le
\beta_H:=g\sqrt{b^2+2b\epsilon\overline t+
\epsilon^2 T_{\rm rms}^2}
\le g(b+\epsilon T_{\rm rms}).}
\]

Proof: H^(1/2) K H^(-1/2) is skew, so ||exp(tK)|| <= g for
every real t. Duhamel gives ||exp(tK)-exp(tA)|| <= g epsilon t for t>=0.
The integral of the time derivative gives
||exp((t+d)K)-exp(tK)|| <= g(4+epsilon)|d|, even when the first
jittered time is negative. The readout-error term is <= rho g. The jth block
error is therefore <= g[b+epsilon tj]. Squaring, averaging and using the
triangle bound for a stacked operator yields the displayed RMS expression.
These bounds do not assume that H commutes with A or K.

If an H-skew structure is unavailable, the same epsilon still yields the
unstructured bound, with T=(M-1)/2:

\[
\boxed{\beta_U=e^{\epsilon(T+\tau)}
 [\rho+\epsilon T_{\rm rms}+(4+\epsilon)\tau].}
\]

Indeed A is skew and K=A+Delta has two-sided propagator bound
||exp(tK)|| <= exp(epsilon |t|). Duhamel and the jitter integral then bound
each block by exp(epsilon(T+tau))[rho+epsilon tj+(4+epsilon)tau].
The exponential factor cannot in general be dropped: Delta=epsilon I gives
exp(tK)=exp(epsilon t)exp(tA).

For either valid bound beta < sM, singular-value perturbation gives

\[
\sigma_{\min}(\widetilde F_M)\ge s_M-\beta>0,\qquad
\sigma_{\max}(\widetilde F_M)\le1+\beta,\qquad
\kappa_2(\widetilde F_M)\le\frac{1+\beta}{s_M-\beta}.
\]

Thus every plant within the stated bounds has rank 2640 and kernel zero.
This is a uniform rank certificate. It does not identify an unknown K or Cj.

## 3. Rates and metric: three distinct meanings

**DERIVED — rate perturbation.** Let
A_w=a A1+b A2+c A3, with each of |a-1|,|b-1|,|c-1| <= r.
The mutually orthogonal active subspaces ran(Ai) follow from Ai Aj=0
and skew symmetry. On ran(Ai), A acts as Ai; on the common kernel it vanishes.
Hence ||A_w-A|| <= r||A|| <= 4r. The exact sparse identities were checked
on all 2640 coordinates; this bound does not pay an unnecessary factor of three.
In the H=I rate-only branch K=A_w, one can take epsilon=4r.

**DERIVED — metric as reporting norm.** If the state evolution and readout are
unchanged, merely reporting ||x||H does not alter rank or create a generator
error. The norm relations are

\[
\sqrt{1-\eta}\|x\|\le\|x\|_H\le\sqrt{1+\eta}\|x\|.
\]

For Euclidean observation norm and H state norm, the lower singular bound
is divided by sqrt(1+eta), the upper by sqrt(1-eta), and the condition
bound is multiplied by at most g.

**CANDIDATE constitutive rule — metric affects evolution.** For the declared
rule K=H^(-1) A_w, H-skewness follows exactly from HK=A_w. Moreover

\[
\|K-A\|\le
\|H^{-1}\|\|A_w-A\|+\|H^{-1}-I\|\|A\|
\le\boxed{\frac{4(r+\eta)}{1-\eta}}.
\]

This rule is a branch chosen for the calculation. No result here proves that
UD or any apparatus selects it. For a different metric-to-generator rule,
one must supply its own epsilon; a metric discrepancy alone is insufficient.

## 4. Certified joint envelope

The following exact rational ceilings may hold **simultaneously**, using the
candidate constitutive branch. Rates and metric are fixed over acquisition;
readout and jitter may vary by sample.

| Quantity | Joint ceiling | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| r | 3/10^9 | Each of three rates relative to nominal 1 |
| eta | 3/10^9 | ||H-I|| in the fixed state coordinates |
| rho | 1/100000 | ||Ej||, absolute operator error relative to ||R||=1 |
| tau | 3/10^6 | Absolute jitter in internal model time |

Use epsilon=4(r+eta)/(1-eta)=24/999999997. With Arb at 256 bits,
the constructor verifies beta_H < (3/100)sM for all three protocols.
The unstructured bound beta_U also passes the same 3% margin for the same
direct epsilon, rho and tau ceilings, without invoking H-skewness.

| M | beta_H/sM, display approximation | Actual condition bound | Actual kernel |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 0.0253487801 | <748 | 0 |
| 4096 | 0.0176253407 | <375 | 0 |
| 8192 | 0.0226422504 | <306 | 0 |

The displayed ratios are approximations, not inequality thresholds. The JSON
contains interval enclosures; the exact common threshold is 3/100.
In particular sigma_min(actual)^2 >= (97/100)^2 sM^2.
This is a sufficient envelope; it is not a necessary limit or an optimized
hardware specification. The very small rate/metric budget reflects a
conservative long-horizon phase-error bound. More samples improve the nominal
noise bound but increase accumulated generator mismatch; the 4096 profile
has the smallest certified mismatch ratio for this selected envelope.

For comparison, isolated 5% budgets with H=I and all other errors zero are:

\[
\epsilon\le\frac{s_M}{20T_{\rm rms}},\quad
r\le\frac{s_M}{80T_{\rm rms}},\quad
\rho\le\frac{s_M}{20},\quad
\tau\le\frac{s_M}{80}.
\]

These isolated maxima cannot be combined as a joint budget. Their interval
values are retained in ROBUSTNESS_CERTIFICATE.json.

## 5. Reconstruction error and the meaning of 8%

**DERIVED.** Let measured normalized data be y=Ftilde x+e, with
delta=||e||=(M^(-1) sum_j ||e_j||^2)^(1/2), i.e. vector RMS noise across
snapshots. The nominal least-squares decoder has error

\[
\boxed{\|F_M^\dagger y-x\|\le
 \frac{\beta\|x\|+\delta}{s_M}.}
\]

The systematic mismatch term is present even at zero measurement noise. A
decoder calibrated to the actual map instead has noise error
delta/(sM-beta). Full observability alone does not justify replacing the
nominal decoder with an unknown actual decoder.

For a declared state bound ||x|| <= X, the joint 3% envelope and
delta <= sM X/20 imply an **absolute** error ceiling

\[
\|\widehat x-x\|\le\frac{2}{25}X.
\]

This is 8% of the supplied state bound X. It is not a uniform 8% relative
error guarantee for arbitrarily small states. If the stronger signal-specific
noise hypothesis delta <= sM||x||/20 holds, then the relative bound follows.
A per-scalar deterministic noise ceiling nu only implies delta <= sqrt(189)nu;
no averaging improvement from independent noise is assumed here.

## 6. Exact calibration obstructions

**NO-GO for joint gain/state identification.** For any c>0, the models
(C=R,x0,K=A) and (C'=cR,x0'=x0/c,K'=A) give exactly the same history
at every time. For c arbitrarily close to 1, both satisfy arbitrarily small
nonzero readout neighborhoods. Therefore rank 2640 for each known readout
does not establish joint unknown-gain and state-amplitude identification.
An amplitude reference or other gain constraint is needed.

**NO-GO for separating common metric/rate scale in the candidate branch.**
The change (H,w) -> (cH,cw) leaves K=H^(-1)A_w exactly unchanged.
Dynamics alone cannot separate the two scales without a further anchor.

**NO-GO for separating common clock/rate scale from unconstrained data.**
The change (K,t) -> (cK,t/c) leaves exp(tK) unchanged. An external time
reference or fixed rate scale is required to attach physical time units.

These are changed unknown-parameter inverse problems, not new kernels of the
known-parameter linear observer. None authorizes calling missing modes gauge
redundancy, reconstructs topology from a scalar coincidence, or promotes physics.

## 7. Reproduction, provenance and remaining work

Install the pinned requirements and run `python certify_robustness.py` from any
directory. It checks exact skew symmetry, distinct coordinates, six vanishing
cross-channel products, the parent band enclosures, three joint interval
budgets, unstructured budgets and condition bounds. JSON decimal display fields
are explanatory; exact fractions and Arb comparisons carry the inequalities.
The script checks the actual full carrier identities without building a dense
million-row finite history. The analytic theorem handles arbitrary admissible
perturbations, so a random simulation is not the certificate.

Sources are frozen copies and hashes of the preceding observer outputs, with
its source register and annihilator retained. Source register names upstream
PR heads and issues #136 and #144; this addendum does not update or close them.
The report and proof are new; no supplied private attachment is copied.

**OPEN:** choose a source-supported constitutive rule, independently validate
the mathematical certificates, supply gain/time/metric anchors, and compare
measured operator errors and noise with the budget. An apparatus specification
and measurements are absent. The present result makes an experimental contract
possible, but does not qualify an experiment.
