# UD spectral extraction without the dense Hankel matrix v0.1

RESULT / STATUS: **DERIVED method, constructor verified**. Exact arithmetic and direct spectral enclosures replace dense Hankel storage. Thirteen checks and three frozen-dimension constructed spectral controls are supplied. No nominal600-cell full-history run or apparatus dataset was supplied or certified. Independent review pending; physical promotion **0**. Development — no registry entry.

## Disposition of the parallel appendix

The appendix reproduces the acquisition arithmetic correctly, with its original conditions. Its additional leakage-sieve interpretation is not supported by the frozen source chain.

| Submitted claim | Review result |
|---|---|
| M4096;8191 timestamps;37 preparations;18790154 readings | Retain |
| delta2^-20 per62-vector; scalar2^-23 sufficient | Retain as bounded-error contracts |
| 1893 retained signals; condition<2029 | Retain conditionally; requires numeric and acquisition evidence |
| 62 auxiliary diagnostic ports | Correct:62 original history channels;189 diagnostic outputs; four extra six-ratio ports |
| One port per frequency block | Reject: a coordinate readout generally mixes frequencies |
| Every port residual<2^-49 | Not implied by the frozen budget; would require a new experiment contract |
| Borel-shear norm<=2^-38 | Undefined new proposal;2^-38 belongs to a particular source shape statistic |
| 1146-dimensional invariant plane | No such certificate in this chain |
| Finite-field leakage, real norms and physical currents share one provenance | No transfer supplied |
| Monitoring detects phases confined to the747 hidden directions | No-go for the nominal invariant hidden sector |
| ACTIVE_MONITOR and causal diagnosis of failure | Unsupported; no hardware run or causal isolation supplied |

Two exact counterexamples make the distinction concrete. Port0 is coordinate33. The source operator has A[33,120]=−1, so the initial state e120 gives y0(0)=0 and y0'(0)=−1. That port is not stationary-only. A scalar instrument error2^-24 is allowed by the frozen allocation and exceeds the proposed2^-49 residual gate by2^25; the strict gate cannot be inferred from the existing contract.

Let N=intersection over k>=0 of ker(RA^k), the nominal747-dimensional dynamical unobservable space. A preservesN, and skewness makes N-perpendicular invariant too. If J is any skew operator supported entirely insideN, then

\[
R e^{t(A+J)}x=R e^{tA}x\quad\text{for every }x,t.
\]

There are747×746/2=278631 such skew degrees of freedom. No history processing of this observer can diagnose them without a separately specified coupling that makes them observable. The dimension747 is tied to the frozenA,R; it is not a universal claim about every altered plant. The replacement `CORRECTED_MONITORING_APPENDIX.md` preserves the valid finite-observer scope. The full claim audit is `PARALLEL_APPENDIX_REVIEW.json`.

## Exact Hankel action and total energy

Write the encoded numeric history as Y[a,k,c]/q with p=37 preparations, c=62 channels, M=4096 and q=2^48. The exact data matrix is

Here q is only the encoding denominator, not the parent common-rate multiplier. The candidate V below is an input-history basis, distinct from the parent's105-column temporal frame.

\[
H[(i,c),(j,a)]=Y[a,i+j,c]/(Mq).
\]

For an integer candidate vector v, define P_ac(z)=sum_k Y[a,k,c]z^k and W_a(z)=sum_j v[j,a]z^(M−1−j). Then

\[
(Mq)(Hv)[i,c]=\sum_a[z^{i+M-1}]P_{ac}(z)W_a(z).
\]

The transpose action exchanges the preparation/channel summation. Python-FLINT integer polynomial multiplication computes both exactly; there is no floating FFT error in the verifier. The separate numerical proposer uses FFTs only to suggest a basis. It has no authority to certify rank or convergence.

The exact squared Frobenius norm is one pass over the time record:

\[
E=\|H\|_F^2=\frac1{M^2q^2}\sum_{k=0}^{2M-2}m_k\sum_{a,c}Y[a,k,c]^2,
\quad m_k=\min(k+1,M,2M-1-k).
\]

The multiplicities are essential. Counting each raw value once, ignoring duplicated Hankel antidiagonals, would understate the energy and invalidate completeness checks.

## Projection-tail certificate

Let V be any proposed real right signal basis with r=1893 columns. It need not be exactly orthonormal. The proof recomputes

\[
G_V=V^TV,\qquad C=HV,\qquad G_C=C^TC
\]

from the numeric input and candidate, using integer numerators and common denominators. Suppose the exact calculation gives an outward bound

\[
\|G_V-I\|_2\le\|G_V-I\|_F\le\eta<1.
\]

The exact orthogonal projection onto the candidate space is P=V G_V^-1 V^T. Its full discarded energy obeys

\[
\begin{aligned}
\|H(I-P)\|_F^2
&=E-\operatorname{tr}(G_V^{-1}G_C)\\
&\le E-\frac{\operatorname{tr}G_C}{1+\eta}
=:\rho^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

The trace inequality follows from G_V^-1 >= I/(1+eta) and G_C positive semidefinite. The code never clamps a negative inconsistent energy to zero; inconsistent cores are rejected. A candidate with eta>=1 returnsHOLD.

This section's rho is the projection-tail bound. It is distinct from the readout-operator error tolerance denoted rho in the parent acquisition model.

For each ordered eigenvalue of G_C, suppose an exact/validated bound is ell_i <= lambda_i(G_C) <= u_i. Define

\[
L_i=\max(0,\ell_i)/(1+\eta),\qquad
U_i=u_i/(1-\eta)+\rho^2.
\]

Then direct enclosures of the exact data spectrum are

\[
\boxed{\sqrt{L_i}\le\sigma_i(H)\le\sqrt{U_i}\ (i\le r),
\qquad \sigma_{r+1}(H)\le\rho.}
\]

Proof: the nonzero spectrum of HP equals that of C G_V^-1/2. Singular-product inequalities give its ordered squared bounds ell_i/(1+eta),u_i/(1−eta). Also

\[
HH^T=(HP)(HP)^T+H(I-P)(H(I-P))^T.
\]

The second summand is positive semidefinite with norm at most rho². Min-max therefore gives the displayed lower/upper bounds, and the rank-r approximation HP bounds the entire remaining tail. This is a completeness certificate, not only a residual check for a few computed singular triplets.

The frozen target is certified when

\[
L_r>T^2,\qquad \rho^2<T^2,\qquad U_1<2029^2L_r,
\quad T=2B
\]

using the exact unchanged threshold from the parent contract. The output includes enclosures for all1893 retained singular values. A failure isHOLD: a poor candidate or a conservative bound can fail even when the underlying record has a valid signature. The code never lowers the target or moves the threshold to force acceptance.

These are direct enclosures for the exact encodedH. No approximate matrix Htilde is substituted, so the matrix-perturbation error entry is0. Scalar interval rounding is already included in the outward endpoints. This uses the frozen contract's explicit alternative of directly verified singular-value enclosures; it does not spend or silently enlarge its B/4096 allowance for an approximate-matrix solver.

## Verified small-core eigenvalue bounds

The inexpensive first bound uses d_i, the sorted diagonal entries of G_C, and nu=max_i sum_(j!=i)|G_C[i,j]|. Symmetry implies ||G_C−diag(G_C)||_2<=nu, hence each eigenvalue lies in [d_i−nu,d_i+nu].

A correct candidate span can have a core that is not diagonally dominant. The verifier then proposes a small-core numerical eigensystem Q,D and recomputes its orthogonality defect and eigen-residual **exactly**. Let eta_Q bound ||Q^TQ−I||_2, R_Q=G_C Q−QD, and S=(Q^TQ)^1/2. With U=Q S^-1 orthogonal,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\|G_C-U D U^T\|_2\le{}&\|G_C\|_2\eta_Q
+\|R_Q\|_F\sqrt{1+\eta_Q}\\
&+\|D\|_2\frac{\eta_Q}{1+\sqrt{1-\eta_Q}}
(1+\sqrt{1+\eta_Q}).
\end{aligned}
\]

To check the formula, first use G_C−QDQ^T=G_C(I−QQ^T)+R_QQ^T, then bound QDQ^T−UDU^T with ||Q−U||<=eta_Q/(1+sqrt(1−eta_Q)). The resulting outward dyadic radius certifies every ordered eigenvalue against the sorted entries ofD. The original floating eigenvalues/vectors are proposals only. The verifier refuses an inadequately orthogonal proposal rather than trusting its convergence flag.

## What is extracted

For any input-history vector x, the candidate coordinates are z=G_V^-1 V^Tx and its projected representative is Vz. The left image is Cz. The coordinate system is stable because the candidate singular values lie in [sqrt(1−eta),sqrt(1+eta)]. It is a basis for the retained history signal space, not a reconstruction of the2640-dimensional chain state.

If W contains the true leading-r right singular vectors, then

\[
\|(I-P)W\|_2
\le\frac{\|H(I-P)\|_2}{\sigma_r(H)}
\le\frac\rho{\sqrt{L_r}}.
\]

Indeed W=H^TU_r Sigma_r^-1. This gives a certified right-subspace leakage/angle bound for the numeric matrix. It does not identify microscopic hidden phases or label C10 sectors. Temporal eigenfrequencies and physical mode coordinates require their own operator mappings.

## Implementation and storage

The method also has a quantitative sufficient precision contract for the native family, recorded in `NATIVE_PRECISION_CONTRACT.json`. Let H0 be the matched nominal matrix for the run, with the parent singular bounds s0,S0 and the parent's Frobenius perturbation bound ||H−H0||_F<=B. The script reproduces that Frobenius bound directly from the weighted response-error formula. Suppose:

- candidate Gram defect eta<=2^-40;
- missed nominal mass ||H0(I−P)||_F<=zeta=B/4096;
- the total slack of the verified core eigenvalue bounds is at most xi=2^-41; a validated eigen-radius at most2^-42 suffices.

These are **new sufficient computational targets**, not experimental receipts. In particular, zeta and the parent's approximate-matrix solver allowance happen to use the same fraction B/4096; one does not prove the other. Their objects and proof obligations remain distinct.

Set Emax=(sqrt(r)S0+B)^2. The exact projector residual is at most(B+zeta)^2. The conservative trace replacement adds at most2eta Emax/(1−eta), so the verifier's rho² is bounded by their sum. Its smallest retained squared bound is at least

\[
\frac{(1-\eta)(s_0-B-\zeta)^2-\xi}{1+\eta},
\]

and its largest bound is at most

\[
\frac{(1+\eta)(S_0+B)^2+\xi}{1-\eta}+\rho^2.
\]

Outward interval evaluation verifies a retained condition bound below**2028.403** and a tail bound below**0.689T**, preserving the frozen2029 andT gates. This proves that finite positive candidate/core tolerances suffice for the native family. It does not assert that a generated candidate or an actual run meets those tolerances; that remains a data-dependent verification requirement.

`propose_basis.py` uses an FFT operator and fixed-seed block power proposals, storing the basis on disk. Its output is an **untrusted numerical proposal**. `run_certificate.py` binds the exact frozen protocol hash, recomputes exact cores from the encoded data and candidate, and produces `SPECTRAL_PROOF.json`. On success it also writes `FROZEN_SIGNATURE_ENCLOSURES.json` in the prior receipt auditor's interval layout. Input hashes are checked before and after verification. Evidence and physical provenance are still separate.

The dense candidate is int64 at denominator2^60. Exact H actions are stored as signed128-bit integer numerators with a common denominator, in column order. The frozen amplitude and candidate bounds imply a numerator magnitude below2^127; overflow raises an error, with no clipping. Gram products use arbitrary-precision FLINT integers and row blocks. Linux mapped pages are released between blocks; no denseH is allocated.

| Object | Storage |
|---|---:|
| Avoided denseH in binary64 | 307895468032 bytes =286.75GiB |
| Encoded history record | 150321232 bytes |
| Dense candidate,151552×1893 int64 | 2295103488 bytes |
| Exact C,253952×1893 signed128 | 7691698176 bytes |
| Each core | 1893×1893 arbitrary-precision integers |

Provision disk space for the candidate,exactC,small cores and proposer scratch, rather than287GiB forH. Exact Gram accumulation can be expensive. A full dense1893-vector nominal/measured verification has not been benchmarked; this version certifies correctness and storage structure, not an experimental processing deadline.

## Verification evidence

Thirteen tests compare exact actions, transpose duality, duplicated energy and streamed cores with independently constructed **tiny** dense matrices. They also cover missing candidate modes, orthogonality defects, inconsistent energy, noninteger input rejection, a non-diagonal core, floating proposals followed by exact verification, and individual spectral intervals.

The full frozen dimensions are tested separately with constructed records:

| Constructed record | Algebraic rank | Signals aboveT | Certificate |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Clean impulse control |1893|1893|Certified numeric signature |
| Additional weak rank-one component |1894|1893|Certified numeric signature |
| Additional strong rank-one component |1894|1894|HOLD |

The impulse control has36 preparation/channel blocks of rank51 and one of rank57:36×51+57=1893. Its nonzero singular value is2^-12. The extra constant channel has amplitude2^-19 or2^-14. Its additional singular value follows from an independent2×2 eigenvalue formula, which verifies the expected threshold counts. These records deliberately are not600-cell trajectories: they demonstrate the certifier and also demonstrate that the spectral signature alone does not identify the UD generator.

A dense separable record additionally exercises all37×62 preparation/channel polynomial products at M4096. Both exact action and exact transpose are checked against closed-form integer sums. No dense Hankel matrix is formed. `CONTROL_PERFORMANCE.json` records the observed runtime and RSS for these constructed controls only; those figures must not be extrapolated to a dense1893-vector certificate.

Fresh-directory replay reproduces the mathematical control and appendix-review artifacts. Runtime/RSS logs are kept separate because they are operational observations, not exact mathematics. The inherited modal/diagnostic proofs are not independently rerun, and no new experiment or physical correspondence is certified.

## Use and remaining work

```sh
python review_parallel.py
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m unittest -v test_spectral.py
python full_size_controls.py
python native_precision_contract.py
python validate_spectral.py
python propose_basis.py normalized_history.i64le candidate.npy
python run_certificate.py normalized_history.i64le candidate.npy NEW_PROOF_DIRECTORY
```

The last two commands require an actual complete encoded history record. None was supplied, so they were not executed at full dense1893-vector scale. Their end-to-end path is tested on a small independent record, and their full-size exact action kernels are tested as above. Basis proposal can fail or yieldHOLD; it is not guaranteed to converge for every admitted record. A valid proof, rather than a favorable numerical rank printout, controls the result.

Next recommended step — priority **98/100**: benchmark the complete candidate/core pipeline on a frozen nominal trajectory or independently supplied record, then obtain non-constructor review. Preserve the frozen threshold,all raw records and rejected/inconclusive results. Physical promotion remains0; the nominal747-dimensional hidden subspace remains unreconstructed.

The frozen exact threshold is `9093197064441289377 / 604462909807314587353088`. The primary spectral bounds are exact outward dyadic pairs in `BENCHMARK_RESULT.json`; readable bounds follow.

| Quantity | Verified result |
|---|---:|
| Full scalar readings generated | 18,790,154 |
| Singular values above frozen threshold | 1,893 |
| Retained condition number | <706.570 |
| Complete discarded projection tail, Frobenius | <9.615×10^-14 |
| Smallest retained singular value | >0.00011935053 |

Exact source moments, all preparations, direct phase enclosures, Cholesky/SVD residuals, complete record energy, both full-size probe actions, adjoint/direct-entry checks and dense small-case regressions passed. The encoded payload SHA-256 is `812ede167804a754f1e7343cc370cdc72a231d3f255a8656080e5cc7a2753ff7`.

This completes the **known-nominal spectral benchmark**. It uses temporal factor structure to form actual factor Grams; the generic candidate-basis adapter on unknown measured records remains open. The inherited 747-dimensional hidden subspace is not identified or monitored by this run.

# Frozen nominal Hankel benchmark, v0.2

Constructor verification only. Physical promotion: **0**. Independent review: pending.

This benchmark generates the nominal observation record from the pinned integer 600-cell operator, original 62-coordinate readout and 37 pinned preparations. It does not substitute identity Gram matrices, random matrices or artificial residual noise. All thresholds come from the frozen contract; the shape gate and diagnostic outputs have no role in the spectral tail test.

## Frozen object and method

The record is `Y[a,k,c]`, with 37 preparations, 8191 times `t=k/2`, and 62 history outputs. There are **18,790,154** scalar readings. The payload consists of little-endian signed int64 numerators, quantum `2^-48`, nearest ties-even. NPY files have a header; the recorded payload hash excludes that header.

The normalized matrix is

\[
H_{(i,c),(j,a)}=Y[a,i+j,c]/(4096\,2^{48}),\qquad 0\leq i,j<4096.
\]

Its shape is 253952 by 151552. A dense float64 copy would take **307,895,468,032 bytes = 286.75 GiB**. None is constructed.

1. Recompute every exact moment `R(-A²)^k S` and `RA(-A²)^k S`, `k=0,...,52`, from the actual sparse operator and sign matrix. Check the degree-53 annihilator on all preparations, isolate its 53 distinct real roots and verify the operator is skew symmetric.
2. Use its spectral projectors to reconstruct the stationary component and 52 positive-frequency pairs, with interval arithmetic at 512 bits. Round modal coefficients and direct trigonometric phases to dyadic rationals. Generate the complete encoded record through exact integer matrix products and ties-even quantization.
3. Factor each modal observation block as `Lλ Rλ*`, with a rigorously bounded residual, retaining a total of 1893 signed-mode directions. The selected ranks are a numerical construction choice; the residual bound, not that choice, justifies the discarded tail.
4. Write `H̃=F_L F_R*`, where the temporal vectors in the left factor use `exp(+iωj/2)/sqrt(M)` and those in the right factor use its conjugate. Construct the two **actual 1893 by 1893 factor Grams** using exact integer factor inner products and enclosed geometric sums. Convert conjugate pairs to real factors by `[f++f−,−i(f+−f−)]` on the left and half that transformation on the right. These are a structured nominal alternative to the generic candidate-basis Grams in the parent verifier; they are not claimed to be the same matrices.
5. Verify Cholesky and SVD proposals using exact integer matrix products, Frobenius residual bounds and polar corrections. Independently check all 240870 coefficient entries, 851864 nonstationary phase components and 5460 temporal pairs against uniform dyadic bounds. Recompute temporal and modal frame bounds directly by Gershgorin enclosures.
6. Evaluate the exact weighted energy of the encoded record, full-size `Hx` and `Hᵀz` on deterministic dense integer probes, their exact adjoint identity and 32 direct entries in each direction. Compare the energy with the factor-Gram trace and its error bound. Small dense regression cases separately check the factor identities and their singular spectra.

## Why the enclosures hold

For dyadic factor Grams `Ĝ_L,Ĝ_R`, let `γ_L,γ_R` include both Gram construction error and exact Cholesky residuals. With verified positive lower bounds `a_L,a_R` for the true Grams, the normalized factor defects satisfy

\[
\eta_L\leq\gamma_L/(a_L-\gamma_L),\qquad
\eta_R\leq\gamma_R/(a_R-\gamma_R).
\]

For the exact core `S=L_LᵀL_R`, verified proposed singular values `s_i` have an error enclosure `e`. Consequently,

\[
\sqrt{(1-\eta_L)(1-\eta_R)}(s_i-e)
\leq\sigma_i(\widetilde H)\leq
\sqrt{(1+\eta_L)(1+\eta_R)}(s_i+e).
\]

The uniform phase and coefficient checks give a scalar trajectory error at most `210·2^-60+2^-49`. Therefore its Hankel Frobenius error is at most `sqrt(37·62)` times that quantity. If `b` bounds the temporal Gram norm and `ε_modal` is the combined modal Frobenius residual, then

\[
\|H-\widetilde H\|_2\leq\|H-\widetilde H\|_F
\leq\delta=\delta_{trajectory}+b\varepsilon_{modal}.
\]

Weyl's inequality adds `±δ` to the core enclosures and yields `σ_1894(H)≤δ`. The Frobenius discarded tail is also at most `δ`: projecting onto the exact right factor's range annihilates `H̃(I−P)`, so `||H(I−P)||F≤δ`. # Record-only Hankel extraction: verified development result

Lane: **development — no registry entry**. Physical promotion: **0**. Independent review: **pending**. This is a benchmark on previously seen, constructed nominal data. It is not a blinded apparatus run or a CRL promotion.

## Inputs and distinction from the previous benchmark

The previous nominal benchmark used the known 600-cell frequencies and modal blocks. The present learner and verifier receive **only** the complete encoded record, frozen contract, and an untrusted proposal learned from that record. They do not load the cell operator, preparation vectors, annihilator, spectral roots, prior modal blocks or character projectors.

The proposal family is a stationary term plus real oscillatory pairs. This is a modeling choice for the numerical optimizer; the final proof does **not** assume the record was produced by that family. It checks the approximation against every reading. A failed proposal returns HOLD or produces no acceptance certificate.

Discovery cutoffs, sketch width and seed are protocol controls under ledger O03, not UD coefficients. They are fixed in this version's code; the frozen target count, selection threshold and condition cap are unchanged. This new implementation does not retrospectively satisfy the original contract's requirement for an independently reviewed, pre-data analysis freeze.

## Theorem 1: full-record residual bound

Let `Y[a,k,c]` be the integer record, with quantum `2^-48`, and

\[
H_{(i,c),(j,a)}=\frac{Y[a,i+j,c]}{M2^{48}},\quad M=4096.
\]

A proposed real temporal model has dyadic coefficients `C_l,c,a` and phases `theta_j`. The verifier evaluates every phase directly with 512-bit interval arithmetic. If `P_kl` are its dyadic phase numerators, scale `2^-60`, and coefficient numerators have the same scale, define

\[
D_{k,c,a}=2^{72}Y[a,k,c]-\sum_l P_{kl}C_{l,c,a},
\quad w_k=\min(k+1,2M-1-k,M).
\]

The dyadic model's Hankel residual is exactly

\[
\epsilon_D^2=\frac{\sum_{k,c,a} w_kD_{k,c,a}^{2}}{M^2 2^{240}}.
\]

If every nonconstant phase has error less than `2^-60`, the difference between this dyadic model and the exact trigonometric model is at most

\[
\epsilon_P\leq\sqrt{62\cdot37}\,2^{-120}
\sum_{l>0}\max_{c,a}|C_{l,c,a}|.
\]

Thus `||H-H_model||F <= epsilon_D+epsilon_P`. This is a finite numeric-record statement; it does not use a continuous generator, excitation assumption or nominal spectral decomposition.

## Theorem 2: retained spectrum and complete projection tail

Factor each fitted complex observation block as `L_j R_j*`, allowing an enclosed truncation residual. Let `epsilon_B` be the Frobenius norm of the block-diagonal residual over all signed modes. If the temporal Gram has norm at most `b`, the resulting rank-r factorization satisfies

\[
\|H-\widetilde H\|_F\leq\delta
=\epsilon_D+\epsilon_P+b\epsilon_B.
\]

Construct both actual r-by-r factor Grams from dyadic inner products and enclosed geometric sums. Certified Cholesky residuals normalize the factors to near-isometries. Exact small-core SVD residuals and polar corrections enclose its singular values; frame distortions enclose those of `H_tilde`. Weyl then expands the retained intervals by `±delta` and gives

\[
\sigma_{r+1}(H)\leq\delta,\qquad
\|H(I-P_{\mathrm{range}(F_R)})\|_F\leq\delta.
\]

If the certified rth lower bound exceeds the frozen threshold, `delta` lies below that threshold, and the certified ratio of largest to smallest retained singular values is below 2029, the numeric record has exactly **1893 singular values above the frozen threshold**. This does not assert that its exact algebraic rank equals 1893: integer quantization or small perturbations may add nonzero singular values below the threshold.

The bounds apply only to the frozen finite sample window; future prediction is not certified. The proof needs no dense Hankel array. It also does not require a small floating-point energy difference to resolve the tail. Exact full-record energy is retained as a separate check.

## Theorem 3: complete full-size perturbation controls

Changing the central reading `[a=0,k=M-1,c=0]` by amplitude `u` adds an M-by-M anti-diagonal block inside the full Hankel operator. Its M nonzero singular values are all `|u|/M` and its Frobenius norm is `|u|/sqrt(M)`.

For `u=2^-20`, this norm is exactly **2^-26**. Applying Weyl to the verified base bounds certifies the same frozen numeric signature. This is a single-vector perturbation control, not a calibration receipt.

For `u=1`, rank-r perturbation inequalities imply that at least `M-r=2203` singular values exceed `1/M-delta` when `r=1893`. This exceeds the frozen threshold and proves an actual rank-signature breach, rather than just an inconclusive tail estimate. Both complete modified records are scanned to verify the one-entry difference. The learner is not rerun for these perturbation certificates.

## Theorem 4: a conditional stability radius from the actual certificate

Write `l,u,tau` for the certified rth lower bound, largest upper bound and tail bound, `T` for the exact frozen threshold and `K=2029`. The numeric signature is preserved for every perturbation `E` satisfying

\[
\|E\|_2<\rho=\min\left(T-\tau,\ l-T,\frac{Kl-u}{K+1}\right).
\]

The source ceiling `B=9093197064441289377/1208925819614629174706176` lies strictly inside this radius. Conditional on `||E||2<=B`, the actual record certificate gives **condition <754.162**, with 1893 values above the frozen threshold. This is a perturbation theorem, not verification that an apparatus satisfies B.

Separately, if each complete 62-vector changes by at most `delta=2^-20` in Euclidean norm, the triangular Hankel weights sum to `M²` per preparation, giving `||E||F<=sqrt(37)·delta`. The retained condition bound then stays below **742.718**, and the Frobenius projection-tail bound follows as well. An operator-norm bound alone does not provide this Frobenius-tail claim.

## No-go: samples do not uniquely identify the continuous generator

On a real rotation plane, sampled evolutions with angular frequencies `omega` and `omega+2*pi*n/h` coincide at every integer multiple of sampling interval `h`. A record-only spectral certificate therefore cannot choose a unique continuous skew generator without an independently justified frequency range or other source information. Nor can it infer a global 747-dimensional unobservable subspace from one collection of sampled preparations. The earlier kernel theorem remains confined to the specified nominal operator and observer.

## Lossless replay input

The package stores a learned codec dictionary plus **every integer residual** needed to restore the original 150,321,232-byte record. These residuals are not omitted, smoothed or thresholded. The restored payload must match the original SHA-256 before processing. The learner then receives only the restored raw record and contract; the codec dictionary is not passed to the learner or verifier as a spectral hypothesis.

## Review and limitations

All verification here is by the constructor. The attached CRL-2 amendment is a governance proposal; its non-constructor review requirement has not been satisfied by these checks. No registry entry or physical promotion is claimed.

The numerical proposer has a finite resource envelope: at most 160 sketched temporal columns, stationary-plus-oscillatory frames, and conservative rank/range checks. It may HOLD on valid but noisier or more complicated records. Successful certification of this benchmark does not guarantee successful proposal generation for every admissible acquisition. The generic dense-candidate method remains available as a separate, unbenchmarked alternative.

The 62 history outputs remain distinct from 189 diagnostic outputs and additional six-ratio ports. This work does not re-certify six-ratio calibration, the source-defined shape statistic, apparatus error receipts or physical clock units.

## Noise-campaign corrections

The five listed cases have mathematical evidence about the global additive-vector budget and/or finite numeric signatures. They were not demonstrations of complete apparatus, calibration and model-family compliance.

In particular, the single-vector edit has amplitude `1/1048576 = 2^-20`. It attains the global vector ceiling at equality and is eight times the sufficient coordinate ceiling `1/8388608 = 2^-23`. Exceeding this *sufficient* coordinate criterion alone does not negate the separately proved vector bound; it does prevent describing the test as strictly inside every stated acquisition bound. The legacy failure included **over-ranking**, not merely rank deficiency. Coherent DC noise raised its stationary proposal count from1 to37 and its total real proposal count from1893 to1929. The already certified single-vector record gives a concrete distinction. The central impulse of amplitude `u=2^-20` contributes an embedded4096-by4096 anti-diagonal block with4096 singular values `u/4096=2^-32`. The baseline certificate supplies a rank1893 approximant with error at most `tau`.

A rank1893 perturbation can remove at most1893 of those4096 directions. Weyl therefore gives

\[
\sigma_{2203}(H_{\mathrm{single}})\geq 2^{-32}-\tau
=\frac{146856907921586914997}{633825300114114700748351602688}>0.
\]

Thus this encoded matrix has **algebraic rank at least2203**, while its certified count above the frozen threshold is **1893**. `RANK_COUNTEREXAMPLE.json` binds the result to the same record hash used in both campaigns. This does not establish what the baseline exact rank was or whether its exact rank changed.

## Lossless history is not bulk-state reconstruction

The supported codec result is that a specified dictionary, **every exact integer residual**, and the specified decoder restore the frozen encoded history byte for byte. Its hash round trip was checked. A general bijection over arbitrary record/dictionary pairs was not proved; the codec has a residual-range check and can refuse an input.

For the specified nominal operator and observer, define

\[
N=\bigcap_{k\geq0}\ker(RA^k).
\]

If `n` belongs to `N`, then `R exp(tA)(x+n)=R exp(tA)x` for every time. Any codec or deterministic processing of those observations is identical for both states. A codec therefore cannot distinguish the747 nominal hidden directions, recover them from their absence, or establish a unique continuous generator. In the supplied second evaluation, “state” must be replaced by “encoded observation record.” “Closure without leakage across the projection boundary” is unsupported as a physical or hidden-state claim.

The mathematical mechanism is simple: lossless coding preserves distinguishability already present in the data. It adds no observation channels. Known preparations, a chosen section or extra constraints can select a representative, but those are additional assumptions or inputs.

A graph Rayleigh bound gives f(U,z)+rho>=0 globally; near the orbit it is <=10*d². Thus pure base norm loss spends no positive norm-work budget, while norm gain does. Other norm-dependent errors require their separate parameter-derivative contribution in T_parameter.

W_defect_prefix must bound signed defect work at EVERY time prefix. Terminal net energy cancellation can hide an earlier exit; an exact canonical-oscillator counterexample is included. A certified direct prefix-work bound may sharpen the conservative full-tube gradient-times-path-length bound. The constant-rate inequality includes a quadratic duration term because norm drift enlarges the defect-work coefficient.

The exact source equation is Gdot=S in temporal gauge, with S=d_xG[Y]−ell_q*q*q†+ell_w*w*w†, and its covariant multiplier version. Summed trace(S)=ell_w−ell_q. The Gauss norm can drift by at most K_G*L_Y+L_norm_absolute, with K_G explicit. Exact zero-source admissibility requires initial zero Gauss and S=0 pointwise; energy confinement or a small drift bound is not repair. An external charge satisfying the same source equation is only a compatibility prescription, not a physical source sector constructed from UD.

Additive raw matter forcing is decomposed exactly into norm flux and normalized sphere-tangent forcing. A declared radial-loss control can leave normalized distance and relative energy zero while creating Gauss charge. White noise, jumps without a certified bridge, nonunitary/off-sphere outputs and arbitrary integrators are outside this continuous finite-variation theorem.

## Replay and inputs

- `python3 verify_source_work.py`: standard library; 43 exact finite/rational checks, twelve budget examples, invalid-input controls, raw projection and commutator algebra, terminal-work counterexample and rate-horizon identity. Full analytic arguments remain in the manuscript.
- `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 check_source_balance.py`: NumPy/SciPy floating diagnostics at ranks 1,2,3,5; four full-matrix source/trace/raw-force controls and eight centered ground-shift controls. General derivative fixtures with electric norm 0.1 are not endpoint-tube preparations; no trajectories or empirical data.
- `python3 source_work_budget.py INPUT.json`: use any fixture's `input` object from SOURCE_WORK_CERTIFICATE_v0.1.json. Rational strings are required for exact noninteger input. Initial norm intervals default to [N,N] as an illustrative assumption. Every bound requires guaranteed joint coverage; no measurement is inferred from the defaults.

Keys: a,N,eta,nq0,nw0,leakage_q,leakage_w,norm_gain_q,norm_gain_w,parameter_variation,defect_length,work_upper,score_upper,energy_upper,nu,beta_other,g0_upper,source_integral_upper. Norm initial intervals have two positive ordered endpoints. Absolute leakage bounds total variation, not terminal norm change. Optional gain bounds cover positive variation; otherwise absolute variation is used conservatively. `parameter_variation` covers actual explicit and norm-parameter potential derivatives. `work_upper` is an EVERY-PREFIX signed-work upper; `source_integral_upper` bounds the integral of the source norm. The calculator takes the tighter of supplied and speed-derived valid bounds. It does not infer source cancellation or data realizability. Initial Gauss is not assumed zero if its optional bound is absent.

At a=N=1 and inherited eta=1/829538022: B/4≈3.30e-40, norm-only absolute variation amplitude cap≈5.68e-24, and speed-only defect path cap≈1.09e-32 in model units. These are conservative sufficient bounds, not necessary physical precision or feasibility specifications. Mixed inputs share one budget.

Unchanged ERA/PET/GPC support files are hash-bound. Next: select a measurable realization or certify a reconstructed trajectory, then audit published data for the required observables and uncertainty information. No coupling unification, proton decay, monopole or other physical GUT conclusion is promoted. The separate 600-cell observer/sketch/estimator workstream is unchanged.

title: Measurable Realization and Published-Data Audit v0.1
status: CANDIDATE REALIZATION; DATASET-SCOPED AUDIT; PHYSICAL PROMOTION 0
note: One complete circuit waveform content audit, two atomic-data comparators; no full UD realization or GUT inference.
content:
1. Selection and decision
Decision: Select a classical, nonlinear U(1) rotor-matter circuit emulator as the first measurable UD realization candidate. Start at rank one. This is a development choice based on access to classical quadratures and programmable nonlinear interactions, not a claim that a full UD apparatus already exists.
Published anchor: Riechert et al., Physical Review B 105, 205141 (2022), demonstrated five matter sites and four oscillator links using nonlinear LC circuits and three-wave mixing. Its published data and code provide the closest audited component benchmark. The paper reports local Gauss-law measurements, spectra and driven transport. Read the body and appendices, not just the abstract [1-3].
Why not the other platforms first?: Cold-atom experiments supply real gauge-simulator evidence, but the audited experiments use different quantum-link state spaces and readouts. Population measurements cannot be silently identified with the complex classical UD state. Passive linear circuits do not implement the nonlinear matter-link or plaquette interactions. These are reasons for this scoped selection, not a comprehensive ranking of all hardware.
Critical mismatch: The published circuit uses an unconstrained complex link oscillator b. Writing b=sqrt(I) exp(i theta) makes the hopping amplitude depend on link action I. UD instead requires U=exp(i theta) with independent signed electric E, plus an E-squared energy and diamond holonomies. Fixing the oscillator amplitude while claiming its action remains a freely dynamical electric variable is not an exact mapping. No such identification is admitted.
Scope: This audit concerns the finite classical Hamiltonian and its measurement contract. It supplies no evidence for coupling unification, proton decay or monopoles, and no Standard Model or continuum correspondence. Experimental data can test a declared physical realization; they do not prove the mathematical theorem. Independent review and physical validation remain outstanding.

2. What the selected apparatus must represent
Carrier and state: The full rank-one target has 15 nodes, 28 oriented links and 18 diamonds, not a K4 graph with only four oscillator sites. Record theta_e and signed E_e for all 28 links, and two complex matter fields at each of 15 nodes. Before norm constraints this is 116 real state coordinates. This coordinate count is not an independent sensor-count or hardware-cost theorem.
Hamiltonian target: With D_U[i,j]=b_e U_e and h_U=i(D_U^dagger-D_U), retain the frozen Hamiltonian H=(a/2) sum E_e^2 + kappa sum_d(1-Re W_d) + n_q q^dagger h_U q + n_w w^dagger h_U w + mu(n_q+n_w). The normalized matter fields have opposite symplectic signs and their actual positive norm weights. A valid circuit/controller map must reproduce those brackets as well as this energy.
Implementation candidate, not a completed design: Use phase-bearing rotor variables with signed electric integrators, IQ matter channels, nonlinear matter-link mixing and four-link diamond feedback. An analog or hybrid controller may be investigated. Its latency, gain, saturation, noise and filtering enter the actual defect budget; software that integrates the target equations is only a numerical emulator until apparatus correspondence is calibrated. No circuit schematic, component procurement list or realizability theorem is supplied here.
Measurable preparation: Recover the 27 real invariant scalars in GPC: alpha=S^dagger S, gamma=|S^dagger Z|^2, total electric square norm, 14 full cycle traces and 10 negative-cycle active moments. Use s=sqrt(alpha), u=sqrt(gamma/alpha). At rank one the active moments are algebraically redundant with alpha and the corresponding real cycle traces; retain the frozen 27-channel interface conservatively. This does not establish a minimal measurement scheme.
Separate dynamics admission: In addition to the preparation score, obtain actual orbit-relative energy, coefficient/error bounds, positive norm floors and source/defect histories. The SDW budget requires every-prefix work, parameter-gradient variation and absolute/positive norm variation. Exact zero-Gauss admission requires initial G=0 and vanishing covariant source; small observed drift is not a repair. Rank-one tests cannot establish unused-color claims at higher rank.

3. Published data: access and coverage
A / Riechert circuit: selected primary benchmark: heiDATA DOI 10.11588/DATA/6MEKHI, released 3 February 2022, version 1.0: metadata lists 71 unrestricted files, including compressed acquisitions, KiCad files, acquisition code and two notebooks. Data license CC BY 4.0; code BSD 2-Clause. The landing page and ordinary dataset endpoint returned HTTP 500 during this audit; the public metadata export and individual text-file endpoints worked. The README links to tychon/U1CircuitsData. Its audited Git commit is 265b6671dde799d7c73f32247fa3ee93ae70e0f2 [2-3].
A / Content inspected: Read the README, acquisition documentation, Gauss extraction code and relevant notebook cells without executing imported scripts. Downloaded and parsed one complete ten-channel compressed acquisition. Its 30,941,478 bytes and MD5 81771941562f83818f3d905bd6f9e9e2 match heiDATA file 6385, DOI suffix 4PV8ZU. This is a content audit of one file, not a replay of all figures or all 71 files.
B / Yang 71-site experiment: Nature 587, 392-396 (2020); Harvard Dataverse DOI 10.7910/DVN/3RXD5F, version 1.1: 13 unrestricted files, CC0. Inventory includes Codes.rar and 12 figure tables. Read the full Fig.4.tab response, not the RAR or all tables. It has five numeric rows at 0, 30, 60, 90 and 120 ms, two population estimates and their standard deviations. The paper uses correlated atom occupations to assess local gauge-invariant states [4-5].
C / Mil atomic-mixture building block: Science 367, 1128-1130 (2020); Dryad DOI 10.5061/dryad.8gtht76k2 lists seven CSV files, about 4.52 KB. Read three file contents: Fig.2 lithium (9 rows), Fig.2 sodium (20 rows), Fig.3 (20 rows). Each has a time/pulse-length column, mean population or polarization, and error on mean. Remaining four CSV contents were not inspected; the landing-page extraction did not expose license terms, so no reuse-license claim is made here [6].
D / Excluded from experimental evidence: The 2025 article Large-scale 2+1D U(1) gauge theory with dynamical matter in a cold-atom quantum simulator is a proposal with perturbative and iMPS numerical benchmarks, not a newly acquired experimental dataset. Its target also omits the plaquette term. Do not count its simulated low gauge violation as measured UD evidence [7].

4. Raw-content audit: findings and limits
Waveform structure / reproducible PASS: The selected circuit file contains 1,000 rows, six metadata columns and 16,384 voltage samples per row. Channels 1-10 each have 100 records; the filename assigns nine oscillator signals and an empty tenth channel. All parsed values are finite. Sample rate is 1,953,125 Hz: interval 0.512 microseconds, record length 8.388608 ms, full-record FFT-bin spacing 119.2093 Hz. A bin width is not a confidence bound on a fitted frequency.
Acquisition identity and grouping: All ten channel groups share matching first-five metadata arrays. Frequency metadata spans 21-41 kHz in 100 distinct values, while recorded drive amplitude, phase and delay are zero. Therefore these must not automatically be treated as 100 independent repetitions of a single setting, or as a nonzero-drive sweep. Resolve that metadata distinction with the acquisition configuration before inferential fitting. Matching metadata does not establish clock-skew calibration.
Numerical sanity / not a calibration: Observed voltage range is -1.297863 to 1.243786 V, below the notebook's 15 V software clipping guard. That guard does not independently establish ADC headroom, linearity or voltage uncertainty. File SHA-256 is 7966700a6208e2bd2b5829a32b38cce7016f0c3460ace2708c85bac8577c282c. MD5 was used only to compare against published metadata, not as a modern integrity guarantee.
Extraction uncertainty: The notebook forms oscillator energies from voltage envelopes, uses frequency normalization for Gauss quantities and combines error terms in quadrature. Those operations need an explicit covariance model to justify correlated errors. The published extraction code's constants and peak/spline choices must be sensitivity-tested; channel gains, capacitor/frequency calibration, synchronization, feedback and filtering need a joint error record before a simultaneous interval claim.
Cold-atom audit flags: Two of nine lithium Fig.2 rows report zero error on mean. Never interpret those entries as exact, give them infinite inverse-variance weight, or invent an error floor without a declared sensitivity analysis. Yang's Fig.4 labels standard deviation, not guaranteed simultaneous error. Aggregated figure tables do not themselves supply shot-level covariance or the missing complex UD coherences.
Admission verdict: None of the audited datasets admits the full UD theorem: the circuit chain lacks UD topology, unitary rotor links, two-species target and plaquette term; quantum-link datasets use a different state space. No audited record supplies the full GPC/ERA/SDW preparation, actual energy and cumulative source-work package. This is a scoped finding about these records, not a proof that no suitable dataset exists anywhere.

5. Reanalysis and experiment requirements
Reanalysis that is justified next: For circuit data: freeze file/shot/channel identities; independently reconstruct envelopes and rotating-frame quadratures; reproduce published local Gauss curves and spectra; vary peak selection, time window and smoothing; estimate timing/gain/capacitance covariance; compare a calibrated gauge-invariant circuit model against detuned and gauge-breaking alternatives on held-out records. Fit the published circuit model, not UD mislabeled as that model. For atomic data: reproduce the reported population summaries with their stated error convention; obtain shot-level records before covariance-sensitive local tests.
First new experiment / component stage: Build and calibrate one closed diamond with two matter species and independently read signed electric channels. Check canonical rotor response, unit modulus, matter-link current, plaquette response, opposite-species convention and injected Gauss-source balance. A diamond is a component test, not the 15-node theorem. Proceed to the full 15/28/18 carrier only after those mappings and defect budgets are established.
Minimum experimental record: Save synchronized raw quadratures, rotor phases/electric values, channel and orientation maps, clock calibration, offsets/gains/nonlinearity and their covariance, independent preparation repeats, norm histories, applied coefficient schedules, feedback/drive/loss histories and outlier/saturation rules. Predeclare the energy/time conversion, target Hamiltonian, model discrepancy, hypothesis tests, held-out split and simultaneous-coverage construction. Acquire null controls with broken gauge coupling and controlled source injection.
Hard feasibility gate: Frozen endpoint bounds are sufficient, not necessary. At a=N=1 the inherited eta is 1/829538022; the SDW work allowance B/4 is approximately 3.30e-40 in model energy units. These cannot be called voltage, timing or energy tolerances without a calibrated map. Do not promise current hardware can meet them, or weaken them post hoc to claim theorem certification. Seek sharper bounds or test finite-amplitude predictions outside the certificate while labeling that scope honestly.
Promotion gates: Require an explicit canonical state/action/unit map; independently bounded model defects; all frozen initial and every-prefix gates; attributable non-constructor review; and independently acquired physical validation. Only then consider a narrowly scoped bridge receipt. Nominal action, coefficient ledger and existing theorem claims are unchanged. This report is not a new theorem manuscript and changes physical promotion by zero.

References and reproducibility
[1] Primary circuit paper: H. Riechert et al., Engineering a U(1) lattice gauge theory in classical electric circuits, Phys. Rev. B 105, 205141 (2022). DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.105.205141. Body/appendices inspected at https://arxiv.org/html/2108.01086v1 . The HTML rendering carries a later generated date; the paper is cited by its journal year and version identifier.
[2] Primary circuit data: https://doi.org/10.11588/DATA/6MEKHI . Metadata export used: https://heidata.uni-heidelberg.de/api/datasets/export?exporter=dataverse_json&persistentId=doi:10.11588/data/6MEKHI . Waveform DOI: https://doi.org/10.11588/DATA/6MEKHI/4PV8ZU .
[3] Author-linked code and data mirror: https://github.com/tychon/U1CircuitsData/tree/265b6671dde799d7c73f32247fa3ee93ae70e0f2 . The audited compressed file is in 05-21/. Code was inspected as text; acquisition programs and notebook cells were not executed. audit_waveform.py independently parses the selected file and emits WAVEFORM_AUDIT_v0.1.json.
[4-5] Yang experiment and dataset: B. Yang et al., Observation of gauge invariance in a 71-site Bose-Hubbard quantum simulator, Nature 587, 392-396 (2020): https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2910-8 . Public abstract, availability statement and figure metadata inspected; subscription-only body not accessed. Data: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/3RXD5F ; Fig.4 content: https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/access/datafile/4013035 .
[6] Mil data and linked publication: A. Mil et al., A scalable realization of local U(1) gauge invariance in cold atomic mixtures, Science 367, 1128-1130 (2020), DOI 10.1126/science.aaz5312. Dataset: https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.8gtht76k2 . Inspected file_stream IDs 219166, 219165 and 219164. Publication details are linked by the primary data repository; no claim of full Science-body inspection.
[7] Proposal exclusion: https://www.nature.com/articles/s42005-025-02144-8 . Full public body inspected to distinguish proposal/numerical calculations from experimental acquisition.
Provenance and scope: Audit date: 18 October 2026 UTC. Constructor: Codex, at user request. Frozen project base: 57c90583afae95fa8f91ce607194a507edbbf456; GPC, ERA and SDW v0.1 are conditional internal mathematical inputs, not external empirical evidence. No independent reviewer. Source inventories and inspected-text records accompany this report. No full corpus search, all-file replay, confidence interval or experimental validation is claimed.

This completes the **known-nominal spectral benchmark**. It uses temporal factor structure to form actual factor Grams; the generic candidate-basis adapter on unknown measured records remains open. The inherited 747-dimensional hidden subspace is not identified or monitored by this run.

# Frozen nominal Hankel benchmark, v0.2

Constructor verification only. Physical promotion: **0**. Independent review: pending.

This benchmark generates the nominal observation record from the pinned integer 600-cell operator, original 62-coordinate readout and 37 pinned preparations. It does not substitute identity Gram matrices, random matrices or artificial residual noise. All thresholds come from the frozen contract; the shape gate and diagnostic outputs have no role in the spectral tail test.

## Frozen object and method

The record is `Y[a,k,c]`, with 37 preparations, 8191 times `t=k/2`, and 62 history outputs. There are **18,790,154** scalar readings. The payload consists of little-endian signed int64 numerators, quantum `2^-48`, nearest ties-even. NPY files have a header; the recorded payload hash excludes that header.

The normalized matrix is

\[
H_{(i,c),(j,a)}=Y[a,i+j,c]/(4096\,2^{48}),\qquad 0\leq i,j<4096.
\]

Its shape is 253952 by 151552. A dense float64 copy would take **307,895,468,032 bytes = 286.75 GiB**. None is constructed.

1. Recompute every exact moment `R(-A²)^k S` and `RA(-A²)^k S`, `k=0,...,52`, from the actual sparse operator and sign matrix. Check the degree-53 annihilator on all preparations, isolate its 53 distinct real roots and verify the operator is skew symmetric.
2. Use its spectral projectors to reconstruct the stationary component and 52 positive-frequency pairs, with interval arithmetic at 512 bits. Round modal coefficients and direct trigonometric phases to dyadic rationals. Generate the complete encoded record through exact integer matrix products and ties-even quantization.
3. Factor each modal observation block as `Lλ Rλ*`, with a rigorously bounded residual, retaining a total of 1893 signed-mode directions. The selected ranks are a numerical construction choice; the residual bound, not that choice, justifies the discarded tail.
4. Write `H̃=F_L F_R*`, where the temporal vectors in the left factor use `exp(+iωj/2)/sqrt(M)` and those in the right factor use its conjugate. Construct the two **actual 1893 by 1893 factor Grams** using exact integer factor inner products and enclosed geometric sums. Convert conjugate pairs to real factors by `[f++f−,−i(f+−f−)]` on the left and half that transformation on the right. These are a structured nominal alternative to the generic candidate-basis Grams in the parent verifier; they are not claimed to be the same matrices.
5. Verify Cholesky and SVD proposals using exact integer matrix products, Frobenius residual bounds and polar corrections. Independently check all 240870 coefficient entries, 851864 nonstationary phase components and 5460 temporal pairs against uniform dyadic bounds. Recompute temporal and modal frame bounds directly by Gershgorin enclosures.
6. Evaluate the exact weighted energy of the encoded record, full-size `Hx` and `Hᵀz` on deterministic dense integer probes, their exact adjoint identity and 32 direct entries in each direction. Compare the energy with the factor-Gram trace and its error bound. Small dense regression cases separately check the factor identities and their singular spectra.

## Why the enclosures hold

For dyadic factor Grams `Ĝ_L,Ĝ_R`, let `γ_L,γ_R` include both Gram construction error and exact Cholesky residuals. With verified positive lower bounds `a_L,a_R` for the true Grams, the normalized factor defects satisfy

\[
\eta_L\leq\gamma_L/(a_L-\gamma_L),\qquad
\eta_R\leq\gamma_R/(a_R-\gamma_R).
\]

For the exact core `S=L_LᵀL_R`, verified proposed singular values `s_i` have an error enclosure `e`. Consequently,

\[
\sqrt{(1-\eta_L)(1-\eta_R)}(s_i-e)
\leq\sigma_i(\widetilde H)\leq
\sqrt{(1+\eta_L)(1+\eta_R)}(s_i+e).
\]

The uniform phase and coefficient checks give a scalar trajectory error at most `210·2^-60+2^-49`. Therefore its Hankel Frobenius error is at most `sqrt(37·62)` times that quantity. If `b` bounds the temporal Gram norm and `ε_modal` is the combined modal Frobenius residual, then

\[
\|H-\widetilde H\|_2\leq\|H-\widetilde H\|_F
\leq\delta=\delta_{trajectory}+b\varepsilon_{modal}.
\]

Weyl's inequality adds `±δ` to the core enclosures and yields `σ_1894(H)≤δ`. The Frobenius discarded tail is also at most `δ`: projecting onto the exact right factor's range annihilates `H̃(I−P)`, so `||H(I−P)||F≤δ`. The final certificate uses the **exact rational** threshold from the frozen contract. Bounds are also recorded as outward dyadic rational pairs; printed decimals are for reading.

The exact full-record energy is an independent consistency check. The final tail bound comes from the complete source-bound factor residual, rather than subtracting nearly equal floating-point energies.

## Scope and corrections

**DERIVED / constructor verified:** the complete known-nominal spectral calculation, encoded record hash, count above the frozen threshold, conditioning and tail, exact full-size probe actions, total energy and recorded resource usage.

**OPEN:** the generic model-free dense-candidate adapter on an independently acquired record; apparatus and calibration receipts over the acquisition horizon; independent review. This benchmark does not establish the six-ratio calibration or source-defined shape gate anew. It uses 62 history outputs, distinct from 189 diagnostic outputs and four additional six-ratio ports. It neither evaluates the rejected `2^-49` auxiliary gate nor reassigns `2^-38` to a Borel norm.

The nominal 747-dimensional unobservable invariant subspace is inherited from the frozen model. Its invisibility is a structural observer limitation, not evidence of quarantine measured during this computation. The benchmark does not identify hidden dynamics.

The supplied parallel script is a **NO-GO benchmark**: its two `5I` matrices do not derive from the record, it never performs a Hankel action, diagonal random noise is not a discarded projection tail, and its acceptance comparison reuses the unrelated shape gate. `2028.403` was a conditional sufficient ceiling in the parent method, not a previously observed condition number.

A first local draft used interval phase recurrence and a comparison of overlapping interval balls that could understate its error envelope. That draft's phase certificate is superseded. Version 0.2 evaluates phases directly and takes maxima of outward endpoints; a separate uniform-error checker verifies every phase. The fresh rerun reproduced the same encoded payload hash. No initial-draft bound is used in the final refined certificate.

## Reproduction

Install the pinned dependencies in `requirements.txt`. From the package root, execute `python replay.py NEW_DIRECTORY`. The destination must not exist. Replay copies only sources and scripts into an isolated directory, then runs `run_all.py`; it does not trust cached output files. Large record, Gram and SVD intermediates are regenerated locally. The package preserves compact dyadic factors, phases, hashes, interval certificates and logs; it does not need the 150-MB record or a dense Hankel file to preserve its definition.

Timing values are machine-specific numerical benchmark measurements, not physical acquisition times. `PIPELINE_BENCHMARK.json` gives one sequential run, including all verification stages, and the maximum child-process RSS. Resource usage includes exact matrix-product workspaces, beyond the 54.68-MiB pair of stored int64 Grams.

## Construction and scope

The campaign specification was fixed by the constructor before generating its noise records. It is not independently reviewed preregistration. The baseline was already known constructed nominal data. Five bounded noise recipes are tested: a single-vector impulse, dense signs, coherent DC offsets, a rational ramp and an integer period-127 triangular clock. Each bounded recipe satisfies the exact global62-vector ceiling `delta=1/1048576`. The dense, DC, ramp and periodic coordinate amplitudes are at most `1/8388608`. The old relative temporal cutoff fails on several bounded records. It also exposes an indexing error in a diagnostic print when all160 sketch singular values exceed the cutoff. An exact sketch Gram and validated160-dimensional eigensystem prove a uniform separation of105 temporal components over the complete additive vector-error ball. A separate global real-rank allocation shares the frozen1893-dimensional approximation budget among modal blocks. Positive-frequency directions cost two real dimensions each. # Fixed-sketch blind-record audit

Development — no registry entry. Constructor verification only. Independent
review not established; physical promotion 0. This work advances issue #178
without claiming independent data, full acquisition qualification or convergence
for every bounded perturbation.

The frozen 160-column sketch has an exact 2134-dimensional nullspace in its
2294-dimensional preparation/channel input. A concrete integer witness defines
record perturbations whose exact sketches vanish. The new bounded impulse
record nevertheless has **algebraic Hankel rank at least 30,875**. Its full
verifier still certifies **exactly 1893 singular values above the frozen
threshold**. This makes the rank/threshold distinction concrete on a much
larger exact lower bound than the earlier scalar impulse example.

See `THEOREMS.md` for the proof and `EXACT_BLIND_FAMILY_CERTIFICATE.json` for
the integer witness checks, exact minors and rational gap. The rank lower bound
uses a pinned inherited baseline approximation certificate; it does not claim
the baseline's exact rank is 1893 or prove the noisy exact rank increased.

## Execution contract

Three constructed cases were fixed before generation on an already known
synthetic baseline: bounded impulse, bounded alternating clock and an oversized
alternating control. Their additions are exactly invisible to the mathematical
sketch. The original proposer and full verifier are unchanged and hash-frozen.
Each case gets one proposal and one full certificate attempt; HOLDs are kept.
Floating sketches need not agree bit-for-bit despite exact cancellation.

The first two cases satisfy both the sufficient scalar additive ceiling2^-23
and global62-vector ceiling2^-20. This is not the complete acquisition contract.
The third deliberately violates both. All three discover105 temporal components;
discovery order alone is therefore inadequate for certifying the full record.

`CAMPAIGN_RESULTS.json` preserves final pass/HOLD decisions and exact certificates
are in `results/certificate-*`. A HOLD refuses the proposed certificate; it is
not alone proof that the true record's signature fails or that a physical
mechanism caused a failure. The sketch nullspace is unrelated to the nominal
observer's747-dimensional dynamical kernel, which remains unobserved.

# Fixed-sketch blindness and a bounded high-rank record

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0. Constructor checks only;
independent review is not established. These are statements about the frozen
numeric-record pipeline, not the physical 747-dimensional unobservable subspace.

## 1. The declared compression map

Write D[k,37c+a]=Y[a,k,c], with 8191 time rows and 2294 preparation/channel
columns. The proposer uses Z=D W/64, where W is the fixed 2294×160 sign matrix
from seed 172026. An exact nonzero determinant of its first 160 rows proves
rank(W)=160, hence dim ker(W^T)=2134.

The supplied integer witness v has 250 nonzero entries, maximum absolute
coefficient 23 and squared Euclidean norm 16228. Every one of the 160 integer
entries of v^T W is exactly zero. All coordinates after index319 vanish.
The witness was found by LLL on rows [I_320 | 2^36 W_320]. The exact checker
needs only the witness, not trust in that search or an optimality claim.

For every temporal vector f and scale s,

    E = (s/2^48) f v^T  implies  (D+E)W/64 = DW/64.

This is exact mathematical equality. Floating evaluation of two differently
encoded records can differ by roundoff. In particular the complete numerical
proposer need not output byte-identical phases: it also fits coefficients
against the full D after discovery. Discovery alone cannot determine the
full record. No universal complete-record or residual certificate follows
from this fixed sketch without additional restrictions or verification.

## 2. Both additive gates are satisfied by the bounded family

Let s=floor(2^25/23)=1458888 and take an integer clock with |f_k|<=1.
The largest coordinate error numerator is33554424<2^25, and the maximum
62-vector squared error numerator is2145381030116352<2^56.
With encoding denominator2^48, every scalar obeys the sufficient2^-23
gate and every62-vector obeys the2^-20 gate. The latter norm is at most
1.646e-7. This establishes these two additive gates, not the complete
acquisition contract or its calibration, timing, disturbance or custody clauses.

## 3. Exact singular structure of the two noise clocks

Let B[c,a]=v[37c+a]. Exactly eight channel rows are nonzero. Its rank is8.
The leading principal minors of B_active B_active^T -4I are all positive;
they are stored in EXACT_BLIND_FAMILY_CERTIFICATE.json. Sylvester's criterion
therefore gives sigma_min_nonzero(B)>2. This uses exact integer determinants,
not a floating eigenvalue estimate. Its Frobenius norm is sqrt(16228).

Index the normalized Hankel by rows(i,c), columns(j,a), with0<=i,j<4096
and entries Y[a,i+j,c]/4096 in decoded model units.

For f_k=1 at k=4095 and zero elsewhere,

    H(E) = s/(4096*2^48) (J_4096 tensor B),

where J is the reversal permutation. Consequently rank H(E)=32768;
its positive singular values exceed ell=2s/(4096*2^48).

For f_k=(-1)^k, write u_i=(-1)^i. Then

    H(E) = s/2^48 ((u u^T/4096) tensor B).

Its rank is8 and its nonzero singular values are exactly s/2^48 times
those of B. Thus two clocks invisible to the same sketch give very different
Hankel ranks. For a fixed s, their Hankel Frobenius norms are respectively
s sqrt(16228)/(64*2^48) and s sqrt(16228)/2^48.

## 4. At least 30,875 nonzero singular values in the bounded impulse record

The pinned clean record's earlier record-only certificate supplies a real
rank-at-most1893 approximation A_r with ||H_clean-A_r||_F<=tau, where

    tau = 1434089336178995862 / 1267650600228229401496703205376
        < 1.132e-12.

This baseline certificate and its raw-record hash are inherited explicitly;
the new exact checker does not rerun that earlier spectral proof. It makes no
assertion that the clean quantized Hankel has exact rank1893.

The rank perturbation inequality gives

    sigma_(32768-1893)(H(E)+A_r) >= sigma_32768(H(E)) > ell.

Weyl's bound and ||H_clean-A_r||_2<=tau imply

    sigma_30875(H_clean+H(E)) > ell-tau > 1.399e-12 > 0.

All fractions and the positivity comparison are checked exactly. Therefore
the complete bounded impulse record has algebraic rank at least30875.
Its independently executed full-record signature check is a separate
calculation: rank at least30875 is compatible with only1893 singular values
above the much larger frozen selection threshold (about1.504e-5).
No increase in exact rank relative to the clean quantized record is asserted.

## 5. Scope of the oversized control

The third case uses s=floor(2^40/23) and the alternating clock. It remains
exactly invisible to the sketch, but deliberately violates both additive
error gates. Its role is to test whether full-record verification can refuse
a proposal that discovery did not reject. A HOLD is refusal to certify that
proposal; it does not by itself prove the true signature fails, identify a
failure mechanism, or expose the nominal observer's hidden747 dimensions.

The campaign is constructor-predeclared on a previously known synthetic
baseline. It is not independent preregistration, independent data or blinded
review. Universal phase-fitting convergence remains open.

# Exact residual preflight for the record-only spectral certificate

Status: EXACT derivation plus constructor execution tests. Physical promotion 0.
The theorem concerns the current finite, normalized record and its proposed modal fit;
it does not identify a physical system, recover hidden states, or decide a record's
true spectral signature after a failed fit.

## 1. Norm and phase convention

The record is `Y[a,k,c]/2^48`, with 37 preparations, 8191 times and 62 channels.
The normalized Hankel has entries `Y[a,i+j,c]/(4096*2^48)`.
For a proposed temporal model, the existing verifier encloses every sine and cosine
by a dyadic multiple of 2^-60 with error strictly below 2^-60. Coefficients are
int64 numerators scaled by 2^-60. Let `C` be the sum of the largest absolute
coefficient over all 2294 channel/preparation coordinates, separately for each
nonstationary sine/cosine row. The stationary row has no phase error.

Let `w_k=min(k+1,8191-k,4096)`. After checking every reading exactly, define

\[
 F=\frac{\sum_{k,c,a}w_k\,(P_k C_{c,a}-2^{72}Y_{a,k,c})^2}
          {4096^2\,2^{240}}.
\]

Here `P_k` is the integer dyadic-phase row and `C_{c,a}` in the numerator denotes
the coefficient column, not the nonnegative bound `C` above. This is the exact
squared Frobenius norm of the dyadic-phase model's Hankel residual. There is no
SVD tolerance or sampled subset in this computation.

The difference between the dyadic-phase model and the exact-phase model obeys

\[
 \|H_{\rm phase}-H_{\rm dyadic}\|_F
 < e:=48C\,2^{-120},
\]

because `sqrt(37*62)<48`, `sum_k w_k=4096^2`, and each scalar phase-induced
model difference has magnitude at most `C*2^-120`. If `C=0` this difference is zero.
Using `<=e` uniformly also covers this case. This norm refers to the modal phase
approximation, not measurement noise or the contract's source-defined shape gate.

## 2. Exact square-root bracket and early-HOLD theorem

Write `F=u/v>=0` in lowest terms and fix `b=100`. Compute using integer arithmetic

\[
 n=\operatorname{isqrt}\left(\left\lfloor\frac{u2^{2b}}v\right\rfloor\right),\qquad
 \ell=n2^{-b}.
\]

Then `ell^2<=F<(ell+2^-b)^2`. Define `L=max(0,ell-e)`.
By the reverse triangle inequality, the true exact-phase proposed residual
has Frobenius norm at least `L`. The frozen selection threshold is

\[
 T=9093197064441289377/604462909807314587353088.
\]

**Theorem.** If `L>T`, the existing residual-budget certificate for this same
proposal cannot return `CERTIFIED_NUMERIC_RECORD_SIGNATURE`. It is sound to
return `HOLD` before modal factors, factor Grams, Cholesky and core SVD.

**Proof.** The existing proof uses a validated upper enclosure of
`sqrt(F)+phase_error_upper`, plus a nonnegative truncation allowance, as its
residual budget. This upper budget bounds the true proposed residual, which is
at least `L>T`. Therefore its required strict test `total_error<T` cannot pass.
All other outcomes of the old verifier, including an inconclusive arithmetic
step, are already HOLD. Cases where `L<=T` execute the identical old `verify`
function. Thus every accepted outcome is preserved, provided its unchanged proof
executes successfully; the preflight alone can never create a new acceptance.
This theorem presumes the original phase checks and exact residual calculation
have completed and the final input-identity check succeeds. QED.

Equality and unresolved floor-resolution cases continue. No float is used for the
gate. A large residual is a Frobenius residual of a particular approximation;
no inference that a particular true singular value is too large follows. Another
proposal can succeed. The preflight also does not prove fitting convergence,
experimental acquisition admission, independent review, or a leakage mechanism.

## 3. Implementation scope

`residual_preflight.py` implements the integer/rational theorem.
`certify_record.py` calls it only after all 18,790,154 readings and phase components
are checked. The positive branch calls the byte-unchanged `proof_math.py`.
Both branches perform the original final record/contract/proposal SHA-256 recheck.
Early HOLD supplies no fabricated singular-value or condition bounds.
`RESIDUAL_PREFLIGHT.json` is separate from the full positive certificate, so the
existing positive certificate schema/bytes can be compared directly.

The code and planned controls were frozen before these new full executions,
although the constructed control records and their old outcomes were already
known. This is a constructor regression benchmark, not a blinded independent run.

# A complementary finite observation for the fixed temporal sketch

Development lane; constructor proofs and executions. Physical promotion 0.
This is an engineering change to temporal discovery, not a new physical channel
or an independently reviewed bridge. Thresholds and sketch choices are O03
protocol controls; they are not derived physical constants.

## 1. Exact targeted kernel reduction

Use time-by-coordinate record `D[k,37c+a]`, with 8191 times and 2294 coordinates.
The existing sketch is `S=W/64`, where the pinned 2294-by-160 sign matrix has
rank160. The pinned null witness stores320 integer coordinates followed by1974
implicit zeros. Its exact identities are

\[
 v^T W=0,\qquad v^T v=16228.
\]

Add the computed column `g=v/128`, forming `S_+=[W/64 | v/128]`.
The first160 columns are unchanged. Because `g` is nonzero and orthogonal to
their span, `rank S_+=161` and

\[
 \ker S_+^T=\ker W^T\cap v^\perp,\quad
 \dim\ker W^T=2134,\quad \dim\ker S_+^T=2133.
\]

Thus this one-column augmentation removes exactly one sketch null direction.
It does not reduce the nominal dynamical observer's747-dimensional unobservable
subspace. It recombines existing readings and requires no additional physical
measurements.

For every old blind-family perturbation `E=(s/2^48) f v^T`,

\[
 ES_+=(s/2^{48})[0\mid (4057/32) f].
\]

Every nonzero member (`s!=0`, `f!=0`) is exposed algebraically. Exposure does not
mean its amplitude is above a detection threshold. In particular the bounded
impulse and alternating cases should remain below the discovery error floor.
The new kernel still supports other blind families. Any fixed sketch with
fewer than2294 columns has a nonzero nullspace, so this cannot be a universal
adversarial blindness repair.

## 2. Noise transfer and finite conditioning

The complement has squared norm `4057/4096`, so

\[
 \|S_+\|_F^2=371097/4096.
\]

If every one of303067 preparation/time62-vectors has Euclidean error at most
`delta=2^-20`, then the reshaped error matrix obeys

\[
 \|E\|_F\le\sqrt{37\cdot8191}\,\delta,\qquad
 \|ES_+\|_2\le\|E\|_F\|S_+\|_F\le N,
 \quad N^2=112467254499/4503599627370496.
\]

The frozen discovery cutoff is the outward100-bit dyadic upper bound on `2N`
written in SKETCH_RULE.json. No value is retuned after the controls run.
This is the temporal discovery cutoff, distinct from the full Hankel selection
threshold and from the source-defined shape gate.

Let the new exact-Gram certificate for the baseline give lower bound `L0` on
sigma105, upper bound `U0` on sigma1 and upper bound `T0` on sigma106.
Weyl's inequality gives, throughout the stated vector-error ball,

\[
 \sigma_{105}((D_0+E)S_+)\ge L_0-N,\quad
 \sigma_{106}((D_0+E)S_+)\le T_0+N,\quad
 \kappa_{105}\le(U_0+N)/(L_0-N).
\]

The exact interval comparisons verify `L0-N>cutoff>T0+N`. Therefore exactly105
singular values of this finite temporal sketch exceed the cutoff for every
perturbation in that ball, with the stored uniform condition bound.
This does not prove convergence of phase estimation, coefficient fitting,
continuous-generator uniqueness, exact algebraic rank105 or full acquisition
qualification. The declared vector-error ball is not the complete acquisition
contract.

## 3. Validated small-Gram spectral arithmetic

No dense Hankel is used. Set integer `A=[2W|v]`, integer raw data `X=2^48D` and
`Z=XA`. Every partial sum is bounded below signed-int64 overflow before the
integer multiplication. The exact sketch Gram is `G=Z^T Z/2^110` (161-by-161).
The stored Gram entries use decimal strings, not lossy binary64 integers.

Floating eigensolvers supply untrusted, dyadically quantized `Q,Lambda`.
The checker computes exact residual norms with outward interval arithmetic:
`eta>=||Q^TQ-I||_2`, `r>=||GQ-Q Lambda||_2`, `g>=||G||_2`.
If `eta<1`, put

\[
 s=\sqrt{1+\eta},\quad d=\eta/(1+\sqrt{1-\eta}),\quad
 \rho=g\eta+rs+\|\Lambda\|_2d(s+1).
\]

For the orthogonal polar factor `U` of `Q`, `||Q-U||_2<=d` and
`||G-U Lambda U^T||_2<=rho`. The latter follows by splitting
`G-Q Lambda Q^T=G(I-QQ^T)+(GQ-Q Lambda)Q^T` and bounding the polar replacement.
Every true ordered Gram eigenvalue is therefore within `rho` of its proposed
ordered value. Strict squared-cutoff comparisons classify all161 eigenvalues;
square roots yield the retained singular-value and condition bounds.
The portable replay checker rechecks the stored exact Grams and untrusted
factors; it does not silently trust a floating SVD.

## 4. Oversized alternating control

The intentionally out-of-budget alternating perturbation is a Nyquist term
`(-1)^k`. Adding the complement can expose this extra real temporal component.
A certified count106 is legitimate temporal behavior; it is incompatible with
this particular proposer's frozen model of one stationary mode plus conjugate
non-Nyquist pairs. Its resulting HOLD is model/order refusal, not evidence of a
physical fracture or a proof that the full record signature fails.

## 5. Resource and governance scope

The extra float64 trajectory column costs65528 bytes, with2568 extra bytes for
one161-by-161 versus160-by-160 float64 Gram (integer proof storage differs).
The column count rises by1/160=0.625%; the Frobenius noise envelope rises by less
