# Finite-window phase stability around a pinned fitted reference

Development lane; physical promotion 0. Exact conditional matrix analysis plus
constructor computations. Independent review is pending. The reference phases
are learned from a numeric record; they are not nominal source modes, measured
physical truth, or a uniquely identified continuous generator.

## 1. Source model and validated constants

Let `n=8191`, `q=105` and `S=[W/64 | v/128]` be the pinned complementary sketch.
Let `Z0=D0 S` be the pinned clean record's sketch. The previous exact161-by-161
Gram certificate gives `sigma105(Z0)>=L0`. Let

\[
 M_{k,:}=\sum_{j=1}^{q}e^{ik\theta_j}C_{j,:},\quad
 \theta_j\in\{0,\pm\widehat\theta_1,\ldots,\pm\widehat\theta_{52}\}
\]

be the real modal model obtained from the pinned clean learned proposal after
applying the same sketch. The coefficient convention is the original stationary,
cosine and sine convention. The full complex representation is only a change
of basis. Every raw reading contributes to the exact integer sketch; no nominal
600-cell operator or nominal frequencies enter this calculation.

`certify_phase.py` computes an exact unweighted squared residual `F` between
the integer sketch and dyadic approximations to the modal phases. If `CA` is
the integer product of the proposed coefficients with `[2W|v]`, its entries
represent coefficients at scale2^-67. Every sine/cosine dyadic error is less
than2^-60. With `Cmax` the sum of the largest absolute `CA` coefficient in
each nonstationary row,

\[
 \|Z_0-M\|_2\le\|Z_0-M\|_F
 \le\varepsilon_0:=\sqrt F+
 \sqrt{8191\cdot161}\,C_{\max}/2^{127}.
\]

The resulting bound is about2.639e-11. It is a newly computed fit bound, not an
assumption that the quantized record has exact temporal rank105. Since `M` has
rank at most105, Weyl's inequality and
`alpha=L0-epsilon0>0` prove it has rank exactly105 and
`sigma105(M)>=alpha`.

Normalize the Vandermonde frame by `V[k,j]=exp(ik theta_j)/sqrt(n)` and set
`G=V* V`. Off-diagonal entries use the finite geometric sum. Exact interval
bounds and Gershgorin give `a I <= G <= b I`, with `a>0`.
For every pair of distinct reference eigenvalues, the chord separation obeys

\[
 |e^{i\theta_j}-e^{i\theta_l}|\ge s_{\min}>0.
\]

All constants are outward dyadic bounds in PHASE_STABILITY_CERTIFICATE.json.
The minimum reference chord separation is approximately0.00214408.

## 2. Conditional phase-matching theorem

Suppose a new record is `D0+E`, with each62-vector error at most `delta` across
37 preparations and8191 times. Its sketch is `Z=M+R`, where

\[
 \|R\|_2\le e:=\varepsilon_0+
 \sqrt{37\cdot8191\cdot371097/4096}\,\delta.
\]

Consider the **exact-arithmetic** estimator: take an orthonormal basis `U` of
the leading105 left singular vectors of `Z`, delete its last/first row to form
`U_-`, `U_+`, and calculate `T=U_-^dagger U_+` by exact least squares.
This theorem concerns that estimator. It is not an implementation-error proof
for the floating SVD/least-squares routine used in the proposer.

Define

\[
 K=\sqrt{b/a},\quad \beta=\sqrt{1-q/(na)},\quad
 t=e/(\alpha-e),\quad d=\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{1-t^2}},\quad
 r=\frac{K d(1+K)}{\beta-d}.
\]

If `alpha>2e` and `beta>d`, every eigenvalue of `T` lies within distance `r`
of some reference `exp(i theta_j)`. If also `2r<s_min`, these disks are
pairwise disjoint and there is exactly one eigenvalue in each disk, counting
multiplicity. When `r<1`, the corresponding circular phase error is at most
`arcsin(r)` radians per sample.

**Proof.** Put `Q=V G^-1/2`. Then `Q*Q=I` and
`Q_+=Q_- J`, where `J=G^1/2 diag(exp(i theta_j)) G^-1/2` has diagonalizer
condition at most `K` and norm at most `K`. Each row of `Q` has squared norm
at most `q/(na)`. Consequently `sigma_min(Q_-)>=beta`.

Projecting the leading left singular-vector equation for `Z=M+R` off the
column space of `M` gives
`||(I-QQ*)U||_2 <= e/sigma105(Z) <= e/(alpha-e)=t`.
The leading subspace is separated because `alpha>2e`. A unitary alignment of
`U` with `Q` has basis distance at most `d`. After that alignment,

\[
 \|U_+-U_-J\|_2\le d(1+K),\qquad
 \sigma_{\min}(U_-)\ge\beta-d.
\]

Least squares therefore bounds `||T-J||_2<=d(1+K)/(beta-d)`.
Diagonalizing `J` bounds every perturbed eigenvalue within the stated radius
(Bauer-Fike, directly by the diagonal resolvent/Neumann series). Along the
homotopy `J+x(T-J)`, `0<=x<=1`, the eigenvalues stay inside these disks.
If the full disks are disjoint, multiplicity cannot move between them, giving
one-to-one matching. A disk of radius `r<1` about a unit-circle point subtends
at most `arcsin(r)` from the origin. QED.

## 3. Certified grid boundary, not an algorithm-failure boundary

The dyadic grid was frozen as `delta=2^-k`, `k=20,...,40`, before execution.
The largest radius on this grid satisfying unique matching is `2^-27`.
There `r<0.000646029` and phase error `<0.000646029` radians per sample.
At the full `2^-20` vector budget the theorem gives only a one-sided enclosure:
`r<0.088763` and angular error to some reference phase `<0.088880`; the disks
overlap, so unique matching is not certified. This is a limitation of this
sufficient bound, not evidence that actual phase recovery fails there. It does
not establish that2^-27 is an optimal or necessary threshold.

The previous temporal-order theorem remains valid at2^-20. Stable component
count, retained conditioning, individual phase matching and convergence of a
particular numerical fitter are distinct claims.

## 4. Two fitting controls

Two new deterministic coherent phase-shift controls have declared vector-error
budgets2^-28 and2^-20. They shift the lower member of the closest positive
reference pair, using a source-bound coefficient L1 Lipschitz scale. A floating
constructor rounds the additive perturbations to encoded integers; exact
integer checks verify the actual vector/scalar error gates. Both remain known
constructor records, not independent apparatus or blinded data.

Returned phase numerators are compared exactly with the intended constructor
phase numerators. These differences are empirical parameter discrepancies;
the generated quantized record is not asserted to be exactly that modal model.
Passing a control does not close a general numerical-implementation or optimizer
convergence guarantee. One new full-record Hankel certificate separately tests
the higher-budget record against the unchanged selection criteria.

## 5. Two identifiability limits

**EXACT sampled aliasing.** For sampling interval `h=1/2` in normalized model
units, every continuous frequency `omega+4*pi*m` has the same sampled complex
phase as `omega`, for integer `m`. Even perfect sampled phase recovery cannot
select a unique continuous generator without an alias restriction.

**EXACT positive-noise obstruction.** For a nonzero one-mode amplitude vector
`a`, `||a cos((theta+eta)k)-a cos(theta k)||<=||a|| k |eta|`.
For any positive finite error budget there are distinct nearby phase models
whose finite records differ by less than twice that budget at every sample;
their error balls overlap. Thus exact real-valued phase identification is not
uniformly possible under positive bounded error. Approximate/local bounds such
as the theorem above remain meaningful.

No result here identifies unobservable bulk dynamics, promotes an experimental
bridge, supplies SI units, or changes the full-Hankel threshold/count/condition
cap. O03 tolerances remain protocol controls, not theory constants.

# A posteriori validation of the actual floating phase estimator

Development lane; physical promotion 0. Constructor calculations with exact
integer/rational residuals and outward512-bit interval arithmetic. This certifies
captured outputs on pinned records about a pinned fitted reference, not physical
frequencies, global optimizer convergence or all possible error patterns.

## 1. What is captured and what remains untrusted

The instrumented proposer executes the original SVD, least-squares shift solve,
eigvals, angle calculation, phase rounding and coefficient fit without changing
those arithmetic expressions. After that calculation, it saves the actual
binary64 basis U (8191-by-105), shift T, returned complex eigenvalues lambda,
angles and auxiliary untrusted eigenvector/inverse/reduction proposals V, H, B.
Every generated PROPOSAL.npz must be byte-identical to its pinned parent.

All finite floating entries are converted with as_integer_ratio to exact dyadic
integers at a common power-of-two scale. There is no extra quantization of U or T.
The exact record sketch Z=X[2W|v]/2^55 is recomputed from all18,790,154 readings,
with signed-integer partial sums checked against overflow. Thus BLAS errors in
the proposer's floating sketch are included in the residual check below.
Both the floating witness and exact record sketch are retained for portable
verification without the full raw record or dense Hankel.

## 2. A computed subspace certificate without trusting SVD

Let M be the pinned fitted-reference sketch, and retain the previous certified
constants alpha<=sigma105(M), aI<=G<=bI for its normalized Vandermonde Gram,
K=sqrt(b/a), beta=sqrt(1-105/(8191a)), and minimum eigenvalue chord separation s.
The new verifier bounds e>=||Z-M||_2 by a newly computed exact Frobenius residual
plus its enclosed phase-rounding term. This is a measured finite-matrix fit
bound for the actual record, not a worst-case assumption about the whole error
ball.

Compute validated bounds

\[
 \eta\ge\|U^*U-I\|_2,\qquad
 p\ge\|Z-UB\|_2,\qquad b_B\ge\|B\|_2.
\]

Frobenius norms supply these operator-norm upper bounds. If eta<1, the polar
factor Q=U(U*U)^-1/2 is orthonormal and

\[
 d_U=\eta/(1+\sqrt{1-\eta})\ge\|U-Q\|_2,\quad
 \tau=p+d_Ub_B\ge\|(I-QQ^*)Z\|_2.
\]

Let Q0 be the reference model's orthonormal frame. Since M has rank105 with
sigma105(M)>=alpha,

\[
 t=(e+\tau)/\alpha\ge\|(I-QQ^*)Q_0\|_2.
\]

For t<1 there is a unitary basis alignment with

\[
 \|U O-Q_0\|_2\le d:=d_U+\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{1-t^2}}.
\]

No correctness or optimality of the floating SVD is assumed: its returned basis
must satisfy these data-bound residuals. Additionally alpha-e>cutoff>e certifies
exactly105 sketch values above the discovery cutoff on each tested record.

## 3. Validate the returned floating shift

The reference frame satisfies Q0_+=Q0_- J, with ||J||_2<=K and a diagonalizer
condition at most K. Its deleted-row singular value is at least beta.
Compute r_T>=||U_+-U_- T||_2 exactly from the captured floating matrices.
After unitary alignment, put x=||T'-J||_2. Then

\[
 \beta x\le r_T+d(1+\|T'\|_2)\le r_T+d(1+K+x).
\]

If d<beta, this gives

\[
 x\le\Delta_T:=\frac{r_T+d(1+K)}{\beta-d}.
\]

This step validates the actual floating shift matrix using its residual, rather
than replacing it by an ideal least-squares answer.

## 4. Validate the returned floating eigenvalues

The actual lambda values from eigvals are retained. Separate untrusted calls
supply paired right vectors V and an inverse witness H. Compute exact bounds

\[
 \rho\ge\|VH-I\|_2<1,\quad h\ge\|H\|_2,\quad
 r_\lambda\ge\|TV-V\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)\|_2.
\]

The first inequality proves V invertible and
`||V^-1||_2<=h/(1-rho)`. Therefore the exact matrix
A=V diag(lambda) V^-1 has exactly the captured lambda values as its eigenvalues,
and

\[
 \|A-T\|_2\le\Delta_\lambda:=r_\lambda h/(1-\rho).
\]

After the same unitary alignment, every eigenvalue of A lies within
`R=K(Delta_T+Delta_lambda)` of a reference exp(i theta_j). If 2R<s, the disks are
disjoint and each contains one captured eigenvalue, counting multiplicity. This
follows by the diagonal resolvent bound and the homotopy from J to A, as in the
previous conditional theorem. Inverse/eigenpair residuals close the floating
eigensolver step; its numerical eigenvalues are not accepted on trust.

## 5. Validate the actual emitted phases

For each selected positive angle, exact integer arithmetic checks that the
emitted theta numerator is the ties-to-even rounding of the captured angle times
2^60. Validated complex argument intervals then directly bound

\[
 \epsilon_{arg}\ge\max_j|
 \arg(\lambda_j)-\widehat\theta_j|.
\]

This accounts for the actual angle routine and emitted-grid error without
assuming an atan2 accuracy specification. When R<1, the output phase bound is

\[
 |\widehat\theta_j-\theta_{ref,j}|_{circle}
 \le\arcsin(R)+\epsilon_{arg}.
\]

The checker also requires twice this bound to be less than the reference chord
separation (a conservative sufficient condition for angular matching).
Only52 positive phases are emitted; their negatives and stationary0 form the105-mode model.
The reference phases are fitted parameters, not a source rule for a physical
generator. A small residual does not remove sampled-frequency aliasing.

## 6. Scope of the completed validation

The frozen campaign covers the clean record and both prior coherent controls.
For every accepted case, the actual regenerated proposal matches its parent
bytes, the exact record sketch and floating arrays are retained, and all residual
and matching gates pass. This supplies a posteriori validation of those floating
outputs. It does not certify convergence or acceptance on every future input,
unique matching throughout the entire2^-20 error ball, independent review,
physical measurements, full acquisition admission or hidden-state recovery.
The original full-Hankel criteria and nominal747-dimensional observer kernel are
unchanged. O03 tolerances remain protocol controls, not theory constants.

# Exact PSD Gram bounds for the actual floating-estimator certificate

Development lane; physical promotion 0; independent review pending.

For a real residual R=N/2^b with exact integer N, let G=N^T N. Then

\[
 \|R\|_2^2=\lambda_{max}(G)/2^{2b}
 \le\frac{\min\{\operatorname{tr}G,\max_i\sum_j|G_{ij}|\}}{2^{2b}}.
\]

Proof: G is positive semidefinite, so its largest eigenvalue is bounded by its
trace. Every eigenvalue is bounded in modulus by the induced infinity norm,
which is the maximum absolute row sum. Taking the minimum preserves both upper
bounds. Trace is exactly the squared Frobenius norm, hence this refinement is
never worse. It is an upper bound on the operator norm, not an exact evaluation
of the largest eigenvalue. Integer Grams have only 161-by-161 entries here.

For Z minus the reference sketch, phase values are enclosed by the same 512-bit
validated arithmetic as PR186. The integer residual uses the same 2^-60 phase
approximants and 2^-127 total scale. The exact Gram upper bound is supplemented
by the identical, validated phase-approximation allowance. No floating phase
value is treated as exact transcendental arithmetic.

For Z-U B, the actual captured binary64 U and B are encoded exactly as integers
at a common dyadic scale. Its Gram uses the exact residual integer matrix;
there is no additional approximation of the saved floats.

Substitute these two upper bounds for e>=||Z-M||_2 and p>=||Z-UB||_2 in the
unchanged PR186 residual-to-phase theorem, reproduced in
PARENT_FLOATING_THEOREM.md. Every other bound and gate is unchanged, including
orthogonality/polar correction, shift residual, eigenvector inverse, actual
returned-eigenvalue residual, captured angle rounding, and strict separation.
The proof uses only upper bounds, so the substitution is valid. The verifier
records both the old Frobenius decision and the refined operator-bound decision
on exactly the same output arrays; a HOLD is not an estimator failure theorem.

Each accepted record has a conditional a posteriori certificate relative to the
pinned fitted reference. The discovery-order check is separately recorded.
Neither finite tests nor this refinement establish matching over the whole
2^-20 error ball, physical frequencies, independent review, acquisition
admission, hidden-state recovery, or convergence of the estimator on all inputs.
The 747-dimensional nominal dynamical kernel remains unchanged. The full
253952-by-151552 Hankel matrix is never allocated. Raw-to-sketch verification
and portable saved-sketch replay have distinct provenance.

# Fixed-reference temporal-span certificate

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0. Exact conditional
finite-matrix theorem with validated constructor computations; independent
review pending. The reference phases are fitted parameters, not physical truth.

## 1. Amplitudes and the temporal frame are separate objects

Let n=8191, q=105 and let F have columns 1 and exp(plus/minus i k theta_j),
using the fixed 52 positive dyadic reference phases. Let P have the real columns
1, cos(k theta_j), sin(k theta_j). The complex change of columns from F to P has
singular values 1 (stationary column) and 1/sqrt(2) (each paired column). If

\[
 aI\preceq F^*F/n\preceq bI,
\]

then sigma_min(P)>=sqrt(na/2). These constants and the minimum reference
unit-circle chord separation s are recomputed from the fixed phases by validated
finite geometric sums and Gershgorin bounds, not accepted merely from a receipt.

If Z=P_v(C+E)+N with ||N||2<=nu, after any common-origin rotation,

\[
 \|Z-P(C+E)\|_2\le
 e:=\Omega\|v\|_2(\|C\|_2+p)+\nu.
\]

For raw62-vector errors bounded by delta over37 preparations and n times,
||raw_error S||2<=sqrt(37 n 371097/4096) delta. The numeric grid uses
nu=nu_model+this bound, with the pinned clean fitted-reference residual as the
DECLARED nu_model floor. This is a conditional model-family example; a past fit
residual is not a guaranteed noise/model floor of a future instrument or a
changed preparation. Future acquisition must independently justify its own nu.

## 3. Transport to the exact SVD/least-squares estimator

For the exact top105-SVD basis of Z and its exact least-squares shift, define

\[
 t=e/(L-e),\quad d=\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{1-t^2}},\quad
 K=\sqrt{b/a},\quad\beta=\sqrt{1-q/(na)},\quad
 R=K d(1+K)/(\beta-d).
\]

If L>2e, the leading model subspace is separated. Projection of its singular
vector equation gives principal sine<=t. Unitarily aligning orthonormal bases
gives distance<=d. The reference frame's deleted-row singular value is>=beta;
its shift J has norm and diagonalizer condition<=K. Least-squares residual
transport gives ||T-J||<=d(1+K)/(beta-d). The diagonal resolvent bound and a
reference-to-perturbed-matrix homotopy then place one eigenvalue in each reference
disk when d<beta,R<1 and2R<s, where s is the minimum unit-circle chord separation.
The circular phase error is<=asin(R). Frame constants and s are recomputed
from fixed phase integers, not accepted on citation alone.

This is an a priori theorem for the EXACT estimator. It does not prove the
behavior or convergence of every floating SVD/LS implementation. Actual
floating outputs still require the orthogonality, span/shift, eigenpair,
inverse and emitted-argument checks of PR189. No new actual-floating run or
full-Hankel signature execution is claimed in this return.

The74 grid rows and the separate joint example are conditional sufficient
bounds. The largest passing dyadic budget on a frozen grid is not optimal or
necessary, and isolated maximum budgets cannot be combined without adding their
error contributions. ONE_SIDED/HOLD outcomes are proof limitations, not measured
failures. The full raw vector budget2^-20 remains without unique matching here.

## 4. Preparation-specific offsets and clocks

Constant offsets for different preparations can each be absorbed into their own
coefficient-column pair rotations, leaving the declared reference temporal
space available. They do not necessarily preserve its excitation. Different
column rotations are not one common left-orthogonal transform. The finite
control with C=I3 and one sine preparation shifted by minus one quarter-turn
has adjusted C=[[1,0,0],[0,1,-1],[0,0,0]], rank2. A fresh coefficient-rank
margin or a justified coefficient-error bound is necessary.

Preparation-dependent time-varying clocks likewise cannot use P_v C with a
single common P_v. For raw preparation a, a sufficient vector Lipschitz constant
is L_a=sum_j |theta_j| sqrt(||A_ja||2^2+||B_ja||2^2). A separately bounded
raw error delta_ak<=p_a+noise_ak+L_a(k mu_a+j_a) yields
||raw_error S||<=||S|| sqrt(sum_ak delta_ak^2). Adjusted comparison amplitudes
must retain a separately certified excitation margin. This extension is derived
but is not instantiated by the common-clock numeric grid in this package.

## 5. Two exact identifiability obstructions

ALIAS/JITTER NO-GO. Modes theta and theta+2pi m agree at every integer k. At
u=1/(2m), their relative phase is exp(i2pi m u)=-1, so their unit-complex sample
discrepancy is exactly2 although u tends to0. Thus sampled phases alone imply
no finite uniform jitter Lipschitz bound. An unwrapped interpolation, bandwidth
restriction or independently bounded source generator is essential. Choosing
the principal representative internally does not establish a physical band.

CLOCK-SCALE NO-GO. A source theta sampled with clock1+epsilon is identical at
every k to a source theta'=(1+epsilon)theta sampled with clock1, within any
suitable interior band. Even infinitely many noiseless samples cannot separate
source scale from clock rate without an external clock convention/calibration.
Finite controls validate instances; the algebra proves the general obstruction.

Loss of an entire mode pair or a preparation in the sketch kernel also leaves
that phase unexcited. No amount of observer history recovers an absent mode
without an excitation/source assumption. None of these results changes the
nominal747-dimensional dynamical observer kernel or implies hidden-state leaks.

## 6. Experimental obligations and governance

Before applying these model-unit bounds, supply a source/band justification,
calibrated clock-rate/jitter bounds, preparation-to-coefficient map and error
bound, excitation margin, acquisition/model-noise floor and their dependence
assumptions. Convert sample-index quantities to SI only through a separately
calibrated sample interval. Then validate actual floating outputs and apply
full record/Hankel/acquisition criteria separately. Temporal order, phase
matching, exact algebraic rank and the retained1893-value spectral signature
are distinct.62 history channels and189 diagnostic outputs remain distinct.

Two parallel assistants provided same-team mathematical review, not an
independent non-constructor attestation. Review HOLD177 and independent replay130
remain open. O03 tolerances remain protocol controls, never theory constants.
Physical promotion0; development — no registry entry.

# Preparation-specific clock and excitation certificate

Development lane; physical promotion **0**; independent review pending.

This extends PR193 from one common clock to 37 preparation-specific origins,
rate errors and jitter sequences. Each preparation's clock is common across its
62 channels. Errors may be arbitrarily correlated across preparations.

## Results

- All four frozen declared-origin profiles certify positive temporal excitation:
  zero, common one-sample shift, alternating quarter-sample shifts, and a ramp
  from minus one-half to plus one-half sample.
- The conservative unknown-origin bound certifies excitation for deviations up
  to **2^-14 sample units** from a common origin, without other preparation error.
  The failed bound at 2^-13 is inconclusive about actual rank.
- The joint unknown-origin example uses offset box 2^-16, one-quarter excitation
  allocation for preparation error, jitter 2^-34, rate error 2^-48, raw vector
  error 2^-36 and the declared parent model floor. It certifies ideal-estimator
  phase error **<4.492e-5 radians/sample**.
- All 80 frozen budget cases, four profile witnesses, five control families and
  ten tests replay. Outcomes include 52 conditional matching certificates,
  19 one-sided enclosures and nine HOLDs; every outcome is retained.

Different preparation origins can destroy rank and amplify a global preparation
operator norm. The proof uses per-preparation modal-block error bounds and exact
right-inverse/Gram certificates, including validated rotation approximation error.
A common origin preserves true singular values exactly; coordinate-dependent
certificate lower bounds may differ without contradicting that fact.

The separate largest passing jitter and rate budgets in RESULT_SUMMARY.json
must not be combined. Known-profile certificates apply to the exact declared
origins; unknown deviations need their own error charge.

## Replay

Install requirements.txt in an isolated Python environment, extract the complete
ZIP into an empty directory, then run:

```bash
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python replay_package.py
```

Replay checks every package file hash, regenerates the validated profile
rotations, verifies exact right-inverse/Gram witnesses and all budget cases,
and runs controls and ten tests in a temporary copy. No full Hankel allocation
or new actual floating phase-estimator execution is required by this replay.

THEOREMS.md supplies assumptions and proof; CERTIFICATE.json contains rational
bounds; RESULT_SUMMARY.json presents results; ACQUISITION_REQUIREMENTS.json
lists outstanding source and metrology inputs. Profile witnesses are untrusted
proposals until their exact residual and norm checks pass.

These are conditional results for the pinned learned real modal model and
principal-band interpolation. They are not SI timing specifications, future
instrument-noise guarantees, full-Hankel certificates or independent review.
Actual floating outputs retain PR189's residual/rounding requirements. Issues
144, 178 and the independent review intake remain open.

# Preparation-specific origins, excitation and clocks

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion0; independent review pending.
All bounds use the learned real modal model and an explicit unwrapped principal
frequency-band interpolation. They do not identify a physical clock, preparation
source, native metric or SI units. Same-team review is not independent review.

## 1. Raw modal blocks and origin rotations

Write the raw time-by-coordinate model as D[k,:]=p(k)B, with
p(t)=[1,cos(theta_j t),sin(theta_j t),...] and B of size105-by2294. Preparation a
selects the62 columns c*37+a, c=0,...,61. Its block is B_a. The learned theta and
integer B numerators are the pinned reference proposal, at scale2^-60.
The sketch is S=[W/64|v/128], size2294-by161; C=B S.

For a constant origin o_a,

\[
 p(k+o_a)B_a=p(k)R(o_a)B_a,\quad
 R_j(o)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta_j o)&\sin(\theta_j o)\\
 -\sin(\theta_j o)&\cos(\theta_j o)\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The stationary block is1. The forward sine signs are checked by an exact
quarter-turn waveform control and a production-layout interleaving test.
A common origin multiplies all B by ONE orthogonal left matrix, preserving
singular values of C exactly. Different origins act on different column blocks;
there is no single common left matrix. Let B_o collect those adjusted blocks,
and C_o=B_o S.

A simple exact counterexample uses stationary/cosine/sine preparations C=I3.
Moving only the sine preparation by a negative quarter-turn gives
C_o=[[1,0,0],[0,1,-1],[0,0,0]], rank2. Independent origins need not preserve
excitation. Likewise raw perturbation columns e_cos,e_sin, each norm1, become
e_cos,e_cos after rotating only the second column. The global operator norm
grows from1 to sqrt2. Per-column/block orthogonality is not global norm invariance.

## 2. Unknown origin box

Because ||R_j(o)-I||<=|theta_j o|, for any known origin vector

\[
 \|C_o-C\|_2\le\|S\|_F
 \sqrt{\sum_{a,j}\theta_j^2 o_a^2
 (\|A_{ja}\|_2^2+\|B_{ja}\|_2^2)}.
\]

For |o_a|<=xi this is <=K_o xi, with
K_o=||S||F sqrt(sum_aj theta_j^2(||A_ja||²+||B_ja||²)). This multiplier is computed
from exact learned integer coefficients and fixed phase numerators. A common
origin can be removed first; xi may bound remaining deviations from that origin.
If gamma<=sigma105(C), then gamma-K_o xi is a sufficient excitation margin.
A negative bound is inconclusive, not evidence of actual rank loss.

The current source gives K_o<16.771765. The frozen unknown-origin box2^-14 sample
units proves margin>0.00018941124, with no other preparation perturbation.
Box2^-13 is inconclusive by this proof. These are model-unit bounds, not SI clock
specifications or a necessary boundary.

## 3. Stronger certificates for declared offset patterns

For four frozen origin vectors, sine/cosine rotations are validated at512-bit
precision and rounded to60-bit dyadics, entry error<2^-60. There is no intermediate
coefficient rounding: exact multiplication by B produces approximate B_o at
scale2^-120, then approximate C_o at scale2^-127. Every rotation block error has
operator norm<=2^(1-60), so

\[
 \|C_o-\widetilde C_o\|_2\le
 \epsilon_{rot}:=2^{1-60}\|B_{osc}\|_F\|S\|_F.
\]

This is<2.152e-17 for the pinned source. For the exactly zero origin the error
is exactly0. Stored rotation integers are recomputed and checked against the
same rational origins during replay; no object-pickle matrix is trusted.

An untrusted binary64 H_o is encoded exactly. Small integer Grams validate
rho_o>=||tilde C_o H_o-I||<1 and h_o>=||H_o||. Then

\[
 \sigma_{105}(C_o)\ge\gamma_o:=(1-\rho_o)/h_o-\epsilon_{rot}>0.
\]

Both right-inverse accuracy and transcendental rotation error are accounted for.
The specific profile must be the declared comparison profile; unknown deviations
need their own origin-box or timing-residual budget. Stored known-profile cases
use origin-box0, not an additional uncharged offset uncertainty.

Common-origin singular values are invariant, but the row-sum upper bounds used
for H_o are basis-dependent. Different conservative LOWER bounds for zero and
common origins do not imply a physical or true conditioning change. Larger
lower bounds alone do not order the true condition numbers of two profiles.

## 4. Preparation errors require block bounds

Let E_a be an uncertain raw modal block for preparation a, ||E_a||2<=p_a. The
same-preparation origin rotation preserves this block operator norm. With
arbitrary dependence between preparations,

\[
 \|E_o\|_2\le\sqrt{\sum_a p_a^2},\quad
 \|E_o S\|_2\le\|S\|_F\sqrt{\sum_a p_a^2}=:p_C.
\]

For unknown origins a sufficient remaining coefficient margin is
gamma-K_o xi-p_C. For a declared directly certified profile it is gamma_o-p_C.
It must be strictly positive. The numeric grid chooses uniform p_a so that
p_C<=r gamma (or r gamma_o for the specific profile), with r frozen in advance.
The exact reported dyadic p_a bound is rounded down; the computed r gamma loss
therefore safely upper-bounds the actual loss.

This per-preparation raw modal bound is not a physical state-preparation error
or a state-to-coefficient map. A prior global ||E||2 bound cannot simply be kept
unchanged after differential origins. The sqrt(sum p_a²) rule, rather than an
unsupported global invariance assumption, is used in every numeric budget here.

## 5. Preparation-specific rate and jitter

Assume times tau_ak=o_a+(1+epsilon_a)k+u_ak, common across the62 channels of a
preparation but not necessarily common across preparations. Declare
|epsilon_a|<=mu_a and |u_ak|<=j_a. With

\[
 L_a=\sum_j |\theta_j|
 \sqrt{\|A_{ja}\|_2^2+\|B_{ja}\|_2^2},\qquad
 \Omega^2=\sum_j\theta_j^2,
\]

the nominal raw output derivative norm is<=L_a. Pair rotations preserve each
pair energy, so nominal L_a is unchanged by constant o_a. Preparation uncertainty
adds at most Omega p_a, because the real derivative row has norm Omega and
||p'(t)E_a||<=Omega||E_a||. There is no assumption that the coefficientwise sum
of perturbation pair norms is itself <=Omega p_a.

Define w_a=mu_a sqrt(sum k²)+sqrt(n)j_a, where sum k²=n(n-1)(2n-1)/6 exactly.
Then the sketched timing residual obeys the global, non-linearization bound

\[
 e_t\le\|S\|_F
 \sqrt{\sum_a(L_a+\Omega p_a)^2 w_a^2}.
\]

No statistical independence of clocks, jitters, preparations or channels is
required. The numeric grid uses common UPPER BOUNDS mu,j,p_a across preparations;
the actual errors can differ arbitrarily within them. With uniform upper bounds,
e_t<=||S||F sqrt(sum_a(L_a+Omega p_a)²)(mu sqrt(sum k²)+sqrt(n)j).

Add raw62-vector acquisition error delta and a separately justified model floor:
e=e_t+sqrt(37 n)||S||F delta+nu_model. The grid uses the inherited clean-fit
residual as a DECLARED nu_model example. It is not a future-instrument or
changed-preparation guarantee. Constant deviations from a declared origin profile
may be charged as part of u_ak; they are not silently free.

## 6. Ideal-estimator phase transport

Let g be the remaining positive coefficient margin. Then
L=sqrt(na/2)g lower-bounds sigma105 of the comparison model P C_adjusted.
For exact top105 SVD and exact least-squares shift, use

\[
 t=e/(L-e),\quad d=\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{1-t^2}},\quad
 K=\sqrt{b/a},\quad\beta=\sqrt{1-q/(na)},\quad
 R=K d(1+K)/(\beta-d).
\]

Require L>2e,d<beta,R<1,2R<s. The singular-subspace projection, orthonormal
alignment, deleted-row bound, diagonal resolvent and homotopy proof then yield
unique reference-phase matching and phase error<=asin(R). The complete parent
argument is reproduced in PARENT_CLOCK_THEOREMS.md. Reference frame constants
and s are recomputed here. Actual data need not have exact rank105; this is
leading-subspace separation around a rank105 comparison model.

This is an exact-estimator theorem, not general floating convergence or a new
actual floating-output run. Future outputs still need PR189's basis/shift,
eigenpair/inverse and emitted-argument residual checks. There is no new
full-Hankel1893-value certificate, acquisition admission or raw-record generation.

## 7. Scope and metrology obligations

The unwrapped principal-band interpolation is declared. Integer-sampled aliases
alone do not bound jitter sensitivity; source-frequency scale remains confounded
with clock rate without calibration. Preparation-specific clocks are covered
only with the stated maps, source bandwidth/interpolation, modal-block errors,
positive excitation margin and noise bounds. Physical preparation/readout/metric
sources, SI sample interval, instrument clock bounds, covariance and dependence
models, cost/disturbance and actual acquisition validation remain open.

Grid maxima are sufficient budgets on frozen dyadic grids, not optimal boundaries.
Individually varied maxima cannot be combined without summing their errors.
Known-pattern certificates and worst-case boxes have different scopes; large
specific offsets may certify when the worst-case box proof is inconclusive.
All HOLD/one-sided cases are preserved as proof limitations, not measured failure.
Two parallel same-team reviews do not close independent review/replay obligations.
The nominal747-dimensional hidden space,62 history channels and separate189
diagnostic outputs remain unchanged. O03 parameters are protocol controls,
never theory constants. Physical promotion0; development — no registry entry.

# Actual floating-estimator timing campaign

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion **0**; independent review pending.

This campaign constructs four fresh complete records from the pinned learned
real modal model, then runs the unchanged original and instrumented floating
estimators on each. All source recipes and code were frozen before generation;
all raw hashes were frozen before fitting. The actual output certificates are
in VALIDATION.json; every pass and HOLD is retained.

| Record | Preparation origins | Rate magnitude | Alternating jitter magnitude |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| modal_zero | zero | 0 | 0 |
| origin_alternating | alternating +1/4 and -1/4 sample | 0 | 0 |
| ramp_joint_clocks | (a-18)/36 sample | 2^-48 | 2^-34 sample |
| ramp_clock_stress | (a-18)/36 sample | 2^-20 | 1/16 sample |

Rate signs alternate with preparation; jitter signs alternate with preparation
and sample. Each preparation has one clock across 62 channels, with prescribed
cross-preparation dependence. These are finite synthetic constructor fixtures,
not independently obtained observations. The source uses exactly the fitted
reference model against which phase discrepancy is checked.

## Actual results

| Record | Floating sketch count | Certified emitted phase-error upper bound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| modal_zero | 105 | <4.835e-12 radians/sample |
| origin_alternating | 105 | <4.659e-12 radians/sample |
| ramp_joint_clocks | 105 | <6.645e-9 radians/sample |
| ramp_clock_stress | 161 (full sketch width) | Proposer model/order HOLD |

All three available original proposals are byte-identical to the instrumented
ones. Both stress executions have identical HOLD receipts. The stress count is
a floating threshold count in a 161-column sketch, not its exact temporal rank
or a full-Hankel spectral failure. All three complete saved-array certificate
replays and 14 tests pass. Raw regeneration is reported separately.

## Three checks with distinct meanings

1. Validated Arb anchors, a proved 96-bit integer recurrence error bound and exact
   coefficient contraction give a uniform waveform-evaluation/encoding error.
   DATA_FREEZE.json binds all 75,160,616 encoded readings by range/layout/hash.
   DIRECT_SOURCE_AUDIT.json separately reports 45,880 direct Arb spot checks.
2. Original and instrumented proposals are compared byte-for-byte. The actual
   computed basis, shift, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, inverse, angles and emitted
   phases are saved. No reference phase is supplied to the floating proposer.
3. The unchanged PR189 mathematical proof verifies saved-array residuals and
   rounding against the pinned reference frame. It does not trust floating
   SVD, least squares, eigensolver or atan2 merely because they were computed.

Constant preparation origins retain the reference frame while changing its
coefficients. Rates/jitter can leave that span and introduce additional modes.
A pass certifies bounded discrepancy from the original fitted reference;
it does not certify exact identification of clock-distorted native modes.
Orders outside 105 and all proof HOLDs are retained without forced truncation.
No old clean residual or additive-to-old-clean acquisition gate is inherited.

## Portable saved-output replay

empty folder. With the pinned requirements installed, run:

```bash
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python replay_package.py
```

proposer or regenerate raw records. Every available floating witness and original

instead of duplicating the large int64 source arrays.

## Optional complete raw regeneration

From the extracted package, run:

```bash
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python make_records.py --destination /new/empty/path
```

The destination must not exist. This regenerates all four raw records and
requires byte-identical SHA256 hashes and identical generation-bound receipts.
It needs no parent codec or external dataset. RAW_REGENERATION_RECEIPT.json,
when present, records the separate complete execution performed for this return.
Normal portable replay makes no silent claim to regenerate those bytes.

THEOREMS.md states the timing/evaluation argument; PARENT_FRAME_THEOREMS.md
states the output-residual theorem. SOURCE_IDENTITY.json and adapter patches

# Timing-source evaluation and actual-output phase validation

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review pending.

## 1. Declared source and clocks

The pinned learned coefficient matrix B has shape 105-by-2294, stored as integer
numerators at scale 2^-60. Preparation a selects columns c*37+a. Its exact model
waveform is p(t)B_a, where p(t)=[1,cos(theta_j t),sin(theta_j t),...]. The pinned
52 positive theta_j are dyadics at scale 2^-60. This interpolation is declared;
it is not a consequence of integer samples alone or a physical source law.

For a=0,...,36 and k=0,...,8190, the frozen times are

\[
 t_{ak}=o_a+(1+(-1)^a\mu)k+(-1)^{a+k}j.
\]

There is one clock across all 62 channels within each preparation. Cross-
preparation errors are fully dependent, with explicitly fixed signs. Four
records use zero clocks, alternating quarter-sample origins, ramp origins with
small clocks, and the same ramp with larger clocks. Rational controls are in
CAMPAIGN_FREEZE.json. Their units are nominal sample-index units; O03 controls
remain protocol controls, not theory constants or SI specifications.

## 2. Certified fixed-point evaluation

Set Q=2^96. Validated Arb512 enclosures choose complex start, step and alternating
jitter factors whose real and imaginary component errors are each <=1/Q. The
complex norm of any anchor error is therefore less than e=2^-95. Multiplication
uses exact Python integers followed by ties-to-even rounding of each component
to Q; the complex rounding error is less than e.

Let z_k be the true unit phase at origin plus affine time and zhat_k the
recurrence. Its error E_k obeys

\[
 E_0<e,\qquad E_{k+1}<(1+e)E_k+2e,\qquad
 E_k<(2k+1)e(1+e)^k.
\]

For k<=8191, (1+e)^k<2: the binomial expansion is bounded by the geometric
series sum_m(ke)^m, and ke<1/2. Hence E_k<2(2k+1)e<2^-79. Multiplication by
one jitter factor, with one further exact rounded product, adds less than
(2+E_k)e. Rounding the resulting phase components to scale 2^-60 adds at most
2^-61. The total error in each sine/cosine component is strictly below 2^-60.
This is a finite recurrence bound. Tests include a full 8191-step endpoint.

The phase/coeff contraction uses exact integer matrix multiplication. Only the
resulting coordinate is rounded once to raw scale 2^-48. If
L=max_c sum_{r>0}|B_integer[r,c]|, then every encoded scalar has waveform error

\[
 |y_{akc}^{encoded}-[p(t_{ak})B_a]_c|
 \le L\,2^{-120}+2^{-49}=:d_{eval}.
\]

Thus each 62-vector has squared error <=62*d_eval^2. The integer L and rational
bounds are recorded in DATA_FREEZE.json. All raw layouts, ranges, byte counts
and SHA256 hashes are checked before fitting. A separate direct Arb512 audit
checks five frozen times per preparation and channel; it is a spot audit, while
the uniform bound follows from the recurrence proof. No old clean-fit residual
or future instrument-noise allowance is inherited. These are newly generated
modal-source records, not old raw samples at newly measured times.

## 3. What the unchanged output certificate proves

Preparation-specific constant origins rotate coefficient blocks and retain the
original temporal frame P(k), if excitation survives. Differential rates and
jitter generally leave that exact frame and can introduce additional modes.
The unchanged floating proposer learns its own temporal order from each raw
record. Orders outside 105 are retained with an explicit applicability HOLD;
no forced truncation or threshold adjustment is permitted.

For each applicable run, the uninstrumented and instrumented original proposals
must be byte-identical. The saved basis U, actual shift T, returned eigenvalues,
eigenvectors, inverse, angle outputs and emitted dyadic phases are retained.
An untrusted new reduction D is computed only to verify ||P-U D||. No reference
phases are supplied to the floating proposer. Reference phases are used by the
verifier to state and prove the comparison target.

PARENT_FRAME_THEOREMS.md gives the complete PR189 amplitude-independent proof.
The mathematical helper modules retain their published bytes. Exact binary64
encodings, integer residual Grams, validated frame constants, inverse/eigenpair
residuals, argument enclosures and ties-to-even emission checks enclose the
actual output, without assuming SVD/LS/eigensolver/atan2 accuracy.
A pass certifies bounded discrepancy of actual emitted phases from the original
fitted reference. It does not certify exact recovery of the clock-distorted
native components or general estimator convergence.

Every discovery/order, adapter or phase-proof HOLD is retained. A HOLD refuses
this sufficient proof attempt; it does not establish a failed physical model,
a true full-Hankel signature failure or a general failure of the estimator.

## 4. Scope

These are synthetic same-constructor executions, not blinded independent data,
independent review, SI calibration or a physical bridge. Phase certificates do
not prove full-Hankel retained count 1893, exact spatial rank, future acquisition
admission, continuous-generator uniqueness or hidden-state recovery. No dense
Hankel matrix is allocated. The nominal 747-dimensional observer kernel is not
altered. Independent replay/review and physical source/metric mapping remain
separate requirements. Physical promotion stays 0.

# Wider-sketch diagnosis of the preparation-clock HOLD

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion **0**; independent review pending.

The larger PR195 timing record saturated the 161-column sketch. A frozen nested
extension now certifies additional signal directions without changing those
old columns or rewriting the original HOLD.

| Existing record | Width | Count at common cutoff | Count at noise-scaled cutoff |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Small joint clocks | 161 | 105 | 105 |
| Small joint clocks | 257 | 105 | 105 |
| Small joint clocks | 321 | 105 | 105 |
| Larger clock control | 161 | 161 (saturated) | 161 (saturated) |
| Larger clock control | 257 | 202 | 200 |
| Larger clock control | 321 | **205** | **204** |

The common cutoff is the exact parent dyadic, approximately 0.0099945479322.
The scaled cutoffs are approximately 0.0126162731959 at width 257 and
0.0140957413193 at width 321; their squared values are exact rational controls.
Scaling preserves the parent's threshold/noise-envelope ratio for the wider
sketch. It does not admit this stress record into the original acquisition
contract. Both rules were frozen before these executions; no outcomes were
used to choose widths, seeds or thresholds.

At width 321, the larger control has retained condition <421.439 for 205 values
at the common cutoff, or <378.019 for 204 values at the scaled cutoff. The small
clock record's 105-value condition improves from <27.968 to <15.687 in these
particular sketches. These are bounds for the mathematical encoded sketch,
not full-Hankel conditioning or an optimal sketch comparison.

## Structural finding

Two rate classes with alternating jitter have a comparison waveform span of
at most 209 real dimensions. Their tied sidebands can require a one-step shift
closure of at most 417 dimensions. These are upper bounds, not proven exact
dimensions. Two-step shifts preserve the smaller waveform family exactly.

The 205-value lower certificate and source evaluation bound place the comparison
model rank in **[205,209]**. Encoded rounding can add tiny algebraic directions:
at width 321, sigma210 of the encoded sketch is **<1.034e-10** by the source
model tail bound. This does not assert exact encoded rank 209 or all 209 signal
coordinates being recoverable.

## Checks completed

- Exact integer projections read all 37,580,308 coordinates of the two existing
  records. Separate full raw-projection replays reproduce both 321-by321 Grams.
- Validated eigenvalue enclosures classify every value for all six case/width
  combinations and both frozen cutoff rules. Untrusted floating eigensystems
  are checked through exact integer orthogonality and eigenpair residuals.
- Complete small-Gram replays agree; five tests pass. No full Hankel allocated.

The result concerns the EXACT mathematical sketch of encoded bytes. It does
not certify a separate floating BLAS sketch or new actual phase outputs.
The PR195 phase certificates and stress model/order HOLD retain their scope.

## Portable replay

Extract the ZIP into an empty folder, install requirements.txt, then run:

```bash
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python replay_package.py
```

This checks all package hashes, recomputes the six small-Gram spectral proofs
and source-tail bounds, preserves all count/HOLD outcomes and runs five tests.
It does not regenerate raw records, reproject them or rerun a phase estimator.

For separate full raw projection replay, first regenerate the source records
using the PR195 package's make_records.py --destination option. Check the raw
hashes in WIDE_FREEZE.json, then from this package run:

```bash
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python project.py ramp_joint_clocks --records /path/to/regenerated/records --replay
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python project.py ramp_clock_stress --records /path/to/regenerated/records --replay
```

Use a fresh extracted copy without existing PROJECTION_REPLAY.json receipts;
never overwrite evidence. Both exact projections were separately rerun in
this return. THEOREMS.md proves the mode/threshold/Gram bounds; RESULT_SUMMARY.json
and per-case certificates provide rational values.

Next bounded work is a separately frozen stride-two phase adapter with sampled
collision, excitation, finite-conditioning and actual-output checks. This
return closes a sketch-saturation diagnostic, not independent review, global
fitter convergence, full acquisition qualification, SI clocks, the native
observer/metric source, full-Hankel acceptance or hidden-state recovery.
The nominal 747-dimensional dynamical observer kernel is unchanged.

# Wider timing sketch: finite counts and temporal closure

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review pending.
This is a diagnostic of two already known synthetic PR195 records. It is not
independent discovery, a new acquisition, or an extension of the phase adapter.

## 1. Waveform span and shift closure are different

For preparation a, set s=(-1)^a and
t_ak=o_a+(1+s mu)k+s j0(-1)^k. Origins are preparation-specific constants.
For each of the 52 positive reference phases theta_j, let

\[
 \omega_{js}=(1+s\mu)\theta_j,\qquad
 g_{js}(k)=e^{i\omega_{js}k}e^{is\theta_jj_0(-1)^k}.
\]

The factor e^(i theta_j o_a) rotates that preparation's coefficients and does
not add a temporal function. With two rate classes, the real waveform family
has at most one stationary column and two real functions per pair per class:

\[
 \operatorname{rank}D_{\rm model}\le1+52\cdot2\cdot2=209.
\]

The sideband decomposition is

\[
 g_{js}(k)=\cos(\theta_jj_0)e^{i\omega_{js}k}
       +is\sin(\theta_jj_0)e^{i(\omega_{js}+\pi)k}.
\]

The two sideband amplitudes are tied. Counting them independently would wrongly
identify the observation-column bound as 417. One-step shifts can separate the
tied components, giving a shift-invariant closure bound of at most
1+52*2*4=417. Both are upper bounds: collisions, absent amplitudes or coefficient
dependence may lower them. No exact dimension 209 or 417 is asserted.

Two-step shifts instead preserve the original waveform family exactly:

\[
 g_{js}(k+2)=e^{2i\omega_{js}}g_{js}(k).
\]

This supplies a possible future stride-two adapter. It does not extend PR189
automatically: sampled collisions modulo pi, excitation, finite conditioning,
subspace truncation, actual solver residuals and phase emission all need checks.

## 2. Nested sketches and two threshold rules

The integer sketch matrix is A=[2W_old | v | 2W_new], with denominator 128.
W_old is regenerated in its ORIGINAL 2294-by-160 shape with seed172026.
W_new is a separately frozen 2294-by-160 sign matrix with seed184052.
Widths 161,257,321 select nested column prefixes. Generating a larger matrix
with the old seed and selecting its first160 columns would not preserve the
old sketch because its row stride changes RNG consumption.

For S_m=A_m/128, its exact squared Frobenius norm s_m^2 is recomputed.
Let tau be the exact positive dyadic cutoff from the parent SKETCH_RULE.json.
The two frozen diagnostic thresholds are

\[
 t_{m,\rm common}^2=\tau^2,\qquad
 t_{m,\rm scaled}^2=\tau^2s_m^2/s_{161}^2.
\]

Both squared thresholds are exact rationals. Their comparisons do not use
rounded displayed decimals. For a declared per-preparation62-vector error delta,
||E S_m||2 <=sqrt(37*8191)*delta*||S_m||F. The scaled rule preserves the parent's
threshold/noise-envelope ratio, using delta=2^-20 for that diagnostic comparison.
The stress record is NOT asserted to satisfy an additive-to-old-clean error
ball. Neither rule creates acquisition admission or a new theory constant.

Nested prefixes imply Z_next Z_next^T-Z_old Z_old^T is positive semidefinite.
Therefore counts above a COMMON threshold cannot decrease. Scaled-threshold
counts have no such monotonicity requirement.

## 3. Exact small Grams from every encoded reading

The raw little-endian int64 records have shape(37,8191,62), quantum2^-48.
Reshape to X of size8191-by2294 with coordinate index c*37+a. Before int64
matrix multiplication, verify max|X|*max_column_l1(A)<2^63, which bounds every
partial sum. Hence N=X A is exact, and the mathematical sketch is Z=N/2^55.

\[
 G=Z^TZ=N^TN/2^{110}.
\]

The integer numerator Gram is formed exactly with FLINT and stored losslessly
as decimal integers. Its dimension is321, with smaller widths using principal
prefixes. Hashes bind the complete raw record before/after projection. A second
complete raw projection reproduces every Gram integer. No8191-by8191 temporal
Gram or full Hankel array is stored.

This certifies the exact mathematical sketch of the encoded bytes. It does
not silently equate that sketch with a separately computed floating BLAS
product. Floating eigensystems below are untrusted certificate proposals.

## 4. Validated eigenvalue enclosure

Let Q be an untrusted square dyadic eigenvector proposal, Lambda a sorted real
dyadic diagonal proposal, and compute exact residual norms with validated roots:

\[
 \eta\ge\|Q^TQ-I\|_2<1,\quad
 r\ge\|GQ-Q\Lambda\|_2,\quad g\ge\|G\|_2.
\]

Frobenius norms bound each operator norm; all residual numerators and scales
are exact integers. Set qnorm=sqrt(1+eta) and
d=eta/(1+sqrt(1-eta)). The polar factor O of Q is orthogonal with ||Q-O||<=d.
The identities and triangle inequality give

\[
 \|G-Q\Lambda Q^T\|\le g\eta+r\,qnorm,
\]
\[
 \|Q\Lambda Q^T-O\Lambda O^T\|
 \le\|\Lambda\|d(qnorm+1).
\]

Thus each ordered eigenvalue of symmetric G lies within
R=g*eta+r*qnorm+||Lambda||*d*(qnorm+1) of the corresponding Lambda entry.
The checker uses512-bit interval arithmetic and outward rational rounding.
Strict lower>threshold_squared certifies above; strict upper<threshold_squared
certifies below. Any intersection is retained as HOLD. This proves counts for
the encoded mathematical sketch, rather than trusting floating eigenvalues.

Retained singular extrema, discarded-value bounds and retained condition bounds
follow by validated square roots. No full-Hankel spectrum follows.

## 5. Source-aware model tail, not exact encoded rank

PR195's validated generator gives each scalar waveform/encoding error at most
d_eval=L*2^-120+2^-49, with L=max_column sum_oscillatory |B_integer|.
L is recomputed from the pinned coefficient array. Hence

\[
 \|Z-Z_{\rm model}\|_2
 \le\sqrt{8191\cdot2294}\,d_{\rm eval}\|S_m\|_F=:\epsilon_m.
\]

Since rank(Z_model)<=209, Weyl gives sigma210(Z)<=epsilon_m. At width321,
epsilon_m<1.034e-10. Rounding can still give encoded Z a higher EXACT algebraic
rank; the theorem controls its tail, not that exact rank.

The certified205 values above the common cutoff at width321, together with
epsilon321 below that cutoff, prove rank(Z_model)>=205. Thus this return
places the comparison-model rank in[205,209], without proving its exact value.
The scaled rule instead certifies204 retained values for its larger cutoff.

## 6. Limits

These are source-aware finite constructor diagnostics. The PR195 stress
proposer's HOLD remains immutable; no new phase outputs are certified. The
nominal747-dimensional dynamical observer kernel is unchanged. Source/metric
selection, SI clocks, independent review and the full acquisition contract
remain open. O03 thresholds and seeds are protocol controls.

# Actual two-step phase adapter: source-precision audit

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion **0**; independent review pending.

The new record-only adapter learns 105 baseline modes and 209 stress modes at a
separately frozen encoding-precision cutoff **2^-24**. Its actual saved outputs
pass the direct similarity, inverse, eigenpair and emitted-angle checks:

| Existing synthetic record | Certified source-precision order | Circular two-step phase error |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Modal baseline | 105 | **<1.373e-13 radians** |
| Larger preparation-clock control | 209 | **<8.961e-10 radians** |

The stress minimum target chord separation is >7.285423493e-7. Its exact encoded
sketch has sigma209>0.0028804 and sigma210<1.034e-10, so the comparison model's
previous rank interval [205,209] closes at 209. Encoded algebraic rank can still
be larger because of tiny rounding directions.

**The earlier instrument-noise counts 205/204 and original stress HOLD remain
unchanged.** The new cutoff audits these known synthetic records at their
proved generation/encoding precision; it does not qualify them under the old
instrument-noise contract. No target rank was forced: the adapter's floating
count and independent source-aware encoded-sketch count agree.

## What was checked

- Four fresh original/instrumented adapter runs; both phase proposals are
  byte-identical. The adapter receives no numerical source phases, clock rates,
  jitter or coefficients. A verifier-only source reduction is proposed later.
- Exact source projections read 37,580,308 existing encoded readings. Source-order
  Gram replays and complete actual-output residual replays agree on both cases.
- Six tests and two frozen actual-array corruption controls pass: a zero source
  inverse and a changed emitted phase are refused. Original witnesses remain
  unchanged. These controls are finite fault checks, not stochastic coverage.
- All available bases, shifts, eigenvalues/eigenvectors, inverse witnesses,
  actual angles, emitted phases, source reductions and exact Grams are retained.

The phase theorem uses normal two-step rotation blocks and directly validates
TD-DJ. It does not multiply by a guessed reference conditioning constant or
assume floating SVD, least-squares, inverse, eigensolver or atan2 accuracy.
THEOREMS.md gives the finite proof and the strict separation gates.

## Aliasing contract

Primary errors are circular **two-step phases**. They identify original phase
only modulo **pi**. The per-target lift integers and divided-by-two bounds in
certificates are conditional on the explicitly declared source labels. They
are not unrestricted one-step generator identification or physical frequencies.
All 209 source targets, including folded signed branches, are checked for
pairwise unit-circle separation and explicit unique returned-value assignment.

## Portable saved-output replay

Extract the core and every WITNESS ZIP listed in WITNESS_INDEX.json into one
empty folder. Install requirements.txt and run:

```bash
python verify_structure.py
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python replay_package.py
```

The structural guard checks exact Gram symmetry, dimensions and descending
witness eigenvalues. It was added after execution as a packaging check; it
changes no estimator arithmetic, threshold, fitted output or numerical bound.
The estimator, mathematical core and corruption recipes retain their initial
ADAPTER_FREEZE.json hashes.

Portable replay verifies all file/array hashes, repeats both exact source-order
and actual two-step phase certificates from saved witnesses, preserves HOLDs
and runs six tests in a temporary copy. It does not regenerate raw records,
reproject them, rerun the adapter or rerun the actual-array corruption campaign;
CONTROL_RESULTS.json retains that separate executed campaign.

For full raw recovery, use PR195's frozen generation package and
make_records.py --destination /new/empty/path; raw hashes must match the current
ADAPTER_FREEZE.json. OMISSION details and source lineage are in OMITTED_DATA.json.
Original/instrumented adapter and source-projection execution receipts are
retained in RUN_EXECUTIONS.json and per-case receipts/logs.

## Remaining scope

These are same-constructor known-model fixtures, not independent/blinded data
or review. The comparison source itself is fitted and declared. No uniform
whole-instrument-noise-ball result, general convergence, original-contract
admission, full-Hankel spectrum, native observer/metric selection, SI clock
qualification, physical identification or hidden-state recovery is asserted.
No full Hankel is allocated; the nominal 747-dimensional observer kernel is
unchanged. O03 cutoffs remain protocol controls. Independent replay/review and
source/band/preparation/clock/noise metrology remain open.

# Two-step source-precision adapter and actual-output certificate

Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0; independent review pending.
All results concern two known synthetic PR195 records and their pinned learned
modal source. They do not establish physical-frequency truth.

## 1. A different audit rule, preserving prior outcomes

The original instrument-noise diagnostic retains its common/scaled cutoff
counts205/204 on the wider stress sketch and its original proposer HOLD.
This return defines a separate encoding-precision audit with frozen cutoff
tau=2^-24. It does not change that older noise contract.

The record-only adapter uses the same nested321-column sketch as PR196, but
learns its order by its own SVD count above tau. It receives no source phases,
rates, jitter or coefficients. Source hashes are checked for lineage only.
Expected source orders105 and209 are used by the verifier as applicability
conditions, never forced onto a different learned order.

## 2. Source-aware order and excitation

Let X be the encoded time-by-coordinate record, quantum2^-48, and S=A/128 the
dyadic sketch. Its mathematical value is Z=X_integer A/2^55. Integer products
are guarded against overflow before execution, then FLINT forms exact G=Z^T Z
at scale2^-110. All18,790,154 readings per record are projected and raw hashes
checked before/after. Exact Grams and untrusted sorted dyadic eigenproposals
are retained. STRUCTURAL_AUDIT.json checks symmetry, shapes and descending
eigenproposal order for the actual hash-bound witnesses.

As in PR196, exact orthogonality/eigenpair residuals and a polar/Weyl bound
enclose each ordered eigenvalue of G. Let l_q be the qth lower enclosure.
The declared source comparison has rank at most q, where q=105 for zero
clocks and q=209 for the two-rate stress model.

PR195's generator error is independently re-evaluated from the pinned
coefficient numerators:

\[
 d_{\rm eval}=L\,2^{-120}+2^{-49},\qquad
 L=\max_c\sum_{r>0}|B_{{\rm integer},rc}|.
\]

Hence

\[
 \|Z-Z_{\rm model}\|_2
 \le\sqrt{8191\cdot2294}\,d_{\rm eval}\|S\|_F
 =:\epsilon<1.034\,10^{-10}.
\]

If l_q>tau^2 and epsilon<tau, then exactly q singular values of encoded Z
exceed tau: the qth is bounded below by sqrt(l_q), and Weyl bounds the
(q+1)th above by epsilon. This is NOT a statement that encoded algebraic
rank equals q; rounding may add smaller directions.

The actual lower bounds are sigma105>0.3585086 for the baseline and
sigma209>0.0028804 for stress. Both exceed tau, while the next value is below
epsilon. The floating counts105/209 agree with these source-aware exact
encoded-sketch certificates. The source comparison itself therefore has
exact rank105/209, because its qth singular value is still positive after
subtracting epsilon.

The exact-sketch count is not silently a certificate of every intermediate
floating BLAS entry. The output proof below uses saved actual arrays directly
and does not assume SVD or BLAS accuracy to transport phases.

## 3. Two-step closure and aliasing

For stress, s=+1 or-1 labels the preparation rate class and

\[
 g_{js}(k)=e^{i(1+s\mu)\theta_j k}
          e^{is\theta_jj_0(-1)^k},\quad
 \mu=2^{-20},\ j_0=1/16.
\]

Preparation origins rotate coefficients without adding temporal functions.
Since parity is unchanged by two steps,

\[
 g_{js}(k+2)=e^{2i(1+s\mu)\theta_j}g_{js}(k).
\]

The real comparison frame P has columns1,cos,sin for each j and rate class.
It obeys P[2:]=P[:-2]J, where J is block diagonal with stationary block1 and
orthogonal blocks

\[
 J_{js}=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(2\omega_{js})&\sin(2\omega_{js})\\
 -\sin(2\omega_{js})&\cos(2\omega_{js})\end{pmatrix},
 \quad\omega_{js}=(1+s\mu)\theta_j.
\]

Thus J is normal. Its complete target list is1 and exp(plus/minus2i*omega_js).
Every pairwise unit-circle chord is recomputed with validated arithmetic;
the minimum is bounded below by7.285423493e-7 for stress. This checks folded
cross-pair collisions as well as same-pair rate-class splitting.

Two-step eigenvalues identify omega only modulo pi. Primary results are
circular two-step phase errors. Dividing by2 is only a conditional lift about
the named source target; each target's lift integer is retained. No
unrestricted continuous generator or SI frequency is identified.

## 4. Actual floating adapter and saved arrays

For the learned order q, the actual adapter forms
T=lstsq(U[:-2],U[2:]), calls the floating eigensolver, captures its arguments,
and rounds all signed phase arguments onto the2^-60 grid. The original and
instrumented variants share all proposal arithmetic; instrumentation runs
only after proposal emission. Their proposal bytes match on both records.

Saved witnesses include the actual U,T,eigenvalues,eigenvectors,inverse,
angle outputs and emitted phase integers. The large U is split into two row
archives without changing bytes. A verifier-only untrusted reduction
D=U^T P_tilde and inverse witness K are proposed after the record-only fit.
The source frame is generated with the validated96-bit recurrence from PR195;
each nonstationary component is within2^-60 of its exact value.

The basis orthogonality, two-step shift residual and source-frame span
residual are checked and retained. The direct similarity proof does not
require a guessed deleted-row or reference conditioning bound.

## 5. Direct similarity certificate

Let T be the actual shift matrix, D an arbitrary square reduction witness,
and K an inverse witness. Verify exact binary64 encodings and bounds

\[
 \rho_D\ge\|DK-I\|_2<1,\quad
 h_D=\|K\|_{2,\rm upper}/(1-\rho_D),\quad
 d\ge\|D\|_2,\quad L_J\ge\|TD-DJ\|_2.
\]

All residual products use exact integers. J is evaluated as a validated
dyadic block rotation; its component errors below2^-60 contribute an operator
error at most2^-59, so d*2^-59 is charged to L_J.

For the actual returned diagonal Lambda and an eigenvector/inverse witness
V,H, verify

\[
 \rho_V\ge\|VH-I\|_2<1,\qquad
 \delta_\lambda=
 \|TV-V\Lambda\|_{2,\rm upper}
 \frac{\|H\|_{2,\rm upper}}{1-\rho_V}.
\]

Then A=V Lambda V^-1 has exactly the returned eigenvalues and
||A-T||<=delta_lambda. Both V and D are certified invertible by their
Neumann residual bounds. Consequently

\[
 \|D^{-1}AD-J\|_2
 \le h_D\bigl(L_J+d\,\delta_\lambda\bigr)=:R.
\]

Because J is normal, every eigenvalue lies in a radius-R disk about its
unit-circle spectrum. Along the homotopy from J to D^-1 A D, all spectra
stay inside these disks. If2R<s_min, disjoint disks retain one eigenvalue
each, counting multiplicity. The checker also explicitly verifies a unique
assignment of every actual eigenvalue to every labeled target.

Exact real residuals use PSD Gram trace/absolute-row-sum upper bounds.
For complex matrices, the Hermitian Gram's absolute row sums are bounded
using |Re|+|Im|; the minimum with its trace remains an operator-norm upper
bound. Frobenius bounds are used where stated. Square roots and target
exponentials use512-bit interval arithmetic; reported dyadic bounds round
outward. No floating SVD/eigenvalue/inverse accuracy is assumed.

## 6. Actual angle emission

For every captured angle bit pattern, the checker recomputes exact
ties-to-even2^-60 rounding using integer ratios. It then bounds the circular
difference between the validated complex argument of the actual returned
eigenvalue and the emitted phase. Let this maximum be epsilon_arg.
For R<1, the circular emitted-phase error is at most

\[
 \arcsin R+\epsilon_{\rm arg}.
\]

Both2R<s_min and the conservative2*phase_error<s_min gates must pass.
The baseline error is<1.373e-13 and stress error<8.961e-10 radians per two-step
sample. Stress's209-way matching is certified only under this source-precision
audit; prior noise-cutoff outcomes are unchanged.

Two frozen corruption controls on isolated copies refuse a zero source inverse
and a changed emitted phase integer. Original witnesses remain unchanged.
All source-order and actual-output proofs replay from saved arrays.

## 7. Scope

These are finite synthetic constructor fixtures. The source phases, rate and
jitter are declared model parameters used by the verifier, not physical
measurements or independently identified laws. No claim of blinded execution,
general optimizer convergence, uniform whole-noise-ball recovery, independent
review, original-contract admission, full-Hankel certification, native physical
observer/metric selection or SI calibration follows. The nominal747-dimensional
dynamical observer kernel is unchanged. O03 cutoffs remain protocol controls.

# Two-step noise tolerance on the frozen PR195 stress trajectory

The arbitrary-noise order guarantee is **δ≤2^-37 per62-channel vector** (about7.276×10^-12). This guarantees209 singular values above the unchanged source cutoff2^-24. The certified open radius is approximately8.0513436013×10^-12. It is an order guarantee, not a uniform actual-floating phase guarantee.

All six noisy records were frozen before fitting. Both noise Grams and all six raw hashes were reproduced in a separate generation pass. All nine squared-signal peak bins lie within one bin of twice the signed-voltage peak bin. The post-crop FFT bin width is 1,953,125/16,184 Hz. # Signed-voltage reconstruction contract v0.1

21 October 2026. Development — no registry entry. Constructor verification only; independent review pending. Physical promotion = 0. EXIT-03 HOLD.

## Result and disposition

The signed finite-DFT analytic representation round-trips all 891 evaluated channel-records to a maximum absolute error of 1.5543122344752192e-15 V. The frozen narrow-band reconstruction passes **0/891** composite diagnostic gates. No interior point in any evaluated record passes the conservative uniform phase floor. This is a failure of the specified reconstruction/phase-certification gate, not evidence against the simulator or UD dynamics. No native clock, action ratio, physical correspondence or quantum normalization is estimated.

Carrier selection used each live channel's record 0, which was already explored in the preceding content audit. The extension evaluates records 1–99 of channels 1–9, totaling 891; these have varying drive-frequency metadata and are not identical repeated trials. CONTRACT.json was written before running this extension; this is a constructor freeze, not a blinded preregistration or independent review.

## Frozen apparatus-to-signal map

Input: Riechert et al., Heidelberg data DOI https://doi.org/10.11588/DATA/6MEKHI, file ID 6385, v1.0. Source SHA-256: 7966700a6208e2bd2b5829a32b38cce7016f0c3460ace2708c85bac8577c282c. The release filename identifies CH1/3/5/7/9 as sites 1–5 and CH2/4/6/8 as links 1–4; CH10 is labeled empty, not a certified noise witness. No new physical channel calibration is asserted. Imported scripts/notebooks are not executed.

Six metadata columns precede 16384 voltage samples. Retain samples 200–16383, N=16184, fs=1953125 Hz; define t_j=j/fs relative to the documented trigger sample. Demean each retained trace. Let Z=DFT(V) and H double strictly positive-frequency bins, retain DC and Nyquist once, and zero negative-frequency bins. The complex analytic signal is z=IDFT(HZ); Re(z)=V in exact arithmetic. DC removal is preprocessing and does not recover the circuit's physical baseline.

Select fixed fc per channel from its record-0 demeaned Hann-window power maximum in 10–200 kHz. On each subsequent record, form z_f by rectangular projection of z onto strictly positive DFT bins within 5000 Hz of that fc. No per-record retuning, resampling or decimation occurs. The rotating-frame envelope is u(t)=z_f(t) exp(-2 pi i fc t), and signed reconstruction is Re(u(t) exp(2 pi i fc t)). Complex u retains phase that |u| and |u|² discard. Carrier choice is a coordinate convention and does not establish a native primitive period.

The entire post-trigger record supplies RMS residual and delta=max_j|z_j-z_f,j|. Interior diagnostics discard 1024 samples at each end. Accept phase at an interior point only when |u|>10 delta. Accept a record only if relative signed RMS residual <= 0.05 and accepted interior phase fraction >=0.95. These are design thresholds, not statistical confidence levels or UD acceptance criteria.

## Explicit finite-record error statements

For this finite-DFT reference, the residual gives |z-z_f|<=delta by definition. The reverse triangle inequality yields ||z|-|z_f||<=delta. Consequently

    ||z|²-|z_f|²| <= delta (2 |z_f| + delta).

If |z_f|>delta, the disk of radius delta around z_f excludes the origin. Its tangent angle gives

    |arg(z/z_f)| <= asin(delta/|z_f|).

Thus an accepted point has phase error < asin(1/10) = 0.1001674211615598 radians relative to the full finite-DFT analytic reference. Demodulation preserves this bound because its multiplier has unit modulus. A physical error certificate must add instrument, gain, timing and nonperiodic-boundary errors; they are not bounded by this numerical residual.

If an independently known capacitor C applies to the same voltage, the nominal envelope proxy E_env=C|u|²/2 has truncation error <= C delta(2|u|+delta)/2. This is a conditional voltage-derived proxy. The source notebook uses nominal C=20 nF for an envelope routine; that does not certify total LC/coupler energy, baseline, physical Hamiltonian or native energy unit. No new energy number is promoted here.

## Numerical results

| Channel | Fixed fc (Hz) | Median signed RMS residual | Phase fraction (all records) | Composite passes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 31015.393290 | 0.098608 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 2 | 55634.615979 | 0.090683 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 3 | 84960.454770 | 0.046812 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 4 | 56238.028300 | 0.057923 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 5 | 30774.028361 | 0.071944 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 6 | 58048.265262 | 0.067882 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 7 | 87012.056661 | 0.052373 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 8 | 57444.852941 | 0.081110 | 0 | 0/99 |
| 9 | 32101.535467 | 0.042596 | 0 | 0/99 |

The global maximum residual makes the phase gate conservative: excluding endpoint samples from the evaluation region does not remove their contribution to delta. Periodic-extension artifacts can affect this maximum. The present run does not establish whether endpoints, omitted bands, instrument response or other effects dominate. A guard interval alone supplies no certified edge-error bound. The failed threshold is preserved rather than relaxed after seeing the result.

Five synthetic controls check signed round-trip (6.66e-16 maximum), complex modulated-envelope recovery (2.93e-13 maximum), exact opposite-sign ambiguity under squaring, rejection of zero-signal phase, and rejection of an omitted 0.3-amplitude harmonic (relative RMS 0.28735). All 891 records satisfy the amplitude and squared-envelope inequalities numerically. Accepted-point empirical phase checks have zero eligible points and are vacuous; only the synthetic nonzero case tests successful envelope recovery. NumPy floating-point assertions are constructor checks, not formal interval arithmetic or independent metrology.

## Reproduce and proceed

Use Python 3 and NumPy; download source file 6385 from https://heidata.uni-heidelberg.de/api/access/datafile/6385, retaining the original gzip bytes. Run `python3 reconstruct.py /path/to/riechert_waveform.gz`. The script verifies the source hash and contract, then regenerates RECORDS.csv and RESULTS.json. No downloaded executable code is used.

Next freeze a boundary-treatment comparison using synthetic transients and nonperiodic carriers, with known injected amplitude/phase error. Distinguish edge effects from genuine omitted-band content before revising a reconstruction contract. Any revision must keep v0.1's failed result and use a new version. Independently audit acquisition gain/skew and full circuit energy before any cross-channel phase or native-support claim. The absolute apparatus-to-native map, EXIT-03 specification and action anchor remain OPEN/HOLD.
