# Boundary treatment and omitted-band benchmark v0.1

21 October 2026. NUMERICAL SYNTHETIC / DERIVED CONDITIONAL. Development — no registry entry. Constructor checks only; independent review pending. Physical promotion = 0. EXIT-03 HOLD.

## Result

No tested boundary treatment recovers every injected signal. Of six cases, periodic projection passes 2, zero padding 4, reflection padding 4 and Hann taper/division 4. All four fail the narrow-pulse and omitted-sideband full-state diagnostics. There is no empirical rerun, replacement gate, selected winner or action estimate in this milestone. The previous signed-reconstruction contract's **0/891** composite result remains intact.

The benchmark separates two failure mechanisms in known synthetic controls: nonperiodic boundary mismatch and genuine content outside the retained carrier band. It does **not** determine their relative contributions in the experimental traces. The four treatments are candidate signal-processing choices, not physical continuations.

## Frozen setup

CONTRACT.json and benchmark.py were written before execution. The six explicit generators, four methods and metrics are fixed in those files, with no search or post-result adjustment. This is constructor-frozen analysis, not independently reviewed preregistration. The supplied v0.39 ledger is historical context; it does not replace the previously recovered v0.85 source. The supplied CRL-2 subdivision document remains a governance proposal. Nothing is promoted by citation.

Use N=16184 samples, fs=1953125 Hz, trigger-relative t_j=j/fs, carrier fc=257 fs/N=31015.39328966881 Hz and retained half-bandwidth 5000 Hz. Noninteger cases use fc+(37/100)fs/N. All generators have initial phase 73/100 rad. Interior evaluation discards 1024 samples at each end. A synthetic diagnostic passes if complex relative RMS error <=1/100 and maximum phase error <=1/50 rad at points whose true amplitude is at least 1/5 V. These ground-truth-based thresholds differ from v0.1's empirical residual gate; their pass rates must not be compared as if they were the same test.

All methods first subtract the original voltage-record mean, then double retained positive-frequency DFT bins and discard all other bins. Periodic uses the original record. Zero and reflection padding append one original record length on both sides; reflection excludes endpoint replication. Hann uses the original symmetric taper and divides the complex output by its taper only at nonzero-weight points; metrics use the fixed interior, not the endpoints. No carrier fitting, decimation or empirical calibration occurs.

Let P(a,f,p)=a exp(i(2 pi f t+0.73+p)). Synthetic real observations are the real part of the following explicit complex phasors:

| Case | Full injected reference |
|---|---|
| exact_bin | P(1,fc,0) |
| off_bin | P(1,f_off,0) |
| smooth_AM_PM | P(1+0.2 cos(2 pi 600 t), f_off, 0.15 sin(2 pi 200 t)) |
| smooth_turnon | P(0.1+0.45[1+tanh((t-0.001)/0.0002)], f_off,0) |
| narrow_pulse | P(0.05+exp(-((t-0.004)/0.00012)^2),f_off,0) |
| omitted_sideband | P(1,f_off,0)+P(0.3,f_off+12000,0) |

For smooth transients these phasors are declared generative references, not a claim that finite-record or infinite-line analytic transforms equal them exactly. The sideband case separately reports error to its fundamental-only target. Removing a sideband can improve fundamental extraction while failing full-state recovery; those are distinct objectives.

## Results: complex relative RMS error on fixed interior

| Case | Periodic | Zero pad | Reflect pad | Hann/divide |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Exact bin | 5.83e-14 | 0.003822 | 0.004897 | 3.00e-7 |
| Off bin | 0.009294 | 0.005652 | 0.004530 | 2.99e-5 |
| Smooth AM/PM | 0.010865 | 0.006702 | 0.005559 | 3.53e-5 |
| Smooth turn-on | 0.005640 | 0.003784 | 0.001692 | 2.18e-5 |
| Narrow pulse | 0.011585 | 0.011194 | 0.011291 | 0.022994 |
| Omitted sideband, full truth | 0.287532 | 0.287424 | 0.287431 | 0.287377 |
| Omitted sideband, fundamental only | 0.009303 | 0.005685 | 0.004521 | 2.97e-5 |

Phase also matters: periodic turn-on fails its phase threshold (0.05813 rad) even though its RMS error is below 1/100. Complete amplitude/phase metrics and eligible counts are retained in METRICS.csv and RESULTS.json. Hann strongly improves these smooth-signal cases but roughly doubles the pulse RMS error compared with the other methods. No uniform dominance follows from this finite bank.

## Explicit boundary uncertainty bound

This is a standard finite-dimensional linear-filter statement, recorded with its exact scope, not a new UD physical theorem. For a fixed padded length L, retained positive bin set B and inverse-DFT convention 1/L, define

    k_r = (2/L) sum_{b in B} exp(2 pi i b r/L).

The reconstructed complex signal on input x is (k*x)_j. For two extensions x and x+e that agree on the measured segment and satisfy |e_l|<=epsilon_l outside it,

    |Delta z_j| <= sum_{l outside} |k_{j-l}| epsilon_l.

If epsilon_l<=epsilon uniformly, the bound is epsilon times the outside-row absolute sum. Cauchy–Schwarz and DFT orthogonality also give

    |Delta z_j| <= 2 sqrt(|B|/L) ||e||_2.

Proof: expand the convolution difference and apply the triangle inequality; orthogonality gives sum_r|k_r|²=4|B|/L, then Cauchy–Schwarz. Both are exact conditional statements in real arithmetic; evaluated constants below are numerical, not outward-rounded interval enclosures.

For L=48552 and the frozen band, |B|=249 and row l2 norm is approximately 0.1432274. The outside-row absolute sum over the fixed interior ranges approximately 1.06749–1.64220. A unit voltage-sample impulse just outside the measured segment produces maximum interior complex effect approximately 0.00059509 V, despite the 1024-sample guard. The FFT convolution equals the explicitly shifted kernel to 3.88e-18 maximum error. A nonzero coefficient supplies a direct counterexample to “the guard removes all boundary influence”; scaling that impulse precludes a finite uniform continuation-error bound without some amplitude, norm or source restriction.

These bounds apply to extension differences at the same length/filter. The Hann method changes the operator and requires its own error analysis, including division amplification. They are not a bound on unknown infinite-time dynamics or an experimental gain/skew certificate.

Given a separately justified total complex error budget d_j against a specified reference and estimate zhat_j with |zhat_j|>d_j, elementary disk geometry yields phase error <=asin(d_j/|zhat_j|). The reverse triangle inequality yields amplitude error <=d_j and squared-amplitude error <=d_j(2|zhat_j|+d_j). A physical use must include continuation, omitted-band/model, noise, gain, timing and numerical contributions without double-counting. This milestone bounds none of those unknown physical inputs merely by choosing padding.

## Verification and next gate

Run `python3 benchmark.py` with Python 3 and NumPy. Assertions cover exact-bin recovery, preservation of the injected omitted-band full-state failure, the explicit kernel identity, an l2 impulse bound and nonzero guarded boundary influence. There are 24 method/case evaluations. The primary waveforms are generated locally; no imported scripts or notebooks execute. No experimental data are analyzed anew and no independent review is claimed.

Next construct a finite-support quadrature estimator with a fixed demodulation kernel and explicit transfer response. A valid interior estimate should depend only on measured samples, while source assumptions and omitted-band uncertainty remain visible. Freeze its filter, delay, evaluation window and synthetic calibration bank before any experimental rerun. This can remove assumed padded samples from the estimator, but cannot make a finite record identify unrestricted external physics. Gain/skew, total energy/baseline, absolute native support and EXIT-03 remain open.

A. CURRENT MISSION TRAJECTORY — Certify signed reconstruction before using phase or action observables.

B. WHAT WAS DONE — Frozen six-case/four-method synthetic bank; full-state versus fundamental diagnostics; explicit finite-filter boundary bounds.

C. FINDING — Padding can reduce smooth-signal error, but cannot recover excluded content or eliminate continuation uncertainty by guard alone.

D. UD GAP IMPACT — Constructor-checked development only. No new action anchor, native clock, independent review or physical promotion.

# Finite-support quadrature with local source and input-error bounds

Theorem manuscript v0.1 — 21 October 2026. DERIVED / EXACT CONDITIONAL in real arithmetic. Standard weighted least-squares construction applied to the UD measurement protocol; no novelty or physical-identification claim. Constructor checked; independent review pending. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0.

## Theorem

Let offsets k=-m,...,m have sample times s_k=k/fs, nonnegative weights w_k, and real design rows D_k=(cos(omega s_k),-sin(omega s_k),1). Assume G=D^T W D is invertible. Define Q=G^{-1}D^T W and h_k=Q_{0k}+i Q_{1k}. At a measured center j whose complete window is available, put

    zhat_j = sum_k h_k V_{j+k},
    uhat_j = exp(-i omega j/fs) zhat_j.

Then:

1. The three moments are sum h cos=1, sum h(-sin)=i, sum h=0. A signal V_{j+k}=Re(Z_j exp(i omega s_k))+b_j, with constant local phasor Z_j and real constant baseline b_j, is reconstructed exactly as zhat_j=Z_j.
2. Suppose V_{j+k}=Re(u_{j+k} exp(i omega(j+k)/fs))+b_j+e_{j+k}, with |u_{j+k}-u_j|<=L_j |k|/fs and |e_{j+k}|<=epsilon_j. Define H0=sum|h_k| and H1=sum|h_k||k|/fs. Then

       |zhat_j-u_j exp(i omega j/fs)| <= d_j := L_j H1+epsilon_j H0.

   The same bound holds for |uhat_j-u_j|. Time-varying baseline error must enter e; only a constant local baseline cancels.
3. For a constant-amplitude tone Z_j=Z exp(i(omega+delta)j/fs), its exact finite-filter transfer is

       zhat_j = A(delta) Z_j+B(delta) conjugate(Z_j),
       A(delta)=(1/2)sum h_k exp(i(omega+delta)s_k),
       B(delta)=(1/2)sum h_k exp(-i(omega+delta)s_k).

   Therefore |zhat_j-Z_j| <= (|A-1|+|B|)|Z_j|. At delta=0, A=1 and B=0.
4. If d_j<|zhat_j|, then the phase error relative to the specified true phasor is <=asin(d_j/|zhat_j|), amplitude error <=d_j, and squared-amplitude error <=d_j(2|zhat_j|+d_j). These are deterministic conditional bounds, not confidence intervals.

## Proof

Invertibility gives QD=I, hence the moments in (1). Expand Re(Z_j exp(i omega s_k))=Re(Z_j)cos(omega s_k)-Im(Z_j)sin(omega s_k) and apply those moments; the baseline term vanishes. For (2), subtract the exact local constant-phasor reconstruction. The residual at offset k has magnitude at most L_j|k|/fs+epsilon_j because |Re(a)|<=|a| and the oscillatory multiplier has modulus one. Multiply by |h_k|, sum, and use the triangle inequality. Demodulation has unit modulus. For (3), expand the real tone into its positive and negative complex exponentials and collect the two sums. For (4), apply the reverse triangle inequality, factor the difference of squared magnitudes, and use the tangent angle to the disk of radius d_j centered on zhat_j. QED.

## Applicability and limits

This theorem uses only the measured window. It does not use a periodic extension, unseen padding, a Hilbert-transform continuation or whole-record demeaning. With a centered window, the timestamp is j/fs but real-time availability is delayed by m/fs. Discarding the unavailable endpoint centers is essential.

Invertibility is a premise; arbitrary carrier/sample combinations can make the columns dependent. The numerical implementation checks conditioning and moments for its frozen design but does not supply formal outward-rounded enclosures. A deployed bound needs an additional certified numerical allowance.

Input uncertainty can be budgeted, conditionally, as epsilon<=epsilon_noise+g_max V_max+tau_max D_max+epsilon_baseline if independently justified bounds hold for additive noise, relative gain error, voltage magnitude, sampling-time error, voltage derivative and nonconstant baseline residual. This is a sufficient triangle-inequality budget, not a calibration supplied by this work. Fixed carrier error appears through the envelope variation L or the explicit transfer law; do not silently count or omit it twice. Cross-channel synchronization, absolute time units and the apparatus-to-native map need their own evidence.

If an independently calibrated energy proxy C|u|²/2 applies, its estimator contribution is bounded by C d_j(2|uhat_j|+d_j)/2. This does not establish a full Hamiltonian, native support, primitive state recurrence or action normalization.

The accompanying verifier checks the finite transfer identity, source-regularity inequalities and negative controls numerically. No claim advances beyond constructor-checked development.

# A continuous-band quadrature error budget for a saved finite kernel

Theorem manuscript v0.1. 21 October 2026. DERIVED / EXACT CONDITIONAL. Constructor checked; independent review pending. Development — no registry entry. Physical promotion 0. This is a finite-filter measurement theorem, not a physical UD identification or novelty claim.

## Source and estimator

Let fs>0, offsets k=-m,...,m, s_k=k/fs and a fixed complex kernel h_k. Define zhat_j=sum h_k V_{j+k} on centers with a complete measured window. Define its tone responses at carrier fc by

    A(f)=(1/2)sum h_k exp(2pi i(fc+f)s_k),
    B(f)=(1/2)sum h_k exp(-2pi i(fc+f)s_k).

Assume the complex envelope u(t)=integral[-W,W]exp(2pi i f t)dmu(f) for a finite complex measure mu with total variation <=M. Measured samples satisfy

    V_{j+k}=Re(u(t_j+s_k)exp(2pi i fc(t_j+s_k)))+b+e_{j+k},

where |b|<=beta is constant on the window and |e_{j+k}|<=epsilon. This source assumption constrains a global generative signal; its satisfaction cannot be inferred merely from filtering one finite record.

Let D0>=|A(0)-1|+|B(0)| and D1>=|A'(0)|+|B'(0)|. Choose upper bounds H0>=sum|h_k|, H2>=sum|h_k|s_k² and C0>=|sum h_k|. Put

    R(W)=D0+W D1+2pi² H2 W²,
    d=M R(W)+beta C0+epsilon H0+E_fp.

## Theorem

In real arithmetic, estimator error relative to Z_j=u(t_j)exp(2pi i fc t_j) is <=M R(W)+beta C0+epsilon H0. If a declared implementation has complex evaluation error <=E_fp, total output error is <=d. At centers with |Z_j|>=a_min>d, phase error is <=asin(d/a_min). Amplitude error is <=d and squared-amplitude error <=d(2|zhat_j|+d).

A complete measured window introduces no external-sample continuation assumption. A centered window becomes available only at delay m/fs; no phase statement is made where the amplitude premise fails.

Taylor's integral remainder gives |A(f)-1|+|B(f)|<=D0+|f|D1+(f²/2)sup_q(|A''(q)|+|B''(q)|). Each derivative contributes at most (1/2)(2pi)² sum|h_k|s_k²; together the supremum is <=4pi²H2. Thus the response bound R(W) holds for every real f in [-W,W], without interpolation from a frequency grid.

For each spectral tone the real input contains positive and conjugate exponentials. Its response is A(f) times the positive phasor plus B(f) times the conjugate phasor. Subtract the positive reference, integrate and use the total-variation inequality to obtain M R(W). A constant baseline contributes at most beta C0; bounded sample error contributes epsilon H0. Add implementation error by the triangle inequality. The disk of radius d about the true phasor has tangent angle asin(d/|Z_j|), proving the stated phase bound. Reverse triangle and the difference of squares prove the remaining statements. QED.

## Instantiated certificate

Use the unchanged 2049-sample kernel from local-quadrature v0.1, interpreting each saved parsed binary64 coefficient as an exact dyadic rational; fs=1953125 Hz and fc=257fs/16184. Real/imaginary absolute-value sums bound complex magnitudes conservatively. Coefficients are not reoptimized or re-solved. All comparison fields in CERTIFICATE.json contain exact rational fractions. Decimal approximations are explanatory only.     E_eval <= [n u/(1-n u)] 5 H0 + 2 n eta/(1-n u) < 2^-30 V.

This follows by propagating each primitive relative/absolute rounding bound through the finite sums. It bounds that declared evaluation, not arbitrary BLAS/convolution libraries, demodulation, atan2 calls or every platform. The certificate is not a new native runtime-validation receipt. The stored coefficient quantization is already included in A,B and their derivatives.

The phase ratio r=d/a_min is below1/10. Instead of computing inverse sine numerically, use asin(r)<=r/sqrt(1-r²)<=100r/99 for 0<=r<=1/10. The resulting rational phase bound passes1/50 rad. The numerical delay1024/1953125 s passes3/5000 s.

# Leakage-tolerant full-state quadrature and joint instrument budget

Theorem manuscript v0.1 —21 October2026. DERIVED / EXACT CONDITIONAL. Constructor checked, independent review pending. Development —no registry entry. Physical promotion0. Standard linear-filter bounds, not physical UD identification or a novelty claim.

## Theorem

Use the unchanged finite complex kernel h and full measured-window estimator zhat=sum h_k V_{j+k} from local-quadrature v0.1. Let H>=sum|h_k|, C0>=|sum h_k|, and let R bound |A(f)-1|+|B(f)| throughout the declared in-band envelope support. Write the complex envelope u=u_in+u_tail, where the in-band spectral measure has total variation<=M and the tail spectral measure has total variation<=T. The tail may occupy arbitrary frequencies for the estimator-error theorem; in particular no unproved anti-alias suppression is assumed. Assume constant baseline magnitude<=beta, input sample errors<=epsilon and implementation evaluation error<=E_fp.

Then the error against the **full** phasor Z_j=u(t_j)exp(2pi i fc t_j) obeys

    d_full <= M R+(H+1) T+H epsilon+beta C0+E_fp.

Against the **in-band-only** reference, instead,

    d_in <= M R+H T+H epsilon+beta C0+E_fp.

These are different targets. At full-reference amplitude>=a_min>d_full, geometric phase error<=asin(d_full/a_min). For d_full/a_min<=1/10, the rational upper bound100 d_full/(99 a_min) suffices.

## Proof

The existing continuous-band theorem bounds the in-band error by M R. At any time, total variation bounds |u_tail|<=T, hence the tail's real voltage has magnitude<=T. The finite kernel's response to that voltage is at most H T. Comparing the output against the full reference also subtracts the tail phasor itself, whose magnitude is<=T, producing (H+1)T. Comparing only with the in-band reference does not subtract that phasor, producing H T. Baseline, sample and evaluation terms follow by triangle inequalities. Apply disk geometry and the previously proved rational inverse-sine bound for phase. QED.

The full-state tail coefficient is a conservative sufficient bound, not asserted optimal for a particular frequency distribution. It cannot be replaced by the in-band formula while retaining the full reference: even an ideal rejection of a tail leaves that tail absent from the recovered full state. Frequency-specific response bounds can sharpen the coefficient only under additional spectral information.

## Exact sufficient frontier

With M=1, beta=3, a_min=1/2, absolute target1/100 V and phase target1/50 rad, the rational phase certificate imposes d<=99/10000 V, which also satisfies the absolute target. Put C=R+3C0+E_fp. The sufficient feasible set is

    (H+1)T+H epsilon <= 99/10000-C,    T>=0, epsilon>=0.

At fixed epsilon, the largest admitted T under this certificate is (99/10000-C-H epsilon)/(H+1), provided the numerator is nonnegative. At fixed T, the admitted epsilon is (99/10000-C-(H+1)T)/H for H>0. Frontier equality is included. This is the feasible set of this sufficient certificate, not the physically optimal frontier across all kernels or uncertainty models.

## Instrument allocation

Suppose measured-input uncertainty is bounded by

    epsilon <= epsilon_noise+g_max V_max+tau_max D_max+epsilon_baseline,

where additive noise includes quantization, gain error is relative to a signal of magnitude<=V_max, timing error is<=tau_max and the clean voltage derivative is bounded by D_max throughout every displaced sampling interval. Any baseline variation beyond the locally constant component is included in epsilon_baseline. This sufficient allocation uses worst-case addition, with no assumed statistical independence or cancellation.

The declared split is noise/quantization1/10000 V plus gain, timing and baseline1/20000 V each, totaling1/4000 V. Relative gain<=1/100000 with V_max=5 V supplies the gain share. tau_max=1/5000000000 s (0.2 ns) and D_max=250000 V/s supply the timing share. Under an additional physical tail-frequency cutoff|fc+f|<=200000 Hz,

    |V_clean'| <= 2pi[(fc+50) M+200000 T] <196526 V/s

for the frozen fc and T=1/1000 V, excluding baseline variation handled separately. Using pi<22/7 makes this a rational sufficient derivative bound. The cutoff is not needed for the generic leakage theorem, but is needed for this illustrative timing justification. No observed hardware capability or cross-channel skew calibration is claimed.

## Limits of finite-record tail certification

A finite set of voltage samples does not itself bound unrestricted out-of-band spectral-measure total variation. For N real sample constraints, choose N+1 distinct real sinusoidal basis functions with frequencies in an allowed tail interval. The N-by-(N+1) evaluation matrix has a nonzero real null vector; linear independence of distinct sinusoidal functions implies that combination is not identically zero as a function. It vanishes at all measured sample times and can be scaled to arbitrarily large finite spectral variation. Thus the same finite samples can coexist with arbitrarily large unobserved tails unless an independent source, norm or model restriction excludes them. This is an identifiability obstruction under unrestricted amplitudes, not a no-go against calibrated source controls or source-class assumptions.

Therefore an FFT of the same finite record, even after filtering, is not by itself an independent tail-TV certificate. Source restrictions, calibrated monitor bounds, justified transfer/anti-alias models or other independent evidence must close that premise. # Leakage witness with uncertain frequencies and monitor duration

Theorem manuscript v0.1. 21 October2026 America/Chicago. DERIVED / EXACT CONDITIONAL. Constructor checked; independent review pending. Development —no registry entry; physical promotion0. Standard Gram/coercivity inequalities applied to measurement requirements, not a physical UD identification or novelty claim.

## General Gram witness

On the actual monitor interval I of duration T, use normalized inner product (1/T)integral_I conjugate(v)w dt. Let p(t)=sum_{l=1}^K a_l exp(2pi i f_l t) with distinct constant frequencies. Let G be their Hermitian Gram matrix. If G>=lambda_* I with lambda_*>0, a calibrated estimate phat satisfies ||p-phat||_{L2(I)/sqrt(T)}<=epsilon_mon, and r_meas bounds ||phat||_{L2(I)/sqrt(T)}, then

    T_tail <= sqrt(K/lambda_*) (r_meas+epsilon_mon)+T_out,

provided an independent outside-model spectral-measure TV bound<=T_out holds.

Proof: ||p||²=a*Ga>=lambda_*||a||². Cauchy–Schwarz gives sum|a_l|<=sqrt(K)||a||, and the L2 triangle inequality gives ||p||<=r_meas+epsilon_mon. Add the outside-model measure by the TV triangle inequality. QED.

The monitor error here is a **waveform L2 error**, including frequency/clock normalization, gain, reference error, numerical integration/reconstruction and outside-model contamination/isolation error. It differs from a directly certified coefficient-vector error in the preceding orthogonal theorem. If such a coefficient-error certificate already exists, its direct l1/l2 bound remains valid without this Gram route; do not substitute one error type for the other.

## Robust lower bound from nominal integer modes

Let T0>0, distinct integers n_l and f_l=f_common+n_l/T0+e_l with |e_l|<=eta. Assume the actual interval satisfies |T/T0-1|<=rho, rho>=0. For d_lm=|n_l-n_m|, define

    q_lm=d_lm rho+2 eta T0(1+rho).

If q_lm<d_lm for every pair, then

    |G_lm| <= q_lm/(d_lm-q_lm), l!=m,
    lambda_min(G) >= 1-max_l sum_{m!=l} q_lm/(d_lm-q_lm).

Proof: the frequency difference obeys |(f_l-f_m)T-(n_l-n_m)|<=q_lm. The normalized exponential inner product has magnitude |sinc((f_l-f_m)T)|, with sinc(x)=sin(pi x)/(pi x). Since the nominal difference is a nonzero integer, |sin(pi(integer+v))|<=pi|v| and |integer+v|>=d_lm-q_lm. This gives the pair bound. G has diagonal1 and is Hermitian, so its smallest eigenvalue is bounded below by1 minus the largest off-diagonal absolute row sum. Equivalently bound the off-diagonal quadratic form by its maximal row sum. QED.

An arbitrary common frequency shift cancels from pair differences and changes Gram entries only by an interval-location phase convention. This invariance does not certify that the shifted modes remain in a physical tail-frequency band; that premise remains separate. A time-varying frequency or nonlinear clock warp is not covered by the constant-frequency/duration model and needs its own error bound.

## Exact instantiated design

Freeze K=100 nominal modes n=100,...,199, T0=1s, eta=1/200Hz and rho=1/100000000. Exact rational row sums give lambda_min(G)>=lambda_G, where the authoritative fraction appears in CERTIFICATE.json and lambda_G is approximately0.9098874884. In particular lambda_G>9/10.

    T_tail <=(211/20)(15/200000)+1/5000
           =793/800000 V=0.00099125V <1/1000V.

The supplied error/TV premises are proposed requirements, not measurements. Outside-mode projection contamination cannot be assumed zero, particularly when T_out exceeds epsilon_mon. Independent isolation/transfer or contamination evidence remains essential.

On a centered one-second interval, take distinct frequencies f1=201/2-1/2000000Hz and f2=201/2+1/2000000Hz with coefficients+1V and-1V. Their spectral measure has TV2V. Their separation is delta=1/1000000Hz, and pointwise

    |exp(2pi i f1 t)-exp(2pi i f2 t)| <=2pi delta |t| <=pi delta.

## Direct sampled witness

Let the finite-mode component be

$$p(t)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{K}a_\ell e^{2\pi i f_\ell t},$$

and the full source tail be p+r_out, with outside-model complex spectral-measure total variation at most T_out. For actual sample times t_j, j=0,...,N-1, define the sample norm ||v||_d²=N^{-1}sum_j|v_j|². Let the complex-monitor outputs satisfy

$$y_j=p(t_j)+r_{\rm out}(t_j)+e_j,\qquad \|e\|_d\le\epsilon_d.$$

The monitor must be independent and applicable to this source; e includes I/Q/path calibration, acquisition, quantization, baseline, reference and numerical errors. Put Phi_{j,l}=exp(2pi i f_l t_j) and G_d=Phi*Phi/N. If G_d>=lambda_d I with lambda_d>0 and r_d>=||y||_d, then

$$T_{\rm tail}\le\sqrt{K/\lambda_d}\,(r_d+\epsilon_d+T_{\rm out})+T_{\rm out}.$$

Proof: ||p(t_j)||_d²=a*G_d a>=lambda_d||a||_2². Also |r_out(t)|<=T_out, so ||p(t_j)||_d<=||y||_d+epsilon_d+T_out. Apply ||a||_1<=sqrt(K)||a||_2 and add the outside-model measure. QED.

This bound explicitly charges outside-mode contamination inside the sample norm as well as its contribution to the full spectral tail. It does not assume a perfect isolation filter or infer a continuous-time RMS by interpolating the samples. The finite-mode source model must hold on the claimed source scope; finite samples alone cannot establish it.

## Timing-robust sampled Gram bound

Assume T0>0, distinct integer nominal modes n_l and fixed frequencies f_l=f_common+n_l/T0+e_l, |e_l|<=eta. Actual sample times obey

$$t_j=t_{\rm epoch}+(1+\alpha)jT_0/N+\xi_j,\quad |\alpha|\le\rho,\quad |\xi_j|\le\tau.$$

Epoch is arbitrary. A common frequency or epoch shift contributes only unit-modulus row/column factors and leaves Gram eigenvalues unchanged. It does not certify absolute phase or physical band membership. For d_lm=|n_l-n_m|, set

$$q_{\ell m}=d_{\ell m}\rho+2\eta T_0(1+\rho),\qquad s_{\ell m}=1-\frac{1}{6}\left[\frac{\pi(d_{\ell m}+q_{\ell m})}{N}\right]^2.$$

Suppose all nominal modes are distinct modulo N and every pair satisfies q<d, d+q<N/2 and s>0. Then

$$|(G_d)_{\ell m}|\le b_{\ell m}:=\frac{q_{\ell m}}{(d_{\ell m}-q_{\ell m})s_{\ell m}}+2\pi\left(\frac{d_{\ell m}}{T_0}+2\eta\right)\tau,$$

and

$$\lambda_{\min}(G_d)\ge 1-\max_\ell\sum_{m\ne\ell}b_{\ell m}.$$

Proof: first set xi_j=0. Write u=(f_l-f_m)(1+alpha)T0. Its distance from the signed nominal integer gap is at most q. The geometric-series magnitude is |sin(pi u)|/[N|sin(pi u/N)|]. The numerator is <=pi q. With |u| between d-q and d+q, sin(x)>=x-x³/6 on this guarded interval gives denominator>=pi(d-q)s. Now restore xi_j. The change of each pair-phase factor has magnitude<=2pi|f_l-f_m||xi_j|, and |f_l-f_m|<=d/T0+2eta. Average these perturbations and apply the maximal absolute-row-sum lower bound for a Hermitian matrix with diagonal1. QED.

In the rational certificate, pi is conservatively replaced by22/7 in upper terms and in the denominator factor's subtracted upper term. No floating trigonometry or eigenvalue is used for acceptance. These are sufficient guards; a failed row bound does not imply that a particular Gram matrix is singular.

## Instantiated sampled design

Freeze N=1024, T0=1s, n_l=100,...,199, eta=1/200Hz, rho=1/100000000 and tau=1/100000000s=10ns. T0 is the nominal cyclic grid span; the first-to-last nominal sample separation is1023/1024s. This is an independent complex-envelope monitor design, not the original acquisition clock or its0.2ns requirement.

Exact rational row sums yield lambda_d>0.9096. Therefore lambda_d>=9/10 is certified, and C=211/20 satisfies C²*(9/10)>=100. Choose r_d<=55microvolts, epsilon_d<=20microvolts and T_out<=10microvolts. Then

$$T_{\rm tail}\le\frac{211}{20}(55+20+10)\,\mu{\rm V}+10\,\mu{\rm V}=906.75\,\mu{\rm V}<1\,{\rm mV}.$$

The new outside-model ceiling is prospectively stricter than the previous200microvolt proposal. With that previous ceiling and the same direct-monitor formula, the sufficient bound is3.10125mV, which misses the1mV target. The earlier isolated-waveform/coefficient-error routes remain valid under their own assumptions; this is not a retraction of those theorems or evidence that every source with the larger ceiling fails.

## Quadrature and digital arithmetic

One sufficient independent-monitor error split is10microvolts calibrated acquisition/quantization,5microvolts quadrature-matrix error,3microvolts residual baseline and2microvolts numerical error. These sum to20microvolts. For a calibrated real two-component input vector of norm<=5V, operator-norm matrix uncertainty<=1/1000000 gives a5microvolt output contribution. Applicable full-path frequency response, reference uncertainty, nonlinearity and any conditioning/amplification must be included; a static matrix label alone does not establish them.

For exact serialized binary64 complex values y_j, compute E=N^{-1}sum[(Re y_j)²+(Im y_j)²] as a rational number. E<=r_max² certifies the digital RMS ceiling without a floating square root. An explanatory rational RMS upper bound can be obtained with an integer ceiling square root. This certifies arithmetic on the stored values, not that they equal physical source samples or that calibration errors satisfy epsilon_d. The previous steps producing those values retain their own numerical/error obligations.

## Aliasing and evidence limits

On the nominal1024-point grid, integer modes100 and1124 are identical at every sample. Their opposite1V coefficients produce zero sampled signal while distinct source atoms have TV2V. A continuous-time Gram theorem alone cannot exclude this sampled alias. The declared100..199 bank, non-alias guard and independent outside-model bound are essential. With only64 samples the proposed100-mode bank also has a rank obstruction.

No time-varying coefficients, unrestricted off-bank modes, clock warping or arbitrary transfer errors are admitted by the fixed-mode contract. The source completeness and10microvolt outside-model TV bound cannot be inferred solely from the same finite samples. No physical gain, skew, I/Q accuracy, independent reference identity, native support, full energy, primitive clock, eta_A or EXIT-03 closure is supplied here. No experiment is executed.

# Sampled-monitor receipt graph v0.1

**RESULT: PASS_SCOPED — constructor software controls.** Nine reviewed evidence roles now connect the sampled-monitor design to an unsigned tail-bound proposal. One author-controlled positive fixture and 56 rejection controls passed (57 cases). This is a structural contract and reproducible computation, not independent review or empirical admission. **Physical Promotion = 0; EXIT-03 HOLD; independent review pending.**

## What is bound

Every evidence node binds one frozen apparatus/run, source preparation, acquisition profile, channel mapping, monitor epoch, units, residual reference, kernel and source-contract hash. Receipts bind exact node bytes, witness bytes, role and fixture designation. Config and receipt allowlist must be controlled outside the submitting packet. The bundled allowlist and reviewer labels are entirely synthetic and author controlled; they confer no review authority.

| Evidence role | Required witness and scope |
|---|---|
| Samples | 1024 ordered signed complex residual samples in V; canonical finite binary64 hex words; original bytes included and reviewed |
| Clock | Timestamp bytes plus metrology supporting **true physical times**; affine error ≤10 ppb and total sample residual ≤10 ns, including timestamp/metrology uncertainty |
| I/Q path | Complete residual measurement/extraction path, applicable frequency/voltage range, loading and conditioning; matrix error ≤1/10⁶ at raw two-vector norm ≤5 V |
| Error budget | Deterministic complex sample RMS shares ≤10 µV acquisition/quantization, 5 µV quadrature, 3 µV baseline, 2 µV numerical; matrix charge cannot be omitted |
| Source class | Fixed coefficients/frequencies across both intervals, modes100–199, 1 s grid span, ≤5 mHz mode errors; independent preparation/completeness evidence |
| Outside-model TV | Independently supported complex spectral-measure variation ≤10 µV; same monitor FFT, assumptions or standard deviation do not establish this |
| Transfer | Same residual complex spectral measure, simultaneous preparation and common epoch across monitor and acquisition intervals |
| Computation | Source hashes; recomputed exact digital energy/RMS, rational sampled-Gram floor and tail calculation |
| Tail TV | Unsigned deterministic upper-bound proposal carrying graph/config/profile hashes and dependency roles |

The clock contract is distinct from the original acquisition's 0.2 ns error requirement. Timestamp residual checks verify the submitted numerical list; the reviewed calibration must establish its relationship to actual sampling events. A correctly formatted list alone supplies no time calibration.

The prototype coverage is [−1/10⁸,100000001/10⁸] seconds, containing the 1024 nominal monitor samples at j/1024 and the acquisition interval [0,16183/1953125] seconds. This is a **synthetic prospective acquisition profile**, separate from the unresolved historical profile. A source must maintain the reviewed preparation and residual decomposition over that entire interval. The transfer receipt must account for any primary-signal subtraction, reference conversion and loading. Their errors must fit the stated allocations; matching apparatus names is insufficient.

## Exact arithmetic and output boundary

The inherited theorem gives, conditionally,

\[
T_{\rm tail}\le\frac{211}{20}(r_d+\epsilon_d+T_{\rm out})+T_{\rm out}.
\]

At the frozen ceilings r_d=11/200000 V, epsilon_d=1/50000 V and T_out=1/100000 V, the design upper bound is

\[
T_{\rm tail}\le\frac{3627}{4000000}\,\mathrm V
=0.00090675\,\mathrm V<\frac1{1000}\,\mathrm V.
\]

The new checker replays the rational sampled-Gram lower bound and computes the mean squared complex norm of the exact serialized binary64 sample values. An integer ceiling square root produces its rational RMS upper bound. The design uses the 55 µV ceiling, not an unproved continuous-time RMS interpolation. The synthetic waveform and its copied bytes are inherited from the prior fixture; they are not measured I/Q data.

`TAIL_BOUND_PROPOSAL_FIXTURE.json` is **UD_UNSIGNED_MONITOR_TAIL_PROPOSAL_1**, not a v0.1 acquisition evidence packet or an approved receipt. Importing it requires independent review of the graph and an explicit reviewed bridge/policy integration. The v0.1 checker is unchanged; there is no automatic twelve-role admission. The other eleven acquisition roles, including full amplitude and tail absolute frequency, remain required. A TV bound alone does not discharge absolute bandwidth, energy, native support or an action bridge. No new mathematical theorem is asserted in this software milestone.

## Adversarial verification

The suite checks run/channel/epoch/unit/kernel/source mismatches; stale coverage; clock bounds and actual submitted timestamp deviations; I/Q multiplication and undercharging; invalid, excessive or statistical bounds; unsupported source/FFT roots; stationary-mode requirements and alias intrusion; unproved historical transfer; changed computation source, energy, Gram constants and tail export; missing, duplicate, unknown and cyclic references; corrupted sample/method bytes; nonfinite and short sample records; unapproved receipts, constructor labels, fixture laundering, unsafe paths and duplicate JSON keys.

These controls verify implementation behavior under the chosen schema. They cannot authenticate a reviewer, prove the truth of a witness report, establish statistical coverage as deterministic support, or demonstrate physical independence. # A source-to-path bound for spectral leakage under widely linear response and polynomial distortion

Version 0.1 · 24 October 2026 · Conditional mathematical theorem

## 1. Signal class and conventions

For a finite complex Borel measure μ on the real frequency line, define

\[
\mathcal F^{-1}\mu(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{2\pi i f t}\,d\mu(f),
\qquad \|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=|\mu|(\mathbb R).
\]

The measure has voltage units when its Fourier–Stieltjes transform is a complex voltage. Its norm bounds the voltage uniformly in time. A bounded Borel multiplier H acts on measures by d(Hμ)=H dμ, with norm at most sup|H|. Here conjugation of a signal corresponds to reflection and conjugation of its measure and preserves total variation. Multiplication of two such signals corresponds to convolution of their finite measures, whose norm satisfies

\[
\|\mu*\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\|\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]

All measures below are fixed descriptions of the source and path, not reconstructions inferred from finitely many target samples. Bounds on their norms are assumptions requiring separate physical evidence in an application.

## 2. Source-to-path leakage theorem

Let the input have decomposition u=b+s+r, with respective finite complex measures μ_b, μ_s, μ_r and

\[
\|\mu_b\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le B,\qquad
\mu_s=\sum_{\ell=1}^{K}a_\ell\delta_{f_\ell},\quad
\sum_\ell|a_\ell|\le A,\qquad
\|\mu_r\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le R.
\]

The frequencies f_l are distinct and fixed. Let U=B+A+R. Suppose the complex output is exactly

\[
z=H_+u+H_-\overline u
+\sum_{d=2}^{D_*}\ \sum_{m+n=d}
 c_{mn}V_*\left(\frac{u}{V_*}\right)^m
                  \left(\frac{\overline u}{V_*}\right)^n+w,
\]

where H_± denote fixed spectral multipliers, V_*>0 is a reference voltage, the coefficients c_mn are dimensionless and fixed, and w has a finite measure μ_w. Assume

\[
\sup_f|H_+(f)|\le M,\quad
\sup_f|H_-(f)|\le J,\quad
\sum_{m+n=d}|c_{mn}|\le\beta_d,\quad
\|\mu_w\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le D.
\]

The multiplier bounds need only hold on the support of the measures they multiply, but that support must be established independently. In the absence of such a support restriction, a global bound is required. Omitted orders, memory effects, start-up transients, drift, additive terms and any primary-reference subtraction error must be included in the finite-measure remainder; a pointwise residual or RMS fit is insufficient.

Define the ideal residual q=z−H_+b. Then q=p+e, where

\[
p(t)=\sum_\ell H_+(f_\ell)a_\ell e^{2\pi i f_\ell t},
\]

and e has a finite measure satisfying

\[
\boxed{\quad
T_{\mathrm{out}}:=\|\mu_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le MR+JU+\sum_{d=2}^{D_*}\beta_d\frac{U^d}{V_*^{d-1}}+D.
\quad}
\tag{1}
\]

This is a bound on the entire remainder measure; it is therefore also an upper bound on its restriction outside the declared finite mode set. It permits remainder mass on that set and does not assume an orthogonal spectral projection. Moreover,

\[
\|\mu_q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le MA+T_{\mathrm{out}}.
\tag{2}
\]

**Proof.** The input measure satisfies ||μ_u||_TV≤U. Expanding the stated output model and subtracting H_+b leaves H_+s as the finite component. The linear source impurity H_+r has norm at most MR. The image term H_- conjugate(u) has norm at most JU. For every monomial, convolution submultiplicativity and preservation of norm under conjugate reflection give

\[
\left\|\mathcal M\!\left[
 c_{mn}V_*\left(\frac u{V_*}\right)^m
                 \left(\frac{\overline u}{V_*}\right)^n
\right]\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le |c_{mn}|\frac{U^{m+n}}{V_*^{m+n-1}},
\]

where M[·] denotes its representing finite measure. Summing at each degree and adding μ_w proves (1). The finite component has norm Σ|H_+(f_l)a_l|≤MA. The triangle inequality proves (2). Every term in (1) has voltage units. ∎

The full input U is essential. For b=1 V and s=a exp(2πift), quadratic distortion has constant, mixed and second-harmonic terms. Budgeting only β₂A²/V_* omits the primary-driven distortion, including the mixed coefficient 2ba. Even perfect subtraction of the **linear** primary does not remove these terms. Likewise, image response acts on the full input, not only its small residual.

## 3. Sample-norm feasibility corollary

Let Φ_jl=exp(2πif_l t_j), G=Φ*Φ/N, and suppose λ_max(G)≤Λ. Let ||a||₂≤a₂ and let y_j=q(t_j)+v_j with complex sample error ||v||_d≤ε, where ||x||_d²=N⁻¹Σ|x_j|². Then

\[
\boxed{\quad \|y\|_d\le\sqrt\Lambda\,M a_2+T_{\mathrm{out}}+\varepsilon.\quad}
\tag{3}
\]

**Proof.** For h_l=H_+(f_l)a_l, the sampled finite component has norm squared h*Gh≤Λ||h||₂²≤ΛM²a₂². The remainder is uniformly bounded by T_out, so its sampled norm is at most T_out. Add the sample error by the triangle inequality. ∎

For the previously derived 1024-sample design, the row-sum argument gives both λ_min(G)≥9/10 and λ_max(G)≤11/10. Thus √Λ≤21/20 is a rational upper bound. The design permits mode indices100–199, a one-second nominal cyclic span, per-mode errors≤5 mHz, relative affine timing error≤10 ppb and per-sample residual≤10 ns. An arbitrary common frequency shift and epoch leave this Gram bound invariant; they do not establish physical band membership or absolute phase.

## 4. Exact proposed instance

Take a 1 V primary TV bound, 100 finite lines each of amplitude 1/400000 V, independently bounded source impurity R=1/10⁶ V, M=51/50, J=1/10⁶, V_*=1 V, β₂=β₃=1/10⁶ and D=1/500000 V. The aggregate line bounds are A=1/4000 V and a₂=1/40000 V. These are requirements for a source-controlled calibration fixture, not measured apparatus properties.

Equation (1) gives

\[
T_{\mathrm{out}}\le
\frac{6021506252019813251}{10^{24}}\,\mathrm V
\approx6.021506252020\,\mu\mathrm V
<10\,\mu\mathrm V.
\]

With ε=20 µV, equation (3) gives

\[
\|y\|_d\le
\frac{52796506252019813251}{10^{24}}\,\mathrm V
\approx52.796506252020\,\mu\mathrm V
<55\,\mu\mathrm V.
\]

The same source assumptions already give the stronger direct tail-TV bound MA+T_out≈0.261021506253 mV. Consequently this engineered fixture tests consistency of the measurement path and the conditional monitor theorem; it does not infer an unknown native dynamics or obtain source completeness from monitor data. The inherited general monitor ceiling0.90675 mV remains valid under its separate55/20/10 µV ceilings.

## 5. Scope of physical use

A finite set of gain/distortion measurements does not by itself establish the uniform multiplier, coefficient and spectral-remainder bounds assumed above. A measured PSD, noise RMS, or pointwise polynomial-fit residual is not automatically a deterministic complex spectral-TV bound. If such bounds cannot be justified, the theorem remains conditional.

For example, nominal sampling at j/1024 cannot distinguish opposite atoms at100 and1124 Hz: their sum vanishes at every sample, while the source spectral variation can be arbitrarily large. Source preparation and outside-model evidence must therefore come from independently justified restrictions, not the same output FFT. A prospective calibration fixture supplies no retrospective transfer to an unresolved historical run.

Mathematical status: constructor-proved conditional theorem; independent review pending. No empirical source/path bound, native action scale, or physical identification is asserted.
